text:
# SOP-P1-L1-01 Line startup - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the standardized method to start the Hot Forge line for production readiness, focusing on safe energization, equipment verification, and attainment of target billet condition prior to forming operations.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance technicians, and line leads responsible for EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 on P1-L1 only. Refer to MM-P1-L1-IH03 for maintenance records, SB-1009 for safety bulletin information, and SOP-P1-L1-03 for shutdown sequence.

Preconditions
3. Line area clear of nonessential personnel; permit-to-work closed for any open electrical or mechanical work. All lockout/tagout work orders must be returned and verified complete per plant LOTO practice. Machine guards and interlocks must be installed and functional. Control room operator must have clear line of sight or video feed of line entry points.

PPE
4. Required PPE: heat-resistant gloves, face shield with splash protection, safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear, flame-resistant clothing. Verify PPE condition and certifications before entry into controlled hot zones around EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and forming stations.

Background and rationale
5. Proper startup reduces thermal gradients that cause billet distortion and reduces mechanical stress on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 mandrel and clamping systems. Preheat and staging minimize scrap and protect tooling. This SOP ensures the billet reaches specified metallurgical readiness and mechanical components are torqued to required specification to prevent slippage and fatigue failures during radial ring rolling.

Critical target parameters
6. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C. Monitor and record the temperature readback from the EQ-P1-L1-IH03 control panel. Do not proceed to forming until the target reading is stable and within process tolerance defined in the heating system HMI.

7. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 635 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench; log torque verification to the equipment maintenance record.

Step-by-step startup procedure
8. Visual and documentation check
   8.1 Verify that the daily prestart checklist is completed and signed by the shift lead.  
   8.2 Confirm there are no active maintenance tags on EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, or EQ-P1-L1-IH03.  
   8.3 Inspect emergency stops, light curtains, and guarding for correct operation.

9. Power and control verification
   9.1 Ensure main supply breakers are in the ready state per control room protocol.  
   9.2 Bring PLCs and HMIs online and verify communications to each equipment PLC. Check alarm logs for persistent faults and clear only those faults that are documented and resolved.

10. Mechanical readiness for EQ-P1-L1-RR01
   10.1 Inspect mandrel and clamp assembly for foreign material, wear, and lubricant condition.  
   10.2 Verify mandrel clamp bolt torque is 635 N·m. Record the measured torque values and the torque tool serial number in the maintenance log. If torque cannot be achieved, tag out and escalate to maintenance.

11. Conveyor and feeder checks for EQ-P1-L1-CN02
   11.1 Confirm conveyor tracking and belt integrity visually. Ensure sensors are aligned and clean. Verify feed position limits and speed command response in manual jog mode prior to automated feed.

12. Induction heater procedure for EQ-P1-L1-IH03
   12.1 Confirm refractory containment and cooling circuits are functional.  
   12.2 Engage heater controls in manual heat-up mode and observe ramp behavior on the EQ-P1-L1-IH03 HMI. Monitor for unusual noises or vibrations.  
   12.3 Wait for the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C. Log the time and temperature when target is reached and confirm stability before initiating feed.

13. Trial billet and process confirmation
   13.1 Load a trial billet and follow controlled feed to EQ-P1-L1-RR01 with operators in position. Observe material flow, mandrel engagement, and clamp behavior.  
   13.2 Inspect the trial part for dimensional fidelity and surface defects. Compare against the process acceptance criteria in operator work instructions.

14. Production enable
   14.1 If trial part meets acceptance criteria, enable automatic cycle and monitor the first production run.  
   14.2 Continue to sample parts at the frequency specified in the production control plan and log results.

Examples and rationale
15. Example record entry: "EQ-P1-L1-IH03 temp steady at 1180 °C as of 07:45; mandrel bolts torqued to 635 N·m; trial part passed visual and dimensional acceptance." Such entries provide traceability for thermal and mechanical readiness decisions.

Records to keep
16. Maintain the following records in the equipment folder and digital document control system:
   - Completed prestart checklist with signatures.  
   - Torque verification log showing mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 is 635 N·m.  
   - EQ-P1-L1-IH03 temperature log showing attainment of 1180 °C.  
   - Trial part inspection report and photos.  
   - Any alarms or faults encountered during startup and their corrective actions.

Deviation handling
17. If any parameter cannot be met (temperature, torque, interlock status), stop startup and log a deviation. Notify maintenance and line management. Follow MM-P1-L1-IH03 for maintenance escalation and SB-1009 for safety incident reporting.

Related documents
18. See MM-P1-L1-IH03, SB-1009, SOP-P1-L1-03 for maintenance, safety, and shutdown references.

Sign-off
19. Operator: ______________________ Date: ______________________  
20. Shift Lead: ____________________ Date: ______________________  
21. Maintenance Representative: ____________________ Date: ______________________

End of procedure.
title: Line startup - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P1-L1-02 Product changeover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03  
Related: ECN-2026-003, SB-1009, SB-1025

1. Purpose and scope  
   1.1 Purpose: Define required activities, roles, and records to perform a safe, repeatable product changeover on the Hot Forge line (P1-L1) covering EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03.  
   1.2 Scope: Applies to operations, maintenance, and quality personnel executing mechanical, tooling, and CNC configuration steps during changeover.

2. Background and rationale  
   2.1 Background: Changeovers on the Hot Forge line include mechanical setups on the radial ring rolling mill, tooling and lubrication verification on CNC turning centers, and inspection handling at the induction heater. Consistent procedure reduces scrap, prevents equipment damage, and preserves process traceability.  
   2.2 Rationale: Explicit torque and lubricant specifications are provided to eliminate variability that leads to mandrel slippage, premature tool wear, or part out-of-spec. The specification below is mandatory for the named equipment models.

3. Preconditions (must be confirmed before starting)  
   3.1 Work permit for mechanical work is valid and visible at equipment site.  
   3.2 Machine power is locked out and tagged per site lockout policy.  
   3.3 All required tooling and materials are staged at the work area.  
   3.4 Required personnel have completed job-specific training and read ECN-2026-003 and SB-1009 where referenced.  
   3.5 Inspection measurements and previous run sheets for the outgoing product are archived and available.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE) required  
   4.1 Hearing protection certified for facility noise environment.  
   4.2 Cut-resistant gloves for handling tooling and mandrels.  
   4.3 Safety glasses with side shields.  
   4.4 Flame-resistant clothing when working adjacent to induction heater operations on EQ-P1-L1-IH03.  
   4.5 Steel-toe footwear.  
   Note: Ensure PPE is donned before work begins and remain in place until sign-off.

5. Preparatory steps (verify before mechanical steps)  
   5.1 Verify that the incoming work order and ECN-2026-003 change instruction match the new product configuration.  
   5.2 Confirm tooling list against SB-1009. Remove obsolete tooling and tag for return or maintenance.  
   5.3 Stage calibration gages and inspection fixtures referenced in SB-1025.

6. Changeover sequence (mechanical, CNC, inspection)  
   6.1 Radial ring rolling mill (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) mechanical setup  
       6.1.1 Remove previous mandrel and clean seating surfaces using lint-free cloth and approved solvent.  
       6.1.2 Install new mandrel. Confirm mandrel keying aligns with locating features.  
       6.1.3 The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 635 N·m. Apply torque using a calibrated torque wrench and confirm reading on the torque wrench calibration label. Document torque reading on the changeover record.  
       6.1.4 Rotate mandrel by hand to verify free rotation and absence of binding after torquing.

   6.2 CNC turning center (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) setup  
       6.2.1 Load new program and verify program revision matches the work order. Cross-reference SB-1009 for acceptable program versions.  
       6.2.2 Install turning tools and set tool offsets according to the program tool list. Use protected hands and eye protection while changing tools.  
       6.2.3 Apply lubricant to specified points. The lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508. Record the lubricant part number and lot number on the maintenance checklist.  
       6.2.4 Verify spindle and turret interlocks before enabling automatic motion.

   6.3 Induction heater and transfer (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) checks  
       6.3.1 Confirm heater control file matches the product family per ECN-2026-003.  
       6.3.2 Inspect conveyor and handling fixtures for wear and secure attachments. Replace or tag items requiring maintenance.  
       6.3.3 Conduct a dry run of part transfer without heat or workpiece to validate timing and sequence.

7. Validation and trial run  
   7.1 Perform a low-risk trial run using a setup coupon or the first production piece as designated.  
   7.2 Measure critical dimensions and surface condition per SB-1025. Log measurement results on the first-piece inspection form.  
   7.3 If measurements are within acceptance, authorize full production. If out of tolerance, stop and perform corrective actions documented and approved per change control ECN-2026-003.

8. Examples and common failure modes (for operator awareness)  
   8.1 Example: Under-torqued mandrel clamp may allow axial slip visible as part ovality on final inspection. Confirm torque and re-check first-piece geometry if slip is suspected.  
   8.2 Example: Wrong lubricant may cause increased spindle temperature or abnormal tool wear. Always confirm CFW-LUB-508 visually and by lot label before use.  
   8.3 Common failure modes: incorrect program version, loose tooling set screws, and contaminated mating surfaces. Address each with the corrective checklist.

9. Records to keep and retention  
   9.1 Changeover checklist with signatures and timestamps.  
   9.2 Torque verification entry for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 showing applied torque.  
   9.3 Lubricant usage record for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 showing CFW-LUB-508 lot and quantity used.  
   9.4 First-piece inspection report as per SB-1025.  
   9.5 Any deviation reports and associated corrective actions referenced to ECN-2026-003.  
   Retention: Maintain records in the document control system per plant policy and attach to the production lot file.

10. Sign-off and handover  
   10.1 Operations lead verifies completion of steps and signs the changeover checklist.  
   10.2 Maintenance verifies mechanical torque and lubrication actions and signs the maintenance verification block.  
   10.3 Quality signs the first-piece acceptance block after review of measurements and surface inspection.  
   10.4 Handover: Only after all three signatures is the line authorized to commence production. Attach related documents ECN-2026-003, SB-1009, and SB-1025 to the changeover record.

11. References  
   ECN-2026-003  
   SB-1009  
   SB-1025

12. Revision notes  
   Rev B: Consolidated torque and lubricant specifications; clarified sign-off flow and records to keep.

text:
# SOP-P1-L1-03 First-article inspection - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03  
Related documents: MM-P1-L1-RR01, SOP-P1-L1-01, SOP-P1-L1-05

Purpose
1. Define the standard operating procedure for first-article inspection on the Hot Forge line to verify conformance of initial production parts before release to process flow.

Scope
2. Applies to first-article parts produced on the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill, CNC turning center, and induction heater at plant P1, line P1-L1. Affected equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03.

Preconditions
3. The production order and drawing package must be available and approved per SOP-P1-L1-01.  
4. Maintenance and calibration records for measurement instruments must be current and available; refer to MM-P1-L1-RR01 for rolling mill maintenance criteria and calibration linkage.  
5. The machine status must be verified against the machine master tag and cleared for trial run by the equipment owner listed in SOP-P1-L1-05.

PPE
6. Required personal protective equipment for first-article inspection activities on the Hot Forge line: safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, hearing protection, and protective footwear. Ensure PPE is inspected prior to entry.

Background and rationale
7. First-article inspection validates that process settings, tooling, and material handling produce parts that meet drawing requirements before full production. EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and EQ-P1-L1-CN02 are critical process steps; issues in these machines propagate defects downstream. The inspection captures setup defects, tooling errors, and handling impacts, reducing scrap and rework.

Key inspection criteria
8. Maximum ring outer diameter is a critical dimensional requirement for rings produced on EQ-P1-L1-RR01. The maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 1240 mm. Confirm ring outer diameter does not exceed this value per drawing tolerance control.  
9. Chuck jaw mounting and retention integrity on EQ-P1-L1-CN02 are critical to operator safety and part accuracy. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m. Verify bolts are torqued to this value during first-article setup and after any jaw change.

Procedure (numbered steps)
10. Preparation
   10.1. Verify production drawing and first-article checklist are present and reference SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 for drawing release and process change control.  
   10.2. Confirm material lot and heat treatment traceability are attached to the first-article record.  
   10.3. Confirm calibration stickers on measuring instruments and gauges are current.

11. Machine setup verification
   11.1. For EQ-P1-L1-RR01, confirm tooling and backup rolls are installed per setup sheets and that rolling path is clear of debris. Refer to MM-P1-L1-RR01 for maintenance-derived setup requirements.  
   11.2. For EQ-P1-L1-CN02, install the chuck jaws and bring bolts to specification. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m; record the torque application event in the setup log.  
   11.3. For EQ-P1-L1-IH03, confirm induction coil alignment and thermal barrier placement per SOP-P1-L1-05.

12. Trial run and sample extraction
   12.1. Execute a controlled single-piece run through EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-IH03, and EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Monitor for abnormal vibration, sound, or handling issues.  
   12.2. Extract the first-article part at the inspection station using designated handling tools and PPE.

13. Dimensional inspection
   13.1. Measure the ring outer diameter first; confirm the part’s outer diameter is at or below the maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) which is 1240 mm. Record the measured value and inspector initials on the first-article form.  
   13.2. Complete all critical dimension checks referenced on the drawing and checklist. Note any deviations and whether they are process-related or measurement artifacts.

14. Functional and visual inspection
   14.1. Conduct visual inspection for surface defects introduced during rolling, heating, or turning. Document the type and location of any feature outside acceptable cosmetic standards.  
   14.2. Verify concentricity and runout where called out on the drawing using calibrated instruments; document instrument ID and calibration status.

15. Nonconformance handling
   15.1. If any critical dimension or safety item is out of tolerance, stop production and notify the process engineer per SOP-P1-L1-01. Tag the part and area to prevent inadvertent use.  
   15.2. Capture root cause and corrective action; update the first-article record and attach to the production order.

Records to keep
16. Maintain the following records in the document control system attached to the production order: first-article inspection form, instrument calibration certificates, torque application log showing the chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m, photographs of the first-article part, and the dimensional measurement sheet confirming the maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 1240 mm threshold status. Link maintenance verification to MM-P1-L1-RR01 where applicable.

Examples and notes
17. Example entry: inspector records measured outer diameter and notes “outer diameter 1238 mm — within limit 1240 mm” then initials and timestamps the form. Use this style for clarity and traceability. (Note: examples should be accompanied by actual measured values from the inspection event.)

Rationale for key checks
18. Verifying the chuck jaw bolt torque to the specified value prevents chuck slippage and enhances concentricity, reducing scrap and safety risk. Confirming the ring outer diameter against the specified maximum prevents downstream interference and handling issues.

PPE and safety reminders
19. Ensure PPE is worn during all handling and inspection steps. Do not remove hot parts from the line without heat-rated gloves and handling tools. Follow lockout-tagout procedures per SOP-P1-L1-05 for any machine intervention.

Sign-off
20. Completion and acceptance of the first-article requires signatures from the following roles recorded on the first-article form: inspector, process engineer, and production supervisor. Each signatory must reference related documents MM-P1-L1-RR01, SOP-P1-L1-01, and SOP-P1-L1-05 as part of their acceptance review.

Revision control
21. Maintain this SOP in the document control system and reference the file by id SOP-P1-L1-03. Any changes to the critical values specified herein must be approved through the revision process cited in SOP-P1-L1-01.
title: First-article inspection - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P1-L1-04 Shift handover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Purpose
1. Provide a consistent, auditable handover procedure for shift-to-shift transfer of responsibility on the Hot Forge line (P1-L1), minimizing safety and production risk and ensuring continuity of maintenance actions.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, lead technicians, and supervisors assigned to EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 during normal production shifts.

Preconditions
3. Shift incoming and outgoing personnel have completed site access and induction training per SOP-P1-L1-01.  
4. Any active maintenance or intervention on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03 must be documented and the status communicated during handover.  
5. Control room and shop floor communications are functional; any failure must be escalated before completing the handover.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
6. Minimum PPE required for handover walkthroughs at the Hot Forge line: hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, safety glasses, high-visibility garment, and steel-toe footwear. Any additional PPE required for a specific task must be noted in SOP-P1-L1-02 and observed.

Handover procedure (numbered steps)
7. Outgoing shift preparation
   7.1. Review the shift log for EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and summarize open items, completed actions, and any deviations.  
   7.2. Verify that lubricant stock levels and part numbers for critical lubrication points are recorded. Explicitly confirm that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is CFW-LUB-188 and that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508. Note any discrepancies for follow-up.  
   7.3. Ensure that any tools, fixtures, and portable equipment placed in service are accounted for and stored per site practice.

8. Joint walkthrough and verbal transfer
   8.1. Conduct a floor walkthrough with outgoing and incoming personnel together, covering EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03. Use the printed shift log as the working document.  
   8.2. For each machine, communicate status items including current job, scrap or quality concerns, known faults, temporary guards or bypasses, and required follow-up actions. Use clear, specific language and confirm understanding by asking the incoming operator to repeat safety-critical items.  
   8.3. Where maintenance remains outstanding, reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 for EQ-P1-L1-IH03-related maintenance history and outstanding tasks. Confirm whether equipment is available for production or is locked/tagged out.

9. Records and documentation
   9.1. Update the shift log with a concise summary of handover contents, including open actions, responsible person for follow-up, and the time of transfer. Retain the completed log in accordance with site record retention practice.  
   9.2. Record any lubricant usage events or replenishments against the equipment record, making explicit entries for CFW-LUB-188 and CFW-LUB-508 when used. Attach purchase requisition or stock issuance records as required.  
   9.3. If any non-routine intervention is performed, create or update a maintenance request and reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 where relevant.

10. Examples and clarifications
   10.1. Example: If EQ-P1-L1-IH03 shows intermittent temperature control instability and a technician has scheduled a sensor verification, the outgoing operator notes the open work in the shift log, references MM-P1-L1-IH03, confirms lock/tag status if applicable, and states the technician assigned. The incoming operator acknowledges and signs the handover.  
   10.2. Example: If EQ-P1-L1-CN02 requires lubrication, the outgoing operator documents the lubricant used (CFW-LUB-508), the quantity taken from stock, and the location serviced. Records are attached to the shift log.

11. Rationale and expected outcomes
   11.1. Structured, verbal-plus-documented handovers reduce missed actions and latent hazards. Explicit naming of lubricant part numbers for equipment removes ambiguity in replenishment and maintenance records.  
   11.2. Joint walkthroughs provide a chance to observe latent issues and reinforce safe behaviors; documented follow-up prevents repeated interruptions to production while ensuring safety defects are addressed.

12. Escalation
   12.1. If the incoming operator does not accept the handover due to unresolved safety concerns, stop production activity related to the hazard and escalate to the on-duty supervisor per SOP-P1-L1-02.

Sign-off
13. The outgoing operator, incoming operator, and on-duty supervisor must sign the shift log. The sign-off must include printed name, signature, and a short acknowledgement that the incoming operator was briefed on open safety items, lubricant status including explicit confirmation of CFW-LUB-188 for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and CFW-LUB-508 for EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and any active maintenance per MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Records to keep
14. - Completed shift log with sign-offs.  
    - Lubricant issuance or usage records that reference CFW-LUB-188 and CFW-LUB-508.  
    - Any maintenance requests or completed work orders tied to MM-P1-L1-IH03.  
    - Exception reports and incident forms per SOP-P1-L1-02.

Related documents
15. - MM-P1-L1-IH03  
    - SOP-P1-L1-01  
    - SOP-P1-L1-02

Revision control
16. Rev A: initial controlled release.
title: Shift handover - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P1-L1-05 Planned shutdown - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03  
Related: ECN-2026-003, MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-02

Purpose
1. Describe controlled sequence for planned shutdown of the Hot Forge line to protect personnel and equipment, preserve process setpoints and provide clear handoff for restart.

Scope
2. Applies to maintenance, operations and supervision responsible for EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 during planned line outages.

Preconditions
3. Confirm planned outage has been authorized per ECN-2026-003.  
4. Verify maintenance work orders are issued and approved where required.  
5. Ensure affected production orders have been stopped and work-in-process is managed per SOP-P1-L1-02.  
6. Confirm maintenance reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 is available for induction heater specific procedures.

PPE
7. The following PPE is required for shutdown and maintenance activities: arc-rated clothing, face shield, dielectric gloves, hearing protection, safety footwear, and safety glasses. Site safety officer may add task-specific PPE per hazard assessment.

Critical values
8. The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes.  
9. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min.

Procedure
10. Notify
10.1 Notify the production supervisor, maintenance planner and shift safety representative that the planned shutdown will commence. Reference ECN-2026-003 authorization code as applicable.  
Rationale: clear notification prevents unscheduled tooling damage and allows safe isolation.

11. Secure material
11.1 Remove or secure billets and fixtures from EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and EQ-P1-L1-CN02.  
11.2 Tag and isolate any tooling that will remain in place.  
Rationale: prevents entrapment or unintentional motion during energy isolation.

12. Control of hazardous energy
12.1 Isolate electrical feeds to EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 using lockout-tagout processes in accordance with site policy.  
12.2 Verify zero energy at point of work with appropriate test instruments before proceeding.  
Rationale: ensures personnel safety during maintenance.

13. Induction heater checklist
13.1 Verify coil cooling water flow is at or above the minimum before de-energizing heated zones. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min.  
13.2 If flow cannot be confirmed, delay de-energization until flow is restored or follow MM-P1-L1-IH03 contingency steps.  
Rationale: protect coil assembly and water-cooled components from thermal shock and damage.

14. CNC turning center actions
14.1 Initiate controlled spindle cooldown sequence on EQ-P1-L1-CN02 per manufacturer guidance. Observe the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes for thermal cycle planning; allow warm-up or cooldown as recommended when sequencing shutdown and restart to avoid bearing stress.  
14.2 Retract tooling and place the machine in a safe state for mechanical inspection and lubrication tasks.  
Rationale: maintaining spindle thermal integrity reduces bearing wear and runout risk.

15. Roll reducer and conveyor
15.1 Lock out drive systems on EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Inspect coupling guards and conveyor tracking before any mechanical work.  
Rationale: avoid mechanical collapse or pinch hazards.

16. Housekeeping and verification
16.1 Drain or secure fluids per maintenance instructions and collect waste in approved containers.  
16.2 Conduct visual inspection of electrical cabinets for moisture ingress, loose terminals, and evidence of overheating.  
Rationale: identify pre-failure indicators and ensure safe work environment.

Examples / scenario notes
17. Example: If scheduled bearing replacement on EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is planned, coordinate spindle cooldown to coincide with bearing prep and allow for the 21 minutes warm-up reference to plan pre-lubrication cycles. Use MM-P1-L1-IH03 only for induction-heater-related tasks.  
18. Example: If coil flow is below 72 L/min during shutdown prep, do not perform electrical isolation of heating elements; instead secure the heater in standby and escalate to maintenance planning.

Records to keep
19. Maintain the following records with the work order:
19.1 LOTO tags and verification test logs.  
19.2 Confirmation of coolant flow rate checks and instrument readouts when available. Record the statement: "The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min." where applicable.  
19.3 Spindle thermally relevant notes referencing the warm-up guidance: "The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes."  
19.4 Photos of isolation points and component conditions.  
19.5 Completed maintenance checklists and sign-off forms.

Post-maintenance verification
20. Before re-energizing:
20.1 Confirm all guards and interlocks are reinstalled and tested.  
20.2 Validate coolant flow meets the stated minimum and is stable.  
20.3 Run equipment through a controlled restart sequence and verify normal operation.  
Rationale: reduces risk of latent faults and ensures return to production readiness.

Sign-off
21. Completion sign-off must include signatures and printed names for the following roles:
21.1 Maintenance lead who performed work.  
21.2 Operations supervisor accepting machine back to service.  
21.3 Safety representative verifying LOTO and hazard controls.  
Records retained with the work order and referenced in the maintenance management system per site retention policy.

References
22. Consult ECN-2026-003 for outage authorization details, MM-P1-L1-IH03 for induction heater maintenance specifics and SOP-P1-L1-02 for production stop and material handling procedures.

Revision history
23. Rev C: Current revision.

text:
# SOP-P1-L2-01 Line startup - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-009, SB-1008, SB-1020

1. Purpose and scope
1.1 Purpose: Define required steps to perform safe, consistent startup of the Ring Rolling line on P1-L2, including mechanical, electrical, lubrication and heat-treat readiness checks prior to production.
1.2 Scope: Applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance staff responsible for EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03.

2. Background and rationale
2.1 Background: The Ring Rolling line has tight interdependencies between the induction heater, ring rolling mill, and the heat-treat furnace. Improper sequence or overlooked readiness items can cause part quality escapes, equipment damage, or personnel hazards.
2.2 Rationale: This procedure sequences checks to verify mechanical clearances, lubrication, control interlocks, and quench timing before introducing parts. The defined steps reduce risk of rework and unscheduled downtime. See ECN-2026-009 for recent control updates and SB-1008 and SB-1020 for safety bulletins that affect startup practices.

3. Preconditions (required conditions before initiating startup)
3.1 Subject matter experts: Operator and one maintenance technician assigned and present.
3.2 Permits: Any applicable lockout/tagout cleared, and permit documentation reviewed per SB-1008.
3.3 Housekeeping: Work area around EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 is free of loose materials and obstructions.
3.4 Controls: PLC and HMI panels are powered, connected to plant network, and show normal boot without active alarms.
3.5 Consumables: Verify lubricant availability; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is CFW-LUB-788. Verify quench media and quench tank readiness for EQ-P1-L2-HT03. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds.

4. Required personal protective equipment (PPE)
4.1 Minimum PPE for personnel during startup: safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, and flame-resistant clothing where directed by SB-1020. Additional PPE as directed by the site safety officer for specific tasks such as handling hot billets.

5. Procedure — numbered steps
5.1 Pre-start verification
5.1.1 Confirm preconditions in section 3 are met.
5.1.2 Notify line control and adjacent work centers that startup is commencing; obtain verbal acknowledgement.

5.2 Mechanical and safety checks
5.2.1 Visual inspect machine guards on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 for secure fasteners and intact interlock switches.
5.2.2 Verify all access doors on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 close and lock; confirm interlock status on HMI.
5.2.3 Inspect quench tank area for water level, flow indicators, and return lines for obstructions. Confirm emergency stop circuits are functional.

5.3 Lubrication and consumables
5.3.1 Replenish lubrication points for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 per lubrication map. For EQ-P1-L2-IH02 confirm lubricant match; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is CFW-LUB-788.
5.3.2 Record batch or lot number of lubricant used in the startup log.

5.4 Electrical and controls
5.4.1 Release local lockouts and perform controlled energization of drive systems. Confirm fault logs clear and baseline alarm set recorded.
5.4.2 Perform control homing routines from HMI and validate interlock logic by simulating a safe interruption.

5.5 Heat-treat furnace staging
5.5.1 With the furnace at idle, verify sensors and thermocouples are reporting and are within operational status on the HMI.
5.5.2 Confirm quench pump primed and flow meters indicate flow. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. Verify controller timing parameter matches this value.

5.6 Dry run and coupling checks
5.6.1 Run the line in dry-run mode without billets to verify synchronization between EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Observe for abnormal vibration, noise, or motion.
5.6.2 If any abnormal condition is detected, stop the line and document observations, reference SB-1008 for safety reporting, and engage maintenance.

5.7 First billet introduction
5.7.1 Introduce a single sacrificial billet with monitoring by the operator and technician. Observe induction heating behavior, roll engagement, and quench timing.
5.7.2 Collect dimensional samples and surface quality checks for immediate evaluation. If the part fails acceptance, halt production and follow ECN-2026-009 for corrective engineering action.

6. Examples and acceptance criteria
6.1 Example observation: If induction heater shows uneven heating zones, document heater zone current imbalance in the startup log and tag for corrective maintenance. Reference SB-1020 for handling instructions of hot parts.
6.2 Acceptance is defined by equipment running without alarms, synchronization achieved in dry-run, lubricant batch recorded, and quench timing verified against the required setting.

7. Records to keep
7.1 Startup log: operator name, technician name, line identifier P1-L2, equipment IDs EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03, lubricant part number used, and any noted observations.
7.2 Alarm and fault snapshot: save PLC/HMI logs for the startup interval and attach to the startup log.
7.3 Sample inspection report: include dimensional and visual inspection records for the first production pieces and any sacrificial billet results.
7.4 Maintenance tags and corrective actions: file per ECN-2026-009 if adjustments or repairs are required.

8. Sign-off
8.1 Operator sign-off: operator verifies all steps completed and initial here.
8.2 Lead technician sign-off: lead technician verifies mechanical and lubrication readiness and initial here.
8.3 Production supervisor sign-off: production supervisor approves line for production and initial here.

9. References
9.1 ECN-2026-009
9.2 SB-1008
9.3 SB-1020

Notes: Follow all site safety policies and document deviations from this SOP in the startup log.

# SOP-P1-L2-02 Product changeover - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-041, MM-P1-L2-RR01, SOP-P1-L2-03

Purpose
1. This procedure defines required steps, safety precautions, and recordkeeping for product changeover on the Ring Rolling line at P1-L2. It covers removal and installation activities for tooling, setup verification, material handling handoffs, and process checks necessary to place the line into production for the new part.

Background and scope
2. The Ring Rolling line comprises the radial ring rolling mill, induction billet heater, and hydraulic transport modules identified as EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03. The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm. This SOP applies to mechanical, process, and electrical technicians performing changeover tasks and to area leads responsible for sign-off.

Preconditions
3. Verify that production authorization for the new part is present and approved per ECN-2026-041. Confirm that maintenance holds are cleared and that MM-P1-L2-RR01 has no active open maintenance work orders affecting changeover scope. Confirm that SOP-P1-L2-03 has been reviewed for line-specific startup sequence for post-changeover validation.

PPE
4. Minimum PPE must be worn during all activities:
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Cut-resistant gloves for tooling handling.
   - Heat-resistant gloves when handling recently heated billets associated with EQ-P1-L2-IH02.
   - Steel-toe safety boots.
   - Hearing protection in designated high-noise zones.
   - High-visibility vest.

Roles and responsibilities
5. Line Lead: Authorize changeover start, assign crew, and verify paperwork.  
6. Mechanical Technician: Execute tooling removal/installation on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and EQ-P1-L2-HT03.  
7. Electrical Technician: Isolate and re-energize electrical panels as required for tooling changes.  
8. Process Technician: Configure induction heater program and confirm lubricant provisioning for EQ-P1-L2-IH02. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is CFW-LUB-788.  
9. Quality Inspector: Measure first article and approve dimensional conformance.

Procedural steps (numbered)
10. Prepare and isolate
   10.1. Convene crew, review scope and permit requirements from ECN-2026-041.  
   10.2. Lockout/tagout affected equipment according to plant LOTO policy. Verify zero energy state before proceeding.

11. Remove current tooling and fixtures
   11.1. Document current tooling identifiers and condition in the changeover log.  
   11.2. Remove rollers, mandrels, and fixture plates from EQ-P1-L2-RR01 following manufacturer guidance recorded in MM-P1-L2-RR01. Store components on designated racks and tag with part IDs.

12. Inspect and prepare equipment
   12.1. Perform visual inspection of the machine bed and lubrication points. Record any abnormal wear or damage in the maintenance log.  
   12.2. Install replacement or adjusted tooling for the new product as per tooling build sheet. Verify fit and fastener engagement by visual and tactile confirmation.

13. Set up induction heater and transfer modules
   13.1. Confirm billet size and material specification match the incoming workorder and ECN-2026-041.  
   13.2. Provision lubricant CFW-LUB-788 to the service reservoir for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and record lot number and quantity dispensed into the equipment maintenance log.  
   13.3. Verify hydraulic couplings and transport guides on EQ-P1-L2-HT03 are positioned for the new part geometry.

14. Functional checks (pre-power)
   14.1. Remove mechanical holds and perform manual rotation or movement checks where applicable to confirm free travel.  
   14.2. Reconfirm no tools or loose items remain in the work envelope.

15. Electrical re-energize and system checks
   15.1. Electrical technician re-energizes control panels and brings systems to ready state following plant procedures.  
   15.2. Execute dry runs and interlock verification. Document controller reported faults and clearing actions.

16. First-article production and inspection
   16.1. Produce an initial ring and route it to Quality. The Quality Inspector must document dimensional results and accept or reject per drawing and ECN-2026-041 disposition.  
   16.2. If rework or adjustment is required, document corrective actions and re-run first article.

17. Recordkeeping and handover
   17.1. Complete the changeover checklist, including tooling IDs, lubricant CFW-LUB-788 lot number, and any deviations from standard settings. File the checklist in the electronic document control system under SOP-P1-L2-02.  
   17.2. Update the line setup entry in the production log and notify planning that the line is ready for production.

Step rationale and examples
18. Tooling documentation prevents incorrect reuse of worn mandrels and ensures traceability. Example: tagging removed rollers with their unique IDs reduces risk of installing a roller with excessive eccentricity.  
19. Recording lubricant lot numbers for CFW-LUB-788 enables root cause tracing in case of surface finish anomalies or lubrication-related wear issues.  
20. Performing a first-article inspection before full-rate production reduces scrap and meets process-control expectations in ECN-2026-041.

Records to keep
21. Changeover checklist completed under SOP-P1-L2-02.  
22. Tooling disposition log and tag photographs.  
23. Lubricant provisioning record including part CFW-LUB-788 lot information.  
24. First-article inspection report and disposition referencing ECN-2026-041.  
25. Any maintenance findings entered into MM-P1-L2-RR01.

Nonconformance and escalation
26. If first-article rejects persist after two documented adjustment cycles, stop the line and escalate to Engineering per ECN-2026-041. Do not resume production until disposition is approved.

Sign-off
27. Signatures required before production handover:
   - Mechanical Technician: ______________________  
   - Electrical Technician: ______________________  
   - Process Technician: ______________________  
   - Quality Inspector: ______________________  
   - Line Lead: ______________________

Revision history
28. See document control for revision history and related change details referenced by ECN-2026-041.

End of SOP-P1-L2-02.

text:
# SOP-P1-L2-03 First-article inspection - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for ring-rolling production on line P1-L2. It documents required preconditions, inspection steps, acceptance rationale, records to retain, and sign-off criteria for release of the first-part lot into routine production.

Scope
2. Applies to first-part submission for any new ring geometry, new material lot, or after process change on equipment EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Maintenance requirements referenced are in MM-P1-L2-IH02, MM-P1-L2-RR01, and MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.

Preconditions
3. Equipment condition
   3.1 Verify EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 are available and have passed the most recent maintenance release per MM-P1-L2-RR01 and MM-P1-L2-IH02.  
   3.2 Confirm the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is CFW-LUB-961 and that the installed reservoir and distribution lines contain that lubricant. Cross-check stock label with machine nameplate and maintenance records.

4. Material and thermal
   4.1 Confirm material certificate accompanies the billet and that chemical and mechanical attributes meet purchase order requirements.  
   4.2 Confirm the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C and that the billet reaches and is held at that target prior to roll engagement. Record the achieved temperature in the process log.

5. Setup verification
   5.1 Verify tooling and mandrel geometry match the part print and setup sheet.  
   5.2 Verify dimensional gauges and measurement instruments are calibrated and within calibration period. Refer to MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 for tooling changeover and quick-verify checks.

PPE
6. Required personal protective equipment for personnel involved in the FAI:
   6.1 Heat-resistant gloves and sleeves.  
   6.2 Face shield with heat-filtering visor.  
   6.3 Hearing protection.  
   6.4 Safety footwear with metatarsal protection.  
   6.5 Flame-retardant apron for handling hot billets.  
   Note: Additional PPE directed by the plant safety officer must be worn as required.

Procedure — Inspection steps
7. Preparation
   7.1 Ensure all preconditions in section 3 through 5 are satisfied and documented.  
   7.2 Perform a preheat cycle on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and confirm that the temperature control readout stabilizes at the target value stated in section 4.2 before introducing the production billet.

8. First part processing
   8.1 Load the first billet following standard handling and hoist procedures. Monitor, log, and confirm the billet temperature reaches the target specified in section 4.2 prior to transfer to EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
   8.2 Observe and verify lubricant flow and distribution on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 at the start of ring engagement; confirm CFW-LUB-961 supply pressure and filter condition per visual and gauge checks. If the lubricant identity or appearance differs from expected, stop and tag the machine out until resolved.

9. Dimensional verification
   9.1 After ring rolling, allow the ring to reach a safe handling temperature per plant safety directions, then perform the full dimensional inspection per the part drawing: concentricity, wall thickness profile, outside diameter, inside diameter and finish. Record all readings in the FAI data sheet.  
   9.2 Compare measured values to the drawing tolerances and document any deviations and the corrective action taken. For borderline outcomes, use the measurement method traceable to the instrument calibration log.

10. Metallurgical and surface checks
   10.1 Perform visual surface inspection for laps, seams, and surface oxide. Document surface condition with photographs and notes.  
   10.2 Remove representative samples for hardness and microstructure checks as specified by the engineering test plan. Attach test reports to the FAI package.

11. Process parameter review
   11.1 Review process logs from EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-RR01 for the first-part cycle. Ensure the recorded billet temperature matches the target in section 4.2 and that no excursion or equipment fault alarms were present.  
   11.2 Record machine settings, tooling identifiers, lubricant batch, and any online adjustments.

12. Final disposition
   12.1 If all dimensional, metallurgical, and surface criteria are met, sign off on the FAI and approve the lot for release into production.  
   12.2 If any nonconformances are identified, quarantine the lot, initiate corrective action, and repeat FAI after resolution.

Rationale and examples
13. Rationale
   13.1 Holding the billet at a documented target temperature in EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is critical to material flow characteristics during rolling; deviation can cause geometry and microstructure variance. The target is documented in section 4.2 to ensure reproducibility.  
   13.2 Using the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-961 on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 ensures consistent frictional conditions and tool life; lubricant substitution alters boundary conditions and invalidates FAI results.

14. Examples
   14.1 Example acceptable outcome: dimensional readings within drawing limits, microstructure showing expected grain flow, and process logs showing stable temperature at the target in section 4.2 with continuous lubricant flow of CFW-LUB-961.  
   14.2 Example rejection cause: measured OD out of tolerance correlating with documented billet temperature below the target in section 4.2 during rolling.

Records to keep
15. Mandatory records for the FAI package:
   15.1 Completed FAI data sheet with all dimensional readings.  
   15.2 Process logs from EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and EQ-P1-L2-RR01 showing temperature and machine state.  
   15.3 Material certificate and heat number traceability.  
   15.4 Lubricant batch label showing CFW-LUB-961 and maintenance acceptance from MM-P1-L2-RR01.  
   15.5 Calibration certificates for measurement instruments.  
   15.6 Photographic record of part surfaces and setup.  
   15.7 Any nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation.

Related documents
16. Reference documents: MM-P1-L2-IH02, MM-P1-L2-RR01, MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.

Sign-off
17. Acceptance sign-off. The FAI package must be reviewed and signed by: production lead, quality engineer, and process engineer. Record names, titles, and signatures in the FAI approval block. Failure to complete sign-off invalidates release into production.
title: First-article inspection - Ring Rolling line

text:
# SOP-P1-L2-04 Shift handover - Ring Rolling line
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: MM-P1-L2-IH02, QS-PROC-02, SB-1035

Purpose
1. Provide a controlled, auditable process for shift-to-shift transfer of responsibility for the Ring Rolling line (P1-L2). This SOP ensures continuity of safe operation, product quality, and equipment protection for EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03.

Background and rationale
2. Ring rolling is a continuous, interdependent process. Handovers are critical points where process setpoints, equipment states, and active nonconformances must be communicated to prevent product scrap, equipment damage, or safety incidents. Retaining a concise log of parameters and actions preserves traceability for quality audits (see QS-PROC-02) and maintenance follow-up (see MM-P1-L2-IH02).

Preconditions (required before initiating handover)
3. Incoming operator has received formal authorization to operate P1-L2.  
4. Both outgoing and incoming operators are free from impairment and have completed required safety briefs for the shift.  
5. All active alarms cleared or documented and actions in progress recorded in the shift log.  
6. Consumables and tooling levels verified against local minimums per line checklist.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
7. Minimum PPE to be worn during handover and any walkdowns: safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, and steel-toed footwear. Use additional PPE as required by task or area hazard signage.

Procedure — numbered handover steps
8. Step 1 — Initial briefing
   - Outgoing operator summarizes overall line status: current product batch ID, material condition, and any deviations. State of EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 must be given.
   - Note any operator actions required immediately at shift start and any work-in-progress that must be completed early in the incoming shift.

9. Step 2 — Critical parameters confirmation
   - Confirm and read back the furnace setpoint for EQ-P1-L2-HT03. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C.
   - Confirm coil cooling water flow at EQ-P1-L2-IH02. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min.
   - Record actual readings at handover in the shift log. If readings deviate from the values above, document actions taken and reference MM-P1-L2-IH02 for instrumentation checks.

10. Step 3 — Equipment condition and safety items
   - Walk down EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, and EQ-P1-L2-HT03 with incoming operator. Point out any mechanical issues, loose guards, or temporary controls. Log items requiring maintenance in the shift log and notify maintenance per MM-P1-L2-IH02.
   - Verify isolation points and tag statuses for any maintenance work. Confirm permits are present for in-progress maintenance.

11. Step 4 — Process quality and nonconformance
   - Review in-line inspection results, scrap or rework since last handover, and any trending concerns. Record product disposition decisions in accordance with QS-PROC-02.
   - If a quality hold exists, confirm the hold protocol and point of contact. Do not release product without QA sign-off per QS-PROC-02.

12. Step 5 — Consumables, materials, and tooling
   - Verify lot numbers and traceability for feedstock and tooling used in production. Log any low-stock items requiring procurement or supervisor notification.

13. Step 6 — HAZOP, safety, and environmental
   - Highlight any recent near-misses or safety observations. Confirm emergency procedures and alarm response responsibilities.
   - Note any environmental releases or deviations and report per SB-1035.

14. Step 7 — Transfer of controls and acknowledgement
   - Outgoing operator transfers documented control of the line to incoming operator only after all items in this SOP are acknowledged and recorded in the shift log.
   - Incoming operator reads back critical parameters and outstanding actions to confirm mutual understanding.

Examples and clarifications
15. Example: If during handover the measured furnace temperature is 10 °C below the austenitizing setpoint, record the discrepancy, implement immediate corrective action if required, and notify maintenance per MM-P1-L2-IH02. Do not resume production until the incoming operator understands the risk and corrective plan.
16. Example: If induction heater coil cooling flow reads below the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min at handover, stop billet feed and initiate cooling system troubleshooting per MM-P1-L2-IH02.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the shift log with:
   - Time-stamped entries for each handover item (parameter confirmations, deviations, corrective actions).
   - Signatures of outgoing and incoming operators and supervising technician.
   - Reference to maintenance tickets or quality nonconformance reports raised during the shift.
   These records support compliance with QS-PROC-02 and facilitate troubleshooting and audits.

Escalation and supervisor notification
18. If unresolved critical deviations exist at the end of the handover, the incoming operator must notify the line supervisor before assuming full control. Document the notification in the shift log and create a maintenance or QA action per MM-P1-L2-IH02 and QS-PROC-02.

Sign-off
19. Outgoing operator prints name and signs to confirm complete and accurate transfer of line responsibility. Incoming operator prints name and signs to accept responsibility. Supervisor reviews and initials the handover record.
   - Retain signed handover records in the line binder and submit electronic copies per QS-PROC-02.

Revision control and references
20. This SOP is Rev E. For maintenance procedures for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 see MM-P1-L2-IH02. For quality hold and disposition follow QS-PROC-02. For safety bulletin and environmental reporting follow SB-1035.

text:
# SOP-P1-L2-05 Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-041, QS-PROC-03, SOP-P1-L2-04

1. Purpose and scope  
1.1 Purpose: Provide a standardized procedure for executing a planned shutdown of the Ring Rolling line to perform preventative maintenance, inspection, and controlled preservation of assets: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. This procedure aligns with ECN-2026-041 for engineering change acceptance and QS-PROC-03 for quality records. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-04 for normal production stop procedures and handover practices.  
1.2 Scope: Applies to maintenance, operations, and safety personnel responsible for the Ring Rolling line at Plant P1, line P1-L2.

2. Background and rationale  
2.1 Background: Planned shutdowns reduce risk of unexpected failures, allow inspection of critical wear items, and ensure lubrication and heating systems are preserved. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C; this target is used to confirm heater control systems and thermocouple function prior to shutdown preservation actions. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is CFW-LUB-961; use for replenishment and compatibility checks during shutdown servicing.  
2.2 Rationale: Verifying the heater target temperature and correct lubricant ensures that process-critical systems remain within design intent when returned to service, minimizing start-up rejects and equipment stress.

3. Preconditions (required before initiating shutdown)  
3.1 Approved work order and authorization per ECN-2026-041.  
3.2 All affected departments notified in accordance with QS-PROC-03.  
3.3 Operators available to perform safe machine isolation and to provide process history.  
3.4 Lockout/tagout devices and procedure verified; verify handover to maintenance only after isolation.  
3.5 Materials staged for protective storage or removal from process line.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE)  
4.1 Required PPE: standard plant safety PPE as defined in site safety rules; hot work PPE for heater access; chemical resistant gloves for lubricant handling when required by material safety data sheets. Consult site safety for any additional PPE needs.

5. Shutdown steps (numbered execution flow)  
5.1 Step 1 — Initiate shutdown authorization  
5.1.1 Confirm work order and scope with maintenance supervisor.  
5.1.2 Notify operations, quality, and production planning per QS-PROC-03.  
5.2 Step 2 — Prepare the line for shutdown  
5.2.1 Stop material feed and secure billets per SOP-P1-L2-04.  
5.2.2 Remove or secure loose workpieces to prevent foreign object damage.  
5.3 Step 3 — Isolate power and energy sources  
5.3.1 Follow lockout/tagout procedure and verify isolation points on EQ-P1-L2-RR01, EQ-P1-L2-IH02, EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Only authorized personnel may apply tags and locks.  
5.4 Step 4 — Verify heater control and temperature reading  
5.4.1 With isolation in place, bring monitoring systems to the attention of maintenance for verification. Use the control panel to confirm that the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C in the system records and control setpoints. This confirms that thermocouple mapping and control logic are correct prior to any mechanical intervention.  
5.5 Step 5 — Drain and preserve process fluids as required  
5.5.1 For lubrication and hydraulic systems, drain per manufacturer guidance. When replenishing or topping, use lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) CFW-LUB-961 to maintain compatibility in reservoirs that will remain in service after shutdown. Record quantities added in maintenance log.  
5.6 Step 6 — Inspect and tag critical components  
5.6.1 Inspect bearings, rollers, heater elements, and mechanical couplings for wear signatures. Tag any items requiring follow-up with work orders referencing ECN-2026-041 when parts or changes are required.  
5.7 Step 7 — Housekeeping and preservation  
5.7.1 Clean surfaces and apply preservation coating where specified. Seal electrical enclosures and cover exposed sensors if recommended by equipment vendor.  
5.8 Step 8 — Update controls and set safe states  
5.8.1 Place control systems into maintenance mode and log the pre-shutdown setpoints and alarm states. Ensure that operator panels show the preserved state and that alarms are acknowledged in the record.  
5.9 Step 9 — Final verification and handover to maintenance stores or preservation team  
5.9.1 Walkdown by responsible supervisor to confirm tasks complete and records updated. Sign the shutdown checklist.

6. Examples and common findings  
6.1 Example: If the control display does not show 1230 °C for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 when expected, document the discrepancy and escalate to engineering per ECN-2026-041. Do not proceed with heater element work until thermocouple verification is resolved.  
6.2 Example: If lubricant on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 is unknown, tag reservoir as quarantined and replace with CFW-LUB-961 after draining and sampling documented in the record.

7. Records to keep (per QS-PROC-03)  
7.1 Completed shutdown checklist with signatures.  
7.2 Lockout/tagout log and energy isolation verification records.  
7.3 Heater setpoint verification printout or screenshot showing target billet temperature 1230 °C for EQ-P1-L2-IH02.  
7.4 Lubricant usage and replenishment record showing lubricant part number CFW-LUB-961 for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
7.5 Inspection findings and follow-up work orders referencing ECN-2026-041 where applicable. All records retained in accordance with QS-PROC-03.

8. Sign-off (required)  
8.1 Operations lead: signature and date.  
8.2 Maintenance supervisor: signature and date.  
8.3 Quality representative: signature and date confirming records conform to QS-PROC-03.  
8.4 Engineering representative: signature and date if deviations require ECN-2026-041 action.

9. References and cross-checks  
9.1 ECN-2026-041 — engineering change directives and approval requirements.  
9.2 QS-PROC-03 — record retention and notification protocols.  
9.3 SOP-P1-L2-04 — production stop and handover procedures.

Notes: Any deviation observed during execution must be recorded and reported immediately. Use examples in section 6 as a guide for escalation.
title: Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

text:
# SOP-P1-L3-01 Line startup - Machining line
Revision: Rev D
Plant: P1, line P1-L3
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03
Related documents: ECN-2026-029, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-02

Purpose
1. Define the required sequence and verification steps for safe startup of the Machining line at P1-L3. This procedure applies to operators and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Preconditions (required before step 1)
2. Authorizing supervisor present and briefed on any outstanding work orders that affect the line. See ECN-2026-029 for configuration changes and SB-1026 for safety bulletins affecting startup behavior.
3. All required lockout/tagout completed for maintenance activities and cleared from the line.
4. Electrical distribution and air/gas supplies to line declared available by Facilities. Confirmed isolation points match drawings in SOP-P1-L3-02.
5. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497. Verify correct stock and fill records before applying lubricant.

PPE
6. Required PPE for all personnel: safety eyewear, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, flame-resistant clothing, and steel-toe footwear. Supervisors must verify PPE compliance prior to entry on the shop floor.

Startup sequence and verification steps
7. Equipment visual check
   7.1. Walk the line to confirm no foreign objects, debris, or tools remain on or adjacent to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, or EQ-P1-L3-CN03.
   7.2. Verify guarding is installed and interlocks show closed condition at control panels.
   Rationale: A thorough visual inspection reduces risk of immediate mechanical interference and protects interlock health.

8. Induction heater initial condition (EQ-P1-L3-IH01)
   8.1. Confirm coolant level and flow indicator are within operational range per manufacturer guidance.
   8.2. Verify electrical connections and control cabinet doors are secured.
   8.3. Confirm the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C and that the PLC setpoint matches that value prior to energizing the heater.
   Rationale: Correct setpoint prevents thermal nonconformance and downstream machining issues. Example: if PLC setpoint does not read 1235 °C, do not proceed; isolate and contact maintenance.

9. Hydraulic forging press pre-energize (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)
   9.1. Confirm hydraulic fluid level and filter condition; verify lubricant inventory includes CFW-LUB-497 and that the fill is logged.
   9.2. Confirm accumulator and reservoir covers installed and that there are no visible leaks.
   9.3. Energize hydraulic power using local control and verify control feedback indicates ready state before actuating any cylinder movement.
   Rationale: Using the specified lubricant prevents pump and valve damage and ensures hydraulic response meets design assumptions.

10. CNC machining cell checks (EQ-P1-L3-CN03)
   10.1. Verify tool magazine installed and that basic interlock tests pass at the operator HMI.
   10.2. Confirm part program selection matches job traveler information from production release in SOP-P1-L3-02.
   Rationale: Program mismatch is a common source of scrap and tool damage; verification avoids costly failures.

11. Dry run sequence
   11.1. Execute a dry run at reduced functional steps without material in the flow path to confirm motion sequences and interlock behavior.
   11.2. Observe emergency stops and verify stop response from all stations on the line.
   Rationale: Dry runs validate control logic and reveal mechanical interference before live billets are introduced.

12. First-billet introduction
   12.1. Introduce the first billet only after all preceding checks are complete and documented.
   12.2. Monitor temperature readback from EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to confirm target 1235 °C is achieved and stabilized prior to forging.
   Rationale: Ensuring billet temperature is stable at the specified target prevents substandard forging outcomes.

13. Production ramp and monitoring
   13.1. Ramp production to standard cadence as defined by the line leader and SOP-P1-L3-02 once the first parts meet dimensional and metallurgical checks.
   13.2. Monitor hydraulic pressures, cycle behavior, and control alarms for aberrant patterns.
   Records: Capture initial production run data and attach to the job traveler.

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following records in the document control folder for the shift:
   - Pre-start checklist signed by operator and supervisor.
   - Lubricant verification log indicating use of CFW-LUB-497 for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
   - Temperature log from EQ-P1-L3-IH01 showing achieved setpoint 1235 °C for initial billets.
   - Dry run completion sign-off and any deviation reports.
   - First-piece inspection report and disposition.
   Example: Attach screenshots or printouts of PLC setpoint displays and the EQ-P1-L3-IH01 temperature trend for the first billet.

Deviations and nonconformance
15. If any step fails verification, stop the startup process, tag the failure per SB-1026, and notify maintenance and supervision. Record the failure in the shift log and reference ECN-2026-029 when configuration changes are suspected.

Operator and supervisor responsibilities
16. The primary operator performs steps 7 through 13 and records observations. The supervising technician verifies steps 2 and 3 preconditions and signs off on the pre-start checklist.

Sign-off
17. Completion sign-off required on the pre-start checklist by both the operator and the supervising technician. Retain signed checklist in the job folder and archive electronically per SOP-P1-L3-02.

Related documents
18. See ECN-2026-029 for engineering changes affecting start parameters, SB-1026 for safety bulletin actions, and SOP-P1-L3-02 for ongoing machining line operations and program control.
title: Line startup - Machining line

text:
# SOP-P1-L3-02 Product changeover - Machining line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related: ECN-2026-043, MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1, SB-1026

1. Purpose and scope  
This procedure defines the required steps for product changeover on the machining line P1-L3. It covers setup, verification, and handover for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03. It ensures consistent thermal, clamping, and machining conditions and documents records to maintain traceability during changeover.

2. Background and rationale  
Changeovers on the machining line directly affect part geometry, metallurgical condition, and tool life. Proper control of billet temperature, chuck clamping, and headstock setup reduces rework and rejects. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. These values are mandatory setpoints established by engineering (see ECN-2026-043) and maintenance standards (see MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1). SB-1026 provides safety boundaries for thermal handling; follow it for material handling steps.

3. Preconditions (must be met before starting)  
3.1 Operator and maintenance personnel briefed on changeover scope and associated engineering change ECN-2026-043.  
3.2 Required spares and fixtures staged at the line and verified against MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.  
3.3 All affected equipment cleared of previous production material and safe to access per SB-1026.  
3.4 All control interlocks in service; emergency stop function verified. (Refer to SB-1026 for verification method.)

4. PPE (minimum required)  
4.1 Heat-resistant gloves and face shield for billet transfer and induction heater access per SB-1026.  
4.2 Mechanical gloves and eye protection for tooling changes and chuck access.  
4.3 Hearing protection when inside the active machining area.  
4.4 Arc-rated clothing if performing live-weld or brazing tasks on fixtures (refer to SB-1026).

5. Materials and references to use during changeover  
5.1 Production order and setup sheet from ECN-2026-043.  
5.2 Machine setup checklist MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 for EQ-P1-L3-CN03.  
5.3 Safety bulletin SB-1026 for thermal and mechanical hazard controls.  
5.4 Calibration records for torque tool used for chuck jaw bolts.

6. Procedure — numbered operational steps

6.1 Prepare and isolate  
6.1.1 Verify preconditions in section 3. Ensure line power and controls are in the required state per SB-1026.  
6.1.2 Lockout-tagout only if tools or fixtures require maintenance; otherwise follow live setup steps allowed by ECN-2026-043.

6.2 Induction heater setup (EQ-P1-L3-IH01)  
6.2.1 Confirm heater control software recipe matches ECN-2026-043.  
6.2.2 Load billet stock and position within heater chamber per operator guidance.  
6.2.3 Set and confirm target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Record actual readback on the changeover log. Rationale: consistent billet temperature ensures predictable machining behavior and metallurgical properties. Example record entry: "IH01 target: 1235 °C, readback: [value shown on heater]."

6.3 Handling and transfer to headstock (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)  
6.3.1 Use specified lifting fixtures and follow SB-1026 for thermal handling.  
6.3.2 Confirm alignment and seating of billet in the headstock; document any corrective actions taken. Rationale: misalignment causes eccentric machining and premature tool wear.

6.4 Lathe/chuck preparation (EQ-P1-L3-CN03)  
6.4.1 Inspect chuck and jaws for wear and cleanliness. Refer to MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 for jaw selection.  
6.4.2 Install appropriate jaws and clamp sample billet. Torque chuck jaw bolts to the specified value: The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and record the serial number of the wrench and the torque applied. Rationale: correct bolt torque secures jaws, prevents slippage, and avoids distortion of the fixture. Example record: "CN03 jaw bolts torqued to 95 N·m, torque tool SN: [calibration tag]."

6.5 Tooling and program load  
6.5.1 Verify tooling pockets and offsets match the production program from ECN-2026-043.  
6.5.2 Load program and perform dry cycle without material if required by MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1. Observe axes motion and run a stationary verification per the checklist.

6.6 First-piece verification and measurement  
6.6.1 Machine first-piece and measure critical dimensions per ECN-2026-043. Record measurements on the changeover record. Rationale: first-piece checks confirm setup validity and avoid batch-wide errors. Example record fields: "dimension, nominal, measured, disposition."

6.7 Adjustment and stabilization  
6.7.1 If measurements are out of tolerance, adjust offsets or fixturing and repeat first-piece verification. Document all adjustments and reason codes. Rationale: traceability required for process audits.

6.8 Documentation and records to keep  
6.8.1 Changeover log: include operator names, start and completion checkpoints, and signatures.  
6.8.2 Thermal log for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 showing target and readback of 1235 °C.  
6.8.3 Torque record for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 showing 95 N·m and torque tool identification.  
6.8.4 First-piece inspection sheet and disposition notes referenced to ECN-2026-043.  
6.8.5 Attach any deviation or NCRs and reference SB-1026 when safety deviations occur.

7. Completion and handover  
7.1 Confirm all records are completed and attached to the production order.  
7.2 Notify production control that the line is ready for production and that verification steps and records conform to ECN-2026-043 and MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.  
7.3 If safety bulletins in SB-1026 required containment or signage, verify removal or continued display as appropriate.

8. Sign-off (required)  
Operator: ____________________  Date: ____________________  
Maintenance: __________________  Date: ____________________  
Line Lead: ____________________  Date: ____________________  

9. Revision control and notes  
Refer to ECN-2026-043 for engineering changes, MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 for machine-specific setup steps, and SB-1026 for safety procedures. Preserve the signed changeover records in the document control system per plant retention policy.
title: Product changeover - Machining line
