# SOP-P1-L3-03 First-article inspection - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related: ECN-2026-035, QS-PROC-04, SB-1026

Purpose
1. Define the standardized first-article inspection (FAI) process for the machining line to verify conformance of the first production piece to engineering and quality requirements prior to lot release.

Background and scope
2. This procedure applies to first articles produced on the machining line served by EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03. It addresses machine and process verifications, setup checks, dimensional and function checks, and required records for FAI. Use ECN-2026-035 for engineering drawing changes, QS-PROC-04 for quality acceptance criteria, and SB-1026 for safety bulletin items that impact setup.

Preconditions
3. Prior to initiating the FAI:
   1. The production order and drawing release must be confirmed per ECN-2026-035.
   2. Equipment maintenance status must be green and any open high-priority safety items from SB-1026 must be cleared or mitigated.
   3. The tool and gauge set for the part must be verified for calibration per QS-PROC-04.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE during the FAI includes safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, and steel-toe footwear. Follow items called out in SB-1026 for any additional protective requirements specific to the operation.

Inspection team and roles
5. Assignments:
   1. Production Technician — performs setup, basic machine checks, and produces the first article.
   2. Quality Inspector — performs dimensional inspection and signs the FAI record.
   3. Process Engineer — reviews setup parameters and approves process capability notes where required.

Key setup verifications and safety checks
6. Verify machine setup and safety devices before producing the first article:
   1. Confirm guarding and interlocks are engaged per SB-1026.
   2. Verify coolant and lubrication supply is operational and meets machine manufacturer guidance.
   3. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Record the measured flow value on the FAI checklist.
   4. For hydraulic press components, perform bolt and fastener torque verification where specified. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m. Record the torque reading and who performed the check.

First-article production
7. Produce the first article using the production tooling and the same program, feeds, and speeds intended for production. Log the program identifier and tool offsets on the FAI checklist.

Dimensional and functional inspection
8. Perform the following inspections on the first article:
   1. Critical dimensions identified on the release drawing as inspection features must be measured and recorded on the FAI report.
   2. Functional checks such as fit, assembly engagement, or movement must be performed and results documented with pass/fail indication and remarks where applicable.
   3. If measured values deviate from drawing tolerances, stop and escalate to the Process Engineer and Quality Manager immediately per QS-PROC-04.

Step rationale and examples
9. Rationale:
   1. Verifying coil cooling flow ensures thermal stability of the induction heater during billet heating and prevents coil damage.
   2. Verifying the main ram bolt torque prevents mechanical loosening and maintains press alignment and safety during forging operations.
   3. Recording actual measured values on the FAI checklist provides traceability and allows correlation of process parameters to part quality.
10. Example entries for the FAI checklist (illustrative content only; record actual measured values):
   1. Coil cooling water flow: recorded measurement and inspector initials.
   2. Main ram bolt torque: 1330 N·m recorded and inspector initials.
   3. Dimensional checks: list of feature identifiers, measured values, tolerance status, and inspector initials.

Nonconformance and disposition
11. If any FAI inspection item fails:
   1. Tag the first article as nonconforming and quarantine according to QS-PROC-04.
   2. Initiate containment and corrective action per QS-PROC-04 and reference ECN-2026-035 if the failure is design related.
   3. Document root cause, corrective action, verification plan, and sign-off before resuming production.

Records and retention
12. Documents to complete and retain:
   1. Completed FAI checklist with all measured values, signatures, and remarks.
   2. Calibrations and tool offsets used during setup, referenced per QS-PROC-04.
   3. Torque verification printout or manual log showing the main ram bolt torque check for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
   4. Flowmeter log or readout showing coil cooling water flow for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
   5. Nonconformance reports, if any, and closure records.
   6. All records shall be filed in the document control system and retained as required by QS-PROC-04.

Sign-off
13. Signatures required to accept the FAI:
   1. Production Technician — confirms setup and first article production.
   2. Quality Inspector — confirms dimensional and functional acceptance.
   3. Process Engineer — approves process parameters and any setup deviations.

Revision and change control
14. Any change to process parameters, tooling, or inspection criteria discovered during the FAI must be documented and submitted as an engineering change request per ECN-2026-035. Update the FAI record and reissue per document control.

Appendix
15. Related documents:
   1. ECN-2026-035
   2. QS-PROC-04
   3. SB-1026

End of procedure.
title: First-article inspection - Machining line

# SOP-P1-L3-04 Shift handover - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-008, MM-P1-L3-IH01, QS-PROC-04

Purpose
- To standardize the shift handover process for the Machining line to ensure continuity of safe operation, product quality, and traceability.

Scope
- Applies to all operators, lead technicians, and supervisors assigned to Plant P1, line P1-L3 and to the equipment identified: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Background and rationale
- The machining line produces forged billets that require controlled heating, hydraulic press operation, and machining. Consistent transfer of process state, outstanding actions, and known issues reduces risk of equipment damage, rejects, and safety incidents. Handover also ensures lubrication and temperature controls are verified against baseline records. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. These values must be confirmed during each handover and recorded.

Preconditions (to be completed before handover)
1. The oncoming operator has reviewed the last shift log and read any open entries in the shift binder.
2. All in-process billets are identified and the current process step is documented.
3. Any required parts, tooling, or consumables for the next shift are staged or ordered per MM-P1-L3-IH01.
4. Safety devices and guards are in place; no safety bypass is active.
5. Outstanding maintenance requests have been logged in accordance with ECN-2026-008 and communicated to maintenance.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, and steel-toe footwear are required on the machining floor.
2. Gloves appropriate for handling hot materials must be worn when handling billets removed from EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
3. Additional PPE for maintenance tasks must follow MM-P1-L3-IH01 and QS-PROC-04.

Numbered handover steps
1. Initial briefing
   - The outgoing operator provides a concise verbal summary of the last shift, including production status, any deviations, and known work-arounds.
   - Confirm all critical alarms, trips, and interlocks that occurred and the current status of restoration.
   - Note any quality concerns observed during the last shift and the disposition of suspect parts.

2. Equipment status verification
   - Inspect EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03 for visible damage, leaks, or abnormal conditions.
   - Confirm lubrication status of EQ-P1-L3-HP02 and verify lubricant part number: CFW-LUB-497.
   - Confirm the target set point for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 is 1235 °C and that actual process control is within acceptable limits per MM-P1-L3-IH01.
   - Record any deviation from nominal equipment state and any temporary protective measures applied.

3. Process and material status
   - List in-process billets, their current process step, and any special instructions for heat soak, machining, or inspection.
   - Document the last measured dimensions or NDT results that affect the next steps.
   - If any billets have been segregated for rework or scrap, identify their location and reason.

4. Quality and measurement handover
   - Review last shift’s sampling and inspection records.
   - Confirm acceptance criteria applied during last shift and any concessions or nonconforming part dispositions.
   - Ensure the next shift has access to any open quality actions and the responsible contacts.

5. Maintenance and technical actions
   - Review outstanding maintenance tasks and their priority as documented in ECN-2026-008.
   - Confirm any temporary repairs, bypasses, or mitigations have been documented and authorized by maintenance or engineering.
   - If any specific tooling or fixture adjustments were made, document the change and reference MM-P1-L3-IH01 for machine-specific instructions.

6. Safety and housekeeping
   - Confirm all safety incidents have been reported per QS-PROC-04 and that corrective actions are in place.
   - Check that work areas around EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03 are free of trip hazards and that required barriers are in place.
   - Verify fire suppression and emergency access routes are unobstructed.

7. Examples and scenarios
   - Example: If the outgoing operator reports a recurring temperature drift on EQ-P1-L3-IH01, the oncoming operator should verify the controller displays the target 1235 °C and note any deviation. If deviation persists, escalate per ECN-2026-008.
   - Example: If a low-lube warning was observed on EQ-P1-L3-HP02, verify lubricant type is CFW-LUB-497 and the reservoir level; if replenished, document batch or lot per MM-P1-L3-IH01 records.

8. Records to complete
   - Shift log entry with summary of verbal handover.
   - Equipment check form for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03.
   - Quality checklist and any nonconformance reports filed per QS-PROC-04.
   - Maintenance request entries for pending actions referenced by ECN-2026-008.

9. Acceptance and acknowledgment
   - The oncoming operator repeats back critical items: active nonconformances, in-process billet status, any temporary modifications, and confirmation of lubricant and target temperature values.
   - Both outgoing and oncoming operators sign the shift log and initial the equipment check forms.

Sign-off (required)
- Outgoing operator name / signature / time (enter in shift log).
- Oncoming operator name / signature / time (enter in shift log).
- Supervisor or lead acknowledgment if non-routine issues or maintenance pending (enter in shift log).

Post-handover follow-up
- The oncoming operator performs a short verification run to confirm stable operation and records results in the shift log.
- Any unresolved items requiring escalation are routed to maintenance or engineering per ECN-2026-008 and documented.

References
- ECN-2026-008
- MM-P1-L3-IH01
- QS-PROC-04

Revision history
- Current revision: Rev D.
title: Shift handover - Machining line

text:
# SOP-P1-L3-05 Planned shutdown - Machining line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, ECN-2026-043

Purpose
This procedure defines the approved sequence and controls for a planned shutdown of the machining line at P1-L3 for maintenance, inspection, and changeover activities. It provides background, rationale for critical steps, examples of typical records to keep, and the required approvals to restart.

Scope
Applies to all maintenance technicians, lead operators, and the maintenance planner responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03 during a planned shutdown event.

Preconditions
1. Work order and shutdown approval completed by maintenance planning and operations.
2. Shift handover has been conducted and the line is in a safe, controlled state.
3. All affected personnel have been notified of the planned shutdown and are present or accounted for.
4. Isolation and lockout/tagout materials are available and inspected for integrity.
5. Permit to work issued for confined space or hot work if required by local rules and related documents ECN-2026-021 and ECN-2026-029 have been reviewed.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Safety footwear and eye protection.
2. Hearing protection where machining noise is present.
3. Thermal protection when working near induction heater components.
4. Gloves and protective clothing appropriate for handling hydraulic fittings and coolant lines.
5. Respiratory protection if fumes or particulates are likely during inspection or cleaning.

Procedure
1. Preparation and safety verification
   1.1. Notify operations control and display shutdown signage at access points.  
   1.2. Verify that all moving parts are stationary and that feed systems are disabled. Lockout/tagout all energy sources to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03. Rationale: prevents unintentional startup and injury during inspection and maintenance.
   1.3. Confirm isolation of electrical supplies and secure keys with authorized personnel only.

2. Induction billet heater (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) tasks
   2.1. Verify target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Record the last logged process temperature prior to shutdown in the maintenance record. Rationale: ensures there is a documented baseline temperature and avoids thermal shock during service.
   2.2. Allow components to reach a safe handling condition per local thermal procedures before removing covers or sensor housings. Example record: note of thermal state, time last temperature logged, and initials of verifying technician.
   2.3. Inspect coil, water cooling connections, and thermal insulation for damage. Document any anomalies and reference ECN-2026-043 if component replacement is required.

3. Hydraulic forging press (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) tasks
   3.1. De-pressurize hydraulic circuits following equipment isolation. Rationale: prevents hydraulic movement during maintenance.
   3.2. Verify the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m when reassembling ram connections after service. Record torque verification in the maintenance log with the technician’s name. Rationale: correct torque ensures structural integrity and consistent press performance.
   3.3. Inspect ram seals, hoses, and mounting hardware for wear. Keep photographic records of any defects and attach to the work order.

4. CNC machining centers (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) tasks
   4.1. Secure spindle and toolholders. Verify tool inventory and condition. Rationale: prevents tool ejection and maintains part quality after restart.
   4.2. Inspect coolant hoses, filtration, and chip removal systems. Record any filter changes and coolant top-up actions in the service log.
   4.3. Validate axis lubrication points are accessible and that lubricant reservoirs are at acceptable levels per manufacturer guidance. Record lubricant batch reference in maintenance records.

5. Testing and verification prior to restart
   5.1. Remove lockout/tagout only after all technicians have cleared the equipment and tool covers, guards, and access panels are secured.
   5.2. Conduct dry functional checks of safety interlocks and emergency stop circuits.
   5.3. Gradual bring-up procedures: initiate systems per the approved start sequence and confirm nominal conditions are achieved. Document performance checks and any deviations.

Step rationale and examples
- Recording the induction heater setpoint (1235 °C) and the hydraulic ram bolt torque (1330 N·m) provides specific, auditable parameters for thermal stability and mechanical integrity. Example: if a post-maintenance part dimension drift is observed, these recorded values assist root cause analysis.
- Photographic and written records of seal conditions, hose chafing, and insulation damage support warranty claims and engineering change requests referenced in ECN-2026-029 and ECN-2026-043.

Records to keep
- Shutdown work order with signatures.
- Temperature log entries for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 showing the documented target of 1235 °C and last measured values.
- Torque verification entry for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 showing the main ram bolt torque of 1330 N·m and the technician initials.
- Photographs of findings, filter change tags, lubricant batch references, and any replaced parts.
- Post-maintenance test checklist and restart authorization.

Sign-off
1. Maintenance technician: name, signature, date, remarks.
2. Shift supervisor: name, signature, date, confirmation of safe restart readiness.
3. Maintenance planner: name, signature, date, attached records review.
4. Engineering approval if component changes were made, referencing ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, or ECN-2026-043 as applicable.

Notes and references
- Review ECN-2026-021, ECN-2026-029, and ECN-2026-043 for design changes, approved replacement parts, and post-change validation steps.
- Deviations from this SOP require documented risk assessment and explicit approval from maintenance management.

text:
# SOP-P1-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
Related: SB-1046, SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04

1. Purpose and scope  
   1.1 Purpose: Provide the controlled procedure to start up the Heat Treat line for production runs, ensuring equipment readiness, process safety, and traceable records.  
   1.2 Scope: Applies to operators, maintenance, and quality personnel working on EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

2. Background and rationale  
   The Heat Treat line integrates CNC pre-machining, hydraulic press operations, and a batch furnace. Proper startup sequences prevent part damage, preserve process capability, and reduce safety risks. The spindle warm-up sequence and controlled furnace quench timing are critical to dimensional stability and metallurgical outcome. Examples: insufficient spindle warm-up increases runout and causes scrap; excessive quench delay in the furnace degrades hardness and results in rework.

3. Preconditions (must be verified before proceeding)  
   3.1 Facility utilities are online and stable per SB-1046.  
   3.2 Last shift maintenance work has been completed and closed in the maintenance system referenced in SOP-P1-L4-03.  
   3.3 All protection interlocks are present and functional; isolation permits removed.  
   3.4 Production plan and heat numbers available and matched to carrier trays as required by SOP-P1-L4-04.

4. Required PPE  
   - Safety glasses with side shields  
   - Heat-resistant gloves when loading/unloading EQ-P1-L4-HT03 per furnace access procedure  
   - Hearing protection while near operating EQ-P1-L4-HP02 during press cycles  
   - High-visibility clothing for shop floor access

5. Startup procedure (numbered steps)  
   5.1 Visual inspection  
       5.1.1 Confirm work area clear of obstructions and loose tooling.  
       5.1.2 Verify emergency stops are accessible and labeled. Rationale: removes mechanical hazards and ensures operator response capability. Example: remove pneumatic hoses left on the floor that can entangle operators or tooling.  
   5.2 Power-up sequence  
       5.2.1 Enable main feed to EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and EQ-P1-L4-HT03 following lockout/tagout verification. Rationale: proper sequenced energization prevents inrush events and alarm floods.  
   5.3 CNC warm-up and verification for EQ-P1-L4-CN01  
       5.3.1 Home axes and confirm position feedback within acceptable limits.  
       5.3.2 Execute spindle warm-up as documented on the operator screen. The spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes. Rationale: thermal stabilization reduces spindle runout and improves first-piece accuracy. Example: when warming from a cold start, run a lightweight program with tool touches to confirm consistent surface finish. Record: spindle warm-up start and stop timestamps in the log.  
   5.4 Hydraulic press readiness for EQ-P1-L4-HP02  
       5.4.1 Verify hydraulic reservoir level and filter condition per maintenance checklist. Rationale: low fluid or clogged filters can change force characteristics. Record: hydraulic checklist signed and filed.  
       5.4.2 Run a no-load cycle to confirm valve sequencing and pressure rise within control band. Rationale: confirms safe actuation prior to loading production pieces.  
   5.5 Furnace startup and control verification for EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
       5.5.1 Validate furnace control communication and that thermocouples report expected steady-state values per operator display. Rationale: ensures accurate soak and ramp control before loading parts.  
       5.5.2 Confirm automatic quench system primed and ready. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Rationale: constraining quench delay preserves metallurgical properties and meets hardness targets. Example: when cycling a dummy load, monitor the quench activation time from furnace door close to quench onset and log the measured delay. Record: quench delay verification entry in the process validation log.  
   5.6 First-piece flow test  
       5.6.1 Process a single carrier through EQ-P1-L4-CN01 → EQ-P1-L4-HP02 → EQ-P1-L4-HT03 following the normal material flow. Observe for mechanical interference, tool breakage, or abnormal temperatures. Rationale: verifies integrated flow before committing full lot. Record: first-piece inspection checklist including dimensional and visual acceptance criteria.

6. Process monitoring and records to keep  
   - Spindle warm-up log for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 (start/stop times).  
   - Hydraulic readiness checklist for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (filter status, fluid level, no-load cycle result).  
   - Furnace control verification and quench delay verification for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 with timestamped readings.  
   - First-piece inspection checklist and material traceability tags.  
   - Any deviations or alarms recorded in the line event log and routed to quality per SOP-P1-L4-03.

7. Abnormal conditions and escalation  
   7.1 If spindle parameters do not stabilize after the warm-up period, stop the line and notify maintenance. Rationale: continued operation risks scrap and tool damage.  
   7.2 If measured quench delay exceeds the maximum referenced value, halt loading into the furnace and follow the stoppage criteria in SOP-P1-L4-04. Rationale: prevents out-of-spec metallurgical results.  
   7.3 For any hydraulic pressure abnormality, depressurize and tag out EQ-P1-L4-HP02 until inspected by maintenance.

8. Training and competency  
   Operators must be trained on the startup checklist, emergency stop actions, and use of the records system. Training completion is documented per site training policy and referenced in SB-1046.

9. Sign-off and acceptance  
   9.1 Operator initiating startup signs and dates the startup checklist and attaches all required logs.  
   9.2 Quality representative verifies first-piece acceptance and initials the checklist to allow full production release.  
   9.3 Maintenance representative signs off when any equipment actions were performed during startup.

10. Revision history and attachments  
   See related documents SB-1046, SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04 for linked procedures, maintenance forms, and detailed quality criteria.

Signatures:  
Operator: ____________________  
Quality: ____________________  
Maintenance: ____________________

text:
# SOP-P1-L4-02 Product changeover - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03
Related documents: MM-P1-L4-HT03, QS-PROC-05, SOP-P1-L4-05

Purpose
1. Describe the standardized steps for product changeover on the Heat Treat line to minimize downtime, ensure process integrity, and maintain traceability. This procedure applies to all operators and technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

Scope and background
2. Changeovers on the Heat Treat line require coordinated mechanical, thermal, and tooling adjustments. The objective is to switch from one product family to another with documented checks and handoffs. Rationale: consistent changeover practice reduces scrap, prevents cross-contamination, and maintains heat-treat cycle integrity. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance-specific tasks, QS-PROC-05 for quality record requirements, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for upstream material preparation steps.

Preconditions (required before starting)
3. Verify the following before initiating changeover:
   - Production schedule authorizes the changeover and the new job number is available.
   - All incoming material is staged and verified per SOP-P1-L4-05.
   - Any open non-conformances related to the Heat Treat line are addressed or documented per QS-PROC-05.
   - Maintenance clearance for mechanical interventions is obtained if required (see MM-P1-L4-HT03).

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for changeover activities:
   - Heat-resistant gloves for handling components from EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Hearing protection when within the active load/unload zone of EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
   - Cut-resistant gloves for tooling adjustment at EQ-P1-L4-CN01.

Changeover steps (numbered)
5. Stop current production and secure area
   5.1. Notify downstream and upstream operators that changeover is starting.
   5.2. Place lockout/tagout per site protocol if any mechanical maintenance is required (see MM-P1-L4-HT03).
   5.3. Record stop time and reason in the shift log required by QS-PROC-05.

6. Clean and clear process path
   6.1. Remove residual parts from EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
   6.2. Wipe down contact surfaces and tooling nests to remove debris. Keep cleaning records as per QS-PROC-05.

7. Inspect and prepare tooling and fixtures
   7.1. Confirm tooling required for the new product is available and tagged for this job.
   7.2. Fit check new tooling on EQ-P1-L4-CN01 and inspect for wear. Document findings in equipment log.
   7.3. Lubrication: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is CFW-LUB-477. Apply lubrication following the lubrication schedule in MM-P1-L4-HT03 and log application.

8. Machine setup and warm-up
   8.1. Load new program and verify program ID matches job sheet.
   8.2. Perform dry-run or air-cycle to verify motion and clearance; record anomalies.
   8.3. Spindle warm-up: For EQ-P1-L4-CN01 allow spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes prior to cutting. Use the spindle-warm log to record start and end of warm-up.

9. Process parameter verification
   9.1. Confirm heat-treat cycle selection at EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is as specified for new product. If a thermal profile change is required, consult MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance input.
   9.2. Verify conveyor and transfer timing at EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to ensure consistent load rates.
   9.3. Document all parameter confirmations on the changeover checklist.

10. Trial run and first-piece inspection
   10.1. Produce a defined number of trial pieces as indicated on the job sheet.
   10.2. Inspect first-piece measurements and features, comparing to the job print and QS-PROC-05 sampling requirements.
   10.3. If trial pieces meet acceptance, sign off to proceed to production. If not, document deviations and escalate to engineering.

11. Bring line back to production
   11.1. Gradually ramp load rates and monitor process stability.
   11.2. Maintain heightened inspection frequency for the first production batch as required by QS-PROC-05.
   11.3. Record start of production and job number in the production log.

Examples and rationale
12. Example: When switching from a short-run part to a long-run part, the spindle warm-up time prevents early dimensional drift during the first cuts. The specified spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes to stabilize bearing temperatures and reduce runout. Using the correct lubricant (CFW-LUB-477) helps maintain consistent spindle performance across changeovers. These steps minimize rework and ensure heat-treat cycles apply to parts within specification.

Records to keep
13. Maintain the following records per QS-PROC-05:
   - Changeover checklist with timestamps.
   - Lubrication application entry specifying the use of CFW-LUB-477.
   - Spindle warm-up log showing the 15 minutes warm-up period for EQ-P1-L4-CN01.
   - First-piece inspection reports and any NCRs.
   - Any maintenance or adjustments recorded per MM-P1-L4-HT03.

Escalation and hold points
14. Hold production and contact engineering if:
   - First-piece inspection fails to meet acceptance criteria.
   - Any abnormal noise, vibration, or thermal readings persist following warm-up and trial run.
   - Tooling mismatches or fixture damage is detected.

Sign-off (required)
15. The following sign-offs are required to close a changeover:
   - Operator signature confirming completion of steps 5 through 11 and records attached.
   - Supervisor signature confirming review of records and first-piece acceptance.
   - Maintenance signature if any MM-P1-L4-HT03 interventions were performed.

Change history
16. Revision history maintained in document control.

Related documents
17. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance tasks and lubrication schedules, QS-PROC-05 for quality and records requirements, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for upstream material preparation.

text:
# SOP-P1-L4-03 First-article inspection - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
Related: ECN-2026-002, ECN-2026-007, SB-1012

1. Purpose and scope  
1.1 Purpose: Define the approved first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for incoming production runs routed through the Heat Treat line at P1-L4. This procedure applies to first-article pieces requiring turning, forging and heat-treatment operations on equipment EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
1.2 Scope: Use this SOP for verification of dimen­sions, surface condition, hardness records, equipment set-up confirmations and traceability prior to release of the first-article lot into continuous production.

2. Background and rationale  
2.1 Background: First-article inspection prevents propagation of process or tooling errors downstream. This SOP combines machine set-up verification, sample measurement and process record retention to provide a documented gateway for production release.  
2.2 Rationale: Key controls include machine set-up confirmation on the CNC turning center, lubrication verification for the press, and heat-treatment cycle traceability. Example failure modes addressed: incorrect chuck clamping, improper press lubrication, and missing heat-treatment records. See ECN-2026-002 for recent tooling updates and ECN-2026-007 for updated fixture drawings. SB-1012 provides sampling acceptance criteria and reporting templates.

3. Preconditions (required before executing steps)  
3.1 Materials and documentation: First-article sample, routing sheet, approved drawing, and sampling form from SB-1012 must be present.  
3.2 Responsible personnel: Qualified setup technician and FAI inspector assigned and available.  
3.3 Equipment readiness: Verify equipment identity matches list: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03. Do not proceed if identification tags do not match.  
3.4 Visual check: Machine guards in place and safety interlocks show normal status. If faults are present, stop and notify Maintenance.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE)  
4.1 Required PPE: safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, and steel-toe footwear. Ensure PPE is worn whenever interacting with machines or handling hot or sharp parts.

5. Step-by-step procedure (numbered actions)  
5.1 Setup verification — EQ-P1-L4-CN01 (CNC turning center)  
5.1.1 Confirm chuck mounting and jaw seating per fixture drawing. Verify chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m. Document the torque reading on the FAI form.  
5.1.2 Install first-article blank and conduct a dry-fit with coolant off. Inspect for runout and secure fit. Record any deviations and corrective actions taken.  
5.2 Lubrication verification — EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (hydraulic forging press)  
5.2.1 Confirm lubricant used in pump/reservoir matches part number listed on maintenance cards: lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195. Note batch or container ID on the FAI form.  
5.2.2 Inspect visible seals and fittings for leaks and verify pump fill level visually against sight glass. Log observations. If leakage is detected, tag equipment and call Maintenance.  
5.3 First-article machining pass  
5.3.1 Perform a programmed cycle or manual supervised cut to produce the first-article part. Measure critical dimensions called out on the drawing and SB-1012 sampling form. Use calibrated gauges and record values.  
5.3.2 If a dimension falls outside the drawing callout, stop and follow containment per ECN-2026-002. Document the nonconformance and corrective action, including tooling change or program update.  
5.4 Forging verification — EQ-P1-L4-HP02  
5.4.1 Feed the machined blank to the press following standard material handling. Verify part orientation and die seating. Monitor first stroke for proper material flow and absence of flash beyond expected condition. Record visual assessment.  
5.5 Heat-treatment confirmation — EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
5.5.1 Place first-article part into the heat-treat batch with traceable tags. Confirm the batch log contains operator initials and part identifiers. Use the furnace/oven recorder output as the primary record. Attach a copy of the record to the FAI packet.  
5.6 Post-process inspection and sampling  
5.6.1 Measure final critical features identified in SB-1012. Perform hardness test and compare to drawing requirements. Log instrument ID and calibration status.  
5.6.2 Surface condition: inspect for scale, decarb, cracking or distortion. Photograph any anomalies and include images in the FAI packet.

6. Examples and acceptable responses  
6.1 Example 1: If the chuck jaw bolt reads 90 N·m and part runout is within tolerance, document “Torque verified; runout acceptable; proceed to machining.”  
6.2 Example 2: If lubricant container labeled CFW-LUB-195 is not available, document “Lubricant mismatch; stop process; request Maintenance review per ECN-2026-007.” Include container label photograph.

7. Records to keep and retention  
7.1 FAI packet: completed FAI form from SB-1012, torque log, lubricant container ID, dimensional measurement sheets, hardness report, furnace/oven recorder output, photographs of defects and corrective action log.  
7.2 Attachments: copies of any ECN referenced corrective actions (ECN-2026-002, ECN-2026-007).  
7.3 Retention: retain the packet in the document control system index under SOP-P1-L4-03 for audit traceability. Ensure packets are signed and dated in the sign-off section.

8. Nonconformance and escalation  
8.1 For any out-of-tolerance dimension, lubrication discrepancy or machine fault, stop the line and enter a hold note in production control. Notify Quality and Maintenance. Escalate per ECN-2026-002 if tooling change is required.

9. Sign-off (required)  
9.1 Setup technician: name, signature, time, confirm items 5.1 through 5.2 completed.  
9.2 FAI inspector: name, signature, time, confirm items 5.3 through 5.6 completed and records attached.  
9.3 Production manager: name, signature, date, approve release to continuous production.

10. Notes and references  
10.1 See ECN-2026-002 for tooling and chucking-related engineering changes.  
10.2 See ECN-2026-007 for maintenance and fixture amendments.  
10.3 Use SB-1012 for sampling forms and FAI packet templates.
title: First-article inspection - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P1-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Purpose
1. Define the standardized shift handover procedure for the Heat Treat line to ensure continuity of operations, safe transfer of process state, and traceable records. This SOP applies to operators and technicians assigned to P1-L4 and interfacing maintenance staff.

Preconditions
2. The departing operator must have completed the shift checklist and all required log entries. All critical alarms must be acknowledged and cleared. Any open maintenance requests must be recorded per MM-P1-L4-CN01. If material or product disposition is unresolved, the issue shall be escalated to the shift supervisor before handover.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
3. Required PPE for handover activities on the Heat Treat line: safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, and hearing protection. Use of additional PPE for charged work or maintenance follows MM-P1-L4-CN01 and facility rules.

Background and rationale
4. The Heat Treat line comprises the CNC turning center, hydraulic press, and heat treat furnace identified as EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03 respectively. Accurate transfer of machine state, process setpoints, and outstanding actions reduces scrap, prevents unplanned downtime, and maintains compliance with quality controls cited in QS-PROC-05. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C; this setpoint must be verified during each handover to confirm process readiness and to flag any deviation requiring QA notification per QS-PROC-05.

Step-by-step handover procedure
5. Handover start
   5.1 The incoming operator shall arrive at the workstation before the recorded end time of the outgoing shift to allow a full verbal and visual transfer.  
   5.2 Confirm identity of both parties and sign the on-shift log to indicate participation in the handover.

6. Visual and physical tour
   6.1 Perform a walk-through of the line with the departing operator. Check EO status lights, guard integrity, and tool storage.  
   6.2 Confirm material staging and label status. Note any deviations or nonconforming parts in the shift log.

7. Machine state verification
   7.1 EQ-P1-L4-CN01: Verify program loaded and tool offsets saved. Confirm that spindle warm-up has been completed; the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes and must be completed prior to production restart. Record the warm-up completion time in the machine log.  
   7.2 EQ-P1-L4-HP02: Confirm press is at rest, safeguards engaged, and that hydraulic parameters are at nominal operating state per MM-P1-L4-CN01. Note any leaks or abnormal noises observed during tour.  
   7.3 EQ-P1-L4-HT03: Verify furnace status and confirm the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Confirm ramp programs and soak timers are as documented in the job packet. Any discrepancy with the 880 °C value requires immediate notification to quality per QS-PROC-05.

8. Alarms and events review
   8.1 Review the alarm history and event log for each piece of equipment. For any unresolved alarms, document the alarm code and corrective actions taken to date. Reference MM-P1-L4-CN01 for troubleshooting guidance and SB-1046 for legacy advisory notes where applicable.

9. Material and work order status
   9.1 Confirm active work orders and lot numbers. Verify inventory on the line matches the work order requirements. Record any shortfalls and expected replenishment actions.  
   9.2 Confirm that all processed parts are labeled and segregated per QS-PROC-05 if they are nonconforming.

10. Quality and inspection
   10.1 Review recent inspection records and sample results. If any trending issues or out-of-spec data exist, document the issue and required hold or rework action. Communicate open quality items to the incoming operator and shift supervisor.

11. Maintenance and safety issues
   11.1 Document any maintenance tasks in the maintenance system and verify that urgent items are flagged in MM-P1-L4-CN01.  
   11.2 Confirm that lockout/tagout status of any isolated equipment is visible and that tags are current. If tags are present, the responsible technician must be identified in the handover log.

12. Records to keep
   12.1 Maintain the shift handover form in the line binder and enter a summary in the electronic log. Include: machine state, confirmation of austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 as 880 °C, confirmation that spindle warm-up for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 completed with the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) recorded as 15 minutes, open issues, and any quality holds.  
   12.2 Retain copies of the signed handover sheet and attach relevant printouts from equipment event logs. Reference QS-PROC-05 for retention guidelines.

Examples and common scenarios
13. Example A — Incoming operator finds furnace setpoint different from 880 °C: Escalate to quality per QS-PROC-05, place the current batch on hold, document the deviation on the handover form, and notify maintenance via MM-P1-L4-CN01 if required.  
14. Example B — Spindle warm-up was not completed: Do not start production cycles. Complete the spindle warm-up process and log the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) as 15 minutes before resuming machining.

Handover sign-off
15. Signatures: The departing operator, incoming operator, and shift supervisor must sign the handover sheet. Required entries: names, start and end of coverage confirmation, verification of austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 as 880 °C, and confirmation that spindle warm-up for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 was completed with the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) recorded as 15 minutes. Attach any supporting logs or printouts.

Related documents
16. See MM-P1-L4-CN01 for maintenance procedures, QS-PROC-05 for quality handling and disposition, and SB-1046 for service bulletin references.

Deviation and escalation
17. Any procedural deviation during handover that impacts safety, product quality, or machine integrity must be escalated immediately to the shift supervisor and documented in the handover records. Use the related documents listed above for further action.
title: Shift handover - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P1-L4-05 Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Purpose
1. Define controlled sequence and responsibilities for a planned shutdown of the Heat Treat line to support maintenance, inspection, or changeover activities while protecting personnel, equipment, and process integrity.

Scope
2. Applies to all technicians, maintenance personnel, and supervision involved with EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03 on P1-L4 during planned shutdowns. Refer to ECN-2026-007 for engineering changes that may affect shutdown scope, and to MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 for machine-specific maintenance sequences.

Background and rationale
3. Planned shutdowns are required to perform inspections, preventive maintenance, and engineering modifications with minimal risk. A controlled shutdown sequence prevents inadvertent energization, avoids hydraulic and thermal stress on components, and ensures safety systems remain functional for the duration of the outage. Example: isolating hydraulic pressure at EQ-P1-L4-HP02 before removing fittings prevents uncontrolled movement; the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar and must not be exceeded during re-pressurization steps specified in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2. For EQ-P1-L4-HT03, maintain quench control parameters to prevent soak and quench timing errors; the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.

Preconditions (required before initiating shutdown)
4. Confirm authorized work order and scope per ECN-2026-007.  
5. Verify required personnel and tools are available and trained.  
6. Review machine-specific maintenance sequences MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 and confirm no outstanding hold points outside the shutdown scope.  
7. Inform downstream and upstream production leads that P1-L4 Heat Treat line will be taken out of service.  
8. Ensure spare parts and consumables referenced in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 are staged.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
9. Mandatory PPE for shutdown tasks: safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, and arc-rated clothing where electrical exposure is possible. Additional PPE required by MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 or MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 must be used when performing those procedures.

Shutdown steps (numbered sequence)
10. Prepare for shutdown:  
   10.1. Post lockout/tagout notification at P1-L4 access points and at control station for EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
   10.2. Verify energy sources identified on single-line diagrams per ECN-2026-007.

11. Isolate utilities:  
   11.1. Close primary feed valves to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and EQ-P1-L4-CN01 following procedures in MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3.  
   11.2. De-energize electrical control panels and apply lockout/tagout.  
   11.3. Drain hydraulic accumulators per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and verify system pressure falls below a safe threshold before work on EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Remember: the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar; do not exceed this limit during any pressurization step.

12. Verification and hold points:  
   12.1. Use pressure indicators and valve position confirmation to verify isolation.  
   12.2. Attempt controlled start on each isolated unit after lockout; equipment must not energize. Record verification results.

13. Safe access and work:  
   13.1. Install physical barriers and signage.  
   13.2. Permit only authorized persons within the work area.  
   13.3. Follow task-specific PPE and procedures in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 for component removal or inspection.

14. Special control - quench system:  
   14.1. When performing maintenance on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 quench circuits, set control parameters to safe mode per MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds; confirm quench delay setting at the controller before returning the unit to service.

15. Reassembly and pre-start checks:  
   15.1. Reinstall guards, panels, and fittings per machine-specific procedures.  
   15.2. Remove lockout/tagout only after inspection and authorization. Conduct pre-start checklist and review items in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3.

16. Controlled startup:  
   16.1. Gradually reintroduce utilities and controls. Monitor pressure and control feedback closely. Ensure system pressure for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 remains within acceptable limit during re-pressurization; the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar.  
   16.2. Validate quench timing on EQ-P1-L4-HT03; verify quench delay setting is not greater than 15 seconds.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following records in the document control folder associated with SOP-P1-L4-05 and linked work order: shutdown authorization, lockout/tagout logs, isolation verification records, pre-start and post-start checklists, parts replaced with reference to MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 or MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 where applicable, pressure and quench configuration snapshots, and final sign-off. Include a reference to ECN-2026-007 for any deviations resulting from engineering changes.

Examples and typical issues
18. Example: During re-pressurization of EQ-P1-L4-HP02, monitor pressure gauge behavior against MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 guidance. If pressure overshoot is observed relative to the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar, stop and investigate.  
19. Example: If quench control on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 logs an unexpected delay above the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds, enter a hold and troubleshoot using MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3.

Responsibilities
20. Maintenance supervisor: authorize shutdown, ensure procedures and spare parts are available, and verify final sign-off.  
21. Lead technician: execute steps, maintain records, and notify supervisor of anomalies.  
22. Operators: secure production interfaces and support isolation verification.

Sign-off
23. Complete the sign-off sheet with: work order number, names and signatures of maintenance supervisor, lead technician, and operations representative, confirmation that ECN-2026-007, MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 were consulted and complied with, and that records listed in section 17 are filed.

Related documents
24. ECN-2026-007  
25. MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2  
26. MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3

text:
# SOP-P2-L1-01 Line startup - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Purpose
This procedure describes the controlled startup sequence for the Hot Forge line at P2-L1, covering permit preconditions, personnel protective equipment, stepwise actions, operational rationale, examples of expected observations, and records required for compliance. It applies to operators and maintenance staff responsible for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03. See related documents SB-1001, SB-1030, and SOP-P2-L1-04 for maintenance details, blast cabinet servicing, and shutdown procedures.

Preconditions
1. All tags, lockout devices, and isolation points have been verified cleared per SB-1001.  
2. Plant control room has acknowledged line status as ready.  
3. Required spare parts and consumables are present as identified in SOP-P2-L1-04 for initial run.  
4. Environmental monitoring is in normal state and there are no pending area alarms referencing EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

PPE
1. Leather or heat-rated gloves, face shield, flame-retardant jacket, and hearing protection appropriate to Hot Forge operations.  
2. Respiratory protection as required by SB-1030 when servicing or verifying shot blast systems.  
3. Steel toe boots and eye protection for all personnel on the shop floor.

Startup Steps (numbered sequence)
1. Pre-start inspection
   - Walk the line and visually inspect EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03 for loose panels, debris, or obvious damage.  
   - Confirm that access panels are secured and guards are in place. Rationale: early visual detection prevents unplanned stops and safety incidents.

2. Verify critical fasteners
   - Confirm maintenance log shows mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) set to 430 N·m. If log absent, verify torque at specified torque value prior to energizing EQ-P2-L1-RR01. Rationale: correct clamp torque ensures mandrel stability and prevents ring distortion during rolling.

3. Blast cabinet system check
   - Verify shot blast cabinet operation readiness for EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Confirm that the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa and that the alarm state is normal. If alarm persists, follow SB-1030 to clear and verify collector performance. Rationale: dust collector performance directly affects air quality and media containment during blast operations.

4. Heater and induction oven verification
   - Confirm IH control interlocks are functional per SOP-P2-L1-04 before enabling EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Rationale: induction heating interlocks protect against overcurrent and control faults.

5. Control system sequence enable
   - From the control room, enable line PLC sequence for Hot Forge. Observe soft interlocks and listen for abnormal noises. Rationale: staged enable reduces risk of mechanical engagement under load.

6. Dry run with no charge
   - Run the line through mechanical motions without load to validate kinematic movement and controls. Observe bearings, belts, and roll surfaces for smooth operation. Example observation: no abnormal vibration at roll shafts and consistent return stroke on radial roll. Rationale: detecting mechanical anomalies before loading limits scrap and damage.

7. Low-load trial
   - Introduce a single test piece per operator instruction and verify clamp engagement, heating profile communication, and blast cabinet capture performance. Monitor for any alarms. Rationale: real-load validation confirms integrated system behavior.

8. Full-rate enable
   - Upon successful low-load trial, enable nominal production feed per line routing. Maintain observation for the first production cycle for consistent dimensions and surface quality. Rationale: early batch validation prevents escalation of quality issues.

9. Alarm response readiness
   - Assign an operator responsibility to monitor EH&S and machine alarms. If the dust collector pressure drop alarm for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 triggers at 1240 Pa, stop feed to the blast cabinet and shift to manual containment per SB-1030. Rationale: prompt response maintains air quality and prevents equipment overloading.

10. Communication and handover
   - Notify control room and floor supervision when the line reaches stable production. Confirm any outstanding issues logged for maintenance.

Step Rationale and Examples
- Mandrel clamp torque rationale: specified clamp torque prevents slippage and concentricity errors. Example: a correctly torqued mandrel yields repeatable ring thickness and eliminates rework associated with eccentric rings.
- Dust collector alarm rationale: maintaining the specified alarm point allows predictable maintenance scheduling and prevents particulate crossover into downstream processes. Example: a triggered dust collector alarm at the specified value requires filter inspection or media rebalancing as recorded in SB-1030.

Records to Keep
1. Startup checklist with operator name, date, and signature. Include verification entries for mandrel clamp bolt torque and dust collector pressure drop alarm with the exact values recorded.  
2. Torque verification certificate for the mandrel clamp bolt on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 indicating 430 N·m.  
3. Blast cabinet service and alarm log for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 showing the dust collector pressure drop alarm threshold and any alarm events at 1240 Pa.  
4. Control room log entry indicating time of enable, low-load trial outcome, and handover confirmation.  
5. Any nonconformance reports or quality hold tags issued during startup, cross-referenced to SB-1001.

Sign-off
Operator name: ______________________  
Operator signature: ___________________  
Supervisor name: _____________________  
Supervisor signature: __________________  
Date: _______________________________

References
- SB-1001  
- SB-1030  
- SOP-P2-L1-04

Change History
Revision: Rev E — current document revision.

text:
# SOP-P2-L1-02 Product changeover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-023, MM-P2-L1-RR01, SOP-P2-L1-05

Purpose
1. Define the controlled steps to perform a product changeover on the Hot Forge line to ensure metallurgical consistency, equipment integrity, and traceable records.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03 during production changeover activities.

Preconditions
3. Verify that ECN-2026-023 has been released and that the change order scope and affected tooling are identified.  
4. Confirm that MM-P2-L1-RR01 preventive maintenance status for EQ-P2-L1-RR01 is current and that no outstanding critical maintenance actions are open against EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, or EQ-P2-L1-SB03.  
5. Ensure SOP-P2-L1-05 is available for reference for downstream cooling and quench adjustments.  
6. Obtain written approval for the planned changeover from production supervision before initiating physical work.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
7. Mandatory PPE for all personnel in the hot area: heat-resistant gloves, face shield, flame-resistant jacket, and safety footwear. Specific items are listed on the local PPE board and must be worn at all times while any part of the process is live. Operators assigned to EQ-P2-L1-IH02 must add hearing protection when the induction heater is active.

Safety and isolation
8. Lockout/tagout is required prior to mechanical adjustments on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 and EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Follow site LOTO procedure. Confirm energy isolation on display at the local control panel. Do not perform mechanical interventions while EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is in induction mode.

Key process targets and constraints
9. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. Maintain records showing that billet temperature measurements during the first production run meet the target specified in the job traveller.  
10. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Do not operate EQ-P2-L1-IH02 if measured coil cooling water flow is below this value; stop the induction cycle and notify maintenance.

Procedure
11. Preparation
    11.1. Review the incoming job traveller and ECN-2026-023 to confirm tooling changes, billet material, and final part requirements.  
    11.2. Inspect EQ-P2-L1-RR01 and EQ-P2-L1-SB03 for visible damage, correct tooling seating, and free movement. Check that MM-P2-L1-RR01 indicates no active holds.  
    11.3. Confirm condition and connections for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 cooling and power systems; visually inspect coil and cooling lines for leaks or damage.

12. Set-up
    12.1. Load the new tooling into EQ-P2-L1-RR01 per the tooling schematic attached to ECN-2026-023. Ensure fasteners are secured and alignment marks match.  
    12.2. Configure feed and transfer orientation to match new billet geometry; verify grippers and guides at EQ-P2-L1-SB03 seat correctly.  
    12.3. Start the induction billet heating system only after verifying coil cooling water flow meets the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min and power interlocks are satisfied.

13. First heat and verification
    13.1. Heat a verification billet and record the measured billet temperature at the exit of EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to confirm the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. If measurement deviates, do not proceed to full production; follow troubleshooting below.  
    13.2. Run the verification billet through EQ-P2-L1-RR01 and EQ-P2-L1-SB03, inspect forged geometry and flash. Adjust press stroke or trim die per ECN-2026-023 instructions if geometry is out of tolerance.

14. Troubleshooting examples and rationale
    14.1. If measured billet temperature is below target: confirm coil cooling water flow is above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min and check for poor electrical connection to the induction coil. The rationale: coil cooling and electrical continuity directly affect heating efficiency.  
    14.2. If surface oxidation or scale is excessive post-forge: verify billet cleaning step and handling per SOP-P2-L1-05 prior to heating. Proper pre-heat handling reduces furnace atmosphere effects and improves finish.

15. Production release
    15.1. Once verification billet meets target temperature and forged part geometry meets ECN-2026-023 acceptance, obtain production sign-off from the area lead.  
    15.2. Record start of production in the changeover log and attach measurement records for billet temperature, coil cooling water flow, and visual part inspections.

Records to keep
16. Maintain the following records in the job folder:
    16.1. Changeover checklist signed by responsible operator and lead.  
    16.2. Verification billet temperature readouts showing the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C.  
    16.3. Coil cooling water flow measurement data showing the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min or greater.  
    16.4. Visual inspection notes and any adjustments performed per ECN-2026-023.  
    16.5. Reference to MM-P2-L1-RR01 maintenance status and any corrective actions taken.

Sign-off
17. Signatures required:
    17.1. Operator performing changeover – name and signature.  
    17.2. Area lead verifying first-piece compliance – name and signature.  
    17.3. Maintenance representative confirming cooling flow and LOTO clearance when applicable – name and signature.  
    17.4. Production supervisor releasing line to run – name and signature.

Appendix
18. Related procedural references for follow-up and ongoing checks: ECN-2026-023, MM-P2-L1-RR01, SOP-P2-L1-05.

text:
# SOP-P2-L1-03 First-article inspection - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03  
Related documents: SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-02

Purpose
1. Establish the controlled process for first-article inspection (FAI) on the Hot Forge line to verify tooling, machine set-up, material condition, and part conformance prior to resuming production. Background, rationale, examples, and required records are provided to support repeatable, auditable inspections.

Scope
2. Applies to all first-article runs on P2-L1 where new or revised tooling, material lot change, or equipment maintenance has occurred on EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, or EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Preconditions
3. Work area must be cleared of non-essential materials and obstructions; material lot and travel documents must be present. Confirm system alarms are cleared and permit-to-work or lockout documentation from maintenance is attached if maintenance occurred. Reference SOP-P2-L1-02 for pre-start mechanical checks and SOP-P2-L1-01 for general line start requirements.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Minimum PPE for FAI personnel: steel-toe footwear, heat-resistant gloves, long-sleeve cotton coveralls, face shield, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Use respiratory protection per SB-1001 when shot blast cabinet access or dust exposure is anticipated.

Critical process values (to be observed, exact values recorded)
5. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. Monitor and log the dust collector pressure differential reading prior to and after shot blast activity; do not proceed if the alarm condition is present.
6. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. Measure and log billet surface temperature using calibrated instruments; ensure measured value is at or consistent with target before forging operations commence.

Step-by-step procedure
7. Verify administrative preconditions:
   - Confirm relevant traveler and engineering drawing are present at the cell.
   - Confirm material lot and heat code match the traveler.
   - Confirm tooling identification and serial numbers match the control plan.

8. Equipment status verification:
   - Inspect EQ-P2-L1-RR01 for visible damage or obstruction of feed and return paths.
   - Verify EQ-P2-L1-IH02 control panel indicates ready and instrumentation is calibrated per plant calibration records.
   - Confirm EQ-P2-L1-SB03 blast cabinet doors and interlocks function; verify dust collector pre-start indicators.

9. Environmental and utility checks:
   - Confirm compressed air and electrical supply indications are within normal operating parameters (visual check of gauges and panel indicators only).
   - Verify area ventilation is operational; reference SB-1001 for dust and ventilation control requirements.

10. Material preparation and heater confirmation:
   - Stage the first billet from the approved lot.
   - Using the calibrated pyrometer or thermocouple, measure the billet temperature at the recommended location per engineering drawing and record the measurement. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. If reading is not consistent with target, follow hold-for-inspection and escalate to engineering.

11. Run a controlled first feed to the roll and forge stations:
   - Feed the first billet into EQ-P2-L1-RR01 and observe feed alignment, bite, and any abnormal vibrations. Pause the line on any abnormal condition.
   - Monitor and log the die fill, flash formation, and part transfer. Capture one representative sample for dimensional inspection.

12. Shot blast and surface finish verification:
   - After forging and trimming, process the sample through EQ-P2-L1-SB03 shot blast cabinet for surface preparation. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa; check the differential prior to shot blast, and after, and document both readings.
   - Inspect blasted surface for uniformity, embedded media, and acceptable cleanliness per engineering drawing.

13. Dimensional and visual inspection:
   - Perform full FAI dimensional checks and visual acceptance criteria on the sample per drawing and control plan. Record all measured features and any nonconformances on the FAI form.
   - If dimensions are within the drawing requirements and visual inspection is acceptable, proceed to produce a minimum verification sample quantity as required by the control plan and document those pieces.

14. Nonconformance and hold procedure:
   - If any critical dimension or process alarm condition occurs, stop the line, notify production supervision and quality engineering, and place affected material on hold.
   - Initiate disposition per plant nonconformance procedures and reference SOP-P2-L1-01 for stop-and-hold criteria.

Records to keep
15. For each FAI event retain:
   - Completed FAI inspection form with part number and revision (as applicable).
   - Equipment status checklist for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
   - Temperature log showing billet measurement and instrument ID.
   - Dust collector differential readings before and after shot blast.
   - Photos of tooling set-up and representative parts (frontal, side, and critical feature close-ups).
   - Calibration certificates for measurement instruments used.
   - Any nonconformance reports and dispositions.

Examples and rationale
16. Example: if billet temperature reads 1170 °C and target is 1180 °C, hold the run and consult engineering — forging at a lower temperature can increase forging forces and increase the risk of die wear and internal defects. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C; recording the actual measurement supports root-cause analysis if defects appear.
17. Example: if dust collector differential reaches or exceeds the alarm setpoint, e.g., the system shows the alarm state associated with 1240 Pa, stop shot blasting and inspect filters and media containment. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa; logging both pre- and post-blast readings demonstrates adequate housekeeping and filter performance.

Sign-off
18. Completion sign-off requires signatures from:
   - Production lead (verifies tooling and equipment set-up).
   - Quality engineer (verifies dimensional and visual acceptance).
   - Maintenance lead (confirms equipment cleared after any maintenance).
   - Records sign-off must reference this document id and related documents: SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P2-L1-02.

Revision control and retention
19. Maintain FAI records in the document control system under this document id for the period specified by corporate retention policy. Reference related documents SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-02 for additional requirements and cross-checks.
title: First-article inspection - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P2-L1-04 Shift handover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03  
Related: MM-P2-L1-SB03, QS-PROC-06, SOP-P2-L1-02

Purpose
1. Provide a consistent, auditable process for shift-to-shift handover on the Hot Forge line to maintain safety, quality, and uptime. This procedure applies to operators, lead hands, and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Preconditions
2. The outgoing operator must complete all running checks and document status in the shift log before initiating handover.  
3. All safety incidents, near-misses, and equipment status changes must be entered into the incident register referenced by QS-PROC-06 prior to the handover.  
4. Any outstanding maintenance work on equipment named in this document must be raised as an active work order and referenced to MM-P2-L1-SB03.

PPE
5. Minimum personal protective equipment for handover personnel: steel-toe footwear, safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, and face shield as required when entering hot zones. See SOP-P2-L1-02 for specific PPE allocation per task.

Procedure — numbered steps
6. Step 1 — Prepare documentation and records
   6.1. Outgoing operator assembles the shift log, start/stop records, any deviation reports, and current production count.  
   6.2. Verify that the log includes entries for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03. If maintenance actions occurred, attach the related MM-P2-L1-SB03 work order number.

7. Step 2 — Perform critical equipment status checks (outgoing)
   7.1. Confirm that EQ-P2-L1-IH02 coil cooling water flow meets operational minimum: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Document measured flow in the log.  
   7.2. Inspect EQ-P2-L1-SB03 blast wheel liner condition and verify fastener security: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. Record verification and who performed the check.  
   7.3. For EQ-P2-L1-RR01, confirm run roll status, any abnormal vibration, and that no un-cleared jams are present; record observations.

8. Step 3 — Communicate process and product status
   8.1. Outgoing operator provides a concise summary: product type being processed, any process parameter deviations, scrap counts, and quality holds. Include references to QS-PROC-06 where quality issues require non-conformance handling.  
   8.2. Highlight any transient conditions or recurring adjustments that the incoming operator should monitor. Use one-line examples: e.g., "intermittent under-temperature events resolved by reducing feed, see log entry."

9. Step 4 — Confirm recent maintenance and modifications
   9.1. Review completed and pending maintenance from MM-P2-L1-SB03. Confirm that all safety guards are reinstalled and lockout/tagout procedures are cleared.  
   9.2. If any weld repairs, liner replacements, or bearing changes were performed, confirm the responsible technician has signed the work order and that the post-maintenance inspection is attached.

10. Step 5 — Handover of controls and verification (incoming)
    10.1. The incoming operator physically inspects the control panel and verifies indicator states against the outgoing operator’s checklist.  
    10.2. Incoming operator independently confirms the coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 if these were cited in the log, and signs the verification entry.

11. Step 6 — Risk items and escalation
    11.1. Identify and list any unresolved safety risks or process risks. For any issue affecting quality, notify Quality per QS-PROC-06.  
    11.2. If a mechanical hazard is identified that cannot be immediately mitigated, escalate to maintenance and reference MM-P2-L1-SB03 for raising a corrective work order.

Rationale and background
12. Consistent, face-to-face handovers reduce miscommunication and prevent latent failures from propagating between shifts. Recording measured values for critical systems (for example the coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min and the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is 50 N·m) ensures that incoming operators have actionable verification points rather than subjective descriptions. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-02 for role definitions and QS-PROC-06 for non-conformance handling.

Examples and acceptable entries
13. Example shift log entries:
    13.1. "EQ-P2-L1-IH02: Coil cooling water measured 60 L/min at 07:45; no trips. See entry #42."  
    13.2. "EQ-P2-L1-SB03: Liner bolts checked and torque recorded at 50 N·m; no abnormal noise observed."  
    13.3. "EQ-P2-L1-RR01: Minor slip observed, cleared; monitor feed rate."

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following records attached to the shift log:
    14.1. Signed handover checklist.  
    14.2. Measurement logs for critical items (coil cooling water, liner bolt torque confirmation).  
    14.3. Copies of any MM-P2-L1-SB03 work orders opened or closed during the shift.  
    14.4. Quality reports referencing QS-PROC-06 when applicable.

Sign-off
15. Both outgoing and incoming personnel must sign and date the handover checklist. The lead operator or supervisor must co-sign to acknowledge receipt of all critical items and confirm that any safety or quality escalations have been actioned or assigned. Store the signed checklist with the shift log in the document control system.

Audit and compliance
16. Routine audits will sample handover checklists to validate compliance with this SOP and cross-check entries against MM-P2-L1-SB03 and QS-PROC-06 records. Non-compliance will be handled per QS-PROC-06.

Revision history
17. Revision history and changes must be recorded in the document control system per SOP-P2-L1-02.
