text:
# SOP-P2-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03  
Related: ECN-2026-045, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-02

Purpose
1. Establish the controlled startup procedure for the Heat Treat line at P2-L4 to ensure safe, repeatable preparation of equipment prior to production, preserve product metallurgical requirements, and document readiness for operations.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance technicians, and shift leads responsible for EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 during initial daily startup, post-maintenance returns, and changeover into Heat Treat mode. See SOP-P2-L4-02 for shutdown and changeover steps.

Preconditions
3. Equipment maintenance status must be confirmed in the maintenance log and match the workpack. Confirm there are no outstanding hold tags on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, or EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Review ECN-2026-045 for recent engineering changes that affect startup sequence. Confirm utilities are available and stable per plant control room communication. Verify required lubricants and consumables are staged per SB-1007.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for startup:
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Heat-resistant glove set per plant PPE matrix.
   - Steel-toe footwear.
   - Hearing protection (insert provided by plant).
   - Flame-retardant jacket as required when in proximity to furnaces.

Lubricants and consumables
5. Confirm lubricant stock and application points:
   - The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450.
   - The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723.
   Apply only specified lubricants to their intended reservoirs and tag the return on the MRO ticket.

Background and rationale
6. The Heat Treat line contains sequential mechanical and thermal stages; mechanical alignment and lubrication affect metallurgical outcomes downstream. Proper startup reduces risk of equipment damage, scrap, and safety incidents. This SOP aligns with engineering change ECN-2026-045 and lubrication guidance in SB-1007.

Startup steps (numbered sequence)
7. Step 1 — Pre-start visual inspection
   - Walk the line and inspect EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 for physical damage, loose guarding, leaks, or foreign objects.
   - Verify furnace doors and safety interlocks are not bypassed and are in the closed/tested position.
   - Record observations in the Startup Checklist.

8. Step 2 — Verify documentation and permits
   - Confirm the machine log and permit to operate are present and signed. Cross-reference recent entries against ECN-2026-045 for any procedure changes.
   - Ensure any outstanding work orders are cleared or approved for operations.

9. Step 3 — Lubrication verification
   - Verify reservoir levels and condition against manufacturer sight gauges and the lubrication schedule in SB-1007.
   - Replenish only with the specified lubricants: CFW-LUB-450 for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and CFW-LUB-723 for EQ-P2-L4-RR01. Document lot number and MRO ticket number in the equipment log.

10. Step 4 — Control system and interlock checks
    - Put the line control in the local test mode. Verify that E-stop circuits, door interlocks, and furnace safety interlocks register correctly on the HMI without disabling permissive logic.
    - If any interlock fails, stop and call maintenance. Create a work request and reference ECN-2026-045 if function was modified.

11. Step 5 — Power-up sequence
    - Energize mechanical drives and actuators following the control system prompts. Allow control PLCs and HMIs to complete their diagnostics.
    - Observe for abnormal noises, vibration, or alarm conditions. Log anomalies and halt further startup until cleared.

12. Step 6 — Dry run and alignment
    - Jog conveyors and feed mechanisms at low speed to confirm mechanical alignment and smooth travel of tooling. Verify references and zero positions shown on the HMI match the mechanical position.
    - If misalignment is observed, stop and perform corrective maintenance with lockout/tagout per SB-1007.

13. Step 7 — Heat-up procedure
    - Follow the heat-up steps defined in the furnace operating section of SOP-P2-L4-02 and record the sequence in the furnace log. Confirm preheat permissives and that furnace chamber atmosphere controls are active.

14. Step 8 — Trial part run
    - Run a controlled trial of production parts through EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HT02 without loading the downstream cell. Inspect trial parts for dimensional and metallurgical indicators per in-process inspection criteria.
    - Record trial results and decisions to approve or reject production start in the Startup Checklist.

15. Step 9 — Transition to production
    - When trial part results are acceptable and all logs are complete, the shift lead signs the Startup Checklist to authorize production.
    - Notify downstream stations that the line is in production-ready status and reference SOP-P2-L4-02 for any required changeover steps.

Examples and common failure modes
16. Example: If EQ-P2-L4-HP03 shows hydraulic reservoir foaming on first run, verify the correct lubricant CFW-LUB-450 was used and that reservoir vents are unobstructed. Document findings and tag the machine until resolved.
17. Example: If EQ-P2-L4-RR01 produces uneven rolls, confirm CFW-LUB-723 was applied at the correct greasing points and review alignment per Step 6.

Records to keep
18. Maintain the following records in the document control system and equipment binder:
    - Startup Checklist with signatures.
    - Lubricant MRO tickets showing CFW-LUB-450 and CFW-LUB-723 usage.
    - Trial part inspection reports.
    - Any maintenance work orders generated during startup.
    - Reference ECN-2026-045 and SB-1007 entries used during verification.

Training and competency
19. Only personnel trained on Heat Treat line startup and with documented competency per plant training records shall perform these steps. Review training records if unfamiliarity is observed.

Deviations
20. Any deviation from this SOP requires written approval from the P2 maintenance supervisor and must reference ECN-2026-045 for engineering authorizations.

Sign-off
21. Completion of startup is confirmed by signatures below. Signatures must include printed name, role, and time in the Startup Checklist.
    - Operator (print and sign)
    - Maintenance technician (print and sign)
    - Shift lead (print and sign)

References
22. Related documents: ECN-2026-045, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-02

Revision history
23. Maintain revision record in the document control header.

# SOP-P2-L4-02 Product changeover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Purpose
1. Provide step-by-step procedure for product changeover on the Heat Treat line (load, furnace, press) to maintain metallurgical integrity, repeatability, and safety.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance personnel performing changeover on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Follow referenced documents: ECN-2026-045, MM-P2-L4-RR01, SOP-P2-L4-03.

Preconditions
3. Only start changeover when production schedule authorizes change and ECN-2026-045 showing approved product configuration is available at the workstation. Verify incoming billets/forgings match ECN-2026-045 disposition before processing.

PPE
4. Required personal protective equipment for all personnel involved:
   - Cut-resistant gloves rated for hot handling tasks.
   - Heat-resistant face shield and apron when loading/unloading furnace or handling fresh parts.
   - Safety footwear with metatarsal protection.
   - Hearing protection in the RR01 and press zones.
   - Arc-rated clothing where indicated by SOP-P2-L4-03.
5. All PPE must be inspected per MM-P2-L4-RR01 before use and recorded on the maintenance log.

Safety limits and critical settings
6. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.
7. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar.
8. Do not override safety interlocks during changeover. Any attempt to bypass will require stop, lockout, and escalation to maintenance per MM-P2-L4-RR01.

Changeover steps (numbered sequence)
9. Prepare and verify documentation
   1. Retrieve ECN-2026-045 and confirm target material, process route, and any special instructions.
   2. Confirm prior-run records and batch IDs match handover sheet. Attach ECN-2026-045 copy to the changeover record.
   3. Notify downstream inspectors and quality that a changeover is starting; list expected checkpoints from SOP-P2-L4-03.
10. Isolate and secure equipment
   1. Stop feed to EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and confirm line empty per MM-P2-L4-RR01 isolation checklist.
   2. Place required lockout/tagout devices on electrical and hydraulic sources for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 before mechanical adjustments.
11. Clean and inspect
   1. Clean loading chutes, furnace chamber access, and press dies of debris and scale. Use approved wire brushes and vacuum extraction per MM-P2-L4-RR01.
   2. Inspect furnace elements and door seals visually; document any abnormalities on the equipment log. If abnormal condition present, notify maintenance and do not proceed.
12. Install tooling and fixturing
   1. Mount new die or carrier assemblies on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 following manufacturer mounting points; verify clamping interfaces are free of burrs.
   2. For rolling or feed fixtures on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, reference MM-P2-L4-RR01 for alignment tolerances and secure per its checklist.
13. Configure furnace
   1. Clear furnace program cache, then load program that corresponds to ECN-2026-045 for the new product batch.
   2. Confirm and document the control displays show the target austenitizing setpoint. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.
   3. Do not modify the setpoint without authorized ECN revision.
14. Configure press
   1. Verify hydraulic system pressure indications are within normal readiness range before release from lockout.
   2. Confirm the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar and ensure the pressure relief setpoints are not altered.
   3. Inspect hoses and fittings and sign off on the prestart hydraulic checklist.
15. Dry-run and verification
   1. Perform a dry-run with empty carriers through EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and without heat or material through the press cycle to verify mechanical timing and clearances.
   2. Run a single instrumented trial piece per SOP-P2-L4-03 sampling plan for metallurgical verification. Note: instrumentation must be installed and removed per MM-P2-L4-RR01 procedures.
16. Production release
   1. If trial piece passes inspection criteria and all checklists are complete, release the line for production. Attach trial piece results and ECN-2026-045 to the batch record.
   2. If trial piece fails, record failure modes, retain trial material, and initiate corrective action per SOP-P2-L4-03.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following documents in the changeover folder:
   - Copy of ECN-2026-045 used for this changeover.
   - Completed MM-P2-L4-RR01 checklists for RR01 and verification signoffs.
   - Furnace program save file and confirmation showing the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
   - Hydraulic prestart checklist and pressure verification showing the system pressure limit for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
   - Trial piece inspection report and any nonconformance records.
   - Operator and lead sign-off pages for this SOP.

Examples and rationale
18. Example: If ECN-2026-045 specifies a different alloy requiring alternate quench handling, the changeover must include the alternate quench container setup and documented training for operators. This prevents metallurgical defects due to improper cooling.
19. Rationale: Verifying furnace setpoint and press pressure limits ensures repeatable phase transformations and avoids over-stressing press components. Lockout and documented verification reduce risk of tooling damage and personal injury.

Deviations
20. Any deviation from this SOP requires documented management approval and a revision to ECN-2026-045 or an attached work instruction per SOP-P2-L4-03.

PPE and sign-off
21. Sign-off block (to be completed by responsible personnel)
   - Operator name / signature / time
   - Lead technician name / signature / time
   - Quality inspector name / signature / time
22. Final acceptance: Production Supervisor signs to indicate release complete and records filed.

Related documents
23. See ECN-2026-045, MM-P2-L4-RR01, SOP-P2-L4-03 for supporting procedures, tooling lists, and inspection criteria.

text:
# SOP-P2-L4-03 First-article inspection - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03  
Related documents: SB-1048, SOP-P2-L4-04, SOP-P2-L4-05

Purpose
1. Describe the procedure and acceptance checks for first-article inspection on parts processed through the Heat Treat line at P2-L4 prior to release to production.

Background and scope
2. This SOP applies to first-article inspections performed after heat treatment and finish operations on new jobs, process changes, or tooling changes for line P2-L4. Inspection verifies conformance to drawing characteristics, metallurgical process intent, and that downstream operations are within expected capability prior to batch release.

Critical system limits (do not exceed)
3. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar.
4. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before starting)
5. Production order and first-article request are approved and documented in the shop order record.
6. All required tooling and gauges are installed and verified against the tooling list referenced in SB-1048.
7. The heat-treat cycle has been completed and the workpiece has been processed through EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and, if applicable, EQ-P2-L4-RR01 or EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
8. A qualified inspector assigned to first-article tasks is available and trained to SOP-P2-L4-04 and SOP-P2-L4-05.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
9. Mandatory PPE for inspection tasks:
   - Safety glasses with side shields
   - Heat-resistant gloves for handling warm parts
   - Steel-toe footwear
   - Hearing protection in designated areas
Note: Use additional PPE as required by local plant safety rules and the job hazard analysis.

Tools and inspection equipment
10. Use calibrated dimensional gauges and surface inspection aids referenced in SB-1048. Verify calibration status prior to use. Record gauge ID and calibration status in the inspection record.

Procedure (stepwise)
11. Step 1 — Document review
    - Review the work order, the drawing, applicable process sheets, and SB-1048. Confirm that the part revision and machining/heat-treat routing correspond to the first-article request.
    - Rationale: Confirms baseline expectations and avoids inspecting to incorrect specifications.

12. Step 2 — Visual and surface inspection
    - Inspect the part from all sides for defects introduced during heat treatment: cracks, scale, distortion, or unacceptable surface condition.
    - Example: If a quench line is observed at a fillet or bore, mark location and proceed to metallurgical review before dimensional checks.
    - Records: Photograph defects and attach to the first-article report.

13. Step 3 — Dimensional inspection
    - Measure key features identified on the drawing. Log each measurement with the gauge ID and calibration status.
    - Rationale: Dimension checks verify that thermal distortion and forming operations remain within expected control.

14. Step 4 — Functional and fit checks
    - If the design requires assembly with mating hardware, perform a fit check using representative hardware or fixtures. Record fit condition as Pass/Fail and note any interference or looseness.
    - Example: Check concentricity with mating sleeve mounted to the reference surface described on the drawing.

15. Step 5 — Process parameter verification
    - Verify process records from the heat-treat cycle and downstream operations. Confirm that the recorded parameters match the approved process sheet.
    - Rationale: Process verification links observed part condition to machine and cycle performance, reducing risk of latent nonconformances.

16. Step 6 — Critical hardware checks
    - Verify that critical machine settings and fasteners related to the part are confirmed per equipment requirements. Ensure that the mandrel clamp bolt has been installed and torqued to the specified value for EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and that records reflect that action.
    - Note: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m.
    - Rationale: Proper clamping prevents mandrel slippage and dimensional failure during rolling.

17. Step 7 — Hydraulic and safety system verification
    - Confirm system health and safety interlocks for the hydraulic press used in heat treat handling. Where applicable, review maintenance records and pressure logs for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
    - Note: The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar.
    - Rationale: Operating within system limits is required for repeatability and safe operation.

18. Step 8 — Nonconformance disposition
    - If any characteristic fails, tag the part and initiate the nonconformance process per SOP-P2-L4-05. Do not return the part to production until disposition is approved.
    - Records: Complete nonconformance report and link to first-article record.

19. Step 9 — Approval for pilot production
    - If the part meets all checked characteristics, sign off on the first-article inspection form and authorize a controlled pilot run. Document any recommended process adjustments.

Records to keep
20. Maintain the following records in the document control system:
    - First-article inspection report, including dimensional data sheets, photographs, and fit-check notes.
    - Gauge IDs and calibration certificates referenced in the inspection.
    - Heat-treat and equipment process logs for EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-RR01, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
    - Any nonconformance reports and dispositions per SOP-P2-L4-05.
    - Reference to SB-1048 for tooling and gauge requirements.

Rationale and examples
21. The combination of visual, dimensional, and process verification reduces the probability of latent defects reaching downstream operations. Example: a small mandrel slip during radial rolling can produce out-of-tolerance keyway dimensions; mandrel torque verification and fit checks catch this before batch release.

Roles and responsibilities
22. Inspector — Execute steps, record results, and sign the first-article inspection form.
23. Process engineer — Review inspection results for process adjustments and approve pilot production.
24. Maintenance — Provide calibration certificates and confirm critical equipment limits per equipment logs.

Sign-off
25. Inspector name / signature / date
26. Process engineer name / signature / date
27. Manufacturing manager name / signature / date

References
28. SB-1048
29. SOP-P2-L4-04
30. SOP-P2-L4-05

Revision notes
31. See document control for revision history and change justification.

text:
# SOP-P2-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03  

Purpose
This procedure defines the required actions, checks, and records for shift-to-shift handover on the Heat Treat line to maintain product quality, machine integrity, and safety continuity. It applies to operators, lead technicians, and maintenance staff assigned to P2-L4. See related documents ECN-2026-042, SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-01 for engineering changes, safety bulletins, and upstream receiving handover references.

Background and rationale
A structured handover reduces the risk of lost information, missed maintenance items, and process drift. The Heat Treat line contains multiple assets with tight mechanical interfaces. Explicit verification of critical fastener torques and process readiness at shift change prevents component loosening and misalignment that can lead to quality escapes or equipment damage. Examples: confirm radial ring rolling mill mandrel clamp torque after clamp servicing; confirm hydraulic press main ram anchorage after die changes.

Required records and permanence
- Shift Handover Log: operator name in, operator name out, time in/out, summary of condition, anomalies, corrective actions taken.
- Equipment Status Tags: attach or update tags on EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03 if equipment is in abnormal state.
- Torque Verification Record: record verified torque values and verifier initials when relevant fasteners are checked.
All records shall be retained according to document retention rules in SOP-P2-L4-01 and filed to the line binder and electronic document control per ECN-2026-042.

Prerequisites (must be satisfied before handover)
1. Incoming operator has completed required qualifications listed in SOP-P2-L4-01 and read applicable sections of SB-1016.
2. Any in-progress maintenance must be documented on the Maintenance Work Order and handed over directly between technicians if work will continue across the shift boundary.
3. All hazardous energy isolation points must be validated and documented in the Lockout/Tagout section of SB-1016 before any physical checks.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. At minimum, wear the line standard PPE as specified in SB-1016. This includes hearing protection, eye protection, steel-toe footwear, and gloves suitable for mechanical inspection tasks.
2. Use insulated gloves when handling or verifying electrical lockouts per SB-1016.
3. Use face shield when observing live operations that present splash, chip, or arc hazards as described in SB-1016.

Step-by-step handover procedure
1. Initial briefing
   1.1. Outgoing operator briefs incoming operator at the machine area with the Shift Handover Log visible.
   1.2. Discuss production status, parts in process, next order priorities, and any deviations from standard process parameters noted during the shift.
   1.3. Highlight any vendor parts, tooling, or consumables that arrived or were used and list the exact location.

2. Safety and energy state verification
   2.1. Confirm that all stored energy sources are identified and that status matches tags on energy isolation points.
   2.2. Verify that emergency stop circuits are functional by confirming resets have been performed and that no residual faults exist.

3. Equipment status and critical checks
   3.1. EQ-P2-L4-RR01: Inspect mandrel clamp assembly. Confirm clamp condition, absence of excessive wear, and verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m. Record verification on the Torque Verification Record along with verifier initials.
   3.2. EQ-P2-L4-HP03: Inspect main ram anchorage and surrounding frame. Verify the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Record verification on the Torque Verification Record along with verifier initials.
   3.3. EQ-P2-L4-HT02: Confirm heater elements and thermocouples report stable status in the operator interface and that any previous temperature alarms have been cleared and logged in the Shift Handover Log.

4. Process and product check
   4.1. Review last produced parts on the conveyor or in the inspection area. Confirm they meet dimensional and visual criteria and that nonconforming parts are isolated with correction notes attached.
   4.2. If an in-process lot is incomplete, state remaining quantity and next steps in the Shift Handover Log and verify setup for continuity.

5. Maintenance and parts
   5.1. Review open maintenance actions for the line and confirm priority items with maintenance planner per SOP-P2-L4-01.
   5.2. If spare parts or special tools were used, confirm replacements are onboard or ordered and update the log.

6. Communications and escalation
   6.1. Document unresolved issues and the recommended escalation path in the Shift Handover Log.
   6.2. For unresolved safety or equipment faults that could impact production or create an unsafe condition, contact maintenance and lead per SB-1016 immediately and log the contact.

Examples of typical handover entries
- "EQ-P2-L4-RR01 clamp torque checked; 525 N·m verified; no play detected; signed."
- "EQ-P2-L4-HP03 ram bolt torque verified 1575 N·m; frame inspected for cracks; none found; signed."
- "In-process lot # on skid; 10 parts remaining; continue next shift with current setup."

Rationale for torque checks
Torque checks on critical fasteners prevent progressive loosening under cyclic loading. Verifying the exact specified torque ensures clamping forces remain within the designed friction envelope, preventing mandrel slip or ram misalignment that could cause die failure or part rework.

Handover completion and sign-off
1. Both outgoing and incoming operators shall complete the Shift Handover Log entries, including a brief description of the equipment state and any actions pending.
2. The incoming operator signs to accept responsibility for the line and confirms that all required checks were performed or that pending actions were documented and communicated.
3. Retain completed log and Torque Verification Record in the line binder and scan to the electronic folder as required by SOP-P2-L4-01 and ECN-2026-042.

Audit and continuous improvement
Periodic audits of handover records will be conducted to ensure compliance with this procedure and to identify recurring issues. Findings will reference ECN-2026-042 for corrective actions and SB-1016 for safety-related observations.

text:
# SOP-P2-L4-05 Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Related documents: MM-P2-L4-HT02, SB-1007, SOP-P2-L4-04

Purpose
1. Provide a repeatable, auditable procedure for a planned shutdown of the Heat Treat line to perform maintenance, inspection, and safe isolation of process equipment. This SOP covers mechanical isolation, lubricant inspection, electrical lockout, purge/vent requirements, and preservation of equipment until restart.

Background and scope
2. The Heat Treat line includes the radial ring rolling mill (EQ-P2-L4-RR01), the heat treat furnace module (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and the hydraulic forging press (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). Planned shutdowns are scheduled to allow alignment, replacement of wear components, lubrication servicing, and to perform safety-critical inspections identified in MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SB-1007. This SOP applies to maintenance and engineering personnel responsible for those tasks and ends at the point of hand-back to operations for restart, which is governed by SOP-P2-L4-04.

Preconditions (must be verified before initiating step 1)
3.1. Work order or shutdown authorization is present and signed by Maintenance Supervisor.  
3.2. Production schedule confirmed and line isolated from upstream/downstream processes.  
3.3. Notify operations and safety teams per plant communication protocol.  
3.4. Required spares and consumables staged per MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
3.5. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723.  
3.6. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450.

PPE and barriers
4.1. Minimum PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves rated for mechanical work, steel-toe boots, and high-visibility vest. Additional PPE such as arc-rated clothing or respirator must be used when performing the specific task that requires it per local hazard assessment.  
4.2. Use barricades and tagout signs to physically isolate the work area from pedestrian routes.  
4.3. Hot work permits and confined space permits must be obtained and co-located with the work package if applicable.

Shutdown procedure (numbered operational steps)
5.1. Notify affected personnel and post signage at access points. Confirm communications with operations lead. Rationale: ensures single point of responsibility and prevents inadvertent energy application during shutdown.  
5.2. Stop production feed and drain inventory from the Heat Treat line per process team instructions. Verify zero material at machine infeed and outfeed points. Rationale: prevents material entrapment and enables safe access.  
5.3. Isolate energy sources: electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and process utilities feeding EQ-P2-L4-RR01, EQ-P2-L4-HT02, and EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Apply lockout/tagout devices according to company LOTO standard. Rationale: eliminates hazard from stored or residual energy.  
5.4. Depressurize and vent hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Verify pressure gauges indicate zero where present. Note: use purge lines provided on the equipment. Rationale: prevents accidental motion or release during maintenance.  
5.5. Disconnect and cap process utility connections to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 if it will be opened for inspection. Follow SB-1007 for furnace purge and inerting sequences when furnace access is required. Rationale: avoids combustion and contamination hazards.  
5.6. Secure mechanical locks or blocks on moving components for EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 to prevent unintentional movement. Rationale: positive mechanical restraint is required in addition to energy isolation.  
5.7. Inventory and document current lubricant state at all lubrication points on EQ-P2-L4-RR01 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Replace or top-up lubricants using the approved lubricants: the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-723; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450. Rationale: prevents premature wear and documents compliance with MM-P2-L4-HT02. Example: record bearing location, existing oil level, and new oil batch/part number.  
5.8. Perform required inspections and maintenance activities per the maintenance work order and MM-P2-L4-HT02 tasks list. Document torque values, clearances, and part replacements on the work order where applicable. Rationale: ensures maintenance meets design intent and is traceable.  
5.9. If welding, grinding, or hot work is performed on or near EQ-P2-L4-HT02, obtain hot work permit and follow SB-1007 procedures for fire watch and inerting. Rationale: control of ignition sources near heat treat equipment is critical.  
5.10. After maintenance is complete, remove tools and foreign material. Conduct a housekeeping inspection of the work area. Rationale: reduces foreign object risk during restart.

Pre-start checks and hand-back to operations
6.1. Reassemble guards and verify interlocks operate per SOP-P2-L4-04. Rationale: protects operators during startup and normal operation.  
6.2. Remove lockout/tagout devices only after verification that all personnel are clear and the maintenance lead agrees. Restore utilities in the sequence identified in the equipment manufacturer guidance and MM-P2-L4-HT02.  
6.3. Perform low-speed functional tests and observe for abnormal noise, leaks, or alarms. Escalate any anomalies to Engineering. Rationale: incremental testing reduces stress on systems and catches issues early.  
6.4. Complete the equipment test checklist and forward to Operations and Maintenance records.

Records to keep
7.1. Signed shutdown authorization and work order.  
7.2. LOTO tags and log showing responsible individuals.  
7.3. Lubrication records documenting that EQ-P2-L4-RR01 used CFW-LUB-723 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 used CFW-LUB-450, including batch/lot numbers where available.  
7.4. Inspection reports and parts replaced, referenced to MM-P2-L4-HT02 work items.  
7.5. Hot work permits and fire watch logs if applicable per SB-1007.  
7.6. Final hand-back sign-off form per SOP-P2-L4-04.

Examples and notes
8.1. Example entry for lubrication record: "EQ-P2-L4-RR01 bearing A: drained, inspected, refilled with CFW-LUB-723, batch 12345, tech J. Smith." Use the exact lubricant part numbers as required.  
8.2. Use the related documents for task-specific checklists: MM-P2-L4-HT02 for mechanical tolerances, SB-1007 for hot work and furnace safety, SOP-P2-L4-04 for startup and safety interlock verification.

Sign-off (to be completed at the end of the shutdown)
9.1. Maintenance Lead name / signature / date.  
9.2. Operations Lead name / signature / date.  
9.3. Safety Representative name / signature / date.

Revision control
10. All changes to this SOP must be submitted through document control with reference to MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SB-1007 where applicable.
title: Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P3-L1-01 Line startup - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: SB-1044, SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04

Purpose
This standard operating procedure (SOP) defines the required preconditions, personal protective equipment (PPE), step-by-step startup actions, verification checks, rationale, examples of common anomalies and required records for bringing the Hot Forge line up to production-ready status. This procedure applies to operators and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

Preconditions
1. Maintenance clearance and lockout/tagout completed per SOP-P3-L1-02.  
2. Preventive maintenance for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01 completed and documented in SB-1044.  
3. Tooling, material, and loading fixtures staged at the work point.  
4. Required consumables and lubricant on-site: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is CFW-LUB-278.  
5. Control system in local mode and interlocks confirmed functional per SOP-P3-L1-04.

PPE
- Protective gloves rated for heat handling and abrasion.  
- Safety glasses with side protection.  
- Face shield for operations at the blast cabinet.  
- Hearing protection per plant requirements.  
- Flame-resistant clothing when handling heated charge material.  

Startup Steps (numbered sequence)
1. Visual walkdown and area clearance  
   1.1. Confirm no tools, debris, or nonessential personnel are in the line path.  
   1.2. Verify guards and access doors are closed and latched on EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Rationale: guards prevent exposure to moving components and thermal hazards.

2. Utilities and systems check  
   2.1. Confirm air, power, and operational pneumatic/hydraulic supply indicators are present and within normal operating indications on local panels. Rationale: ensures actuators and controls will respond during startup. Example: if a supply gauge shows no pressure indicator, suspend startup and call maintenance per SOP-P3-L1-02.

3. Control system initialization  
   3.1. Place PLC/operator station in startup mode and perform the software boot sequence per manufacturer prompts. Rationale: proper initialization avoids false alarms and ensures correct interlock behavior.  
   3.2. Verify alarm log is clear of critical faults before enabling actuators.

4. Shot blast cabinet specific verification (EQ-P3-L1-SB02)  
   4.1. Confirm blast media bin is adequately filled and the media delivery path is unobstructed.  
   4.2. Inspect blast wheel liner and fasteners. If any fastener is suspected loose, torque to the required value: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Rationale: correct torque prevents liner displacement and wheel imbalance. Example: a slightly loose liner bolt can manifest as increased vibration; torque to specified value and recheck vibration after brief operation.

5. Heater and induction systems (EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01) checks  
   5.1. Verify heat source power enable interlocks and sensors report nominal status on the operator panel. Rationale: prevents applying heat without flow or cooling where required.  
   5.2. Confirm any cooling or quench circuits are active and free of leaks.

6. Dry run with no load  
   6.1. With PPE donned, run the line through its startup sequence without material loaded. Observe for unusual noise, vibration, smoke, or smells. Rationale: isolated verification reduces risk to product and personnel. Example: if a conveyor mis-tracks during dry run, stop and realign before loading.

7. Functional checks with sample load  
   7.1. Introduce a controlled sample part and run through the full process route. Verify part handling, indexing accuracy, and process cycle continuity. Rationale: confirms integration of subsystems under real load conditions.  
   7.2. Monitor quality indicators at process checkpoints; if defects are observed, halt production and follow troubleshooting per SOP-P3-L1-04.

8. Final go/no-go verification  
   8.1. Confirm all critical alarms are clear and historical errors resolved.  
   8.2. Notify line lead and production control that line is ready for production start.

Records to keep
- Startup checklist completed and signed. Include operator initials and timestamps.  
- Torque verification record for blast wheel liner bolts on EQ-P3-L1-SB02 recording the applied value: 65 N·m and the lubricant used: CFW-LUB-278. Store this record with PM documentation referenced in SB-1044.  
- Dry run and sample run observation log including anomalies and corrective actions.  
- Any maintenance work orders raised during startup referenced to SOP-P3-L1-02.

Step rationale and examples
- Torque specification example: Correctly torqued blast wheel liner bolts reduce the likelihood of liner failure and imbalanced operation which can cause downstream galling or bearing damage. Recording the applied torque and lubricant ensures traceability for future failure analysis.  
- Dry run rationale example: Running equipment unloaded allows detection of misalignment and loose components without risking parts or process contamination. Common anomalies include loose fasteners, belt tracking issues, and sensor misreads; each should be documented and remediated prior to production.

Abnormal conditions and escalation
- If any critical interlock fails to reset, stop the startup sequence and engage maintenance following SOP-P3-L1-02.  
- If vibration or thermal anomalies persist after corrective action, tag the equipment out and notify engineering per SOP-P3-L1-04.

Sign-off
- Operator name and signature: _______________________  
- Shift supervisor name and signature: _______________________  
- Maintenance verifier name and signature: _______________________  

Retain completed SOP and attached records according to plant document control policy and file with SB-1044 documentation.
title: Line startup - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P3-L1-02 Product changeover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-IH03, SB-1027

Purpose
This procedure defines the required actions, responsibilities, and records for a product changeover on the Hot Forge line to ensure safe, repeatable, and documented transition between billet lots and product families. It applies to the equipment listed above and references control and maintenance requirements in ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-IH03, and SB-1027.

Background and rationale
Changeovers on the Hot Forge line present risks to product quality and equipment integrity if heater, lubrication, or blanking/sizing systems are not set and verified. The Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) must be confirmed to the target billet temperature to meet material flow and grain refinement objectives. Hydraulic press lubrication must use the approved lubricant to prevent premature wear and preserve die life. This SOP standardizes critical verification points and the records required for production traceability and audit.

Preconditions
1. Production leader has approved the upcoming changeover via the line scheduling system and confirmed billet lot release.  
2. All operators and technicians assigned to the changeover are trained and authorized for Hot Forge changeovers.  
3. Lockout/tagout clearance has been obtained where required for access to guarding and tooling, in accordance with plant LOTO policy.  
4. Required materials and consumables are staged: replacement dies, die lubricant, blanking inserts, and the lubricant CFW-LUB-927 for EQ-P3-L1-HP01.  
5. Maintenance has confirmed no active work orders prohibit operation of EQ-P3-L1-IH03, EQ-P3-L1-HP01, or EQ-P3-L1-SB02.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Heat-resistant gloves rated for forging operations.  
2. Face shield and safety glasses.  
3. Hearing protection for operators on the line.  
4. Flame-resistant clothing in accordance with plant PPE policy.  
5. Cut-resistant gloves for die handling.

Procedure (numbered steps)
1. Prepare for shutdown and isolate product flow. Rationale: prevents mixed-lot billets entering the heater or press during changeover and maintains traceability. Example: confirm upstream material feed is secured and tagged. Record: material lot tag attached to feed conveyor and noted on the changeover checklist.

2. Verify and document heater setpoint and actual condition for EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Rationale: ensuring target billet temperature before forging preserves metallurgical properties. Action: confirm that the operator interface and the physical thermometer/readout indicate the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C. Record: print or photograph the heater readout and log the confirmation on the changeover checklist; cross-reference to MM-P3-L1-IH03 for calibration trace.

3. Inspect and install tooling on EQ-P3-L1-HP01 and EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Rationale: proper die seating reduces the risk of flash defects and die damage. Action: verify dies are free of foreign material, correctly oriented, and torqued per die carrier documentation (see SB-1027 for die clamping guidance). Record: tooling inspection form with signatures.

4. Confirm lubricant and lubrication points for EQ-P3-L1-HP01. Rationale: correct lubricant prevents scuffing and protects hydraulic components. Action: verify the lubricant part number for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is CFW-LUB-927 and that the reservoir contains the specified product. Record: attach supplier batch label and lot to the changeover checklist and record reservoir top-up action.

5. Run dry cycle checks without billet feed. Rationale: validate mechanical movements, blanking sequence, and safety interlocks prior to introducing heated material. Action: execute cycle at low stroke/pilot settings as per operator panel and confirm correct sequence for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 and EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Record: dry cycle log entry and any fault codes; reference ECN-2026-006 if sequence changes are required.

6. Introduce a single trial billet and perform initial production verification. Rationale: confirm process stability, dimensional accuracy, and surface condition before full production. Action: feed one billet heated in EQ-P3-L1-IH03 at the confirmed target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C and run through press and sizer. Inspect the first forged part for critical dimensions and surface condition. Record: attach first-part inspection report to the batch record.

7. Quality confirmation and approval to run. Rationale: prevents production of nonconforming product. Action: Quality signs the changeover checklist approving parts for full production only after visual and dimensional acceptance. Record: signed changeover checklist and signed first-part report.

8. Monitor initial production and document stability. Rationale: short-term monitoring captures drift or intermittent issues. Action: log process observations and any deviations on the shift run log. If deviations occur, stop the line and follow nonconformance protocol. Record: run log entries and any corrective action records with references to ECN-2026-006 for required engineering changes.

Examples of common changeover issues and responses
- Heater drift from target temperature: reference MM-P3-L1-IH03 and notify Maintenance; suspend feeding until resolved.  
- Die misalignment producing flash variation: stop press, reseat dies per SB-1027, and repeat steps 3–6.  
- Lubricant mismatch detected: quarantine supply, replace with CFW-LUB-927, and document supplier lot.

Records to keep
1. Changeover checklist signed by operator, supervisor, and Quality.  
2. Heater readout confirmation and calibration reference to MM-P3-L1-IH03.  
3. First-part inspection report and sample photograph.  
4. Lubricant batch label and confirmation that CFW-LUB-927 was installed into EQ-P3-L1-HP01.  
5. Dry cycle and initial run logs, including any fault codes and corrective actions.  
6. Any ECN-2026-006 documentation invoked during the changeover.

Responsibilities
1. Operator: execute steps, complete checklist, and perform first-part inspection.  
2. Maintenance: verify EQ-P3-L1-IH03 calibration and support heater issues, per MM-P3-L1-IH03.  
3. Quality: approve first-part acceptability and sign off the changeover checklist.  
4. Production supervisor: confirm preconditions and authorize resumption of full production.

Sign-off
Operator name and signature: ____________________  
Supervisor name and signature: ____________________  
Quality name and signature: ____________________  

Revision history and references
- See ECN-2026-006 for engineering changes affecting sequence or tooling.  
- See MM-P3-L1-IH03 for maintenance and calibration procedures for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.  
- See SB-1027 for die handling and blanking/sizing guidance.
title: Product changeover - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P3-L1-03 First-article inspection - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P3, line P3-L1
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03
Related documents: ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-SB02, MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the steps required to perform the first-article inspection for the Hot Forge line in P3-L1, verifying process readiness and part conformance prior to production release.

Background and rationale
2. First-article inspection validates the combined performance of induction heating, transfer, and forging systems and confirms material and tooling setup before full production. The critical control point for the heating subsystem is the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) which must reach 1260 °C. Achieving and documenting this target ensures consistent material flow and microstructure after forging and reduces the risk of downstream rework.

Scope
3. Applies to all first-article parts produced on P3-L1 using EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Does not replace routine in-process inspection requirements in MM-P3-L1-SB02 or maintenance directions in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.

Preconditions
4. Verify the following before starting:
   - Engineering change notices affecting the part or tooling have been reviewed: ECN-2026-006.
   - Machine maintenance applicable to EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01 has been completed per MM-P3-L1-SB02 and MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
   - Tooling and dies installed are the approved configuration for the part number under review.
   - Lubrication for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) uses part number CFW-LUB-927.
   - Calibration status of measurement instruments is current and traceable.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
5. Mandatory PPE for all personnel in the hot forge area:
   - Heat-resistant gloves and arm guards.
   - Face shield with thermal protection.
   - Flame-retardant apron or jacket.
   - Safety footwear rated for impact and molten metal splash.
   - Hearing protection as required in the forge area.

Responsibilities
6. Operator: execute process steps and collect inspection data.
7. Quality inspector: perform dimensional and metallurgical checks, verify records.
8. Shift supervisor: authorize first-article approval or hold.
9. Maintenance: support adjustments and corrective action if equipment deviation occurs.

Procedure — numbered steps
10. Prepare the line
   10.1 Confirm preconditions and PPE per Sections 4 and 5.
   10.2 Verify tooling and die part numbers visually and against routing paperwork.
   10.3 Record ambient conditions and instrument identifiers on the first-article checklist.

11. Load and heat billet
   11.1 Confirm material identity and mill certifications match the job ticket.
   11.2 Load a billet into EQ-P3-L1-IH03 following standard transfer protocols for P3-L1.
   11.3 Initiate the induction heating cycle for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and monitor temperature controls.
   11.4 Verify the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C and record the measured value(s) and instrument ID on the checklist.
   Rationale: Reaching 1260 °C ensures the billet attains the required forging temperature window for material flow and metallurgical properties.

12. Transfer and pre-form inspection
   12.1 Transfer the heated billet to the transfer system EQ-P3-L1-SB02.
   12.2 Inspect the billet visually for surface condition, scale, and alignment prior to pressing.
   12.3 Confirm transfer timing and orientation meet die entry requirements and document any deviation.

13. Forge cycle and part capture
   13.1 Position billet in Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01).
   13.2 Ensure lubrication applied to tools is CFW-LUB-927 and document lot or batch identifier associated with the lubricant.
   13.3 Execute the first forge stroke(s) to produce the first-article part.
   13.4 Capture the part and record any observed issues during forming (flash distribution, die fill, surface defects).

14. Inspection and verification
   14.1 Perform dimensional measurements against engineering drawings and record results on the first-article inspection form.
   14.2 Conduct metallurgical checks required by the part specification and record sample IDs and results.
   14.3 If nonconformances are found, tag the part and initiate containment and notification per ECN-2026-006.

15. Examples and acceptance criteria
   15.1 Example documentation entries: list of dimensions measured, instrument serial numbers, temperature reading annotated as 1260 °C for EQ-P3-L1-IH03, lubricant lot tied to CFW-LUB-927.
   15.2 Acceptance is granted when dimensional and metallurgical results conform to the drawing, the temperature reading for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 is recorded as 1260 °C, and no critical process deviations are open.

Records to keep
16. Mandatory records to be retained in the document control system:
   - Completed first-article inspection checklist and signed copy.
   - Temperature log showing EQ-P3-L1-IH03 reading of 1260 °C.
   - Lubricant usage record specifying CFW-LUB-927 and batch/lot traceability.
   - Dimensional inspection sheets and metallurgical test reports.
   - Any related nonconformance reports and corrective actions referencing ECN-2026-006.

Deviations and corrective action
17. If the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 temperature does not reach 1260 °C or stability cannot be achieved, stop the first-article run and notify maintenance. Record the event and reference MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 for maintenance escalation.

Sign-off
18. Signatures required before production release:
   18.1 Operator signature and date.
   18.2 Quality inspector signature and date.
   18.3 Shift supervisor signature and date authorizing release to production.

Appendix — references
19. Referenced documents: ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-SB02, MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
title: First-article inspection - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P3-L1-04 Shift handover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, MM-P3-L1-IH03, SOP-P3-L1-02

Purpose
1. Provide a standardized procedure for shift-to-shift handover on the Hot Forge line to ensure continuity of safe production, equipment integrity, and quality traceability.

Background and rationale
2. Proper handover prevents production interruptions and reduces the risk of equipment damage and quality escapes. The Hot Forge line contains the hydraulic forging press (EQ-P3-L1-HP01), the scraper/breakout station (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), and the induction billet heater (EQ-P3-L1-IH03). Critical conditions and recent maintenance actions must be communicated in a concise, verifiable format. Maintenance follow-up and operator awareness are required to preserve prior preventive actions documented in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 and MM-P3-L1-IH03, and to align with plant procedures in SOP-P3-L1-02.

Preconditions (must be met before handover begins)
3. Incoming operator has reviewed latest production order and quality hold tags.  
4. Outgoing operator has completed and signed all entries in the line log and maintenance request forms.  
5. Any active isolations or lockouts are documented per SOP-P3-L1-02 and clearly displayed at the equipment.  
6. Critical equipment status updates from recent maintenance are available from MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 and MM-P3-L1-IH03.

Required PPE
7. All participants must wear required line PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, flame-resistant clothing, and safety footwear. If maintenance personnel are present, they must also use any additional PPE mandated by MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 or MM-P3-L1-IH03.

Step-by-step handover procedure
8. Start: Conduct the handover at the designated line control point. Limit interruptions and use the standard handover checklist.

9. Operational status report (outgoing operator)
   9.1. Confirm current process step and part family running.  
   9.2. Report any deviations or quality holds, including sample location, serial identifiers, and containment actions taken.  
   9.3. Report production counts and scrap disposition recorded in the line log.

10. Equipment condition and alerts
   10.1. EQ-P3-L1-HP01: Report mechanical status, recent alarms, and whether a maintenance action from MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 is outstanding. Include confirmation of critical fastener condition: the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. State whether the bolt torque has been verified and by whom.  
   10.2. EQ-P3-L1-IH03: Report electrical and cooling status and any interlock events; include process-critical coolant parameter: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Confirm measured flow and whether any maintenance from MM-P3-L1-IH03 is pending.  
   10.3. EQ-P3-L1-SB02: Report mechanical condition and any material handling issues, and confirm no jam conditions remain.

11. Process parameters and records
   11.1. Review the last run sheet and note any nonconformances recorded. Reference SOP-P3-L1-02 for escalation steps when out-of-spec conditions persist.  
   11.2. Confirm calibration status of measuring equipment used during the shift and note any out-of-calibration instruments referenced in the line log.

12. Maintenance and corrective actions
   12.1. List any open work orders and their status. Cross-reference maintenance documentation by id: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 and MM-P3-L1-IH03.  
   12.2. If an isolation is in place, confirm planned removal and responsible technician. Ensure the isolation record is available for the incoming shift to review.

13. Safety and housekeeping
   13.1. Confirm that housekeeping items on the line are addressed, including removal of loose debris and cleanup of spills.  
   13.2. Confirm that all guards and barriers are in place and functional. Note any temporary measures for which a follow-up corrective action exists.

14. Examples of concise handover statements
   14.1. “EQ-P3-L1-HP01: Ran part family X; encountered hydraulic pressure trip twice; main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m and was checked at start of shift by J. Smith; open work order for hydraulic leak.”  
   14.2. “EQ-P3-L1-IH03: Coil cooling flow recorded at shift end; The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min and current measured flow is within acceptable range; no interlock trips.”

15. Incoming operator actions
   15.1. Review all items reported by outgoing operator. Verify critical conditions physically before assuming process control.  
   15.2. Acknowledge understanding of open issues and immediate priorities; request clarifications as needed.  
   15.3. Update the line log to reflect acceptance of handover and any additional notes.

Records to keep
16. Line log: complete entries for production counts, quality holds, nonconformances, and signature blocks for outgoing and incoming operators.  
17. Equipment verification records: torque verification records for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 as referenced in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1; cooling flow verification for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 as referenced in MM-P3-L1-IH03.  
18. Work orders: copies or references to open maintenance requests and completion confirmations.  
19. Handover checklist: completed checklist retained with line documentation and entered into the document control system per SOP-P3-L1-02.

Escalation
20. If any critical parameter cannot be verified or an unresolved safety hazard exists, stop the line and follow escalation in SOP-P3-L1-02. Notify maintenance per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 and MM-P3-L1-IH03 as applicable.

Sign-off
21. Outgoing operator name, signature, date, shift.  
22. Incoming operator name, signature, date, shift.  
23. Supervisor verifier name, signature, date, and any conditional remarks.

Audit and continuous improvement
24. Handover records will be reviewed during routine audits. Patterns of recurring issues should generate corrective actions and potential updates to MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, MM-P3-L1-IH03, or SOP-P3-L1-02.
title: Shift handover - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P3-L1-05 Planned shutdown - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SB-1033, SB-1044

Purpose
This standard operating procedure (SOP) defines the steps required to perform a planned shutdown of the Hot Forge line at P3-L1. It covers isolation, depressurization, mechanical and electrical lockout, and required inspections for EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. The procedure is intended to reduce risk during maintenance and to produce records suitable for compliance and maintenance planning.

Background and rationale
Planned shutdowns are controlled events to allow inspection, maintenance, and repairs on the forging line. All mechanical fastening, hydraulic system integrity, and safety interlocks must be verified when components are exposed for work. Specific critical values for the hydraulic press are noted below and must be observed during the shutdown and pre-start sequence to prevent damage and ensure personnel safety.

Critical values
- The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m.
- The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before initiating step sequence)
1. Maintenance work order issued and approved by line supervisor.
2. A completed risk assessment covering thermal, hydraulic, mechanical, and energy isolation hazards is attached to the work order.
3. Required spare parts and consumables identified on the work order are staged and accessible.
4. A responsible equipment owner is assigned and present during shutdown and startup activities.
5. All operators and maintenance personnel have read this SOP and the referenced documents MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SB-1033, and SB-1044.

Required PPE
1. Flame-resistant coveralls.
2. Safety glasses with side shields.
3. Cut-resistant gloves for mechanical tasks; insulated gloves for electrical work when electrical energy is present.
4. Steel-toe boots.
5. Hearing protection while in the active line area until the line is verified de-energized.
6. Face shield when performing any press disassembly or when pressurized components are exposed.

Sequence of steps (numbered actions)
1. Notify affected personnel and control room. Post a shutdown notice at the line control station and all access points. Confirm notification is acknowledged by control room operator.
2. Verify that the maintenance work order and attached risk assessment are present at the job site and that all attendees have signed the job briefing.
3. Stop production feed to EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and secure incoming material conveyors. Confirm material is removed from the immediate work area.
4. Isolate energy sources:
   4.1. Lock out and tag out electrical supplies feeding the Hot Forge line per site lockout policy. Ensure the electrical disconnects are physically opened and locked.  
   4.2. Isolate hydraulic power to EQ-P3-L1-HP01, confirm hydraulic control valves are in the closed position, and place locks on the hydraulic pump motor starter.  
   4.3. Bleed hydraulic pressure from the press circuit using the manufacturer’s bleed ports and return lines into an approved reservoir, observing the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar during the bleeding operation.  
   4.4. Verify pneumatic and other utilities are isolated and tagged.
5. Verify zero energy state:
   5.1. Attempt start via main control to verify inability to energize; do not operate any controls while personnel are in the danger area.  
   5.2. Use pressure gauges and indicator lights to confirm zero hydraulic pressure at the press.  
   5.3. Ground any stored energy components per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
6. Drain and secure fluids:
   6.1. Drain die cooling lines and hot-oil circuits where required into approved containers.  
   6.2. Label and contain drained fluids in accordance with SB-1033 and SB-1044.
7. Mechanical isolation and access:
   7.1. Remove guards and access panels only after zero energy is confirmed and locks are in place.  
   7.2. Support heavy assemblies with appropriate mechanical supports before unfastening. Verify support stability throughout the activity.
8. Critical fastener and component checks:
   8.1. When reassembling the press, verify the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Document torque readings in the job record.  
   8.2. Inspect hydraulic hoses, fittings, and seals for wear and replace per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
9. Inspections and repairs:
   9.1. Perform visual and dimensional checks on die faces, ram guides, and bolster surfaces. Record findings on the maintenance checklist.  
   9.2. Replace worn components and document part identifiers in the work order; reference SB-1033 and SB-1044 for cleaning and disposal of removed items.
10. Pre-start verification:
   10.1. Reinstall guards and verify all tools and loose items are removed from the work area.  
   10.2. Remove mechanical supports only after hydraulic pressure is restored and components are confirmed secured.  
   10.3. Restore hydraulic fluid to system and bring pressure up while monitoring for leaks; ensure the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is not exceeded during this step.
11. Functional test:
   11.1. Conduct single-stroke tests at reduced control settings while maintaining visual observation from a safe distance. Confirm correct operation and absence of abnormal noise or leaks before returning to full production control.
12. Return to service:
   12.1. Remove lockout/tagout devices in accordance with the site lockout policy after all personnel have cleared the area and the equipment owner approves restoration.  
   12.2. Complete the work order, attach inspection records, torque logs, and any deviation notes.

Records to keep
1. Completed work order with signatures of the responsible equipment owner and line supervisor.
2. Torque log recording the main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) as 1425 N·m and the technician who performed the torqueing.
3. Pressure verification log showing pressures observed during bleed and restart operations; attach any abnormality reports.
4. Visual inspection checklist and photos of critical components, stored per document SB-1033.
5. Fluid handling and disposal records referenced to SB-1044.

Examples and notes
- Example entry for torque log: Component: Ram main bolt; Value: 1425 N·m; Technician: [name]; Date: [job date].  
- If a pressure gauge indicates a trapped pocket above the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is present, stop and re-bleed per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.

Sign-off
1. Equipment owner: name, signature, date.
2. Line supervisor: name, signature, date.
3. Maintenance planner: name, signature, date.
4. Final start permit authorized by control room operator per site procedures.

Referenced documents
- MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1
- SB-1033
- SB-1044
title: Planned shutdown - Hot Forge line

text:
# SOP-P3-L2-01 Line startup - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-044, MM-P3-L2-RR02, SOP-P3-L2-03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled procedure for start-up of the Ring Rolling production line at P3-L2, including safe checks, mechanical verifications, and initial run monitoring to confirm readiness for production.

Scope
2. Applies to all operators, maintenance personnel, and line supervisors conducting line start-up for the Ring Rolling line using EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.

Preconditions
3. Line area clear of non-essential personnel and debris.  
4. Lockout/tagout completed and released per site LOTO rules. Refer to MM-P3-L2-RR02 for maintenance isolation steps.  
5. Required spares, tooling, and records on the work station: shift log, maintenance checklist, and start-up inspection sheet.  
6. Communication devices operational; verify radio channel assignment with supervisor.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
7. Mandatory PPE for start-up crew: safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear, high-visibility vest, and heat-resistant gloves if handling warm components. Additional PPE as directed by site safety rules.

Key parameter confirmations (required before energizing)
8. Verify guarding and interlocks fully engaged on EQ-P3-L2-RR02 and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.  
9. Verify emergency stop circuits and light curtains function. Confirm reset procedure is understood by all crew.  
10. Verify the following equipment-specific items:
   - The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
   - The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463.

Rationale and background
11. The blast wheel liner bolt torque value and lubricant part number are controlled to maintain shot blast performance and prevent unbalance or component loosening that could lead to equipment damage or production defects. Using the specified lubricant part number preserves material compatibility and viscosity required for bearings and seals. Refer to ECN-2026-044 for engineering change details affecting EQ-P3-L2-SB01.

Step-by-step start-up procedure
12. Ready checks
   12.1 Confirm preconditions in section 3 through 6 are satisfied.  
   12.2 Complete the pre-start checklist and attach it to the shift log.

13. Mechanical and electrical verification
   13.1 Visually inspect EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 for loose fasteners, foreign objects, and correct coupling alignment.  
   13.2 Confirm guard position switches read "closed" at the HMI before attempting any motor start.  
   13.3 Confirm the blast wheel liner bolts have been torqued to the documented value and that torque evidence is recorded on the inspection sheet.

14. Lubrication and consumables
   14.1 Confirm lubricant stock and that the lubricant used matches the documented part number; the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463.  
   14.2 Check reservoir and feed indicators per the lubrication checklist. Record fill status and batch code if available.

15. Control system checks
   15.1 Power HMI and verify communication with PLCs for all three equipment items.  
   15.2 Confirm alarm history is clear of active faults. If faults are present, resolve per MM-P3-L2-RR02 before proceeding.

16. Dry run
   16.1 Perform an unloaded dry run using manual jogs to verify motion, end stops, and speed control responses. Observe for abnormal vibration, noise, or heat sources.  
   16.2 If abnormalities are detected, stop and notify maintenance per MM-P3-L2-RR02. Document the condition and corrective actions taken.

17. Initial loaded run
   17.1 With a single test ring piece, initiate normal production sequence at conservative operational parameters as determined by the line engineer.  
   17.2 Monitor product geometry, surface condition after EQ-P3-L2-SB01, and process stability through EQ-P3-L2-RR02 and EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Use sampling examples specified in SOP-P3-L2-03 for initial inspection points.  
   17.3 Record all observations on the start-up run log, including any adjustments and rationale.

Records to keep
18. Maintain the following documents with the start-up package:
   - Completed pre-start checklist.  
   - Torque verification record showing confirmation of The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.  
   - Lubricant verification record showing The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463.  
   - Initial run log and sample inspection results.  
   - Any maintenance actions and parts used, referenced to MM-P3-L2-RR02.

Examples and acceptable outcomes
19. Example 1: Dry run exhibits minor bearing noise that dissipates after a brief run and temperature stabilizes; document and continue to loaded run.  
20. Example 2: Persistent vibration or abnormal noise; stop immediately, tag equipment out of service, and issue a work order per MM-P3-L2-RR02.

Deviation handling
21. Any deviation from this standard operating procedure or failure to meet the documented confirmations requires immediate stop and notification of the line supervisor. Document deviations on the deviation form and reference ECN-2026-044 if related to changed components or configuration.

Sign-off
22. Start-up completion requires signatures from the following roles, recorded on the start-up sheet:
   - Operator performing checks: name, signature, date, time.  
   - Maintenance verifier: name, signature, date, time.  
   - Line supervisor clearance for production release: name, signature, date, time.

Attachments and references
23. Attach the completed pre-start checklist, torque verification, lubricant verification, and initial run log.  
24. Refer to ECN-2026-044 for engineering changes, MM-P3-L2-RR02 for maintenance and isolation procedures, and SOP-P3-L2-03 for inspection sampling during production start-up.

text:
# SOP-P3-L2-02 Product changeover - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
This procedure defines the controlled steps required to perform a product changeover on the Ring Rolling line in P3-L2. It covers mechanical changeover, lubrication, heat-treat interface, safety preconditions, verification checks, and records to be kept. Refer to MM-P3-L2-RR02 for maintenance limits, SB-1041 for safety barriers, and SOP-P3-L2-01 for routine production startup.

Background and rationale
Changeovers on the Ring Rolling line require coordinated actions between the shear/blanking station (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), the radial ring rolling mill (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), and the heat-treat furnace (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). Proper sequencing prevents part damage, reduces downtime, and ensures metallurgical integrity. Key controls are tooling alignment, lubricant selection, and quench timing at the furnace. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930.

Preconditions (must be met before Step 1)
1. Production supervisor has approved changeover and logged the job in the shift board per SOP-P3-L2-01.
2. All affected operators and maintenance staff have read this SOP and the related maintenance document MM-P3-L2-RR02.
3. Safety barriers and lockout points as specified in SB-1041 are in place and verified.
4. Incoming material lot and part print are available and matched to the work order.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Mandatory: safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, and flame-resistant apron where heat exposure is expected.
2. Additional PPE specified by SB-1041 for tasks inside guarded zones.

Changeover steps (numbered sequence)
1. Stop production flow
   1.1. Notify line downstream and upstream about imminent stoppage.  
   1.2. Set conveyor and transfer controls to manual hold.  
   1.3. Verify zero parts in process between EQ-P3-L2-SB01 and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.

2. Lockout and isolation
   2.1. Apply lockout/tagout to electrical and pneumatic sources per SB-1041.  
   2.2. Verify isolation by attempting to actuate pertinent controls and confirming no motion.  
   2.3. Record lockout IDs in the changeover log.

3. Remove and inspect tooling
   3.1. Remove cutting and forming tools from EQ-P3-L2-SB01 and EQ-P3-L2-RR02 using the hoist and fixtures specified by MM-P3-L2-RR02.  
   3.2. Inspect tooling for wear and damage; measure against accepted wear limits in MM-P3-L2-RR02. If out of tolerance, tag tooling and initiate maintenance request.

4. Install new tooling and setup
   4.1. Install new or reconditioned tooling using the alignment fixtures.  
   4.2. Make mechanical alignment adjustments until visual and gauge checks align with the part datum. Rationale: precise alignment prevents eccentricity and reduces rework.  
   4.3. Tighten fasteners to the values specified on the tooling drawsheet (refer to MM-P3-L2-RR02).

5. Lubrication
   5.1. Confirm lubricant part number for EQ-P3-L2-RR02. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930.  
   5.2. Fill reservoirs and prime delivery lines following the pump-priming checklist.  
   5.3. Record lubricant batch and fill volume in the maintenance log.

6. Heat-treat interface and quench configuration
   6.1. Verify furnace recipe and quench system settings for the new part. Rationale: quench timing directly affects microstructure and dimensional stability.  
   6.2. Confirm the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L2-HT03. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds.  
   6.3. Validate quench actuation and interlocks with dry-run (no load) per MM-P3-L2-RR02.

7. Dry-run and trial parts
   7.1. Run a dry-cycle through EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 with safeguards engaged.  
   7.2. Produce trial parts and perform dimensional and metallurgical inspections as specified on the work order. Example: check ring inside diameter at the datum face and verify hardness profile per the part print.  
   7.3. If trial parts pass acceptance, authorize production ramp-up.

8. Production ramp-up
   8.1. Incrementally return controls to automatic and monitor first production pieces.  
   8.2. Maintain increased quality sampling frequency during first production run and record results.

9. Recordkeeping and documentation
   9.1. Complete the changeover checklist and attach trial part inspection results.  
   9.2. Enter lubricant batch, tooling IDs, lockout IDs, and furnace recipe ID into the electronic changeover record.  
   9.3. File the changeover record under the work order and reference MM-P3-L2-RR02 and SB-1041 where applicable.

Examples and common failure modes
1. Example: misaligned tooling resulting in increased scrap. Mitigation: verify alignment per Step 4.2 and re-check after first 10 pieces.  
2. Example: delayed quench leading to soft spots. Mitigation: confirm the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and monitor furnace interlocks during dry-run.

Verification and acceptance criteria
1. Trial parts meet dimensional and hardness acceptance criteria on the inspection sheet.  
2. No safety barrier bypass or unresolved lockout remains in place.  
3. Changeover log and electronic records are complete and signed.

Sign-off
1. Production Supervisor: print name, signature, and time in the changeover log.  
2. Maintenance Lead: confirm tooling and lubrication installation and sign the maintenance portion of the record.  
3. Quality Inspector: confirm trial part acceptance and sign the inspection report.

Related documents
- MM-P3-L2-RR02  
- SB-1041  
- SOP-P3-L2-01

Records to keep
1. Changeover checklist and electronic changeover record.  
2. Trial part inspection reports and hardness trace.  
3. Lubricant batch and tooling ID records.  
4. Lockout/tagout record per SB-1041.

Revision history and control
All changes to this document must be submitted through the document control process and reference MM-P3-L2-RR02 for any tooling or maintenance updates.
