text:
# SOP-P3-L2-03 - First-article inspection - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-017, SB-1015, SOP-P3-L2-04

1. Purpose and scope
   1.1 Purpose: Define the first-article inspection (FAI) sequence for parts processed on the Ring Rolling line for P3-L2, covering the shot blast cabinet, ring roller, and heat treat furnace to verify conformance to drawing and process requirements prior to production release.
   1.2 Scope: Applies to all first-article parts produced on EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03. This SOP controls inspection points, measurement methods, acceptance rationale, examples of nonconforming conditions, and records to be retained.

2. Preconditions (must be met before starting FAI)
   2.1 Engineering change notices and drawings applicable to the part must be current per ECN-2026-017.
   2.2 Equipment must be in reported-ready state in the maintenance log for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
   2.3 Consumables and tooling must match the part setup sheet referenced in SB-1015.
   2.4 Operator and inspector must have completed training per SOP-P3-L2-04.

3. Personal protective equipment (PPE)
   3.1 Mandatory PPE for all steps: safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves when handling parts, and steel-toe footwear. Additional PPE for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 operations per local heat safety posting.

4. Background and rationale
   4.1 Rationale: First-article inspection validates that process settings, tooling, and equipment interactions produce a part that meets drawing tolerances and metallurgical requirements. Inspection at each process checkpoint captures defects early, reduces rework, and documents traceability to equipment and consumables.
   4.2 Example: A blast media mismatch in EQ-P3-L2-SB01 can mask machining marks, leading to false positives at final inspection. Confirming the lubricant and media per control documents prevents downstream rejection.

5. Materials and references
   5.1 Lubricant for EQ-P3-L2-SB01: CFW-LUB-463.
   5.2 Reference documents: ECN-2026-017, SB-1015, SOP-P3-L2-04.

6. Procedure — overview
   6.1 Complete preconditions and PPE checks.
   6.2 Perform process verification and in-process inspection at three control points:
       - After shot blast in EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
       - After ring rolling on EQ-P3-L2-RR02.
       - After heat treat cycle in EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
   6.3 Document results on the FAI checklist and route for sign-off.

7. Procedure — step-by-step
   7.1 Setup verification
       7.1.1 Confirm part drawing and inspection criteria called out by ECN-2026-017 are available at the workstation.
       7.1.2 Verify that the shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L2-SB01 is loaded with the specified lubricant listed as CFW-LUB-463 and that media type matches SB-1015.
       7.1.3 Confirm tooling and chucking for EQ-P3-L2-RR02 per job setup from SOP-P3-L2-04.
       7.1.4 Record the equipment IDs and setup operator initials on the FAI checklist.

   7.2 Shot blast inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-SB01)
       7.2.1 Purpose: Ensure surface condition and cleanliness are acceptable for subsequent rolling and measurement.
       7.2.2 Inspect for media embedment, remaining scale, and uniform surface finish. Example defects: localized pitting from improper media, or residual scale obscuring features.
       7.2.3 If any nonconformance is observed, STOP the sequence and tag the part as nonconforming. Notify maintenance and reference SB-1015 for corrective actions.
       7.2.4 Record inspection results, visual observations, and corrective actions on the FAI checklist.

   7.3 Ring rolling inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-RR02)
       7.3.1 Purpose: Verify dimensional features produced by the ring roller meet drawing criteria.
       7.3.2 Measure critical diameters, radial runout, and section profiles as specified in ECN-2026-017. Use calibrated instruments and note instrument ID on the checklist.
       7.3.3 Evaluate part for physical defects such as laps, cracks, or non-uniform wall thickness. Example: a circumferential crack requires immediate containment and metallurgical evaluation.
       7.3.4 If dimensions or condition are out of tolerance, tag the part, capture measurements, and notify engineering for disposition.

   7.4 Heat treat inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-HT03)
       7.4.1 Purpose: Confirm thermal processing achieved required metallurgical properties without introducing distortion or scale beyond allowable limits.
       7.4.2 Note the process control point: quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 is 13 seconds. Ensure cycle logs reflect a quench delay at or below this value; any exceeded value must be documented and escalated.
       7.4.3 Visually inspect for scale, distortion, and quench cracks. Sample hardness testing per ECN-2026-017 may be conducted where specified.
       7.4.4 Record furnace batch ID, cycle comments, and post-heat-treat observations on the FAI checklist.

8. Acceptance criteria and disposition
   8.1 Accept when all dimensional and metallurgical checks meet the drawing and ECN-2026-017 requirements and when FAI checklist is complete.
   8.2 Nonconforming parts remain quarantined and documented per SB-1015. Engineering disposition required before release.

9. Records to keep
   9.1 Complete FAI checklist for the part, including equipment IDs, operator initials, instrument IDs, and findings.
   9.2 Shot blast media and lubricant verification showing CFW-LUB-463 usage.
   9.3 EQ-P3-L2-HT03 cycle log showing quench delay values and any deviations.
   9.4 All records retained per departmental retention policy and attached to the job traveler referenced in SOP-P3-L2-04.

10. Examples and rationale for common findings
   10.1 Example: If post-blast inspection shows media embedment, the corrective action is media replacement and revalidation of the part after re-blasting. Rationale: embedded media can act as a stress riser in rolling and heat treat.
   10.2 Example: If quench delay exceeds 13 seconds on EQ-P3-L2-HT03, the part must be flagged for hardness verification and metallurgical review. Rationale: delay beyond the maximum can alter hardenability and mechanical properties.

11. Sign-off and responsibilities
   11.1 Operator: complete precondition checks and initial the FAI checklist.
   11.2 Inspector: perform dimensional and visual inspections, record instrument IDs and findings, and initial the FAI checklist.
   11.3 Process engineer: review FAI package, confirm conformity, and provide final release signature on the FAI checklist.
   11.4 All signatures and dates must be recorded on the FAI checklist before parts are released to production.

12. Revision note
   12.1 This SOP references ECN-2026-017 for drawing updates, SB-1015 for shot blast consumable control, and SOP-P3-L2-04 for operator and process training requirements.

text:
# SOP-P3-L2-04 Shift handover - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-019, MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3, MM-P3-L2-SB01

Purpose
1. Define the standardized shift handover for the Ring Rolling line to ensure continuous, safe, and quality production. This procedure applies to operators, leads, and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.

Background and rationale
2. Shift handovers are a critical control point to transfer operational status, outstanding actions, and risk items. Clear and consistent handovers reduce restart time, avoid duplicate work, and preserve quality history. Examples of typical issues transferred: machine alarms, pending maintenance requests, material shortages, or off-spec parts in process.

Key equipment limits and constraints (informational)
3. The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm.  
4. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds.

Preconditions (must be completed before initiating handover)
5. Outgoing crew must complete all running checks on EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and ensure machine status is updated in the line log.  
6. All critical alarms must be acknowledged and documented; unresolved alarms must be listed with current impact and required actions.  
7. Any ongoing maintenance work must be reported and cross-referenced to MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3 or MM-P3-L2-SB01 as applicable.  
8. Quality hold parts or suspect parts must be segregated, tagged, and recorded; reference ECN-2026-019 for disposition guidance.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
9. Outgoing and incoming personnel will wear required PPE for the line: safety helmet, safety glasses, high-visibility vest, cut-resistant gloves, and steel-toe footwear. Follow site PPE policy; if additional containment or respiratory PPE is needed for specific material conditions, note this in the handover log and reference the relevant work instruction.

Handover steps (numbered sequence)
10. Outgoing operator prepares the handover summary:
   a. Complete the line status checklist for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03.  
   b. Log last part processed and current part at process hold. If part requires special handling due to size, include the related limit: The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm.  
   c. Record any excursions, including location, observed effect, and temporary containment actions. Use the quality hold tag and reference ECN-2026-019 for any engineering change impacts.

11. Incoming operator performs visual and functional verification:
   a. Verify machine power and guarding are in correct states.  
   b. Check that safety interlocks are reset and that there are no active emergency stop conditions.  
   c. Confirm the status of pending maintenance entries referenced to MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3 or MM-P3-L2-SB01.

12. Process-specific verifications:
   a. On EQ-P3-L2-RR02 confirm tooling configuration matches the active job and that bore/OD settings are consistent with the job traveler; be mindful of the 1415 mm outer diameter limit when loading material.  
   b. On EQ-P3-L2-HT03 verify furnace program state and that parts in feed are properly staged; confirm the quench system is ready and note the quench delay threshold: The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. If quench delay approaches or exceeds this threshold, record event and notify maintenance.

13. Material and inventory checks:
   a. Verify next-process material availability and any special handling requirements.  
   b. Record heat numbers, traveler IDs, and the location of segregated suspect parts.

14. Communication of open actions:
   a. List outstanding corrective actions with owner name, brief description, and current status.  
   b. For safety-critical or quality-critical holds, require verbal confirmation and written acknowledgement during sign-off.

Records to keep
15. Maintain the following records in the shift handover folder:
   a. Completed handover checklist and line log.  
   b. Alarm log extracts and photographs of any physical damage or abnormal conditions.  
   c. Tags for quality hold parts and disposition notes referencing ECN-2026-019.  
   d. Maintenance request references to MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3 and MM-P3-L2-SB01.

Examples and common scenarios
16. Example 1 — Material short: If billet supply to EQ-P3-L2-SB01 is insufficient, outgoing crew logs the exact location of remaining stock, last heat number, and scheduled replenishment time. The incoming crew confirms receipt and updates production plan. Cross-reference MM-P3-L2-SB01 for feeder adjustments.  
17. Example 2 — Heat treat quench alert: If EQ-P3-L2-HT03 has registered a quench delay approaching the allowed limit, note the event and immediately flag parts processed during the window for inspection. Use the exact quench delay maximum statement in communications.

Escalation and maintenance coordination
18. If an unresolved machine condition could affect safety or product integrity, escalate to line lead and maintenance. Reference MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3 for service-level details and ensure a maintenance work order is documented.

Sign-off
19. Outgoing operator signs and timestamps the handover checklist and provides a verbal briefing to incoming operator. Both parties must initial the line log entry. If supervisory acknowledgement is required, the line lead or supervisor signs after reviewing documented items.

Audit and compliance
20. Handover records will be retained per plant records retention policy. Periodic audits will reference ECN-2026-019, MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3, and MM-P3-L2-SB01 to verify compliance and traceability.

Revision control
21. This document is controlled under the plant document control system. Refer to ECN-2026-019 for approved changes affecting process limits or controls.

text:
# SOP-P3-L2-05 Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-044, MM-P3-L2-SB01, SB-1015

Purpose
1. Define the controlled planned shutdown sequence for the Ring Rolling line to perform maintenance, inspection, lubricant service, and safety verification for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Background and rationale for each major activity are included to support maintenance decisions and records.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before Step 1)
1.1. Production supervisor has authorized the shutdown and issued the work order.  
1.2. All in-process work has been secured and material staged per production hold procedures.  
1.3. Lockout/tagout kits and isolation plans are available and match the equipment IDs listed above.  
1.4. Required spare parts and consumables are staged: lubricants, seals, and filters as specified in maintenance master files. Note the lubricant part numbers: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463. Verify part numbers match order and receipt documentation before use.  
1.5. Notify maintenance, operations, and safety teams via the normal communications channel. Reference ECN-2026-044 for any configuration changes that affect the shutdown scope.

Required PPE (apply to all steps that involve equipment access or energized systems)
1. Hard hat, safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear, leather gloves rated for industrial use.  
2. Arc-rated clothing only if hot work or electrical troubleshooting is authorized by the electrical permit.  
3. Respiratory protection when entering confined spaces or when dust levels exceed routine work exposure per facility monitoring. Use SB-1015 for shot-blast specific respiratory controls.

Shutdown sequence and activities (numbered steps)
2. Lockout/Tagout and isolation
2.1. Coordinate with operations to isolate energy sources for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 following lockout/tagout procedures in MM-P3-L2-SB01. Explain rationale: full isolation prevents accidental startup during inspection and lubricant service.  
2.2. Verify zero energy state with qualified personnel. Record verifier names and time in the shutdown log.

3. External inspection and documentation
3.1. Visually inspect external guards, access panels, and cabling for damage or wear; document findings on the shutdown checklist. Rationale: early detection reduces repair scope and downtime. Example: note frayed cable insulation or missing fasteners and tag components for repair.  
3.2. Update the equipment condition entry in the maintenance management system and attach photographs where possible.

4. Lubricant service and reservoir work
4.1. For EQ-P3-L2-RR02, drain, filter, and refill lubricant reservoirs using only the lubricant identified by the procurement and inventory records. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. Rationale: correct lubricant viscosity and additive package are critical for bearing life and ring form accuracy. Record batch or lot number of the lubricant used on the service form.  
4.2. For EQ-P3-L2-SB01, perform any required chamber or capture-system lubrication using the approved product. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463. Rationale: shot-blast cabinets require lubricants compatible with abrasive media to avoid media contamination. Record quantity used and supplier lot number.

5. Mechanical inspections and corrective actions
5.1. Inspect bearings, couplings, and drive components per the maintenance checklist. Document any axial or radial play observed and list recommended actions. Rationale: uncontrolled play can affect ring geometry and cause catastrophic failure.  
5.2. Replace worn seals and filters; ensure disposal and replacement are documented per environmental procedures.

6. Hydraulic and pneumatic systems
6.1. Depressurize systems, inspect hoses and fittings for leaks, and replace components as required. Record serials or identifiers of replaced components in the work order.

7. Electrical systems and controls
7.1. With electrical lockout in place, perform inspections of motor terminals, control panels, and cable entries. Note any corrosion, loose terminations, or water ingress and record actions taken. Reference MM-P3-L2-SB01 for panel-level verification points.

8. Functional checks and leak test
8.1. After repairs and fluid fills, restore energy under controlled conditions with one qualified operator at the main panel and one safety observer at the equipment. Rationale: staged re-energization allows immediate response to anomalies. Document results, noting any abnormal noises, leaks, or control alarms.  
8.2. If alarms or unexpected behavior occur, return to lockout and troubleshoot. Attach findings to the maintenance record.

9. Housekeeping and component marking
9.1. Clean work areas, remove tools, and verify all guards and covers are reinstalled. Rationale: residual tools or debris increase incident risk.  
9.2. Mark replaced components with tag identifiers linked to the maintenance record.

Records to keep
10. Shutdown log with verifier signatures and times.  
11. Service forms showing lubricant part numbers and batch/lot numbers used. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is CFW-LUB-463.  
12. Photos of before-and-after conditions.  
13. Completed checklist and follow-up corrective action items entered into the maintenance management system and cross-referenced to the work order. Reference ECN-2026-044 for configuration changes and MM-P3-L2-SB01 for maintenance detail records.

Examples and rationale
13.1. Example entry: “Reservoir drained, visual contamination found, filter replaced, refilled with CFW-LUB-930, batch A123, no abnormal vibration; returned to service.” Rationale: concise entries expedite root-cause analysis if failures recur.  
13.2. Example nonconformance: “Shot-blast cabinet seal worn; lubricant contamination suspected; replaced seal, cleaned cabinet, refilled with CFW-LUB-463.” Provide corrective action and monitor for recurrence.

Sign-off
14. Final verification and acceptance
14.1. Maintenance lead, operations lead, and safety officer must sign the shutdown completion section of the work order, confirming that preconditions are met, inspections completed, and functional tests passed.  
14.2. Attach all records, photos, and parts receipts to the work order and file per document control. Reference SB-1015 for shot-blast safety verification requirements.

Appendix and references
15. Referenced documents: ECN-2026-044, MM-P3-L2-SB01, SB-1015 for supplemental procedures, change records, and safety criteria.
title: Planned shutdown - Ring Rolling line

text:
# SOP-P3-L3-01 Line startup - Machining line
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-016, MM-P3-L3-CN02, MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the required pre-start checks, startup sequence, and records for bringing the P3-L3 machining line into production for a single continuous run. It applies to all operators and maintenance staff assigned to EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03.

Background and rationale
2. Consistent startup reduces scrap, prevents equipment damage, and ensures operator safety. The specified lubrication, mounting hardware torque, and sequencing are keyed to the line mechanical layouts and the change notices in ECN-2026-016. Use of the correct lubricant and bolt torque prevents premature wear and structural loosening under load. Example: improper lubricant at the CNC turning center increases spindle temperature and tool wear; incorrect ram bolt torque at the hydraulic press can lead to misalignment and damage to the die set.

Preconditions (required before beginning)
3. Verify the following before any actions:
   - Plant electrical main feed is available and locked in the ON position by authorized control (operator key).
   - Compressed air and hydraulic supply to the line are in service.
   - Machine guards are installed and interlocks function.
   - Housekeeping: aisleways and work platforms around EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03 are clear.
   - Operators and maintenance staff are trained per MM-P3-L3-CN02 and MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Minimum PPE for startup personnel:
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Hearing protection as required by area signage.
   - Cut-resistant gloves for handling tooling and workpieces.
   - Steel-toe safety footwear.
   - Any additional PPE specified on local hazard assessment or job safety analysis.

Critical equipment-specific values (must be used exactly as written)
5. The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is CFW-LUB-611.
6. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m.

Startup sequence (numbered steps)
7. Step 1 — Pre-start inspection
   - Walk the length of the line and perform visual inspection of EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03.
   - Confirm guards and interlocks present and secured. Test interlock function per MM-P3-L3-CN02.
   - Check for leaks, loose fittings, or foreign objects in tooling areas. Address any deficiencies before proceeding.

8. Step 2 — Fluids and consumables verification
   - Confirm CFW-LUB-611 is the lubricant installed in EQ-P3-L3-CN02 lubrication reservoirs and lines per MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
   - Verify hydraulic reservoir levels are within acceptable visible range and filters are clean. Replace or top-up only with approved fluids; use MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for part approvals.

9. Step 3 — Mechanical torque verification
   - Verify main ram bolt torque on EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Adjust only if required and record outcome.
   - The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and document calibration ID in the startup record.

10. Step 4 — Power-up sequence
    - Energize control panels for each piece of equipment in producer-specified order to avoid load spikes: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, then EQ-P3-L3-CN02, then EQ-P3-L3-HP03.
    - Observe control HMI for any fault codes. If fault codes occur, reference ECN-2026-016 for approved corrective actions.

11. Step 5 — Functional checks
    - With machines powered, perform no-load functional cycles for each station:
      - Conveyor indexing and part stop actuation on EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
      - Tool spindle run-up and axis movement verification on EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
      - Ram approach and retract cycle verification on EQ-P3-L3-HP03.
    - Confirm emergency stops stop motion across the line; reset only after condition is cleared.

12. Step 6 — Low-speed trial (example)
    - Run a single-piece trial through the process using approved tooling. Visually confirm part capture, orientation, and tool-to-part clearance.
    - Inspect the trial part for dimensional integrity and surface finish per sample criteria in production pack.

13. Step 7 — Full run commencement
    - If trial acceptable, commence production with standard operating program. Monitor first 10 parts for any deviations. Escalate to maintenance if anomalies observed.

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following records in the document control system and the machine's logbook:
    - Startup checklist with initials and timestamps.
    - Confirmation that CFW-LUB-611 is installed (supply lot and container ID if available).
    - Torque verification entry for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 including technician name and torque wrench calibration ID.
    - Any fault codes and actions taken; reference ECN-2026-016 for corrective action traceability.
    - Trial part inspection results and disposition.

Examples and common findings
15. Example A — Lubricant mismatch: If lubricant other than CFW-LUB-611 is found in EQ-P3-L3-CN02, stop startup and contact maintenance. Record the discrepancy and tag the machine out until correct lubricant is installed and flushed as required by MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
16. Example B — Torque deviation: If main ram bolt torque differs from 1600 N·m, retorque to the specified value and re-run the no-load functional checks before resuming trial runs.

Escalation and hold points
17. Hold startup for any of the following until resolved:
    - Missing or failed safety interlocks.
    - Lubricant not CFW-LUB-611 at EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
    - Main ram bolt torque not at 1600 N·m and cannot be adjusted to spec.
    - Unresolved fault codes referenced in ECN-2026-016.

Training and competency
18. Only personnel trained per MM-P3-L3-CN02 and MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 may perform startup and torque verification. Supervisors must verify training status before authorizing startup.

Sign-off
19. Completion sign-off (to be filled in the machine log and retained for traceability):
   - Operator name and signature
   - Maintenance technician name and signature (if maintenance actions performed)
   - Date/time of startup completion
   - Confirmation entries: CFW-LUB-611 installed; main ram bolt torque verified at 1600 N·m; trial parts verified acceptable.
   - Reference to related documentation used: ECN-2026-016, MM-P3-L3-CN02, MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1

Revision history and notes
20. This procedure incorporates changes outlined in ECN-2026-016. For detailed maintenance methods and lubrication instructions, see MM-P3-L3-CN02 and MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
title: Line startup - Machining line

text:
# SOP-P3-L3-02 Product changeover - Machining line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled procedure for product changeover on the Machining line to ensure consistent setup, safe operations, and traceable records. This procedure addresses mechanical adjustments, hydraulic press maintenance checks, and lubricant verification required to bring the line from run-state to next product configuration.

Background and rationale
2. Changeovers are a primary source of variation and unplanned downtime. Standardizing steps reduces scrap, protects tooling and press components, and ensures operator safety. Sequence is structured to isolate energy, validate tooling, and verify lubrication and bolting critical to press integrity. Where press bolt preload is required, the specified torque must be applied and recorded to maintain press safety and alignment.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before beginning)
3. Line is in a completed production state and halted under controlled stop. Utility and lockout procedures are available from SB-1005 and SB-1010. Operators must have reviewed SOP-P3-L3-04 for material staging rules. All affected equipment present: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Required parts and tooling staged and matched to the next product.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE during changeover: safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection for near-press operations, and face shield when removing guards. Respiratory protection is not required unless specified by task-level hazard assessment.

Tools and consumables
5. Only use calibrated torque tools for fastener verification. Use the lubricant with specified part number for press lubrication. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-340.

Changeover steps (numbered sequence)
6. Step 1 — Prepare and communicate
   - Notify line lead and maintenance that changeover will begin. Post lockout tagout schedule per SB-1005. Confirm tooling list matches next product.

7. Step 2 — Isolate energy sources
   - Execute lockout/tagout on electrical supply and hydraulic isolation per SB-1005 and SB-1010. Verify stored energy is bled and locked. Confirm isolation at EQ-P3-L3-HP03 before any press work.

8. Step 3 — Remove product-specific fixtures
   - Remove and inspect fixtures and soft jaws from EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Clean locating surfaces. Tag and store fixtures in assigned bins for the next run.

9. Step 4 — Inspect press components
   - With energy isolated, inspect EQ-P3-L3-HP03 ram, platen faces, and fasteners for wear, cracks, or foreign material. Replace or escalate any discrepancy through maintenance per SB-1010.

10. Step 5 — Verify and set main ram bolt torque
    - Using a calibrated torque wrench, verify the main ram bolt torque at EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Apply the specified torque and record. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m.
    - Rationale: Correct bolt preload maintains ram alignment and prevents fretting and accelerated wear. Example: if bolt shows evidence of loosening, re-torque to the specified value and escalate for root-cause evaluation.

11. Step 6 — Lubrication
    - Confirm lubricant supply and fill points on EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Use lubricant with the specified part number. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-340.
    - Rationale: Using the specified lubricant ensures proper viscosity and additive package for high-load press components. Record batch or lot identifier for traceability.

12. Step 7 — Install new tooling and perform alignment
    - Mount new tooling to EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Use alignment gauges or mating references. Check for interference and clamp according to tooling manufacturer guidance.

13. Step 8 — Functional checks under low energy
    - Remove locks on control circuits only to permit single-cycle runs at reduced energy per SB-1010. Cycle press with verified guards in place to confirm motion and clearances. Observe hydraulic pressures and motion smoothness; any abnormal noise or drift requires re-isolation.

14. Step 9 — Trial production and inspection
    - Produce trial parts and inspect per product acceptance criteria. Record dimensional checks and any rework. If trial parts pass, proceed to full run following production release protocol.

15. Step 10 — Clean up and return to service
    - Remove tools not required for full production, restore guards, and return all lockout devices. Notify line lead and update production board.

Examples and decision guidance
16. Example: If during Step 5 retorque, bolt turns without achieving specified torque, mark as unacceptable and escalate to maintenance. Example: If lubricant batch tag is missing, quarantine supply and source replacement labeled CFW-LUB-340 before proceeding.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following records in the changeover log:
   - Operator name and signature.
   - Maintenance technician name and signature for torque and lubrication verification.
   - Record of torque application and tool calibration reference.
   - Lubricant part number and batch/lot identifier.
   - Trial part inspection results and disposition.
   - Any nonconformances and corrective actions.
   Store records per document control retention rules and reference SB-1005 for storage location.

Nonconformance and escalation
18. If any step cannot be completed to standard, stop the changeover and escalate to maintenance and production supervision. Use SB-1010 for mechanical repair workflow.

Training and competency
19. Only personnel trained on these procedures and on the specific equipment EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03 may perform changeovers. Training records should be maintained against operator personnel files.

References
20. See SB-1005, SB-1010, SOP-P3-L3-04 for related lockout, maintenance, and material staging procedures.

Sign-off
21. Operator signature: ______________________ Date: ______________________  
22. Maintenance signature (torque/lubrication verification): ______________________ Date: ______________________  
23. Production lead sign-off: ______________________ Date: ______________________

Revision history
24. Rev E current.

text:
# SOP-P3-L3-03 First-article inspection - Machining line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-016, MM-P3-L3-HP03, MM-P3-L3-SB01

Purpose
1. Define the controlled first-article inspection (FAI) workflow for parts produced on P3-L3 machining line. This procedure ensures the first part off a run meets drawing and process requirements before full production release.

Background and scope
2. This SOP applies to first articles produced on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03. It covers visual, dimensional, functional, and process-verification checks, equipment pre-checks, acceptance criteria review, and records retention. For maintenance-related tasks refer to MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01. For engineering changes consult ECN-2026-016.

Preconditions
3. The work order and applicable release documentation must be available at the workstation. The machine program and fixture setup must be loaded as released in the manufacturing system. The part drawing and inspection criteria must be referenced and verified against the latest release. The operator must have completed line-specific setup training and hold current qualifications.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, safety shoes, and any task-specific respiratory protection indicated by the plant safety officer. Ensure PPE is donned before entering the machining and shot blast areas.

Critical material and equipment references
5. Verify the lubricant and wear items for the shot blast cabinet prior to running the first article:
- The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709.
- The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 105 N·m.
6. Confirm tooling and gages are calibrated and their status is current in the calibration system. Use gage blocks and reference standards traceable to the calibration lab.

Step-by-step procedure
7. Step 1 — Pre-run verification
7.1 Confirm work order and part revision. Verify fixture orientation and clamping points. Check tool offsets and program match released operation. Validate coolant and chip management are functional.

8. Step 2 — Machine warm-up and dry run
8.1 Perform a dry run with fixture empty to verify program motion and collision clearance. Observe for abnormal sounds or interference. Correct any program or setup issues before inserting raw material.

9. Step 3 — First-article setup
9.1 Mount raw material and perform single-cycle machining to produce the first article. Record the program ID and operator initials in the run log.

10. Step 4 — Primary inspection at machine (operator)
10.1 Perform visual inspection for surface condition, burrs, and secure fastenings. Verify critical features with at-machine gages as specified on the drawing. Flag any deviations immediately and notify process control.

11. Step 5 — Shot blast and surface preparation
11.1 After primary inspection, move the first article to EQ-P3-L3-SB01 for shot blasting per the surface finish requirement. Verify that consumables and the lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is present and correct prior to operation.
11.2 Reinspect blasted surface for profile, cleanliness, and finish consistency.

12. Step 6 — Secondary inspection (QC)
12.1 QC performs full dimensional inspection using calibrated instruments. Record actual measurements against drawing tolerances on the First-Article Inspection Report (FAIR).
12.2 Functional checks include assembly fit with mating components and verification of critical form features. Document any out-of-tolerance dimensions with disposition recommendation.

13. Step 7 — Process verification and hold point
13.1 If the FAIR passes, QC signs the report and releases the lot for production. If any nonconformance is found, initiate containment and hold subsequent production until corrective action and revalidation are complete. Reference ECN-2026-016 for any engineering changes required.

14. Step 8 — Example nonconformance workflow
14.1 Example: If a critical bore diameter is out of tolerance, QC annotates the FAIR, tags the part as HOLD, notifies Engineering and Maintenance, and stops the run. Engineering evaluates if program correction or fixture adjustment is required. Maintenance performs mechanical checks per MM-P3-L3-HP03 or MM-P3-L3-SB01 as applicable.

Records to keep
15. Maintain the following records in the document control system:
- First-Article Inspection Report (FAIR) with dimensional data and signatures.  
- Machine program ID and revision log.  
- Tooling and gage calibration certificates or references.  
- Process setup photos showing tool orientation and fixture placement.  
- Any nonconformance reports and associated dispositions.  
Store FAIR and associated records per plant retention policy.

Rationale and acceptance criteria
16. The two-stage inspection (operator primary and QC secondary) reduces risk of latent defects entering bulk production. Operator checks catch gross issues; QC confirms dimensional and functional compliance. Acceptance requires all critical dimensions within tolerance and no functional failures. Any deviation must be resolved via formal ECN process when redesign or program change is necessary.

Responsibilities
17. Operators: execute setup, perform primary inspection, and document program and tooling used.  
QC: perform full FAIR, evaluate results, and authorize production release.  
Engineering: support disposition and corrective action for failed FAIs and issue ECN-2026-016 if design or program changes are required.  
Maintenance: perform mechanical checks and corrective maintenance per MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01.

Sign-off
18. Completed FAIR must be signed by:
- Operator (printed name and signature)  
- QC inspector (printed name and signature)  
- Production supervisor (printed name and signature)  
- Engineering representative (printed name and signature) if any nonconformance required disposition

Appendix
19. Examples of FAIR entries, gage checklists, and photo documentation templates are available in the document control folder associated with this SOP. Refer to ECN-2026-016 for change history and to MM-P3-L3-HP03 and MM-P3-L3-SB01 for maintenance procedures related to the equipment listed in this SOP.
title: First-article inspection - Machining line

text:
# SOP-P3-L3-04 Shift handover - Machining line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Purpose
This procedure defines the required activities, checks, and records for shift handover on the Machining line to ensure continuity of safe operation and traceability of actions when responsibility transfers between operators.

Scope
Applies to all operators, maintenance personnel, and supervisors responsible for EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03 on plant P3, line P3-L3.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-016
- SOP-P3-L3-01
- SOP-P3-L3-03

Background and rationale
Handover is a critical control for process safety and quality. Clear, consistent transfer of information prevents unintended machine states, missed maintenance actions, and production losses. This procedure aligns with line operating rules and preserves the asset condition of EQ-P3-L3-HP03 by ensuring hydraulic parameters and fasteners are verified within engineering limits before the receiving operator assumes control.

Key engineering limits to verify during handover
- The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar. Confirm pressure indicators and records reflect operation within this limit.
- The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Confirm torque verification has been completed and documented where required.

Preconditions
1. Incoming operator and outgoing operator are present and available for the handover discussion at the machine or control station.
2. Any open maintenance permits affecting the equipment are visible and available for review.
3. Control system logs and last-shift production and maintenance notes are accessible.

Required personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Safety glasses
2. Hearing protection
3. Safety footwear
4. Cut-resistant gloves (for handling tooling and fasteners)
5. High-visibility vest

Procedure - numbered steps
1. Initial location and introductions
   - Outgoing operator meets incoming operator at the designated handover point for the machine group.
   - Confirm names and roles for the shift-to-shift record.

2. Status overview
   - Outgoing operator provides a concise verbal summary of current line status covering production run, part program, tooling condition, and any abnormal events.
   - Highlight any incomplete tasks or deferred actions tied to SOP-P3-L3-01 or SOP-P3-L3-03.

3. Safety and lockout checks
   - Review any active lockout/tagout or maintenance permits. Confirm permits will be carried forward if unresolved.
   - Verify that safety interlocks and guards on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03 are in place and functional.

4. Hydraulic press verification (EQ-P3-L3-HP03)
   - Review last recorded system pressure and compare with the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar.
   - Confirm any pressure deviations were addressed and that corrective actions are documented.
   - Review torque verification records for the main ram bolt where the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Confirm evidence of verification is attached to the equipment maintenance log if required.

5. Tooling and consumables
   - Inspect tooling condition and confirm tool change status. Note any tool life concerns or pending replacements.
   - Confirm availability of critical consumables and that pick lists or requests are raised per procedures.

6. Control system and program state
   - Confirm active program or recipe and any parameters modified during the outgoing shift.
   - If abnormal parameter changes were made, document the reason and location in the log, and reference ECN-2026-016 if program changes are persistent.

7. Quality and inspection feedback
   - Review last inspected parts, any rejects, and corrective actions taken. Attach measurement records and traceability tags to the shift record.

8. Maintenance and defect reporting
   - Review outstanding defect reports and the status of corrective maintenance. Ensure priority items are clearly communicated.
   - If maintenance included torque checks or hydraulic interventions, ensure the receiving operator has the verification certificate or maintenance entry.

9. Examples of specific handover statements
   - "EQ-P3-L3-HP03 pressure nominal per last read; refer to pressure log and note that the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar."
   - "Main ram bolt torque verified; see maintenance log where the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m."

10. Documentation and sign-off
   - Both operators complete the shift handover form, noting any follow-up actions and attaching relevant logs or permits.
   - Outgoing operator initials the action items and incoming operator accepts responsibility by initialing the form.

Records to keep
1. Completed shift handover form with signatures and attachments.
2. Equipment logs for EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03 including pressure and torque verification entries.
3. Any maintenance permits or defect reports carried forward.
4. Quality inspection records and run reports referenced during handover.

Rationale for record retention
Maintaining these records ensures traceability for quality investigations, maintenance audits, and safety reviews. Linking changes to ECN-2026-016 and operational directives in SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-03 avoids undocumented deviations and supports root cause analysis.

Common issues and mitigations
- Incomplete handover notes: Use the handover form checklist to force completion of critical items.
- Missing verification evidence: Do not accept handover until key verifications for pressure and critical fasteners are present.
- Ambiguous responsibility: Insist on simultaneous presence of both operators during sign-off.

Sign-off
Outgoing operator name / signature / time  
Incoming operator name / signature / time  
Supervisor name / signature / time

References
- ECN-2026-016
- SOP-P3-L3-01
- SOP-P3-L3-03

Revision history
Rev B — Current: updated to include explicit verification steps for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 pressure and main ram bolt torque per maintenance instruction set.

text:
# SOP-P3-L3-05 Planned shutdown - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: SB-1005, SB-1022, SOP-P3-L3-03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled sequence for a planned full shutdown of the Machining line to allow maintenance, inspection, and safe isolation of equipment EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03.

Background and scope
2. This procedure applies to the Machining line in P3-L3 during planned outages where systems will be taken out of service for maintenance tasks that require zero-energy state and mechanical safeguarding. The procedure provides rationale for each step, examples of common maintenance activities, and the mandatory records to be completed.

Preconditions (must be verified before starting)
3. Confirm supervisory authorization for the planned shutdown and scope of work as recorded on the shutdown permit. Verify that affected production schedules have been updated and that downstream departments are notified. Confirm that required spares and tools for the planned tasks are available.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE for personnel on the shutdown team: safety helmet, eye protection, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, and high-visibility clothing. Additional PPE for hydraulic and heavy mechanical work should be identified by the maintenance supervisor based on the task.

Shutdown sequence and steps
5. Step 1 — Initial controls and isolation
   - Notify operators and control room that shutdown is commencing.
   - Place machine controls in manual and stop automatic feeds.
   - Lockout and tagout electrical supply at the line main disconnect and to each equipment item following the site LOTO standard referenced in SB-1005.

6. Step 2 — Hydraulic isolation for EQ-P3-L3-HP03
   - Isolate hydraulic power to EQ-P3-L3-HP03 and relieve residual pressure per the hydraulic isolation instructions in SB-1022.
   - The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar.
   - Verify pressure gauges read zero or are at ambient before opening any hydraulic connections.

7. Step 3 — Mechanical safety
   - Apply mechanical blocks or cribbing to secure movable masses where required for disassembly.
   - De-energize stored energy devices and secure accumulators according to manufacturer guidance.

8. Step 4 — Fastener control for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 main ram
   - When access for main ram removal or adjustment is required, follow the documented torque and fastener sequences.
   - The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m.
   - Use calibrated torque equipment and record the calibration tag reference in the maintenance record.

9. Step 5 — Component removal and inspection
   - Remove covers, guards, and service panels in the order described in SOP-P3-L3-03 to maintain structural integrity.
   - Inspect hydraulic fittings, seals, and structural welds for wear and record findings with photographs attached to the work order.

10. Step 6 — Example maintenance tasks
    - Example A: Replace or reseal a hydraulic cylinder on EQ-P3-L3-HP03 after verifying system is depressurized per SB-1022.
    - Example B: Replace sensor housings on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 with the machine mechanically blocked and electrical lockout applied.
    - For each example, list components removed, serial or tag numbers, and disposition (replaced, reconditioned, scrapped).

11. Step 7 — Pre-start checks and reassembly
    - Reinstall guards and covers in the reverse order of removal. Verify torque values using calibrated tools and record applied torque where specified.
    - Re-pressurize hydraulic systems slowly and verify there are no leaks at fittings or hoses before returning to full operating pressure.

Step rationale
12. Each step is designed to progressively remove energy and provide positive isolation to prevent inadvertent movement or release of stored energy. Isolation of hydraulics before mechanical intervention prevents fluid-driven movement. Controlling bolt torque on the main ram preserves structural clamping and prevents catastrophic failure under load; the specified torque is mandatory to achieve the designed clamping preload.

Records to keep
13. For each shutdown, file the following in the maintenance system:
    - Completed shutdown permit and authorization form.
    - Lockout/tagout checklist and signed LOTO tags.
    - Pressure gauge readings before and after hydraulic isolation.
    - Torque application records showing applied torque for the main ram bolt on EQ-P3-L3-HP03 and the calibration reference for the torque wrench used.
    - Inspection reports with photographic evidence and corrective action notes.
    - Post-maintenance test results and operator handover checklist.

Examples of record entries
14. Example entry: “Hydraulic isolation complete; gauge reads ambient; main ram bolt torque checked with calibrated wrench, applied torque as per spec recorded; no leaks detected during 15-minute pressurization hold.” Attach images of gauges and torque tool calibration label.

Return to service and verification
15. Conduct stepwise re-energization and verify functions at controlled settings. Confirm that safety interlocks and guards operate correctly and that no abnormal noises, leaks, or alarms are present. Complete a functional test run at operator station and obtain operator and maintenance sign-off before releasing equipment back to production.

Sign-off
16. The following signatures are required on the completed shutdown package:
   - Maintenance supervisor (name and signature)
   - Production supervisor (name and signature)
   - Safety representative (name and signature)
   - Date and time of handover to operations

Related documents and references
17. Consult SB-1005 for site lockout/tagout policy, SB-1022 for hydraulic isolation procedures, and SOP-P3-L3-03 for machine-specific disassembly and reassembly sequences.

Revision control
18. Maintain this procedure in the document control system and attach the completed shutdown package for auditing and continuous improvement.

text:
# SOP-P3-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-026, MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-SB03

Purpose
1. Define the required steps to perform a controlled startup of the Heat Treat line at P3-L4 following planned maintenance or an extended shutdown. This procedure addresses mechanical checks, safety verifications, sequence rationale, example observations and mandatory records.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, maintenance technicians and supervisors responsible for EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Do not start the line without completing all preconditions and sign-offs described below.

Background and rationale
3. Heat Treat line startup requires coordinated confirmation of mechanical integrity, electrical readiness and safety systems to prevent damage to tooling and workpieces and to protect personnel. Specific fastener torques are critical for tool retention and safe operation; incorrect torque is a leading cause of component failure. The steps below sequence verification from isolation to live operation to minimize risk.

Preconditions (must be verified before Step 1)
4. a) Lockout/tagout (LOTO) for all power and energy sources completed and verified.  
b) All maintenance activities documented in ECN-2026-026 are closed or deferred with documented mitigation.  
c) Maintenance inspections and corrective actions recorded per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 completed and signed off by responsible technician.  
d) Required spares and consumables available at the work area.  
e) Housekeeping and clear access to emergency stops confirmed.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
5. Minimum PPE for startup team: safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves for handling tooling, high-visibility vest, steel-toe footwear. Additional PPE required by MM-P3-L4-HT02 for heat treat operations must be worn when entering the HT furnace area.

Preparation and communications
6. Notify production control and area supervisor that startup is planned. Establish two-way communication between lead operator and maintenance technician. Post a visible startup tagboard at the line entry indicating status and point of contact.

Startup procedure — numbered steps
7. Step 1 — Visual mechanical inspection
- Verify guards and interlocks are secure and unobstructed.
- Inspect the mandrel and clamp area on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 for foreign objects or tooling misalignment. Clean as required.
- Inspect EQ-P3-L4-SB03 shot blast cabinet interior for loose liner material and debris.

8. Step 2 — Fastener torque verification (critical)
- Verify the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. If the torque is out of tolerance, do not proceed until corrected and rechecked. Record the measured value and the technician initials in the startup log.
- Verify the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. If the torque is out of tolerance, do not proceed until corrected and rechecked. Record the measured value and the technician initials in the startup log.
Rationale: These torques secure rotating components and liners; incorrect torque can lead to catastrophic failure and secondary damage.

9. Step 3 — Functional interlock and sensor test (dry)
- With all power still isolated, operate manual function checks for safety interlocks, door switches, e-stops and emergency stops. Confirm wired and wireless alarms function. Document any failed items and correct per MM-P3-L4-HT02 before continuing.

10. Step 4 — Grease, lubrication and tooling
- Verify lubrication points on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 have been serviced per the MM reference and that lubricant type matches specification. Inspect tooling for wear; replace or rotate tooling if wear exceeds acceptable visual criteria per MM-P3-L4-HT02. Record part IDs and lot IDs in the maintenance log.

11. Step 5 — Low-power electrical energization (control power)
- Restore control power only. Verify control panels boot correctly and PLC interlocks report nominal. Confirm operator HMI displays correct status and no alarm conditions persist from pre-start checks. If fault persists, escalate to electrical maintenance.

12. Step 6 — No-load mechanical run
- With no workpieces loaded, command a slow jog of rotating assemblies and observe for abnormal vibration, noise or heat sources. Confirm that EQ-P3-L4-SB03 blast wheel runs smoothly and that EQ-P3-L4-RR01 mandrel rotation is concentric and free of runout that interferes with clamps or tooling. Stop immediately on abnormal signs and document findings.

13. Step 7 — Simulated process cycle
- Run a complete simulated cycle using a representative scrap or instrumented test piece. Verify sequence logic, tooling actuation, furnace pre-heat and conveyor operations operate in expected order. Monitor alarms and interlocks. If sequence deviations occur, review PLC logic and ECN-2026-026 for recent changes that may affect startup.

14. Step 8 — Initial loaded production
- Move to single-piece loaded production after satisfactory simulated cycle. The operator must remain at the local control during initial pieces and verify quality and mechanical stability. Monitor output and listen for new noises. If defects or unusual conditions arise, stop and investigate.

15. Step 9 — Ramp to normal production
- Ramp production volume only after sign-off by the line supervisor confirming the initial loaded production criteria are met and recorded.

Examples of observations and responses
16. Example: If a mandrel clamp bolt returns a torque reading below the required value, tighten to specification, re-torque and inspect clamp seating for wear. If seating damage is found, replace the clamp and document using MM-P3-L4-HT02 directives.  
Example: If the shot blast cabinet liner shows unusual wear pattern, capture photos, record liner bolt torque as per Step 2, and reference MM-P3-L4-SB03 for liner change procedure.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following records in the line startup packet:
- Startup checklist with initials of responsible personnel.
- Torque verification log entries for the mandrel clamp bolt and blast wheel liner bolt including measured values and technician initials.
- Copies of any corrective maintenance orders generated and referenced to ECN-2026-026 when applicable.
- HMI alarm printouts or exported diagnostic logs during startup.
- Quality inspection results for initial production pieces.

Stop and notify
18. If any condition cannot be corrected by the on-site team, stop the startup and notify the area supervisor and maintenance planner. Log the reason for stop and reference ECN-2026-026 for any related engineering changes.

Responsibilities
19. Operators — perform steps, execute checks, and record results.  
Maintenance technicians — perform torque confirmation, corrective repairs and re-inspections.  
Supervisor — review results and provide final sign-off to enter normal production.

Sign-off (required)
20. Pre-start verification completed by:
- Lead Operator: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________
- Maintenance Technician: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________
- Line Supervisor: Name: __________________ Signature: __________________ Date: __________

Revision notes
21. See ECN-2026-026 for related engineering changes and MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for detailed maintenance procedures and tooling specifications.
title: Line startup - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P3-L4-02 Product changeover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3, MM-P3-L4-SB03, SB-1019

Purpose
1. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the steps required to perform a product changeover on the Heat Treat line at P3-L4, covering roll refeed (EQ-P3-L4-RR01), heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). It ensures consistent setup, protects equipment life, and preserves product quality.

Background and Rationale
2. Changeovers are critical operations where incorrect sequences or undocumented adjustments cause rework or equipment damage. This SOP captures the approved sequence and required verification points to reduce variability. Example rationale: confirming feed and restraint positions on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 prevents misalignment through EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and controlled cleaning/finish settings on EQ-P3-L4-SB03 prevent surface contamination prior to inspection.

Preconditions (must be verified before any step)
3. Verify the line is in Planned Downtime and that the previous production lot has completed all hold points. Confirm authorization from shift lead. Confirm availability of required consumables and tooling for the next product run. Review MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for maintenance status and any open work orders before starting. Confirm no outstanding safety tags on EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, or EQ-P3-L4-SB03 by checking the line board and SB-1019.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for all steps: safety glasses, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves for furnace areas, and a long-sleeve flame-resistant outer garment while accessing EQ-P3-L4-HT02 service panels. Use respiratory protection as specified in MM-P3-L4-SB03 when working inside the shot blast cabinet area.

Step-by-step Changeover Procedure
5. Tag-in and pre-start checks
   5.1. Sign the changeover authorization in the line changeover log.  
   5.2. Confirm that EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 are powered to Safe state as required by SB-1019 before performing mechanical adjustments.  
   5.3. Visually inspect tooling and fixtures for wear or foreign material. If any abnormality is present, refer to MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 for repair procedures.

6. Material handling and fixture setup on EQ-P3-L4-RR01
   6.1. Install the new product fixtures and validate clamp engagement visually.  
   6.2. Jog the feed mechanism slowly to confirm parts seat correctly and that there is no interference with adjacent fixtures.  
   6.3. Verify sensor alignment and presence; if any sensor fault is detected, log the fault and escalate to maintenance per MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3.

7. Heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) configuration and verification
   7.1. Confirm that furnace internal load carriers are set per product tooling layout and that carriers are secure.  
   7.2. Verify control program selection for the new product on the operator console. Do not adjust control recipes unless authorized by the process engineer.  
   7.3. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Ensure the furnace control confirms the quench delay parameter is at or below this value before first heat. If a discrepancy exists, abort start and notify maintenance.

8. Shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) preparation
   8.1. Confirm abrasive media is appropriate and the cabinet internals are free of buildup. Follow cleaning steps in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for cabinet inspection.  
   8.2. Install and verify the lubricant specified: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. Use only this approved part for any pre-blast lubrication operations.  
   8.3. Run a single dry cycle with no parts to confirm blast pattern and media feed. If pattern is non-uniform, consult MM-P3-L4-SB03 for troubleshooting.

9. Dry run and first-piece verification
   9.1. Execute a dry run through EQ-P3-L4-RR01 into EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and through EQ-P3-L4-SB03 with carriers only to confirm material flow and absence of mechanical interference.  
   9.2. Run the first production piece and perform dimensional, visual, and surface-finish checks per product control plan. Record inspection results in the lot start record. If the first-piece inspection fails, stop the line and follow containment steps.

10. Documentation and records to keep
   10.1. Complete the Changeover Checklist and attach copies of first-piece inspection, furnace log printout showing the quench delay parameter, and shot blast setup sheet referencing CFW-LUB-526.  
   10.2. Record any maintenance actions and reference work orders in the maintenance log; cross-reference SB-1019 for safety tag clearances.  
   10.3. Keep records in the electronic Document Control repository and local line binder for traceability.

Examples and common nonconformance scenarios
11. Example: If the quench delay reads above the permitted setting for EQ-P3-L4-HT02, the item must not proceed to quench. Notify maintenance and hold the load until corrected. Log the event and attach furnace control screenshots.  
12. Example: If a non-approved lubricant is found in EQ-P3-L4-SB03, quarantine any affected parts, clean per MM-P3-L4-SB03, and note corrective action.

Process safety and escalation
13. Any equipment alarm or unexpected actuation requires immediate stop of the changeover and notification of the shift supervisor. Follow SB-1019 procedures for lockout/tagout if manual servicing is required. Maintenance approvals per MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 or MM-P3-L4-SB03 are required prior to restart.

Sign-off and authorization
14. Signatures required to release the line for production:
   14.1. Operator completing changeover — print name and sign.  
   14.2. Shift lead verification — print name and sign after confirming all preconditions and first-piece acceptance.  
   14.3. Maintenance representative — print name and sign if any adjustments were made to EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, or EQ-P3-L4-SB03 during changeover.

Change history and document control
15. This SOP is controlled in the Document Control system. Refer to MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for equipment-specific maintenance instructions and to SB-1019 for safety procedures.
