# SOP-P3-L4-03 First-article inspection - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Purpose and scope
This procedure defines the first-article inspection (FAI) process for parts processed through the Heat Treat line at P3-L4. It covers inspection of rings after radial ring rolling (EQ-P3-L4-RR01), heat treatment staging (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and secondary bead/shot operations (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). Use this SOP for initial production runs and whenever controlled process changes affect form, fit, or function.

Related documents
See MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2, SOP-P3-L4-01 for maintenance, setup, and general FAI policy.

Background and rationale
First-article inspection ensures that the combined effect of rolling, heat treat, and bead/shot processes meets drawing requirements and customer expectations before full production continues. Critical machine setup items on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 directly affect dimensional stability and metallurgical response in downstream operations. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Using the specified lubricant reduces wear that can induce dimensional or surface defects; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before starting)
1. Equipment EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 are available and unlocked for inspection activities.
2. Maintenance necessary to bring machines to baseline condition has been completed per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2.
3. First-article sample part(s) are identified and traceable to the production lot and customer drawing.
4. Calibration status of inspection tools is current per SOP-P3-L4-01.
5. Required PPE is donned and area is prepared for safe handling.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Safety glasses with side shields.
2. Cut-resistant gloves for handling metal parts.
3. Hearing protection when machines are under power.
4. Steel-toe footwear.
5. Appropriate protective clothing for heat-treated parts (thermal-resistant gloves available for hot handling).

Procedure — numbered steps
1. Preparation
   1.1 Verify tool and gauge calibration referenced in SOP-P3-L4-01.
   1.2 Confirm maintenance records for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2 are on file and referenceable.
   1.3 Verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-RR01 is set to the specified value: the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Record evidence of torque verification in the FAI checklist.

2. Machine setup verification
   2.1 On EQ-P3-L4-RR01, verify lubricant used matches the part identifier: the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315. Attach a copy of the lubricant label to the FAI record.
   2.2 Confirm that all safety interlocks and guards are engaged and functioning before loading the first-article part.
   2.3 Document any deviations from baseline setup and notify engineering for disposition.

3. First-article processing
   3.1 Load the identified first-article blank into EQ-P3-L4-RR01 following operator guidelines in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   3.2 Observe the rolling operation for abnormal noises, surface indications, or handling issues that could affect part geometry. Note observations on the FAI checklist with clear descriptions.
   3.3 Transfer the part to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 per plant handling protocol, ensuring traceability tags remain attached.
   3.4 Complete heat-treat staging as required and move to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 for any bead or secondary surface operations.

4. Inspection and measurements
   4.1 Perform visual inspection for surface defects per drawing acceptance criteria. Record findings with photographs where useful.
   4.2 Use calibrated gauges to verify critical dimensions listed on the drawing. Record measured values and compare to drawing requirements; attach measurement sheets to the FAI package.
   4.3 Identify any nonconforming features and categorize as critical, major, or minor. For critical or major nonconformances, stop production and initiate engineering review.

5. Metallurgical and hardness verification
   5.1 Coordinate with metallurgical lab when microstructure or hardness verification is required by the part drawing. Include lab reports in the FAI record.
   5.2 If metallurgical results deviate from expectations, hold affected parts and notify process engineering.

6. Final acceptance and disposition
   6.1 If the first-article sample meets all acceptance criteria, sign off the FAI checklist and release the process for production.
   6.2 If rejected, document corrective actions, update process parameters, and repeat FAI per engineering direction.

Examples and rationale
- Example observation: a ring exhibits a circumferential surface mark after rolling. Recording the mark location, photograph, and suspected cause (e.g., foreign material on mandrel) supports targeted corrective action.
- Rationale for torque and lubricant controls: consistent mandrel clamp bolt torque and specified lubricant CFW-LUB-315 maintain mandrel alignment and surface interaction, reducing variability transferred into heat treat and subsequent inspections.

Records to keep
1. Completed FAI checklist with sign-offs and condition statements.
2. Torque verification record showing the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
3. Lubricant verification showing CFW-LUB-315 on EQ-P3-L4-RR01.
4. Measurement sheets and calibrated tool certificates per SOP-P3-L4-01.
5. Photographs of critical features and any nonconforming evidence.
6. Metallurgical and hardness lab reports when applicable.
7. Maintenance and setup reference copies from MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2.

Escalation and nonconformance
- For any critical nonconformance, stop all further processing of the lot and notify process engineering and quality management.
- For repeated minor nonconformances, initiate root cause analysis and corrective action per quality procedure.

Sign-off
Prepared by: ______________________  Role: ______________________
Reviewed by: ______________________  Role: ______________________
Approved by: ______________________  Role: ______________________

Revision history
Refer to document control for historical revisions.
title: First-article inspection - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P3-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-RR01

Purpose
1. To define the standardized shift handover process for the Heat Treat line (P3-L4), ensuring continuity of operations, safe condition of equipment, and accurate transfer of process and maintenance information between operators.

Background and rationale
2. The Heat Treat line includes the re-rolling coil unit EQ-P3-L4-RR01, the heat treat furnace EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and the shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Operational continuity is essential to avoid scrapped parts, quality deviations, and unsafe conditions. Handover must communicate process state, pending actions, issues, and recent maintenance per ECN-2026-001 and machine maintenance procedures MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01. Documented handovers reduce miscommunication and support traceability for audits and root cause analysis.

Preconditions (required before handover)
3. The outgoing operator shall complete: verification of process parameters per MM-P3-L4-HT02, completion of any lockout/tagout per ECN-2026-001 if maintenance occurred, and confirmation that all critical tools and spares are in the designated locations. Any active maintenance tags must reference MM-P3-L4-RR01 or MM-P3-L4-HT02 as applicable.

PPE (minimum for handover walkdown)
4. Outgoing and incoming personnel must wear required PPE for line access and walkdown: ear protection, eye protection, protective footwear, and heat-resistant gloves when opening furnace guards. If entering confined or hot zones, follow PPE per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Handover steps (numbered sequence)
5. Outgoing operator prepares handover notes
   5.1. Record the current job/lot identifier and part code as per the production board.  
   5.2. Note any deviations, rejects, or process parameter excursions and reference the corrective action or temporary workaround. Cite any engineering change requests to ECN-2026-001 if applicable.  
   5.3. List active maintenance work orders or outstanding issues that require follow-up and reference MM-P3-L4-HT02 or MM-P3-L4-RR01.

6. Line status walkdown with incoming operator
   6.1. Conduct a physical walkdown of EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 together. Show current mode (running, standby, or locked out) and location of the last processed piece.  
   6.2. Point out any abnormal sounds, leaks, or visible wear. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03, show the blast wheel and liner access panels and the condition of the blast media. Ensure the incoming operator understands the location of spares and the lubricant spares box.

7. Critical maintenance and lubrication information
   7.1. Confirm next planned maintenance and any deferred items against MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01 records.  
   7.2. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03: confirm lubricant part and fastener information. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. Record when these were last checked and whether any fasteners were loosened during the shift.

8. Safety-critical items and alarms
   8.1. Demonstrate recent alarm history on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Explain root-cause status for any recurring alarms and the mitigation in place. Reference troubleshooting steps in MM-P3-L4-HT02.  
   8.2. Confirm emergency stop circuits and access to local isolators. If any isolator is tagged out, ensure the tag references ECN-2026-001 and the associated work order.

9. Material and quality transfer
   9.1. Show incoming operator the inventory of in-process material, quarantined parts, and any parts under inspection. Note any quality hold and the reason.  
   9.2. Transfer any sample pieces for incoming operator inspection and note where process data and logs are stored.

10. Examples and typical notes to include
   10.1. Example entry: "Lot XYZ in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 paused at chamber 2; furnace ramp complete; awaiting QA sign-off."  
   10.2. Example entry: "EQ-P3-L4-SB03 blast media judgement: requires top-up; liner bolts checked—no movement; lubricant on hand: CFW-LUB-526."  
   10.3. Use concise, factual entries; avoid subjective language.

11. Records to keep
   11.1. Outgoing operator shall upload the signed handover log to the line control folder and retain a paper copy in the shift binder.  
   11.2. Record references to ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, and MM-P3-L4-RR01 where relevant. Include timestamps and operator signatures.

12. Sign-off and acceptance
   12.1. Incoming operator shall read the handover notes, complete a walkdown with the outgoing operator, and confirm acceptance by signing the handover log.  
   12.2. If the incoming operator cannot accept the line due to unresolved safety or quality issues, escalate to the shift lead and annotate the reason in the log. Reference MM-P3-L4-HT02 or MM-P3-L4-RR01 for escalation steps.

Roles and responsibilities
13. Outgoing operator: prepare accurate notes, perform complete walkdown, verify maintenance tags and PPE compliance.  
14. Incoming operator: review notes, perform independent verification, accept or escalate.  
15. Shift lead: adjudicate disputes, approve transfer of responsibility, ensure records are filed.

Change control and references
16. Any procedural changes that affect handover content or responsibilities must be proposed through ECN-2026-001. Maintenance requirements are governed by MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01.

Appendix: audit and verification guidance
17. Auditors should verify that handover logs contain: job/lot identifier, any active maintenance references, lubricant confirmation for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 as CFW-LUB-526, and that the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is recorded as 90 N·m when applicable. Ensure handover logs cite ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, and MM-P3-L4-RR01 where maintenance or engineering changes are involved.

Sign-off
18. Handover complete when both operators sign the handover log and the incoming operator assumes control of P3-L4 line operations.
title: Shift handover - Heat Treat line

text:
# SOP-P3-L4-05 Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03
Related documents: MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2, SOP-P3-L4-01

1. Purpose and scope
   1.1. This procedure defines the planned shutdown sequence for the Heat Treat line (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) and associated roller return (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) and shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). It covers isolation, lubrication, dust control checks and safe restart preparations for scheduled maintenance aligned to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
   1.2. Background and rationale: Planned shutdowns prevent unplanned downtime and reduce risk to personnel and equipment. Coordinated isolation and verification steps reduce the chance of trapped energy, contamination of heat treat atmospheres, and damage to conveyor and blast subsystems. Follow-up records enable trend analysis and support MM-P3-L4-HT02 preventative tasks.

2. Preconditions (must be verified before step 3)
   2.1. Production schedule has authorized line outage per SOP-P3-L4-01.
   2.2. Maintenance work order created and attached to the shutdown record.
   2.3. Notify operations, quality, and safety departments per site notification procedures in SOP-P3-L4-01.
   2.4. Ensure spares and consumables listed in MM-P3-L4-HT02 are on site.
   2.5. Confirm the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. Record this value on the shutdown checklist before isolation.

3. Required PPE
   3.1. Mandatory: flame-resistant coveralls, safety glasses with side shields, heat-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection.
   3.2. For work inside ovens or cabinets: supplied-air respirator if atmosphere monitoring indicates contaminants above action levels per MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
   3.3. Lockout/tagout (LOTO) kits and arc flash PPE as required by site LOTO policy referenced in SOP-P3-L4-01.

4. Shutdown sequence (stepwise actions and rationale)
   4.1. Coordinate and confirm line hold. Rationale: prevents inadvertent loading of parts during isolation.
   4.2. Stop material feed and clear workstations. Rationale: ensures no parts are in the heat treat envelope or on conveyors.
   4.3. Isolate power to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-RR01 using approved LOTO procedure. Verify zero energy at specified disconnect points. Rationale: eliminates electrical energy and motion hazard for maintenance crews.
   4.4. Isolate compressed air and any process gas feeds to EQ-P3-L4-HT02. Rationale: prevents unintended flow into the oven atmosphere and hazards to technicians.
   4.5. De-energize and lock out the dust collector serving EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Verify the dust collector pressure drop alarm reading and record; if the recorded alarm differs from the precondition value, flag in the maintenance record and notify the maintenance supervisor. Example: precondition entry shows 1510 Pa. Rationale: dust collector condition affects air quality and blast cabinet function; pressure drop trend informs filter replacement planning in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   4.6. Drain and tag hydraulic or lubricant circuits where work will be performed; secure lines per MM-P3-L4-HT02 procedures. Rationale: prevents accidental release of hydraulic pressure and contamination of parts.
   4.7. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03 lubrication: verify lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 is the dispense material to be used for bearings and separator plates during reassembly. Rationale: using the specified lubricant ensures compatibility with blast media and avoids premature bearing failure.
   4.8. Perform verification walkdown with maintenance lead and safety officer to confirm all isolation points are controlled and areas are safe for entry. Rationale: face-to-face verification reduces communication errors.
   4.9. Perform maintenance tasks as defined on the attached work order and MM-P3-L4-HT02 preventive task lists. Rationale: ensures all required inspections, replacements, and adjustments are completed during the planned outage.

5. Examples of common maintenance activities to schedule during this shutdown
   5.1. Replace or inspect oven element connections and refractory panels per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   5.2. Inspect conveyors on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 for wear and alignment; adjust clearances as required.
   5.3. On EQ-P3-L4-SB03, replace filters if pressure drop trend indicates near-limit readings; document filter serials in the record.
   5.4. Lubricate bearings using CFW-LUB-526; note batch or lot on maintenance record.

6. Records to keep
   6.1. Completed shutdown checklist with timestamps and initials for each isolation and verification step.
   6.2. Work order with completed tasks, parts used, and signatures of performing technicians and maintenance lead.
   6.3. Dust collector pressure drop readings before and after maintenance, including the precondition reading of 1510 Pa.
   6.4. Lubricant usage log showing CFW-LUB-526 used for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and quantity dispensed.
   6.5. Any non-conformance reports and corrective action plans created during the outage.
   6.6. Attachments or references to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 task pages executed during the shutdown.

7. Restart and verification
   7.1. Remove lockout/tagout only after all work is complete, tools and materials are cleared, and a final permit-to-start review is signed by the maintenance lead and safety officer.
   7.2. Re-energize systems in a controlled sequence per MM-P3-L4-HT02. Perform functional tests and run a validation piece through the heat treat process where required.
   7.3. Verify dust collector operation and confirm post-maintenance pressure drop is acceptable and recorded.

8. Sign-off
   8.1. Performed by: Lead Technician (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________
   8.2. Verified by: Maintenance Supervisor (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________
   8.3. Safety approval: Safety Officer (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________

9. References
   9.1. MM-P3-L4-HT02
   9.2. MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2
   9.3. SOP-P3-L4-01

Notes: Deviations from this SOP require documented approval and an updated risk assessment. Maintain all closure records in the document control system per site retention policy.

text:
# MM-P1-L1-RR01 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Scope
-------
This document establishes required preventive maintenance and controlled adjustment procedures for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1, EQ-P1-L1-RR01. It covers the mandrel clamp bolt torque setting and main roll bearing lubrication interval, inspection rationale, safe handling notes, example record entries, and criteria for acceptance after maintenance activities. Refer to SB-1025 for safety barriers and to SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 for lockout, permit, and standard operating procedures that apply during execution.

Background and rationale
------------------------
Radial ring rolling mills subject the mandrel and bearing systems to high mechanical loads and thermal cycles. Proper clamp bolt preload and disciplined lubrication intervals maintain alignment, minimize fretting, and extend component life. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 635 N·m. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. These values are field-proven for the installed assemblies and must not be modified without engineering authorization and cross reference to supplier documentation.

Tools
-----
Required items for the procedures below are general maintenance hand tools, calibration equipment, and records. Use industry standard torque wrench and calibrated oil cup or grease dispensing system per SOP-P1-L1-05. Personal protective equipment should follow SB-1025 and SOP-P1-L1-01. Keep a calibrated torque wrench with current calibration certificate available. Maintain a lubrication log and a clamp torque verification record in the equipment file.

Procedure
---------
Preparation
- Follow lockout and permit requirements from SOP-P1-L1-01 prior to any work. Confirm isolation of electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic sources. Use the required protective barriers described in SB-1025.
- Ensure the work area is clean and free of billets, tooling, and material handling tongs. Communicate with operations and maintenance scheduling.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and setting
- Complete pre-torque inspection. Check clamp bolt threads and mating surfaces for damage, corrosion, and contamination. Clean and lightly lubricate threads and bearing surfaces if specified by the clamp manufacturer. Remove visible debris and old compound. Inspect clamp faces for even wear and proper contact.
- Using a calibrated torque wrench, set each mandrel clamp bolt to the specified torque. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 635 N·m. Apply torque in a cross pattern to ensure even preload, and use a smooth, steady application of force to reach the required value. If a bolt does not reach the specified torque without excessive handle travel, remove and inspect for damage and replace per vendor practice.
- After initial torque, allow the assembly to settle and recheck torques. Record readings in the clamp torque verification record.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Access lubrication fittings as described in the equipment as-built and lubrication diagram. Clean fittings prior to connection to avoid contamination.
- Supply lubricant consistent with the equipment lubrication specification and pump method described in SOP-P1-L1-05. Apply lubricant until fresh lubricant appears at the bearing seals or as indicated by the bearing fill method in the equipment lubrication diagram.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. Log the start time of bearing service and schedule the next lubrication event according to the stated interval. If operating conditions change significantly from those expected, consult engineering and SOP-P1-L1-05 to assess interval adjustments.

Inspection and verification
- After torque and lubrication operations, run a controlled slow rotation of the mandrel and rolls under observed conditions following SOP-P1-L1-01 guidance. Verify absence of unusual noise, vibration, or thermal signs.
- Check for lubricant leaks, thread back-off, or progressive movement of clamp bolts. If any abnormal condition is observed, stop and isolate; perform corrective actions and document findings.

Examples and troubleshooting
- Example entry for clamp torque verification record: include equipment id, date, technician initials, bolt location, applied torque value, and any remedial actions taken. For lubrication log: include equipment id, lubricant type, quantity dispensed, start time, technician initials, and next scheduled service based on the stated lubrication interval.
- If repeated loss of clamp torque is observed, inspect for sleeve wear, thread stripping, or elastic deformation. If excessive bearing temperature or noise is present after lubrication, verify lubricant type and cleanliness and check for bearing preloading or alignment issues. Refer to SOP-P1-L1-05 for lubricant selection and SB-1025 for safe handling of overheated components.

Records to keep
----------------
Maintain a clamp torque verification record and a lubrication log in the equipment maintenance file. Records should include technician identification, reference to this document id, any deviations and corrective actions, and links to packaging or supplier certificates where replacement parts are used. Retain records per plant document control requirements as noted in SOP-P1-L1-01.

Acceptance criteria
-------------------
Successful completion of the maintenance activity for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 requires that all actuated clamp bolts read the specified torque when rechecked, that the main roll bearings have been serviced within the stated interval, and that no abnormal vibration or thermal signatures are present during the controlled run. Specifically, the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) must be 635 N·m, and the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) must be adhered to at 120 hours. Any deviation must be documented and addressed with corrective action before returning the mill to production.

Related documents
-----------------
SB-1025  
SOP-P1-L1-01  
SOP-P1-L1-05

Revision history
----------------
Rev B — current maintenance recommendations and verification details for EQ-P1-L1-RR01.

# MM-P1-L1-CN02 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-CN02

Scope
This manual defines preventive maintenance tasks, safe work rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2, EQ-P1-L1-CN02. It applies to technicians assigned to P1, line P1-L1 and to engineering staff responsible for equipment reliability. This document supplements operating procedures and standard work, and references related documents SOP-P1-L1-03, SOP-P1-L1-04, and SOP-P1-L1-05 for operator-level steps and lockout/tagout requirements.

Background and purpose
EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is a production turning center used in hot forging finishing. Regular maintenance preserves spindle life, chuck integrity, and process accuracy. This manual provides the rationale for each task to prioritize actions that reduce risk of component failure, maintain concentricity, and ensure operator safety. Tasks are designed to be compatible with the referenced SOPs and to generate records suitable for trend analysis and root-cause investigation.

Tools
Approved tools and materials:
- Torque wrench calibrated and traceable to calibration records.
- Socket set compatible with chuck jaw bolt heads as specified by the manufacturer.
- Spindle warm-up control or programmable interface.
- Clean, lint-free rags and non-conductive brushes for debris removal.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal checks.
- Gasket materials and fasteners as specified by OEM manuals (refer to equipment file).
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-04.

Procedure
Overview and timing rationale
Maintenance actions are sequenced to minimize thermal and mechanical stress. The spindle warm-up sequence reduces thermal gradients that can cause chatter or premature bearing wear. The chuck torque specification preserves clamping integrity without overstressing components.

Pre-maintenance preparation
- Review last maintenance entries for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and the operator shift log to identify recurring issues.
- Follow lockout/tagout per SOP-P1-L1-05 before accessing guarded areas.
- Verify the torque wrench calibration sticker is current and record the calibration reference in the maintenance log.

Spindle warm-up
- Initiate the spindle warm-up routine using the machine control or the warm-up control panel. Warm-up is required to condition bearings and preload prior to load-bearing operations. The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes. Allow the full warm-up time to elapse before proceeding to high-load operations or before performing precision measurement tasks.
- Rationale: Controlled warm-up reduces thermal distortion, stabilizes concentricity, and reduces the likelihood of differential expansion between spindle and chuck.

Chuck maintenance and bolt torque
- Access the chuck per OEM access guidance and SOP-P1-L1-04.
- Clean mating surfaces and inspect for burrs, scoring, or foreign material that would affect seating.
- Reassemble chuck components and install chuck jaw bolts. Tighten bolts in a crossing pattern to the specified value. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m. Use the calibrated torque wrench and follow the specified tightening sequence to ensure even clamping load.
- Rationale: Correct torque prevents bolt loosening under dynamic loads and avoids over-tension that can induce fatigue failure in bolts or distortion in chuck components.

Inspection and verification
- After torque application, perform a static runout check using an appropriate dial or electronic indicator setup to confirm chuck and spindle concentricity meet the machine capability as documented in the equipment file.
- Perform a controlled trial run at low load following the warm-up period to listen for abnormal noises and to observe vibration behavior. Refer to SOP-P1-L1-03 for acceptable acoustic and vibration check methods.
- Document any deviations and initiate corrective maintenance if runout or vibration exceed acceptable limits in EQ-P1-L1-CN02 equipment file.

Examples and common fault patterns
- Example: Bolt loosening observed after high-temperature cycle may present as incremental increase in runout readings across shifts. If this pattern appears, verify torque setting against the documented chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m and inspect for thread damage or galling.
- Example: Premature bearing noise following an incomplete warm-up cycle can be mitigated by enforcing the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes prior to production start.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order with date, technician name, and start/finish times.
- Torque application log showing bolt identification and confirmation of the applied value: 100 N·m.
- Spindle warm-up log confirming that the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes and indicating the timestamp when warm-up completed.
- Runout and vibration measurement records, annotated with pre- and post-maintenance results.
- Calibration certificate reference for the torque wrench used.
- Any nonconformance reports and corrective action records tied to the equipment serial file.

Acceptance criteria
- Chuck jaw bolts must be torqued to the documented value. Compliance evidence: torque application log entry showing bolts set to 100 N·m and signed by the performing technician.
- Spindle shall be warmed up for the full documented duration before precision operations or load testing. Compliance evidence: warm-up log entry confirming the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes and timestamped completion.
- Post-maintenance dynamic check must show runout and vibration within limits specified in the EQ-P1-L1-CN02 equipment file. If limits are exceeded, the unit must be removed from service and a corrective maintenance work order raised.
- No visible debris, burrs, or compromised fasteners on chuck mating surfaces. Visual inspection must be recorded and signed.

References
- SOP-P1-L1-03
- SOP-P1-L1-04
- SOP-P1-L1-05

Revision control
All maintenance entries performed under this manual must be filed in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Any deviations from this manual require engineering authorization and a revision to this document.

# MM-P1-L1-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Scope
This document provides maintenance guidance for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03). It covers preventive and corrective tasks required to maintain safe and reliable heating of billets prior to forging operations. Tasks include inspection of electrical and cooling systems, coil integrity checks, thermal verification, and housekeeping that could affect heater performance. Refer to related documents MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3, SB-1009, and SOP-P1-L1-01 for supplementary procedures, safety bulletins, and operating instructions.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L1-IH03 is a high-power induction heater that must deliver consistent billet surface temperature to ensure metallurgical and dimensional outcomes in the subsequent forge operation. The specified target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C. Maintaining coil condition and cooling system performance is critical to prevent overheating of the coil assembly and power electronics, and to ensure uniform heat transfer to billets. Coil cooling water flow must be verified because reduced flow increases local coil temperature and risk of damage; the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min. The steps below prioritize verification of those parameters and provide acceptance criteria tied to those values.

Tools
- Electrical insulated hand tools and torque tools as defined in SOP-P1-L1-01.  
- Infrared surface pyrometer and contact thermocouple as directed in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 for temperature verification.  
- Portable flow meter compatible with induction coil cooling circuit for measurement against the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03).  
- Coil inspection mirror and borescope for internal visual checks.  
- Thermal imaging camera for trend analysis and hotspot identification, used in accordance with SB-1009.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P1-L1-01 and SB-1009.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify isolation and lockout of EQ-P1-L1-IH03 per SOP-P1-L1-01 prior to any invasive inspection. Confirm that power and cooling supplies are secured and that area access is restricted.
- Review previous records for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 for recurring issues referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 and SB-1009 to focus inspection on known weak points.

Visual and mechanical inspection
- Inspect coil external surfaces for scoring, deformation, or discoloration. Use the borescope to inspect internal coil channels and insulation joints. Look for signs of arcing, carbon tracking, or erosion of insulation materials.
- Inspect cooling hose and fittings for chafing, hardening, or contamination. Clean and secure fittings as needed. Rationale: mechanical wear can cause leaks that reduce flow and allow air ingress that degrades cooling effectiveness.

Cooling system verification
- Re-establish cooling supply and check for flow continuity using the portable flow meter placed on the coil circuit. Verify that the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is achieved. Rationale: flow at or above the specified minimum is required to remove heat from the coil and prevent thermal runaway.
- Record flow meter readings and note any transient variability. If flow is below the required minimum, execute corrective actions per SB-1009 and stop heating operations until resolved.

Electrical and control checks
- With power re-applied under controlled conditions per SOP-P1-L1-01, perform insulation resistance checks to the grounded structure using approved test equipment. Observe manufacturer guidance for acceptable procedures as referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Verify control interlocks and safety trips related to coil temperature and cooling flow are operational. Rationale: interlocks are the last line of defense against equipment damage.

Thermal verification
- Run a controlled heat cycle using a representative billet following SOP-P1-L1-01. Use the infrared pyrometer and contact thermocouple to measure billet temperature at the workpiece surface. Confirm that the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is reached within acceptable process behavior as described in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Use the thermal imaging camera to inspect the coil and surrounding structure during heating for any abnormal hotspots identified by SB-1009. Rationale: hotspots indicate cooling deficiency or electrical fault.

Corrective actions
- If coil damage or insulation degradation is found, remove the coil from service and follow repair or replacement actions authorized in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3. Document condition and vendor communications.
- If flow is below the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), trace the circuit for partial blockages, valve settings, or pump performance issues. Implement corrective measures and re-verify flow.

Examples and troubleshooting notes
- Example: If thermal imaging shows a localized hotspot near a coil end connection while measured flow meets the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), inspect the connection for poor contact or degraded insulation. Tighten or replace connectors per manufacturer guidance in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 and re-check thermal signature.
- Example: If billet temperatures fluctuate below the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) despite normal coil condition and cooling flow, verify coil coupling and alignment, and consult the control system diagnostics referenced in SOP-P1-L1-01.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 including inspection findings, flow meter readings, thermal measurements, and actions taken. Cross-reference log to MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 records when repairs are performed.
- Thermal images and pyrometer/thermocouple readings stored in the equipment folder along with flow meter reports. Include any deviation reports generated under SB-1009 and corrective action closure per SOP-P1-L1-01.
- Supplier communication and replacement part documentation when coil repair or replacement is performed.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible coil damage or compromised insulation remaining in service.  
- Coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min as measured during verification.  
- Billet heating performance achieves the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C under normal process conditions as verified by pyrometer or thermocouple.  
- All safety interlocks and alarms pass functional checks and documentation is filed in accordance with SOP-P1-L1-01 and referencing MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 and SB-1009 where applicable.

End of document.

# MM-P1-L2-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Scope
This manual covers preventive maintenance and routine inspection for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) installed in plant P1, line P1-L2. It is intended for use by maintenance technicians qualified on ring rolling equipment and by rotating equipment engineers responsible for reliability and safety. The document addresses mechanical fastening checks on the mandrel assembly, lubrication of the main roll bearing, visual inspections of drive components, and records to be retained. For procedure updates and engineering changes see ECN-2026-041. For operator handover and process-related steps, see SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated to read and apply the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque. Use calibration certificates traceable to plant metrology.
- Manufacturer-approved grease gun and grease cartridges compatible with the main roll bearing.
- Clean lint-free rags, inspection mirror, LED inspection light.
- Bearing puller and mounting sleeves as required for bearing removal and installation during corrective work.
- Lockout/tagout kit compliant with plant P1 standards, electrical and mechanical isolation devices.
- Maintenance tag forms and digital record entry device.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Coordinate with operations using SOP-P1-L2-01 for scheduled downtime and handover. Ensure process temperature is at safe handling condition in accordance with operational procedures prior to work.
- Apply lockout/tagout on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 following plant P1 LOTO protocol. Verify isolation mechanically and electrically before any disassembly.
- Review ECN-2026-041 to confirm that no recent engineering change affects the mandrel clamp or bearing assembly before proceeding.

Mandrel clamp bolt check and torque
- Inspect mandrel area for evidence of fretting, displacement, or shear on clamp hardware. Clean mating surfaces of debris and old lubricant to allow accurate assessment.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the tool to the specified value for the mandrel clamp bolts. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.
- With the wrench, apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt in a crisscross pattern to ensure even seating of the clamp. If any bolt fails to achieve the specified torque due to rounded heads, thread damage, or excessive run-down, do not reuse the bolt; replace per parts list and record the condition.
- After torquing, perform a torque verification pass to confirm retention of the specified torque after a short settling period. Document results in the maintenance record.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm cleanliness of grease fittings and purge contaminant before applying fresh lubricant. Use recommended grease as described in OEM documentation linked in the equipment file.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 145 hours. Maintain a lubrication log indicating start time, end time, and bearing condition at each lubrication event.
- Apply grease until factory-specified purge characteristics are observed from relief points, or until resistance indicates full charge. Avoid overfilling which can lead to thermal and seal issues.
- After lubrication, operate the machine under no-load conditions briefly to redistribute lubricant and then perform a visual check for leaks and seal integrity.

Bearing inspection and replacement
- If bearing condition monitoring or visual inspection indicates abnormal noise, temperature, or lubricant contamination, schedule bearing removal. Follow plant bearing handling practices and use clean staging area to prevent contamination.
- On reinstallation, ensure alignment of mounting surfaces and follow tightness practices described for mandrel clamp bolts where applicable. Retain all removed hardware for inspection and record replacement parts.

Routine visual inspection
- Inspect drive belts, couplings, and guards for wear or looseness. Confirm guard fastenings are secure and safety interlocks are functional.
- Check hydraulic and pneumatic connections for seepage. Any suspected line or fitting requiring tightening should be deferred to a qualified technician following isolation.
- Confirm the condition of electrical cable routing and strain reliefs. Do not perform electrical work without authorization and proper isolation.

Records and examples
- Maintain the maintenance log for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 in the plant document control system. Entries must include date, technician name, work performed, and readings or observations. Reference to related documents ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, and SOP-P1-L2-04 must be included when actions were performed because of or in support of those documents.
- Example entry: “Lubrication performed; main roll bearing reported normal clearance; grease applied per procedure; next lubrication scheduled after the interval recorded in system.” Record the exact interval as specified in this manual.
- Retain torque verification stickers or tags on the equipment with date and technician initials after each mandrel clamp bolt torque event. Archive torque wrench calibration certificate copies with the job file.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts retain the specified torque without evidence of thread stripping, rounding, or seating movement. No relative movement of the mandrel under static inspection after torque application.
- Main roll bearing shows no signs of grease contamination, pitting, or excessive play after lubrication and normal operation. Bearing condition is acceptable if no abnormal noise or heating is observed following the lubricating event and operational checks.
- All guards and safety interlocks remain functional, with no temporary bypasses in place. Any temporary condition must be corrected before return to operation.
- Records contain complete entries referencing ECN-2026-041, SOP-P1-L2-01, or SOP-P1-L2-04 when applicable, and include technician name, date, and observed condition.

Notes and rationale
- Tightness of mandrel clamp bolts directly affects ring concentricity and roll loading; therefore torque specification is enforced as a reliability control. Verification and documentation create an auditable trail.
- Regular lubrication at the specified interval controls contamination and wear in the main roll bearing. The interval balances lubricant life and production availability to maximize bearing life while minimizing unplanned downtime.
- Cross-reference to ECN-2026-041 ensures changes in component design are incorporated into the maintenance baseline. Operator procedures in SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-04 are cited to ensure safe coordination between maintenance and production.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P1-L2-IH02 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-IH02

Scope
This document provides preventive maintenance, inspection, and corrective action guidance for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02). The intent is to ensure consistent billet heating performance, safe operation, and reliable integration with the ring rolling line. Tasks described apply to the heater housing, coil assembly, cooling system, power connections, controls, and instrumentation necessary to meet process targets and safety requirements. Reference procedures and quality requirements are identified at the end of the document; consult those documents for sampling, record retention, and permit requirements.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is a medium-frequency induction billet heater used to heat forging billets prior to ring rolling. Maintaining coil integrity, cooling capacity, and accurate temperature control is critical to achieving metallurgical targets and preventing equipment damage. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. These values are process-critical: temperature directly affects microstructure and formability; cooling water flow prevents coil overheating and insulation failure. Maintenance tasks prioritize checks that ensure these two parameters can be reliably achieved and sustained.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools appropriate for electrical enclosure access
- Multimeter and high-voltage insulation tester for coil and bus inspections
- Portable infrared pyrometer for verification of surface temperatures and component checks related to heat soak
- Flow meter and pressure gauge for cooling loop verification (calibrate per SOP-P1-L2-02 prior to use)
- Leak detection materials and appropriate sealing compounds compatible with cooling circuit materials
- Personal protective equipment compliant with site requirements

Procedure
Preparation
- Lockout and tagout the heater power and energy sources per SOP-P1-L2-04 before opening panels or performing any work. Verify absence of hazardous energy and allow hot components to cool to safe touch levels.
- Review recent operating logs and alarm history for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 to identify recurring trends prior to disassembly.

External inspection
- Inspect external housing for deformation, signs of coolant leakage, or compromised cable entry seals. Confirm integrity of access panels and fasteners.
- Verify routing and strain relief of power and control cabling. Look for discoloration, abrasive wear, or insulation compromise.

Coil assembly and bus checks
- Visually inspect coil for surface cracks, hot spots, or displaced winding supports. Check insulation condition on coil terminations and supports.
- Perform electrical continuity and insulation resistance testing on the coil and buswork using the appropriate test adapters while following safety protocols. Record test values in the maintenance log.
- Verify mechanical retention of coil clamp blocks and supporting brackets. Replace any fasteners or supports that show deformation or looseness.

Cooling system maintenance
- Verify supply and return lines for leaks, erosion, or blockage. Clean strainers and screens in-line with the cooling supply.
- Confirm flow through the coil circuit meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min at nominal pump head. Adjust valves and clean screens as required to achieve minimum flow.
- Inspect heat exchanger surfaces and pump seals for signs of contamination or degradation. Replace sealing elements showing compromise and flush the loop to remove particulate contamination.

Controls and instrumentation
- Confirm that temperature control loops and feedback sensors are free of wiring faults and properly anchored to prevent vibration-induced failure.
- Verify calibration status of temperature measurement devices used for process control; if calibration verification is required, follow SOP-P1-L2-02.
- Check interlock functionality that inhibits heater operation when coil cooling water flow falls below required minimum or when safety doors are open.

Functional verification and example checks
- After reassembly and re-energization, perform a controlled heat cycle to confirm stable operation and verify that the control system can achieve and hold the target billet temperature. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C; use process thermocouples and the control interface to confirm setpoint tracking and stability.
- Monitor coil inlet and outlet water temperature delta and flow indicator to ensure no emergent restriction; flow should not be permitted to operate below the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min.
- Example anomaly: if temperature overshoot occurs with normal flow, suspect control loop tuning or sensor placement; if temperature lag occurs, suspect reduced power transfer or clogged cooling passages.

Corrective actions
- Replace damaged coil insulation or windings in accordance with vendor repair standards. If replacement is performed, re-test insulation resistance and document before returning to service.
- Repair or replace leaking cooling components and flush system to remove particulates. Re-verify flow against the stated minimum.
- If control or sensor replacement is necessary, follow calibration procedures in SOP-P1-L2-02 before returning to production.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil mechanical condition: no visible cracks, broken supports, or loose terminations.
- Electrical insulation and continuity: no insulation test failures and continuity within vendor-specified limits as recorded in the maintenance log.
- Cooling loop performance: measured flow equals or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min with no system leaks or observable cavitation.
- Process performance: heater must be capable of achieving and holding the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C under normal operating load without tripping protective interlocks attributable to heater fault conditions.
- Instrumentation and controls: all safety interlocks and process controls function as designed and calibration records are current per SOP-P1-L2-02.

Records to keep
- Completed maintenance checklist and defect reports stored under the equipment record for EQ-P1-L2-IH02.
- Test results for insulation resistance, continuity, and cooling flow, with instrument identification and calibration references recorded per QS-PROC-02.
- Calibration certificates and replacement part receipts filed with routine maintenance records listed under SOP-P1-L2-04 for permit and safety audit traceability.
- Post-maintenance functional verification report showing achievement of the process target temperature and cooling flow acceptance criteria.

Related documents
- QS-PROC-02
- SOP-P1-L2-02
- SOP-P1-L2-04

# MM-P1-L2-HT03 Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
- This manual defines preventive maintenance and verification tasks for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03).  
- Activities covered include visual inspection, control system verification, thermocouple verification, atmosphere and door seal checks, and record keeping required to support process control for ring rolling heat treat operations.  
- This document is intended for maintenance technicians and process engineers assigned to P1-L2 and references operational procedures for normal use and safety. See SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-04, and SOP-P1-L2-05 for related operational and safety controls.

Background and rationale
- Furnace condition and sensor accuracy directly affect metallurgical outcomes for ring rolling operations. The defined steps aim to provide a repeatable approach to preserve equipment integrity and traceability of actions.  
- Critical control point: austenitizing temperature. Maintaining the setpoint and verifying sensor integrity reduces rework and scrap risk. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C.  
- Sensor drift is a common failure mode. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 95 days. Adhering to this interval supports consistent process control and audit readiness.

Tools
- Hand tools appropriate for electrical and mechanical access as defined in SOP-P1-L2-01.  
- Portable reference thermometer or temperature calibration bath and reference thermocouple traceable to the laboratory standard.  
- Sealant inspection mirror and flashlight.  
- Electrical safety test instrument as specified in SOP-P1-L2-04.  
- Logbook or electronic maintenance record access device and calibrated tags as described in SOP-P1-L2-05.

Procedure
- Pre-checks and safety
  - Confirm furnace is in safe state for maintenance according to SOP-P1-L2-01. Lockout-tagout per plant practice before any mechanical or electrical work begins. Consult SOP-P1-L2-04 for electrical isolation verification.  
  - Review last maintenance record and thermocouple calibration entry in the maintenance log.

- Visual and mechanical inspection
  - Inspect door seals for continuity and integrity. Look for gaps, distortion, or worn material that could allow atmosphere purge loss. Document findings in the maintenance log with a brief description and action taken.  
  - Inspect furnace interior lining for spalling or deformation. Photograph any anomalies and attach images to the maintenance record. Note condition and expected repair plan per SOP-P1-L2-05.

- Control system verification
  - With the furnace in a safe mode, verify operator interface communicates with the controller. Exercise basic control commands as allowed by SOP-P1-L2-01. Record any alarm conditions and reference error codes to the control vendor documentation.  
  - Confirm alarm setpoints and interlocks are present and functioning. Update records with date, technician initials, and any changes.

- Thermocouple verification and calibration
  - Remove thermocouple covers and inspect leads for mechanical damage, oxidation, and secure connections. Replace leads if insulation or sheath is compromised. Record parts replaced and serial tags used.  
  - Perform calibration check using the reference thermometer or calibration bath. Compare readings at stable points representative of operating range. If drift exceeds allowable tolerance defined in plant calibration policy, replace or recalibrate the thermocouple assembly. Document outcomes in the calibration worksheet.  
  - The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 95 days. Schedule next calibration in the maintenance management system and attach calibration certificate to the equipment file.

- Atmosphere and purge systems
  - Inspect purge line connections and flow indicators. Verify that purge delivery hardware is secure and free of leaks. Replace any suspect fittings and log replacements.  
  - Verify the furnace atmosphere monitoring system is reporting correctly and that sample points are unobstructed.

- Post-maintenance verification
  - Bring the furnace back to an operational ready state in accordance with SOP-P1-L2-01. Run a controlled heat cycle if permitted to verify that the controller reaches the austenitizing setpoint and holds stability. Log cycle data and attach waveform capture if available.  
  - Update maintenance records with a summary of work performed, parts replaced, calibration certificates, and recommended follow-up actions.

Acceptance criteria
- All mechanical defects identified are addressed or scheduled for corrective action; documentation includes photographic evidence and action plans.  
- Thermocouple calibration results are within the plant allowable tolerance or the thermocouple has been replaced and a certificate attached. The calibration date and next due date are entered into the maintenance management system consistent with the thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 95 days.  
- Control verification demonstrates stable control at the target process value. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C; recorded cycle data must show controller reaching and holding this setpoint during verification.  
- No active safety interlocks are bypassed and all lockout-tagout steps are released following verification procedures in SOP-P1-L2-04.  
- Records to keep
  - Maintenance log entry including date, technician name, summary of work, and follow-up actions.  
  - Photograph attachments for door seals and refractory condition.  
  - Calibration certificate for the thermocouple and reference instrument.  
  - Controller data exports demonstrating attainment and control at the austenitizing setpoint.  
  - Copy of any purchase orders or parts replacement receipts and serial numbers tied to equipment file per SOP-P1-L2-05.

Notes and examples
- Example entry: maintenance record indicating thermocouple replaced, calibration certificate attached, next calibration scheduled per interval. Include the reason for replacement such as documented drift or physical damage.  
- Use the related SOPs for specific safety and isolation steps: SOP-P1-L2-01 for operational checks, SOP-P1-L2-04 for electrical procedures, and SOP-P1-L2-05 for records and traceability.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

# MM-P1-L3-IH01 - Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Scope
- This document defines required maintenance tasks, rationale, and acceptance criteria for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01). It is intended for maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for upkeep of the induction heater in the P1, line P1-L3 machining cell.
- Tasks covered include inspection of the induction coil and water cooling circuit, verification of control interlocks, replacement of wear items, and functional checks after maintenance.
- Refer to ECN-2026-005 for design changes applicable to this equipment and to SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05 for operational start/stop and safety procedures.

Background and rationale
- The induction heater raises billets to the target billet temperature for downstream machining operations. Maintaining coil integrity and cooling performance prevents overheating, reduces the risk of coil failure, and preserves metallurgical quality before machining.
- The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. This value is the process requirement for the machining cell; deviations can affect part geometry and tool life.
- Coil cooling water is the primary method to remove heat from the coil assembly. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Maintaining at or above this flow prevents coil temperature rise that can lead to insulation damage and premature failure.
- This manual focuses on tasks that directly affect temperature control and cooling performance. Non-critical cleaning and housekeeping are covered in SOP-P1-L3-03.

Tools
- Multimeter capable of verifying low-voltage control signals and continuity.
- Portable flow meter compatible with the plant cooling water system for spot-check verification.
- Infrared thermal scanner for surface temperature trend checks on accessible coil housings (do not use for process temperature calibration).
- Torque tools are not specified here; use manufacturer torque requirements referenced in ECN-2026-005 where applicable.
- Insulated hand tools for electrical isolation work.
- Lockout/tagout kit per SOP-P1-L3-05.

Procedure
Preparation
- Notify production and operations per SOP-P1-L3-03 before starting maintenance. Confirm that the heater is placed in a maintenance hold condition and that material feed is stopped.
- Apply lockout/tagout following SOP-P1-L3-05 on all energy sources to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, including electrical and hydraulic supplies. Verify zero energy state before any disassembly.

Visual inspection
- Inspect coil assembly for signs of physical damage: cracks in coil housing, discoloration indicating overheating, and loosened fasteners. Replace any components found delaminated or with obvious insulation damage; consult ECN-2026-005 for replacement part references.
- Inspect cooling water hoses and connections for chafing, kinks, or leaks. Replace hoses showing wear or compromised fittings.

Cooling circuit verification
- With the system returned to a drained and isolated condition per SOP-P1-L3-05, attach the portable flow meter to a test point on the coil cooling inlet or to the maintenance bypass as allowed by plant procedures.
- Reintroduce cooling water under controlled conditions and verify flow. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. If flow is below this value, troubleshoot upstream filters, pump supply, and strainer conditions before returning to service.
- Check for proper routing of hoses to ensure there are no high points where air could be trapped; purge air as required by plant water system practice in SOP-P1-L3-03.

Electrical and control checks
- Inspect control wiring and connections for evidence of overheating or corrosion. Verify continuity of primary interlock circuits using the multimeter.
- Inspect power contactors and control relays for pitting or excessive wear; replace per ECN-2026-005 guidance where specified.
- Verify that thermal and flow interlocks are present and configured to alert or shut down when cooling flow is below the specified minimum or when coil temperatures exceed safe operating limits.

Functional verification
- After completing inspections and repairs, return the equipment to service per SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05. Conduct a staged bring-up with close monitoring of control alarms and cooling flow.
- Confirm through process indications that billets reach the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 1235 °C as indicated by the process control system or calibrated process pyrometers. If the control system indicates difficulty attaining or holding this temperature, document deviations and escalate to process engineering with reference to ECN-2026-005.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example: If cooling flow measures below 79 L/min and strainers are clean, suspect pump cavitation or upstream valve position. Verify valve alignment and pump condition per plant pump maintenance practices and escalate if necessary.
- Example: If coil surface shows localized hot spots on thermal scan, inspect for loose coil clamps or degraded insulation and replace affected coil segments per ECN-2026-005.

Records to keep
- Maintain a maintenance log entry for each intervention that includes:
  - Equipment id: EQ-P1-L3-IH01
  - Date and revision id: Rev C
  - Description of work performed and parts replaced with reference to ECN-2026-005 when applicable
  - Measured coil cooling water flow value(s) and indication that coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min was verified
  - Verified process indication that target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C or notes on deviation
  - Names and signatures of technician and supervisor
- Retain instrument calibration records for the portable flow meter and thermal scanner used to verify conditions.
- File copies of any non-conformance reports and follow-up corrective actions linked to ECN-2026-005 references.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil cooling water flow at the measurement point meets or exceeds coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 79 L/min.
- No visible coil insulation damage or loose fasteners remain after maintenance; any replaced components are recorded with ECN-2026-005 part guidance.
- Control interlocks and alarms for cooling flow and temperature are functional and verified to actuate per SOP-P1-L3-05 during simulated fault conditions.
- Process control indicates billets reach the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 1235 °C under normal operating load or documented deviations are entered and addressed with process engineering.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-005
- SOP-P1-L3-03
- SOP-P1-L3-05
title: Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #1

# MM-P1-L3-HP02 - Maintenance manual - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

Scope
- This manual defines required preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for Machining hydraulic forging press #2, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, while installed in Plant P1, line P1-L3.
- Applies to mechanical and hydraulic systems directly associated with the main ram and primary pressure control loop. Does not cover ancillary electrical control cabinet repairs that are governed by separate electrical procedures and lockout/tagout policies.
- Refer to related design changes and operating procedures before any modification: ECN-2026-035, SOP-P1-L3-03, SOP-P1-L3-04.

Background and rationale
- The main ram is the critical load-bearing component for forging operations on EQ-P1-L3-HP02. Proper clamping of the ram retention assembly and maintenance of hydraulic system pressure containment are the primary contributors to machine safety and process stability.
- The specified main ram bolt torque and the system pressure limit are mandatory design values verified during machine commissioning and after any disassembly of the ram assembly. These values reflect manufacturer requirements and engineering change orders documented in ECN-2026-035.
- This manual provides clear, auditable steps to achieve and verify those values without introducing new numeric specifications beyond the approved design data.

Tools
- Calibrated hydraulic torque wrench compatible with socket fittings used on EQ-P1-L3-HP02 main ram bolts.
- Certified pressure gauge or calibrated pressure transducer with appropriate fittings for the system test port(s).
- Appropriate lifting and rigging gear certified for the mass of the ram assembly (use rigging per plant standard).
- Standard mechanical hand tools as required for disassembly and reassembly of ram retention hardware.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE): eye protection, gloves, hearing protection, steel-toe footwear, and any PPE required by SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-04.
- Maintenance log forms and the machine history folder for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.

Procedure
- Preliminary verification
  - Confirm machine is isolated and secured according to SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-04. Confirm permit-to-work and responsible technician assignments are recorded in the maintenance log.
  - Review the machine history folder and ECN-2026-035 for any special instructions or deviations that affect the ram assembly.

- Access and prepare the main ram assembly
  - De-pressurize the hydraulic system by following approved steps in SOP-P1-L3-03. Ensure pressure test points are accessible and clear of obstructions.
  - Use certified lifting equipment to support the ram if partial disassembly is required. Ensure rigging is attached at designated lift points.

- Fastener torque verification and application
  - Clean bolt threads and seating faces. Inspect hardware for wear or damage; replace per manufacturer guidance if any defect compromises integrity.
  - Using the calibrated hydraulic torque wrench, apply and verify the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m. Document the torque reading and the wrench calibration ID in the maintenance record.
  - Rationale: Achieving the specified torque ensures proper preload to resist axial loads and prevent fretting or fatigue failure during forging cycles. Under-torqued fasteners can loosen; over-torqued fasteners can induce material yielding—both conditions risk structural failure.

- Hydraulic pressure verification
  - Refill and purge hydraulic fluid per fluid supplier and SOP-P1-L3-04. Restore system to standby condition following isolation procedures.
  - Connect the certified pressure gauge to the system test port as specified in the machine drawing set and ECN-2026-035.
  - Bring the pressure control system online per SOP-P1-L3-04 and monitor at the test port to confirm the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Record static and controlled readings and the gauge calibration ID in the maintenance record.
  - Rationale: Confirming the pressure limit ensures relief valves and control components are set to prevent overpressure events that could compromise pressure-containing assemblies.

- Functional checks and reassembly
  - Cycle the machine through a supervised check cycle per SOP-P1-L3-04 to confirm stable operation. Observe for leaks at fittings, unusual noises from the ram area, and consistent position control.
  - If leaks or anomalies are detected, return the machine to safe hold and complete corrective repairs per governing procedures. Do not proceed until resolved and re-verified.

- Examples and special cases
  - Example record entry: "Main ram bolts torqued to 1330 N·m using wrench ID W-234 (cal date noted). Pressure verified 295 bar at test port using gauge G-87 (cal date noted). No leaks observed. Signed: Technician name, Permit ID."
  - If an ECN modifies hardware affecting the torque or pressure values, update records and notify maintenance scheduling to ensure future work follows the revised specifications. Cross-reference ECN-2026-035 in any such entries.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry documenting technician, date, permit ID, torque wrench ID, torque value (1330 N·m), pressure gauge ID, pressure reading (295 bar), and observations.
- Copies of torque wrench and pressure gauge calibration certificates used during the task.
- Any nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation linked to the machine history folder and traced to ECN-2026-035 where applicable.

Acceptance criteria
- Visual and mechanical inspection: No evidence of thread damage, hardware deformation, or compromised sealing surfaces in the ram assembly after reassembly.
- Torque acceptance: Main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) shall be recorded as 1330 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench; calibration ID must be recorded.
- Pressure acceptance: System pressure reading at the specified test port shall be recorded as 295 bar using a calibrated gauge; calibration ID must be recorded.
- Functional acceptance: Machine completes supervised check cycle without leakage, abnormal noise, or control instability. Any deviation requires troubleshooting, corrective action, and re-verification before return to service.

References
- ECN-2026-035
- SOP-P1-L3-03
- SOP-P1-L3-04

End of document.
title: Maintenance manual - Machining hydraulic forging press #2
