# MM-P1-L3-CN03 Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, required tools, stepwise procedure, rationale and acceptance criteria for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) at P1-L3. It supplements standard operating procedures referenced below and provides equipment‑specific instructions that are not covered in generic documents. Use this manual when performing scheduled maintenance, after corrective interventions on the spindle or chuck, and when restoring the machine to service following extended downtime. Related documents: MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1, SOP-P1-L3-01, SOP-P1-L3-03.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L3-CN03 is a high‑use machining center with a hydraulic chuck and precision spindle. Proper maintenance of the chuck and spindle affects concentricity, part quality and tool life. The procedures below emphasize prestart warm‑up and fastener integrity checks to prevent runout and abrupt failures. The spindle warm‑up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 27 minutes. This warm‑up minimizes thermal gradients in the spindle bearings and housing prior to precision boring or finish turning operations. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 95 N·m. That torque value is the required clamp on the chuck jaw bolts after any service that removes or adjusts jaws.

Tools
List of tools and materials required for the procedures below:
- Torque wrench capable of the specified torque range and with a calibrated readout.
- Appropriate socket and extension to access chuck jaw bolts.
- Manufacturer‑approved hydraulic fluid and lubricant as per MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.
- Clean, lint‑free rags and solvent for degreasing contact surfaces.
- Dial indicator or runout gauge for spindle and chuck verification.
- Personal protective equipment as required in SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-03.
- Maintenance log forms and nonconformance report forms as specified in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.

Procedure
Preparation
- Confirm lockout/tagout and electrical isolation per SOP-P1-L3-01 before starting any maintenance that exposes moving parts or hydraulic components.
- Review equipment history and previous maintenance notes in the local maintenance log and MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 to identify recurring issues.

Spindle warm‑up
- With the machine powered and in a safe state per SOP-P1-L3-03, initiate the spindle warm‑up sequence according to the machine control panel instructions.
- Maintain the spindle at controlled speeds and load profile recommended by the machine vendor until the spindle warm‑up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is reached.
- After warm‑up, verify bearing temperature stabilization by observation of the control panel and by touch at safe contact points only when permitted by SOP-P1-L3-01.

Chuck jaw inspection and torque verification
- Retract chuck jaws and clean mating surfaces with approved solvent. Inspect jaws and jaw seats for wear, cracks or score marks. Log any anomalies.
- Reassemble jaws and hand‑tighten to seat them. Using the calibrated torque wrench, set and apply the chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) to the specified value.
- Apply torque in a cross pattern to ensure even seating. Confirm each bolt reaches the specified torque. If the wrench cannot achieve the torque due to rounding of the bolt head or seized threads, tag as nonconforming and escalate per MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.

Runout and function checks
- Mount a test bar or gauge per SOP-P1-L3-03 and measure radial runout with the dial indicator. Record pre‑ and post‑torque readings.
- Conduct a low‑speed test cut or spindle rotation to observe vibration, noises, and stability. If excessive runout or vibration persists after correct torque and warm‑up, follow escalation steps in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.

Hydraulic and lubrication systems
- Inspect hydraulic lines and fittings for leaks and degradation. Replace seals only with manufacturer‑approved parts as referenced in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.
- Top up or change lubricant according to the schedule and products listed in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If jaw bolt threads are damaged, document the thread condition with photographs, remove the bolt and replace with manufacturer‑specified fastener per MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1. After replacement, perform the torque sequence and runout verification steps.
- Example: If spindle temperature stabilizes slowly during warm‑up, extend the controlled speed ramp (per vendor guidance in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1) and verify environmental factors such as coolant temperature and ambient drafts per SOP-P1-L3-01.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry that includes date, technician name, tasks performed, the spindle warm‑up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) was achieved, the chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) was applied, and all measurement results.
- Photographs of any defects or deviations.
- Torque wrench calibration certificate reference and the calibration date recorded per MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.
- Nonconformance reports filed according to MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 when acceptance criteria are not met.

Acceptance criteria
- Spindle acceptance: After completion of the warm‑up sequence and verification steps, spindle behavior must be free of abnormal vibration and abnormal noises as assessed by the technician and documented in the maintenance log.
- Runout acceptance: Radial runout must be within the limits specified in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 when measured with the dial indicator following the torque application procedure.
- Fastener acceptance: All chuck jaw bolts must be tightened to the chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) and show no evidence of slippage, rounding or thread damage.
- Hydraulic and lubrication acceptance: No active hydraulic leaks and lubrication levels within the bounds specified in MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1.

If any acceptance criterion is not met, stop machine use and notify maintenance supervision per MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1. Complete corrective actions, document all findings and re‑verify per this manual and SOP-P1-L3-03 before returning EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to production service.

# MM-P1-L4-CN01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Scope
This maintenance manual covers preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 identified as EQ-P1-L4-CN01. It describes the tools required, the recommended procedure for warm-up, chuck jaw bolt torque verification, inspection points relevant to heat treat production, and the acceptance criteria for return to service. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance technicians assigned to P1-L4 and for use in coordination with operating procedures. Consult related documents MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2, SB-1046, and SOP-P1-L4-01 for complementary electrical, safety bulletin, and operator-level instructions.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L4-CN01 operates in a heat treat cell and components are exposed to thermal cycling. Proper warm-up prevents thermal shock to bearings and spindle seals and stabilizes dimensions before machining critical features. Correct chuck jaw bolt torque secures workholding and reduces the risk of jaw slippage or part ejection during turning operations. The values specified in this manual reflect OEM recommendations and plant validation for stable production and safety.

Tools
- Torque wrench capable of applying and holding the specified torque for chuck jaw bolts; use the torque head recommended by the tool supplier.  
- Socket or bit compatible with chuck jaw bolt heads specified on EQ-P1-L4-CN01.  
- Infrared thermometer or surface temperature indicator for non-contact verification of spindle housing temperature.  
- Clean, lint-free rags and approved solvent for degreasing contact faces.  
- Permanent maintenance log or electronic maintenance record entry device for documentation.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P1-L4-01 and SB-1046.

Procedure
Overview: Perform operations in a controlled sequence to warm the spindle, inspect, set chuck jaw bolt torque, and record results. Follow lockout/tagout and machine-specific safety checks in SOP-P1-L4-01 before starting any mechanical work.

Warm-up
Begin warm-up with the machine powered and in a safe condition for unattended spindle rotation per SOP-P1-L4-01. Run the spindle through a progressive ramp to operating speed to bring bearings and seals to thermal equilibrium. Maintain continuous rotation for the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes to achieve dimensional stability and reduce the risk of concentricity error once heavy cuts begin. Use the infrared thermometer to verify uniform warming of the spindle housing; allow the warm-up routine to complete fully before proceeding to clamp verification.

Inspection
After warm-up, perform a visual inspection of the chuck, jaws, and surrounding guard. Clean all mating surfaces and remove swarf and debris from the chuck throat. Inspect jaw threads and bolt heads for signs of galling, wear, or corrosion. If damage is suspected, escalate per the corrective maintenance flow in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.

Torque verification and adjustment
Ensure the chuck is in the safe maintenance position and that power and motion state comply with SOP-P1-L4-01 controls for securing tooling. Using the torque wrench, verify and, if required, tighten the chuck jaw bolts to the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m. Apply torque in a star pattern across the jaw bolts to distribute clamp load evenly and to avoid inducing uneven stress. If bolts repeatedly lose torque or show signs of thread stripping, remove the jaw assembly and follow the component repair procedure in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.

Examples and special cases
- Example: For a workpiece showing axial runout after initial clamping, re-run the warm-up routine and re-verify the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m before attempting further corrections.  
- Example: If the spindle feels rough during warm-up, stop the machine and follow inspection checklist in SB-1046 before resuming. Do not proceed to production until mechanical integrity is confirmed.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance entry for each action taken. Each record must include the following fields: equipment id, maintenance technician identifier, reason for maintenance, actions performed (including notation that the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes was completed), torque values observed and applied with notation that the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m was used, any parts replaced or escalated, and references to related documents cited in this manual. Store logs in the plant maintenance record system and attach any relevant photos or torque wrench calibration stickers per SB-1046.

Acceptance criteria
Return to service is allowed only when all of the following are confirmed:
- Visual inspection shows no damage or excessive wear to chuck jaws, jaw bolts, or mating surfaces.  
- Warm-up procedure completed and documented indicating the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes was performed.  
- All jaw bolts verified and set to the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m and torque wrench readings recorded.  
- No abnormal noise or vibration observed during a monitored run at machine idle and during a no-load spindle acceleration as defined in SOP-P1-L4-01.  
- Maintenance entries and any required escalation actions recorded and accessible alongside MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 and SB-1046 references.

Related documents
MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2  
SB-1046  
SOP-P1-L4-01
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

# MM-P1-L4-HP02 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Scope
This manual covers planned and reactive maintenance activities for the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press identified as EQ-P1-L4-HP02 in line P1-L4. It defines approved tools, safety controls, stepwise procedures for mechanical and hydraulic maintenance actions, acceptance criteria for returned-to-service condition, and recordkeeping expectations. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance technicians trained on press systems and controls and operating under the plant maintenance policy. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-01, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-03 for operational procedures and lockout/tagout requirements.

Background and rationale
The hydraulic forging press is a high-energy mechanical system where fastener integrity and hydraulic pressure management are critical for safe operation and product quality. Main ram retention hardware and system pressure controls are key failure modes. The main ram bolt is the primary restraint for the ram assembly; its clamping preload must be verified and maintained to ensure alignment and prevent progressive loosening that can lead to catastrophic component separation. The hydraulic system pressure limit is set to protect seals, hoses, and pressure vessels while maintaining forging capability. Adhering to specified bolt clamping and pressure limits preserves press life and reduces unplanned downtime.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of achieving the specified main ram bolt torque.
- Hydraulic system pressure gauge calibrated to plant standards for verification against the system pressure limit.
- Manufacturer-approved fastener retention compound where required by OEM procedures.
- Clean rags, appropriate lifting and support stands, and non-marring drift tools for component alignment.
- Lockout/tagout kit and personal protective equipment per SOP-P1-L4-02.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Coordinate with production and maintenance supervision to schedule the work window and confirm isolation of press electrical and hydraulic sources per SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Apply lockout/tagout and verify zero energy state on the press. Confirm notification of affected operators per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Inspect the work area for hazards and ensure suitable lighting and access. Assemble tools and verify calibration certificates for torque and pressure instruments.

Main ram bolt verification and torque application
- Support the ram assembly to remove axial load from the main ram bolt before any measurement or torque application. Use only suitable mechanical supports and stands rated for the assembly weight.
- Clean bolt threads and clamping surfaces to remove corrosion, debris, and old compound. If the OEM indicates a retention compound is required, apply manufacturer-approved compound sparingly to the threads per product datasheet.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the wrench to the main ram bolt torque specified for EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.
- Apply torque in controlled increments to achieve final specified torque. If multiple torquing passes are recommended by the OEM, follow their sequence while maintaining alignment of the ram assembly.
- After torquing, inspect the bolt and surrounding components for proper seating and absence of distortion or damage.

Hydraulic system pressure verification
- With mechanical work complete and supports verified, remove isolation devices per SOP-P1-L4-02 and slowly reintroduce hydraulic supply while monitoring for leaks and abnormal noise.
- Use the calibrated pressure gauge to confirm that no pressure source exceeds the system pressure limit for this press. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar.
- If any component forces system pressure above the specified limit during normal operation or test cycles, cease operation and follow fault isolation procedures in SOP-P1-L4-03.

Functional checks and run-in
- Perform controlled operational cycles at low actuator demand to confirm proper ram guidance, smooth travel, and absence of binding. Observe hydraulic manifold for leaks or pressure spikes and listen for unusual sounds.
- Validate safety interlocks and emergency stop functions per SOP-P1-L4-01 before returning the press to production.

Examples and diagnostic notes
- Example condition: observable thread damage on main ram bolt. Rationale: damaged threads cannot reliably retain required preload; replace bolt per OEM parts guidance and re-torque to the specified value after installation and verification of thread integrity.
- Example condition: transient pressure spike observed during initial run-in that approaches the specified limit. Rationale: spikes near the system limit may indicate relief valve drift, blocked return, or actuator binding. Isolate hydraulic circuit, drain to safe condition, and inspect relief valves and actuator seals per SOP-P1-L4-03.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical: main ram bolt is torqued to the specified value and shows no signs of thread stripping, head rounding, or component distortion. Fastener seating surfaces are clean and secure.
- Hydraulic: system pressure during static and dynamic checks does not exceed the system pressure limit and operates smoothly without uncontained fluid leaks.
- Functional: press completes operational checks with safety interlocks functioning and no abnormal vibration, noise, or thermal anomalies noted during run-in.
- Records: all inspection results, torque wrench calibration references, pressure gauge calibration references, part replacement notes, and signatures of performing and verifying technicians must be recorded. Include date and reference to this document id and revision.

Records to keep
- Work order or maintenance ticket referencing this manual id MM-P1-L4-HP02 and revision Rev B.
- Torque application log showing the instrument ID and calibration reference used when applying the main ram bolt torque.
- Hydraulic pressure verification log showing the pressure instrument ID and calibration reference used when confirming the system pressure limit.
- Photographic evidence of bolt condition and torque marking where applicable, and any replacement fastener or component serial traces.
- Incident or deviation report if acceptance criteria are not met, including corrective action and re-verification notes.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L4-01
- SOP-P1-L4-02
- SOP-P1-L4-03

Revision control
Maintain this document in the controlled document system. Update only through the approved document change process and reference change justification when revising.

# MM-P1-L4-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance, calibration, and verification tasks required to maintain the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, in a condition that ensures process control and product conformance. The scope covers austenitizing controls, thermocouple calibration, control loop checks, door seals, atmosphere control verification, and recordkeeping required by plant quality and safety programs. Related documents include ECN-2026-002, SB-1006, and SOP-P1-L4-02 and must be consulted for change notices, safety bulletins, and operating procedures.

Background and rationale
The furnace is used for critical heat treat cycles where core microstructure and mechanical properties are sensitive to temperature uniformity and setpoint accuracy. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Maintaining accurate temperature measurement and control at this setpoint is essential to avoid under- or over-austenitizing, which can lead to nonconforming forgings. Thermocouple drift and control loop degradation are the most common sources of process deviation; therefore, a dedicated calibration and verification regimen is required. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated reference temperature source appropriate for high-temperature thermocouple checks (refer to SB-1006 for equipment approval).  
- Portable thermocouple calibrator and cold-junction reference.  
- Replacement thermocouple elements and connectors approved for use in EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Door seal inspection kit and approved gasketing materials.  
- Logbooks, electronic maintenance entry device, or CMMS entry template per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by ECN-2026-002 and plant safety rules.

Procedure
Prepare
- Review applicable process setpoints and recent furnace run history in the electronic records system. Cross-reference any recent engineering changes per ECN-2026-002 before starting work.  
- Notify production and quality leads of planned maintenance and obtain furnace lockout/tagout in accordance with plant safety procedures referenced in SB-1006. Ensure all personnel are trained per SOP-P1-L4-02.

Thermocouple verification and calibration
- Verify the last calibration record in the CMMS or logbook. If the interval since last calibration exceeds the allowed interval, schedule calibration. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 95 days.  
- Remove the thermocouple probe following manufacturer handling procedures. Inspect the probe for mechanical damage, insulation breakdown, or contamination. Replace if any defect is found.  
- Perform a two-point check using a calibrated reference source and ambient reference. Document offsets and calculate correction factors. Record raw readings and corrected values in the calibration record.  
- Reinstall the thermocouple in the original sensing location. Verify the cold-junction compensation is set and that connector types match control panel inputs.

Control setpoint and loop check
- With the furnace empty and at a safe state, bring the control system up and confirm the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C in the controller configuration. Confirm that the setpoint stored in the controller matches the shop floor operating sheet.  
- Execute a control loop exercise to observe controller response to setpoint changes and confirm that output signals actuate the heating elements or power control devices correctly. Document any asymmetric response or oscillation. Note: do not alter PID parameters without engineering approval per ECN-2026-002.

Mechanical checks and atmosphere verification
- Inspect door seals and gasketing for integrity. Replace degraded seals and document material batch per the parts log. Check door latching hardware for smooth engagement.  
- Verify atmosphere feed and exhaust paths for obstructions. If furnace uses controlled atmosphere, confirm oxygen sensor signals are within expected ranges relative to recorded history. If any deviation exists, tag the furnace out and escalate.

Example corrective action scenarios
- If thermocouple offset exceeds acceptable tolerance documented in SB-1006, replace the thermocouple element and re-run calibration. Record reason for replacement and serial of replacement part.  
- If door seal condition results in measurable heat loss during a verification cycle, replace seal and document energy loss comparison before and after replacement as evidence of correction.

Records to keep
- Calibration certificate for thermocouple including raw readings, correction factors, technician name, and reference equipment identifier. File per SOP-P1-L4-02.  
- Maintenance activity log entry detailing tasks performed, observations, parts replaced, and any process deviations. Include operator and supervisor signoff.  
- Control configuration snapshot showing setpoint and controller model data. Attach any ECN-2026-002 references if configuration differs from baseline.  
- Safety and lockout documentation per SB-1006.

Acceptance criteria
The furnace shall be returned to service only when all of the following conditions are met:
- Thermocouple calibration records show readings within acceptable limits after correction, and the thermocouple is reinstalled with connectors secured.  
- Controller setpoint for austenitizing is confirmed at 880 °C and matches the documented operating sheet used in production.  
- No mechanical defects remain that could compromise temperature uniformity or furnace sealing.  
- All records described above are completed, reviewed, and filed in the CMMS per SOP-P1-L4-02, and the maintenance entry is signed by the responsible technician and reviewer.

Notes and references
- Follow ECN-2026-002 for engineering change implementation.  
- Consult SB-1006 for approved safety devices and PPE requirements.  
- Use SOP-P1-L4-02 for CMMS and recordkeeping workflows.

# MM-P2-L1-RR01 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Scope
- This document defines preventative maintenance tasks, acceptance criteria, and records for the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) used in plant P2, line P2-L1.
- Tasks are intended to be performed by trained maintenance technicians in accordance with governing procedures: ECN-2026-023, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-02.
- The manual covers mechanical clamp inspection and lubrication of the main roll bearing, explaining rationale, method, and documentation requirements. Repairs beyond scope shall be referred to engineering under ECN-2026-023.

Tools
- Torque wrench capable of the required setting for the mandrel clamp. Verify calibration traceable to plant calibration program per SOP-P2-L1-01.
- Standard hand tools for access panels and fastener removal as required by SOP-P2-L1-02.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent for surface cleaning.
- Grease gun compatible with machine lubrication fittings and the grease specified in SOP-P2-L1-02.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P2-L1-01.

Procedure
Background and rationale
- The mandrel clamp maintains axial position and radial engagement of the ring during forming operations. Correct clamp bolt torque ensures consistent clamp preload, prevents slippage, and avoids localized overload on mating components.
- The main roll bearing supports the primary rolling element and requires consistent lubrication to prevent metal-to-metal contact and progressive wear. Lubrication interval is based on operating load and environment; adhere to the specified service interval to reduce bearing fatigue risk.

Step sequence
- Prepare the machine following SOP-P2-L1-01 and lockout/tagout per SOP-P2-L1-02 before accessing the mandrel clamp or main roll bearing areas.
- Clean exterior of the mandrel clamp assembly using approved solvent and lint-free rags. Inspect surfaces for signs of wear, corrosion, fretting, or deformation. Note any scoring or non-uniform contact patterns.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, verify the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. If torque is below the specified value, tighten to 430 N·m. If bolt requires torque above 430 N·m to reach specification, stop and escalate per ECN-2026-023 for further engineering assessment.
- After torque confirmation, cycle the clamp through its normal engagement travel by following SOP-P2-L1-01 operational checks (static movement only while in a safe, locked state). Observe for smooth clamping action, consistent seating, and absence of abnormal noises.
- Access the lubrication point for the main roll bearing per machine access panels. Prime the grease gun with the approved lubricant from SOP-P2-L1-02 and purge any air in the line.
- Lubricate the main roll bearing at the established service point. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 220 hours. Record the service in the maintenance log immediately after completion.
- After lubrication, operate the bearing manually where safe and practical to distribute lubricant. Inspect seals and relubrication fittings for damage or contamination. Replace any compromised seals per SOP-P2-L1-02 and notify engineering under ECN-2026-023 if replacement parts are different from original specification.

Examples and special conditions
- Example: If post-torque inspection reveals uneven clamp seating, mark the affected face and compare to prior inspection records. If repeat occurrence is observed, raise an ECN-2026-023 change request for investigation.
- Example: If grease expelled from bearing seals appears contaminated or shows metal particulate, secure the machine, take a grease sample per SOP-P2-L1-02 sampling protocol, and submit to condition monitoring. Escalate immediately under ECN-2026-023 if wear particles indicate abnormal degradation.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each task including technician initials, date, time in/out, tasks performed, and observations. Include the exact torque verification statement: mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m.
- Lubrication register entry indicating the main roll bearing lubrication interval adherence: main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 220 hours. Include cumulative hours run since last lubrication as recorded in equipment runtime log per SOP-P2-L1-01.
- Any nonconformances or escalation actions referenced to ECN-2026-023 must be recorded with ECN id and a brief description of the issue.
- Store photographs of clamp condition and bearing seals in the maintenance record when anomalies are observed.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification complete and recorded. Acceptance criterion: torque reading matches the specified value and clamp seating is uniform. If torque confirmation cannot be achieved without abnormal tightening, the component is not acceptable until engineering review under ECN-2026-023.
- Main roll bearing lubrication performed within the defined interval and recorded. Acceptance criterion: lubrication entry shows adherence to the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 220 hours and post-lubrication inspection shows seals intact and no contamination.
- No leakage, abnormal noise, or excessive play observed after maintenance actions. If any of these conditions are present, the machine shall not be returned to service until corrective actions are completed and documented per ECN-2026-023.

References
- ECN-2026-023
- SOP-P2-L1-01
- SOP-P2-L1-02

Notes
- Follow training and competency verification requirements in SOP-P2-L1-01 before performing these tasks.
- For part replacement or design changes, submit documentation through ECN-2026-023.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

text:
# MM-P2-L1-IH02 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
- This manual defines required maintenance activities, inspection rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2, equipment id EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Applies to mechanical, electrical, and cooling subsystems that directly affect billet heating performance and operator safety.
- Related change documents and procedures: ECN-2026-013, ECN-2026-039, SOP-P2-L1-01.

Background and purpose
- EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is an induction billet heater used to prepare billets for hot forging operations on line P2-L1. Proper maintenance ensures consistent heating profile, coil integrity, and cooling system reliability.
- The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. Achieving and holding this target requires verified coil geometry, correct power delivery, and adequate coil cooling.
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Maintaining at-or-above this flow prevents coil overheating and rapid insulation degradation.
- This manual focuses on preventive measures and acceptance checks that mitigate unplanned downtime and extend component life.

Tools
- Standard electrical troubleshooting kit capable of verifying continuity and insulation resistance.
- Pressure-rated hose and fittings compatible with the plant cooling water supply and hose connection hardware on EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Thermal imaging device for surface temperature mapping and verification of uniform heat distribution across the billet path.
- Non-destructive inspection tools for coil and busbar inspection (visual magnifier, borescope).
- Torque tools and calibration certificates are maintained per plant calibration control. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-01 for tool control and calibration traceability.

Procedure
- General approach: Perform visual and functional inspections, verify cooling flow, and map heating performance. Record observations in the equipment maintenance log and attach supporting data from thermal imaging and flow verification.
- Pre-maintenance safety: Isolate EQ-P2-L1-IH02 from power and lockout per SOP-P2-L1-01. Verify cooling water valves are in the safe position and draining is complete before accessing coil assemblies. Confirm with the shift supervisor before proceeding.
- Coil and busbar inspection: Visually inspect coil windings for signs of insulation cracking, coolant leakage, or displacement. Use borescope to inspect internal turns where accessible. Inspect busbar connections for discoloration or loose connectors. Clean external surfaces with compatible solvents and lint-free cloths as required.
- Cooling system verification: Connect a calibrated flow indicator to the coil supply line and verify the coil cooling water flow is at or above 55 L/min. If flow is below the minimum, do not operate the heater. Trace and repair restricted sections in the supply line, verify inlet and outlet valves, and remove any inline strainers for inspection and cleaning. Record pre- and post-repair flow values in the maintenance log.
- Electrical checks: With power isolated, perform insulation resistance tests on coil windings per plant electrical standards. Verify continuity and absence of short circuits before reapplying power. Inspect power feed connectors and contactors for wear; replace per vendor guidance if degradation is evident.
- Functional heat mapping: After completing mechanical and electrical checks and restoring normal coolant flow, restore power and perform a controlled heat validation using a test billet or calibrated thermal simulator. Use thermal imaging device to map temperature uniformity across the billet path and verify the billet reaches the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C at the specified measurement point. Document the thermal map and any deviations.
- Corrective actions and examples: If thermal mapping shows a cold zone near a specific coil segment, inspect that coil segment for turn-to-turn shorts, insulation breakdown, or coolant obstructions. Example corrective actions include reseating coil clamps, repairing coolant channels, or replacing damaged coil segments. If repeated heating shortfalls occur after corrective action, escalate to engineering and reference ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 for previous change history and modifications that may affect coil transfer function.
- Post-maintenance steps: Update the equipment maintenance log with serial identifiers of replaced components, test results from insulation checks, coolant flow verification entries, and attached thermal maps. Notify operations that the heater is returned to service and include any operational limits or observations that operators should monitor during the initial production period.

Records to keep
- Equipment maintenance log entry for each maintenance event, including technician name, date, and summaries of inspections and tests.
- Thermal imaging files and annotated maps showing temperature distribution and indicating the location where the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C was measured.
- Cooling flow verification records showing measured flow at coil supply before and after any corrective action, confirming coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min is met.
- Insulation resistance and continuity test reports with pass/fail status and measured values.
- Parts replaced and disposition records, and any escalation records referencing ECN-2026-013 or ECN-2026-039.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical: Coil windings show no visible insulation failure or coolant leakage; busbar connectors are secure and free of overheating indicators.
- Cooling: Measured coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds 55 L/min. If flow is below this minimum, the heater must remain offline until flow is restored and verified.
- Electrical: Insulation resistance and continuity tests meet plant electrical acceptance thresholds per SOP-P2-L1-01. No shorts or grounding faults present.
- Thermal performance: Billet temperature mapping demonstrates that the billet reaches the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C within the defined billet travel path and exhibits acceptable uniformity. Any deviation that could affect forging outcomes must be corrected and retested before return to production.
- Documentation: All required records are filed in the equipment maintenance folder and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L1-01 and change documents ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 as applicable.

Notes and rationale
- Verifying cooling flow is prioritized because inadequate flow accelerates coil damage and leads to rapid failure modes that are more costly and hazardous.
- Thermal mapping provides direct evidence that electrical power and mechanical coil geometry produce the expected billet heating outcome; it is the final acceptance check prior to returning EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to production.
- Use the related documents ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 for historical modification details and SOP-P2-L1-01 for lockout/tagout and tool calibration governance.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

# MM-P2-L1-SB03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Scope
This manual covers preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet identified as EQ-P2-L1-SB03. It is intended for maintenance technicians and shift engineers responsible for preserving media containment, blast performance, and safe operation in the hot-forge cell. Tasks include inspection of wear components, replacement of consumables, torque verification of critical fasteners, media top-up, and documentation of condition and corrective actions. Refer to design change notices and operating procedures for context: ECN-2026-033, ECN-2026-036, SOP-P2-L1-01.

Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet is subject to abrasive wear and heavy loading in the hot-forge process. Wear of the blast wheel liner and loss of media inventory degrade cleaning effectiveness and increase risk of component failure. Tightening and confirming critical fasteners prevents accelerated wear and unplanned downtime. Media top-up at the prescribed interval preserves shot flow characteristics and surface finish repeatability. Maintenance interventions are sequenced to reduce exposure to abrasive dust and to limit handling of hot parts consistent with SOP-P2-L1-01.

Tools
- Handheld torque wrench calibrated to traceable standard capable of reading the specified torque value.  
- Impact-rated socket set compatible with equipment fasteners.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P2-L1-01, including respirator and abrasive-handling gloves.  
- Clean containers and approved media storage sacks for recovered shot.  
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal visual checks.  
- Magnetic pick and mesh sieve for checking media contamination.  
- Maintenance log forms and camera for condition records.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify work authorization under SOP-P2-L1-01 and lockout-tagout protocols before accessing the cabinet. Confirm that the blast wheel assembly is stationary and that drive power has been isolated. Use PPE specified in SOP-P2-L1-01 for abrasive handling and dust exposure.  
- Position collection containers and lay out tools on a clean surface to prevent cross-contamination of media.

Inspection
- Access the interior by opening the service access panel per machine guidance and visually inspect the blast wheel liner for grooving, thinning, or cracking. Use the borescope for areas not visible by eye. Inspect adjacent wear plates and the feed hopper for fines accumulation and contamination.  
- Inspect media for fractured particles, foreign material, and fines. Use the mesh sieve to separate fines and the magnetic pick to remove tramp metal. Record qualitative observations and capture images of abnormal wear patterns.

Liner fastener torque verification
- Identify the blast wheel liner fasteners and clean the joint surfaces to ensure accurate torque application. Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply the specified setting to confirm retention. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. If any fastener does not hold to the specified setting, mark that fastener for replacement and record the original condition and any signs of thread damage or loss of clamping.

Media top-up
- Evaluate remaining media volume and condition against operational feel and appearance. When media requires replenishment, add approved shot media from traceable stock. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Plan top-up activities to occur before media degradation affects process quality. When top-up is performed, blend new media with recovered media by sieving to remove fines, and document batch codes of media used.

Wear component replacement and alignment
- If the blast wheel liner shows excessive wear beyond acceptable limits per engineering guidance in ECN-2026-036, replace the liner using manufacturer procedures and alignment checks. After replacement, re-inspect adjacent wear parts and verify that fasteners meet the specified torque. Align the liner to maintain clearance to the impeller and housing to optimize shot trajectory.

Cleanup and verification
- Remove fines and dust from the cabinet and adjacent areas using approved vacuum equipment. Dispose of collected fines per environmental and plant procedures. Reassemble access panels and remove lockout-tagout only after completing functional checks per SOP-P2-L1-01. Conduct a dry-run blast under supervised conditions to validate media feed and cabinet containment before returning to production.

Records and examples
- Maintain the maintenance log for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 with entries including date, technician name, observed wear conditions, fastener torque confirmation results, media batch codes used for top-up, and any parts replaced. Attach photos of significant wear or damage. Example entry fields: equipment id, maintenance activity, findings, corrective actions taken, signatures. Keep records in the document control system and reference ECN-2026-033 for configuration history when part replacements alter fit or material.

Acceptance criteria
- Blast wheel liner fasteners must retain clamping at the specified torque setting. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. A verified torque reading within the calibration tolerance of the torque wrench indicates acceptance. If a fastener cannot achieve the specified torque due to damaged threads or distorted mating surfaces, the liner assembly is unacceptable until corrective repairs are completed and re-torqued to specification.  
- Media condition and quantity must support consistent blasting performance until the next scheduled top-up. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Acceptance requires that media be free of excessive fines and foreign contaminants so that blast pattern and cleaning efficiency meet production requirements.  
- Post-maintenance functional checks must show stable media feed, no significant leakage of shot from the cabinet, and absence of unusual vibration or noise attributable to misalignment or loose components. Any deviation from these acceptance criteria mandates corrective action and re-evaluation prior to returning the cabinet to service.

Related documentation
- ECN-2026-033  
- ECN-2026-036  
- SOP-P2-L1-01

Revision history and approvals
Record revision, author, and approval signatures in the document control system per plant practice. Ensure traceability of maintenance events for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and linkage to related ECN entries.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

text:
# MM-P2-L2-IH01 Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01  
Revision: Rev D

Scope
This manual defines required maintenance activities, rationale, and records for Ring Rolling induction billet heater EQ-P2-L2-IH01. It covers routine inspection, preventive maintenance, and corrective actions needed to maintain safe and reliable operation. This document is intended for maintenance technicians and engineers responsible for furnace performance and material quality. Refer to ECN-2026-012, ECN-2026-048, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for related design changes, electrical schematics, and plant operating procedures.

Background and performance target
The induction billet heater is used to bring feedstock to forming temperature prior to ring rolling. The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Maintaining uniform temperature profile and consistent coil cooling prevents premature coil degradation and ensures repeatable ring geometry. Coil cooling water must meet flow requirements to avoid coil overheating; the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.

Tools and consumables
- Insulation-safe temperature probe compatible with high-temperature billet measurement as called out in SOP-P2-L2-05.  
- Infrared thermometer for surface checks and verification.  
- Multimeter and clamp ammeter for electrical checks per ECN-2026-048.  
- Spanner set, insulated hand tools, lifting strap suitable for coil handling.  
- Replacement coil fasteners and insulation panels specified in ECN-2026-012.  
- Degreasing solvent and lint-free cloths for coil and connector cleaning.  
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device per plant document control.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Review SOP-P2-L2-05 and coordinate with line control before entry. Lockout and tagout all power supplies to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and post signage at the line staging area. Verify absence of residual charge using appropriate procedures in ECN-2026-048 prior to touching exposed conductors. Wear heat-rated gloves and eye protection when working near recent heat cycles.

Visual inspection
- Inspect induction coil assembly for visible deformation, cracking, or discoloration indicative of overheating. Inspect coil insulation and fasteners for mechanical integrity. Check water lines and fittings for wetting, corrosion, or external leaks. Verify coil connectors are free from soot and buildup that would impede electrical contact.

Electrical checks
- With lockout in place and panels accessible, visually inspect bus connections and current leads. Clean contact surfaces with specified solvent and reinstall fasteners to recommended tightening practice found in ECN-2026-048. Confirm that protective covers and grounding straps are intact and secured.

Cooling system verification
- Restore control to cooling system only under supervision and permissive conditions required by SOP-P2-L2-05. Verify that inlet and outlet hoses are unobstructed and strainers are clean. Use flow measurement device at the coil water connection and confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min. If flow is below this value, do not operate the heater. Trace the cooling circuit to locate restriction and repair according to plant piping maintenance practices cited in ECN-2026-012.

Thermal performance check
- After completing mechanical and cooling verifications, energize the system under monitored conditions as specified in SOP-P2-L2-05. Heat a billet and monitor temperature profile using the mandated probe placement and data logging method. Ensure billet temperature reaches the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Evaluate temperature uniformity across the billet length to confirm consistent heating. If target temperature is not achieved with correct power and feed settings per operating procedures, investigate coil impedance, power supply output, and refractory condition referencing ECN-2026-048.

Corrective actions
- Replace coils or insulation panels that show structural compromise as per parts list in ECN-2026-012. Repair water leaks with approved fittings and document component replacement in the maintenance log. If electrical anomalies are found, escalate to electrical engineering with test data and photographs attached.

Examples and rationale
- Example scenario: If measured coil cooling flow is marginally below the required threshold, a typical cause is a partially clogged strainer or a kinked hose. Cleaning the strainer restores cooling and prevents temperature excursions that reduce coil life. Rationale: Maintaining the specified minimum flow protects against coil overheating, which otherwise shortens service life and may cause rapid failure under load.
- Example scenario: If billets fail to reach target temperature despite adequate power, degraded coil turns or recessing insulation may be responsible. Rationale: Coil geometry and insulation determine coupling efficiency; restoring original geometry improves energy transfer and repeatability.

Acceptance criteria
- Visual: No visible cracks, deformation, or compromised insulation on coils and associated refractory at the completion of maintenance.  
- Cooling: Verified coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min at the coil inlet connection.  
- Thermal: Measured billet temperature reaches the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C during the validation heat cycle under standard operating feed and power conditions as defined in SOP-P2-L2-05.  
- Electrical: Connections cleaned and secured; no abnormal resistance or intermittent contacts recorded during post-maintenance checks as referenced in ECN-2026-048.  
- Documentation: Maintenance log updated with description of work performed, parts replaced as per ECN-2026-012, flow and temperature verification records, and name of technician completing the maintenance in accordance with plant record retention practices.

Records to keep
- Completed maintenance checklist and log entry per SOP-P2-L2-05.  
- Photographs of coil condition before and after work.  
- Flow measurement printouts or handwritten verification showing compliance with coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.  
- Temperature data file proving billet reached the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C.  
- Parts replacement records referencing ECN-2026-012 and electrical test sheets referencing ECN-2026-048.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-012  
- ECN-2026-048  
- SOP-P2-L2-05

# MM-P2-L2-HT02 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance and verification tasks for the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) used in the P2 line. It covers the austenitizing setpoint verification, thermocouple calibration schedule, general furnace checks, and the acceptance criteria required to return the furnace to production. This manual is intended for maintenance technicians and heat treat operators and supplements operating procedures SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-05. See also MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 for parts and spares information.

Background and rationale
The stability of the austenitizing temperature directly affects microstructure and dimensional repeatability of ring-rolled components. Thermocouple accuracy and sensor placement are critical to achieving consistent metallurgical results. The procedures in this manual are structured to verify that the furnace reaches and holds the specified austenitizing setpoint and that thermocouples are within calibration tolerance before production cycles. Where calibration or repairs are required, documented evidence is retained to demonstrate process control.

Tools and equipment
- Calibrated reference thermocouple and readout compatible with furnace controllers
- Portable temperature datalogger capable of mapping chamber temperatures
- Hand tools and safety gear as required by SOP-P2-L2-02
- Replacement thermocouple assemblies listed in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1
- Lockout/tagout kit as required by SOP-P2-L2-05

Procedure
Pre-work verification
- Review last maintenance record and calibration certificate for EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Confirm that no work is in progress on the associated line and that production is scheduled around the planned maintenance window as coordinated with operations.
- Apply lockout/tagout per SOP-P2-L2-05 and confirm isolation of energy sources.

Thermocouple calibration and check
- Install the calibrated reference thermocouple into the furnace at the representative load position used during production. Ensure probe entry follows manufacturer routing and strain relief practices referenced in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
- Run a controlled heat cycle to ramp the furnace to the austenitizing setpoint and hold to allow chamber stabilization.
- Compare the furnace controller readout to the reference thermocouple at stabilized condition. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 40 days. Ensure that calibration is current before authorizing production.
- If reference readings show drift outside allowable tolerance per MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, tag the thermocouple assembly for replacement and proceed to the replacement steps.

Austenitizing setpoint verification
- Set the furnace controller to the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) as specified at 855 °C.
- Allow the furnace to stabilize at that setpoint with the standardized load or ballast specified in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 to reproduce production thermal mass conditions.
- Use the portable datalogger to map temperature uniformity across the load zone. Record the controller setpoint, controller readout, and datalogger measurements in the maintenance record.
- If the furnace cannot reach or maintain 855 °C within process tolerances defined in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, escalate to the supervisor and schedule the corrective action specified in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.

Mechanical and electrical checks
- Inspect furnace door seals, chamber lining, and heat elements for signs of localized damage or degradation. Document condition and retain images in the maintenance record.
- Verify control wiring connections at the thermocouple terminal block and controller input for secure terminations. Replace or tighten per MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 if corrosion or looseness is observed.
- Confirm the functionality of alarm indicators and interlocks per SOP-P2-L2-02.

Records and examples
- Maintain a maintenance log entry for each calibration and verification activity. The log must include equipment id EQ-P2-L2-HT02, date of action, technician name, reference thermocouple serial, controller readout, datalogger output files, and any corrective action performed.
- Example record entries should include the controller setpoint, reference thermocouple peak reading, and remarks on uniformity mapping. Store digital temperature maps and calibration certificates attached to the log in the document control system and reference MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 for file naming conventions.

Acceptance criteria
- Thermocouple calibration is valid and within tolerance per MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 40 days; a current calibration certificate must be on file.
- Furnace is capable of reaching and maintaining the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) at 855 °C with thermal uniformity across the load zone as specified in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
- All mechanical inspections show no damage that would compromise process control. Electrical connections and controller inputs pass continuity and integrity checks per SOP-P2-L2-02.
- Associated alarms and interlocks function as designed. Any deviation must be documented and corrected prior to returning equipment to service.

Disposition and return to service
- If acceptance criteria are met, remove lockout/tagout and notify operations that EQ-P2-L2-HT02 is available for production. Attach completed maintenance record to the equipment history file.
- If corrective actions were required, include descriptions of parts replaced and reference MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 parts used. Hold a supervisory review before re-issuing the equipment to production.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1
- SOP-P2-L2-02
- SOP-P2-L2-05

Records to keep
- Calibration certificate for reference thermocouple
- Datalogger temperature maps and raw files
- Maintenance log entry for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 including images and corrective action notes
- Replacement part receipts referenced to MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1

End of document.
