text:
# MM-P2-L2-RR03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Scope
This document describes routine preventive maintenance and critical adjustment procedures for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). It covers pre-maintenance safety checks, required tools, stepwise maintenance actions for the mandrel clamp and main roll bearing lubrication, acceptance criteria for return to service, and records to retain. Procedures reference SB-1049 and SOP-P2-L2-03 for safety and lockout practices, and SOP-P2-L2-05 for lubrication material selection and handling.

Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated to the range appropriate for mandrel clamp bolts and fitted with a compatible drive and socket for the clamp hardware. Ensure calibration certificate available before use.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent per SOP-P2-L2-05 for cleaning bearing surfaces.
- Grease gun compatible with lubrication fittings specified in SOP-P2-L2-05.
- Dial indicator or runout measurement device for mandrel alignment verification.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SB-1049 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Procedure
Background and rationale
The mandrel clamp secures the mandrel during rolling operations; correct clamp bolt preload is critical to prevent mandrel slippage and maintain ring geometry. The main roll bearing requires a scheduled lubrication frequency to preserve lubricant film, minimize wear, and prevent bearing failure. The following tasks focus on ensuring correct clamp torque and maintaining the main roll bearing lubrication according to the specified interval and industry best practices.

Pre-maintenance actions
- Confirm work authorization and permit requirements in accordance with SB-1049 and SOP-P2-L2-03. Verify that the equipment is isolated and locked out per SOP-P2-L2-03 before any work near moving components.
- Review last maintenance record and confirm that the next scheduled lubrication is due based on operating logs and the interval specified below.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque adjustment
- Clean the mandrel clamp area of oil and debris with approved solvent. Wipe with lint-free rag and inspect for wear or damage.
- Hand-tighten each clamp bolt in a star pattern until snug to seat the clamp uniformly.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each clamp bolt to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m.
- After applying torque, allow a short settling period, then re-check each bolt to confirm torque retention. If torque loss is observed, inspect threads and mating surfaces for damage and correct before re-torquing.
- Verify mandrel runout at the specified inspection points and compare to baseline measurements in the equipment history record. Adjust clamp position if runout exceeds historical baseline values.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm lubricant type and quantity per SOP-P2-L2-05. Prepare grease gun and purge air from the delivery system to ensure consistent flow.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Document operating hours since the last lubrication in the maintenance log prior to replenishment.
- Clean grease fittings and surrounding area to prevent contamination. Apply lubricant until fresh grease is observed at the bearing seals or until resistance indicates the cavity is adequately filled as described in SOP-P2-L2-05.
- Wipe away excess lubricant and inspect for signs of leakage or seal degradation. Record the quantity dispensed and any anomalies observed.

Examples and troubleshooting
- Example: If clamp bolts repeatedly lose torque, inspect for elongated bolt holes, damaged threads, or inadequate clamp seating. Replace defective hardware and re-establish torque to the specified value.
- Example: If bearing temperatures rise after lubrication, verify lubricant compatibility per SOP-P2-L2-05, inspect for contamination, and check for misalignment or excessive preload. Refer to SB-1049 for hot-work and thermal safety guidance during diagnosis.
- If grease fitting is blocked, use approved fitting cleaning tools and re-test delivery before applying lubricant. If blockage persists, replace the fitting and record the replacement action in the maintenance log.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolts must hold the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Torque readings must remain within tool calibration tolerance after settling. No visible mechanical damage or plastic deformation of clamp components is acceptable.
- Mandrel runout must be within historical baseline limits recorded in the equipment history. Any deviation that exceeds baseline limits requires inspection and corrective action before return to service.
- Main roll bearing lubrication must be performed in accordance with the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Bearings must show consistent, smooth rotation with no abnormal noise on manual spin and no signs of lubricant contamination or leakage.
- No safety interlocks or guards shall be bypassed during maintenance. Equipment must pass pre-start checks in SOP-P2-L2-03 before resumption of operations.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order documenting mandrel clamp torque application, including torque tool ID and calibration status, and the exact torque value applied as specified above.
- Lubrication log entry showing operating hours at time of lubrication, lubricant type per SOP-P2-L2-05, quantity dispensed, and technician initials.
- Inspection notes for mandrel runout and any corrective actions taken. Attach photos where applicable.
- References to related documents: SB-1049, SOP-P2-L2-03, SOP-P2-L2-05.

Revision control and feedback
Record any deviations, part replacements, or process improvements in the equipment maintenance history and propose updates to this document through the document control process. Technical feedback and nonconformance reports should reference this document id: MM-P2-L2-RR03 and be submitted per plant document control procedures.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

text:
# MM-P2-L3-RR01 Maintenance manual - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance actions required to keep the Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) operating within acceptable performance limits for machining operations on forged rings. It covers background, required tools, a stepwise maintenance procedure oriented to safe access and verification, acceptance criteria for restored condition, rationale for each action, examples of typical wear modes, and records to retain. For change history, refer to ECN-2026-018. For routine operational start/stop and safety procedures, consult SOP-P2-L3-01 and SOP-P2-L3-03.

Background and rationale
The radial ring rolling mill is a high-load, high-precision machine subject to cyclical contact stresses and contamination from swarf and coolant. Preventive maintenance focuses on clamping integrity, bearing lubrication, alignment verification, and contamination control. Clamping integrity ensures concentricity and repeatability; bearing lubrication controls friction, heat, and wear. The specified mandrel clamp bolt torque of 470 N·m is the factory-recommended clamping preload required to maintain mandrel positional stability during machining cycles. The main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours is established from bearing supplier life models and machine duty cycles to prevent lubricant starvation and contamination-related failure.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of achieving and verifying the mandrel clamp bolt torque specified as 470 N·m.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent for degreasing mating surfaces.
- Approved bearing grease and dispensing tool as specified in SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal visual inspection.
- Dial indicator or comparable alignment verification gauge for concentricity checks.
- Torque audit log form and equipment maintenance record forms as defined in SOP-P2-L3-01.

Procedure
Prepare for maintenance:
- Follow lockout/tagout and machine isolation steps in SOP-P2-L3-01 before accessing the machine.
- Clean visible swarf from external surfaces to reduce contamination ingress during maintenance.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification:
- Clean bolt heads and mating surfaces using approved solvent and lint-free rags. Rationale: contamination under the bolt head causes inaccurate torque readings and inconsistent clamping force.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply the mandrel clamp bolt torque exactly to 470 N·m. Rationale: the specified torque produces the designed clamp preload; under-torque increases risk of mandrel slip, over-torque risks fastener yield. Example: in a recent shop incident, inadequate clamp preload led to concentricity drift and rework; strict torque application prevented recurrence.
- Record applied torque values and any anomalies on the torque audit log form. Include operator initials and equipment serial tag.

Main roll bearing lubrication:
- Inspect bearing housing seals for damage or leakage. Rationale: effective seals maintain lubricant cleanliness and retention.
- Remove access plugs as needed following safe handling guidelines in SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Apply approved lubricant to the main roll bearing following the fill method prescribed in SOP-P2-L3-03. Note the lubrication schedule requirement: main roll bearing lubrication interval for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 165 hours. Rationale: repeating lubrication at the stated interval prevents lubricant degradation and reduces metal-to-metal contact that accelerates wear.
- Log the lubrication event on the maintenance record, noting the equipment id and lubricant batch/lot per traceability requirements.

Alignment and functional checks:
- Verify mandrel to machine frame concentricity using the alignment gauge. If concentricity exceeds acceptable limits defined in ECN-2026-018, escalate to the engineering team for corrective alignment per ECN-2026-018 instructions.
- Conduct a low-speed functional run per SOP-P2-L3-01 to confirm absence of abnormal vibration or noise. If any abnormal condition is detected, stop and record findings; do not resume production until corrected.

Contamination control and housekeeping:
- Replace or clean coolant screens and filters according to SOP-P2-L3-03. Rationale: coolant contamination contributes to bearing and clamp surface degradation.
- Inspect and clean chip conveyors and collection areas to prevent reintroduction of swarf into critical assemblies.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolt torque recorded as 470 N·m and verified with a calibrated instrument. Closure condition: torque audit form completed and stored.
- Main roll bearing lubrication event logged with lubricant identification and timestamp, with the interval adherence noted as 165 hours between events. Closure condition: lubrication entry recorded in equipment maintenance record.
- Concentricity within limits specified in ECN-2026-018. Closure condition: alignment verification sheet attached to the maintenance record.
- No abnormal vibration or noise observed during functional verification after maintenance. Closure condition: run test checklist in SOP-P2-L3-01 marked pass.
- Seals intact with no evidence of fresh leakage at bearings or clamp interfaces. Closure condition: visual inspection checklist completed.

Records to keep
- Torque audit log with applied torque values and operator identification. Retain per SOP-P2-L3-01 record retention guidance.
- Bearing lubrication log entries documenting lubricant type and batch, and confirmation that the main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours is observed.
- Alignment verification sheet referencing ECN-2026-018 limits and any corrective actions taken.
- Functional run test checklist from SOP-P2-L3-01 and any deviation reports if issues were found.

Examples and troubleshooting notes
- Example symptom: repeatable concentricity drift observed between shifts. Typical root cause: clamp bolt torque loss from contamination under bolt heads or inadequate torque application. Mitigation: clean bolt interfaces and apply mandrel clamp bolt torque of 470 N·m, then reverify concentricity.
- Example symptom: elevated bearing temperature with increased noise. Typical root cause: lubricant degradation or contamination. Mitigation: inspect seals, replace lubricant, and verify that lubrication events are occurring at the main roll bearing lubrication interval of 165 hours.

References
- ECN-2026-018
- SOP-P2-L3-01
- SOP-P2-L3-03

Revision and change control
All changes to this maintenance manual shall be processed through ECN-2026-018. Record completed maintenance activities on the equipment record for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and retain records per site document retention practice as described in SOP-P2-L3-01.
title: Maintenance manual - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

text:
# MM-P2-L3-HT02 Maintenance manual - Machining heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
- This manual covers routine maintenance, verification, and documentation practices for Machining heat treat furnace #2, EQ-P2-L3-HT02. It applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for furnace reliability, thermal uniformity, and safety in the P2, line P2-L3 work area.
- Exclusions: major rebuilds, control system replacement beyond modular component swap, and vendor factory repairs. For those activities, contact engineering and reference service bulletins SB-1023 and SB-1045.

Background and rationale
- The furnace supports machining hardening cycles where metallurgical outcomes depend on accurate austenitizing temperature and stable soak profiles. Drift in control elements or sensing circuits leads to out-of-spec microstructure and rework.
- Maintaining sensor accuracy and control integrity reduces scrap, improves process repeatability, and preserves tool life downstream. The thermocouple sensing network and control setpoint are primary process inputs and therefore subject to scheduled verification and adjustment.

Key settings and intervals
- The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C.
- The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.

Tools and supplies
- Portable reference thermocouple and calibrated data logger with certificate traceable to laboratory standards. Use the reference channel for comparison only.
- Insulating gloves, face shield, and heat-resistant tools as per plant PPE requirements.
- Non conductive handheld multimeter for sensor circuit continuity checks.
- Small hand tools for terminal access and clamp adjustment.
- Calibration stickers and log forms for records.
- Replacement thermocouple assemblies and mounting hardware as stocked for EQ-P2-L3-HT02.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Confirm authorization to enter the heat treat area and lockout as required by plant safety procedures. Coordinate with production to isolate furnace cycles.
  - Review related documents SOP-P2-L3-03 for operational controls and SB-1023 and SB-1045 for any known service notes that affect inspection or parts.
  - Verify availability of the portable reference thermocouple and its calibration certificate before work begins.

- Visual and mechanical inspection
  - With furnace de-energized per plant lockout requirements, inspect thermocouple sheath routing, anchor points, and electrical terminations for signs of wear, corrosion, or loose connections.
  - Check furnace door seals and refractory conditions at accessible locations to confirm no local hot spots that could affect sensor readings.

- Thermocouple verification and calibration
  - Install the portable reference thermocouple in the process zone adjacent to the installed process thermocouple location, using the same mounting arrangement where practicable to minimize spatial gradients.
  - Bring the furnace up to the austenitizing setpoint defined above, following SOP-P2-L3-03 for controlled ramp and soak. Monitor both reference logger and process controller readings concurrently.
  - Compare the process thermocouple output to the portable reference over the soak period. If the deviation exceeds acceptable drift noted in SOP-P2-L3-03, replace the process thermocouple assembly and retest.
  - Record the comparison trace on the calibration log and attach the portable reference certificate to the maintenance record.

- Control verification
  - Confirm the controller is commanding the setpoint value specified above and that output influences heater elements as described in SOP-P2-L3-03.
  - Validate alarm thresholds and operator interface setpoints to ensure they match process documentation.

- Post-calibration actions
  - Apply calibration sticker indicating next calibration due per the interval specified above and record the action in the equipment maintenance log.
  - Return the furnace to normal operation in coordination with production and note any deviations or corrective actions in the shift handover log.

Examples and troubleshooting notes
- Example: If the process thermocouple reads lower than the portable reference by a consistent offset, suspect connector corrosion or sheath degradation. Tighten or replace termination hardware, then repeat verification. If offset persists after terminal work, replace the thermocouple assembly.
- Example: If controller display reads the setpoint correctly but the actual chamber temperature lags during soak, inspect element load distribution and refractory for insulation loss. Document findings and escalate to engineering if replacement is required; reference SB-1023 for element failure guidance.
- If intermittent sensor readings occur only during door operation, check for mechanical stress at the mounting point and secure the probe to prevent flexing.

Records to keep
- Attach to the EQ-P2-L3-HT02 maintenance file:
  - Calibration log and portable reference certificate for each verification event.
  - Inspection checklist documenting visual observations and any replaced parts.
  - Controller output and reference logger trace for the soak at the austenitizing setpoint.
  - Copy of completed calibration sticker photograph showing next calibration due per the thermocouple interval above.
  - Any deviation reports and corrective action records, including cross-reference to SB-1023, SB-1045, and SOP-P2-L3-03 where applicable.

Acceptance criteria
- After maintenance and verification, the furnace meets the following:
  - Controller displays the austenitizing setpoint specified above and maintains stable control during soak as evidenced by reference logger trace.
  - Process thermocouple agrees with the portable reference within the acceptance window defined in SOP-P2-L3-03 for the full soak duration.
  - Thermocouple has been calibrated and documented according to the interval specified above with sticker and maintenance log entry present.
  - No active mechanical defects or loose electrical terminations remain at the probe mounting and connection points.

Related documents
- SB-1023
- SB-1045
- SOP-P2-L3-03

End of document.
title: Maintenance manual - Machining heat treat furnace #2

text:
# MM-P2-L3-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This document provides preventive and corrective maintenance instructions for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) located on line P2-L3. It covers mechanical, electrical and cooling system checks necessary to maintain reliable heating to the target billet temperature and safe operation of the induction coil system.
- This procedure supplements site-level quality and process requirements; follow QS-PROC-10 and SOP-P2-L3-02 for production interface and lockout/tagout. Refer to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for schematic and spare-parts mapping.

Background and rationale
- EQ-P2-L3-IH03 is a high-power induction heater used to bring billets to machining temperature. Proper maintenance reduces thermal non-uniformity, prevents coil damage, and avoids production rejects. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C. Maintaining design cooling and electrical parameters is essential to achieve this target without overstressing components.
- The coil requires continuous cooling during operation. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Operating below this flow risks rapid coil failure and compromised heating performance.

Tools
- Insulated hand tools suitable for electrical work.
- Flow indicator calibrator and inline flow meter compatible with the system.
- Thermal imaging camera or surface pyrometer for coil and housing inspection.
- Vibration meter and strobe light for rotation checks (if applicable to drive components).
- Multimeter and clamp ammeter rated for system voltages/currents.
- Torque tools only where factory torque specifications are provided in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- Personal protective equipment: arc-rated gloves, face shield, insulated boots, and hearing protection.

Procedure
Preparation
- Coordinate with production per SOP-P2-L3-02 before starting any maintenance. Ensure process owner signs off on billet flow and that replacement billets are not in the heater path.
- Apply lockout/tagout per QS-PROC-10 for electrical supply and water supply isolation. Verify zero energy state before opening panels.

Visual inspection
- Inspect the induction coil for signs of cracking, discoloration, or insulation breakdown. Use thermal imaging to identify hot spots when safe and permitted.
- Verify coil mounting hardware is secure per drawing in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3. Replace any fasteners or insulators that show damage.
- Inspect water connections, hoses, and quick-disconnect fittings for leakage, abrasion, and proper sealing. Check for scale or biofouling at visible joints and strainers.

Cooling system verification
- Confirm the cooling water supply system is delivering adequate flow and pressure to the heater. Use the inline flow meter to confirm that coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is achieved. If flow is below minimum, stop and trace to pump, filter, or valve issues.
- Clean strainers and filters according to the service schedule in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3. If deposits are found, collect samples and log condition in the maintenance record.

Electrical checks
- With power isolated and lockout in place, inspect power connections for looseness, corrosion, or overheating signs. Measure contact resistance where accessible and compare to historical records.
- Inspect and test protective interlocks and thermal cutouts. Verify wiring to control relays and sensors matches the schematic in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
- After reassembly and removal of lockout/tagout, perform controlled power-up following SOP-P2-L3-02. Monitor for abnormal current or alarm conditions and be prepared to isolate system immediately.

Operational verification and tuning
- Bring the heater to operational state under supervision of process engineer. Monitor billet temperature feedback and compare to the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03): 1175 °C. Adjust tuning parameters only within limits provided in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 and in consultation with process engineering.
- If temperature cannot be achieved while coil cooling water flow remains at or above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min, escalate to engineering for further diagnostic steps.

Examples and common fault modes
- Example: If the heater reaches setpoint intermittently and then falls away, check for intermittent loss of cooling flow, contaminated flow meter, or partial clogging of internal passages. Record instances and compare with pump operation logs.
- Example: Visible coil hot spot with normal flow suggests coil insulation breach or localized shorting; remove from service and tag for coil replacement per MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.

Records to keep
- Record of lockout/tagout authorization and completion per QS-PROC-10.
- Maintenance log entry with date, technician name, work performed, parts replaced (referenced by MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3), and measured cooling flow values. Include explicit statement when coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min is met or not met.
- Calibration certificates for flow meter and temperature sensors used during verification.
- Incident report and corrective action if target billet temperature is not achievable: include observed temperature, steps taken, and reference to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 diagnostics.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical and electrical integrity verified with no loose connections or coolant leaks present.
- Coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min as measured at the heater inlet.
- Heater achieves and holds the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 1175 °C under normal process load, with stable control signals and no protective trips.
- All work completed is recorded in the maintenance management system and referenced to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for parts and QS-PROC-10 for procedural adherence.
- If any acceptance criterion is not met, the heater shall remain tagged out and escalated per SOP-P2-L3-02 until corrective actions are implemented and re-verification is successful.

# MM-P2-L4-RR01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance and corrective restart procedures for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) installed on line P2-L4. It covers mechanical inspection, lubrication, mandrel clamp verification, bearing condition checks, and records to be kept after each activity. For related operational and safety procedures, see SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SOP-P2-L4-04.

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills are subject to high radial and axial loads during operation. Wear accumulates on bearings and on the mandrel clamp system. Proper clamp bolt preload and timely lubrication reduce vibration, prevent ovality of formed parts, and extend component life. The listed mandrel clamp bolt torque and lubrication interval are derived from factory fitment data and field trial run-in behavior for this specific machine arrangement. Adhering to the specified torque minimizes clamp slippage without overstressing fasteners. The specified lubrication interval balances operating duty cycles with grease life to prevent metal-to-metal contact in the main roll bearings.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the required torque
- Socket set compatible with mandrel clamp bolt heads
- Bearing grease gun with fittings compatible with main roll bearing grease points
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent for wipe-down (per SOP-P2-L4-03)
- Dial indicator and magnetic base for runout checks
- Vibration analyzer and handheld strobe for dynamic inspection (optional for trend analysis)
- Maintenance log forms and mill usage runtime report (see Records to Keep)
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-04

Procedure
General safety: Verify lockout/tagout in accordance with SOP-P2-L4-02 before performing any maintenance. Ensure electrical and hydraulic energy sources are isolated and stored energy is bled. Wear PPE required by SOP-P2-L4-04.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and adjustment
- Remove any protective covers to access the mandrel clamp bolts. Clean the bolt heads and threads of debris and old lubricant following methods in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the wrench to 525 N·m. Slowly apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt until the wrench indicates the specified value. Apply torque in an alternating pattern around the mandrel to attain even clamp loading; the alternating approach prevents eccentric clamp loading and ensures uniform mandrel contact.
- After initial tightening, rotate the mandrel slowly by hand and check clamp engagement. If there is evidence of clamp slippage or rotation relative to the mandrel, repeat the torque application sequence.
- Rationale: Specifying a consistent torque reduces variability between maintenance crews and prevents under- or over-clamping which can lead to product defects or bolt fatigue.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm machine is at rest and bearings are at ambient conditions. Wipe grease fittings clean before attaching the grease gun to prevent contamination.
- Apply grease using the bearing grease gun until fresh grease is observed at the seal or purge point, taking care not to introduce contaminants. Record the lubrication event in the maintenance log with machine runtime at the time of service.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours. Schedule the next lubrication based on accumulated runtime and verify during shift handover.
- Rationale: Lubrication at the prescribed interval ensures a protective film is maintained on bearing surfaces. Over-greasing can be as damaging as under-greasing; follow the purge indicator or manufacturer guidance during application.

Bearing and roll condition inspection
- Perform a visual inspection for leaks, seal integrity, and abnormal wear on roll journals and housings. Use a dial indicator to measure runout; document readings and compare to prior records for trend detection.
- Perform a vibration scan during a light run if conditions allow (follow SOP-P2-L4-02 for restart checks). Compare spectrum signatures to baseline trends to identify bearing degradation early.
- Rationale: Trend monitoring allows maintenance to be scheduled proactively and avoids unplanned shutdowns.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If after applying the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque a clamp bolt shows evidence of thread stripping or cannot hold torque, remove and tag the hardware for replacement per spare parts procedure. Log the event and notify engineering to review clamp alignment before reassembly.
- Example: If excessive grease purge occurs or bearings feel unusually warm after lubrication, stop further lubrication and escalate to maintenance engineering for contamination analysis.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each torque verification including date, technician initials, torque wrench serial or calibration ID, and confirmation that 525 N·m was applied.
- Lubrication record noting the date, technician initials, grease type, and machine runtime at the time of service. Include note that the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours and the calculated next due runtime.
- Inspection checklist documenting visual findings, runout measurements, vibration scan results, and any corrective actions taken.
- Nonconformance report for any failed hardware or abnormal findings, cross-referenced to work order number and corrective action plan.

Acceptance criteria
- All mandrel clamp bolts must register 525 N·m when checked with a calibrated torque wrench. No bolt shall show signs of thread damage or plastic deformation after torque application.
- Main roll bearings must be lubricated within the prescribed lubrication interval and show no signs of contamination or severe leakage on inspection. Acceptance is based on clean purge appearance and normal running temperature and vibration profiles relative to baseline.
- Runout and vibration measurements must fall within historical trending limits as documented in the machine condition log. Any deviation beyond established trend thresholds requires corrective action before returning to production.
- Records for torque application, lubrication, inspections, and any corrective actions must be complete and filed in the document control system following SOP-P2-L4-03.

References
SOP-P2-L4-02  
SOP-P2-L4-03  
SOP-P2-L4-04

Revision history and approvals are maintained in the document control system.

# MM-P2-L4-HT02 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Scope
This document describes required maintenance activities for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) used on line P2-L4. It covers preventive maintenance, calibration, inspection, and acceptance criteria necessary to maintain process control and product quality. This manual applies to maintenance technicians, process engineers, and quality inspectors responsible for upkeep and verification of EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Refer to SB-1016 for safety boundaries and to SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-03 for operational procedures and sample handling that interact with furnace maintenance.

Background and rationale: The furnace provides critical thermal cycles for final part properties. Consistent control of the austenitizing temperature profile and reliable sensor performance are essential to ensure mechanical properties and metallurgical transformation targets are met. Maintenance activities in this manual are intended to minimize unplanned downtime and to ensure data integrity for process records.

## Tools
Required tools and records for routine maintenance and calibration:
- Temperature calibrator and reference thermocouple compatible with furnace input.
- Insulation inspection mirror and non-sparking probes for internal inspections.
- Electrical multimeter for continuity and connection checks.
- Hand tools for access panel removal and fastener verification.
- Clean, dry lint-free cloths and approved furnace cleaning agents.
- Calibration logbook and electronic maintenance record entry system.
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SB-1016.
- Relevant SOPs: SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03.

Tool rationale: The temperature calibrator and reference thermocouple are used to verify sensor accuracy without removing permanent instrumentation. The inspection mirror and probes allow visual verification of insulation condition and element surfaces. The multimeter is used for safe verification of signal wiring and continuity. Records are required to demonstrate compliance and to support root cause analysis should deviations occur.

## Procedure
General notes: Perform maintenance with the furnace in a de-energized state unless otherwise specified in SB-1016. Follow lockout-tagout and permit procedures consistent with SB-1016 and local plant practice. Before any work begins, review SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-03 to confirm the furnace is in an acceptable state for maintenance relative to current production schedules.

Preventive inspection
- Exterior inspection: Verify that external panels, hinges, and seals are intact and that door latches operate smoothly. Look for signs of mechanical damage or misalignment that could affect door sealing.
- Internal inspection: With the furnace cold and de-energized, inspect internal insulation surfaces and element mounts. Check for local displacement or degradation of insulation that might expose heating elements or change thermal distribution.
- Wiring and connection checks: Inspect sensor wiring and terminal connections for corrosion, tightness, and proper routing. Verify that protective sheaths are intact and that strain reliefs prevent chafing.

Thermocouple calibration
- Frequency: Calibrate thermocouples at the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days.
- Method: Use a certified temperature calibrator and a reference thermocouple to perform a two-point verification across the relevant operational range. Record the reference readings and instrument readings in the calibration log. Document any deviation beyond allowable limits and initiate corrective action per SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Example entry for the calibration log: equipment id EQ-P2-L4-HT02, thermocouple location, reference reading, instrument reading, technician initials, and signoff. Maintain copies per local document control.

Austenitizing setpoint verification
- The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.
- Verification method: Compare controller setpoint and logged profile against the nominal setpoint value. If recorded process profiles deviate, investigate controller parameters, sensor offsets, and mechanical conditions such as door seal integrity and element performance. Corrective measures may include recalibration, replacement of the affected thermocouple, or adjustment of controller tuning as documented in SOP-P2-L4-02.

Cleaning and minor repair
- Clean the interior of loose debris and oxide residues using approved tools and cleaning agents. Avoid abrasive contact with sensor junctions and heating elements.
- Tighten mounting hardware and replace failed fasteners as needed. For any component replacement that impacts process control, update the maintenance record and notify process engineering.

Records and reporting
- Maintain a calibration log and a maintenance action record for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Records must include the thermocouple calibration interval compliance, any corrective actions taken, and outcome verification.
- For any nonconformance identified during inspection or calibration, complete an incident report referencing the related SOPs and SB-1016 for safety implications. Retain records in the document control system.

Safety and isolation
- Always comply with SB-1016 for electrical isolation and hot work permits. Ensure that any work inside the furnace follows appropriate respiratory and heat exposure guidance as specified in SB-1016.

## Acceptance criteria
Acceptance is based on measurable verification and documented evidence. The following criteria must be met before returning the furnace to production.

- Thermocouple accuracy: After calibration performed at the thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days, thermocouples must read within the limits specified in the calibration procedure in SOP-P2-L4-03. Calibration records must be signed and filed.
- Setpoint conformance: The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C and controller setpoint and profile logs must demonstrate consistent attainment of this setpoint within process control limits. Any persistent deviation requires corrective action and re-verification before approval.
- Mechanical integrity: Door seals, insulation, and element mounts must show no condition that could compromise temperature uniformity. Any repair must be documented and verified with a subsequent temperature profile or calibration.
- Documentation: All maintenance, calibration, and corrective actions must be entered into the maintenance record system and cross-referenced to EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Records shall reference SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SB-1016 where relevant.

Examples of acceptable records: calibration log with thermocouple readings and signatures, post-maintenance temperature profile showing setpoint attainment at 885 °C, and inspection checklist entries confirming sealing and insulation conditions. These deliver traceability for audits and process control reviews.

Related documents: SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03.

# MM-P2-L4-HP03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Scope
This manual provides removal, inspection, torque verification, reinstallation, and acceptance criteria for the main ram bolt and hydraulic system verification on Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). It applies to preventive and corrective maintenance activities performed on the press at Plant P2, line P2-L4. For design changes, modifications, or field engineering requests, refer to ECN-2026-042. For safety bulletins and retrofit advisories, consult SB-1007. For normal operating lockout and procedural prerequisites, see SOP-P2-L4-01.

Background and rationale
The main ram bolt secures the ram assembly to the actuating interface and is a primary structural fastener. Correct bolt preload is essential to prevent relative movement, fatigue cracking, and alignment shift that can cause tooling damage or hydraulic failure. Hydraulic system overpressure or underperforming reliefs can induce dynamic loads on the bolted joint beyond the original design assumptions. Verifying both mechanical torque and system pressure limits ensures the assembly operates within safe envelopes and maintains uptime.

Critical values
- The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m.
- The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar.

Tools and materials
Required tools include certified torque wrench calibrated and traceable to lab standards, impact wrench for removal where allowed by procedure, thread cleaning tools, torque extension adapters as needed, non-ferrous alignment drift, anti-seize compound where specified, and personal protective equipment consistent with SB-1007 and SOP-P2-L4-01. Prepare inspection mirrors and dye penetrant kit for fastener and adjacent surface inspection.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review SOP-P2-L4-01 for lockout-tagout and machine isolation steps prior to any mechanical access. Verify documentation of isolation in the maintenance log.
- Inform operations and schedule downtime through the plant maintenance coordinator per local rules.

Removal and inspection
- Remove covers to access the main ram bolt as described in the equipment schematics and job aids.
- Clean the bolt and mating surfaces to allow visual and nondestructive inspection. Use dye penetrant on the bolt shank and head seating area where accessible.
- Inspect for thread damage, head rounding, corrosion, or evidence of yield. If damage is present, submit a replacement request using ECN-2026-042 and do not reuse the bolt.

Thread preparation and lubrication
- Clean threads in the nut and bolt using specified solvents and wire tools. Remove all debris.
- Apply anti-seize compound only where specified by the equipment manufacturer. Excess compound on torque shoulders or on threads beyond the specified area will invalidate the torque outcome.

Reinstallation and torqueing
- Begin hand-starting the nut to ensure proper thread engagement and alignment. Use non-impact tools for final alignment steps.
- Using a calibrated torque wrench, apply the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) to the specified value: 1575 N·m.
- If a torque sequence is required to maintain flange parallelism, follow the sequence described in the equipment assembly drawing and tighten in incremental passes to the final torque using the calibrated instrument.
- Record the torque wrench calibration identifier and the applied torque value in the maintenance record.

Hydraulic system check
- Confirm hydraulic fluid levels and filter condition per OEM recommendations prior to pressurization.
- With pressure sources isolated, perform a controlled pressure test. Ensure system controls and reliefs are functional and verify that system pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03): 320 bar.
- Monitor for leaks, pressure fluctuations, or unusual noises during the test. If pressure attempts to exceed the limit, stop and bleed system pressure, then investigate relief valves and pilot circuits. Reference SB-1007 for additional safety considerations.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If the torque wrench indicates slippage or inconsistent readings while attempting to apply 1575 N·m, stop and verify tool calibration and mechanical condition of the wrench. Do not proceed until the measurement tool is verified.
- Example: If during pressurization the system tops at a value near but below 320 bar and then slowly rises, suspect relief valve drift or thermal expansion. Document findings and request an engineering assessment under ECN-2026-042 if adjustments are necessary.

Records to keep
- Complete the Maintenance Activity Record with: maintenance technician name, equipment id EQ-P2-L4-HP03, pre- and post-maintenance condition notes, the exact applied torque 1575 N·m, the hydraulic test result noting that system pressure did not exceed 320 bar, torque wrench calibration id, and references to SOP-P2-L4-01 and SB-1007 when relevant.
- Retain dye penetrant inspection reports and photographs in the equipment file.
- If any nonconformance is found, file a corrective action and link to ECN-2026-042 for traceability.

Acceptance criteria
- Main ram bolt is free of visible damage, correctly seated, and torqued to 1575 N·m with evidence recorded.
- Hydraulic system holds pressure without exceeding the system pressure limit of 320 bar during functional checks and exhibits no uncontrolled leaks or relief chatter.
- No unusual vibration or misalignment detected during a controlled low-force cycle as described in SOP-P2-L4-01.
- All records are complete and filed in the equipment maintenance log and electronic document control system.

References
- ECN-2026-042
- SB-1007
- SOP-P2-L4-01

Safety and remarks
Follow all lockout-tagout procedures and PPE requirements in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SB-1007. If any measured condition deviates from the values cited in this document, cease operations and escalate to engineering using ECN-2026-042 for corrective action.

# MM-P3-L1-HP01 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01

Scope
- This manual covers planned maintenance tasks and verification steps for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1, model EQ-P3-L1-HP01, located on line P3-L1. Activities include mechanical fastener verification, hydraulic system pressure verification, basic lubrication checks, and documentation practices required before returning the press to production.
- Exclusions: detailed electrical diagnostics beyond visual inspection and logic controller programming changes are not included; consult SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 for electrical and operational procedures respectively.

Background and rationale
- The forging press is a process-critical machine where ram alignment and hydraulic integrity directly affect part quality and operator safety. The main ram bolt secures the ram assembly and transmits forging loads to the frame. Fastener preload influences joint stiffness and fatigue life. The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Adhering to this torque value ensures the fastener achieves the designed clamp load and joint performance.
- Hydraulic system overpressure is a primary hazard for seals, hoses, and valves. The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Maintenance checks verify that safety devices and relief settings maintain system pressure within that limit.
- Reference maintenance and operating standards: MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1, SOP-P3-L1-01, SOP-P3-L1-02.

Tools
- Torque tool suitable for applying and verifying the specified main ram bolt torque. Use a calibrated torque device with traceable calibration certificate. Ensure the torque tool has suitable adapters for the bolt head geometry used on EQ-P3-L1-HP01.
- Pressure measurement equipment compatible with hydraulic systems, rated to exceed the system pressure limit and supplied with calibration documentation. Use fittings and hoses rated for hydraulic fluid and the referenced system pressure limit.
- Hand tools for access panels, retaining hardware, and witness markings. Use non-sparking tools as required by local safety rules.
- Clean cloths, inspection mirror, thickness feeler or shim pack for visual gap assessment, and approved seal repair kit as specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Lockout/tagout materials and personal protective equipment required by SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Coordinate with production and operations using SOP-P3-L1-02 to establish machine downtime and safety perimeter.
  - Apply lockout/tagout in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-01 before any mechanical or hydraulic work. Verify energy isolation visually and by test where applicable.
  - Review MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for component removal and reassembly drawings. Confirm availability of a calibrated torque tool and pressure gauge.
- Mechanical fastener verification and re-torque
  - Remove access covers to expose the main ram bolt and bearing housing. Clean the bolt head and surrounding area to remove scale and lubricant that could affect torque readings.
  - Inspect the bolt, washer, and threads for visible damage, corrosion, or galling. If damage is found, tag the component and consult MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for replacement guidance prior to reassembly.
  - Using the calibrated torque tool, verify the tensile condition of the main ram bolt. The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Apply torque smoothly to avoid shock loads and use the same tool orientation used during calibration.
  - If torque does not achieve the specified reading, remove the bolt, inspect threads, and clean or replace as required per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Reinstall and apply torque to the specified value.
  - Mark witness points on bolt head and adjoining surface to indicate verified torque. Record the torque verification value and torque tool serial number in the maintenance record.
- Hydraulic system verification
  - With mechanical checks complete and covers replaced as required, prepare to verify system pressure. Confirm that hydraulic fluid level and condition meet the criteria in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 before pressurizing.
  - Attach the calibrated pressure measurement equipment to the test port specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Follow safe pressurization steps described in SOP-P3-L1-01.
  - Verify that the system attains normal operating pressure and that pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Monitor relief valve response and look for pressure spikes during a controlled test cycle.
  - If pressure exceeds the system pressure limit, stop testing immediately, isolate the circuit, and follow troubleshooting in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1. Do not place the machine back into service until the cause is identified and corrected.
- Lubrication and ancillary checks
  - Inspect lubrication points for continuity of supply and accumulation of contamination. Replace worn hoses or fittings per MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 guidance.
  - Conduct a short functional test cycle under observation to detect leaks, unusual noise, or movement anomalies. Use SOP-P3-L1-02 for operational sequencing if energized testing is required.
- Completion
  - Restore safety covers and remove lockout/tagout following SOP-P3-L1-01 procedures. Inform operations that the machine is ready for return to service.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical
  - Main ram bolt is installed and verified to the specified main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Witness marking present and legible.
  - No visible damage to bolt threads, housing, or surrounding structure; if present, corrective action documented and replacement parts procured as specified in MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1.
- Hydraulic
  - Hydraulic circuit maintains pressure within safe operating limits and does not exceed the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar during controlled verification. Relief valve operation and set points are documented.
  - No active fluid leaks at inspected connections, seals, or hoses during a monitored test cycle.
- Records to keep
  - Maintenance entry documenting tasks performed, parts replaced, and safety steps followed. Include the calibrated torque tool serial number and pressure gauge calibration reference. Cite MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 for any parts replaced.
  - Signed completion checklist referencing SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 as applicable, including witness signature from maintenance and production representatives.
  - Photographs of critical areas before and after work where practical, and copies of any nonconformance reports generated during the activity.
- Example entries
  - Example record should include statement of torque verification with the torque value 1425 N·m, the torque tool identifier, pressure verification with reading relative to 330 bar, and a note on any corrective action taken. Maintain records in the document control system as required by local plant policy.

Related documents
- MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1
- SOP-P3-L1-01
- SOP-P3-L1-02

# MM-P3-L1-SB02 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Scope
This manual covers planned preventive maintenance and in-service inspection activities for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02). It is intended for use by qualified maintenance technicians and shift engineers. The document includes background and rationale for tasks, required tools, stepwise procedures written for clarity, and acceptance criteria for completed work. Use this manual in conjunction with related documentation: MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3, SB-1027, and SOP-P3-L1-04.

Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet provides surface conditioning of hot-forged parts prior to downstream operations. Regular maintenance is required to preserve blast efficiency, prevent component damage, and limit downtime. Wear on the blast wheel liner affects pattern distribution and media containment; incorrect clamping or loose fasteners accelerates wear and increases risk of foreign object ingress. Maintaining the shot media inventory within specified levels ensures consistent abrasive exposure and avoids impact energy drift. The specified bolt torque and media top-up interval are based on manufacturer recommendations and plant validation to provide repeatable, safe operation.

Tools
- Torque wrench set suitable for 65 N·m
- Socket to suit blast wheel liner bolts
- Portable vacuum suited for abrasive media recovery
- Replacement wear liners as specified in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3
- Media sampling container and visual comparator as detailed in SB-1027
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L1-04

Procedure
Pre-maintenance checks and preparations
- Confirm lockout/tagout and energy isolation per SOP-P3-L1-04. Verify isolation before any access to the cabinet interior.
- Notify operations and log planned work in the maintenance schedule system referenced by MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3. Record the equipment id EQ-P3-L1-SB02 on all entries.
- Inspect the cabinet exterior for signs of leaking seals or fastener damage that may indicate internal issues.

Blast wheel liner inspection and replacement
- Remove access panels to expose the blast wheel and liner area. Clean loose media and dust with a portable vacuum to allow clear visual inspection.
- Visually inspect the liner for cracking, deformation, or local thinning. Refer to MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 for liner part selection and fitment orientation.
- If liner replacement is required, loosen bolts sufficiently to remove the liner. When reinstalling or securing a liner, apply the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and follow the star pattern described in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 to ensure uniform clamp load.
- Rationale: consistent bolt torque prevents vibration-driven loosening and minimizes differential wear between liner segments.

Shot media management
- Prior to media sampling, isolate the media hopper and ensure dust extraction is operational. Draw a representative sample and compare against the visual comparator protocol in SB-1027 to determine contamination level and shot size degradation.
- When the sample indicates need for top-up, add shot media to the hopper until normal operating level is restored. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours. Record each top-up action in the media log.
- Rationale: regular top-ups at the specified interval maintain consistent abrasive mass flow and mitigate overloading of separation systems.

Wear monitoring and auxiliary components
- Inspect separator screens, dust collector connections, and feed gates for accumulation and wear. Clear obstructions and replace components per MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 where visible degradation is present.
- Check feed rates and observe blast pattern with a test panel (use a known reference part) to confirm efficacy after maintenance. Record observations and attach photos to the work order.

Safety and housekeeping
- Remove debris and ensure that all guards and access panels are reinstated. Confirm torque values on critical fasteners and enter readings in the maintenance log.
- Perform a functional run in single-cycle mode as permitted by SOP-P3-L1-04 to verify normal operation before returning the cabinet to production.

Examples and notes
- Example record entry: equipment EQ-P3-L1-SB02; activity: liner torque check; bolt torque applied: 65 N·m; media top-up performed: yes; media interval observed: 45 hours; inspector: technician name; attached photos: yes. Use MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 forms for part references and SB-1027 for media analysis.
- If recurring loosening of liner bolts is observed despite correct torque application, escalate to engineering and reference SB-1027 for contamination-related causes. Document any deviation from the normal procedure and the corrective action taken.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order including date, technician name, and equipment id EQ-P3-L1-SB02.
- Torque readings and tool calibration reference for the torque wrench used.
- Media sampling results and comparator records as per SB-1027.
- Media top-up log entries showing that the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours was adhered to.
- Replacement liner part traceability and installation records per MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.

Acceptance criteria
- All blast wheel liner bolts are torqued to the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m; torque readings entered and tool calibration confirmed.
- Visual inspection confirms liners are free of cracking and within acceptable wear limits defined in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
- Media sample meets acceptance per SB-1027 or corrective actions are recorded and executed.
- Media top-up activity and interval are recorded, demonstrating compliance with the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours.
- Functional test run demonstrates normal blast pattern and no abnormal vibrations or leaks. Any deviation must be documented and corrected before returning to production.

References
- MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3
- SB-1027
- SOP-P3-L1-04

# MM-P3-L1-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Scope
- This manual provides maintenance tasks, safe work rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03).  
- Applies to preventive and corrective maintenance activities necessary to ensure reliable heating to process setpoints and safe handling of induction coil and cooling systems.  
- Refer to SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05 for wiring diagrams, safety barriers, and operational procedures.

Background and purpose
- EQ-P3-L1-IH03 is an induction billet heater used to raise billets to process temperature prior to forging. Proper coil condition and cooling are critical to maintain heat transfer efficiency and asset life.  
- The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C. Maintaining uniform coil impedance and adequate cooling prevents overheating of the coil and nearby components, reduces unplanned downtime, and ensures part quality.

Tools and consumables
- Insulation-resistant gloves and arc-rated face shield per site PPE protocol (see SOP-P3-L1-05).  
- Hand tools for coil clamp adjustment and fastener torqueing (match OEM tool list in SB-1044).  
- Infrared pyrometer or thermocouple reader calibrated to site standard (refer SB-1047 for calibration certificate location).  
- Flow meter portable test rig compatible with induction coil cooling lines.  
- Non-contact vibration scanner for detecting loose coil assemblies.  
- Cooling system test fluid and hose fittings as specified in SB-1044.  
- Tagout/lockout kit consistent with SOP-P3-L1-05.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify permit and lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L1-05. Confirm isolations: electrical supply to induction inverter and cooling pump circuits isolated and verified.  
- Inspect PPE and ensure all personnel in the work area are briefed on hazards associated with high temperature, stored energy in capacitors, and pressurized cooling circuits.  
- Gather records: most recent coil impedance baseline and cooling system test log (see records to keep).

Visual and electrical inspection
- With system deenergized and capacitors discharged per SB-1044, inspect coil windings for cracked insulation, hot spots, or evidence of arcing. Remove scale and debris from coil exterior using nonconductive tools. Rationale: physical damage increases localized heating and impedance variance.  
- Inspect coil clamping hardware for looseness; verify mounting studs are secure. Rationale: vibration-driven loosening can change coil geometry and reduce heating uniformity.

Cooling system verification
- Restore cooling system power while maintaining induction inverter locked out to perform cooling checks. Activate cooling pumps and verify flow using the portable flow meter. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Rationale: insufficient flow reduces heat removal capability and can lead to coil failure.  
- Inspect inlet and outlet lines for leaks, kinks, or deposits. Flush and strain cooling lines if evidence of contamination is found. Note: maintain containment and disposal records per SB-1047.

Electrical continuity and impedance
- With inverter still locked out and safety permits in place, measure coil impedance and compare to baseline documented in the coil condition record. Rationale: impedance drift indicates insulation breakdown, shorted turns, or changes in coil geometry. If deviation from baseline exceeds limits defined in SB-1044, escalate for coil repair or replacement.

Operational functional test
- Return system to normal configuration per SOP-P3-L1-05. Energize induction inverter and perform a low-power heat cycle using operator controls with test billet or equivalent thermal load. Monitor temperature rise with calibrated pyrometer to verify expected heating profile toward the target. Use thermal imaging to verify uniformity across the billet surface. Rationale: small functional tests confirm combined electrical and fluid system health without stressing components.

Examples and troubleshooting
- Example: If flow is measured below the specified 65 L/min, first inspect for closed valves or blocked strainers. If strainers contain debris, clean and retest. If pump output remains low, tag out and initiate pump maintenance as per SB-1044.  
- Example: If measured impedance has increased since baseline, check for loose connections and retighten per torque values in SB-1044, then remeasure. If impedance remains high, schedule coil rewinding or replacement per SB-1044.

Records to keep
- Coil condition inspection report (include photos and measured impedance values).  
- Cooling flow verification log with measured flow and corrective actions. Include the measured coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min entry where applicable.  
- Functional test report with pyrometer readings showing approach toward the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C, thermal images, and operator sign-off.  
- Lockout/tagout permit and personnel safety brief record per SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- Any parts replaced, referencing SB-1044 for part identification and SB-1047 for calibration and certification documentation.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil mechanical inspection shows no cracked insulation, no loose mountings, and no signs of arcing.  
- Measured coil impedance falls within the acceptable range documented in SB-1044 compared to baseline.  
- Cooling system achieves at or above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min with no leakage.  
- Operational test demonstrates heating behavior consistent with previous performance and shows control system achieving or trending toward the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C.  
- All maintenance actions are recorded, and documentation uploaded to the equipment history file with references to SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05.

Notes and escalation
- If any acceptance criterion is not met, cease operation and raise a maintenance work order as per SOP-P3-L1-05. Include all records listed above and notify process engineering and shift supervision.  
- For questions about coil repair scope or inverter interface, consult SB-1044 and SB-1047 prior to performing nonstandard repairs.
title: Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

text:
# MM-P3-L2-SB01 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, inspection criteria, and records required for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) in plant P3, line P3-L2. It covers routine access, lining inspection and replacement guidance, shot media replenishment, and verification activities needed to maintain cleaning performance and component life. Use this manual in conjunction with ECN-2026-019 and SOP-P3-L2-01 for change notices and safe work procedures, and SOP-P3-L2-05 for lockout/tagout and confined space guidance where applicable.

Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet is critical to surface preparation of ring-rolled forgings prior to downstream machining and inspection. Wear of the blast wheel liner and loss of shot media both degrade blasting efficiency, increase cycle variability, and accelerate wear to internal components. Regular inspection and preventive replacement of wear items minimizes unscheduled downtime and prevents damage to blast wheel components. Maintaining consistent media level preserves shot flow characteristics and reduces the risk of nozzle plugging and uneven blast coverage.

Mandatory values
- The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
- The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours.

Tools
- Standard hand tools sufficient for access panel removal and fastener torqueing; use a calibrated torque wrench set to the specified torque for liner bolts.
- Inspection flashlight and wear gauge for liner and door seal inspection.
- Replacement liner hardware and gaskets as specified in ECN-2026-019.
- Clean container and sieve for media cleanliness check, plus approved shot media for top-up.
- Records log (electronic or paper) for maintenance entries, component serials, and media batch numbers.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review relevant safety procedures in SOP-P3-L2-05 and permit requirements in SOP-P3-L2-01 prior to work. Establish isolation and lockout per plant policy and verify energy sources are controlled.
- Inspect the area and prepare tools and parts at the worksite. Ensure access panels are clear and that a suitably calibrated torque wrench is available.

Inspection and fastener verification
- Remove the access cover for the blast wheel housing following the manufacturer access sequence. Visually inspect the blast wheel liner for wear patterns, cracks, or deformation. Pay attention to the liner segments adjacent to the wheel inlet and along the high-impact zone.
- Verify each liner bolt is torqued to the specified value. Use the calibrated torque wrench and set to the mandated torque prior to re-installation: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
- If any bolt does not meet the torque requirement due to head rounding, elongation, or thread damage, remove and replace the bolt with new hardware per ECN-2026-019 before proceeding.

Liner replacement guidance
- Replace liner segments when surface loss or deformation compromises the original profile such that grit retention or wheel clearance is outside acceptable contact geometry. When replacing, ensure mating surfaces are clean and gaskets or seals are seated correctly.
- Install new liner segments using manufacturer-specified orientation. Hand-start all bolts before performing final torque sequence to ensure even seating. Apply the specified torque to each bolt using the calibrated torque wrench.

Shot media inspection and top-up
- Confirm media cleanliness and particle integrity by sampling from the media hopper into the sieve and remove fines and contaminants. Maintain records of media batch or lot number when adding new media.
- Top up shot media according to operational consumption: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Use only approved shot media as documented in ECN-2026-019.
- After topping up, run a short verification cycle to confirm even media flow and absence of unusual noise or vibration. Observe machine behavior and inspect for dust leaks or abnormal discharge.

Reassembly and functional check
- Reinstall access covers and secure all fasteners. Verify guard and interlock function per SOP-P3-L2-01 requirements.
- Return the machine to service per SOP-P3-L2-05 procedures and monitor the first production run for consistent blast quality.

Examples and situational notes
- Example scenario: If an operator reports localized over-blasting on part circumferences, inspect the liner for localized thinning in the corresponding azimuth. Corrective action typically involves replacing the affected liner segment and verifying bolt torque per this manual.
- Example scenario: If media contamination is discovered during inspection, isolate the cabinet, remove contaminated media, clean the hopper, and replenish with certified media lots documented in ECN-2026-019.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each inspection and maintenance activity, including component serials and liner segment identifiers, media batch or lot numbers, and a note that the blast wheel liner bolt torque verification was performed to the specified value.
- Media top-up entries showing the interval reference and the media lot added; include operator name and machine shift where applicable.
- Any nonconformance or corrective action records generated and cross-referenced to ECN-2026-019 when parts or procedures differ from baseline.

Acceptance criteria
- Liner bolt torque verification complete and recorded with the specified torque applied: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
- Blast wheel liners exhibit no cracks, catastrophic loss of section, or misalignment after maintenance. Wear patterns may be present but must not expose base structure or produce sharp edges that alter shot stream.
- Media level has been assessed and replenished per operational consumption and interval guidance: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Media cleanliness confirmed and batch recorded.
- Functional check demonstrates consistent blast coverage and normal machine acoustics with no new leaks or abnormal vibrations.
- All records completed and filed according to plant document control and linked to ECN-2026-019, SOP-P3-L2-01, and SOP-P3-L2-05.

References
- ECN-2026-019
- SOP-P3-L2-01
- SOP-P3-L2-05
