# MM-P3-L2-RR02 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2

Revision: Rev B
Plant: P3, line P3-L2
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-RR02

Scope
This document defines the preventive maintenance procedure for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02). The intent is to preserve machine integrity, prevent unplanned downtime, and maintain product quality through recurring inspection and service activities focused on the mandrel clamp and main roll bearing system. This manual supplements and references standard operating procedures and engineering change notices listed in Related Documents. Refer to ECN-2026-044 for recent engineering modifications and to SOP-P3-L2-01 and SOP-P3-L2-04 for operating and lockout procedures.

Tools
Basic mechanical service toolkit including torque wrench capable of the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque, spanners, impact-rated sockets, grease gun compatible with specified lubricant fittings, inspection mirror, flashlight, lint-free wipes, and calibrated vibration pickup if available. Use personal protective equipment consistent with plant standards and SOP-P3-L2-01.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Regular maintenance of the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings reduces risk of clamp slippage, mandrel runout, and bearing failure that can produce scrap rings or catastrophic equipment damage. The mandrel clamp bolt must be torqued to a validated value to maintain clamping force while avoiding fastener overstress. Main roll bearings require periodic lubrication to maintain an oil or grease film and to evacuate debris introduced during rolling.

Preparation
Follow SOP-P3-L2-01 for machine shutdown and electrical lockout. Verify that any changes in ECN-2026-044 have been implemented on the machine and that relevant schematics and fastener access points match the as-installed condition.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque
Clean the mandrel clamp bolt and mating thread area of any lubricant and debris using lint-free wipes. Inspect bolt for visible damage and the clamp assembly for deformation. If the bolt shows evidence of damage, tag it out and initiate replacement per plant parts procedures; do not re-use damaged hardware.

Set the calibrated torque wrench to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), which is 475 N·m. Apply torque in a single continuous motion until the wrench indicates the set value. If a torque extension or adapter is used, compensate using a calibration chart for the tool; do not exceed the specified torque. Record the measured torque and tool serial identifier in the maintenance log.

If the clamp assembly uses multiple bolts, torque each bolt to the specified value using a radial or cross pattern to ensure uniform clamp load distribution. After completing torquing, run the mandrel at low speed per SOP-P3-L2-04 to seat the assembly and re-check torques after the first production shift.

Main roll bearing lubrication
Prior to lubrication, confirm the type of lubricant in use per lubricant data maintained in the lubrication register and any changes noted in ECN-2026-044. Clean grease fittings and surrounding areas to prevent contamination. Attach the grease gun and deliver lubricant until old grease is displaced from the bearing seals or until slight resistance indicates full charge, taking care not to overfill.

The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 105 hours. Use this interval as the scheduling baseline for the lubrication program. Create a maintenance calendar entry keyed to machine run hours or production shifts as governed by the plant CMMS.

If vibration monitoring equipment is available, sample bearing vibration before and after lubrication to confirm reduction in bearing amplitude. Note any persistent increase in vibration or unusual noise; if present, follow escalation in this document.

Inspection and acceptance checks during procedure
Visually inspect seals and housings for leakage after lubrication. Verify that runout and axial play of the mandrel remain within acceptable limits as defined in SOP-P3-L2-04. If readings are out of tolerance, complete the corrective action path outlined in ECN-2026-044.

Examples and troubleshooting
Example condition: After torquing the mandrel clamp bolt to 475 N·m, the clamp shows a slight shift during the initial production run. Action: Stop the line per SOP-P3-L2-01, re-check bolt torque, inspect mating surfaces for wear or foreign material, and consult ECN-2026-044 for any design-specific guidance on clamp seating. If clamp seating cannot be achieved, tag for replacement.

Example condition: Main roll bearing shows elevated temperature or noise between scheduled lubrication events. Action: Schedule an immediate inspection, sample lubricant for contamination, grease-bearing per procedure, and increase monitoring frequency until stable. Document findings and notify maintenance supervision.

Records to keep
Record actual mandrel clamp bolt torque values, torque tool calibration identifier, technician name, and date in the equipment maintenance log. Record the main roll bearing lubrication action, lubricant type, lubricant batch if applicable, hours at time of service, and technician name. Store records consistent with plant record retention policy and reference them during audits or after encountering repeat failures.

Acceptance criteria
The equipment is acceptable for return to service when all of the following conditions are satisfied:
- The mandrel clamp bolt has been torqued to the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), which is 475 N·m, and recorded in the maintenance log.
- The main roll bearings have been lubricated and the action recorded; lubrication adheres to the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), which is 105 hours.
- No visible leakage, excessive vibration, or abnormal noise persists after procedure completion. If any of these issues remain, escalate per SOP-P3-L2-01 and reference ECN-2026-044 for any corrective engineering instructions.

Related documents
ECN-2026-044
SOP-P3-L2-01
SOP-P3-L2-04

End of document.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2

text:
# MM-P3-L2-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
This manual describes the preventive and corrective maintenance required to maintain safe, repeatable heat treat cycles for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). The content focuses on the furnace systems that affect metallurgical outcomes: atmosphere control, heating elements, thermocouple integrity, door seals, and the control system. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days. Use this document as the controlled reference for maintenance planning, execution, and record keeping. For procedural details on safe lockout and tagout, reference SOP-P3-L2-01. For shipping and spares bulletins, reference SB-1015 and SB-1041.

Tools and consumables
Required tools are those commonly used for furnace maintenance and instrumentation work, including calibrated handheld thermometry, insulation handling tools, soft nonmetallic scrapers, and instrumentation hand tools appropriate for the control vendor. Consumables include replacement thermocouples matched to the control system, replacement door seals compatible with the furnace design, high temperature gasket cement manufacturer recommended for this furnace, and cleaning solvents approved in plant procedures. Ensure all tools and consumables are approved by maintenance supervision and are traceable in stores.

Background and rationale
Maintaining the austenitizing setpoint and thermocouple accuracy directly affects microstructure, mechanical properties, and scrap rates for ring rolling feedstock. The specified austenitizing setpoint ensures full austenitization of the chosen steel grades while minimizing excessive grain growth. Thermocouple drift over time can produce significant process variation; the stated calibration interval is set to balance downtime and process control risk. The maintenance actions in this manual are designed to detect and correct common failure modes that lead to setpoint deviation or thermal nonuniformity.

Procedure
Preliminary steps
Confirm control system alarms are acknowledged and logged prior to work. Isolate power and follow the lockout procedure in SOP-P3-L2-01. Verify the furnace chamber is at ambient conditions before removing insulation or accessing internal components.

Inspection of heating elements and insulation
Visually inspect heating elements for breaks, deformation, or discoloration indicative of overheating. Inspect insulation modules for compression, bridging, or contamination from scale or quench residue. Remove loose debris with nonmetallic tools and vacuum with approved high temperature vacuum equipment. Replace insulation modules showing loss of shape or breaches in the compressive face. When reinstalling insulation, seat modules to prevent hot spots at element supports.

Door seal and mechanical system
Inspect the door seal for continuity, tears, or separation from the backing. Clean mating surfaces and apply approved gasket cement where minor gaps are present. If the seal shows material breakdown or there is evidence of gas leakage during a heat cycle, install the replacement seal per vendor guidance. Verify door hinge and latch function and that door closes uniformly. Adjustments should be made to ensure an even contact surface between the door seal and furnace face.

Thermocouple inspection and calibration
Inspect thermocouple leads and junctions for mechanical damage, abrasions, or loose fittings at process connections. Replace any thermocouple showing physical damage. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days; schedule calibration events in maintenance planning to ensure continuity of control accuracy. During calibration, perform a comparison against a laboratory reference standard following the control vendor procedure and record the correction factors. If a thermocouple shows deviation beyond the vendor tolerance, replace it and document the replacement.

Control system and atmosphere control
Verify control loops for heating zones are responding and that setpoint tracking is within expected behavior. Confirm atmosphere supply and return lines are free of obstructions and that purge cycles operate per process requirements. Inspect atmosphere generator components and filtration per SB-1015 guidance for spares and replacement items. Log any variances and tag components for corrective action.

Corrective repairs
For element failure, replace elements using the manufacturer specified replacement items. For insulation breaches, replace affected modules. For control card failures, refer to SB-1041 for spare card handling and vendor contact information. After any corrective repair, perform a controlled heat cycle using an empty load to validate uniformity and control accuracy before returning the furnace to production.

Acceptance criteria
Successful completion of maintenance is confirmed when the following conditions are met:
- Control maintains the austenitizing setpoint within the control system limits established by the furnace vendor and process engineering.
- Thermocouples read consistently with the laboratory reference within the vendor tolerance after calibration.
- Door seal provides no measurable leakage during a monitored purge or heat cycle.
- Visual inspection reveals no degraded insulation or compromised heating elements.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance log for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 that includes a description of work performed, parts replaced, serial numbers where applicable, and the name of the technician and supervisor who authorized the action. Log thermocouple calibration results and any correction factors applied to control settings. Retain pre- and post-maintenance furnace temperature profile captures for each validation run. File all entries in the document control system and link maintenance records to the equipment history as required.

Examples and notes
Example maintenance entries should document the observed condition, corrective action, parts used, and references to the related documents SB-1015, SB-1041, and SOP-P3-L2-01. When scheduling thermocouple calibration events, align planned outage windows with production planning. If recurring deviations are observed after repeated maintenance, escalate to process engineering for metallurgical investigation.

References
SB-1015  
SB-1041  
SOP-P3-L2-01

Revision history and approvals are maintained in the document control system associated with this manual.
title: Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

text:
# MM-P3-L3-SB01 Maintenance manual - Machining shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Scope
This manual defines the preventive maintenance tasks, methods, and acceptance criteria for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01). It applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for preserving part quality, safety, and equipment availability on line P3-L3. This document references related procedures and records as listed in the related documents section and supplements the operational controls in SOP-P3-L3-03.

Background and rationale
The cabinet provides controlled abrasive cleaning of machined castings prior to downstream handling. Key failure modes affecting part finish and cycle reliability include wear of the blast wheel components, loss of media volume, and contamination of recycled media. Regular inspection and adjustment reduce scrap and unplanned downtime, and preserve blast pattern consistency. The tasks below prioritize fast inspection of critical items and corrective actions that restore the system to known condition.

Related documents
- MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2
- SB-1022
- SOP-P3-L3-03

Tools and materials
- Hand tools as specified by the manufacturer and maintenance group; use only tools that match fastener head geometry and access profile.
- Torque wrench capable of achieving the required torque range for the blast wheel liner bolts.
- Media handling container and scale for inventory record entries.
- Replacement liner segments and gasket materials as listed in SB-1022.
- Personal protective equipment consistent with SOP-P3-L3-03.

Safety notes and controls
Follow lockout-tagout and isolation procedures defined in SOP-P3-L3-03 before entering the cabinet or exposing rotating assemblies. Verify energy isolation and test for stored energy. Use hearing protection and impact-rated eye protection while performing any test run or inspection with the cabinet energized. Ensure the cabinet door interlocks are validated during reassembly.

Procedure
The procedure is organized into inspection, service, and functional verification stages. Use the steady-state routines described here for scheduled preventive maintenance and after any corrective replacement of blast wheel or cabinet internals.

- Preparation
  - Secure isolation in accordance with SOP-P3-L3-03. Record the isolation action in the work order and maintenance log.
  - Confirm required replacement parts are staged per SB-1022 and review any previous findings in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

- Inspection and cleaning
  - Open the cabinet access panel and visually inspect the blast wheel housing and liner surfaces for signs of uneven wear, cracking, or missing segments. Pay attention to the mating faces and seam locations.
  - Remove accumulated fines and dust from the media hopper and return lines. Capture and contain the fines for disposal per local waste procedure.
  - Inspect media quality in the hopper for contamination with tramp material or excessive fines. Segregate questionable media for analysis and possible replacement.

- Liner and wheel maintenance
  - Remove liner segments as needed to access the blast wheel assembly. Clean mating surfaces and prepare for reassembly.
  - When reinstalling liner segments, ensure all liner bolt threads are clean and free of media debris. Apply the required bolt clamp using the torque wrench set to the specified torque.
  - The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 105 N·m.
  - Reinstall wheel housing covers and fasteners to restore the cabinet envelope.

- Media top-up and inventory
  - Verify media level in the hopper and compare to the media inventory record. Top up media as required to maintain consistent feed to the wheel.
  - The shot media top-up interval for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 22 hours. Use this interval as the planning cadence for media checks and top-up activities in the CMMS.
  - Record media addition volumes and source lot identifiers in the maintenance log and link to production batches as required for traceability.

- Functional verification
  - Re-establish isolation controls and remove tagouts only when instructed by a qualified supervisor. Perform a guarded test run per SOP-P3-L3-03 and verify blast pattern uniformity on a verification panel or sacrificial coupon.
  - Inspect for abnormal vibration, unusual noise, or loose fasteners after the initial run. If any anomaly is detected, stop the machine and re-check mounting and liner fasteners.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example: If edge wear is concentrated on a single liner segment, inspect the wheel balance and orientation. Corrective action may include repositioning the wheel or replacing the affected liner segment per SB-1022.
- Example: If media consumption is excessive without corresponding process load increase, sample the media for fines and contamination. Replace contaminated media and document the findings in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.
- If a fastener is found loose during inspection, re-torque to the specified value and note the discrepancy in the work order. If repeat loosening occurs, escalate to engineering for a root cause analysis.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order documenting tasks performed, parts replaced, and observations. Reference MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for historic trend data.
- Media inventory and top-up log with lot identifiers and date/time stamps consistent with CMMS entries. Link records to production batch numbers where required by SOP-P3-L3-03.
- Torque verification sheet showing the blast wheel liner bolt torque values recorded after reassembly.
- Inspection checklists and functional verification coupons stored per site record retention policy. Include any nonconformances raised and corrective actions taken.

Acceptance criteria
The cabinet is acceptable for return to service when all of the following conditions are met:
- Visual inspection shows liner segments properly seated and free of visible cracks or missing pieces.
- All blast wheel liner bolts hold the specified clamp and are recorded at the specified torque value.
- Media level and quality meet production specifications and the media top-up cadence is documented in the media log.
- Functional verification demonstrates uniform blast pattern, acceptable vibration, and no abnormal noises during the guarded test run.
- All records are completed and linked to the work order, and any deviations are entered into the corrective action system referenced in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

Revision and change control
Refer to MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for the revision history and SB-1022 for parts lists and replacement instructions. Any suggested changes to this manual should be submitted through the engineering change process and cross-referenced to SOP-P3-L3-03 for operational alignment.
title: Maintenance manual - Machining shot blast cabinet #1

text:
# MM-P3-L3-CN02 Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

Scope
This document provides maintenance instructions for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It covers routine mechanical checks, chuck jaw bolt verification, spindle warm-up procedure prior to production, and required records. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance personnel and machine operators performing routine preventive maintenance and pre-production checks. Reference related procedural and safety requirements in MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1, SOP-P3-L3-02, and SOP-P3-L3-04.

Tools
Required items for the procedures that follow: calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the chuck jaw bolt torque specified below, basic hand tools, cleaning supplies appropriate for machine tool environments, lint-free shop cloths, manufacturer-approved lubricants and grease guns as called out in equipment manufacturer guidance, and the machine control pendant for executing spindle warm-up cycles. Ensure the torque wrench calibration certificate is available per traceability practice.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Proper clamping of workpieces and stable spindle operation are critical to part accuracy and operator safety. The chuck jaw bolts secure the jaws to the chuck body; incorrect bolt preload can lead to jaw loosening, runout, and component damage. The spindle assembly requires a controlled warm-up to achieve stable thermal conditions, which reduces dimensional drift during the initial production run.

Preparation
Verify machine is in a safe state for maintenance per SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-04. Lockout and tagout the machine as required by site practice before performing mechanical adjustments when exposed rotating elements are involved. Confirm presence of required tools and torque wrench calibration documentation. Consult MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for any model-specific notes.

Chuck jaw bolt torque verification
Inspect the chuck and jaws visually for debris, visible damage, or abnormal wear. Clean the mating surfaces of the jaw and chuck using an appropriate solvent and cloth. Seat the jaw on the chuck and hand-thread the jaw bolts to ensure proper engagement.

Set the calibrated torque wrench to the specified value and apply torque to each chuck jaw bolt in a cross-pattern sequence to achieve even preload. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 75 N·m. After completing the torque sequence, perform a second pass to verify bolts remain at the specified torque.

Rationale: Applying the specified torque ensures consistent clamping force and prevents loosening during operation. Using a cross pattern equalizes load and minimizes distortion of the chuck face.

Spindle warm-up
Prior to loading hardened work material or beginning critical production, perform the spindle warm-up routine with the machine in run-permit state. Activate the spindle warm-up cycle using the control pendant and monitor spindle behavior throughout the sequence. The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 24 minutes.

Rationale: Gradual thermal stabilization of spindle bearings and spindle headstock reduces dimensional drift and runout, improving first-piece accuracy and prolonging bearing life.

Examples and special cases
If a jaw bolt fails to reach the specified torque without evidence of thread strip or damage, remove the bolt and inspect threads and mating insert. Replace damaged hardware using manufacturer-approved parts and re-torque. If the spindle exhibits abnormal vibration, noise, or temperature behavior during warm-up, stop the warm-up routine and escalate to maintenance diagnostics per SOP-P3-L3-04. Record observations and any corrective actions taken.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance log entry for each completed chuck torque verification and each spindle warm-up event. The log entry should include the equipment id, date, personnel performing the action, confirmation that the chuck jaw bolt torque was set to 75 N·m, confirmation that the spindle warm-up was completed for 24 minutes, and any anomalies or corrective actions. Retain torque wrench calibration records with the maintenance log per document control practice. If parts are replaced, reference MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for part identification and record supplier lot or traceability per site requirements.

Acceptance criteria
Acceptance is achieved when the following conditions are met: all chuck jaw bolts are torqued to the specified value and hold after verification; the spindle warm-up sequence completes without abnormal vibration or audible distress and is completed for the specified duration; no visible damage or contamination remains on the chuck mating surfaces; and entries in the maintenance log are complete and legible, including notation of the applied chuck jaw bolt torque and spindle warm-up time as stated.

Nonconformance and corrective action
If any condition fails to meet acceptance criteria, cease production and follow escalation procedures in SOP-P3-L3-04. Tag the machine out of service until corrective actions are documented and verified. Document all corrective steps in the maintenance log and reference MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for replacement part guidance.

Related documents
MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1  
SOP-P3-L3-02  
SOP-P3-L3-04

Revision history and approvals
Revision control and approval signatures are maintained in the document control system. Store completed maintenance logs and torque calibration records alongside this manual entry in the equipment folder for EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
title: Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2

# MM-P3-L3-HP03 - Maintenance manual - Machining hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03). It covers preventive maintenance tasks, inspection checkpoints, and corrective actions required to keep the press in safe, repeatable operating condition for machining operations. The procedures align with applicable safety practices and reference operational and service bulletins listed in Related Documents. The intent is to ensure mechanical integrity of the ram and hydraulic system and to document condition and repairs for traceability.

Tools
Required tools and consumables include industry-standard wrenches and sockets sized for the main ram bolt, a calibrated hydraulic pressure gauge compatible with the machine service port, inspection mirrors, LED inspection lights, clean lint-free rags, hydraulic system filter elements as specified by OEM guidance, approved hydraulic fluid as specified in the machine log, thread lubricant or anti-seize per OEM guidance, torque measurement device calibrated to traceable standards, and personal protective equipment consistent with plant policy. Use the torque measurement device to verify the main ram bolt torque stated below.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
Shut down the press per plant lockout/tagout requirements and relieve hydraulic pressure through the machine service ports. Verify energy isolation and post appropriate signs. Consult SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03 for operator-level shutdown and startup sequences and for specific machine safety interlocks before beginning maintenance.

Visual inspection
Inspect the ram, gland, seals, and surrounds for evidence of leakage, scoring, or abnormal wear. Use inspection mirrors and LED lights to examine the ram surface beyond the visible area. Record any fluid or metal contamination found on rags after wiping the ram. Check fasteners for corrosion and movement by hand prior to torque verification.

Hydraulic system pressure verification
Connect a calibrated hydraulic pressure gauge to the approved service port and slowly prime the gauge per manufacturer instructions. Confirm the system pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) which is 295 bar. If system pressure is at or above the system pressure limit, stop and consult hydraulic service procedures and Related Documents before further operation.

Main ram bolt verification and torque
Access the main ram retention bolt per machine disassembly guidance. Clean bolt threads and seating surfaces of debris and contamination. Using a calibrated torque measurement device, verify the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. If the measured torque is below specification, apply thread lubricant or anti-seize as required by OEM guidance and torque the bolt to the specified value using a calibrated torque tool. If the bolt cannot reach or maintain the specified torque, record the condition, secure the machine, and escalate to mechanical engineering for further evaluation.

Seal and gland service
If seals or gland components are worn or leaking, follow OEM replacement steps, taking care to maintain cleanliness to prevent contamination of the hydraulic system. Use lint-free materials for wiping and ensure replacement parts conform to machine specifications. After reassembly, perform a pressure verification and leak test as described above.

Functional verification
After mechanical tasks are complete and energy is restored per SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03, run a controlled test cycle per operational guidance using the documented startup procedure. Monitor for abnormal noises, seal leakage, or drifting pressures. Confirm repeatability of ram movement and that no external fluid appears at gland or bolt interfaces.

Records and documentation
Maintain a maintenance entry in the machine history log describing work performed, observations, parts replaced, measurements taken, and the names of personnel performing the work. Attach calibrated torque device and pressure gauge calibration certificates to the maintenance record when used for verification. Use the Related Documents section to link work to applicable SOPs and service bulletins.

Acceptance criteria
The press is acceptable to return to service when the following conditions are met:
- No external hydraulic leakage is present at the ram gland, bolt interfaces, or hydraulic connections after reassembly and test cycle.
- The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m as verified with a calibrated tool.
- System pressure during functional verification does not exceed the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) which is 295 bar.
- Operational performance of the ram is consistent with pre-maintenance behavior and no abnormal noises or vibrations are observed during controlled test cycles.
- All maintenance actions and measurements are recorded in the equipment history log and calibration certificates are filed with the maintenance record.

Background and rationale
Maintaining correct clamping and torque on the main ram bolt is critical to ensure axial preload and to prevent relative movement that can cause accelerated wear of the ram surface and seal damage. Verifying that hydraulic pressure remains below the system pressure limit protects system components and safety devices from overpressure conditions. Measuring and recording these parameters provide a defensible maintenance history that supports root cause analysis if repeat failures occur.

Examples and real-world notes
Example entries in the maintenance log should include the exact measured torque value as read from the calibrated instrument and the make/model of the torque device, along with the calibrated pressure gauge reading observed during verification. If a pressure spike occurred during test cycling, note the conditions that produced the spike and reference SB-1011 for any bulletin-specific guidance. When repeated torque loss or pressure excursions are observed, escalate per plant mechanical engineering policy.

Records to keep
Retain the maintenance work order, the equipment history log entry, calibration certificates for torque and pressure instruments, parts replaced invoices, and any photos documenting condition. File all records in the document control system under this manual’s document id for traceability.

Related documents
SB-1011  
SOP-P3-L3-02  
SOP-P3-L3-03

# MM-P3-L4-RR01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions and acceptance criteria for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) installed on line P3-L4. It covers preventive lubrication, clamp bolt torque verification, bearings inspection, and record keeping required to support safe, repeatable operation in the heat treat cell. This document aligns with shop best practices and references related procedural documents (SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03).

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills in heat treat service are subject to cyclic loading, elevated ambient conditions near furnaces, and contamination from scale and quench media. Critical interfaces include the mandrel clamp and main roll bearings. The mandrel clamp bolt preload directly affects ring control and concentricity during rolling; loss of preload can produce out-of-tolerance parts and pose safety risks. Main roll bearings require a consistent lubrication cadence to preserve film thickness and prevent premature fatigue. Prescribed torque and lubrication intervals are set to maintain preload and bearing life while accommodating the mill's operating environment.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the required clamp bolt torque as specified below, with current calibration certificate referenced in maintenance records.
- Clean, lint-free rags and approved bearing-grade grease compatible with the bearing manufacturer recommendations and SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Low-pressure grease gun compatible with the mill grease fittings.
- Inspection lamp and borescope for visual assessment of bearing seals and mandrel surfaces.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P3-L4-03 and SB-1028, including heat-resistant gloves and eye protection.
- Maintenance log forms and electronic entry device for records retention.

Critical values
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify lockout/tagout and energy isolation in accordance with SOP-P3-L4-03 before any disassembly or torque application. Ensure the mill is at a safe cool-down state per SB-1028 prior to hand contact with components.
- Review the bearing and clamp maintenance history in the equipment records to confirm the last torque verification and lubrication entry. Retrieve the torque wrench calibration certificate.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification
- Clean the clamp bolt head and surrounding area to remove grease and debris so the torque wrench can seat properly.
- Set the calibrated torque wrench to the specified value: the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Use the wrench slowly and smoothly to achieve the value; apply final torque in a controlled motion to avoid impact loading.
- If the bolt does not reach the specified torque due to rotation, remove, inspect threads and seating surfaces for wear or contamination, clean or replace as required, and reapply torque to the specified value.
- Document the applied torque, torque wrench serial number, and operator initials in the maintenance log. Note any deviations and corrective actions taken.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is up to date in the maintenance schedule. If the interval has elapsed, proceed with lubrication.
- Clean grease fitting area and attach grease gun. Pump grease until purge from the bearing seal indicates adequate fill, taking care not to over-grease bearing housings. Use grease types and quantities recommended by the bearing supplier as recorded in equipment procurement and SB-1028.
- Inspect bearing seals, housings, and adjacent components for signs of overheating, contamination, or grease degradation. If abnormal conditions are observed, tag out the equipment and escalate per SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Record lubricant type, lot code, grease gun identifier, and date/time of lubrication in the maintenance log.

Bearing and component inspection
- Using the inspection lamp and borescope, examine bearing seals, mandrel surface, and roll journals for scoring, spalling, corrosion, or contamination. Note presence of embedded particles or discoloration indicative of overheating or contamination.
- If damage is detected that could compromise operation, document findings with photos, remove the component for shop-level inspection, and reference corrective actions in SB-1028.

Examples and rationale
- Example record entry: torque confirmation entry should list the applied torque value (605 N·m), torque wrench ID, calibration date, and operator initials. This provides traceability for audits and failure analysis.
- Rationale for lubrication cadence: the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours to maintain consistent grease film under cyclic loading and elevated ambient conditions near heat treat equipment. Deviating from this interval increases risk of fatigue failure.

Records to keep
- Torque verification form including applied torque (605 N·m), torque tool identifier, calibration certificate reference, operator, date/time, and any corrective actions.
- Lubrication log noting lubricant type, lot code, grease gun ID, interval completion (main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours), operator, and observations.
- Inspection reports and photos for bearing and clamp surfaces.
- Reference to related procedural documents: SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03.

Acceptance criteria
- Mandrel clamp bolt torque is confirmed at the specified value: the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Torque verification form completed and signed.
- Main roll bearings have received lubrication within the scheduled cadence: the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 160 hours, and the lubrication log entry is present.
- No visual indications of bearing distress, mandrel damage, or contamination above limits described in SB-1028. Any deviations must be escalated per SOP-P3-L4-02 and corrective actions documented.
- Maintenance actions and records must be retained per plant records policy and be available for review alongside SB-1028, SOP-P3-L4-02, and SOP-P3-L4-03.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P3-L4-HT02 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Scope
This manual prescribes preventive maintenance, inspection, calibration, and acceptance criteria for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). It applies to maintenance technicians and furnace operators responsible for safe operation, metallurgical control, and traceable records retention. Activities described here are intended to maintain process capability, safety interlocks, and repeatable thermal profiles required by process engineering and quality assurance.

Background and rationale
Maintaining stable austenitizing and cooling profiles in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 is essential to achieve specified microstructure and mechanical properties in forged components. Out-of-tolerance temperatures or degraded thermocouple performance lead to nonconforming parts and potential rework. This manual aligns with change control and operating procedures; see ECN-2026-001 for design changes and SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05 for operation and control-zone responsibilities. Calibration of temperature sensing and verification of setpoints ensure process reproducibility and regulatory traceability.

Critical settings
The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.  
The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 110 days.

Tools and consumables
- Portable data logger capable of NIST-traceable calibration and independent of furnace controller.  
- Spare temperature-sensing elements compatible with furnace input, logged and tagged as calibrated.  
- Non-sparking hand tools for enclosure service, insulated handling gloves, and PPE per site rules.  
- Pre-approved calibration bath or dry-block standard against which thermocouples are compared.  
- Maintenance log forms and electronic records access to document results and corrective actions.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify lockout-tagout and safety clearance per SOP-P3-L4-05 before any maintenance or calibration work begins.  
- Ensure records from the previous inspection are available for review and that ECN-2026-001 changes are incorporated into wiring and controller settings where applicable.

Visual inspection and housekeeping
- Inspect chamber interior for scale accumulation, damaged insulation, or foreign material that could affect thermal distribution. Remove residues following furnace-specific cleaning procedures detailed in SOP-P3-L4-02, ensuring no abrasive actions expose sensor mounts or thermocouple wells.  
- Check door seals and mechanical interlocks for secure engagement. Any damaged seal or interlock shall be documented and repaired prior to process use.

Thermocouple verification and calibration
- Remove the process thermocouple from the control position and perform a bench comparison to the site standard reference using the calibration bath or dry-block. Record baseline offset for each thermocouple channel.  
- The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 110 days. Maintain a calibrated tag on each sensor that indicates the last calibration event and links to electronic records. If a sensor shows drift beyond site acceptance (see Acceptance criteria), replace or recondition the sensor and document corrective action.

Controller setpoint confirmation
- With the chamber empty and following warm-up guidance in SOP-P3-L4-02, verify controller reads and maintains the austenitizing setpoint. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Confirm the controller displays stable indication and that independent data logger confirms the controller output corresponds to actual chamber temperature within acceptance limits.

Sensor redundancy and fail-safes
- Verify redundant sensing channels and alarm thresholds are functioning. Simulate sensor open-circuit and short conditions to confirm alarms and interlocks trip as defined in SOP-P3-L4-05. Document alarm response and any deviations for engineering review.

Mechanical and support systems
- Inspect active cooling connections, circulation ducts, and fans for blockage or degradation that could affect cooling uniformity post-austenitizing. Verify external fixtures and retorts are secure and free from deformation.

Records and documentation
- Complete the maintenance log for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and attach calibration certificates for any sensors or data loggers used. Include reference to any ECN-2026-001 implementation details and operator procedure changes per SOP-P3-L4-02 and SOP-P3-L4-05. Keep records in the document control system per site policy and ensure traceability from part lots to furnace maintenance events.

Examples of typical entries to keep
- Sensor ID, bench offset, calibration standard used, technician name, and link to calibration certificate.  
- Verification run data from independent data logger showing time-stamped temperature vs. controller setpoint.  
- Description and disposition of any nonconforming reading or replaced component, with reference to ECN-2026-001 when applicable.

Acceptance criteria
- Controller must hold the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) at 885 °C within the allowable controller control band defined in SOP-P3-L4-02. Independent data logger verification must demonstrate agreement with controller indication under steady-state conditions.  
- Thermocouples used for process control must meet accuracy and stability requirements on their calibration certificate. The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 110 days; sensors out of interval are not acceptable for process use until calibrated and tagged.  
- Any repaired or replaced sensor, seal, or interlock must be reverified against the acceptance criteria above before the furnace returns to production.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-001  
- SOP-P3-L4-02  
- SOP-P3-L4-05

Revision control
Maintain this document in the document control system. Record each maintenance event under EQ-P3-L4-HT02 entries and reference the applicable SOPs and the ECN where design changes impact maintenance scope.
title: Maintenance manual - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

# MM-P3-L4-SB03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3
Revision: Rev C
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Scope
- This document defines the preventive maintenance tasks, method, and acceptance criteria for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) in plant P3, line P3-L4.
- Tasks cover inspection, cleaning, wear measurement, media management, and fastener torque verification required to maintain safe and consistent blasting performance.
- This manual applies to maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Reference related documents for complementary procedures: SB-1019, SB-1038, SOP-P3-L4-02.

Background and rationale
- EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is a blast cabinet used after heat treat operations to remove scale and residue prior to downstream handling. Consistent blast energy, media condition, and wheel integrity are critical to part quality and process repeatability.
- The blast wheel liner secures the wheel assembly and maintains alignment. Fastener preload affects wheel vibration and media trajectory; improper torque leads to accelerated wear or unsafe operation. Therefore, verification of the blast wheel liner bolt torque is required.
- Shot media degrades and fines accumulate during operation. Topping up media maintains charge level and abrasive characteristics; regular intervals prevent process drift and reduce the need for corrective interventions during production.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of reading and applying 90 N·m.
- Hand tools and socket set suitable for cabinet fasteners.
- Personal protective equipment: hearing protection, eye protection, respirator per SOP-P3-L4-02, gloves.
- Shop vacuum and non-sparking hand brush.
- Media handling container and funnel for controlled top-up.
- Inspection mirror and flashlight.
- Maintenance logbook or electronic maintenance record entry device.

Procedure
Preparation
- Lockout/tagout the isolation defined in SOP-P3-L4-02 for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 before any work. Verify energy sources are isolated per SOP-P3-L4-02 prior to opening access panels.
- Don required PPE before entry into the work area.

Inspection and cleaning
- Open the access panel to the blast wheel housing following the sequence in SB-1019 for safe access. Visually inspect the wheel, liner, and surrounding structure for cracks, unusual wear, or foreign objects.
- Remove accumulated dust and media fines from the housing and inlet areas using a shop vacuum and brush. Collect vacuumed material in the provided container for disposal or analysis per SB-1038.
- Use an inspection mirror to check wheel hub and inner surfaces not visible directly. Document any surface anomalies in the maintenance log.

Blast wheel liner bolt torque verification
- With the wheel immobilized and lockout verified, clean the threads and bolt heads of the blast wheel liner fasteners to remove dust and debris that may affect torque readings.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, apply torque to each blast wheel liner bolt until the wrench indicates the target torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. If any bolt does not achieve the target due to thread damage or slippage, replace the affected fastener and re-torque.
- Sequence torquing in a star pattern to ensure even clamping where applicable; consult SB-1019 for wheel removal/reinstallation detail when disassembly is required.
- Record the torque verification results in the maintenance log, noting bolt locations and any corrective actions.

Shot media management
- Check media level and condition after cleaning. Top-up media as necessary to maintain consistent blast performance. The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Perform top-up at or before the specified interval during scheduled preventive rounds rather than waiting for visible depletion.
- When adding media, use the dedicated media container and funnel to minimize contamination. Avoid mixing different media grades unless validated by process engineering and documented in SB-1038.
- Collect a representative media sample for periodic analysis per SB-1038 to track degradation and contamination trends. Label and retain samples as directed.

Functional check and restart
- After maintenance tasks, verify that all access panels and guards are secured per SB-1019. Remove lockout/tagout only after all tools and personnel are clear and checks are complete.
- Conduct a controlled startup and observe for abnormal vibration, noise, or leakage. If anomalies occur, shut down and investigate per SOP-P3-L4-02.

Examples and rationale for actions
- Example: If during torque verification a bolt loosens below specification repeatedly after successive checks, suspect thread galling, liner seat distortion, or wheel imbalance. Replace the bolt and evaluate wheel runout per SB-1019 before returning the machine to service.
- Rationale: Regular torque verification at the specified value prevents eccentric loading that increases abrasive wear and reduces fatigue life of the wheel assembly.

Acceptance criteria
- All blast wheel liner bolts meet or exceed the specified torque: blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. No bolt may be below this value at the time of inspection.
- No loose fasteners, cracks, or foreign objects remain in the wheel housing after cleaning and inspection.
- Shot media has been topped up within the prescribed period: shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Records show top-up actions were performed within this interval.
- No abnormal vibration or noise observed during functional check that would suggest imbalance or misassembly.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each visit including date/time, technician name, tasks performed, torque readings for each bolt, media top-up amount (qualitative note of top-up performed), and any defects found.
- Media sample identification and retention record per SB-1038.
- Copy of any corrective actions and parts replaced filed with the equipment history and referenced to SB-1019 when wheel removal or reinstallation was required.
- All records must refer to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and be retained per plant documentation retention practice and reviewed during periodic audits.

References
- SB-1019
- SB-1038
- SOP-P3-L4-02

# MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

## Scope
This maintenance manual section defines lubrication and fluid handling controls for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). It covers acceptable lubricants, transfer and storage practices, fill and service procedures, and recordkeeping required to support consistent quench and handling performance during heat treatment operations. This document applies to maintenance and process technicians responsible for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and to quality personnel performing verification audits in accordance with QS-PROC-08 and the operating sequences referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Background and rationale: improper lubrication or contaminated fluids can compromise part geometry, surface finish, and metallurgical outcomes. Controls in this document are intended to prevent cross-contamination, ensure fluid integrity during service, and preserve the defined quench characteristics necessary for process repeatability.

Note: The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376.

## Tools and materials
- Clean service cart or tray dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Filter-equipped transfer pump compatible with CFW-LUB-376.
- Closed-top, labeled containers for temporary holding that are dedicated to CFW-LUB-376.
- Particle and water-testing kits suitable for the lubricant formulation CFW-LUB-376.
- Personal protective equipment as required by site safety procedures and SOP-P2-L2-01.
- Clean, lint-free wipes and funnel with particulate screen.
- Seals and gasket kits approved for contact with CFW-LUB-376.
- Logbook or electronic record entry device for maintenance records, per QS-PROC-08.

All tools that contact lubricants or fluids must be cleaned and dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02 or clearly marked for single-equipment use to prevent cross-contamination between lines.

## Procedure
Preparation
- Verify authorization: confirm maintenance task is authorized by the shift supervisor and documented per SOP-P2-L2-03.
- PPE and containment: don required PPE and place drip trays under service points to catch incidental spills.
- Identification: confirm lubricant to be used is the part number CFW-LUB-376. Only use containers labeled with CFW-LUB-376 and inspect seals prior to opening.

Fluid handling and transfer
- Inspect source container for integrity and verify labeling includes CFW-LUB-376. If label or seal is compromised, do not use and escalate per SOP-P2-L2-03.
- Use the dedicated, clean transfer pump fitted with a particle filter. Replace filter cartridges if they show visible loading prior to transfer to prevent particulate introduction.
- When topping or refilling systems, pour using a funnel with screen and collect runoff in the drip tray. Do not transfer lubricant via open buckets that are used elsewhere on site.

Service and component replacement rationale
- Replace seals and gaskets that contact lubricant whenever service access requires disassembly. Old seals can shed particles and introduce contaminants that affect quench performance.
- If any unexpected visual change in fluid appearance is observed during service, capture a sample for particle and water analysis using the testing kits provided. Document findings in the maintenance log.

Sample take and testing
- Collect lubricant samples after initial fill and following any event that could introduce contamination. Use clean sample bottles dedicated to CFW-LUB-376 and label with equipment id EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and the date of sampling.
- Perform particle count and water content analysis per the test kit instructions. If results exceed acceptable ranges as defined by the lubricant supplier documentation, remove the fluid from service and replace per the disposal and refill steps referenced in QS-PROC-08.

Quench and timing awareness
- Maintain awareness of process timing during service windows. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds. Any activity that could extend quench delay beyond this limit must be coordinated with production to avoid processing parts outside specified quench timing.

Cleaning and contamination control
- Clean all external surfaces of service points after completing work to prevent foreign material ingress.
- Dispose of used wipes, filters, and contaminated absorbents according to site waste procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01.

Examples and common actions
- Example: during a seal replacement, collect a post-service sample and perform particle analysis. If particle levels are within supplier guidance, return the unit to service and note the action in the maintenance log. If not, schedule fluid replacement and notify quality per QS-PROC-08.
- Example: when topping to compensate for minor consumption, ensure label CFW-LUB-376 is confirmed and filter the top-up fluid inline to prevent introducing particulates.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each service action including date, technician initials, parts replaced (list part numbers used), and confirmation that CFW-LUB-376 was used.
- Sample analysis reports for lubricant quality checks identified during or after service.
- Incident reports for any event that may have affected quench timing, including actions taken to return the furnace to compliant operation.
- All records shall reference EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and be filed per QS-PROC-08.

## Acceptance criteria
- Lubricant in service at the conclusion of maintenance is confirmed to be the part number CFW-LUB-376 and is free of visible contamination.
- Post-service particle and water test results must indicate fluid condition acceptable for continued operation as determined by the lubricant supplier guidance and recorded in the maintenance log.
- No service activity results in a quench delay exceeding the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds. Any deviation must be reported and resolved before returning to normal production.
- Records for the service action, testing, and materials used are complete and filed in accordance with QS-PROC-08 and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Revision control and change management
- Any proposed changes to lubricant specification, handling methods, or acceptance criteria must be submitted through the site change control process and reference QS-PROC-08 for documentation requirements.

End of document.
title: Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

# MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Scope
- This maintenance manual covers fastener inspection, torque verification practices, and way lube refill coordination for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01). It applies to maintenance technicians and shift leads performing scheduled or condition-based work on this machine.
- The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is CFW-LUB-477.
- Use this document together with SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for related safety, lockout/tagout, and lubrication tasks.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on the machine secure structural components, guards, ways, and motion assemblies. Vibration, thermal cycling from the heat treat process, and cutting forces can lead to loosening or preload loss over time. Regular inspection and controlled torque application reduce the risk of component movement, misalignment, and bearing overload.
- Way lubrication maintains film thickness and prevents metal-to-metal contact. The specified refill interval and lubricant part number are established from vendor guidance and in-plant testing to balance contamination control and service life.
- Torque verification is required after any access that removes or disturbs fasteners on load-bearing or motion-critical components to ensure repeatable preload and to avoid overstress or fatigue.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench appropriate to the fastener head type.
- Socket set and driver handles compatible with the fastener head geometry used on EQ-P1-L4-CN01.
- Fastener-specific bit inserts or washers as required by the fastener design.
- Clean lint-free rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for hard-to-see locations.
- Torque verification witness log sheet and maintenance work order forms.
- Manufacturer fastener details and assembly drawings referenced in the maintenance system; consult SOP-P1-L4-03 for documentation handling.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify machine is in a safe condition for maintenance per SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05. Ensure lockout/tagout is applied where required and that all energy sources affecting the work area are controlled.
- Gather tools and the correct lubricant CFW-LUB-477. Confirm cleanliness of torque wrench and sockets.

Visual inspection
- Conduct a systematic visual check of all external and accessible internal fasteners associated with guards, covers, baseplates, and motion components. Look for signs of fretting, corrosion, washer deformation, or thread damage. Use mirror or borescope for obscured locations.
- Identify any fasteners showing thread engagement loss or physical damage. Tag compromised fasteners for replacement and generate a work order.

Torque verification and controlled re-torque
- Where fastener preload must be controlled, use the calibrated torque wrench to verify torque. If a fastener is found below expected preload, bring it to the specified assembly procedure requirement for that component, then verify with the torque wrench again.
- For assemblies that require sequential tightening, follow the manufacturer sequence documented in the machine assembly drawings. Use small incremental rotations when seating components to avoid inducing misalignment.
- If a fastener shows signs of yielding, galling, cross-threading, or has damaged head geometry, replace it rather than attempting re-torque.

Way lube refill coordination
- Refill way lube in accordance with the established interval. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Use only lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 for refills and top-offs to maintain compatibility and additive package consistency.
- Before refill, clean the filler area per SOP-P1-L4-04 to prevent contamination ingress. Record the refill action on the maintenance log and note the lubricant part number used.

Examples and scenarios
- Example: After replacing a spindle housing cover, re-check the perimeter fasteners for torque. If multiple fasteners around the cover show preload loss, suspect seat distortion; loosen and re-seat the cover, clean mating faces, apply specified fasteners or replacements, and re-torque per assembly procedure.
- Example: During routine inspection a technician observes minor oil seepage near a way wiper. Clean the area, replace the wiper if degraded, and perform a way lube top-off using CFW-LUB-477. Log the top-off and plan the next refill based on the operating hours accumulation using the interval provided.

Records to keep
- Maintain a torque verification log with the following entries: equipment id, fastener location description, inspection finding, torque verification outcome, any fastener replacements, technician initials, and work order reference. Archive logs per plant document retention practices and reference SOP-P1-L4-03 for record handling.
- Maintain way lube refill records that include equipment id, lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477, date/time of refill, quantity added, technician initials, and associated work order. Note the operating hour counter at time of refill where available.
- Tag replaced fasteners and retain failed components for analysis when requested. Record part numbers for replacements in the asset history.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must show no visible thread or head damage and must meet the assembly preload criterion when verified with a calibrated torque wrench. Any fastener that cannot be brought to the required preload without signs of material failure must be replaced.
- Way lubrication must be performed using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 and logged. The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours and refills must be documented accordingly.
- Maintenance actions are complete when torque verification logs and lubricant refill records are entered into the maintenance management system and a closure note is added to the work order. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for related procedural and safety requirements.
title: Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

# MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 Calibration checks - Machining heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
This document describes calibration verification checks required for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02). It covers the critical checks that influence quench timing, sensor response, and lubrication interface function for production runs. The intent is to provide clear procedural steps, background rationale, and recordkeeping expectations so that technicians performing maintenance can demonstrate the furnace meets operational readiness before release to process.

Background and rationale
EQ-P2-L3-HT02 has controls and actuators that directly affect the quenching sequence and the mechanical handling interfaces. Variability in quench initiation and in actuator response can lead to nonconforming metallurgy or increased mechanical wear. Calibration verification focuses on sensing elements, timing outputs, and the lubrication interface. The quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Compliance to this value is critical to maintain process repeatability. Use lubricant specified by the maintenance parts list for bearing locations and moving slides; the lubricant part number for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is CFW-LUB-373.

Tools
- Standard instrumentation used for signal verification and functional check of furnace controls as specified in SOP-P2-L3-05.  
- Calibration reference for timing verification and signal capture as required by SB-1023.  
- Approved lubricant container labeled with CFW-LUB-373.  
- Hand tools and protective equipment as required by plant safety protocols found in SB-1039.

Procedure
Preparation
- Verify work authorization and lockout/tagout in accordance with plant maintenance rules. Confirm SOP-P2-L3-05 for any safety-specific preparatory steps. Ensure the area around EQ-P2-L3-HT02 is clean and free of process material so instrumentation can be mounted and read without obstruction.

Functional baseline
- With controls in service mode, initiate the furnace through a controlled functional cycle that exercises the quench initiation pathway and the handling actuators. Capture the timing sequence with the timing capture device and with control panel status indicators. The focus is on the time between the final heat profile hold release signal and the quench valve actuation. Compare captured timing to the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds.

Sensor verification
- Visually inspect sensors for physical damage, secure mounting, and clean sensing surfaces. Verify electrical and signal connections are secure. For any sensor that exhibits intermittent or noisy output during the functional baseline, remove for bench testing and compare against the sensor manufacturer calibration guidelines referenced in SB-1023.

Timing verification
- Use the timing capture device to record multiple cycles through the quench initiation event. Record start and stop markers as defined in SOP-P2-L3-05. If the measured delay exceeds the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds on any recorded cycle, follow the corrective actions in the acceptance criteria section.

Actuator and lubrication check
- Inspect mechanical actuators for free movement, end play, and visible wear. Clean contact surfaces and apply lubricant CFW-LUB-373 to specified points. The use of any other lubricant is not permitted during calibration checks. After lubrication, cycle the actuator and verify motion is smooth and repeatable. Record any deviation from expected smooth movement and note whether additional mechanical repair is required.

Examples and step rationale
- Example observation: if timing capture shows consistent delay values close to the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds but not exceeding it, document the trend and schedule follow up inspection. Rationale: trending near limits indicates wear or drift that may progress into nonconformance.  
- Example observation: if a sensor shows a drifting output during hold-to-quench transition, replacing or recalibrating the sensor will reduce variability. Rationale: sensors with degraded response directly affect control timing and thus quench performance.

Records to keep
- Timing capture files annotated with cycle identifiers and operator initials.  
- Completed calibration checklist that includes sensor inspection notes, actuator condition, lubricant application confirmation showing CFW-LUB-373.  
- Any deviation reports and corrective action documentation linked to the furnace work order.  
- Reference to supporting documentation and criteria used during verification, namely SB-1023, SB-1039, and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Acceptance criteria
- Timing and functional: All recorded cycles must show quench initiation delay at or below the quench delay maximum for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 8 seconds. Any cycle exceeding this value requires immediate investigation, corrective action, and re-test before returning to production.  
- Sensor and signal quality: Sensors must provide stable and repeatable signals during the full hold-to-quench transition. Any sensor that fails bench comparison per SB-1023 must be replaced or recalibrated.  
- Mechanical and lubrication: Actuators and moving components must operate smoothly after application of CFW-LUB-373 and must not show binding, excessive play, or evidence of imminent failure. If mechanical defects are observed, document and escalate per SB-1039.

Disposition and follow up
If all acceptance criteria are met, complete the calibration checklist and attach timing capture files and lubricant confirmation to the equipment maintenance record. If any acceptance criterion is not met, implement corrective actions, document the root cause analysis, and repeat verification steps until acceptance is achieved. Reference SOP-P2-L3-05 for any procedure deviations and SB-1023 and SB-1039 for calibration and safety compliance requirements.
title: Calibration checks - Machining heat treat furnace #2

# MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
This document provides controlled maintenance instructions for lubrication and fluid handling on EQ-P1-L2-HT03. It covers selection, inventory, delivery, application, and recordkeeping necessary to maintain reliable operation of the heat treat quench and fluid management subsystems. It applies to maintenance personnel and technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 in plant P1, line P1-L2. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03 for related operating and safety procedures.

Tools
- Clean funnel and spill tray dedicated to EQ-P1-L2-HT03 fluid fills.  
- Labeled containers compatible with CFW-LUB-465.  
- Approved personal protective equipment as defined in SOP-P1-L2-02.  
- Electronic maintenance log terminal or paper log forms per SOP-P1-L2-01.  
- Visual inspection mirror and flashlight for inaccessible lubrication points.

Background and rationale
Proper lubrication and quench fluid control reduce wear, prevent unplanned downtime, and ensure consistent metallurgical results from the heat treat cycle. The quench timing is critical to metallurgical outcome; control of post-quench handling reduces distortion and surface defects. The lubricant specified for moving mechanical linkage and pump bearings is identified to ensure chemical compatibility with seals and quench fluid. Adherence to the documented maximum for quench delay is required to maintain process capability and repeatability.

Critical values
- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds.  
- The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-465.

Procedure
Pre-activity checks
- Verify machine is in maintenance mode and locked and tagged per SOP-P1-L2-02 before any fluid handling.  
- Confirm that required PPE is in place and that spill containment is prepared.  
- Pull the maintenance history for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 from the maintenance log. Cross-reference the last lubricant change and quench system inspection against SOP-P1-L2-01.

Lubricant handling and application
- Use only lubricant with part number CFW-LUB-465 for the specified bearing points and linear guides on EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Confirm label legibility before opening containers.  
- Clean the lubrication fitting area to remove contaminants and old residue using lint-free cloths.  
- Dispense lubricant using clean dispensers dedicated to CFW-LUB-465 to avoid cross-contamination. Apply until the fitted clearance is visibly saturated and excess is wiped away. Do not add any other additives or fluids.

Quench system fluid checks and control
- Inspect the quench fluid reservoir for clarity and free-floating contaminants. If visible contamination is present, follow SOP-P1-L2-03 for fluid replacement and filtration.  
- Confirm all valve positions and pump priming per SOP-P1-L2-03 before returning the furnace to operation. Ensure that quench delivery lines are free of kinks and that the spray nozzles are seated and oriented per original equipment layout.

Quench timing confirmation
- After maintenance, perform a dry run of the sequence up to the quench event to verify mechanical actuation and timing. When initiating the quench sequence, measure the interval between furnace temperature control signal and quench engagement and ensure it does not exceed the documented maximum. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. If measured delay exceeds this value, stop and investigate timing source, control logic, and actuation hardware. Document findings and remedial actions in the maintenance log.

Examples and failure modes
- Example: A sticky solenoid actuator allowed a delayed valve opening. Cleaning and lubrication of the actuator linkage with CFW-LUB-465 restored actuation speed and brought measured quench delay below the maximum.  
- Failure mode: Cross-contamination of lubricant with incompatible oil causes seal swelling and pump cavitation; to mitigate, use only CFW-LUB-465 containers and dedicated dispensing tools.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 including: technician name, tasks performed, lubricant part number used, observations of contamination, actions taken, and measured quench timing verification. Use forms and fields specified in SOP-P1-L2-01.  
- A copy of any fluid sample analyses or filter change records generated per SOP-P1-L2-03.  
- Any corrective action reports generated when quench delay exceeded the maximum, including root cause analysis and closure verification.

Acceptance criteria
- No leakage or drips present at lubrication points after completion of maintenance.  
- Only lubricant identified as CFW-LUB-465 was used; container lot identifiers and labels must be recorded in the maintenance log.  
- Quench timing validated at or below the maximum. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds; measured values must be at or below this threshold.  
- No unresolved contamination in quench reservoir; if contamination remains, SOP-P1-L2-03 procedures must be completed prior to return to service.  
- All records filed to the controlled file cabinet and electronic maintenance system as specified in SOP-P1-L2-01.

References
- SOP-P1-L2-01  
- SOP-P1-L2-02  
- SOP-P1-L2-03

Revision and approval
- Revision control and signatures are managed electronically per SOP-P1-L2-01.
title: Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3
