# MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

Scope
- This procedure covers fastener inspection, lubrication, and torque control for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02). It applies to bolted and threaded assemblies that affect structural integrity, safety interlocks, quench system, and process-critical components on EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- This document supplements MM-P2-L4-HT02 and operational guidance in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-04. When torque values or tightening sequences are required but not specified here, follow the referenced documents or the component manufacturer’s instructions.

Background and rationale
- Fastener condition and correct preload are essential to maintain alignment of heating elements, seals on the quench chamber, and reliable actuation of safety devices. Improper torque or degraded fasteners can produce misalignment, leaks, or electrical discontinuities that lead to process excursions or equipment damage.
- Lubrication of threaded interfaces reduces friction variability and improves repeatability of achieved preload. Use the approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-426. Using any other lubricant may change torque-to-preload relationships and void conformity with maintenance records.
- Quench timing impacts thermal shock and component stresses. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. Fastener-related failures that change thermal mass or distortion can influence quench performance; inspect fasteners where dimensional change would affect the quench path.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench and appropriate socket/bit set compatible with fastener heads on EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Verify calibration status per plant calibration program and the guidance in MM-P2-L4-HT02.
- Thread-cleaning tools (wire brush, thread chaser) for disassembly where corrosion or debris is present.
- Solvent and lint-free cloths for cleaning clamped surfaces prior to torque.
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-426.
- Inspection magnifier and dye-penetrant kit or equivalent for crack detection where visual inspection is inconclusive.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-04.

Procedure
Preparation
1. Lockout/tagout EQ-P2-L4-HT02 per SOP-P2-L4-01 before any fastener work. Confirm energy isolation and verify the furnace is at a safe state for mechanical work.
2. Review MM-P2-L4-HT02 for equipment-specific assemblies and any documented tightening sequences. If MM-P2-L4-HT02 references a manufacturer sequence, use that sequence.

Inspection
3. Visually inspect fastener heads and washers for corrosion, rounded corners, fretting, or evidence of loosening (gap, paint lines broken).
4. Where visible damage or cracking is suspected, perform a detailed inspection using magnifier and dye-penetrant. Record findings on the maintenance record.
5. For assemblies affecting quench chamber integrity or load-bearing connections, ensure no distortion of mating surfaces. Clean contact faces with solvent and ensure they are dry and free of debris.

Cleaning and preparation
6. If threads are contaminated, use a thread chaser or brush to remove debris. Do not rework damaged threads beyond cleaning; replace the fastener if integrity is compromised.
7. Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-426 to the male threads only where the design requires lubrication. Wipe excess from bearing surfaces; avoid contaminating seals and electrical contacts.

Tightening
8. Follow the tightening sequence documented in MM-P2-L4-HT02 or the manufacturer procedure. If a sequence is not specified in those documents, use a symmetrical approach working across the flange or assembly to distribute load evenly.
9. Use the calibrated torque wrench to apply torque. Do not apply impact tools where preload consistency is required.
10. For assemblies that require verification of preload after thermal cycles or commissioning, include follow-up checks per MM-P2-L4-HT02.

Examples and notes
- Example: For a multi-bolt flange, tighten in a star or cross pattern to bring all bolts to snug condition before final torque. The star pattern prevents uneven seating and minimizes flange distortion.
- Use CFW-LUB-426 on threads where the assembly documentation allows. Document lubricant application to maintain traceability.
- If any fastener must be replaced, record part identification and reason for replacement in the maintenance record and update MM-P2-L4-HT02 as applicable.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 including:
  - Technician(s) name and signature.
  - Reference to MM-P2-L4-HT02 and SOP-P2-L4-01 or SOP-P2-L4-04 as applicable.
  - Fastener locations inspected and status (OK, replaced, reworked).
  - Lubricant applied: CFW-LUB-426 where used.
  - Findings from dye-penetrant or magnifier inspections.
  - Any deviations from procedure and corrective actions taken.
- Calibration certificate reference for the torque wrench used.
- Replacement fastener part numbers and batch/traceability information if parts were changed.
- Any follow-up actions scheduled in the CMMS with reference to this document id.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners show no signs of structural damage, cracking, or excessive corrosion that would impair function.
- Fasteners on process-critical assemblies are seated and tightened per the sequence in MM-P2-L4-HT02 and verified using a calibrated torque wrench. Where lubrication was applied, the lubricant used is CFW-LUB-426 and recorded.
- Assemblies affecting the quench function do not introduce measurable gaps or distortions that could alter the quench path or timing; recall that the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. Any condition that could cause quench delay beyond this requirement must be corrected prior to return to service.
- All inspection and torque actions are recorded and traceable in the maintenance log and CMMS with references to MM-P2-L4-HT02, SOP-P2-L4-01, and SOP-P2-L4-04.

References
- MM-P2-L4-HT02
- SOP-P2-L4-01
- SOP-P2-L4-04
title: Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

text:
# MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This document defines calibration check activities and acceptance criteria for instrumentation and control elements associated with Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3. It is intended for maintenance technicians and process engineers performing pre-shift and in-service verification of measurement and timing functions that impact quench control and lubricant application interfaces. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for full equipment history and drawings and to SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03 for operational and safety procedures that bound these checks.

Background and rationale
Calibration checks confirm that control signals, sensors, and timing logic operate within acceptable behavior before parts are processed. The focus for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is on the quench timing chain and auxiliary sensors that influence quench initiation. A failure in timing or sensor drift can result in nonconforming heat treat outcomes; timely verification mitigates production risk and reduces rework. The quench delay parameter and lubrication interfaces are high priority because they directly affect part microstructure and machine reliability.

Tools
- Reference calibrator or signal source appropriate to the instrument type
- Portable multimeter rated for the control system voltages
- Clean, lint-free cloth and approved solvent per SOP-P1-L4-02
- Manufacturer diagnostic interface or programming cable as required
- Notebook or electronic maintenance record entry per plant practice
- Approved lubricant identified in system documentation

Procedure
Overview: Perform a sequence of visual, functional, and signal verification checks while the furnace is in a safe state as described in SOP-P1-L4-02 and with lockout/tagout applied per SOP-P1-L4-03. Record all observations and test values in the equipment maintenance record.

Preparation
- Confirm work authorization and that the furnace is in the safe condition required by SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Inspect wiring and connector housings for physical damage, loose connections, or contamination that could affect signals. Clean per approved procedure if contamination is present.
- Verify the lubricant supply and fittings for the lubrication system are present and free of leaks. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is CFW-LUB-231.

Calibration check steps
- Visual and mechanical inspection: Check sensor mounting and alignment for slippage or movement that may alter signal quality. Tighten or secure mounts if required.
- Sensor zero and span confirmation: Using the reference calibrator, inject known reference signals and observe the controller and readback. Confirm the readback follows the injected signal trend without erratic jumps.
- Timing and logic verification: Initiate the test routine in diagnostic mode and monitor the control sequence that leads to quench initiation. Use trace logging or the diagnostic interface to capture the sequence events and confirm predictable behavior.
- Quench delay verification: Observe the measured delay between the command to initiate quench and the actual actuation event in the control logs or diagnostic output. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. If the measured delay exceeds this parameter, follow corrective actions in MM-P1-L4-HT03 and coordinate with process engineering for disposition.
- Lubrication interface check: Confirm that any lubrication interlocks or sensors that affect heat treat cycles report correctly to the controller. Verify linkage continuity and signal integrity back to the input modules.

Examples and expected behavior
- Example diagnostic trace: When a simulated quench command appears in the diagnostic interface, the control logic should sequence through pre-actuation checks, open any required valves or actuators, and issue the actuation command. The event timestamps should show the actuation event within the quench delay maximum allowed. If an actuator shows repeated attempts without response, tag the actuator for repair and document findings.
- Example lubrication confirmation: When the lubrication system is exercised in manual mode, flow or presence sensors should change state and report to the controller. The controller should allow cycle progression only when sensor states meet required conditions.

Acceptance criteria
- Sensors return stable, repeatable readbacks that track injected reference signals within normal operational variance documented in MM-P1-L4-HT03.
- Control logic initiates quench actuation and other control outputs without anomalous intermediate states. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.
- Lubrication presence and interlock sensors report correctly and the lubrication system is free of leaks; lubricant in use is identified as CFW-LUB-231.
- Any deviation from the above criteria requires immediate tagging of the affected item out of service and notification to maintenance supervision and process engineering. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for escalation and repair workflows.

Records to keep
- Complete the equipment maintenance record entry with date, technician initials, diagnostic trace files, and any screenshots or exported log files. Link all entries to MM-P1-L4-HT03 records.
- Document any corrective actions taken, parts replaced, or field adjustments made. When lubrication reservoir or fittings are serviced, note the lubricant part number used: CFW-LUB-231.
- Retain a copy of the diagnostic output that demonstrates the quench timing measurement, and archive it in the maintenance system per plant document control practice.

Notes and references
- Follow all applicable lockout/tagout and safety protocols in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-03 before performing any checks that require access to live control cabinets or actuators.
- For repair parts, calibration procedures, or further diagnostic routines not contained in this check sheet, consult MM-P1-L4-HT03.

Revision history
- Rev D: Current release. See MM-P1-L4-HT03 for equipment history and prior revision detail.

# MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Related documents: SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04

Scope
- This manual covers lubrication and fluid handling for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) located on line P1-L3. It defines required lubricants, refill triggers, approved procedures for filling and verification, and recordkeeping expectations. Refer to SB-1014 for safety barriers and to SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-04 for lockout and local work area procedures during servicing.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubrication is critical to preserve spindle accuracy, guideway life, feed drive performance, and to prevent premature component wear. The guidelines in this document are engineered to align maintenance effort with machine duty cycles and to minimize downtime risk while maintaining machining precision. Service technicians are expected to follow the procedures to ensure consistent application, avoid contamination, and provide auditable maintenance records.

Critical values (do not alter)
- The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 60 hours.  
- The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is CFW-LUB-662.

Tools and materials
- Manufacturer approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-662. Use only the specified part.  
- Clean dispensing funnel with integrated breather.  
- Portable pump rated for approved lubricant compatibility.  
- Lint-free wipes and approved solvent for cleaning fill caps and ports.  
- Static-resistant gloves and eye protection as required by SB-1014.  
- Machine-specific fill cup or adapter as described in SOP-P1-L3-02.  
- Maintenance log form and replacement tag stock for indicating next service.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review machine status and production schedule to select a planned opportunity for servicing that minimizes impact on operations. Consult SOP-P1-L3-04 for required isolation and lockout steps before accessing lubrication ports. Ensure a clean work area and that no coolant splash or swarf is present around fill points.

Verification
- Confirm current lubricant type in machine documentation and visual inspection by verifying labeling at the fill reservoir. Do not introduce any lubricant other than CFW-LUB-662. If label mismatch or contamination is suspected, escalate per SOP-P1-L3-02.

Access and cleaning
- Isolate the machine following SOP-P1-L3-04. Remove the fill cap and clean the immediate area with lint-free wipes and approved solvent. Avoid introducing airborne dust into open ports. Hold the cap over a clean surface to prevent contamination.

Refill sequence
- Top up the way lube reservoir using the clean dispensing funnel and portable pump until the reservoir reaches the fill indicator as designed by the equipment manufacturer. If the reservoir design does not provide a visible indicator, follow the visual and tactile cues described in the equipment maintenance drawing. Ensure no overfill; excess oil should be removed and returned to a sealed container labeled for disposal or return to stores according to site waste handling procedures.

Post-fill checks
- Replace the fill cap and secure all fittings. Run the machine through a controlled lubrication cycle as recommended by the equipment control panel to distribute lube to guideways. Observe for drip, leak, or unusual sound during the cycle. If leakage is observed, secure machine, clean the area, and remediate per SOP-P1-L3-02 before returning to service.

Examples and contextual guidance
- Example scenario: During a production shift change, the operator notes reduced slide motion smoothness. Maintenance reviews the machine log, confirms that the scheduled lubrication point is approaching the refill marker, and performs the refill using CFW-LUB-662 following the steps above. After servicing, feel test and a brief lubrication cycle confirm restoration of smooth motion and the machine returns to production without further adjustment.

Contamination control and handling
- Never mix lubricants. If contamination is suspected, drain the suspect lubricant into an approved container and tag it. Notify the maintenance planner and follow the contamination response in SB-1014. Clean reservoirs and ancillary piping prior to introducing a new batch of CFW-LUB-662.

Records and traceability
- For each service event, complete the maintenance log form. Record technician name, equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03, lubricant part number used CFW-LUB-662, the service action performed, and the reason for service. If servicing performed as part of scheduled activity tied to the way lube refill interval, reference the interval in the log entry. Attach any deviation or defect notes and reference SB-1014 and SOP-P1-L3-02 where applicable. Maintain records in the equipment file for audit and trending.

Acceptance criteria
- After completion of the procedure, acceptance is achieved when:
  - The reservoir contains the approved lubricant CFW-LUB-662 and is free from visible contamination.  
  - Machine lubricant distribution cycle runs without leakage or abnormal noise.  
  - Maintenance log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 is completed with lubricant part number recorded and the action described.  
  - Any deviations have been recorded and corrective actions initiated in accordance with SB-1014 and SOP-P1-L3-02.

Notes on scheduling and monitoring
- Use the way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 60 hours as the planning datum for preventive service scheduling. For high-use circumstances or abnormal wear indicators, increase inspection frequency and document rationale in the maintenance log.

Disposition and waste
- Dispose of used wipes, contaminated lubricant, and empty lubricant containers per site environmental procedures and SB-1014. Label containers and maintain disposal receipts in the equipment maintenance folder.

Revision control and references
- This document is controlled as Revision Rev D. For safety and lockout procedures consult SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-04. Any requests for change to procedures or to the specified lubricant must be submitted through the controlled document change process and reference the related documents listed above.

# MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Scope
- Purpose: Provide standardized instructions for inspection, verification, and application of torque to structural and rotating machine fasteners on the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03). This procedure focuses on fasteners that affect safety, rigging, alignment, and load transfer on the mill, including roll housings, radial arms, gearbox housings, and guard and access panels.
- Applicability: Maintenance and reliability technicians, mill electricians, and the shift lead responsible for startup clearance prior to production. Use in conjunction with referenced system and safety procedures listed in Related documents.

Background and rationale
- Fastener integrity is critical for dimensional stability, operator safety, and preventing unplanned downtime. Loss of preload or improper torque can permit fretting, fatigue cracking, and component movement that propagates into the ring forming process. Inspection combined with controlled re-torquing restores clamp load and documents machine condition.
- The mill processes rings up to the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 1525 mm. Components and fastener choices are sized and selected to support these workpiece dimensions; maintain fastener integrity accordingly.
- Lubrication of bearing and gearbox interfaces is governed by the plant lubrication schedule. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is CFW-LUB-101. Use only the specified lubricant in gearbox and bearing fill operations; record part numbers used in maintenance records.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench suitable for industrial fasteners and traceable to calibration records.
- Torque multipliers and reaction bars for inaccessible or high-preload bolting locations.
- Dial or digital tension indicator for verification where specified by OEM or critical joints.
- Clean lint-free rags, solvent approved by plant material safety, and anti-seize compound specified by OEM or plant lubrication policy.
- Fastener identification tags and durable marker for marking inspected and torqued hardware.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for concealed head and thread inspection.
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P2-L2-01 and plant safety policies.

Procedure
- Pre-inspection actions:
  - Obtain machine isolation following lockout-tagout procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01. Confirm power and stored energy isolation before any work near rotating parts.
  - Review last maintenance history and fastener records. Consult SB-1049 for any safety bulletins affecting fastener assemblies or threadlocker usage on this equipment.
  - Verify tool calibration status and ensure torque wrench calibration traceability is available for attachment to the work order.

- Visual inspection:
  - Inspect each accessible fastener for thread exposure, head condition, corrosion, and evidence of movement such as paint witness marks that do not align. Use mirror or borescope for concealed heads.
  - Inspect mating surfaces for signs of bearing movement, fretting, or contact wear that could indicate preload loss.
  - For flange interfaces and guard mounts, verify gasket or spacer condition; replace if deformation or extrusion is present.

- Marking and documentation:
  - Mark each fastener head with a durable tag or marker to indicate inspection status and technician initials. Record fastener location, head type, and any observed anomalies on the maintenance record.
  - Note lubricant part number used on records when lubrication tasks are performed: CFW-LUB-101.

- Torque verification and application:
  - Where joint design and access allow, verify preload using calibrated tools. If preload verification indicates acceptable clamp load, note result on record and proceed to next fastener.
  - When re-torquing is required due to evidence of preload loss or per engineering direction, apply torque using calibrated equipment. Use reaction bars and multipliers to prevent tool drift and ensure safe application.
  - For critical rotating joints and structural connections, follow OEM recommendations for sequence and method of achieving final clamp load. If OEM guidance is not available, use progressive and symmetrical tightening to re-establish even joint compression.
  - After torque application, mark heads or tags to indicate final torque verification and sign the record.

- Special cases and safety considerations:
  - For studs welded into housings or pressed-in anchor studs, do not apply external torque that could induce shear; consult engineering and SB-1049 before any corrective action.
  - If a fastener shows thread damage, head rounding, or evidence of fatigue, remove and replace the fastener. Record replacement and reason on the maintenance log. Use OEM-specified replacement parts, and confirm compatibility with structural loads.
  - For joints with specified lubricant or thread treatment, apply thread compound per product data and SOP-P2-L2-05 before installation.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners inspected and documented as compliant have:
  - No visible thread damage or head deformation.
  - Witness marks or stamp indicators showing no relative movement after torque confirmation.
  - Maintenance record entries with location, technician initials, method used for verification, and lubricant part number when applicable: CFW-LUB-101.
- Fasteners requiring replacement or further engineering review are those with damaged threads, signs of fatigue cracking, or weld damage at stud bases; these items must be tagged out and escalated to maintenance engineering and recorded.
- All re-torqued joints shall show evidence of verification on the maintenance record and be signed by the performing technician and the shift lead prior to machine release for production.

Records to keep
- Complete maintenance record for the inspection event, including fastener locations, inspection findings, torque verification method, and signatures. Attach torque tool calibration certificate for traceability.
- Parts used record showing replacement fastener part numbers, and lubricant usage recorded with exact part number: CFW-LUB-101.
- Any deviation reports and engineering dispositions referencing SB-1049 where safety bulletins or deviations were applied.

Related documents
- SB-1049
- SOP-P2-L2-01
- SOP-P2-L2-05

Notes
- Follow site-specific safety and PPE requirements. Do not operate machine until sign-off is obtained on the maintenance record.
title: Fastener inspection and torque - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

# MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

Scope
- This document describes calibration check activities for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) used in the heat treatment cell on line P3-L4.
- Applies to routine calibration verification performed after maintenance, before production cycles, and whenever accuracy concerns are raised.
- The maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 1720 mm. Use this value when verifying travel limits, detector positioning, and setup envelopes.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 for related operational and safety procedures.

Background and intent
- The radial ring rolling mill is used to manipulate and position ring blanks for heat treatment. Calibration checks ensure that positional feedback, travel limits, and sensing systems match physical reality and the control system model.
- This procedure focuses on verification rather than full calibration. Full calibration actions that change sensor scaling or controller parameters must be performed and documented in accordance with the relevant SOPs and change control.
- The objective is to detect drift, sensor misalignment, and mechanical freeplay before these issues impact part quality or cause equipment damage.

Tools
- Portable position indicator or dimensional reference compatible with machine axes and capable of matching the maximum ring size envelope.
- Dial or electronic gauge suitable for measuring alignment references at interfaces.
- Reference ring fixture sized to envelope margins; must be compatible with the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01).
- Inspection mirror and light for access to sensor mounting points.
- Lubricant supply with part number CFW-LUB-315 for any lubrication verification steps. Do not substitute part numbers.
- Calibration log form and defect report template per document control.

Procedure
- Preparatory checks
  - Confirm machine is in a safe, de-energized access state following SOP-P3-L4-02. Lockout/tagout must be verified before accessing mechanical or sensing elements.
  - Review the last recorded calibration check entries and any outstanding defects. Identify any recurring items and note them on the calibration log.

- Mechanical envelope verification
  - Install the reference ring fixture sized to the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) to validate clearance and travel limits.
  - Move machine axes slowly by manual jog function to approach the envelope boundaries. Observe for interference, unexpected contact, or abnormal noises. Use the portable position indicator to verify actual travel endpoints correspond to controller readouts.
  - Rationale: Physical interference can cause latent offset in sensing and damage to parts. Verifying with a reference ring ensures the machine will not overtravel parts beyond the intended envelope.

- Sensor and limit switch inspection
  - Visually inspect sensor mounts for looseness, abrasion, or misalignment. Use the inspection mirror and light for hard-to-see areas.
  - Apply the electronic or dial gauge at sensor reference points and compare to controller feedback. If the sensor output deviates from the physical reading, document the delta and tag for follow-up calibration or repair.
  - Rationale: Sensors can shift due to vibration or mechanical impact. Early detection prevents drift in control loops.

- Alignment and squareness checks
  - Using the dial or electronic gauge, check alignment of key bearing housings and guide surfaces against the machine datum. Record readings on the calibration log.
  - If misalignment is detected, record severity and suspected cause. Minor adjustments may be permitted in accordance with mechanical maintenance protocols; major interventions require coordination with engineering.
  - Rationale: Proper alignment preserves tool life and maintains predictable kinematics for ring handling.

- Verification of lubrication points
  - Inspect lubrication distribution at grease fittings and contact surfaces. Confirm lubricant stock and that lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 is in use where required.
  - Note any dry bearings or contamination and schedule corrective lubrication actions per maintenance rules.
  - Rationale: Correct lubricant specification and application prevent premature wear and sensor errors caused by mechanical looseness.

- Control system feedback check
  - With the machine powered in a controlled mode, command slow, incremental movements and compare controller-reported positions to the portable position indicator.
  - Document any discrepancies and the axis or sensor involved. If the discrepancy exceeds acceptable limits, escalate to calibration adjustment per SOP-P3-L4-03.
  - Rationale: Ensures that control system readings reflect true machine position and that operator setpoints will result in expected part motion.

Examples and expected observations
- Example: If the controller reports a travel limit at a position that physically contacts the reference ring fixture before the indicator reaches the expected value, this indicates sensor scaling or offset error. Document the discrepancy and annotate the calibration log.
- Example: If lens housings or proximity switches show a shift from their documented mounting positions, note the movement and the suspected origin such as mechanical impact or inadequate clamp torque. Follow SOP-P3-L4-05 for repair authorization.

Acceptance criteria
- All mechanical travel limits must allow clearance for the reference ring sized at the maximum ring outer diameter for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) without unintended contact.
- Sensor position feedback must match physical measurements within the tolerances defined in the active calibration standard. Any exception must be entered into the calibration log and escalated.
- Lubrication points must be serviced with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-315 where specified. Any deviation from this part number is not acceptable.
- Any corrective actions that alter sensor scaling or mechanical datum must be recorded and tracked via the change control process and referenced in the calibration log.

Records to keep
- The calibration log must capture date, technician name, items inspected, measurement results, discrepancies observed, corrective actions taken, and references to SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05 as applicable.
- Defect reports for items outside acceptance criteria must be filed and routed per maintenance workflow. Attach photographic evidence where practical.
- Retain all records in the document control system and reference them during subsequent calibration checks.

Notes and escalation
- If uncertainty exists about the acceptability of any measurement or finding, consult engineering and reference SOP-P3-L4-03 before making adjustments that affect production parameters.
- Do not proceed with production use of the machine until all critical discrepancies affecting safety or part integrity are resolved and documented.
title: Calibration checks - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

## Scope
This document defines lubrication and fluid handling for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01). It covers lubricant selection, lubrication points, fluid storage and transfer precautions, and inspection acceptance criteria relevant to normal production and maintenance activities. This procedure applies to operations where the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm. Related references: ECN-2026-009, SB-1020, SOP-P1-L2-01.

## Background and rationale
Proper lubrication and fluid control on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 reduce wear, prevent seizure, and maintain dimensional stability of rolled rings. The specified lubricant minimizes metal-to-metal contact at sliding interfaces and is compatible with the machine's seals and bearings. Using the correct lubricant part number ensures supply chain traceability and material safety data sheet (MSDS) compliance: CFW-LUB-961.

This mill is used for rings up to the stated maximum outer diameter; larger rings require alternative equipment or process approval per ECN-2026-009. The goals of this document are to standardize lubrication practice, document inspection points, and define acceptance criteria for service records and fluid condition.

## Tools and materials
- Manufacturer-approved dispensing system with appropriate filtering and contamination control
- Clean containers labeled per SB-1020
- Funnel with anti-contamination screen
- Lint-free wipes and particle-free applicators
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P1-L2-01 and the lubricant MSDS: CFW-LUB-961
- Sample bottles for fluid condition sampling, labeled and sealed
- Inspection mirror and borescope for visual access to bearings and housings
- Permanent logbook or electronic maintenance record system conforming to SB-1020

Do not substitute CFW-LUB-961 without written authorization captured in ECN-2026-009.

## Procedure
Overview: The procedure is divided into preparatory controls, lubricant application, condition monitoring, and records. Follow SOP-P1-L2-01 for lockout and safety steps before any disassembly.

Preparatory controls
- Verify work area is clean and free of swarf and coolant carryover. Use lint-free wipes to remove visible debris from lubrication points.
- Ensure lubricant stock is verified against part number CFW-LUB-961 and MSDS is available at the point of use.
- Confirm the current production profile is within the machine rating; recall that the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm and do not attempt rings larger than this rating.

Lubricant application
- Use the approved dispensing system to deliver CFW-LUB-961 to bearings, slides, and gear interfaces. Avoid introducing particulate contamination by using the filtering capability of the dispenser.
- Apply lubricant to exposed sliding surfaces with a clean applicator. For internal bearings or gearboxes, use the fill or lubrication port designed by the equipment manufacturer; wipe the port clean before opening.
- For greasing of external fittings, apply lubricant until a light purge at the bearing seal is observed or until the applied film is continuous across the sliding surface. Wipe excess lubricant to prevent entrapment of debris.

Condition monitoring and sampling
- Visually inspect lubricant-exposed surfaces for film continuity, leakage paths, and signs of overheating or discoloration indicative of contamination.
- Collect fluid samples in labeled sample bottles after agitation of the reservoir per good-sampling practice. Seal and tag samples for laboratory analysis if there is visual indication of contamination or following a major event. Coordinate laboratory submission with SB-1020.
- Record observed anomalies in the maintenance log and escalate per SOP-P1-L2-01 if contamination, abnormal leakage, or evidence of lubricant incompatibility is found.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If gear mesh shows light scoring but lubricant appears clean, perform a containment cleaning and resume service while increasing inspection frequency. If scoring progresses, prepare an engineering change request per ECN-2026-009.
- Example: If a batch of CFW-LUB-961 is suspected contaminated, quarantine the lot, tag containers, and reference SB-1020 for disposal and replacement actions.

Rationale for steps
- Cleaning prior to application prevents entrapment of abrasive particles that accelerate wear.
- Using the correct part number CFW-LUB-961 prevents seal degradation from incompatible chemistries.
- Sampling and record retention enable trend analysis and root cause identification for rolling quality issues.

## Records to keep
- Maintenance log entries capturing date, technician name, equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01, lubricant part used CFW-LUB-961, observed condition, and action taken. Use the format specified in SB-1020.
- Fluid sample labels and laboratory reports when samples are submitted. Reference ECN-2026-009 if sample results prompt an engineering action.
- Receipt and quarantine records for lubricant lots when nonconformance is suspected, retained per SB-1020.

## Acceptance criteria
The lubrication and fluids condition for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 are acceptable when:
- Lubricant in service matches part number CFW-LUB-961 and is within supplier specifications as documented in receiving records.
- Visual inspection shows a continuous protective film at lubrication points with no evidence of abrasive contamination or rapid film breakdown.
- No leakage paths exist that contaminate the rolling surface or interfere with ring handling, and no residue is present that could transfer to parts within the machine envelope.
- Records are complete and include entries per SB-1020 and SOP-P1-L2-01, with any nonconforming findings escalated through ECN-2026-009.

If any acceptance criterion is not met, stop the affected operation and follow escalation and corrective action per SOP-P1-L2-01 and ECN-2026-009.

End of document.
title: Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

# MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 — Fastener inspection and torque - Machining shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Scope
- This maintenance manual covers inspection and torque verification for all accessible fasteners on Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01).  
- Activities in this document apply to mechanical and access fasteners that affect structural integrity, guarding, and component alignment.  
- Do not use this document for electrical terminations, pneumatic fittings, or for subsystems controlled by separate work instructions; see related documents SB-1010, SOP-P3-L3-04, and SOP-P3-L3-05 for interface requirements and permit processes.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on shot blast cabinets are exposed to vibration, abrasive media flow, and repeated access. Loose or overtorqued fasteners can cause misalignment, loss of containment, or premature wear of components.  
- Regular inspection and recorded torque verification reduce unplanned downtime and help detect progressive loosening or thread damage. Torque verification is a preventive measure to confirm that assembly clamping forces remain within acceptable condition for safe operation and correct alignments.  
- The cabinet interfaces with the building dust collection system. Note the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 1590 Pa. This value is a process alarm threshold and must be recorded during any maintenance that opens media containment to ensure correct resealing and system integrity.

Tools
- Adjustable torque wrench suitable for fastener sizes used on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Calibrate under the plant calibration program before use.  
- Hand tools as required for access panels and guards. Use non-marring tools where finish damage is a concern.  
- Inspection lamp and mirror for visual access to hidden fasteners.  
- Thread lubricant and anti-seize as specified in equipment BOM; the lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709. Apply only where threads show corrosion or where assembly documentation specifies lubrication for torque control.  
- Fastener identification tags and cable ties for temporary labeling of inspected items.  
- Records forms or electronic device for recording torque values, condition notes, and signatures.

Procedure
- Preparation and safety: Verify permissions and lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L3-04 and SOP-P3-L3-05. Confirm that media flow is stopped and that access is allowed. Consult SB-1010 for dust collection interface and confirm the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is not active before opening the cabinet. Wear required PPE for abrasive media and dust exposure.  
- Visual survey: Perform a walkthrough of the cabinet exterior and interior access points. Note any missing or damaged fasteners, signs of movement, or areas with abrasion. Mark locations requiring torque verification with temporary tags. This step documents baseline condition and identifies fasteners needing replacement rather than torque adjustment.  
- Fastener selection: Prioritize structural hold-downs, access panel retainers, hinge bolts, and guard fasteners. Where fasteners show corrosion or thread damage, replace rather than attempt to torque. Use fasteners and lubrication consistent with equipment parts lists and use CFW-LUB-709 only when lubrication is specified or when threads require treatment to achieve correct torque values.  
- Torque verification: Clean thread engagement surfaces and remove media deposits. Use the calibrated torque wrench to apply torque until the specified assembly feel is reached. If the assembly has no documented torque value in legacy records, confirm clamp condition visually and check for manufacturer torque data referenced in SB-1010 or equipment OEM files. Do not invent torque values; if values are not available, document condition and escalate to maintenance engineering. Record each torque verification entry on the maintenance record form with location, measured condition (tight, loose, or damaged), lubricant used if any, and operator initials.  
- Actions for nonconformance: If a fastener is loose, tighten to the documented value if available; if not available, replace the fastener and note the replacement on the record. If threads are damaged or stripped, install replacement hardware and update the parts list. If repeated loosening is observed at a location, add notes recommending lockwashers, threadlocker per engineering approval, or design review. For any activity that affects media containment, verify reseal before restarting operation and confirm dust collector alarm state as per SB-1010.  
- Post-maintenance verification: Close and secure all access panels. Perform a functional walk-around and, where practical, a short run-in verification per SOP-P3-L3-04 to confirm no abnormal vibration or noise. Verify that the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) remains within normal indication and that no alarm is present.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners are verified as serviceable, properly torqued, or replaced and documented.  
- Records include location, condition notes, lubricant usage (CFW-LUB-709 if applied), and technician identification.  
- No evidence of progressive loosening remains at inspected interfaces; where repeated issues were found, engineering recommendations are recorded.  
- Dust collection alarm status is confirmed as normal following maintenance; the specific alarm threshold to reference is 1590 Pa for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01).  
- Any unresolved fastener condition that could affect safety or containment is escalated and a stop-work hold is placed until corrective actions are approved.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry for maintenance log: location: access panel hinge, condition: light corrosion on threads, action: cleaned, CFW-LUB-709 applied, fastener torqued to documented value, technician: initials.  
- Example nonconformance entry: location: front guard lower bolt, condition: stripped thread, action: replaced fastener, note: recommend thread repair, technician: initials.  
- Required records: completed inspection checklist, torque verification sheet, replacement parts log, and any escalation paperwork. Retain all records per plant document retention policy and reference SB-1010 for storage location of dust collection interface records. Use SOP-P3-L3-05 for forms and sign-off workflow.

Related documents
- SB-1010

# MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 - Calibration checks - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Scope
This procedure defines the calibration check activity for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 control and monitoring instrumentation, focusing on dust collector differential monitoring, media feed detection, and lubrication confirmation for moving components. The objective is to verify that detection thresholds, alarms, and status indicators are functioning and that maintenance records capture the results required for traceability. This procedure is supplemental to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05 and assumes operators have reviewed those documents prior to performing this activity.

Tools
- Calibrated differential pressure gauge compatible with the dust collector tap.  
- Portable signal simulator for discrete and analog inputs.  
- Inspected inspection mirror and flashlight for visual checks.  
- Clean rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P3-L1-04.  
- Lubricant stock labeled CFW-LUB-278 and tools for application.  
- Equipment logbook or electronic maintenance record access per SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by site PPE standards referenced in SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
Background and rationale
Routine calibration checks confirm that sensors and alarms reflect actual process conditions. The dust collector differential monitoring is critical for maintaining capture efficiency; an incorrect reading may mask filter loading or bypass conditions. Verifying the media feed detection ensures shot delivery consistency. Confirming proper lubricant presence and application protects mechanical drive components and reduces wear that can lead to off-spec parts.

Preparatory actions
Verify lockout and tagout per SOP-P3-L1-02 before opening access panels or performing any work that exposes moving parts. Confirm that the equipment is in a safe state and that blast media is retained or isolated to prevent inadvertent release. Review previous calibration entries in the equipment log to identify recurring trends.

Calibration check sequence
- Visual inspection: With access panels secured per safety requirements, inspect housings, ductwork, and sensor mounts for damage, blockage, or loose wiring. Clean sightlines for the dust collector tap using approved solvent and rags if deposits are present. Note any physical anomalies in the logbook and attach photographs where helpful for future review.

- Dust collector differential verification: Connect the calibrated differential pressure gauge to the dust collector tap. Compare the gauge reading to the cabinet’s differential pressure transducer output using the portable signal simulator or the instrument display. Confirm that the system will trigger at the documented alarm threshold and that the alarm annunciation is functional. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Document the gauge reading and the corresponding transducer output in the maintenance record. If the transducer output does not correspond to the gauge reading within expected operational tolerance, flag for corrective action and reference SOP-P3-L1-04 for instrument repair workflow.

- Media feed detector check: Use the signal simulator to reproduce an absence and a presence condition at the detector input. Observe PLC ladder status and local indicator lamps for correct transition and interlock behavior. Record simulated input values and the cabinet response. If detector response is inconsistent, perform connector and wiring continuity checks and reference SOP-P3-L1-05 for sensor replacement parts and procurement.

- Lubrication confirmation: Verify that the moving components identified in the preventive maintenance plan are free-moving and that lubricant is present. Confirm that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is CFW-LUB-278 and that the batch label on the lubricant used matches site inventory records. Apply lubricants sparingly to specified points, working to a clean finish, and wipe any excess. Note any unusual friction or play and escalate for mechanical inspection if present.

- Alarm and HMI validation: Simulate alarm conditions where permitted and verify that the cabinet HMI and central monitoring receive and display correct alarm text and severity. Confirm that acknowledgement and reset function as per operator interface design in SOP-P3-L1-02. Log any discrepancies and attach HMI screenshots when available.

Examples and expected outcomes
A typical acceptable outcome for the differential verification will show the calibrated gauge reading aligned with the transducer output and alarm annunciation at the configured setpoint. An example record entry would include the gauge model, serial, reading taken at the tap, instrument display value, and signature of the technician. For lubricant confirmation, an example acceptable record will state the lubricant part number used, the visible condition of the lubrication points, and the batch or lot code from inventory.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration checklist with instrument identifiers and serial numbers.  
- Dust collector differential verification record including the calibrated gauge reading and transducer output, and explicit notation of the alarm threshold "2025 Pa".  
- Lubrication confirmation record citing lubricant part number "CFW-LUB-278" and batch code.  
- Photographs of suspect conditions and HMI screenshots for alarm tests.  
- Electronic entry or scanned logbook page uploaded to the equipment record in accordance with SOP-P3-L1-05.

Acceptance criteria
- Instrument readings are consistent between calibration gauge and equipment transducer, and recorded values are within the documented operating envelope. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is confirmed to actuate at 2025 Pa.  
- Media feed detector responds to simulated conditions and PLC/HMI reflect correct status and interlocks.  
- Lubrication points are serviced using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-278 and inventory batch is recorded. No evidence of abnormal wear or binding is observed that would require immediate mechanical repair.  
- All results are logged and signed, and any nonconformance is entered into the corrective action system with references to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04, and SOP-P3-L1-05.

When acceptance criteria are not met, initiate corrective action per SOP-P3-L1-04 and document interim protective measures. Close out actions are recorded per SOP-P3-L1-05 and require supervisor verification before returning the equipment to production.
title: Calibration checks - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

# MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Scope
- This maintenance manual section defines lubrication and permitted fluids for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01). It covers background, rationale for lubrication and fluid checks, coil inspection cadence, permissible lubricant part number, procedure for lubricant application and fluid handling, records to retain, and acceptance criteria for service completion.
- This document is to be used in conjunction with referenced procedures and safety bulletins: MM-P2-L2-IH01, SB-1024, SOP-P2-L2-01.

Background and rationale
- The induction billet heater coil and ancillary moving or sealing elements require controlled lubrication to maintain electrical and mechanical performance and to prevent premature wear, arcing, or contamination of the heated billet path.
- Lubrication choice is based on compatibility with electrical components and high-resistance prevention. The authorized lubricant for this unit is listed to ensure traceability and consistency across maintenance actions.
- Regular coil inspection reduces the risk of unexpected downtime by identifying insulation degradation, loose terminations, or conductive deposits that can lead to failure. The coil inspection interval for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 365 hours. This interval must be tracked in maintenance logs and aligned with production schedules using SOP-P2-L2-01.

Tools
- Personal protective equipment as required by SB-1024 and site PPE policy; consult SOP-P2-L2-01 for lockout/tagout and hot work controls.
- Insulation resistance meter suitable for induction equipment (consult MM-P2-L2-IH01 for model selection guidance).
- Non-conductive cleaning brushes and lint-free wipes.
- Approved solvent or cleaner consistent with electrical equipment cleaning; reference MM-P2-L2-IH01 for approved chemistries.
- Applicator suitable for controlled dispensing of lubricant to avoid over-application.
- Waste collection containers and absorbents in compliance with site environmental procedures.
- Maintenance log or electronic maintenance system entry form.

Approved fluids and parts
- Lubricant: CFW-LUB-938. Use only CFW-LUB-938 for the components specified in this document. The lubricant provides the required film properties while being compatible with adjacent insulation and sealing materials.
- For any fluid not explicitly listed in this document, obtain approval per MM-P2-L2-IH01 before use.

Procedure
- Prepare: Coordinate with operations per SOP-P2-L2-01 to schedule a maintenance window. Follow SB-1024 for all safety precautions, isolation, and energization controls. Verify lockout/tagout is in place and voltage is verified absent before accessing coil or electrical terminations.
- Inspect visual condition of coil assembly, support insulators, and termination points. Look for discoloration, cracking of insulation, loose connections, or conductive residues. If contaminants are present, clean using non-conductive cleaner per MM-P2-L2-IH01 and allow components to dry fully before further inspection.
- Test insulation resistance across the coil and to ground with the insulation resistance meter. Compare readings to acceptance criteria referenced in MM-P2-L2-IH01. If values are outside accepted ranges, escalate per MM-P2-L2-IH01.
- Lubricate mechanical sliding interfaces, bearings, and seals identified in the equipment maintenance diagram using CFW-LUB-938. Apply minimal quantity necessary to achieve a continuous film without excess drip or transfer to the heated billet path. Use an applicator to control deposit location. Avoid application on electrical terminations or on surfaces that contact the billet.
- After lubrication, rotate or actuate the component through its normal range to distribute the lubricant evenly. Observe for any leakage, unusual resistance to movement, or transfer of lubricant into areas where it may contact hot metal.
- Re-inspect coil area for any lubricant overspray or residues. If lubricant is found on electrical surfaces or within the coil window, clean immediately with approved non-conductive cleaner and re-verify insulation resistance.
- Restore equipment to service following SOP-P2-L2-01 energization and warm-up procedures. Monitor first production pieces for signs of oil transfer, smoke, or abnormal readings; if detected, de-energize and correct.
- Frequency and scheduling: Record the date and meter hours at completion. The coil inspection interval for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 365 hours; schedule the next inspection in the maintenance system accordingly.

Examples and step rationale
- Example scenario: If a technician finds light discoloration at a coil termination but insulation resistance remains within acceptable range per MM-P2-L2-IH01, the technician should perform a targeted cleaning and apply lubrication to nearby mechanical supports only, then re-check resistance before return to service. This approach avoids unnecessary part replacement while preserving electrical integrity.
- Rationale: Limiting lubricant type to CFW-LUB-938 prevents chemical incompatibilities that can degrade insulation varnish or create conductive films when exposed to high temperatures. Minimal application prevents migration into the heated billet path.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry including date, technician name, description of actions taken, readings from insulation resistance meter, part number of lubricant used (CFW-LUB-938), and meter hours at service completion.
- Attach or reference any photos taken during inspection and cleaning in the maintenance record.
- Record any deviations from this procedure and justification, with reference to MM-P2-L2-IH01 for approval steps.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil visual inspection reveals no open or cracked insulation that would expose conductive surfaces; any marginal conditions documented and approved per MM-P2-L2-IH01.
- Post-service insulation resistance readings meet the acceptance bands defined in MM-P2-L2-IH01. If not, remedial action is required before return to service.
- Lubricant used is documented as CFW-LUB-938 and applied such that no lubricant is present on electrical terminations or inside the coil window.
- No oil transfer or smoking observed during initial production after service. If any of these are observed, stop production and perform corrective action per MM-P2-L2-IH01 and SOP-P2-L2-01.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L2-IH01
- SB-1024
- SOP-P2-L2-01

# MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Scope
This procedure defines the required inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification for structural and pressure boundary fasteners on EQ-P1-L4-HP02. It applies to bolted connections on the press frame, platen assemblies, cylinder mounts, guide columns, and accessory attachments that participate in load transfer or sealing. The intent is to prevent loosening under dynamic load, ensure consistent clamp load, and protect threaded assemblies from corrosion and galling. Related documents: ECN-2026-047, SB-1012, SOP-P1-L4-03.

Background and rationale
Fastener integrity on a hydraulic forging press directly affects safety, dimensional accuracy of forgings, and hydraulic component life. Vibration, thermal cycling from process transfers, and lubricant degradation contribute to preload loss and thread damage. Periodic inspection and controlled re-torque restore clamp load and reveal damaged components early. The hydraulic oil change interval for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 2680 hours; coordinating fastener inspections with the oil change reduces downtime and ensures access during planned maintenance windows. Use of the specified lubricant minimizes compatibility issues; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195.

Tools
- Calibrated, traceable torque tool capable of documenting applied torque and capture of tool output in maintenance record. Verify calibration traceability per SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Torque angle measurement accessory if required by fastener type, per manufacturer instruction referenced in ECN-2026-047.
- Clean lint-free rags and solvent compatible with painted and plated surfaces as identified in SB-1012.
- Wire brush and thread chase for light thread cleaning; use only as required and avoid damage to preload surfaces.
- Lubricant CFW-LUB-195 and application equipment (brush or aerosol delivery specified by manufacturer).
- Personal protective equipment per plant requirements in SOP-P1-L4-03.

Procedure
Preparation
- Lock out and tag out energy sources per plant LOTO practices in SOP-P1-L4-03 and render the press mechanically safe for access to bolted connections.
- Identify target fasteners using the equipment assembly drawings and ECN-2026-047. Prioritize fasteners associated with load paths, sealing faces, and cylinder mounts.

Inspection
- Visually inspect each fastener and surrounding area for evidence of corrosion, fretting, paint loss, thread deformation, and witness marks indicating rotation. Document location and condition in the maintenance record.
- For fasteners showing evidence of damage or suspected loss of preload, perform a sleeve or nut removal and thread inspection. Use thread chase only to remove light contamination; replace fasteners that show thread flattening, galling, or significant corrosion.
- Where witness marks are present, compare to previous records to determine whether rotation occurred since the last inspection. Note any discrepancies.

Cleaning and preparation
- Clean bearing surfaces, washer faces, and mating threads with a solvent approved in SB-1012. Remove loose rust and debris. Do not use abrasives that will alter bearing face geometry or seating surfaces.
- Lightly apply lubricant CFW-LUB-195 to threads where manufacturer assembly practice or ECN-2026-047 specifies lubricated torque. Do not apply lubricant to preload bearing faces unless specified by the fastener manufacturer or change control.

Torque application and verification
- Establish the required torque or assembly method from the fastener specification retained with the press assembly drawings in ECN-2026-047. When a torque-plus-angle method is called out use the torque tool with angle capture as required.
- Seat fasteners uniformly where multiple fasteners share a flange or clamp. Apply torque in a cross or star pattern appropriate to the joint geometry until final assembly condition is reached for all fasteners in the joint.
- Use the calibrated torque tool to apply torque and record the tool output to the maintenance record. For critical connections, perform a second pass to verify torque values after the joint has relaxed and re-seated.
- If any fastener fails to achieve the specified torque due to thread stripping or failure of the substrate, do not reuse the fastener. Document the failure and obtain replacement parts and disposition per ECN-2026-047.

Examples and decision logic
- Example: For a collapsed nut or rounded hex head discovered during inspection, remove the fastener and record the failure mode. Replace with new hardware and torque per the specification in ECN-2026-047. Retain removed hardware with the maintenance record until disposition is completed.
- Example: If preload loss is inferred from witness mark displacement but fastener and threads are otherwise acceptable, re-torque to specified assembly values and re-mark with witness paint at the final torque state. Enter the action and justification into the maintenance log.

Records to keep
- Complete an inspection log for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 that includes fastener location identifiers, condition notes, actions taken, lubricant applied (CFW-LUB-195), and torque tool outputs. Attach supporting photos for any degraded or failed hardware.
- Retain calibration certificates for torque tools used, consistent with SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Record linkage to the hydraulic oil change cycle; note that the hydraulic oil change interval for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 2680 hours as a point of coordination for scheduling.
- File all records in the document control system and reference ECN-2026-047 for parts and replaced hardware disposition.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must meet one of the following conditions: acceptable as-is with no intervention required and documented; acceptable after cleaning and re-torque per referenced specification; or replaced and documented with root cause for replacement.
- Torque verification records must show applied torque values consistent with the fastener specification in ECN-2026-047 and must be supported by calibrated tool output records in the maintenance file.
- Lubricant application must be documented as CFW-LUB-195 where lubrication is specified.
- Any instance of stripped threads, failed fastener, or substrate failure must be documented and reported following ECN-2026-047 and SB-1012 for corrective action and part disposition.

References
- ECN-2026-047
- SB-1012
- SOP-P1-L4-03
title: Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

# MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 - Calibration checks - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Scope
This maintenance manual covers calibration checks and associated verification activities for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03). The document provides background, required tools, stepwise procedure, acceptance criteria, examples of common findings, and recordkeeping requirements. This is intended for certified maintenance technicians and shift engineers performing routine calibration checks and coil inspections. For full preventive maintenance schedules and detailed component replacement procedures, see MM-P1-L1-IH03. Operational startup and shutdown procedures are covered in SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and rationale
Calibration checks on induction billet heaters ensure consistent heating performance, safe operation, and predictable billet quality. The coil assembly, sensing elements, and control feedback loops are susceptible to drift and mechanical wear from thermal cycling and vibration. Regular verification detects changes before they affect forging quality or cause unplanned downtime. To reduce risk, this document emphasizes verifying sensor linearity, coil condition, and control loop response. The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Adhering to this interval aligns coil condition monitoring with heating duty cycles and minimizes the chance of insulation failure or shorting.

Tools
- Appropriate multimeter and insulation resistance tester rated for the equipment voltage class.
- Portable oscilloscope or control-loop analyzer for verifying waveform shape and timing.
- Contact thermometer or non-contact temperature verification device for spot checks of sensor outputs against expected values.
- Hand tools and insulated handling tools as required by site safety policy.
- Approved lubricant for moving linkages and bearings: CFW-LUB-188.
- Personal protective equipment as required by plant standards.

Procedure
Pre-checks and safety
- Coordinate with operations to establish a safe work window and lockout-tagout condition in accordance with plant safety policies. Verify power is removed and controls are in a verified zero-energy state before accessing the coil or sensing assemblies.
- Confirm necessary documentation is available at the worksite including MM-P1-L1-IH03 and the applicable operating procedures SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05. Review previous calibration records for trends.

Visual and mechanical inspection
- Perform a thorough visual inspection of the coil assembly and surrounding insulation. Look for signs of charring, discoloration, abraded insulation, loose terminations, or evidence of coolant leakage where applicable. Check mechanical fasteners for securement and for signs of galling or fretting.
- Where moving parts are present, apply the approved lubricant CFW-LUB-188 to sliding interfaces per manufacturer guidance. Note: only the specified lubricant part number shall be used to preserve compatibility with insulation and seal materials.

Electrical and sensor verification
- Verify insulation resistance of coil windings to ground per site electrical acceptance guidance. Document readings in the maintenance record and compare to previous entries to detect progressive degradation.
- Using a multimeter and control-loop analyzer, verify that sensor outputs correspond to reference checks. For thermocouples or RTD circuits, confirm continuity and stable resistance values under ambient conditions.
- Capture waveform characteristics with a portable oscilloscope to verify the drive waveform shape and timing relative to control commands. Look for abnormalities such as distorted waveforms or unexpected noise that could indicate power electronics issues.

Calibration checks and control loop response
- Simulate a known sensor stimulus and observe the control system response. Verify that setpoint to sensor reading mapping remains within acceptable tolerance as defined in the referenced documents. If drift is observed, adjust calibration per MM-P1-L1-IH03 calibration adjustment steps.
- Reverify loop stability after any adjustment. Ensure that the controller output responds smoothly and without oscillation when a gradual change in setpoint is commanded via operator interface as described in SOP-P1-L1-03.

Examples of common findings and recommended actions
- Insulation discoloration with elevated resistance to ground: recommend coil cleaning and re-insulation; schedule detailed coil maintenance per MM-P1-L1-IH03.
- Loose terminations with intermittent contacts: tighten or replace affected connectors and recheck measurements; log action and retest.
- Sensor drift exceeding documented tolerance: perform sensor replacement or calibration following MM-P1-L1-IH03 instructions and update calibration tag.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil mechanical integrity confirmed with no visible insulation breach or loose fasteners. Insulation resistance measurements consistent with historical baseline and within acceptable degradation bounds specified in MM-P1-L1-IH03.
- Sensor and control-loop verification show stable and repeatable responses. Waveform characteristics and control outputs free of abnormal distortion or excessive noise when compared to baseline capture maintained in system records.
- Lubricated interfaces show smooth mechanical operation after application of lubricant CFW-LUB-188 and require no immediate corrective maintenance.
- Any corrective actions taken are validated by a repeat set of verification checks and documented in the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration checklist with pre- and post-test readings attached to the work order and filed in the equipment history archive. Include oscilloscope captures and multimeter readings as attachments.
- A summary of coil condition assessed at the coil inspection interval: the coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Record the actual equipment run hours at time of inspection and note any interval deviations in the comment field.
- Lubrication log entries specifying the use of lubricant CFW-LUB-188 and the location serviced.
- References to executed procedures and any corrective work orders raised. Link to MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-03, and SOP-P1-L1-05 in the record entry.

Notes
Follow site quality procedures when updating calibration baselines. Any parameter change outside established acceptance criteria requires engineering approval and update of MM-P1-L1-IH03 documentation as applicable.
title: Calibration checks - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

# MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
- This document defines lubrication and fluid handling for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01). It covers selection, application, verification, and recordkeeping for lubricants and auxiliary fluids used during machining operations in the P2-L3 line. Refer to MM-P2-L3-RR01 for comprehensive equipment maintenance tasks and to SOP-P2-L3-05 for safe work practices during fluid handling. Service bulletin SB-1036 contains vendor-supplied compatibility notes that must be reviewed prior to fluid changeovers.
- The maximum ring outer diameter for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 1310 mm.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubricant selection and management preserve component life, ensure process stability, and reduce contamination risk to downstream operations. The lubricant specified for this machine balances film strength and wash-off resistance appropriate to the machining operations performed on the P2-L3 line. Using the correct lubricant reduces spindle and bearing wear, supports consistent surface finish, and mitigates corrosion risk during intermediate storage.
- Lubricant inventory and traceability are critical to satisfy manufacturing quality requirements and to support root cause analysis in the event of process excursions. The lubricant part number for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is CFW-LUB-225. Only the specified lubricant shall be used unless written authorization is issued by maintenance engineering and documented with reference to SB-1036.

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-225. Use stock from labeled containers only. Reject containers with damaged seals or illegible labels.
- Personal protective equipment as defined in SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Clean transfer pump and dedicated dispensing nozzle marked for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 use.
- Clean, lint-free rags and capped waste bins for used materials.
- Secondary containment trays for fluid decanting operations.
- Portable collection vessels that are clean and dedicated to machining fluids to avoid cross-contamination.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 before starting. Confirm maintenance authorization and work order documentation is available.
  - Inspect CFW-LUB-225 containers for label integrity and expiry indicators. Verify the container seal is intact prior to opening.
  - Prepare secondary containment and position portable waste vessels. Don PPE per SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Drain and disposal
  - Isolate fluid circuits using approved lockout procedures. Capture used fluid in clean, labeled collection vessels. Prevent mixing of used fluids from different sources.
  - Transfer used fluid to waste storage in accordance with SB-1036 and plant environmental procedures. Record the batch or container identifier for traceability.
- Cleaning and inspection
  - Wipe accessible reservoirs and surfaces with lint-free rags to remove deposits. Inspect reservoirs and mating surfaces for signs of contamination, corrosion, or foreign material. Document findings on the work order and photograph any anomalies for inclusion in the maintenance record.
- Refill and fill verification
  - Use the dedicated transfer pump and nozzle to dispense CFW-LUB-225 into reservoirs. Avoid spills and overfilling by dispensing incrementally and checking fluid level visually as specified in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
  - After fill, run the machine through no-load cycles to circulate the fluid. Observe for leaks, foam, or unusual odors. If abnormal conditions appear, stop the machine and consult maintenance engineering and SB-1036 for corrective guidance.
- Post-maintenance actions
  - Reconcile used and new fluid quantities on the work order. Label replenished reservoirs with date and lubricant part number CFW-LUB-225.
  - Return tools and contaminated materials to designated bins. Complete all fields in the maintenance record, noting any deviations from procedure and corrective actions taken.
  - Notify process engineering if the work affected production parameters or if further sampling is recommended.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If a bulk transfer container has a compromised seal, do not use the material. Isolate the container, tag it with its container identifier, and notify stores and maintenance engineering for quarantine and testing per SB-1036.
- Example: If fluid exhibits visual degradation after circulation, collect a sample and initiate fluid analysis per plant sampling protocol. Retain the sample with the work order and reference MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SB-1036 for further disposition.

Acceptance criteria
- Fluid identification and quantity
  - Reservoirs and circulating systems must contain only CFW-LUB-225 where applicable. Work order and inventory records must show container identifiers and quantities used.
- Cleanliness and absence of contamination
  - Reservoirs and accessible wetted components shall be visibly free of sludge, metal flakes, or water pockets after cleaning steps. Any detected contamination shall be documented and addressed before returning equipment to service.
- Circulation and leak checks
  - After filling and circulation, no active leaks shall be present. If leakage persists, the machine remains out of service until repairs are completed and verified.
- Records and traceability
  - Completed maintenance work order must include:
    - Reference to this document id MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1.
    - Original lubricant container identifier and confirmation of CFW-LUB-225 usage.
    - Notes on any deviations and references to MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 as applicable.
    - Photographs of reservoir condition where anomalies were found.
  - Maintain records in the document control system and attach to the equipment history per MM-P2-L3-RR01.

Records to keep
- Work order with signatures, container identifiers, and quantity reconciliation.
- Photographs and inspection notes for reservoirs and components.
- Any fluid analysis reports and quarantine records stemming from SB-1036 procedures.
- Copies of any authorizations for alternative lubricants or deviations, including reference to MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-RR01
- SB-1036
- SOP-P2-L3-05
title: Lubrication and fluids - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1
