# MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Scope
- This document defines the required fastener inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification activities for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, during scheduled preventive maintenance and after component replacement or repair. It supplements general procedures in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and operational controls in SOP-P3-L4-01 and provides specific fastener handling guidance referenced in SB-1043.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 are subject to repeated thermal cycling and exposure to quench media. Proper inspection, cleaning, and lubrication prevent galling, maintain clamp load, and reduce risk of loosening that can lead to part damage or process variation. Lubricant selection and quench timing are critical contextual controls for this equipment. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. This constraint affects how fastener servicing interfaces with furnace cycles and quench operations.
- Use of the specified lubricant maintains repeatable friction conditions at the mating surfaces of non-sealed fasteners and ensures more consistent applied torque translates to target clamp load. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-407.

Tools
- Hand torque tool calibrated per facility calibration program; follow calibration records and acceptance per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Clean, lint‑free rags and approved cleaning solvent per SOP-P3-L4-01.
- Soft nylon brush for thread cleaning to preserve plating.
- Inspection mirror and bright task light for visual assessment of flank contact and seat surfaces.
- Fastener boards or trays to control orientation and prevent loss of hardware.
- Personal protective equipment as required in SOP-P3-L4-01.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SB-1043 for any component-specific fastener requirements before starting work.
  - Coordinate with operations to confirm furnace is in a maintenance state and that quench operations will not begin while fasteners are being handled, respecting the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02. Allow operations to acknowledge that quench initiation will be deferred to avoid quench‑related thermal shock during mechanical servicing.
  - Lay out tools and parts in designated clean area. Verify torque tool calibration status against the current calibration record.

- Fastener removal and inspection
  - Remove fasteners carefully, controlling orientation and storing hardware in trays to prevent contamination.
  - Visually inspect threads, bearing surface, and head for wear, corrosion, galling, strip, or any deformation that could affect clamping performance. Use inspection mirror and light for concealed surfaces.
  - Clean fasteners with approved solvent and nylon brush. Dry immediately and inspect again.
  - Reject any fastener exhibiting compromised thread form, significant corrosion, or damage. Refer to MM-P3-L4-HT02 for disposition and replacement guidance.

- Preparation prior to reassembly
  - Clean mating threads and bearing surfaces on equipment. Remove old lubricant, carbon, scale, and foreign material per SOP-P3-L4-01.
  - Apply lubricant CFW-LUB-407 to mating threads and to the underside of bolt heads or nut faces where required. Apply uniformly to the threaded portion that will be engaged, wiping away excess so that only a light, even film remains. Document lot or batch identification of lubricant used on the maintenance record.

- Torque application and verification
  - Assemble fasteners hand tight to ensure proper alignment and seating. Use the torque tool to apply torque in a controlled sequence that ensures even loading of the assembly; follow the sequence recommended in MM-P3-L4-HT02 for the specific component, or use a star or cross pattern where no specific sequence is provided.
  - Apply torque using the calibrated torque tool. Do not substitute a non-calibrated tool. If a documented clamp load target is required, refer to MM-P3-L4-HT02 for required values; otherwise follow the assembly guidance in MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SOP-P3-L4-01.
  - After initial torque application, allow a short settle period per maintenance practice then recheck torque to confirm retention. If torque values vary beyond acceptable repeatability as defined in MM-P3-L4-HT02, investigate for relaxation causes such as embedment, cross‑threading, or incorrect lubricant application.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners are accepted for service when:
  - Threads and bearing surfaces show no evidence of damage that would prevent proper clamp load transfer as defined by inspection criteria in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
  - Lubricant applied is CFW-LUB-407 and lot identification is recorded.
  - Torque application was performed with a calibrated tool and the post‑assembly verification shows retention within the repeatability limits defined in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
  - Operating controls respecting the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 were confirmed with operations prior to returning equipment to service.

Examples and clarifications
- Example: During inspection of a vacuum jacket cover, threads that show light surface corrosion that can be fully cleaned without loss of thread form may be reused after cleaning and lubricant application. Threads with crest damage or galling that reduces clearance require replacement per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
- Clarification: Application of CFW-LUB-407 is required only to the surfaces specified in component documentation and MM-P3-L4-HT02; do not apply to threadlocker surfaces unless explicitly directed in SB-1043 or MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry that includes equipment id EQ-P3-L4-HT02, description of work, name of technician, date, and time.
- Torque verification strip or printout from calibrated torque tool for the job, filed with maintenance records.
- Lubricant usage record including lubricant part number CFW-LUB-407 and lot identification.
- Disposition records for any replaced fasteners, referenced to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and SB-1043 where applicable.
- A note in the work order attesting that operations were notified and that the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 was observed during the task.

References
- MM-P3-L4-HT02
- SB-1043
- SOP-P3-L4-01

End of document.

# MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 Calibration checks - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
- This procedure defines calibration checks and verification activities required on Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). It covers the functional checks that must be performed prior to production after maintenance, after control system changes, or when drift is suspected. The objective is to confirm that measurement, timing, and control elements that affect quench timing and atmosphere control are within acceptable performance prior to processing parts.
- This document applies to maintenance and quality personnel responsible for furnace readiness and calibration verification. Refer to related change notices and equipment manuals for installation and design assumptions: ECN-2026-017, MM-P3-L2-HT03, SB-1041.

Background and rationale
- Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) uses a controlled quench event that must occur within a verified timing window to achieve metallurgical targets. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. This limit is a control parameter for acceptable furnace-to-quench actuator response and is critical to maintain heat treat consistency.
- Calibration checks focus on sensors, timing relays, control logic, and associated actuators whose performance influences the quench timing and atmosphere control. Ensuring these instruments are within tolerance reduces variability in part hardness and microstructure.
- Where lubrication of actuators or mechanical linkages is required during calibration checks, use the approved lubricant identified for this equipment. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-159.

Tools
- Calibration test instrument capable of recording event timing and trigger response as required for furnace control verification. Instrument must be appropriate for the signal types present on EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
- Hand tools and mechanical access equipment as required to access sensors and actuators.
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-159.
- Calibration records and forms per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and SB-1041.
- Lockout/tagout and machine isolation devices per plant procedures referenced in ECN-2026-017.

Procedure
- Prepare: Verify that the furnace is in a safe status for test activities following lockout/tagout procedures. Confirm that the control system is in a diagnostic mode that allows simulated cycles without introducing production parts to process.
- Sensor verification: Inspect signal cables and connectors to ensure secure connections and no visible damage. Exercise each sensor by simulating the condition it detects and observe the control input. Record the observed response timing using the calibration test instrument. The purpose is to detect sensor delays or intermittent signals that could add latency to the quench event.
- Timing path trace: Trace the control path from sensor input through control logic to the quench actuator. Use the calibration test instrument to capture timestamps at key points: sensor out, controller output, and actuator actuation. The rationale is to isolate which element contributes most to total delay and to provide evidence when adjustments or repairs are needed.
- Actuator check and lubrication: Verify mechanical freedom of motion for the quench actuator and linkage. If friction or stiffness is observed, apply the approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-159 to the specified lubrication points. Operate the actuator through its cycle and measure response time to confirm improvement. Record before-and-after timing values to demonstrate effectiveness.
- Control logic verification: Place the control system into a test mode that permits single-step or simulated events. Command a simulated quench event and capture the elapsed time from command issuance to physical actuator response. Compare the measured elapsed time to the allowable maximum. The purpose is to verify that logic sequencing and communications do not introduce excess delay.
- Repeatability checks: Perform multiple simulated quench events to assess repeatability of response timing. The intent is to identify intermittent delays that could be masked by a single successful test.
- Post-test restoration: Return control system to normal operating mode, remove test instrumentation, and re-secure any access points opened for testing. Ensure lubrication points are properly cleaned and excess lubricant removed.

Acceptance criteria
- Timing performance: The measured total elapsed time from control command to physical quench actuation must be at or below the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03), which is 13 seconds. Any measurement that exceeds this value constitutes a fail and requires troubleshooting per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and ECN-2026-017.
- Sensor and actuator function: Sensors must produce a clean, repeatable signal that triggers control logic without intermittent dropout. Actuators must operate smoothly after any required lubrication with CFW-LUB-159 and must return to their rest positions reliably.
- Repeatability: Timing variability between simulated events should be consistent with historical performance documented in maintenance records; large unexplained variation requires corrective action and root cause analysis as described in ECN-2026-017.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example scenario: If the measured elapsed time exceeds 13 seconds, capture timestamps at each node in the control path to localize the delay source. Typical findings may include slow sensor response due to contamination, delayed controller output due to queued logic, or mechanical binding in the actuator linkage. Use the recorded timestamps to determine the corrective action scope—electrical, software, or mechanical.
- Use this evidence to support any changes or part replacements and document per ECN-2026-017 and SB-1041. If lubrication reduced timing but timing remains above the limit, escalate to control specialist for logic and I/O verification.

Records to keep
- Completed calibration check form per MM-P3-L2-HT03. Include raw timestamp logs from the calibration test instrument and annotated traces showing the timing path.
- Lubrication log entries when CFW-LUB-159 is applied, including location and maintenance technician identification.
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action records if measured timing exceeds the acceptance criteria, with reference to ECN-2026-017 for change control.
- Retain records in the equipment maintenance file and submit copies to quality per SB-1041.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-017
- MM-P3-L2-HT03
- SB-1041

# MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

## Scope
This maintenance manual specifies lubrication and fluid handling for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It defines required consumables, inspection points, refill routing, and recordkeeping for normal production operations. This document applies to maintenance technicians and machine operators responsible for preventive lubrication and fluid control during line P3-L3 production runs. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-03, and SOP-P3-L3-05 for complementary safe work and lockout procedures.

Background: Proper lubrication of slideways, ball screws, bearings, and tooling interfaces is essential to maintain machining accuracy, minimize wear, and prevent unplanned downtime. This document captures the method and rationale for lubrication frequency and fluid identification for EQ-P3-L3-CN02.

The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours.  
The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is CFW-LUB-611.

## Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-611 (as above). Use only this part for all factory-specified lubrication points on EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
- Clean dispensing pump with filter sock and tagged spout (dedicated to CFW-LUB-611).
- Lint-free rags and lint-free gloves.
- Fluid-level inspection mirror and flashlight.
- Absorbent pads and drip tray for spill control.
- Records logbook or tablet entry configured per local CMMS referencing MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-03.

Rationale for materials: A dedicated pump and filtered dispensing minimizes particulate contamination that accelerates wear and leads to premature failure. Using the exact lubricant part CFW-LUB-611 ensures consistent viscosity and additive performance across bearings and slides.

## Procedure
Overview: The procedure below provides step-by-step actions for safe, consistent lubrication of EQ-P3-L3-CN02 during scheduled maintenance windows and as required by production observations. Follow lockout/tagout instructions in SOP-P3-L3-05 when access to guarded components is required.

Pre-task
- Confirm machine status and notify production. Obtain permission to access machine work envelope.
- Review recent maintenance log entries for EQ-P3-L3-CN02 to identify any recurring issues.
- Verify availability of CFW-LUB-611 and that dispensing equipment is clean and properly labeled.

Inspection and preparation
- Visually inspect lubricant reservoirs and sight glasses for contamination, water ingress, and level indication.
- Where applicable, wipe sight glass and cap area to clean before opening filler ports.
- Place drip tray under access panels and have absorbent pads ready.

Dispensing and refill
- Use the dedicated pump to add CFW-LUB-611 to the designated refill ports. Fill only to the indicated level on the machine sight glass or reservoir mark.
- After refill, cycle affected axes through their full travel at low speed to distribute lubricant into circulation paths. Observe for any leaks or abnormal noises.
- If any contamination or emulsion is observed during the refill, stop the procedure, contain the fluid, and escalate to maintenance supervision per SOP-P3-L3-03.

Examples and special cases
- If machining cadence is increased or heavy cutting is observed, document the event and consider additional visual checks between scheduled refills. Record the reason for the additional check in the logbook.
- If an operator reports excessive axis friction or stick-slip, perform the inspection steps and confirm that CFW-LUB-611 was used in the last refill entry.

Rationale for procedure choices: Sight-glass leveling and cycling axes after adding lubricant ensures trapped air is released and lubricant reaches bearing interfaces. Using a dedicated pump prevents cross-contamination from other fluid types that are not compatible with CFW-LUB-611.

Records and documentation
- Log each refill and inspection entry in the EQ-P3-L3-CN02 maintenance log. Required entry fields: equipment id (EQ-P3-L3-CN02), technician name, lubricant part number (CFW-LUB-611), machine operating hours at time of refill, anomalies observed, and corrective actions taken.
- Attach any digital photos of contamination or abnormal wear to the CMMS work order and reference SOP-P3-L3-05 for corrective action steps.
- Retain spill reports and disposal records according to site environmental procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L3-01.

The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. This interval is based on typical machine duty cycles and OEM lubricant life characteristics; deviations must be documented and justified in the maintenance log.

## Acceptance criteria
Lubrication outcome for EQ-P3-L3-CN02 is acceptable when all of the following are met:
- Reservoirs and sight glasses show correct level following refill and no visible contamination is present.
- Post-refill axis cycling shows smooth motion without abnormal vibration or noise.
- Maintenance log entries contain the required fields and explicitly list CFW-LUB-611 for the service event.
- No fluid leaks are observed in the immediate area and no evidence of cross-contamination is present.

Unacceptable conditions and corrective action
- Any sign of contamination, water intrusion, or incompatible fluid requires immediate containment, sampling, and replacement of contaminated fluid with CFW-LUB-611. Escalate per SOP-P3-L3-03.
- Missing or incomplete records trigger a follow-up audit and repeat of the refill procedure to confirm compliance.
- Repeated lubrication-related alarms or wear patterns should prompt a full lubrication system inspection and possible component replacement per SOP-P3-L3-05.

Notes on continuous improvement
- Track lubricant consumption and log trends against the scheduled 70 hours interval to identify potential leaks or increased consumption.
- Feedback from operators and technicians should be recorded and used to refine access, labeling, and dispenser maintenance to reduce contamination risk.

Related documents: SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-03, SOP-P3-L3-05

# MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Scope
This document defines the method, tools, acceptance criteria, and recordkeeping for inspection and torque verification of structural and rotating assembly fasteners on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01). It applies to all maintenance and reliability tasks that require removal, replacement, or torque verification of bolt, nut, and stud connections on this machine. The maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 1125 mm. Follow related procedure guidance in MM-P2-L1-RR01, use safety resources in SB-1013, and follow shop-level routines in SOP-P2-L1-02.

Background and rationale
Proper clamp force on fasteners is essential for maintaining alignment, preventing fretting damage, and avoiding accelerated wear on bearings and mating surfaces. Inspection identifies corrosion, tensile overload, and loss of preload. Torque verification confirms that clamping force is within the range required by the original equipment manufacturer and the engineering drawings referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01. Where joint condition has changed (galling, deformation, or lubrication change), replacement of hardware and reassembly according to the assembly procedure in MM-P2-L1-RR01 is required.

Tools and consumables
- Calibrated torque wrench suitable for the fastener sizes on EQ-P2-L1-RR01; calibration traceable per plant calibration practice and SB-1013 records.  
- Angle gauge or joint-stretch measurement tool if required by referenced procedures in MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Anti-seize, assembly lubricant, or thread lubricant as specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01; lubricant part number for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is CFW-LUB-724.  
- Socket and driver set compatible with fastener heads on EQ-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Torque audit log and inspection checklist form as specified in SOP-P2-L1-02.  
- Clean lint-free rags, solvent for degreasing, and corrosion inhibitor for reassembly as required by MM-P2-L1-RR01.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review the equipment history in MM-P2-L1-RR01 and any recent anomaly reports. Confirm the joint assembly method required for the specific subassembly being serviced. Consult SOP-P2-L1-02 for permits and lockout procedures. Use personal protective equipment per SB-1013 for hot work, pinch points, and lifting.

Initial inspection
- With the area de-energized and the assembly secured, perform a visual inspection of fasteners and mating surfaces. Look for head rounding, thread damage, corrosion, elongation, or evidence of hydrogen embrittlement. Inspect washers and locking devices for distortion or wear. Note any fastener that does not sit flush with its contact surface or that shows asymmetric loading marks.

Cleaning and assessment
- Clean threads and bearing surfaces with a compatible solvent and a lint-free cloth. Remove old lubricant and debris sufficiently to allow accurate torque application and measurement. If threads are damaged beyond assembly tolerance specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01, replace with new hardware per procurement and material control.

Assembly preparation
- Apply the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-724 to threads and bearing faces where the referenced procedure requires lubrication. Use only quantities and application methods defined in MM-P2-L1-RR01; excess or different products can change clamp force characteristics.

Torque verification and application
- Confirm the correct fastener grade and size as required by MM-P2-L1-RR01. Use the calibrated torque wrench and perform a test check outside the assembly to ensure calibration is functioning. For joints where MM-P2-L1-RR01 specifies a direct torque method, apply torque using a smooth, continuous stroke. Where an angle or stretch method is referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01, use the appropriate measurement tool and follow the sequence required by the engineering notes. For multi-bolt flanges or bearing caps, follow a progressive, opposing sequence to minimize distortion as described in MM-P2-L1-RR01.

Examples and special cases
- Example joint: a loaded bearing cap with matched pairs of bolts. Follow the sequence and method in MM-P2-L1-RR01, clean and relubricate with CFW-LUB-724 before reassembly, then verify clamp force using the method specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Example condition: if a fastener shows evidence of yielding or elongation, tag it and replace per MM-P2-L1-RR01. Do not attempt to reuse fasteners that fail visual or mechanical inspection.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners must be free of damage, threads must engage fully without cross-threading, and hardware must be the specified grade and condition per MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- After assembly or verification, all fasteners shall demonstrate clamping performance as required in the engineering documentation referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01. If nonconformance is detected, or if a fastener shows any sign of deformation or compromised integrity, the component shall be replaced and the joint reassembled following MM-P2-L1-RR01 guidance.  
- Lubrication at assembly must match the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-724 where the referenced procedure indicates a specific thread or seat lubricant.  
- For components that interact with rings, note that the maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 1125 mm; ensure clearances and guards are restored per MM-P2-L1-RR01 after maintenance.

Records and reporting
- Complete the torque audit log and inspection checklist specified in SOP-P2-L1-02 for every maintenance activity affecting fasteners. Record hardware disposition, lubricant used (record CFW-LUB-724 where applicable), inspection findings, corrective actions, and the identifier of the technician performing the work. Retain records with the maintenance job file and reference MM-P2-L1-RR01 for traceability.  
- If anomalies are found that meet reportable criteria in SB-1013, raise an incident report per SB-1013 and attach inspection documentation.

References
- MM-P2-L1-RR01  
- SB-1013  
- SOP-P2-L1-02

Revision history
- See document control notes in MM-P2-L1-RR01 for revision linkage and superseded procedures.

# MM-P3-L2-RR02-S3 Calibration checks - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2

Revision: Rev B
Plant: P3, line P3-L2
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-RR02

Scope
This document defines the calibration check procedure for measuring and verifying radial positioning and diameter control on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02). The procedure covers pre-check preparations, tools required, stepwise verification of measurement systems used to control ring diameter, acceptable tolerance verification, and recording requirements. This procedure complements operational and maintenance instructions contained in SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04, and SOP-P3-L2-05.

Background and rationale
Accurate radial positioning and outer diameter control are critical for product quality and mill longevity. Calibration checks reduce risk of producing out-of-spec forgings and support predictive maintenance by ensuring sensors, scales, and mechanical stops report true positions. The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm; verification of measurement systems must demonstrate accurate performance across the usable range, including near the maximum value. Lubrication can affect mechanical backlash and sensor repeatability; use of the specified lubricant supports consistent behavior. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930.

Tools
- Calibrated diameter master set suitable for ring rolling application and traceable to laboratory reference.
- Precision gap gauge set for contact checks.
- Portable linear encoder or laser displacement gauge with traceable calibration certificate.
- Surface condition inspection mirror and non-marring probe.
- Clean lint-free wipes and compatible cleaning solvent.
- Lubricant inventory label indicating CFW-LUB-930.
- Calibration log forms and digital capture device as specified in related SOPs SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review the three related SOPs SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05 for safety, lockout-tagout, and operational context before beginning.
- Verify calibration status and traceability of all measurement tools. Do not proceed if any tool lacks a valid calibration certificate.
- Inspect mechanical surfaces and contact faces for damage, contamination, or wear. Clean contact areas with lint-free wipes and approved solvent.
- Confirm lubricant inventory and apply only the lubricant identified by part number CFW-LUB-930 to moving contact points where required by maintenance practice. Record lubricant application event on the calibration log.

Mechanical alignment and zero check
- Position the mill in a safe, verified idle state per SOP-P3-L2-03. Engage mechanical locks as required.
- Using the precision gap gauge set, perform a contact check at known reference points to confirm that physical stops and reference faces are free of debris and seated properly. Record any deviation observed between physical stop and gauge reading.
- Mount the portable linear encoder or laser displacement gauge to the designated reference bracket. Align measurement axis with the radial movement direction and perform a zeroing operation in accordance with the gauge manufacturer procedure.

Diameter verification
- Select an appropriate diameter master from the calibrated set that represents a target within the mill’s usable range; include at least one measurement near the maximum ring outer diameter. When using a master at the maximum ring outer diameter, ensure the master dimension does not exceed the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm.
- Place the master on the roller path and bring the radial control into nominal contact following safe handling practices. Use non-marring probes to avoid surface damage.
- Record the instrument reading and compare to the master dimension. Note the absolute deviation, repeatability over three consecutive contacts, and any hysteresis observed when approaching from different directions.
- If deviations exceed the acceptance criteria in this document, follow corrective actions under “Acceptance criteria” before returning the mill to production.

Sensor and scale checks
- Inspect and verify encoder mounts and cable connections for secure attachment and absence of damage.
- Perform a dynamic check by moving the radial axis through the range of travel while observing the gauge output. Verify smooth output without jumps or noise indicative of electrical or mechanical faults.
- Check for consistent readings when returning to common reference points; log all results.

Lubrication influence check
- After initial measurements, apply the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930 to the specified contact points. Allow moving parts to settle, then repeat the diameter verification and sensor checks to observe any change in measurement behavior attributable to lubrication.
- Record before-and-after readings and comment on differences in repeatability, hysteresis, or offset.

Examples and rationale
- Example entry: master dimension 1415 mm used for verification at maximum perimeter. Instrument reading 1415 mm with repeatability within documented tolerance demonstrates acceptable performance at the design limit.
- Rationale: including a measurement near the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is necessary because mechanical deflections and sensor performance can vary near travel limits.

Records to keep
- Complete calibration log including: tool serials and calibration certificate references, measurement master IDs, raw instrument readings, computed deviations, lubricant application records referencing CFW-LUB-930, technician name and signatures, and references to the related SOPs SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05.
- Attach supporting photographs or data files exported from portable instruments. Retain records in the document control system per plant retention policy.

Acceptance criteria
- Measurements must demonstrate consistent repeatability and agreement with calibrated masters across the usable range, including at or near the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm.
- Sensor outputs must be smooth and free of intermittent errors during dynamic travel checks. Any persistent offset or erratic behavior requires repair or recalibration of the sensor or associated mechanical elements before returning equipment to service.
- Lubrication must be performed using the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930; deviations from this lubricant must be documented and approved through maintenance governance.
- Nonconforming results must be recorded and escalated according to SOP-P3-L2-04 for corrective action and SOP-P3-L2-05 for parts replacement authorization.

Revision and references
- This procedure must be reviewed in conjunction with SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05. All calibration activities shall be recorded in the plant document control system.
title: Calibration checks - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2

text:
# MM-P3-L1-HP01-S1 — Lubrication and fluids - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01

Scope
This document specifies lubrication and hydraulic fluid maintenance for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press EQ-P3-L1-HP01. It defines the required hydraulic oil change interval and the approved lubricant part number, outlines required tools, presents the maintenance procedure with rationale, and states acceptance criteria. This procedure supports safe, reliable operation and is supplemental to general maintenance practices in MM-P3-L1-HP01 and to operational wet checks in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.

Background and rationale
Hydraulic fluid condition directly affects system responsiveness, component wear, and contamination control. The specified oil change interval and approved lubricant are selected to balance component life, fluid cleanliness, and operational cost for the press duty profile. Adherence to this procedure keeps contamination levels within machine design limits and reduces the risk of unplanned stoppages and damage to valves, pumps, and cylinders. Records from planned changes inform trending for future optimization.

Specified values
- The hydraulic oil change interval for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 2425 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is CFW-LUB-927.

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-927 (use only this part number for top-up or full change).
- Clean, lint-free containers and funnels compatible with the lubricant.
- Particle contamination test kit and fluid sample bottles per MM-P3-L1-HP01.
- Portable vacuum transfer pump or manufacturer-approved drain and fill equipment.
- Clean rags, suitable drip trays, and containment to prevent plant floor contamination.
- Personal protective equipment appropriate for handling hydraulic oil and cleaning agents.
- Record forms or electronic entry prepared as per MM-P3-L1-HP01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Procedure
Prepare machine and area
- Place appropriate signage and isolate press from operation following lockout-tagout procedures referenced in MM-P3-L1-HP01. Ensure the area under the reservoir and all drip points is protected with drip trays and absorbent material. Purging or flushing activities must minimize airborne contamination; ensure ventilation as required by site practice.

Obtain fluid sample
- Before any fluid change, take a representative sample from the reservoir using the sample bottle and sampling method in MM-P3-L1-01. Label the sample with equipment id EQ-P3-L1-HP01 and current operating hours. Use the particle contamination test kit and record results. Retain the sample for the equipment maintenance record.

Drain and capture used fluid
- Place a clean container to capture drained fluid. Use the vacuum transfer pump or approved drain method to remove fluid from the reservoir until the reservoir level is below the sump where contamination accumulates. Capture all used fluid in sealed containers for proper disposal according to plant environmental procedures. Clean the reservoir interior with lint-free rags to remove varnish and sediment; collect and dispose of waste rags per plant policy.

Inspect and clean ancillary components
- With the reservoir open, inspect suction screens, return lines, and visible hose ends for debris. Replace or clean filters and strainers per MM-P3-L1-HP01. If particle contamination exceeds limits cited in MM-P3-L1-01, escalate for corrective action and note this in the maintenance record.

Refill with approved lubricant
- Using only CFW-LUB-927, refill to the reservoir fill level prescribed in manufacturer documentation and MM-P3-L1-HP01. Use a clean funnel and sealed lubricant containers to prevent contamination. When topping or filling, ensure the lubricant source is clean and within acceptable condition.

Bleed and operate
- After refill, purge any trapped air following manufacturer guidance and confirm hydraulic system returns to normal operating conditions per SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03. Monitor for unusual noise, temperature rise, or leaks during initial operation and log observations.

Sampling post-change
- After the system has run long enough for the fluid to circulate, take a post-change sample for particle analysis. Record results and place the sample with prior samples as required by MM-P3-L1-01.

Records and documentation
- Complete the maintenance record entry for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 in the equipment history log. Record the operating hours at change, the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927, particle counts before and after change, and any anomalies found. Attach the sample labels and contamination test results. File a copy per MM-P3-L1-01.

Procedure rationale and examples
- The pre-change sample establishes baseline contamination and helps determine if additional system flushing is required. The post-change sample verifies that contamination levels returned to acceptable ranges and that filters are performing. Using only the approved part number CFW-LUB-927 avoids fluid incompatibility that can cause varnish, seal swelling, or additive depletion. The capture and disposal steps prevent plant contamination and preserve environmental compliance.

Acceptance criteria
- Reservoir refill completed with lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927 documented in the maintenance record.
- Pre-change and post-change particle contamination results recorded and retained per MM-P3-L1-01.
- No visible contamination or residue remaining in the reservoir; suction screens and strainers clean to the extent accessible.
- System operates normally after restart with no abnormal noises, leaks, or functional degradation observed in the period immediately following the change; observations documented and cross-referenced with SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.
- The hydraulic oil change interval for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 2425 hours and is recorded in the equipment maintenance schedule.

Records to keep
- Completed maintenance record for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 including lubricant part number CFW-LUB-927 and oil change hour reading.
- Pre- and post-change fluid sample labels and contamination test results.
- Disposal manifests or waste documentation for removed fluid as required by plant environmental procedures.
- Any corrective actions taken if contamination or component issues were identified.

Related documents
- See MM-P3-L1-HP01 for system-level maintenance policies.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L1-02 for operational checks after fluid service.
- Refer to SOP-P3-L1-03 for start-up and validation procedures after maintenance.
title: Lubrication and fluids - Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1

# MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related: ECN-2026-026, MM-P3-L4-SB03, SB-1019

Scope
- This document establishes the approved process for inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification of fasteners on Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). 
- It covers structural fasteners, access panel fasteners, and selected machine-mounted hardware that affect containment, alignment, and operator safety. 
- For electrical enclosures and components, follow the applicable procedures referenced in ECN-2026-026 and MM-P3-L4-SB03.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on shot blast cabinets are exposed to abrasive media, dust loading, and vibration. Over time they can loosen, seize, or corrode, compromising containment and mechanical alignments. 
- Proper inspection and controlled torque application preserve cabinet integrity, reduce unplanned downtime, and maintain safe dust handling performance.
- The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. Maintaining fastener integrity helps ensure seals and access interfaces do not contribute to premature alarm condition.

Tools and consumables
- Torque wrench suitable for specified fastener torque ranges referenced in design documents and manufacturer data. Calibrate per plant calibration policy. 
- Non-marring pry tool for panel extraction. 
- Cleaning brushes and lint-free rags. 
- Penetrating lubricant and anti-seize materials compatible with substrate; use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 for general fastener lubrication on EQ-P3-L4-SB03. 
- Torque indicator tags and tamper-evident seals for post-torque marking. 
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1019 and site safety rules.

Procedure
- Pre-work verification
  - Confirm authorization to work on EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and review lockout/tagout requirements in SB-1019.
  - Notify operations and log the planned work in the maintenance schedule and equipment history records referenced in MM-P3-L4-SB03.

- Visual inspection and preparation
  - Visually inspect all exposed fasteners on cabinet panels, access doors, and mounting brackets. Look for signs of back-off, rounding, corrosion, material build-up, or evidence of previous rework.
  - Clean the fastener and surrounding seating surface of abrasive media and dust using brushes and lint-free cloths to ensure accurate torque.
  - Where threads are contaminated or corroded, apply an appropriate penetrating lubricant, then clean again to remove loosened debris. Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 for routine lubrication as it is approved for EQ-P3-L4-SB03.

- Fastener removal where required
  - If removal is necessary for inspection of seating surfaces or hardware condition, label each fastener and matcher point to maintain assembly orientation. Preserve thread engagement features and inspect washers, lock devices, and captive inserts.

- Torque verification and application
  - Refer to the fastener torque specification tables held in ECN-2026-026 and the equipment assembly records in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for the correct torque values for each fastener type. Do not apply a torque value unless it is confirmed in those documents or by the component manufacturer.
  - Use a calibrated torque wrench. Apply torque in a controlled pattern appropriate to the fastener grouping (for example, opposing sequence for panel bolts) to assure uniform seating. Mark each fastener with a torque indicator tag or tamper-evident seal after verification.
  - Document any deviation from specified torque values and the rationale in the maintenance record. If a fastener is found to be damaged or fails to hold torque, replace it and record the replacement per the parts control process.

- Post-assembly checks
  - Confirm panel gaps and seal compression conform to the cabinet assembly condition recorded in MM-P3-L4-SB03.
  - Perform a functional check of the dust collection interface and observe for immediate changes in pressure drop or alarm behavior. Log findings and any corrective actions taken.

Examples and judgement notes
- Example: if an access door fastener shows rounding of the head but the seating surface is intact, replace the fastener and, after replacement, confirm torque value from ECN-2026-026 before final tightening. Tag the new fastener and note the part used in the records.
- Example: where a captive stud exhibits surface corrosion confined to the outside diameter, clean and coat with CFW-LUB-526 then verify retained torque per the specification table. If threads are compromised, replace the stud assembly.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners show no evidence of progressive loosening at re-inspection and pass the torque verification to the values specified in ECN-2026-026 and MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Access panels and sealing interfaces exhibit consistent seating and no visible gaps affecting containment. Where applicable, no new dust ingress pathways are observed.
- Lubrication is applied using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 where specified and documented.
- Any replacement hardware is recorded with the part description and associated justification in the maintenance log.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order and completion report filed in the equipment history for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 per MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Torque verification checklist including torque wrench calibration reference, operator name, date, and fastener identifiers. Retain with the preventive maintenance record.
- Any deviation reports and corrective action records referenced to ECN-2026-026 when changes to hardware or torque values are proposed.
- Safety and LOTO confirmation form per SB-1019.

References
- ECN-2026-026
- MM-P3-L4-SB03
- SB-1019

Notes
- This procedure does not provide specific torque values. Use the authoritative specification documents cited above for numeric torque values and any changes to fastener selection or torque practice.
title: Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3

# MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 Calibration checks - Machining induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This document defines the calibration check procedure for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03). It is intended for qualified maintenance and process personnel performing periodic verification and return-to-service checks after corrective work.
- The coil inspection interval for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 390 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is CFW-LUB-725.
- This document supports compliance with preventive maintenance planning and process control; see related documents MM-P2-L3-IH03, QS-PROC-10, and SOP-P2-L3-01 for broader maintenance history, quality system requirements, and operational startup/shutdown steps respectively.

Tools
- Digital multimeter with AC/DC capability suitable for induction system verification.
- Clamp meter rated for induction heater current measurement.
- Insulation resistance tester (megger) appropriate for high-power winding checks.
- Hand tools for access panels and clamps; non-sparking set where required by line safety policy in SOP-P2-L3-01.
- Cleaning supplies and lint-free rags compatible with electrical components.
- Manufacturer-approved lubricant CFW-LUB-725 for bearing and mechanical lubrication tasks.
- Lockout/tagout hardware per plant policy referenced in QS-PROC-10.
- Calibration status tags and the inspection form template from MM-P2-L3-IH03.

Procedure
- Preparation and safety
  - Confirm authorization to work on EQ-P2-L3-IH03 per SOP-P2-L3-01. Coordinate with line control to hold process billets and establish a safe work window.
  - Apply lockout/tagout following QS-PROC-10 before opening access covers or disconnecting power. Verify absence of hazardous stored energy in capacitance banks and cooling lines.
  - Review the last coil inspection entry in MM-P2-L3-IH03 to note any recurring observations prior to starting checks.

- Visual inspection and mechanical checks
  - Inspect coil windings and busbar connections for signs of overheating, discoloration, deformation, or loose fasteners. Rationale: early visual detection reduces risk of progressive insulation degradation.
  - Inspect water-cooling connections and hose routing for leaks, kinks, or evidence of erosion near fittings. Rationale: proper cooling maintains thermal stability critical to repeatable heating results.
  - Check alignment and condition of billet guides and proximity sensors to ensure consistent billet positioning; correct minor misalignment per SOP-P2-L3-01 before electrical checks.
  - Apply manufacturer-approved lubricant CFW-LUB-725 only to designated bearing points; avoid contact with electrical insulation. Rationale: correct lubrication preserves mechanical movement without compromising electrical integrity.

- Electrical and calibration checks
  - Verify power input connections are torqued to the values specified in the OEM documentation located in MM-P2-L3-IH03 prior to energizing. Rationale: secure connections reduce resistive heating and measurement variability.
  - Measure winding insulation resistance with the insulation resistance tester. Compare to the baseline values recorded in MM-P2-L3-IH03; investigate if values deviate from historical trends. Rationale: insulation resistance trends predict impending winding failure.
  - With power applied under a controlled no-load condition as allowed by SOP-P2-L3-01, measure primary and secondary currents using the clamp meter and verify that readings match expected ratios in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Rationale: current balance and magnitude are primary calibration indicators for induction heating performance.
  - Check control system sensor calibrations per the interface specifications in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Calibrate temperature and flow sensors against calibrated reference equipment if drift is observed. Rationale: sensor accuracy directly affects process reproducibility.

- Functional verification
  - Perform a controlled heat cycle with a billet or calibrated test tag as described in SOP-P2-L3-01 and record outcome variables: heating time, sensor responses, and control setpoint adherence. Use the comparison method in MM-P2-L3-IH03 to assess performance against baseline behavior.
  - If anomalies are found, follow corrective work flow in QS-PROC-10 and update MM-P2-L3-IH03 records with actions taken, parts used, and observations.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible damage to coil windings or busbars; connectors secure and free of discoloration indicative of overheating. Refer to photographic examples in MM-P2-L3-IH03 for acceptable appearance.
- Cooling system intact with no active leaks; flow sensors and temperature sensors reporting within expected operational range as defined in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Insulation resistance values within acceptable trend band compared to prior entries in MM-P2-L3-IH03. If values fall outside the trend band, component replacement or repair is required before return to service.
- Electrical current and control responses consistent with baseline verification tests recorded in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Deviations must be investigated and documented under QS-PROC-10.
- Functional heat cycle produces repeatable billet temperature profile and control stability consistent with SOP-P2-L3-01 run parameters. Any failure to meet stability or repeatability requires root cause analysis and corrective action.

Background and rationale
- Induction heating relies on tight control of coil condition, electrical connections, and cooling to maintain repeatable thermal delivery. Regular inspection reduces unplanned downtime and part quality variation. The coil inspection interval of 390 hours balances wear progression and operational availability based on historical failure modes documented in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Lubrication with the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-725 protects mechanical components without degrading electrical insulation or contaminating billet paths.

Records to keep
- Complete the inspection checklist and attach measurement outputs to the equipment maintenance record in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Record any deviations, corrective actions, parts used, and approval signatures per QS-PROC-10.
- Retain functional verification logs and sensor calibration certificates as supporting evidence for process audits. Cross-reference entries to SOP-P2-L3-01 run sheets when calibrations are performed during operational windows.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-IH03
- QS-PROC-10
- SOP-P2-L3-01
title: Calibration checks - Machining induction billet heater #3

# SB-1001: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Hazard description
------------------

Operations around the Hot Forge induction billet heater present an elevated noise hazard generated by combined sources including induction coil excitation, hydraulics, billet handling, and forging press interaction. Prolonged exposure to the sound field in proximity to the heater and billet transfer path can result in hearing damage and impair communication critical to safe operation. Noise events are most pronounced during billet feed, dwell at temperature, and transfer into the press. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C, and operations conducted to achieve and maintain this temperature require sustained equipment excitation and material movement that contribute to the noise profile.

This bulletin addresses the exposure pathway from source to worker and clarifies administrative and engineering measures required to reduce personnel exposure and maintain situational awareness. The guidance applies where workers are routinely present in or pass through the area surrounding EQ-P2-L1-IH02 during normal operation, maintenance access, and changeover activities.

Affected equipment
------------------

Primary coverage is required for the following equipment and zones:

- Induction heater: EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Refer to MM-P2-L1-IH02 for mechanical maintenance history and component access points that influence noise generation.
- Billet handling path adjacent to the induction heater including loading chute, transfer robot, and alignment fixtures documented in SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Immediate operator stations, maintenance stands, and walkways that provide access to the heater and transfer path.

Required controls
-----------------

Control measures follow the established hierarchy of controls and are tailored to the operational context of EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Implementation must align with machine maintenance and operation procedures in MM-P2-L1-IH02, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-05.

Engineering controls
- Where feasible, apply source attenuation by fitting vibration isolation and dampening components at confirmed excitation points documented in MM-P2-L1-IH02. Adjustments to clamping and fixture contact surfaces should be made per MM-P2-L1-IH02 to minimize resonant amplification.
- Enclose or shield the immediate transfer path with acoustically absorptive barriers compatible with the thermal environment around the billet target temperature of 1180 °C. Barrier material selection must tolerate radiant heat and comply with existing fire and thermal resistance requirements.
- Optimize alignment and feed mechanics documented in SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-05 to reduce impact events during billet launch and receipt. Eliminate loose tolerances and worn interface components that contribute to impulsive noise.

Administrative controls
- Limit time spent in the highest exposure locations by rotating tasks and consolidating work to minimize cumulative exposure for any single worker. Task assignments should follow the risk assessment protocols in SOP-P2-L1-01.
- Conduct routine noise surveys after implementation of engineering controls and after any maintenance activity referenced in MM-P2-L1-IH02 that could alter the noise signature. Record survey results in the equipment noise log and attach findings to the MM folder.
- Provide pre-shift briefings that highlight expected loud events during heating and transfer sequences and remind workers of hearing protection requirements and communication methods.

Personal protective equipment
- Where engineering and administrative controls do not reduce exposure to a level that eliminates risk, provide hearing protection appropriate to the environment. Fit testing and training on correct wear and care shall be documented and retained in the employee health files.

Examples and operational rationale
----------------------------------

Example 1: During a billet feed cycle, small impact noise from a worn rail interface can produce sharp peaks that are disruptive and damaging. Replacing or resurfacing the contact point per MM-P2-L1-IH02 reduces impact magnitude and duration, thereby lowering risk without altering process throughput.

Example 2: An operator conducting alignment using handheld tools in the transfer zone is exposed to combined continuous and impulsive noise. Scheduling alignment tasks to occur during planned downtime, coordinating with the heater cycle, and using remote adjustment where possible decreases exposure and maintains production quality as described in SOP-P2-L1-05.

Records to keep
---------------

Maintain the following records in the document control system and equipment folder associated with EQ-P2-L1-IH02:
- Noise survey reports and trend charts following each survey event. Reference the associated maintenance activities in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Hearing protection issue logs and fit verification records for personnel routinely assigned to work zones described in SOP-P2-L1-01.
- Engineering change records for any barrier installation, damping retrofit, or alignment modification that affects the billet path or induction heater enclosures.
- Pre-shift briefing attendance logs and incident reports that reference noise as a contributing factor.

Training and communication
--------------------------

Train affected personnel on the hazards, control rationale, and procedures. Training content must reference operational steps in SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-05 and maintenance practices in MM-P2-L1-IH02. Include scenario-based drills that simulate high-noise events and require use of established communication protocols and hearing protection.

Effective date
--------------

Effective date: Upon release

References
----------

- MM-P2-L1-IH02
- SOP-P2-L1-01
- SOP-P2-L1-05

Action required
---------------

Site leadership must review and approve an implementation plan that prioritizes engineering controls, schedules required maintenance work referenced in MM-P2-L1-IH02, and updates local SOPs SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-05 to reflect the controls and records requirements described above.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

# SB-1002 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Hazard description
- Summary: An arc flash originating at the induction power cabinet adjacent to the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet has the potential to cause severe burns, ignition of shot media, and secondary energetic ejection of shot particles. The initiating mechanism is an electrical fault within the induction power cabinet that can produce a high-energy flashover into nearby metallic structures and particulate media. Personnel working at or near EQ-P2-L1-SB03 during cabinet access or routine top-up operations are at risk of direct thermal injury and of being struck by high-velocity shot media expelled from the cabinet.
- Background and recent observations: During routine maintenance rounds and archival review of maintenance records, an electrical incident was identified with root causes linked to inadequate control of stored conductive charge paths, proximity of unshielded terminals, and personnel presence during live work. The combination of conductive shot media and an arc flash source increases injury severity because hot ejecta can be propelled by the explosive pressure wave. Past procedural audits revealed inconsistent enforcement of work boundaries and incomplete isolation verification prior to access. This bulletin clarifies required actions to reduce likelihood and severity of arc flash events associated with the induction power cabinet serving the shot blast cabinet.
- Rationale for controls: Controls focus on eliminating or strictly controlling energy sources near particulate media, preventing ignition of shot media, and ensuring personnel are physically protected or absent during higher-risk activities. Controls emphasize administrative rigor, verification of isolation, physical barriers, and documented records to demonstrate compliance. Implementing the controls reduces the probability of initiating an arc and mitigates consequences if one occurs.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P2-L1-SB03
- Location: P2, line P2-L1
- Interfaces: induction power cabinet adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-SB03; access panels and shot media top-up points; local control housings and operator stations servicing the shot blast cabinet.
- Operational scope: all activities that require access to the shot blast cabinet or its adjacent service cabinets, including media top-up, inspection of wear lining, and any electrical work in the induction power cabinet vicinity.

Required controls
- Work authorization and isolation
  - All electrical work at the induction power cabinet shall be performed only after completion of lockout/tagout in accordance with SOP-P2-L1-03. Verification of zero energy and referenced isolation steps must be completed and recorded.
  - No routine maintenance, inspection, or media top-up shall occur while the induction power cabinet is energized and capable of supplying arc energy unless work is performed under an approved energized work permit in accordance with MM-P2-L1-SB03.
- Access restrictions and exclusion zones
  - Establish a controlled exclusion zone around the induction power cabinet and the shot blast cabinet during any condition where conductive particulate could be present within the cabinet and access is required. Personnel not involved in the task must remain outside the exclusion zone.
  - Access gates or temporary physical barriers must be used to define the perimeter when personnel are within the exclusion zone for authorized activities.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE) and procedural protections
  - When any live electrical exposure is unavoidable under an approved permit, affected personnel must wear PPE consistent with the highest hazard anticipated and per SOP-P2-L1-04. PPE selection, inspection, and replacement must be documented.
  - For media top-up operations and cabinet entry, use non-conductive tools and grounding verification devices approved under existing procedures. Avoid introduction of metal tools that could bridge energised terminals.
- Shot media controls
  - The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Use this interval to schedule media replenishment to avoid unattended accumulation of media near the induction cabinet during periods of electrical work.
  - When top-up is performed, ensure the induction power cabinet is isolated and verified safe according to SOP-P2-L1-03 before any access to media ports or removal of access panels.
- Inspection, maintenance, and housekeeping
  - Increase frequency of visual inspection of insulation, cable routing, and barrier integrity in the area adjacent to EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Document inspections and corrective actions in the cabinet maintenance log.
  - Keep the footprint around the induction power cabinet free of loose shot media and metallic debris that could create conductive paths. Housekeeping records shall be maintained and made available for review during audits.
- Training and communications
  - Conduct targeted refresher training for all personnel working on P2, line P2-L1 that covers arc flash risks specific to induction equipment, procedural steps from SOP-P2-L1-03 and SOP-P2-L1-04, and the administrative requirements in MM-P2-L1-SB03.
  - Post site-specific hazard notices at the entry to the cabinet area outlining required isolation, PPE, and the shot media top-up interval.

Examples and operational scenarios
- Example A: A technician scheduled media top-up during a routine production shift. Before opening the top-up port they must confirm LOTO per SOP-P2-L1-03 and log the activity. If induction power cannot be isolated immediately, defer the top-up until isolation is achieved to avoid creating a concurrent exposure to energized equipment.
- Example B: Electrical troubleshooting identified a hot terminal requiring observation. An energized work permit per MM-P2-L1-SB03 was issued; boundaries were established, PPE per SOP-P2-L1-04 was donned, and a non-conductive barrier was positioned between the terminal and the shot blast cabinet. The permit holder documented the start and stop times and attached the permit to the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Lockout/tagout verification forms and LOTO completion checklists as required by SOP-P2-L1-03.
- Energized work permits and associated hazard analyses per MM-P2-L1-SB03.
- PPE inspection and issue logs aligned with SOP-P2-L1-04.
- Shot media top-up records showing adherence to the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours.
- Inspection logs and corrective action reports for the induction power cabinet area.
- Training attendance rosters and refresher quiz results for personnel assigned to P2, line P2-L1.

Effective date
- This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue and supersedes prior guidance for the induction power cabinet area. All affected personnel must comply with the required controls in this bulletin and reference the procedures MM-P2-L1-SB03, SOP-P2-L1-03, and SOP-P2-L1-04 when performing related activities. Compliance will be monitored through routine audits and review of the records listed above.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1003: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses a recurring arc flash hazard observed at the induction power cabinet serving the heat treat line on P2-L3. Faults inside the cabinet have produced energetic electrical arcing during component failure and during maintenance access when the cabinet was assumed to be de-energized but residual or backfeed energy remained. Arc flash events have the potential to cause severe thermal injury, blast-related trauma, and ignition of surrounding materials. Contributing factors identified in recent inspections include degraded insulation at high-current conductors, loose connections at power distribution terminations, and inconsistent thermocouple signal integrity that has led to unexpected control behavior at the heat treat furnace. The work environment at the cabinet includes confined access, limited egress, and proximity to combustible oils and process wiring bundles, increasing the consequence of an arc event.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to the induction power cabinet and associated control and sensing equipment for Machining heat treat furnace #2. The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. The scope includes the cabinet enclosure, main bus connections, control contactors and solid state devices, sensing harnesses routed into the cabinet, and the immediate work area that maintenance and electrical staff must access. Operations personnel who perform furnace starts or parameter changes and maintenance personnel who perform inspection, troubleshooting, or repair on the cabinet are included in the affected population.

Required controls
Controls are organized as administrative, engineering, and personal protective measures. These controls are mandatory for any personnel entering the cabinet work area for tasks that expose energized conductors or that involve opening the cabinet.

- Administrative controls
  - Implement a job briefing and documented risk assessment prior to any work at the cabinet. The briefing must identify potential arc flash sources, confirm isolation steps to be followed, and assign roles for an observer and a qualified person to conduct verification. Record the briefing outcome in the equipment maintenance log and attach to the work order.
  - Require use of the pre-work checklist from SOP-P2-L3-02 for all cabinet access activities. The checklist must be completed and signed by the assigned qualified person and retained with the maintenance record.
  - Schedule thermocouple calibration activities per the stated calibration interval to prevent sensor drift that can cause improper control actions leading to unexpected energization sequences.
  - Restrict access to authorized qualified personnel only. Non-qualified personnel are prohibited from opening or adjusting the cabinet.

- Engineering controls
  - Before any access, ensure full isolation of the cabinet supply per the isolation procedure in MM-P2-L3-HT02. Verify that isolation is complete and documented in the isolation log.
  - Use a tagout and lockout system consistent with MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3. Locks and tags must remain in place until verification tests confirm de-energized conditions and all work is complete.
  - Where practical, relocate frequently adjusted low-voltage controls to an external control panel or provide remote access to reduce the frequency of cabinet openings.
  - Replace or secure suspected degraded terminations and insulation identified during inspection. Any repairs that require energization for testing must follow a written plan that minimizes exposure and uses remote testing where available.

- Personal protective measures
  - Qualified personnel must use PPE appropriate for arc hazard exposures as defined by site procedures. Ensure PPE is inspected and maintained. Do not improvise or omit required clothing or face protection.
  - Establish and enforce a minimum clearance zone around the cabinet during energized testing. Only essential personnel are permitted inside the zone, and a safety observer must be positioned outside the immediate clearance area to communicate emergency stop commands.

Step rationale and examples
The requirement to adhere to the thermocouple calibration interval addresses a root cause of unexpected behavior in the control system. When thermocouples drift outside acceptable accuracy, the furnace control logic may initiate sequences that alter power demand or engage switching devices in a manner not anticipated by operators. Ensuring the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days reduces the probability of control-induced energization events that can precede an arc flash.

Example scenario: A drifted thermocouple signal caused a control controller to command a rapid power change while an operator was accessing the cabinet for an unrelated inspection. The unexpected command energized a section of the bus that had been assumed safe, producing an arc at a loose termination. Following the controls in this bulletin—pre-work checklist, isolation verification, and strict adherence to the calibration interval—would have interrupted the chain of events.

Records to keep
Maintain the following documentation in the equipment file and the plant electronic maintenance record system:
- Completed pre-work checklists and risk assessments from SOP-P2-L3-02 attached to the work order.
- Isolation verification tags and the isolation log entries as required by MM-P2-L3-HT02.
- Lockout/tagout records and any deviations documented under MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
- Thermocouple calibration certificates and calibration dates showing compliance with the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.
- Repair and inspection reports for terminations, insulation condition, and any component replacements performed inside the cabinet.
- Incident reports for any arc flash or near-miss events including root cause analysis and corrective actions.

Effective date
Revision: Rev A

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-HT02
- MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3
- SOP-P2-L3-02

Actions required by recipients
Review this bulletin, update local job plans and procedures to incorporate the controls described, and verify that maintenance and calibration schedules reflect the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days. Supervisors are to confirm completion of these actions and file the verification records in the equipment maintenance folder.
