# SB-1015: Safety bulletin: noise exposure
Revision: Rev D
Plant: P3, line P3-L2
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses elevated noise exposures associated with the heat treat area adjacent to the Ring Rolling process served by EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Background investigations and employee feedback indicate that troubleshooting, maintenance activities, and process upsets in the heat treat cell can produce impulsive and sustained noise levels that increase the risk of hearing injury and reduce communication clarity for operators and maintenance technicians. Contributing factors include open access during loading and unloading sequences, compressed air use for part handling, and metal-to-metal impact noise during improper quench sequencing. Noise sources are intermittent and can be amplified by the cell geometry and adjacent conveyor systems. In addition to direct auditory risk, elevated noise complicates the identification of equipment faults, which can delay corrective action and prolong exposure.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Ring Rolling heat treat furnace equipment identified as EQ-P3-L2-HT03 located on line P3-L2 at Plant P3. It also applies to tasks performed in the immediate work zone during loading, unloading, quench handling, troubleshooting, and preventive maintenance when workers are expected to be within the noise field generated by EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Refer to MM-P3-L2-HT03 for machine maintenance requirements and SB-1041 for related hearing protection program expectations. For engineering change implications, see ECN-2026-017.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Ensure acoustic barriers and full enclosures are installed and maintained per design drawings referenced in ECN-2026-017. Barriers must be in place during normal operation and immediately reinstalled after maintenance to prevent sound leakage into the workplace.
- Confirm quench sequencing controls are set and verified prior to production startup. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. This limit is to prevent extended exposure to impact and splashing noise from delayed quench events and to ensure consistent process timing that reduces the likelihood of secondary handling that generates noise.

Administrative controls
- Limit personnel access to the immediate work zone during known high-noise activities by using the line P3-L2 access control procedures and signage. When troubleshooting or adjustments must be performed, designate a single, trained performer when practicable and schedule work to minimize concurrent noisy tasks.
- Implement a mandatory pre-task briefing for non-routine interventions in the EQ-P3-L2-HT03 zone that includes planned duration, expected noise sources, and required protective measures. Briefings must reference MM-P3-L2-HT03 for lockout/tagout and safe isolation steps.

Personal protective equipment
- Use the hearing protection devices and wearing criteria established in SB-1041 for the heat treat area. Replace disposable inserts and cushions per supplier guidance and records in MM-P3-L2-HT03. Selection should prioritize both attenuation and the ability to maintain communication during critical steps.

Monitoring and verification
- Conduct periodic noise assessments whenever process changes are implemented or after mechanical repairs that could alter acoustic characteristics. Findings and corrective actions must be recorded and retained with the equipment maintenance file referenced in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Use supervisor observations, employee reports, and the records noted below to verify that engineering and administrative controls remain effective. Follow-up measurements should be scheduled after any event that exceeds expected acoustic behavior or after the actions documented in ECN-2026-017 are performed.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for the quench delay limit: extended delay between transfer and quench causes operators to intervene in non-standard ways to stabilize parts, increasing handling noise and creating impact events as parts shift. Limiting delay to the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds reduces transient noise and minimizes opportunities for manual intervention that elevate exposure.
- Example scenario A: During a transfer command failure, parts remained in the transfer position. With the delay limit enforced and an immediate automated fallback, the system completed quench within the prescribed delay and avoided additional handling. Administrative controls ensured only one technician entered the zone to reset commands, wearing hearing protection per SB-1041.
- Example scenario B: During preventive maintenance, acoustic barrier panels were removed for access but not reinstalled. Work planning per MM-P3-L2-HT03 and this bulletin required temporary barriers and signage. The combination of administrative control and PPE maintained acceptable exposure while the panels were refitted.

Records to keep
- Noise assessment reports and measurement data for EQ-P3-L2-HT03, retained with the maintenance records in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Pre-task briefings and authorization forms for interventions in the heat treat zone, filed with the line P3-L2 job safety records.
- Corrective action documentation following any event that triggers a review, including references to applicable design or change documents such as ECN-2026-017.
- Hearing protection issue and replacement logs, consistent with the practices in SB-1041.

Effective date
Effective date: upon release of this bulletin.

References
- ECN-2026-017
- MM-P3-L2-HT03
- SB-1041

Distribution and responsibilities
Supervisors on line P3-L2 are responsible for ensuring compliance with the controls in this bulletin and for maintaining the records noted above. Maintenance leads must coordinate with engineering to verify that any changes outlined in ECN-2026-017 do not compromise the acoustic controls. Safety personnel will audit compliance and support noise assessments and training aligned with SB-1041.
title: Safety bulletin: noise exposure

# SB-1016 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Hazard description

An unplanned arc flash event occurred adjacent to the induction power cabinet serving the Heat Treat heat treat furnace identified as EQ-P2-L4-HT02. The event originated during a quench cycle and resulted in localized burning of insulation on control wiring, damage to the power cabinet door, and a brief loss of control communication to the furnace. Root-cause analysis indicates that the arc flash was initiated by a rapid energy transfer in the cabinet coincident with a delayed quench sequence. The energy release pathway included cabinet internal metallic surfaces and exposed terminal blocks not isolated by the existing barrier arrangement.

This hazard poses risk of severe thermal injury to personnel performing energized troubleshooting or routine access, risk of collateral equipment damage that can interrupt heat treat processing on line P2-L4, and risk of ignition of nearby combustibles if not addressed. The incident demonstrates that the current protection and procedural controls were insufficient to prevent an arc flash during abnormal sequencing of the quench system.

Background: EQ-P2-L4-HT02 operates with an electrically actuated quench process. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. The control logic permits a maximum delay before the quench actuation completes; delays beyond expected behavior can create conditions for arcing if power paths remain live and contacts are exposed. Existing risk assessments did not fully account for an arc initiation occurring during extended quench delay.

## Affected equipment

- Induction power cabinet for EQ-P2-L4-HT02, including high-current bus runs, contactor assemblies, and control terminal plates.  
- Adjacent control panels and wiring harnesses located within the same cabinet footprint on line P2-L4.  
- Personnel performing cabinet access, troubleshooting, or any activity that requires the cabinet to be energized or open while power is present.

Reference related maintenance and operating documents for detailed procedures: MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04.

## Required controls

The following controls are required immediately and must be implemented before any energized access to the induction power cabinet:

- Administrative control: All energized troubleshooting or access to the induction power cabinet must be authorized through the site energy control coordination process specified in SOP-P2-L4-02. Authorization must document that arc flash hazards have been reviewed and that electrical isolation is impractical only after documented justification consistent with MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.

- Work sequencing: When work requires that the cabinet remain energized, the affected work must be planned to eliminate exposure of personnel to live metal parts. Use insulated tooling and extend the use of insulating barriers inside the cabinet as described in SOP-P2-L4-04. If live work is unavoidable, ensure an approved energized work permit is in place that includes task-specific controls and verification requirements.

- Control logic verification: Before returning the cabinet to service after any maintenance or after a quench event, verify that the quench control timing matches documented values and interlocks. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds. Any deviation from the expected timing must be corrected and documented prior to restart.

- Physical barriers and labeling: Install additional insulating barriers to isolate terminal blocks and bus connections exposed during routine access. Apply durable arc-hazard warning labels to the cabinet exterior and to all serviceable panels. Labels and barriers must comply with the signage and guarding guidance in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.

- PPE and training: Personnel entering the arc boundary around the cabinet must wear PPE consistent with the risk assessment defined in SOP-P2-L4-02 and must be trained in energized work safety. Training records required by SOP-P2-L4-04 must be current and available at the worksite.

Rationale: Administrative authorizations and energized work permits reduce the likelihood that personnel will perform unplanned live work. Physical barriers reduce the probability of flashover between live components and accessible metal. Verifying quench timing addresses the specific mechanism identified in the incident and prevents the sequence condition that contributed to the arc flash. PPE and training mitigate consequence should an arc event occur despite controls.

Examples of acceptable controls: using insulated probe extensions to verify control voltages without removing panels; confirming control relay drop-out via remote indicators before door entry; applying temporary insulating shields over known exposure points during diagnostic work as allowed by SOP-P2-L4-04.

## Records to keep

Maintain the following records in the document control system entry for SB-1016 and attach them to the work order when controls are applied:

- Energized work permit or authorization described in SOP-P2-L4-02.  
- Control logic verification checklist signed by responsible engineer. The checklist must reference EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and include a confirmation that the quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 10 seconds.  
- Installation verification of insulating barriers and labels with photos.  
- Training verification records required by SOP-P2-L4-04 for personnel involved in cabinet access.  
- Incident report and root-cause analysis documentation per MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 where applicable.

These records must be retained according to the retention rules in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and be made available for review by plant safety leadership and maintenance auditing.

## Effective date

Effective date: Upon issuance of this bulletin (Rev A). Implement required controls immediately and include verification records with the next maintenance activity involving EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Review the controls during the next scheduled safety audit and update risk assessments in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 as needed.

For questions or clarifications contact the P2 safety lead or the heat treat line engineer assigned to P2-L4. Follow SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-04 for procedural detail and MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 for maintenance specific requirements.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1017 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during abrasive blasting operations within the P2-L2 area presents inhalation and secondary exposure risks to operators, maintenance personnel, and adjacent work zones. Dust from blasting contains particulate metal, spent abrasive, and surface coatings that can be respirable and can deposit on surfaces where it becomes re-entrainable. Short-term exposure can cause irritation of the eyes, nose, throat, and lungs; prolonged or repeated exposure to metal-containing dusts can contribute to chronic respiratory conditions and increase the risk of systemic toxicity depending on composition. Secondary risks include reduced visibility, contamination of controls and sensors, and ignition of pyrophoric fines where applicable. The risk is highest during active blasting, clean-out of blast cabinets and enclosures, and when performing machine maintenance that disturbs accumulated deposits.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to blasting activities and associated dust control when performed in proximity to line P2-L2 and to equipment listed below:
- Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P2-L2-RR03
- Blasting enclosures, portable blast cabinets, and blast recovery systems serving P2-L2
- Adjacent conveyors, ventilation intakes, and local control stations in the P2-L2 work cell

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Use enclosed blasting booths or temporary containment to limit dust spread beyond the immediate blasting area. Enclosures must interface with building ventilation to create negative pressure relative to adjacent workspaces and must discharge through filtration compliant with plant filtration practice (see SOP-P2-L2-03).
- Install and maintain local extraction at the point of blast media impact for processes that cannot be fully enclosed. Extraction inlet placement should capture generated dust before it becomes broadly airborne.
- Ensure blast recovery and media handling systems are sealed to prevent fugitive emissions during transfer and media handling.

Administrative controls
- Plan blasting work to minimize personnel in adjacent workspaces during operations. Post visible signage at the boundary of the blasting zone while operations are active.
- Sequence cleaning and housekeeping to remove settled dust using wet methods or HEPA-filtered vacuuming rather than brushing or compressed air to prevent re-entrainment.
- Coordinate blasting and ring rolling operations to avoid simultaneous activities that could increase personnel exposure in the P2-L2 area.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Respiratory protection selection shall follow the plant respiratory program and be based on task-specific hazard assessment. Where mechanical ventilation and enclosure controls are not sufficient to maintain exposures below acceptable levels per plant policy, use assigned respirators and cartridges appropriate for particulate challenge (see SOP-P2-L2-03).
- Eye and face protection, protective clothing, and gloves should be used to prevent dermal contact and eye irritation from dust.

Maintenance-specific controls and rationale
- During maintenance on EQ-P2-L2-RR03 and related systems, isolate and dampen potentially contaminated systems prior to opening enclosures or accessing internals to reduce airborne re-entrainment of settled dust.
- Where bolted assemblies are exposed to blast-generated dust, clean joint faces with HEPA-vacuuming and wipe-down before disassembly. This reduces abrasive particles that can accelerate wear or create secondary dust clouds.
- Critical fastener torque must be verified after maintenance that exposes structural or load-bearing connections on ring rolling equipment. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Use calibrated torque equipment documented in maintenance records per MM-P2-L2-RR03.

Examples and application
- Example 1: For a scheduled blast cleaning of a ring surface adjacent to EQ-P2-L2-RR03, the blasting area was set up with a temporary containment tent and a dedicated HEPA-filtered exhaust. Extraction inlet was positioned at the immediate impact zone, and a dedicated HEPA vacuum was used to remove settled dust before technicians entered to perform inspection. This prevented dust migration into the mill gap and avoided respiratory exposures in adjacent work benches.
- Example 2: During maintenance on a blast recovery hopper, personnel followed the administrative sequence of lockout/tagout, HEPA vacuum cleanup of the hopper interior, and then opening for inspection. Surfaces were wiped and replaced filters were verified in the local extraction system before resuming blasting operations.

Records to keep
- Blasting activity log: document date, location (P2-L2), work order number, personnel involved, presence and type of containment, type of abrasive media used, and verification that enclosure/ventilation was functioning. Retain according to plant record retention practice; reference SOP-P2-L2-03 for required log fields.
- Maintenance records: include post-maintenance torque verification for relevant fasteners. For EQ-P2-L2-RR03, record the mandrel clamp bolt torque verification entry showing 620 N·m and the calibrated tool used. Cross-reference these entries to MM-P2-L2-RR03 work orders.
- Air monitoring and filter change records: document any personal or area air monitoring performed during blasting events, and retention or disposal records for used HEPA filters or collected media.
- Training and competency records: document that personnel performing blasting, clean-up, and maintenance have completed required training modules and practical assessments per SOP-P2-L2-03.

Step rationale
Controls emphasize elimination and containment of dust at source to reduce reliance on PPE. Engineering controls such as enclosures and local extraction are the most effective means of reducing airborne particulate spread. Administrative measures, including sequencing and documented cleanup methods, prevent secondary exposures. The specific maintenance requirement to verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 at 620 N·m ensures mechanical integrity after activities that may loosen fasteners due to vibration or disassembly; documenting this action provides traceability in case of downstream issues. Refer to MM-P2-L2-RR03 for maintenance procedures and SB-1049 for related airborne particulate guidance.

Related documents
MM-P2-L2-RR03
SB-1049
SOP-P2-L2-03

Effective date
Effective date: Upon release of Rev B

Action required
Supervisors and maintenance planners in P2-L2 must incorporate these controls into job plans and permit-to-work documents immediately. Compliance will be audited during routine safety walks and maintenance reviews.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1018 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

## Hazard description
An arc flash event was observed originating from the induction power cabinet feeding the ring rolling induction coils adjacent to the shot blast cabinet. The initiating fault pathway involved energized conductors within the induction power cabinet and a secondary conductive path established by a dislodged grounding lug on the adjacent blast wheel housing. Arc flash hazards include extreme thermal energy, molten metal ejection, overpressure shock, and conductive debris projection. In the observed incident, personnel within the immediate vicinity experienced exposure to intense light and hot particulate; no fatalities occurred, but there were injuries that required medical attention and resulted in lost time. Root cause analysis identified a combination of mechanical loosening and inadequate verification during maintenance as primary contributors to the event.

Background: The induction power cabinet services high-current equipment and is subject to vibration and thermal cycling during normal operation. The shot blast cabinet mounted nearby contains fittings that are periodically removed and reinstalled during maintenance. Fastener retention on the blast wheel liner assembly is therefore a critical interface for maintaining the electrical isolation and mechanical integrity of the blast wheel housing. A specific fastener relating to the blast wheel liner bolt for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) was found to be under-torqued, which allowed relative movement that contributed to a conductive contact path under fault conditions. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.

Step rationale: Ensuring specified fastener torques are applied and documented prevents mechanical loosening that may create unintended conductive paths. Verifying electrical connections and maintaining mechanical interfaces reduces the probability of arcing and limits available fault energy should an event begin. The controls in this bulletin address work practices, mechanical verification, electrical isolation, and record keeping.

## Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet supplying induction coils in the Ring Rolling cell adjacent to the shot blast cabinet. Identified cabinet: EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
- Blast wheel liner and associated fasteners on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01).
- All portable tooling and maintenance access points used during servicing of the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment.

Affected personnel: maintenance electricians, mechanical fitters, line operators, and contractors performing work in the P3, line P3-L2 area.

Related procedures: See SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-04, SOP-P3-L2-05 for reference to authorized work methods, lockout-tagout sequences, and permit requirements.

## Required controls
The following controls are mandatory for all work on, or within the immediate zone of influence of, the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment.

1. Administrative controls
   - All work on or adjacent to the induction power cabinet requires a pre-job briefing that documents roles, tasks, and hazard controls. The briefing must reference SOP-P3-L2-02 for electrical isolation procedures and SOP-P3-L2-04 for hot work and confined access considerations.
   - Work permits must be issued and retained per SOP-P3-L2-05 for the duration of the job. Permits shall explicitly list the fasteners to be checked and the torque value to be applied to the blast wheel liner bolt for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01).

2. Mechanical verification
   - Before restoring power, verify that all blast wheel liner fasteners are installed and torqued to the specified value. Document application of the specified torque. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m.
   - Use calibrated torque tools. Calibration records for torque equipment must be available at the time of the job and recorded as part of maintenance documentation.

3. Electrical isolation and verification
   - Follow electrical isolation steps in SOP-P3-L2-02. Lockout-tagout must be verified by a qualified electrician and confirmed by a second verifier for critical isolations.
   - Perform voltage verification on the induction power cabinet after isolation and before any conductive contact is made. Document voltage check results on the permit.

4. Work-by-qualified-personnel
   - Only qualified electricians and trained mechanical staff are permitted to perform work within the induction cabinet and on adjacent conductive housings. If contractors are engaged, they must produce training and qualification records before work begins.

5. Zone control and PPE
   - Establish an exclusion zone during energized work; control access and post hazard signage. Enforce PPE appropriate for potential arc flash exposure as determined by site hazard assessment procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L2-04.

6. Post-maintenance inspection and testing
   - After reassembly and prior to energization, inspect all mechanical joints and electrical connectors for correct installation. Record findings and corrective actions.
   - Conduct a controlled re-energization sequence per SOP-P3-L2-02 with a qualified observer and emergency response readiness.

Examples:
- Example 1: During a scheduled bearing replacement on the blast wheel, the liner bolt was removed and reinstalled. The technician applied torque but failed to record the value. Subsequent vibration caused slight loosening; relative movement allowed a conductive contact that coincided with a transient fault from the induction cabinet. Adherence to the requirement to document the applied torque would have flagged the absence of recorded calibration verification and prompted re-checking.
- Example 2: A contractor performed isolation but did not follow the second-verifier requirement in SOP-P3-L2-02. A missed step left a feed energized. The follow-up corrective action included re-training and enforcing the two-verifier confirmation block on the permit.

## Records to keep
- Completed pre-job briefing forms and issued work permits per SOP-P3-L2-05.
- Torque application records showing operator name, torque tool ID, calibration certificate reference, and confirmation of the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) being set to 100 N·m.
- Electrical isolation verification checklists and voltage test results referenced to SOP-P3-L2-02.
- Post-maintenance inspection reports, including any deviations and corrective actions taken.
- Training and qualification records for all personnel who performed the work, including any contractor documentation accepted for the job.

Retention: Records must be filed in the P3 maintenance record system and retained according to site document retention policy as specified in SOP-P3-L2-05.

## Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon release. All activities on the induction power cabinet and adjacent shot blast equipment in P3, line P3-L2 must comply with the controls above before any further work proceeds. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring implementation and for auditing compliance against SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-04, and SOP-P3-L2-05.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1019 - Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
- Background: Recent checks of the dust collection system serving the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) identified an elevated dust collector pressure drop alarm setpoint being reached during normal operation. The dust load on the collector can increase quench oil mist settling in downstream fabric filters and ductwork. Accumulated oil-dust deposits in the collector or downstream plenums present a combustible mixture that can be ignited by hot particulates, electrostatic discharge, or frictional heating from clogged blowers, creating a quench oil fire risk in the heat treat area.
- Observation: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. This alarm level has been confirmed by maintenance logs and transient capture during last shutdowns, indicating the collector has reached a resistance to airflow consistent with significant media loading. A sustained condition at this alarm indicates a decreased capture efficiency for oil mist and increased potential for deposit accumulation. Operators must assume the presence of oil-impregnated dust layers in the system when this alarm value is recorded.
- Step rationale: The alarm value of 1510 Pa is used as the operational trigger to prevent extended operation under high loading conditions. Allowing continued operation beyond this level increases the risk window for ignition events and reduces the ability of emergency mitigation measures to control a fire. Actions below are intended to eliminate fuel sources, interrupt ignition paths, and restore filtration performance.

Affected equipment
- Primary: Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) and its dedicated dust collector and ductwork.
- Adjacent systems: Local ventilation and plenum serving the heat treat bay, portable air handling equipment used for maintenance, and any temporary quench oil application devices that share recovery or drainage systems with EQ-P3-L4-SB03.
- Refer to documented maintenance and machine history in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for past filter change records and SB-1038 for related quench oil incident analyses. Operational steps and permitted startup sequence adjustments are detailed in SOP-P3-L4-02.

Required controls
- Immediate actions upon alarm:
  - Stop production feeds to the shot blast cabinet and place EQ-P3-L4-SB03 in safe shutdown per SOP-P3-L4-02.
  - Isolate sources of quench oil flow to the cabinet and associated conveyors. Verify isolation with visual confirmation and log the action in the equipment downtime record.
  - Notify maintenance and safety supervision and tag the dust collector out of service pending inspection and cleaning. Record the alarm occurrence and actions taken in the shift log and in the equipment corrective action record (see MM-P3-L4-SB03).
- Inspection and cleaning:
  - Qualified maintenance shall perform a visual and hands-off inspection of the collector internals, downstream plenums, duct transitions, and blower housings. Look specifically for oil-wetted dust deposits, smoldering marks, or particulate bridging at seams and transitions. Document findings and attach photographs to the maintenance report.
  - Remove and properly dispose of oil-contaminated filters and accumulated deposits per the hazardous waste handling procedures referenced in MM-P3-L4-SB03. Do not attempt compressed-air cleaning of oil-impregnated media.
- Restart conditions:
  - Return-to-service is permitted only after cleaning and remediation are completed, blower vibration and temperature are verified to be within normal limits per OEM guidance, and the collector demonstrates a cleared pressure drop below the alarm threshold during a controlled test run outlined in SOP-P3-L4-02. Record the test run results in the equipment test log.
- Engineering and administrative controls:
  - Implement routine inspection checkpoints for visible oil carryover at the cabinet exhaust, with findings entered into the preventive maintenance log in MM-P3-L4-SB03.
  - Update SOP-P3-L4-02 to include the 1510 Pa alarm response steps and recordkeeping requirements. Ensure operators and maintenance personnel review the updated SOP before returning EQ-P3-L4-SB03 to production.
  - Prohibit hot work, open flames, or ignition source introduction in the affected bay until a safety clearance is issued by safety supervision and recorded.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario A: During an end-of-shift changeover, the operator observes the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. The operator initiates shutdown per SOP-P3-L4-02, isolates oil feeds, and logs the event. Maintenance finds oil-wetted filter media and schedules replacement. Production resumes only after documentation of cleaning and a successful controlled test run.
- Example scenario B: If the alarm is intermittent, log each occurrence and increase inspection frequency until a pattern is established. Treat every occurrence as a potential hazard and follow immediate actions above until trend analysis from MM-P3-L4-SB03 indicates otherwise.

Records to keep
- Shift log entries documenting alarm occurrence, actions taken, and personnel notified.
- Maintenance inspection report with photos and measurements attached to MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Filter replacement and disposal records linked to the hazardous waste manifest or internal disposal log.
- Return-to-service test run results and signoff per SOP-P3-L4-02.
- Incident follow-up and root cause analysis documentation if any ignition, smoldering, or fire was observed, with cross-reference to SB-1038 for similar event learnings.

Effective date
- Effective: Upon issuance. All operations, maintenance, and safety personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 must comply with the required controls and update their local procedure checklists to reflect this bulletin.

# SB-1020 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated during blasting activities in the vicinity of the Ring Rolling area presents inhalation and contamination hazards to personnel and to sensitive process equipment. The blasting media and removed surface material can produce respirable particulates that migrate along airflows created by process ventilation and mobile equipment movement. Exposure can result in respiratory irritation, contamination of machine surfaces, fouling of bearings and seals, and increased fire risk where fines accumulate on hot surfaces or electrical enclosures. Secondary hazards include the potential for dust to enter bearing housings and tooling interfaces, increasing wear and risking seizure if not controlled.

Background: Blasting is required for surface preparation on cast and forged components prior to machining and rolling operations. The combination of blasting residue and existing process dust creates a mixed particulate field that behaves differently than a single-source dust. This bulletin focuses on controls to reduce airborne particulate migration into the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and immediate work areas, and to ensure maintenance tasks that expose internal interfaces include dust control measures.

Step rationale: Controls emphasize source containment, controlled capture, personal protection, and housekeeping to prevent dust deposition in critical machine areas. Where service access requires removal of covers or exposure of lubrication points, procedural controls mitigate the risk of particulate ingress to bearings, mandrels, clamps and tooling interfaces.

## Affected equipment
- Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) located on P1-L2.
- Surrounding support zones where blasting is performed and where airflow paths can reach the equipment.
- Portable process auxiliary equipment that transfers parts between blasting stations and the mill.

The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.

Technicians who perform mandrel installation, clamp adjustment, seal replacement, or bearing service on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 are considered affected personnel and must follow the controls below.

Related documents: ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05

## Required controls
Controls are grouped by priority: source control, capture and containment, administrative procedures, personal protective equipment, and verification records.

- Source control: Coordinate blasting schedules to avoid performing abrasive blasting immediately upwind or in direct airflow paths toward EQ-P1-L2-RR01. When blasting is required near the line, use contained blasting booths or portable enclosures with negative pressure capture to prevent fugitive dust migration into the mill area. Exhaust from blasting containments must be filtered before release to the plant environment as described in ECN-2026-009.

- Capture and containment at the mill: When EQ-P1-L2-RR01 is idle for maintenance that exposes internal assemblies, install temporary sealed covers over exposed openings and apply local extraction at the access point to prevent dust ingress. Use cleanable covers that do not shed fibers. Avoid using permeable cloth as a final barrier where particulate control is required.

- Administrative procedures: Work planning for blasting and for maintenance on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 must be coordinated through line supervision. All blasting work orders that could affect P1-L2 must reference SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05. Maintenance work that requires mandrel removal or clamp bolt access must include pre-task hazard assessment noting potential dust exposure and specifying isolation and cleaning steps prior to reassembly.

- Personal protective equipment: Personnel working near blasting operations or during cleanup shall wear approved respiratory protection and eye protection as required by site PPE policy. Respiratory selection and fit must be consistent with SOP-P1-L2-05 and the applicable exposure assessment referenced in ECN-2026-009.

- Housekeeping: Implement targeted cleaning of handrails, control panels, junction boxes, and mill housings at regular intervals determined by local supervision and recorded in the maintenance log. Use vacuum capture designed for industrial dusts rather than compressed air for cleaning machine surfaces.

- Reassembly and torque control: After any activity that could result in dust ingress into clamps or mandrel interfaces, clean mating surfaces using approved non-shedding wipes and re-lubricate per SOP-P1-L2-03. Reinstall mandrel clamp bolts and apply the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.

Examples: A blasting job performed at the adjacent prep area created visible dust migration toward the mill during a shift change. Corrective practice was to delay blasting until after completion of scheduled mandrel changeout and to use a portable enclosure with filtered exhaust during all subsequent near-line blasting operations. Another example: a bearing housing was found to contain abrasive fines after an unscheduled blast; the maintenance team quarantined the assembly, performed controlled disassembly within a downdraft booth, replaced contaminated lubricant, and documented actions in the maintenance record as required below.

## Records to keep
- Blast job coordination records that reference SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05 and note measures taken to protect P1-L2 equipment. Retain in the line coordination folder and attach to the work order record.
- Maintenance reports for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 that document cleaning steps performed, verification of sealing measures, and confirmation that the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m was applied during reassembly. Include technician initials and supervisor approval.
- Air capture and filter maintenance logs for any temporary enclosures used during blasting activities, referenced to ECN-2026-009.
- Incident and observation reports related to dust migration or contamination near EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Enter into the plant safety database and notify line management.

Verification: Supervision shall inspect the equipment area after blasting events and before restarting EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Verification includes visual inspection for dust accumulation on control surfaces and key interfaces, review of the maintenance report for torque confirmation, and spot checks of temporary enclosures.

## Effective date
Effective upon release Rev A. All blasting and maintenance planning that could affect P1-L2 shall implement the controls above and reference ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05 for detailed procedures.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1021 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Hazard description
------------------

An arc flash event occurred adjacent to the induction power cabinet that supplies the Hot Forge induction heaters. Investigation identified interaction between a dust collector alarm condition and maintenance activity at the nearby shot blast cabinet ventilation plenum as a credible contributor to an unusual transient on the local electrical distribution. The immediate hazard is thermal and blast energy from an electrical arc, with potential for severe injury and equipment damage. Secondary hazards include ignition of combustible dust, exposure to metal fragments, and interruption of critical controls for forging operations.

Root cause analysis identified an uncontrolled dust collector pressure drop alarm condition on the shot blast cabinet ventilation that coincided with a planned maintenance activity at the induction power cabinet. The dust handling condition is documented as follows: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. That alarm threshold and the cabinet identifier are relevant to sequencing of work and to permit conditions.

Affected equipment
------------------

This bulletin applies to the induction power cabinet and associated feeder switchgear serving the Hot Forge induction heaters in plant P2, line P2-L1. It specifically references the shot blast dust collection system feeding cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and any auxiliary ventilation or interlock panels that share local control circuits or common fusing. Personnel who perform activities on or near the induction power cabinet, the shot blast cabinet ventilation plenum, or the dust collector should consider the conditions described here before entry.

Required controls
-----------------

Engineering and administrative controls must be applied immediately to reduce arc flash risk when work is planned or underway in the area described above.

- Prework verification: Before any maintenance, testing, or cleaning at the induction power cabinet or at the adjacent shot blast cabinet ventilation, verify alarm states and dust collector pressure readings using the site control system and physical inspection of the collector differential gauge. Confirm that the dust collector pressure drop alarm state is not active. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa; treat any alarm condition matching that descriptor as a stop condition for electrical work until resolved.

- Work sequencing: Coordinate electrical isolation and lockout procedures with ventilation maintenance. If dust collector alarms are present, do not energize or reenergize cabinet power until alarms are cleared and interlocks are confirmed stable. Maintain clear communication between the electrical crew and the ventilation maintenance lead. Use the communication procedure in SOP-P2-L1-01 for coordination of multi-discipline work.

- Hazard mitigation: Apply electrically safe work practices per the established arc flash program. Where deenergized maintenance is not practicable, treat the cabinet as live and use appropriate personal protective equipment for energized work. Limit personnel in the arc flash boundary to authorized, trained individuals. Use insulated tools and maintain grounding continuity for portable grounded equipment.

- Controls verification: After any change to ventilation or dust collector status, perform post-change verification of control interlocks, protective relays, and cabinet door microswitches before permitting energized operations. Record verification actions in the maintenance log and reference ECN-2026-036 for any recent engineering changes that could affect local interlocks.

- Training and permits: Require a documented prejob brief and an energized work permit when work involves potential exposure to arc flash. Include a line item to check the dust collector alarm state for EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Use SOP-P2-L1-03 for electrical isolation and lockout-tagout detail during permits that include induction power components.

Implementation rationale and examples
------------------------------------

The dust collector alarm value is an operational indicator of abnormal airflow or filter loading at the shot blast cabinet. When the alarm threshold shown above is reached, airflow transients and local control responses can create unintended sequences in shared control cabinets. For example, a maintenance crew replacing filters on the shot blast cabinet can momentarily change the load on the collector fan, which may cause an auxiliary contact to change state and initiate a temporary undervoltage or relay chase. If electrical work is in progress at the induction power cabinet at the same time, transient relay operations can allow a phase to reenergize or close a breaker unexpectedly. Coordinating work and ensuring alarms are cleared prevents overlapping events that increase arc flash likelihood.

Records to keep
----------------

Maintain the following records for each work activity affected by this bulletin:

- Prework verification checklist that includes confirmation of dust collector alarm state for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and the exact text of the alarm condition where practical.

- Communication logs between electrical and ventilation teams citing use of SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-03 as references for coordination and lockout procedures.

- Copies of energized work permits and permits to work that reference this bulletin.

- Postwork lockout removal verification and any control adjustments made as a result of resolving the alarm. Note any references to ECN-2026-036 when hardware or wiring changes were involved.

Effective date
--------------

Effective immediately. All work planning and permits for the induction power cabinet area and for shot blast cabinet ventilation must comply with this bulletin and with the procedures cited below. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-03 for detailed procedures and to ECN-2026-036 for recent engineering change information that may affect implementation.

References
----------

ECN-2026-036  
SOP-P2-L1-01  
SOP-P2-L1-03

Contact
-------

Maintenance engineering and the electrical safety officer on site should be consulted for interpretation and for assistance with implementation of controls described in this bulletin.
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

# SB-1022 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy in press and shot blast auxiliary systems presents a latent release hazard during maintenance, inspection, and tooling changes. Residual pressure trapped in hydraulic accumulators, hoses, cylinders, valves, and cylinder end caps can cause sudden actuator movement, high-velocity fluid discharge, or component separation when a restraint is removed or a fitting is loosened. In the shot blast cabinet environment, hydraulic release can inject particulate into the workspace, displace guarding, or create slip hazards when hydraulic lubricant reaches floor surfaces. Stored energy incidents can occur without obvious external indications because system gauges may show no pressure or because mechanical locks mask internal spring preloads or trapped charge.

Background and rationale
This bulletin addresses EQ-P3-L3-SB01, a machining shot blast cabinet that integrates hydraulic components for door actuation and auxiliary tool positioning. The presence of stored hydraulic energy is a common industrial risk that has led to injuries at other facilities when procedures do not explicitly verify zero energy or use positive isolation methods. Eliminating or controlling stored energy is a basic safety principle aligned with lockout/tagout best practices.

The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709. Knowledge of the correct lubricant is required for contamination control and for maintenance steps that involve fluid handling. Use of the specified lubricant prevents incompatibilities that could alter seal behavior and affect the reliability of pressure-retaining components.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L3-SB01 (Machining shot blast cabinet #1) and all connected hydraulic lines, accumulators, cylinders, valves, quick disconnects, and end fittings located on line P3-L3.  
- Any portable hydraulic test equipment temporarily connected during troubleshooting or maintenance.  
- Local guarding, sensors, and interlocks that rely on hydraulic positioners for safe function.

Required controls
Administrative controls
- Work on any hydraulic component on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 must be planned and authorized by maintenance supervision and documented in the maintenance work record. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03 for procedure steps related to isolation and task-specific permits. Citation: SOP-P3-L3-02; SOP-P3-L3-03.
- A job safety brief must be held before starting any activity that could expose personnel to stored hydraulic energy. The brief must identify potential trapped energy sources, planned isolation points, and rescue communications.
- Use the maintenance manual and schematic for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 for identification of isolation valves and accumulator locations. Citation: MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

Isolation and verification
- Before any disassembly or exposure of hydraulic fittings, isolate energy sources using positive physical isolation methods described in SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03. Where applicable, follow the isolation sequence in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.
- Establish a verified zero-energy state by venting residual fluid to a dedicated recovery container and by cycling actuators to their defined safe positions. Verification shall include a physical attempt to move the isolated component using the manual override method described in SOP-P3-L3-03. If motion occurs, re-evaluate isolation.
- Tag and lock isolation points per site lockout/tagout requirements until the work scope is complete and the responsible maintenance technician releases the lock.

Engineering controls
- Where practical, install manual bleed valves or lockable mechanical stops that allow positive mechanical blocking in addition to hydraulic isolation. Use of lockable mechanical stops reduces reliance on hydraulic seals to maintain a safe condition.
- Inspect quick-disconnect fittings and hose assemblies for rated condition prior to reconnecting after maintenance. Replace suspect components with approved parts in the maintenance inventory that reference MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for compatibility.

Personal protective equipment and work practices
- Required PPE for work involving potential hydraulic fluid release includes splash-resistant eye protection, fluid-resistant gloves, and footwear with slip-resistant soles. Avoid skin contact with hydraulic fluid; wash exposed skin promptly and document exposure events in the safety log.
- Never loosen hydraulic fittings while system pressure status is unknown or while the system has not been isolated and verified to be at zero energy.

Examples and illustrative scenarios
- Example scenario A: A technician plans to remove a door cylinder. Following the administrative controls above, the technician isolates the hydraulic supply, vents the line into a recovery container, applies a mechanical stop to the door, and uses the verification step in SOP-P3-L3-03 to ensure the cylinder cannot move before loosening fittings. This prevents accidental door closure and fluid spray.
- Example scenario B: A faulted quick-disconnect is suspected of leaking. The technician uses MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 to locate the isolation valve upstream, tags and locks the valve, bleeds residual fluid to the recovery container, and then replaces the fitting with a unit from approved parts. The lubricant specified for EQ-P3-L3-SB01, CFW-LUB-709, is applied at reassembly to the connection as required by the maintenance checklist.

Records to keep
- A maintenance work record must be completed for every intervention that involves hydraulic components on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Records shall reference the performed isolation steps, verification actions, the personnel who executed lockout/tagout, and the related document citations: MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2; SOP-P3-L3-02; SOP-P3-L3-03.
- PPE inspection notes, any contamination cleanup logs, and incident or near-miss reports related to stored hydraulic energy must be filed with the maintenance supervisor and retained in the plant safety folder for review.
- Lubricant usage records for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 shall note the part number CFW-LUB-709 and be entered into the lubrication log.

Effective date
Effective date: See issuance record held in the document control system.
title: Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

# SB-1023 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Hazard description
- Summary: An arc flash event occurred at the induction power cabinet feeding the Machining heat treat furnace during routine maintenance. The incident produced a high-energy flash and molten material projection from within the cabinet, presenting burn and impact hazards to personnel and risk of cascade failures to adjacent equipment. This bulletin documents the hazard, root-cause contributors observed during the event investigation, and controls to prevent recurrence.
- Background and scenario detail: The arc initiated within the power cabinet where bolted connections and a thermocouple harness interface are routed. Investigation identified compromised insulation and a localized loose power connection as the initiating fault path. The event progressed rapidly, with ejection of panels and concentrated thermal energy at the cabinet face. Personnel were outside the immediate clearance zone but within equipment-room proximity and were exposed to smoke and secondary debris.
- Rationale for controls: Arc flash energy release is a function of fault current and duration. Eliminating initiation sources (loose connections, damaged wiring, contaminated terminations) and limiting available energy via proper isolation procedures and lockout-tagout reduces both likelihood and severity. Administrative controls and inspection intervals are necessary to detect progressive degradation before a failure.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P2-L3-HT02 induction power cabinet associated with Machining heat treat furnace #2.
- Area: P2, line P2-L3 electrical room and adjacent furnace work area where maintenance, thermocouple access, and power cabinet operations occur.
- Interlocks and related systems: cabinet door interlocks, door-mounted indicators, and the cabinet power disconnects used during maintenance activities.
- Calibration note: The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.
- Related documents: MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3, SB-1039, SOP-P2-L3-05.

Required controls
- Immediate actions (administrative and physical)
  - Isolate: Before any entry into the power cabinet area or before removal of panels, ensure full isolation in accordance with SOP-P2-L3-05 and applicable lockout-tagout procedures. Do not assume controls are de-energized until verified by qualified personnel.
  - Verify: Use only calibrated test equipment and follow the verification steps in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 for confirming absence of voltage on conductors and buswork prior to work on or adjacent to the cabinet.
  - Restrict access: During any power cabinet inspection or maintenance, restrict the work area to qualified electrical personnel only. Maintain a minimum boundary consistent with company arc-flash PPE philosophy and the risk assessment documented in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
- Preventive maintenance and inspection
  - Connection integrity: Inspect and re-torque accessible bolted electrical connections during scheduled maintenance windows described in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3. Where bolted connections are not accessible without panel removal, perform visual and infrared thermographic surveys following applicable procedures.
  - Wiring and harness condition: Inspect the thermocouple harness and associated routing for chafing, insulation degradation, and contamination. Replace or re-route harnesses that are subject to mechanical damage or proximity to heat sources.
  - Housekeeping: Keep the cabinet interior free of foreign materials, dust accumulation, and liquids. Any signs of contamination or corrosion discovered during inspection must be remediated before returning the cabinet to service.
- Work practice controls
  - Panel removal: When panel or component removal is required, perform a documented risk assessment and implement barriers or blast shields where exposure risk is identified. Use appropriate PPE and maintain a watch to prevent nonessential personnel from entering the hazard zone.
  - Energized work: Energized work inside the power cabinet is not permitted except under conditions described in SOP-P2-L3-05 and only with written authorization from the Responsible Electrical Supervisor. Energized work requires a formal energized work permit, justification, and specialized PPE.
  - Thermocouple handling: Thermocouple insertion, removal, and calibration activities should be performed following MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 to avoid introducing loose terminations or stray wiring into the power compartment.
- Training and qualification
  - Ensure all personnel who perform inspections or maintenance on EQ-P2-L3-HT02 have current qualifications per SOP-P2-L3-05 and have received specific training on arc-flash hazard recognition and mitigation.
  - Document training completion and maintain records in the training management system as required by MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
- Examples of application
  - Example 1: During routine thermocouple calibration, a technician preparing to remove an access panel identified a frayed harness. The technician stopped work, notified the supervisor, and performed isolation and verification steps prior to removal. A replacement harness was installed and routed to avoid contact with high-temperature surfaces.
  - Example 2: Building maintenance noted discoloration on an exterior cabinet door indicating thermal stress. A thermographic inspection per MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 was scheduled. The inspection identified an elevated joint temperature and the bolted connection was reconditioned after isolation and verification.
- Records to keep
  - Inspection and maintenance logs for EQ-P2-L3-HT02, including any corrective actions taken and parts replaced; retain entries in accordance with MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
  - Thermocouple calibration records for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), noting that calibrations are scheduled to meet the calibration interval specified above; store calibration certificates with the equipment calibration file referenced in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
  - Training and qualification records required by SOP-P2-L3-05 for personnel performing cabinet work.
  - Incident report and root cause analysis for the event that prompted this bulletin; retain per corporate incident record policy and refer to SB-1039 for related communications.

Effective date
- Revision status: Rev B. This bulletin is issued as Rev B for immediate implementation for all P2, line P2-L3 personnel and vendors performing work on EQ-P2-L3-HT02.
- Implementation note: Apply the required controls at the next scheduled access or maintenance activity for the EQ-P2-L3-HT02 cabinet and include inspection and record updates as described above.

References
- MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3
- SB-1039
- SOP-P2-L3-05
title: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

text:
# SB-1024 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated by blasting operations in the Ring Rolling area can present inhalation, slip, electrical contamination, and equipment fouling hazards. Dust from media attrition, degraded coatings, and removed surface contaminants can remain suspended in work zones and re-deposit on nearby controls, motors, and heat-exchange surfaces. In addition to immediate respiratory irritation for personnel, accumulated dust can mask visual indicators, obstruct ventilation intakes, and compromise electrical connectors. The potential for secondary ignition is elevated where dust coats hot surfaces or electrical enclosures. This bulletin focuses on controls and administrative measures to reduce exposure and prevent equipment degradation related to blasting activities adjacent to the Ring Rolling induction billet heater identified as EQ-P2-L2-IH01.

Background and rationale
Recent observations during blasting adjacent to line P2-L2 documented visible dust migration into the Ring Rolling enclosure and onto sensitive equipment surfaces. The presence of conductive or hygroscopic residues on electrical components increases the risk of nuisance trips and corrosion. Housekeeping alone will not fully mitigate airborne transport during blasting; a combination of engineering containment, targeted PPE, modified work sequencing, and documented lubrication and maintenance practices is required. Controls recommended here align with established process and safety expectations in QS-PROC-07 and with local operating procedures SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-05.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L2-IH01 (Ring Rolling induction billet heater). Note: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938.
- Motors, drives, sensors, and control panels located within the P2-L2 enclosure or within the documented blast drift path.
- Fixed ventilation intakes and filtration elements serving the P2-L2 line.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Temporary physical containment: install flexible containment barriers and closing flaps at the blast interface to limit direct dispersion into the Ring Rolling enclosure. Ensure barriers do not obstruct emergency egress or access to safety devices.
- Directed local exhaust: position portable capture hoods with inline filtration between the blast area and sensitive equipment when blasting cannot be isolated by distance or complete barriers. Route exhausted air to safe discharge points using continuous ducting to prevent re-entrainment.
- Seal penetrations: apply removable gasketing or tape over open cable penetrations and panel seams on equipment adjacent to the blast zone prior to blasting. Remove and inspect seals after cleaning before restoring service.

Administrative controls
- Work sequencing: schedule blasting operations during times of minimal Line P2-L2 operation or during designated maintenance windows to limit personnel presence and exposure.
- Pre-blast checks: consult SOP-P2-L2-01 for isolation checklists and confirm that sensitive equipment has been de-energized or protected according to SOP-P2-L2-05 when applicable.
- Area notification: issue advance notice to affected trades and control room personnel with clear boundaries for the temporary exclusion zone.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Require fit-appropriate respiratory protection for personnel performing or supervising blasting where engineering containment or exhaust does not fully control airborne dust. Selection and fit-testing must follow site respiratory program and QS-PROC-07.
- Require eye protection and protective clothing to limit skin contact with abrasive residues.

Operational and maintenance measures
- Post-blast cleaning: use HEPA-filtered vacuums for deposition removal on and around EQ-P2-L2-IH01, control panels, and ventilation intakes. Avoid dry sweeping that re-entrains dust.
- Inspection and lubrication: after cleaning, inspect electrical connectors and motor cooling passages. Apply lubrication and protective corrosion control as directed by maintenance procedures. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938; document its application on the maintenance log entry for the asset.
- Filtration checks: inspect and replace intake and portable filter cartridges per serviceability guidelines recorded in maintenance logs and as referenced by SOP-P2-L2-05. Capture filter disposal records in waste management logs.

Examples and practical scenarios
- Example A: When blasting must occur within the same room as EQ-P2-L2-IH01, set up dual containment: a temporary curtain at the blast boundary and a portable local exhaust hood positioned between the blast face and the heater intake. Evacuate nonessential personnel from the enclosure and record the operation in the local shift log.
- Example B: For short, intermittent grit removal where full containment is impractical, apply panel sealing on adjacent equipment, operate continuous HEPA vacuuming, and limit blasting duration. After completion, perform a targeted visual and vacuum cleaning of EQ-P2-L2-IH01, then note CFW-LUB-938 application in the equipment maintenance record if lubrication is disturbed during cleaning.

Records to keep
- Pre-blast notification log: time, personnel notified, containment methods employed, reference to SOP-P2-L2-01 or SOP-P2-L2-05 as applicable.
- Cleaning and inspection log: description of cleaning method, areas cleaned, photographic record where possible, and confirmation that HEPA vacuums were used.
- Maintenance log for EQ-P2-L2-IH01: record any application of CFW-LUB-938, who performed the work, and any observations of deposits, corrosion, or component fouling.
- Filter and waste disposal records: identity of filters removed, containment of used media, and disposition documented per waste handling procedures.
- Incident and deviation reports: any excursions, personnel exposure incidents, equipment faults, or unexpected ignitions recorded and routed according to QS-PROC-07.

Implementation and follow-up
- Supervisors for P2-L2 shall brief affected crews on these controls prior to the next blasting event and update the shift handover records. Compliance will be reviewed during the next scheduled safety audit and during ad hoc inspections following any blasting activity that occurs without full containment.
- Reference material: review QS-PROC-07 for process safety expectations and SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-05 for local operating and maintenance procedures when preparing for and performing blasting adjacent to the Ring Rolling system.

Effective date
Effective immediately.

# SB-1025 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Hazard description
- Overview: Recent inspections and incident trend analysis identify an elevated quench oil fire risk associated with the radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P1-L1-RR01. The primary mechanism is oil ingress to the hot work zone followed by contact with heated surfaces and ignition. Contributing factors include oil leaks, excessive oil carryover from roll surfaces, degraded oil quality, and inadequate housekeeping in the quench and transfer zones.
- Failure modes: Oil that accumulates on machine housings, guards, or roll surfaces can reach ignition temperature when exposed to hot billets, frictional heating, or nearby radiant heat sources. Restricted drain paths or contaminated sump screens allow oil to pool near heat sources. Inadequate ventilation increases local temperature and delays dispersion of vapors.
- Consequences: Fire involving quench oil can rapidly spread to adjacent equipment, compromise structural guards, and endanger personnel during shift change or maintenance activities. Secondary risks include smoke inhalation, loss of process capability, and extended downtime while fire damage is remediated.

Affected equipment
- Scope: The controls in this bulletin apply to EQ-P1-L1-RR01 located in Plant P1, line P1-L1. Referenced maintenance and operating procedures for this equipment are MM-P1-L1-RR01, SOP-P1-L1-04, and SOP-P1-L1-05.
- Components of concern: Quench tank(s), quench oil delivery lines, roll housings, bearings adjacent to the quench zone, transfer conveyors, splash shields, and local ventilation systems. The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill EQ-P1-L1-RR01 is 120 hours. Lubrication practices that permit excess oil to escape toward the quench zone are a primary focus.
- Past observations: Inspections revealed oil wicking along bearing seals into lower housings and oil film on roll collars that transfers to the quench area during loading. Housekeeping records show accumulation of oily rags and dust in vicinity of the quench tank at several recent walkdowns; refer to MM-P1-L1-RR01 for inspection checklists.

Required controls
- Immediate controls (apply immediately): 
  - Stopwork rule in the quench area if visible oil pooling or active oil leaks are observed. Personnel must notify supervision and tag equipment out until corrected.
  - Increase frequency of visual inspection for oil carryover along roll collars and housings during shift turnover and before hot work. Use the inspection checklist in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to document condition and actions taken.
- Engineering and administrative controls:
  - Implement oil containment and drainage improvements to prevent pooling near hot zones. Ensure drain paths lead to closed sumps and are free of debris; use the containment guidance in SOP-P1-L1-04.
  - Apply drip shields or splash guards on bearing housings and delivery lines to deflect stray oil away from hot surfaces. Maintain shields per SOP-P1-L1-05.
  - Review lubrication practices that result in excess oil application. For EQ-P1-L1-RR01, adhere to the specified main roll bearing lubrication interval of 120 hours and follow the lubrication steps in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to avoid over-application.
  - Control ignition sources by enforcing hot surface clearance and restricting hot work permits in adjacent zones. Coordinate with the permit issuing authority per SOP-P1-L1-04.
  - Ensure ventilation in the quench zone is operating nominally and filters or ducts are not clogged; include ventilation checks in the pre-shift inspection list.
- Training and PPE:
  - Conduct targeted toolbox talks for operators and maintenance staff on recognizing early signs of oil migration and safe isolation of quench oil systems. Include examples drawn from MM-P1-L1-RR01.
  - Ensure fire-resistant PPE and appropriate extinguishing equipment for oil fires are available at designated stations and that staff are trained in their use in accordance with site procedures.
- Monitoring and verification:
  - Use the inspection and repair log in MM-P1-L1-RR01 to record leak discovery, corrective actions, and verification checks. Entries must include observed condition, corrective action taken, and name of individual performing the work.
  - Maintenance planning must incorporate adherence to the 120 hours lubrication interval. Scheduling records shall reference MM-P1-L1-RR01 and be available for audit.
  - Conduct a focused safety audit after implementation of controls and again at regular intervals to verify effectiveness as described in SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and step rationale
- Why controls are required: Quench oils are hydrocarbon-based and present a flammable liquid hazard when placed in contact with hot surfaces or dispersed as vapor in confined hot zones. Preventing oil migration and accumulation is more effective than relying solely on fire response, because prevention reduces probability of ignition and scope of exposure.
- Rationale for lubrication interval emphasis: Ensuring the main roll bearings on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 follow the documented lubrication interval of 120 hours and proper application technique reduces the likelihood of over-lubrication that can lead to oil escape into the quench zone. Corrective action focuses on technique, containment, and inspection rather than arbitrary increases in lubrication frequency.

Examples and practical notes
- Example inspection entry: "Quench sump screen cleared; small oil film on lower roll collar observed; applied containment shield and wiped film per SOP-P1-L1-05; notified maintenance and scheduled bearing lubrication per MM-P1-L1-RR01."
- Example corrective action: Temporary drip shield installed and oil supply line clamp replaced; leak sealed and area cleaned using absorbents; repair recorded in MM-P1-L1-RR01.
- Avoid using loose rags for oil cleanup. Place used absorbents in sealed containers and dispose per waste handling procedure referenced in MM-P1-L1-RR01.

Records to keep
- Inspection logs maintained under MM-P1-L1-RR01 documenting pre-shift checks, discovery of oil accumulation, and corrective actions.
- Lubrication schedule and service records showing adherence to the 120 hours interval for the main roll bearing on EQ-P1-L1-RR01.
- Training attendance records and toolbox talk sign-in sheets referencing SOP-P1-L1-04 and SOP-P1-L1-05.
- Repair and audit reports demonstrating completion of engineering controls and verification checks; retain records in the equipment file for EQ-P1-L1-RR01.

Effective date
- Effective: immediately upon issuance of this bulletin. All affected personnel shall implement the required controls without delay and document actions in the records specified above.
