# SB-1048 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

## Hazard description
Airborne dust generated by dry media blasting operations can present inhalation hazards, combustible dust risks in confined zones, and surface contamination that impacts downstream heat treat performance. Recent observations on P2, line P2-L4 blasting stations show fugitive dust migrating into adjacent work zones and into the heat treat room serving EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Airborne particulates from blasting can adhere to workpieces and furnace internals, increasing the potential for furnace contamination and creating maintenance burdens. In addition, increased particulate loading on filters and ventilation elements raises the risk of unexpected service interruptions and degraded air quality for personnel.

Background: Blasting is a necessary pre-heat-treat cleaning step on P2, line P2-L4 to remove scale and prepare surfaces for treatment in EQ-P2-L4-HT02. However, when blasting containment and local extraction controls fail or are insufficient, dust can escape the blast booth envelope and accumulate where it creates safety and process-control issues. This bulletin addresses controls to limit airborne dust exposure and to prevent migration into EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

Rationale: Controlling dust at source reduces inhalation exposure, minimizes combustible dust layering, and preserves heat treat furnace integrity. Mitigation measures also lower long-term maintenance and downtime by preventing abrasive or reactive dust from entering furnace load paths.

Applicable documents: ECN-2026-020, MM-P2-L4-HT02, SOP-P2-L4-03

## Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P2-L4-HT02 (Heat Treat furnace number two serving line P2-L4)  
Stations: All blasting booths and work cells on P2, line P2-L4 that perform dry media blasting prior to furnace loading.  
Supporting: Local ventilation units and exhaust ducts adjacent to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 and blast booths; material staging areas between blasting and heat treat operations.

Lubricant specification: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-426.

Examples of affected scenarios:
- Workpiece moved from a blasting booth on P2, line P2-L4 into the staging area adjacent to EQ-P2-L4-HT02 without interim cleaning or control, resulting in visible dust transfer onto furnace load carts.
- Dust accumulation on exterior furnace doors and seals of EQ-P2-L4-HT02 leading to increased sealing wear and ingress of particulates into the furnace chamber.
- Extraction failures in booths that allow plume escape into the work environment in the vicinity of EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

## Required controls
Engineering controls
- Verify containment integrity of all blasting booths on P2, line P2-L4. Booth doors, seals, and curtain interfaces must prevent visible leakage of dust to adjacent zones.
- Confirm functioning of local exhaust ventilation for blast booths and neighboring areas; ensure duct routing prevents re-entrainment toward EQ-P2-L4-HT02.
- Install or verify existing capture ventilation at the loading interface between blasting stations and the staging area that leads into EQ-P2-L4-HT02.

Administrative controls
- Implement a staging protocol for parts moving from blasting to EQ-P2-L4-HT02: parts must be placed on a designated cleaned surface and visually inspected for residual dust prior to transfer to furnace loading carts.
- Require operators to follow SOP-P2-L4-03 for pre-heat treat staging and handling on P2, line P2-L4. Deviations must be documented and routed per ECN-2026-020 when they affect process flow.
- Use line-side checklists referenced in MM-P2-L4-HT02 for furnace servicing and cleaning to ensure lubricant and maintenance actions for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 use the specified lubricant part number CFW-LUB-426 and that surface contamination risks are evaluated before furnace access.

Personal protective equipment
- Ensure blasting operators and receiving personnel wear approved respiratory protection whenever visual dust is present in the breathing zone, per site respiratory protection program. Respirator selection and fit verification are governed by site program requirements.

Housekeeping and cleaning
- Clean staging surfaces and load carts prior to placing parts destined for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Use HEPA-filtered vacuums or wet-clean methods; avoid dry sweeping that re-entrains dust.
- Maintain records of cleaning actions for staging areas and load carts as part of the records listed below.

Monitoring and response
- Conduct visual monitoring of blast booths and staging areas during operation shifts. If visible dust migration toward EQ-P2-L4-HT02 is observed, pause transfers and implement corrective actions identified in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Escalate persistent or recurring dust migration issues to maintenance using MM-P2-L4-HT02 as the maintenance reference and to process engineering per ECN-2026-020 for potential design changes.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for verifying booth containment: preventing escape at the source reduces load on downstream controls and prevents furnace contamination, preserving part quality and reducing time spent on corrective cleaning.
- Example: If blast curtain overlap is found to gap at the lower edge during visual inspection, secure temporary sealing until permanent repair via MM-P2-L4-HT02 is scheduled through the normal maintenance request flow.
- Rationale for staging inspections: small particulate loads that are not noticeable during blasting can transfer into furnace loads and plate out on furnace internals, causing hot spots or surface staining. A brief inspection step at staging is a low-effort control that prevents higher-cost corrective actions.

Records to keep
- Staging inspection logs for transfers from blasting to furnace staging. Include operator name and description of action taken if residual dust was found.
- Booth containment and ventilation check records, maintained as part of the preventative maintenance files referenced in MM-P2-L4-HT02.
- Cleaning action records for staging surfaces and loading carts, with method used (HEPA vacuum or wet-clean) and operator initials.
- Any deviations or process changes routed per ECN-2026-020 and any SOP exceptions tracked against SOP-P2-L4-03.

Roles and responsibilities
- Operators: follow SOP-P2-L4-03 and perform staging inspections and cleaning prior to furnace loading.
- Maintenance: address containment and ventilation defects using MM-P2-L4-HT02 procedures and ensure EQ-P2-L4-HT02 lubrication uses CFW-LUB-426 as specified.
- Supervisors: ensure training and checklist completion, and escalate design or persistent issues to engineering via ECN-2026-020.

## Effective date
Effective immediately.
title: Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

# SB-1049 Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Hazard description
- During die change operations on radial ring rolling mill EQ-P2-L2-RR03, exposed moving components near the die area create significant pinch point hazards. Typical work tasks include die extraction/insertion, adjustment of die clamps, and alignment of workpieces. These activities frequently bring operator hands and tools into close proximity with rotating and reciprocating interfaces where uncontrolled movement or stored energy can result in crushing or amputation injuries.
- Contributing factors observed in recent near-miss reports include inadequate blocking of machine motion, incomplete isolation of drive sources, manual holding of heavy parts during lift and transfer, and work performed in constrained stances that limit escape from an unexpected movement. Loose tooling, damaged die handling attachments, and slippery surfaces around the die change zone increase the risk that a part will shift unexpectedly and trap an operator.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Maintenance and lubrication planning must account for access and safe work practices during lubrication and associated maintenance tasks, as failures in routine maintenance can increase the likelihood of unplanned movement during die change.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P2-L2-RR03 (radial ring rolling mill). The die change envelope on this machine includes the die sets, clamp assemblies, roll housings, and any interlinked handling fixtures used to position dies.
- Ancillary: die handling carts, hoists and balance arms used in the die area, local guarding assemblies, and any temporary blocking or cribbing used during die change activities.
- Applicable maintenance and operating procedures: MM-P2-L2-RR03 and MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2. Review these procedures prior to conducting die change activities for machine-specific requirements and allowed handling methods.
- Relevant safety precedent and prior bulletins: SB-1017.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Maintain and verify all fixed guards and interlocks that prevent access to the die change envelope while the main drive or auxiliary motion sources are enabled. Where guards are removed for die change, provide temporary physical barriers or presence-sensing devices that maintain a defined safe perimeter.
- Use mechanical die support fixtures that lock in place and prevent uncontrolled vertical or lateral movement of die components. Fixtures must be rated for the expected mass and must fully support dies without reliance on manual holding.
- Ensure hoists and balance arms are secured with secondary restraints during transfers into the die change envelope. Where chain slings, straps, or shackles are used, inspect them for wear and secure attachment before lifting.

Administrative controls
- Before beginning a die change, perform a documented pre-task risk assessment using the forms and checklists in MM-P2-L2-RR03. The assessment must verify isolation of energy sources, availability of support fixtures, and assignment of roles (lead operator, spotter, and maintainer).
- Execute lockout-tagout and energy isolation per MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 for all electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic sources that could generate motion. Verify isolation through attempt-to-start procedures described in MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2.
- Use a two-person minimum team for all die changes on EQ-P2-L2-RR03: one person to control the lifting/handling device and a second trained observer/spotter to monitor pinch point exposure and communicate. The spotter is responsible for immediate stoppage if a hazardous condition develops.
- Restrict access to the die change area to trained personnel only and post signage during active die change operations.

Personal protective equipment and behavior
- Require cut-resistant gloves and impact protection suitable for heavy handling tasks. Ensure gloves allow sufficient dexterity to handle fasteners and alignment tools without placing fingers in pinch zones.
- Train personnel to keep hands and their tools outside the defined die change envelope except when secured and protected by fixtures. Emphasize using alignment tools that keep hands at a distance rather than fingers or palms for alignment.
- Enforce a strict housekeeping standard: keep the die change work area free of loose tools and debris that can contribute to slips or sudden shifts of parts.

Step rationale and examples
- Lockout-tagout and attempt-to-start verification directly address the root cause of many pinch injuries, which is unexpected energization or stored energy release. The procedures in MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 provide machine-specific steps to ensure isolation; following those steps reduces the probability of unintended movement.
- Two-person operations with a designated spotter reduce cognitive load on the operator performing lifts and provide an additional set of eyes to detect incipient hazards such as shifting loads or misalignment of fixtures.
- Use of locking mechanical supports prevents reliance on manual holding during critical phases of transport and alignment. An example: when removing a die set from EQ-P2-L2-RR03, the die should be landed on a certified support cradle and secured before any clamps are released. This prevents the die from dropping or tilting and creating a pinch point between the die edge and the roll housing.

Records to keep
- Complete the die change checklist from MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 for every die change and retain the completed checklist in the machine logbook. The checklist documents isolation, fixture verification, personnel present, and post-change verification steps.
- Log all inspections and maintenance actions performed on die handling fixtures and hoists in the equipment maintenance record as stipulated in MM-P2-L2-RR03.
- Record any deviation, near miss, or incident associated with die changes in the site safety incident register and notify the line safety coordinator for review and follow-up actions. Cross-reference these entries to SB-1017 where similar hazards were addressed.

Effective date
- Effective upon publication. All personnel working on or around EQ-P2-L2-RR03 must implement the required controls prior to the next scheduled die change. Review MM-P2-L2-RR03 and MM-P2-L2-RR03-S2 for procedure details and SB-1017 for related guidance.
title: Safety bulletin: pinch points during die change

text:
# SB-1050 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy associated with the induction billet heater coil cooling and billet handling systems presents a risk of sudden unintended motion, fluid injection, and contact with energized components. Loss of coil cooling flow or failure in the cooling circuit can lead to rapid pressure transients in associated hydraulic utilities and actuators that are downstream of isolation devices. These transients can displace components, expel fluid from fittings, and cause pinch, crush, or injection injuries to personnel working on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Additionally, inadequate coil cooling performance can cause reactive valve and actuator behavior that defeats interlocks and permits unexpected movement of billet handling fixtures.

Background and rationale
Recent inspections and engineering change notices have identified scenarios where cooling flow reduction allowed elevated forces to develop in associated systems. The coil loop on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 is a common-mode element: it interfaces with cooling supply, return, leak detection, and control valves. Loss of sufficient coil cooling flow can alter dynamics in the hydraulic support systems and may make stored energy in accumulators, supply lines, and actuator chambers available for work. This bulletin consolidates controls and clarifies responsibilities to reduce personnel exposure to stored hydraulic energy when performing maintenance, inspection, and adjustment tasks on EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

For clarity and to support verification, the following mandatory specification is declared: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and all ancillary cooling and hydraulic circuits that connect directly to or provide support functions to EQ-P3-L1-IH03.  
- Billet handling fixtures and actuators that rely on the induction heater cooling circuit for safe operation.  
- Electrical and control panels housing valve drives and interlock logic that reference coil cooling flow status.

Required controls
Engineering controls and administrative measures listed below are required whenever work is performed on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

- Monitoring and verification
  - Before any work that could expose personnel to moving parts or hydraulic interfaces, verify coil cooling flow at the established minimum. Record the verification in the work or maintenance record. Use the plant-approved flow measurement device tied to the cooling loop. Reference SOP-P3-L1-01 for acceptable verification steps and required record fields.
  - If measured flow is below the stated minimum, do not start or continue work until flow is restored to meet or exceed the declared minimum.

- Isolation and release of stored energy
  - Where maintenance requires exposure of hydraulic lines, actuators, or fittings, isolate hydraulic supplies in accordance with MM-P3-L1-IH03. Depressurize and lockout sources of hydraulic energy per MM-P3-L1-IH03 procedure steps before opening any hydraulic circuit.
  - Verify zero energy state locally at the workpiece; the person performing the work must confirm lack of stored pressure or movement and document the verification.

- Physical restraints and safety devices
  - Apply mechanical blocks, restraints, or positive supports to prevent uncommanded motion of fixtures or billets when hydraulic restraint is removed. Select restraint methods consistent with MM-P3-L1-IH03 guidance.
  - Maintain control of fittings and hoses; where hoses must be disconnected, use drip containment and protective barriers to avoid fluid injection into work zones.

- Administrative controls
  - All work on EQ-P3-L1-IH03 that may expose personnel to stored hydraulic energy requires a documented job hazard analysis and a competent person designated to verify isolation steps. Include a clear re-energization checklist that references restoration of coil cooling flow to the declared minimum.
  - Training: personnel assigned to work on or near EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be trained to recognize hazards from stored hydraulic energy and to use the required lockout/tagout and verification methods in SOP-P3-L1-01 and MM-P3-L1-IH03.

Examples and scenarios
- Example scenario A: A maintenance task requires removal of a hydraulic actuator cover. Prior to work, the technician follows SOP-P3-L1-01 to confirm coil cooling flow meets the minimum. After confirmation, hydraulic supply is isolated and depressurized per MM-P3-L1-IH03. Mechanical blocks are installed. Work proceeds with the competent person maintaining the documented verification.
- Example scenario B: During inspection, an operator observes reduced coil cooling flow. The operator records the condition, tags the equipment out of service under SOP-P3-L1-01, and escalates to maintenance engineering using the escalation path described in ECN-2026-006 to address root causes prior to any personnel exposure to hydraulic interfaces.

Records to keep
- Flow verification records: include name of verifier, equipment id, measured flow indicator readout or instrument identification, reference to this bulletin, and signature. Store these records with the maintenance order and attach to equipment history.
- Isolation checklists and zero-energy verification forms: completed and signed forms must be filed with the work order and retained as part of the plant maintenance archive per MM-P3-L1-IH03.
- Training and qualification records: document personnel who completed the required training and are authorized to perform or verify work associated with EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Reference SOP-P3-L1-01 for curriculum requirements.
- Incident and abnormal condition reports: any deviation from the declared coil cooling flow minimum or any event where stored hydraulic energy resulted in unexpected motion must be reported and investigated using ECN-2026-006.

Responsibilities
- Maintenance supervisors: ensure compliance with isolation and verification procedures and that records are completed and filed.
- Operators: monitor coil cooling flow and take equipment out of service if the minimum is not met; initiate required notifications.
- Engineering: evaluate root causes of recurrent low flow conditions and implement corrective changes as documented in ECN-2026-006.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon issue. All affected personnel must comply with the controls herein and update local procedures and checklists to reference SB-1050 and the citation documents SOP-P3-L1-01, MM-P3-L1-IH03, and ECN-2026-006.
title: Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

text:
# QS-CFW-3043-62 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-3043-62 (4140) Rev D

Plant: P1  
Part: CFW-3043-62

Scope
This quality specification defines the metallurgical and dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for flange blank CFW-3043-62 produced from 4140 material at Plant P1. It is intended for use by forging, heat treat, machining, quality, and shipping personnel to ensure consistent part quality and traceability through production. Background rationale is provided to explain why each requirement is controlled and how inspection records shall be maintained. This document applies to all production lots of flange blank CFW-3043-62 and to material received for processing that will be converted to that part.

Requirements table
The table below lists the controlled characteristics, the acceptance criteria, and the required record to be retained with the lot traveler.

| Characteristic | Acceptance criterion | Record to retain |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 per purchase specification | Mill certificate attached to lot traveler |
| Hardness (through-thickness, final condition) | The hardness range for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 37-43 HRC. | Hardness test report with location map |
| Bore diameter tolerance (as-formed) | The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is ±0.04 mm. | Dimensional inspection report showing measured bore and nominal |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-3043-62 (CFW-3043-62) is 28.1 kg. | Forging log with actual gross and net weights recorded |
| Surface condition | Free from forge laps, cold shuts, and cracks that penetrate inspection acceptance depth | Visual inspection report |
| Traceability | Each blank must be marked with lot identifier and included on traveler | Marking record and traveler |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Take hardness measurements on each representative blank following a defined sampling plan. Measure at locations that represent critical section changes and the bore ID; provide a location map on the report. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale and technique for through-thickness evaluation. Report individual readings and the location map; record any outlier and its disposition. The hardness data shall be filed with the lot documentation.
- Rationale: Hardness controls are used to confirm heat treatment and material condition; the specified hardness range reduces risk of premature wear or excessive brittleness while preserving toughness for subsequent machining and service.

Dimensional inspection
- Verify the bore diameter at the specified critical plane(s) using a calibrated bore gauge or micrometric method that provides the resolution required to demonstrate compliance with the stated tolerance. Record the nominal dimension and the measured size for each inspected blank on the dimensional inspection report.
- Examples:
  - For a blank measured at the critical bore plane, list nominal, measured, and deviation. Indicate compliance when deviation is within the stated tolerance. Nonconforming bores shall be segregated and submitted for disposition.
- Rationale: Tight bore control minimizes rework and ensures fitment in assembly. The bore tolerance is set to accommodate downstream machining allowances and to control concentricity requirements.

Weight control
- Record forging weight for each blank immediately after the primary forging operation. Compare the recorded weight to the maximum forging weight specified. Blanks exceeding the maximum forging weight shall be quarantined for review.
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure die life, press capacity, and handling safety; it also identifies potential material or process deviations.

Surface and visual inspection
- Perform visual and tactile inspection under adequate lighting for surface defects. Mark and document areas of concern on the part sketch. Small, non-penetrating surface irregularities may be eligible for repair by approved grinding procedures; deeper defects require engineering disposition.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement instruments used for hardness, bore, and weight verification must be calibrated and traceable to national standards. Calibration records shall be available for audit.

Sampling and acceptance
- Sampling for destructive and nondestructive tests shall follow the plant’s sampling procedure. Acceptance is based on the requirements table. Material that meets all listed criteria shall be released with the lot traveler; material that fails any criterion shall follow the nonconformance handling procedure below.

Records to keep
- Mill certificate for material grade.  
- Hardness test report with location map and individual readings.  
- Dimensional inspection report showing nominal, measured, and deviation values for the bore.  
- Forging log showing recorded forging weight and operator initials.  
- Visual inspection report and marked part sketch for any surface findings.  
- Calibration certificates for instruments used.  
- Traveler indicating lot identifier and final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any blank found outside the acceptance criteria in the requirements table shall be clearly identified, marked, and segregated from acceptable material. The lot traveler must be annotated to indicate the nonconforming status and the nature of the failure.

Disposition and review
- The quality engineer shall evaluate nonconforming blanks and propose one of the following dispositions: repair, rework, or scrap. Repair must follow an approved engineering repair instruction and be documented explicitly on the traveler. Rework that affects controlled dimensions or material condition requires reinspection to the original acceptance criteria prior to release.

Root cause and corrective action
- For any nonconformance, initiate a cause analysis to determine source of failure. Document containment and corrective action in the plant quality system records. Examples of typical corrective actions include adjustments to forging operation, maintenance on tooling, or changes in heat treat practice; all corrective actions must be validated to prevent recurrence.

Disposition records
- Maintain a complete record of nonconformance, investigation, disposition, and verification of corrective action with the lot documentation. Records shall include the nonconformance description, photos if applicable, calculated deviations, disposition decision, and signatures of the responsible personnel.

Review and release
- Final release of a lot to shipping requires closure of all nonconformance records and completion of required inspections listed in this document. The lot traveler, with attached test and inspection reports, shall be retained as the permanent record for traceability.

# QS-CFW-5798-88 Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5798-88

Scope
This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340) produced at Plant P2. It defines critical acceptance criteria, the prescribed inspection methods, and the nonconformance handling process for material and dimensional requirements specific to the crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88. This document is mandatory for production, first article, incoming material verification, and final inspection activities associated with part CFW-5798-88.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks are safety and performance critical forgings. Control of hardness, bore geometry, and weight is essential to ensure downstream machinability, heat treat response, and handling during machining and assembly. The criteria in this specification reflect metallurgical and process capability limits derived from engineering design and forging process constraints. Inspecting these features at the blank stage prevents costly scrap and rework later in the manufacturing flow.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Material identification | Must be 4340 forging for CFW-5798-88 | Traceable material certification required | Certification must reference part CFW-5798-88 |
| Hardness | Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | 25-29 HRC | Hardness measured as specified in inspection method |
| Bore diameter | Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | ±0.09 mm | Applies to all machined bore features on blank |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | 119.4 kg | Weigh each forging and record value |

Inspection method
General
All inspections shall be performed by trained personnel using calibrated equipment. Calibration records must be current and traceable to national or internal standards. Reference the plant calibration control process for detailed calibration intervals and methods.

Hardness measurement
Select a representative sample from each production lot for hardness testing. Hardness shall be measured using appropriate Rockwell C scale methodology and indenter type consistent with the hardness range in the requirements table. Take readings on the forging surface areas designated for raw blank hardness checks, avoiding quenched or distorted zones. Record individual readings and compute lot disposition based on the range requirement Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 25-29 HRC. If hardness readings vary within the lot, follow the nonconformance handling steps.

Bore diameter measurement
Inspect bore geometry using a bore gauge or coordinate measurement method appropriate for blind and through bores on the blank. The acceptance criterion is Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is ±0.09 mm. Measure at defined locations along the bore axis to identify taper and out-of-round conditions. Record nominal diameter and deviation from nominal for each measured bore feature. For example, record the measured value and the deviation relative to nominal, and mark parts that exceed the permitted deviation for segregation.

Weight verification
Weigh each finished forging on a calibrated industrial scale. Compare the measured mass to Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 119.4 kg. Forgings that exceed the maximum forging weight shall be segregated and placed into nonconforming disposition until reviewed by engineering. Record the as-weighed mass and operator initials on the inspection record.

Sampling and lot disposition
Apply sampling where lot quantities are produced by a single heat and die set. Use inspection sampling practices consistent with plant quality procedures. If any sampled item fails to meet the requirements table criteria, escalate to full lot inspection. Document all inspection data in the quality record for the lot.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Any crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 that does not meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be immediately identified and segregated from acceptable inventory. Mark nonconforming material clearly and apply a nonconformance tag referencing this document and the inspection record.

Containment and evaluation
Containment actions shall prevent inadvertent use of nonconforming crankshaft blanks. The lot or individual pieces shall be evaluated by quality engineering in coordination with production and metallurgical engineering. Evaluation shall determine whether rework, reheat, documentation waiver, or scrap is appropriate. Examples of evaluation outcomes include metallurgical investigation for hardness out of range, dimensional analysis for bore deviations, and mass reconciliation for weight excess.

Disposition
Dispositions may include rework, reheat and re-inspect, use-as-is with documented engineering waiver, or scrap. Engineering waivers shall be documented with justification, risk assessment, and end item impact statement. Waivers require approval by authorized engineering personnel. Any rework or reprocessing must be performed under controlled instructions and re-inspected using the inspection method above to confirm conformance to the requirements table.

Records to keep
Retain the following records with lot traceability:
- Material certification linking heat lot to part CFW-5798-88.
- Hardness test records showing individual readings and lot summary demonstrating compliance with Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 25-29 HRC.
- Bore measurement records listing measured values and deviations demonstrating compliance with Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is ±0.09 mm.
- Weighing records showing measured mass and confirmation of Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 119.4 kg.
- Nonconformance reports, containment evidence, engineering evaluations, and final dispositions.

Audit and review
Quality shall periodically review inspection records for trends indicating process drift. Findings that indicate recurring nonconformance shall trigger corrective action and process improvement activities in accordance with Plant P2 quality procedures.

End of document.

# QS-CFW-1476-90 - Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (1045)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1476-90

## Scope
This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treat verification, machining acceptance, and final inspection of connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) produced at Plant P3. It defines mandatory acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for delivered parts and in-process lots. This document covers dimensional control of the rod bore, material hardness confirmation, and verification that the forging weight does not exceed the permitted maximum.

Background: The connecting rod is manufactured from 1045 material and processed through standard forging and heat treatment flows controlled by Plant P3 process instructions. Tight control of bore geometry and core hardness is required to meet service durability and press-fit assembly requirements. Controlling forging mass prevents die overloading and ensures thermal and metallurgical consistency.

Rationale: The specified acceptance limits were determined from design requirements and field service data to balance fatigue life, assembly clearance, and manufacturability. The bore tolerance ensures reliable fitment to mating components. The hardness band controls core strength without inducing excessive brittleness. The maximum forging weight protects tooling and process stability.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Part identification | CFW-1476-90 |
| Hardness (core, post-heat-treat) | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 35-39 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is ±0.03 mm. |
| Forging mass limit | The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 48.9 kg. |
| Traceability | Each lot must be retained with process route and inspection records in the quality record system for review. |

Notes on table entries: All acceptance decisions are based on measured values compared directly to the listed requirements. Where multiple bores are present on a single rod, each bore must meet the bore diameter tolerance entry. Hardness measurements must represent core condition after the final heat treatment process and prior to any final machining that alters microstructure. Forging mass is to be verified upon removal from the press and before heat treatment to confirm tooling and process stability.

## Inspection method
Visual and dimensional inspection is to be performed in a controlled inspection area following the plant inspection procedures. Use calibrated instruments appropriate to the measurement; calibration records must be current and available with the inspection records.

Hardness verification: Hardness shall be verified on a representative surface that reflects core material condition after heat treatment. Use a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated for the relevant scale. Verify indenter condition and machine calibration prior to testing. Record raw hardness readings and the averaged value for each sample in the inspection record. Compare the averaged value directly to the hardness requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 35-39 HRC.

Bore diameter verification: Bore diameter inspection shall be performed using bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment that deliver resolution sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the stated tolerance. Measurement technique must avoid deformation of the bore during verification. For bores that require gauging, use feeler and gauge methods that preserve surface finish. Record each bore measurement and identify the seated condition. Compare recorded bore diameters to the requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is ±0.03 mm.

Forging mass verification: Verify forging mass on a calibrated mass measurement device capable of accepting the part. Measure each forging prior to heat treatment to confirm it does not exceed the mass limit. Record the measured mass adjacent to the lot identifier in the inspection record. Compare directly to the specified limit: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (CFW-1476-90) is 48.9 kg.

Sampling rationale: Sampling shall represent the production variation and process risk for the lot. Inspectors should select parts from across the lot to capture potential process drift. For lots exhibiting low variation in upstream process records, reduced verification density may be applied on an agreed basis between quality and production, with records documenting the rationale.

Examples:
- If hardness readings cluster narrowly within the range, record the individual results and mark the lot as accepted. If any reading falls outside the range, proceed to nonconformance handling.
- If a bore diameter measurement exceeds the ±0.03 mm tolerance in any dimension relative to nominal, mark the part nonconforming and follow containment steps.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test logs including raw readings, tester calibration certificate reference, operator initials, and part identifiers.
- Bore measurement logs including gauge identifiers, measurement method note, raw measurements, and operator initials.
- Forging mass log showing measured mass, scale calibration certificate reference, and part identifier.
- Lot route card showing processing steps, heat treat parameters reference, and operator acknowledgements.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition documents when applicable.

All records must be entered into the quality record system and linked to the lot or serial identifier for the product.

## Nonconformance handling
Containment: Any part that fails to meet the hardness, bore diameter tolerance, or forging mass requirement must be segregated immediately and clearly labeled as nonconforming. Notify quality engineering and production leadership to initiate investigation.

Disposition options: Quality engineering shall evaluate failed parts for potential rework or scrap. Rework possibilities include controlled machining when dimensional excess allows compliant restoration without violating material property requirements. Hardness failures shall not be corrected by localized heat input without prior approval from materials engineering. Forgings that exceed the maximum forging weight require process review and may be rejected for the lot if tooling or process correction is necessary.

Root cause and corrective action: Perform root cause analysis for any nonconformance that is systemic or repeated. Document findings, corrective actions, and verification steps in the nonconformance report. Apply process controls and operator training as required to prevent recurrence.

Example nonconformance workflow:
- Segregate affected parts.
- Record failure on nonconformance form and attach inspection records that show the deviation.
- Perform detailed review to determine whether rework is feasible without compromising part integrity.
- Implement corrective action and monitor subsequent lots to verify effectiveness.

Escalation: For any out-of-spec condition that could impact safety or field performance, escalate immediately to the plant quality manager for disposition and notification to stakeholders.

Record retention: Maintain all associated records in the quality record system as required by Plant P3 record retention practice. Records shall include inspection data, calibration references, nonconformance reports, and disposition paperwork to provide full traceability for the life of the product.

End of document.
title: Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-1476-90 (1045)

# QS-CFW-3173-95 Quality specification - gear blank CFW-3173-95 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-3173-95

Scope
- This quality specification defines the metallurgical, dimensional, and inspection acceptance criteria for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) produced in Plant P1. It applies to all forged deliveries of the part number listed above and to internal transfers for machining and heat treatment. The specification focuses on requirements necessary to ensure downstream gear manufacture and service performance for forged 8620 material supplied as blank form.

Background and rationale
- The requirements are derived from service load considerations for gears and from historical process capability for the forging and rough-bore operations. The hardness requirement balances core toughness and surface strength after subsequent heat treatment and machining. The bore tolerance supports accurate mounting and minimizes rework at the machining center. The maximum forging weight is controlled to match press capacity and tooling design limits; exceeding this weight risks improper die fill and dimensional deviation.
- Examples: A blank that meets the hardness requirement but has a bore outside tolerance will be rejected for machining because it can induce runout in finish gear cutting. A blank within bore tolerance but above the maximum forging weight will be segregated to prevent damage to press tooling and die alignment.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chemical / material | 8620 forging charge per material control records | Material certificate must accompany each lot. |
| Hardness (core, as-forged or post-forging, pre-heat-treat if applicable) | The hardness range for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 37-43 HRC. | Measured on cross-section surface prepared per Inspection Method. Readings outside this range are nonconforming. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm. | Tolerance applies to nominal bore dimension indicated on manufacturing drawing. Measurement method per Inspection Method. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg. | Weight recorded on heat/lot tag. Blanks exceeding this weight are nonconforming for die and press capacity reasons. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and metal flow interruptions that affect machinability | Visual and tactile inspection criteria per Inspection Method. |

Inspection method
- Sample selection: Inspect all first-piece blanks from a new billet lot and then sample per lot transfer records. Maintain lot traceability on the heat/lot tag with forging weight recorded.
- Hardness measurement:
  - Prepare a representative cross-section by removing scale and cleaning the test surface to expose metal. Use a Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Ensure indent locations avoid surface decarburization and are at a consistent depth from the as-forged surface as practical.
  - Record each reading with the lot identifier and operator initials. The lot is conforming only if recorded readings fall within The hardness range for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 37-43 HRC.
- Bore measurement:
  - Use calibrated bore gauges compatible with the bore feature. Measure at multiple circumferential positions to detect out-of-round. Record the nominal dimension and tolerance and verify The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm.
  - If the bore is produced as a rough-bore during forging, ensure the recorded rough-bore dimensions allow final machining within tolerance; otherwise, segregate the part.
- Weight verification:
  - Weigh each forged blank on a calibrated scale and record the value on the heat/lot tag and inspection record. Verify that the recorded value does not exceed The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg.
- Surface and visual inspection:
  - Inspect for forging defects that could compromise machinability or performance. Document findings and photograph any suspect areas referenced to the lot tag.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation and identification:
  - Any blank failing the hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum forging weight requirements must be immediately segregated and tagged with a nonconformance tag referencing this document id.
- Disposition options and rationale:
  - Hardness out of range: Evaluate whether the deviation is due to surface decarburization or process variation. If the nonconformance is surface-limited and removable by machining without compromising part geometry or subsequent treatments, document the evaluation and the agreed disposition with quality engineering; otherwise, reject the part for return to melt/remanufacture.
  - Bore out of tolerance: Reject for machining; if the deviation is minor and documented evidence shows downstream machining can restore compliance without reducing fatigue life or functional fit, a documented disposition may be approved by quality engineering and process engineering.
  - Weight over maximum forging weight: Reject and prevent shipment. Blanks exceeding The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg must be returned to forging operations for investigation of billet size, forge programming, and die setup adjustments.
- Records to keep:
  - Maintain inspection records for hardness measurements, bore measurements, and weighing with the lot identifier. Keep nonconformance tags and disposition documentation with the lot file. Retain photographic evidence for significant defects and the approval record for any authorized concessions.
- Corrective action:
  - For repeated nonconformances from the same lot source or process step, initiate a formal corrective action to address root cause, including but not limited to forging process setup, material charge control, and equipment calibration. Document actions taken and results, and attach to the lot file.

Traceability and records
- Each blank must retain heat/lot identification from forging through inspection and shipment. Inspection records must reference the lot identifier and be filed in the plant quality system. Records include hardness logs, bore measurement sheets showing The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is ±0.03 mm, weight logs showing The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-3173-95 (CFW-3173-95) is 100.6 kg, and nonconformance documentation where applicable.

End of specification.

# QS-CFW-1466-55 Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (52100)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Part: CFW-1466-55

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 produced in Plant P2 from material grade 52100. It applies to all production forgings, finishing, and final inspection prior to release to assembly or shipment. The intent is to ensure mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy necessary for bearing performance while minimizing false rejects through targeted inspection and documentation.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the critical characteristics and mandatory acceptance criteria for part CFW-1466-55.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material grade | 52100 (as specified on the drawing and order) |
| Hardness | The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 32.2 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cracks, and other defects that compromise machining or function; acceptable machining mark patterns are defined on the drawing. |
| Finish operations | All finishing operations must maintain specified dimensional and metallurgical requirements prior to final inspection. |

Inspection method
- Overview: Final inspection is performed on the finished part after all machining and heat treat operations. Inspection is focused on the characteristics in the requirements table, with emphasis on hardness, bore size, and verification that forging weight did not exceed permitted handling/load limits.

- Hardness verification: Hardness shall be verified using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Perform measurements on machined surfaces representative of the bearing race. Record individual hardness readings and the location of each reading relative to the drawing. When multiple readings are taken on a single ring, report the range and note any local anomalies that indicate inhomogeneity or improper heat treat. Use the recorded data to confirm that the part meets The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC. Calibration status of the hardness tester shall be current and traceable to the laboratory calibration system; calibration records must be retained with the inspection lot documentation.

- Dimensional verification: Bore diameter inspection shall be performed using calibrated bore gauges or equivalent measuring devices capable of resolving to the specification tolerance. Measurement locations must match the drawing characteristic positions. Measure and record bore size, and compare to The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm. If the measured bore is out of tolerance, tag the part as nonconforming and proceed to nonconformance handling. For assemblies that require runout or concentricity checks, perform those checks against the reference surfaces specified on the drawing and document results.

- Weight control: Weigh each forged blank after forging and prior to any material removal operations to ensure handling and tooling limits are respected. The forging process must not produce blanks in excess of The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 32.2 kg. If a blank exceeds this value, it must be segregated and reported as a process deviation; refer to nonconformance handling below.

- Surface and metallurgical checks: Visually inspect for surface discontinuities; use magnification as required for borderline cases. If indications suggest subsurface defects, use accepted non-destructive methods available in P2 to confirm condition. Metallurgical review is required when hardness or visual anomalies are found; document microstructure checks in the inspection record when performed.

- Sampling and lot records: Inspect every finished part for the characteristics in the table. For operations where statistical sampling is used for process control, maintain records that link sampled results to the affected production runs and to the individual parts when deviations occur. Inspection records shall include heat number, hardness readings, bore measurements, forging weight, operator, and inspector signatures or electronic approval, and reference to the drawing revision used for machining.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any part that does not meet the requirements listed in the requirements table is nonconforming. Mark nonconforming parts clearly and segregate them from conforming inventory in a controlled area to prevent unintended use.

- Documentation: For each nonconforming part, complete a nonconformance report that includes part number, serial or batch identifiers where applicable, description of the nonconformity, measured values and locations, responsible operator, and inspector. Attach supporting inspection records, hardness printouts, weight records, and photographs if helpful for root cause assessment.

- Disposition options: Allowed dispositions include rework to drawing tolerances when feasible, use-as-is with documented engineering concession, scrap, or return to forging process for correction. All dispositions require approval by quality and engineering authority designated in Plant P2. Rework proposals must describe the corrective action, the inspection steps to verify compliance, and any impacts on material properties. Concessions granted must include justification and any additional inspection or labeling required to ensure safe use.

- Examples and rationale:
  - Example: If a bore measures outside The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm but material hardness is within the specified range, evaluate whether material removal within drawing limits can restore compliance without compromising section properties. Document the proposed correction and obtain approvals before proceeding.
  - Example: If hardness reading is below The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC., perform a metallurgical assessment and review heat treatment records. Do not return parts to stock until root cause is determined and corrective actions are implemented.

- Records to keep: Retain inspection records, nonconformance reports, disposition approvals, and calibration certificates for tools used in these inspections in the document control system for Plant P2. Records must be sufficient to trace the condition and disposition of each nonconforming part and to support corrective action investigations.

Revision control and note
- This document is controlled as Rev B. Any change to acceptance criteria or inspection methods requires a revision and documented approval through the P2 quality system. Related documents: none.

# QS-CFW-5042-83 Quality specification - valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-5042-83

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forged valve body CFW-5042-83 produced in Plant P3 from material grade F316. It establishes the mandatory acceptance requirements, the required inspection methods, and the process for managing nonconforming items. The purpose is to ensure forged parts meet functional and metallurgical criteria prior to machining and assembly, and that inspection records provide traceability for production and corrective action.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the valve body CFW-5042-83. These attributes are verified at final forge inspection and any subsequent operations that could affect the attribute.

| Attribute | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness range | 33-38 HRC | Hardness measured in the parent forged material, away from finish-machined surfaces. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.06 mm | Applies to the as-forged bore prior to final machining; control dimension for downstream fixtures. |
| Maximum forging weight | 77.3 kg | Net forging weight after flash removal and trimming, prior to heat treat and finish machining. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspection shall be performed by qualified inspection personnel using calibrated instruments appropriate to each attribute. The inspection location is the final forge inspection area prior to heat treatment and machining. Records of inspections shall be retained with the heat lot and forging serial reference.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness testing shall be performed on representative forged surfaces in the parent metal, avoiding areas affected by trimming, heavy deformation, or tooling marks. Test locations shall be documented on the part record. Use a standardized hardness method suitable for HRC scale. Report measured values and note any readings outside the stated hardness range of 33-38 HRC. When borderline readings are encountered, additional tests on adjacent locations are documented until a clear condition is established. All hardness readings, test instrument identification, and calibration references are recorded on the inspection sheet.

Bore diameter verification
- The bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm applies to the as-forged bore prior to machining. Bore inspection is performed with instruments capable of resolving to the tolerance band and set up to verify roundness and concentricity where applicable. Record the measured bore size, measurement method, and instrument identification. If the as-forged bore falls outside ±0.06 mm, the part is treated as nonconforming and handled per the Nonconformance handling section.

Weight confirmation
- Maximum forging weight is recorded after trimming and flash removal and prior to any subsequent heat treatment or machining. The maximum forging weight limit is 77.3 kg. The forging weight is documented on the production record; parts exceeding the maximum forging weight are identified and segregated for review.

Record keeping
- For each inspected lot, records shall include part identification CFW-5042-83, plant P3, heat lot, inspector identity, inspection date and time expressed in local plant format, instrument identifiers, calibration status, measured values for hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight, and any deviation notes. These records are retained in the document control system in association with the forging lot and made available for quality audits and engineering review.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Nonconforming items are controlled to prevent unintended use. Any part that fails to meet one or more requirements in the Requirements table is to be clearly identified and segregated from conforming stock. The nonconforming condition, referring to the specific attribute and measured value, is recorded on the nonconformance tag and the lot record.

Disposition
Disposition options include documented repair, rework, or rejection. Repair and rework actions that could affect metallurgical properties or critical dimensions require engineering review and formal disposition authorization before implementation. For hardness and weight issues, the impact on material properties and downstream processing must be evaluated by engineering. For bore diameter deviations, assess whether corrective machining or rework is practicable without compromising part integrity or functional dimensions after machining.

Examples
- Example: If a part measures below the hardness range of 33-38 HRC, evaluate whether heat treatment variation or material batch condition caused the deviation. Document the investigation and disposition. Record all hardness readings and any corrective actions taken.
- Example: If a part exceeds the maximum forging weight of 77.3 kg after trimming, segregate the part and initiate an investigation into forging parameters and trimming process. Record the measured weight and investigation outcome.

Corrective action and root cause
For repeated or systemic nonconformance, initiate a root cause analysis and corrective action plan. The corrective action record shall reference the affected heat lots and production runs, the measured deviations (as recorded for hardness, bore diameter, or weight), actions taken to prevent recurrence, and verification of effectiveness. All corrective action documentation is linked to the forging lot record.

Disposition authority and records
Only authorized personnel may sign off dispositions. The disposition record shall include the nonconformance description, measured value(s), disposition selected, signatures of reviewer and approver, and references to any engineering approval. Disposition records are maintained with the part history for traceability.

Revision control
This document is controlled under the plant document control system. Changes to inspection methods or acceptance requirements must be approved through the established revision procedure and applied to new production lots only after release.

End of specification.
title: Quality specification - valve body CFW-5042-83 (F316)

# QS-CFW-9852-71 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-9852-71 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-9852-71

Scope
This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treatment acceptance, and final inspection of axle hub CFW-9852-71 manufactured at Plant P1. It defines material acceptance criteria, critical dimensional tolerances, hardness requirements, maximum allowable forging weight for handling and tooling limits, inspection methods, record requirements, and nonconformance handling for production and received forgings. The document is intended for use by process engineers, quality inspectors, production supervisors, and shipping/receiving personnel responsible for CFW-9852-71.

Requirements table
- Part identification: CFW-9852-71 as stamped on routing and inspection records.
- Material: steel specification per internal material control for 4140 forgings.
- Hardness acceptance: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC.
- Critical bore tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 73.0 kg.
- Surface condition: free of laps, seams, and cold shuts that affect fit or function.
- Feature control: all critical features shall conform to the drawing dimensions and tolerances; refer to manufacturing print for feature identification.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors shall perform a sequence of checks from incoming material through final shipment. Inspection combines dimensional verification, hardness testing, visual and NDT where applicable, and weight verification. Records shall document acceptance or disposition.

Incoming material
Verify material certification traceability to the heat number on the mill test report. Confirm alloy and heat treatment class per the purchase order and material control documentation. Record the mill test report reference on inspection documentation.

Dimensional inspection
Use calibrated gauging and measuring instruments appropriate for the feature. For the critical bore, measure at the specified datum, using a bore gauge or coordinate measuring device consistent with the shop procedure. Acceptance criteria for the critical bore follow the requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm. Document each measured value on the inspection record and note any out-of-tolerance condition.

Hardness testing
Perform hardness tests on specified locations identified on the drawing. Use a calibrated hardness tester and produce a traceable test block verification record. Acceptance follows the hardness requirement: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC. Record each hardness reading and the tester verification block result on the inspection sheet.

Weight verification
Confirm forging weight as part of batch control, and to ensure compliance with handling and tooling limits. Verify that production forgings do not exceed the maximum allowed mass by comparing the measured mass against the requirement: The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 73.0 kg. Record mass measurements on the batch load sheet.

Visual and NDT
Inspect visual condition for defects impacting performance. Where required by the manufacturing print, perform nondestructive examination per the applicable shop procedure and record results on the NDT report.

Sampling and acceptance
Perform inspection at defined points in the flow: incoming, post-forge, post-heat-treatment, and final. Any feature that fails to meet the requirement table shall be documented as nonconforming and processed per the nonconformance handling directive below.

Nonconforming handling
Identification and containment
If an item is found to be nonconforming to any requirement in this document, segregate and tag the item clearly to prevent unintended use. The tag shall reference the inspection record and the reason for rejection.

Disposition
Evaluate nonconforming items to determine whether rework, repair, or scrap is applicable. Rework plans must be approved by the process engineer and must explicitly state the affected features and verification steps post-rework. Repair shall not be performed in a manner that would violate metallurgical or dimensional requirements, including hardness and bore tolerance.

Example dispositions
- A hub with a bore out of tolerance shall be submitted to engineering for a rework evaluation. If a rework method is approved, post-rework inspection must confirm compliance with: The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is ±0.06 mm.
- A hub with hardness outside the acceptance range shall be held and reviewed by metallurgical engineering. Any heat treatment adjustment must result in confirmation that: The hardness range for axle hub CFW-9852-71 (CFW-9852-71) is 34-40 HRC before release.

Records to keep
Maintain an inspection packet for each production lot that includes at minimum:
- Incoming material certification and mill test report reference.
- Dimensional inspection records showing measured values for critical features, including the bore and its conformity to the tolerance: ±0.06 mm.
- Hardness test records with tester verification showing conformity to: 34-40 HRC.
- Mass record demonstrating forgings do not exceed: 73.0 kg where applicable.
- NDT reports and visual inspection notes.
- Nonconformance tags, disposition documentation, and rework approvals.

Retention and access
Inspection records shall be retained in the document control system and made available during internal audits and customer inspections. Each record shall reference the part CFW-9852-71 and the production lot identifier.

Rationale and background
Hardness and bore tolerance are critical to ensuring proper fit, fatigue life, and assembly function for axle hub CFW-9852-71. The specified hardness range provides a balance between wear resistance and toughness for the 4140 material condition typical for this hub. The tight bore tolerance is required to achieve proper interference or clearance fits with mating shafts and bearings. Maximum forging weight is specified to prevent overloading of handling equipment and tooling and to ensure that process controls validated at the specified mass remain valid.

Change control
Any change to these requirements must be approved through the formal document revision process and coordinated with process engineering, production, and quality assurance. This is Revision Rev C for Plant P1 for parts CFW-9852-71.

# QS-CFW-5998-73 - Quality specification - track link CFW-5998-73 (15B37)
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5998-73

Scope
This quality specification governs the manufacturing acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forged track links supplied under the part identifier CFW-5998-73. It applies to all process steps performed at Plant P2 for the referenced part and to any subcontracted forging operations that will deliver product to Plant P2 for final machining and assembly. The intent is to control material and process outputs that affect fit, function, and service life of the track link.

Background and rationale
Track link performance in service is governed by hardness, dimensional accuracy of critical features, and mass control during forging. Hardness affects wear and fatigue resistance of the mating surface. Bore geometry governs fitment on the pivot pin and directly impacts assembly clearance and kinematics. Controlling forging mass ensures consistent upset and grain flow for downstream heat treatment and machining. The requirements below are set to balance field durability and manufacturability based on engineering evaluations and service feedback.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance note |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness | The hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 34-38 HRC. | Hardness shall be measured after final heat treatment and prior to any machining that would alter the surface hardness. Localized grinding that removes material from the test surface is not permitted before hardness verification. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is ±0.10 mm. | Applies to the finished bore after any machining operations. Concentricity and roundness shall be controlled to ensure the tolerance is meaningful for assembly; when bore is at tolerance limit, mating pin fit must be confirmed by assembly trial records. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 4.8 kg. | Weight must be recorded on the heat/lot traceability record. Forgings exceeding this mass may have altered material flow and shall not be released without engineering disposition. |

Inspection method
Material traceability and initial verification
- Verify incoming material certification is present for each heat lot and reconcile to the lot/heat number captured in production records. Confirm chemical and mechanical properties meet the base material specification recorded for CFW-5998-73.

Hardness verification
- Hardness testing shall be performed on representative locations defined for the part family and recorded in the inspection record. Test locations shall be selected from non-machined surfaces that represent the worst-case case for hardness after heat treatment. Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Record individual test readings and the test location identifiers on the inspection form. Acceptance is per the hardness range stated in the requirements table. If a reading falls outside the range, tag the part as nonconforming and proceed per the nonconformance handling section.

Bore dimensional inspection
- Inspect the finished bore using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement to verify the bore diameter is within the bore diameter tolerance specified in the requirements table. Record the measured values and the measuring instrument identifier on the inspection form. For production runs where a first-piece inspection is required, retain the first-piece report in the part lot file. If bore inspection shows deviation, stop release of the lot and follow the nonconformance handling procedure.

Forging mass control
- Weigh each forging after trimming and before heat treatment; record the mass on the heat/lot traceability record. Ensure the measured mass does not exceed the maximum forging weight specified in the requirements table. If the mass exceeds the stated maximum, segregate the forging and notify engineering for disposition.

Sampling and acceptance rationale
- The inspection plan focuses on attributes that most affect assembly fit and service life. Hardness is controlled to maintain fatigue and wear resistance. Bore tolerance is controlled to ensure functional fit and to prevent accelerated wear or misalignment. Forging mass is limited to maintain consistent metallurgical properties and prevent process anomalies. Records from each inspection activity are retained to support traceability and to provide data for continuous improvement.

Examples of acceptable and non-acceptable conditions
- Acceptable: Part with recorded hardness readings within the specified hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73), bore measurements all within the stated bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm, and recorded mass at or below the maximum forging weight 4.8 kg.
- Non-acceptable: Part with hardness readings outside 34-38 HRC; part with any bore measurement outside ±0.10 mm of nominal; forging with recorded mass greater than 4.8 kg.

Records to keep
- Heat/lot traceability record including incoming material certification and forging mass for each part.
- Hardness test records including instrument calibration identifier, test locations, and individual readings.
- Bore inspection records including measurement device identifier and raw measured values.
- Disposition records and nonconformance reports for any part that fails the stated requirements.
- Retain records per Plant P2 document retention policy and make available for internal audit and customer inquiries.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part found outside the limits stated in the requirements table shall be tagged as nonconforming and physically segregated from conforming inventory. Marking shall include the part identifier CFW-5998-73 and the reason for nonconformance.

Containment and notification
- Immediately notify production supervision and quality engineering. Capture the nonconformance on the official nonconformance report and attach the inspection records that triggered the report.

Evaluation and disposition
- Quality engineering and manufacturing engineering shall evaluate the cause and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include repair where feasible, rework under an approved procedure, scrap, or engineering review for use-as-is with customer approval. Any repair or rework proposal must include steps to ensure the repaired part will meet the requirements in the table and must be approved in writing by engineering.

Corrective action and records
- Root cause analysis shall be conducted for nonconformances that indicate a systemic issue. Implement corrective actions and document effectiveness. All disposition and corrective action records shall be filed with the lot records for the affected parts and made available for audits.

Revision control
- Changes to this specification require documented approval by quality engineering at Plant P2 and shall be recorded in the revision history.
