# QS-CFW-4540-42 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-4540-42 (4140)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4540-42

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (4140) produced at Plant P3. It covers material hardness, bore dimensional tolerance, maximum forging gross weight, inspection sampling rationale, examples of acceptable and unacceptable conditions, and record retention requirements. This document applies to incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and final inspection prior to release to the machining cell.

Background and rationale
CFW-4540-42 is a medium alloy steel forging requiring controlled mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy to meet downstream machining and assembly processes. Hardness is controlled to ensure machinability and final part performance. Bore concentricity and diameter tolerance are critical to ensure fixture fit and subsequent machining stock. Maximum forging weight is specified to ensure safe handling, proper die fill, and to prevent equipment overload during forging and handling operations. Inspection methods are chosen to be practical on the shop floor and reproducible by qualified inspectors.

Requirements table
The table below lists the controlled characteristics and acceptance criteria for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42).

- Characteristic: Material hardness (as-quenched/tempered)
  - Requirement: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is 38-44 HRC.
  - Rationale: Ensures machinability and strength balance for downstream processing and service.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is ±0.07 mm.
  - Rationale: Controls fit-up to fixtures and initial machining allowances; prevents excessive material removal or rework.

- Characteristic: Forging gross weight
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is 71.9 kg.
  - Rationale: Limits handling risk and ensures compatibility with handling and heating equipment capacities.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections shall be performed by qualified personnel familiar with induction hardness testing, calibrated dimensional measurement instruments, and weighing equipment. Inspectors shall follow written procedures and record results on the indicated inspection form.

Hardness inspection
- Use a portable hardness tester suitable for Rockwell C measurements. Perform verification on calibrated reference blocks before use.
- Inspect hardness at a minimum of three locations representative of the forged web and flange area; avoid edge decarburized zones and through-hardened transitions. Document individual readings and compute the observed range for the part.
- Acceptance criterion: readings must fall within the hardness range specified above. If any reading falls outside the range, proceed to nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter inspection
- Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or inside micrometers appropriate for the bore size. Ensure measurement probes contact clean, cool surfaces free of scale.
- Take measurements at two axial positions and at orthogonal orientations to assess runout and local ovality; record each measurement and note the maximum deviation from nominal.
- Acceptance criterion: measured diameter must conform to the bore diameter tolerance specified above.

Weight verification
- Weigh the forging in its as-forged condition on a calibrated platform scale. Record the gross weight on the inspection record.
- Acceptance criterion: weight must not exceed the maximum forging weight specified above. If weight exceeds that value, follow nonconformance handling.

Examples and interpretation
- Example acceptable condition: hardness readings of values that lie within the specified hardness range across the sampled locations, bore measurements that stay within the specified bore tolerance, and weight under the maximum forging weight. Mark the part as acceptable and release to machining.
- Example reject condition: a single hardness reading above or below the specified hardness range indicates a process control failure in heat treatment or forging; do not release. Similarly, a bore measurement outside the specified tolerance indicates die wear or misalignment; initiate tooling evaluation. A part exceeding the maximum forging weight requires investigation for die overfill or incorrect preform and must be segregated.

Nonconformance handling
Segregation and immediate actions
- Any part failing to meet one or more requirements shall be segregated and labeled with a nonconformance tag. Do not release for machining.

Root cause and disposition
- Initiate a containment and root cause activity. Actions should include review of forging process records, die condition, material heat treatment records, and handling or heating cycle notes to identify the likely source of the nonconformance.
- Disposition options include rework, reheat treatment, machining scrap, or return to forging, subject to engineering approval and demonstration that the final part will meet customer and safety requirements. Document the chosen disposition and approval authority on the nonconformance record.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records for each lot or heat in accordance with plant document control procedures:
- Hardness test logs, including instrument verification, individual readings, and inspector signature.
- Dimensional inspection records for bore measurements, including instrument calibration references.
- Gross weight record from the platform scale, with scale identification and calibration reference.
- Nonconformance reports, root cause analysis notes, disposition decisions, and approvals.
- Process parameter logs relevant to forging and heat treatment when available.

Retention and audit
All records shall be retained and made available for internal and external audits as required by plant quality procedures. Records must include sufficient detail to reconstruct the inspection and disposition decisions.

Revision control
This is Revision Rev D of QS-CFW-4540-42. Changes to this specification must be processed through formal revision procedures at Plant P3.

Related documents
None.
title: Quality specification - flange blank CFW-4540-42 (4140)

# QS-CFW-6160-72 - Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (4340)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6160-72

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 supplied by the P1 forging cell. The document applies to the forged blank state of material grade 4340 intended for downstream machining and heat treatment. It provides background rationale for the selected characteristics, inspection method details for verification, recordkeeping requirements, and examples of disposition outcomes.

## Background and rationale
The crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 is produced for high-stress rotating applications and must meet metallurgical and dimensional characteristics that enable predictable heat treatment and machining yield. Mechanical hardness in the forged condition correlates to prior thermal processing and cooling rate; maintaining the specified hardness range ensures the material will respond to downstream heat treatment as expected. Bore accuracy is critical for fit-up and concentricity during machining operations; the specified tolerance supports effective fixture alignment. Maximum forging weight is a manufacturing constraint driven by die strength and press capacity and is included to prevent equipment overload and to ensure handling safety.

The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC. The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is ±0.09 mm. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4340 | Visual and mill certification match part drawing and purchase order. |
| Hardness (forged blank) | 26-31 HRC | Hardness readings within specified range across verified locations. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.09 mm | Bore measured relative to nominal drawing diameter and within tolerance. |
| Forging weight | ≤ 26.9 kg | Measured mass does not exceed maximum forging weight. |
| Surface condition | No forging laps, cold shuts, or scale beyond normal mill scale | Defects affecting machinability or fatigue rejection per visual acceptance; see inspection method. |
| Heat treatment traceability | Batch heat history documented | Records retained per inspection method. |

Notes:
- The hardness and bore tolerance items are mandatory release criteria. Parts failing these criteria shall be held and processed according to nonconformance handling.
- Maximum forging weight is a production limit; parts produced above this value shall be segregated and dispositioned.

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspection shall consist of documented sampling and 100% checks where specified by downstream needs. Visual inspection, dimensional measurement, hardness testing, and weight verification are the primary activities. All inspections shall be logged on the work order and retained as the quality record.

1. Visual inspection
- Perform a visual examination of the forged blank for laps, cold shuts, cracks, and excessive scale. Use lighting suitable for detection of surface anomalies and compare to the acceptance criteria noted in the requirements table.
- Examples: a shallow surface seam that can be removed in machining without losing effective section may be acceptable; a through-thickness crack is not acceptable.

2. Dimensional inspection - bore
- Verify the bore diameter using a bore gauge, plug gauge, or equivalent calibrated instrument able to resolve the tolerances required for fit-up. Measurement points should include bore entry, mid-length, and exit where geometry allows.
- Record measurements on the inspection checklist and confirm each measured value lies within the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.09 mm from nominal.

3. Hardness testing
- Conduct hardness testing on the forged blank at specified locations representative of the core forging cross-sections. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and follow manufacturer procedures for indenter and load.
- Ensure surfaces are prepared to allow a valid indenter reading. Record individual readings and the location for traceability. The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC; acceptance requires all recorded readings to fall within this range.

4. Weight verification
- Weigh the forged blank using a calibrated scale and capture the value on the inspection record. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg; blanks exceeding that value must be segregated and flagged for disposition.

5. Recording and traceability
- Retain the following records with the batch lot file: material certification, hardness readings with location notations, bore measurement records, weight record, and visual inspection checklist. Records shall accompany material through shipping and be available to Quality on request.

## Nonconformance handling
When a blank fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table, follow this procedure:

- Segregation: Immediately segregate the nonconforming blank and tag with a nonconformance tag indicating the nature of the failure (hardness, bore, weight, surface defect). Maintain physical and administrative control to prevent inadvertent use.
- Notification: Notify the plant quality engineer and production supervisor. Provide the inspection records that document the nonconformance.
- Evaluation and disposition: The quality engineer shall evaluate the nonconformance against downstream process capability and part function. Disposition options include:
  - Rework: If the defect is remediable by machining or minor corrective action without compromising material properties, the blank may be reworked to drawing requirements. Document the rework plan and re-inspect critical characteristics. Example: a localized surface seam that can be removed by machining without reducing required section or altering balance.
  - Scrap: If the defect cannot be corrected without compromising integrity or if the forging weight exceeds limits in a way that prevents safe handling, scrap the part. Document the reason for scrapping and retain photos and inspection records.
  - Return to supplier or remelt: If a systematic forging/process issue is suspected, hold affected lot items and initiate containment plus root cause analysis.

- Records: For every nonconformance, retain the original inspection report, photos (if applicable), disposition form, and evidence of re-inspection or scrap. These records form the corrective action evidence and are kept with the batch file.

- Root cause and corrective action: For repeated or systemic failures, the quality engineer shall lead a root cause analysis, define corrective actions, and track effectiveness. Document the analysis and corrective actions in the lot file and reference in future production reviews.

## Examples and practical notes
- Example 1: A blank records hardness readings within range except one location reading below the specified range. Segregate and evaluate whether the low reading is localized and machinable; disposition by re-inspection after additional hardness testing along adjacent locations.
- Example 2: A bore measurement at one end is outside the tolerance of ±0.09 mm while other points are acceptable. Determine if the deviation affects fixture fit-up; if so, hold and disposition per corrective action.

Quality retention: All inspection and disposition records shall be maintained with the lot documentation for the lifetime required by customer contract. This specification is the controlling acceptance standard for the crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 at plant P1.
title: Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (4340)

# QS-CFW-7434-20 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (1045)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-7434-20

## Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) manufactured from material grade 1045 at Plant P2. It applies to all finished forging deliveries and to in-process forgings proceeding to final machining at Plant P2. The intent is to control mechanical properties and critical dimensions that affect fit, performance, and service life.

Background and rationale: The connecting rod is a safety-critical rotating component. Hardness and bore control are primary determinants of wear life and fatigue performance after heat treatment and machining. Maximum forging weight governs lift and handling constraints for safe material flow and tooling limits. This document sets clear pass/fail criteria and inspection practices to ensure downstream machining and assembly stability.

## Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (post-heat-treatment, finished) | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC. | Within specified range: Accept. Outside specified range: Reject. |
| Bore diameter (as-forged / pre-machining) | The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.07 mm. | Within tolerance: Accept for machining. Outside tolerance: Reject for rework or scrap. |
| Forging mass | The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg. | Less than or equal to maximum: Accept for standard handling. Greater than maximum: Reject for lift review and containment. |

Notes:
- The hardness requirement applies to the measured surface or cross-section specified by the inspection method below. Hardness readings inconsistent with process capability shall trigger corrective action.
- Bore diameter tolerance applies to the diameter measured at the location and method defined in the inspection method. Feature control applies to pre-machining condition and informs machining allowances.
- Maximum forging weight is used to determine handling, tooling and transport limits. Forgings exceeding the stated maximum shall not proceed to normal handling flows.

## Inspection method

General principles: Use calibrated instruments and certified personnel for all inspections. Record the instrument identification and calibration status in the inspection record. Ensure surface cleanliness and representative sampling. Measurements must be taken at controlled locations described below and recorded verbatim.

Hardness inspection procedure:
- Condition: Inspect on the finished, heat-treated surface after any required tempering and prior to any final finish machining operations that would alter near-surface hardness.
- Method: Use an appropriate hardness tester and test block traceable to calibration standards. Take multiple measurements across the cross-section where representative hardness is required, avoiding obvious defects or scale. Ensure readings are stable before recording.
- Recording: Enter the measured values on the inspection record and compare to the requirement. If any recorded value is outside the hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC., mark the part as nonconforming and follow the nonconformance handling procedure.

Bore diameter inspection procedure:
- Condition: Inspect bores on the as-forged pre-machining component after any final forging cleanup but before machining that will alter bore size.
- Method: Use a calibrated dimensional measuring device appropriate for the bore geometry. Measure at locations specified in the part drawing and record the nominal dimension plus the bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.07 mm. Report measured values and indicate conformance to tolerance.
- Recording: All measured values and the instrument used must be documented on the inspection record. Parts found outside the bore diameter tolerance shall be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.

Forging weight verification:
- Condition: Verify forging mass at the first receiving operation after forging removal from the die area.
- Method: Use the facility lifting or weighing system with traceable calibration. Record the measured mass and compare to the maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg.
- Recording: Weighing results shall be logged on the process traveler and attached inspection paperwork. Forgings exceeding the maximum shall be held and tagged.

Examples and rationale:
- Example inspection record entry for hardness: "Measured hardness values at three locations: value A, value B, value C; all compared to the hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC."
- Example inspection record entry for bore: "Nominal bore X.XXX mm; measured Y.YYY mm; tolerance applied ±0.07 mm; disposition: Accept." Use consistent notation and avoid rounding that obscures conformance decisions.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test printouts or digital logs with tester ID and calibration date.
- Dimensional measurement reports including instrument ID and calibration status.
- Weighing records and tags for material handling.
- Part identification and traveler showing inspection outcomes and signatures. Maintain records in the document control system and attach them to the batch lot for traceability.

## Nonconformance handling

Segregation and identification:
- Any part failing to meet the hardness requirement, bore diameter tolerance, or maximum forging weight requirement must be tagged and moved to the designated hold area. Markings must reference the characteristic failed and the inspection record number.

Disposition options:
- Rework may be considered only if a documented engineering evaluation supports a corrective process that restores the product to full conformance without compromising integrity. Rework steps and approvals must be documented on the disposition form.
- If rework is not feasible, parts shall be scrapped or returned to the supplier per internal scrap handling procedures.

Root cause and correction:
- For each nonconformance, perform a root cause analysis and implement corrective action appropriate to the finding. Actions may include equipment maintenance, process parameter review, tooling inspection, or retraining. Document actions taken and verify effectiveness before returning affected lots to production flow.

Escalation and customer notification:
- Notify responsible quality personnel immediately for any nonconformance that may affect delivery or safety. Maintain communication records and final disposition documentation in the batch file.

Records of nonconformance:
- Maintain the hold tag, inspection record, disposition form, root cause analysis, and corrective action verification with the part lot documentation. These records must be available for audit and for review during manufacturing release.

End of document.

# QS-CFW-1931-62 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-1931-62 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1931-62

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62), material designation 8620, produced at Plant P3.  
- The specification defines acceptance criteria for metallurgical hardness, bore geometry, and maximum forging mass, and establishes required inspection methods, documentation, and nonconformance handling for production and incoming inspection.  
- Background: CFW-1931-62 gear blanks are intermediate forgings destined for downstream machining and heat treatment. Consistent hardness and dimensional control of the bore are critical to achieve predictable gear performance after finishing and heat treatment. The limits in this document reflect forged state acceptance intended to ensure process stability and minimize rework downstream.

Requirements table
- Part: CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62)  
- Hardness: The hardness range for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 38-41 HRC. This applies to measured locations on the finished forging surface where machining stock is intended to be removed or where specified by order. Hardness outside this range is a nonconformance subject to disposition.  
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is ±0.08 mm. Inspectable features include the finished bore prior to any final machining operations. Bore runout, concentricity, and surface condition are assessed during inspection; the dimensional tolerance above governs acceptance.  
- Maximum forging mass: The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg. Any forging claimed to exceed this mass at time of final forging inspection shall be segregated and dispositioned per the nonconformance handling section.

Inspection method
- Purpose: Define how to verify each requirement in the requirements table and the records to be retained. Methods are selected to be practical for shop floor verification while providing defensible measurement data for quality records. Rationale: Direct measurement and standardized hardness testing give rapid confirmation of process output and allow timely corrective action if trends indicate drift. Examples given are illustrative of typical checks and recording practice.  
- Hardness measurement: Conduct hardness checks on representative locations on each forging surface intended for subsequent machining or where specified by the purchase order. Use a calibrated Rockwell tester capable of reporting HRC. Perform verification by experienced personnel following instrument manufacturer recommendations for indenter selection and surface preparation. Record each measured value and identify the piece serial or heat reference in the inspection record. Acceptance criterion: hardness must fall within the hardness range for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 38-41 HRC. Example: For a production lot, record the sequence of sample measurements, annotate any outliers, and include a photograph of the test indication when surface finish is marginal.  
- Bore diameter measurement: Measure the bore using an appropriate internal diameter measuring device that provides traceable calibration. Verify at multiple axial positions and record the measurement locations. Acceptance criterion: measurement results must conform to the bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is ±0.08 mm relative to the nominal bore specified on the manufacturing print. Example: Document a set of measurements from near each end of the bore and mid span, noting any taper or irregularity. Any single measurement outside of tolerance requires the part to be segregated and forwarded for engineering disposition.  
- Mass verification: Verify forging mass using a calibrated scale at final forging inspection. Acceptance criterion: the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg. When reported mass equals the maximum forging mass for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg, confirm calculations and ensure packing and tagging accurately reflect measured value. If mass exceeds the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-1931-62 (CFW-1931-62) is 97.9 kg, follow nonconformance handling.  
- Records to keep: Maintain an inspection pack for each lot that includes hardness readings with location map, raw bore measurement data with measurement device ID, mass verification printout, inspector signature, and the process route for the heat/lot. Retain records in the document control system and attach to the batch record used for downstream operations. Records support root cause analysis and are required for any disposition decision.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Any forging found outside the stated acceptance criteria shall be segregated from conforming inventory and clearly tagged with a nonconformance identifier. Bring the piece to the attention of the quality supervisor for immediate evaluation.  
- Evaluation and disposition: Quality shall perform an evaluation that includes review of inspection records, process data, and potential impact on downstream operations. Where an out-of-tolerance condition affects only a removable region or can be corrected without compromising integrity, an engineering disposition may allow rework. Where the condition could affect performance after final processing, the forging must be rejected or reprocessed under engineering authorization. Rationale: Objective evaluation limits unnecessary scrap while protecting product function. Example: a bore out of tolerance that can be corrected by final machining within the allowed tolerance band at the next operation may be accepted under controlled rework instructions; any such acceptance must be recorded.  
- Root cause and corrective action: For each nonconformance, document root cause findings and corrective actions taken, including changes to tooling, process parameters, or inspection frequency. Record verification of corrective action effectiveness in subsequent inspection records.  
- Disposition records: All disposition decisions, approvals, and confirmations of corrective action must be recorded and stored with the inspection records for the lot. These records are the basis for trending and continuous improvement and must be available for internal review.

End of document
title: Quality specification - gear blank CFW-1931-62 (8620)

# QS-CFW-7189-64 — Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (52100)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7189-64

## Scope
This quality specification defines metallurgical and dimensional acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 manufactured from 52100 steel at Plant P1. It applies to finished forgings released for heat treatment and final machining and to any subcontracted processing that affects hardness or bore geometry. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life expectations for assemblies using CFW-7189-64.

Background and rationale: bearing rings are functionally sensitive to core hardness and bore geometry. The specified hardness range controls through-hardened microstructure and residual austenite, while the bore diameter tolerance controls fit and assembly performance. The maximum forging weight constraint limits handling and process capacity within Plant P1 equipment.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | 24-29 HRC | Measured on forged and finished surface per Inspection Method below |
| Bore diameter tolerance, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | ±0.04 mm | Applies after final machining and before assembly |
| Maximum forging weight, bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) | 22.9 kg | Includes any attached mandrels or temporary fixtures during handling |

Notes on the table: Each row describes an acceptance criterion that must be met before a part is released from final inspection. The hardness requirement is a control on heat treat and quench practice; the bore tolerance is a geometry control for final machining; the maximum forging weight is an equipment and handling constraint.

## Inspection method
General approach: Inspectors shall verify each requirement using calibrated equipment and documented procedures. Calibration of instruments must be traceable and records retained.

Hardness verification:
- Take hardness measurements at representative locations around the ring cross-section, avoiding radiused corners and machining marks. Use a Rockwell C tester suitable for hardened steels.
- The hardness requirement is: The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is 24-29 HRC.
- Document each individual reading and the location on the part drawing where it was taken. Report the highest and lowest readings per part together with the part identifier and inspector.

Bore diameter verification:
- Inspect the bore after final internal machining using a bore gauge or calibrated plug gauge system appropriate to the bore size. Measure concentricity and roundness as required by drawing control features.
- The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is ±0.04 mm.
- Record the measured nominal diameter and deviation from nominal. Include measurement equipment ID and calibration date.

Maximum forging weight verification:
- Confirm that the forging batch weight does not exceed factory handling limits by weighing the forging after cooling and removal from dies or fixtures.
- The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (CFW-7189-64) is 22.9 kg.
- If the forging is attached to mandrels or fixtures at weighing, include those items in the reported weight and note their identity.

Sampling and frequency:
- Inspect each lot at receiving inspection and again prior to final release. For multi-piece lots, follow plant sampling rules verified in process control documents. Record sampling rationale in the inspection record.

Equipment and calibration:
- Use calibrated instruments with current calibration labels. Calibration records shall be available for audit. List of equipment used, calibration due status, and inspector signature must be entered in the inspection record for each lot.

Examples of acceptable records:
- A hardness report showing individual readings taken at documented locations, part identifiers, date, and inspector name.
- A dimensional report listing bore measurements, measurement device IDs, calibration dates, and the resulting pass/fail for the ±0.04 mm tolerance.
- A weight ticket from a calibrated scale indicating the forging mass including fixtures, with inspector initials.

## Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment:
- Any part failing to meet a stated requirement shall be identified as nonconforming, segregated from conforming material, and tagged with a nonconformance notice. Include the failed characteristic, measured values, and inspector identity in the notice.

Disposition options and evaluation:
- Evaluate nonconforming items for repair, rework, or scrap based on root cause and feasibility. Rework proposals must include specific steps to bring the part into compliance without compromising metallurgical properties or geometry and must be reviewed by engineering.
- Example dispositions: localized machining if geometry permits, or scrapping if the structural integrity or metallurgical state cannot be restored. For hardness-related failures, engineering must assess whether heat treatment can correct the condition without introducing new risks.

Documentation and approval:
- All nonconformance records must detail the corrective action or disposition decision, the approver’s name and title, and any instructions for re-inspection. Retain records with the lot history.

Corrective action and preventive measures:
- For recurrent nonconformance, perform a root cause analysis and implement process changes. Document corrective action plans and effectiveness checks. Record training or process adjustments taken to prevent recurrence.

Records to keep
- Inspection reports for hardness, bore diameter, and weight for each lot.
- Calibration certificates for all measurement devices used.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition approvals.
- Any engineering evaluations or corrective action records associated with disposition or process changes.

Retention and access
- Maintain records in the document control system associated with QS-CFW-7189-64. Records shall be available for internal audit and customer review as required by contract.

End of document.
title: Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-7189-64 (52100)

# QS-CFW-1730-97 Quality specification - valve body CFW-1730-97 (F316) Rev A

Scope
This quality specification applies to the valve body CFW-1730-97 forged from F316 material produced at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the finished forging prior to any machining operations. Background and rationale: the valve body is a pressure boundary component where mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy are critical for safe assembly and service. The parameters in this document are selected to ensure material hardness, bore integrity, and manageable handling based on maximum forging mass.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Material / Part | CFW-1730-97 | Conforming to purchase and material certification for F316 |
| Hardness | The hardness range for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 25-29 HRC. | Measured values within stated range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is ±0.09 mm. | Dimensional inspection reports must show conformance |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-1730-97 (CFW-1730-97) is 118.5 kg. | Weight records and handling plan must account for this limit |

Inspection method
General approach: Inspect the forging on receipt from the forge line in a controlled inspection area. Use calibrated instruments appropriate to the measured characteristic. Prepare the inspection report and attach material certifications and heat traceability as part of the lot record.

Hardness measurement: Use a portable hardness tester following the manufacturer's procedure for the device and the relevant test standard. Select locations representative of the critical load paths and the wall thickness adjacent to the bore. Ensure surfaces are prepared per the tester requirements so that indenter seating is reliable. Record individual hardness readings and compute a simple pass/fail assessment against the specified range. If any reading falls outside the range, mark the piece and proceed to nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter inspection: Measure the bore diameter using appropriate gauging or measuring devices capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Verify that measurements account for bore roundness and local irregularities; report both nominal diameter and any runout or ovality descriptions in the inspection record. For features with multiple measurement locations, document the measurement positions and the result at each position. Conformance is determined by comparison with the stated bore diameter tolerance.

Weight verification and handling: Weigh the forging using the plant weighing equipment and record the measured mass on the inspection form. Verify that the weight does not exceed the maximum specified mass, and use the weight record to inform lifting plans, storage placement, and transportation within the plant. If the measured mass exceeds the specified maximum, isolate the part and initiate nonconformance handling.

Surface and visual inspection: Conduct a visual inspection for cracks, seams, laps, and other forging defects. Document any discontinuities with photos and location descriptions. Surface finish is inspected qualitatively at this stage; mandatory final machining operations will address finish requirements unless a defect impairs material integrity.

Inspection records and traceability: For each forging, produce an inspection record that includes: part identifier, lot identifier, hardness readings with location annotations, bore diameter measurements with measurement device identifier, measured mass, inspector name, and date. Attach the material certification and heat number traceability to each record. Store records in the document control system under the part folder for Plant P2.

Examples and interpretation
Example of a passing condition: hardness readings within the specified range and bore measurements within the stated tolerance, with recorded mass below the maximum forging weight. In this case, authorize release to machining and update the lot record.

Example of a borderline condition: a hardness reading at the extreme of the allowed range. In this case, review all hardness readings for consistency, review heat certification for documentation of processing, and consider additional hardness measurements around the affected area before final disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment: Any forging that fails to meet the hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum weight requirement must be clearly marked and segregated from conforming stock. Prevent further processing until disposition is completed.

Notification and initial evaluation: Notify the quality supervisor assigned to Plant P2 and document the deviation on a nonconformance report. Include all inspection records, material certification, and any photographic evidence. Perform an initial evaluation to determine the scope of the condition and whether it affects a single piece or an entire lot.

Disposition options: Consider one of the following dispositions based on evaluation and engineering input: rework if the defect is remediable by permitted processes, repair if applicable and approved, or scrap if the integrity is compromised beyond acceptable repair. For weight exceedance, disposition must consider lifting and handling constraints in addition to structural suitability.

Engineering review and approval: Obtain engineering authorization for any disposition that would alter part geometry or material properties. Record the engineering decision on the nonconformance report and attach supporting rationale.

Records and corrective action: Maintain the nonconformance report and the final disposition in the part folder for Plant P2. If a pattern of similar nonconformances emerges, initiate a corrective action request to address root cause, which may include process review at the forging source, change in inspection frequency, or supplier communication. Track corrective actions until closure and include outcomes in the next quality review for CFW-1730-97.

Retention and audit
Retain inspection records, nonconformance reports, and disposition documentation in the controlled filing system for audit and traceability as required by company policy. Ensure records are accessible during internal and external audits and contain the required links to material certification and heat traceability for CFW-1730-97.
title: Quality specification - valve body CFW-1730-97 (F316)

# QS-CFW-2573-68 - Quality specification - axle hub CFW-2573-68 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-2573-68  
Related documents: none

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufacturing, inspection, and disposition of axle hub CFW-2573-68 (CFW-2573-68) produced from material grade 4140 at Plant P3. It defines acceptance criteria for metallurgical and dimensional characteristics that directly affect fit, form, and function in downstream assembly and service. The intent is to provide clear, enforceable criteria for production, in-process control, final inspection, and nonconformance handling to minimize scrap and rework while protecting safety and reliability.

Background and rationale
- Axle hubs carry loads transmitted through bearings and fasteners; their hardness and bore geometry are critical to maintain interference fits and bearing life. The hardness range 25-31 HRC is selected to balance toughness and wear resistance for 4140 material in this application. The bore diameter tolerance ±0.03 mm ensures consistent fit with mating shafts and bearings without excessive rework. The maximum forging weight 97.2 kg establishes limits for forging operations, handling equipment, and heat treatment load capacity.
- These parameters were derived from service requirements and manufacturing capability assessments. Hardness outside the specified range can indicate improper quench or temper conditions or decarburization. Bore out of tolerance can cause assembly interference or looseness; uncontrolled forging weight can exceed press or furnace capacity and compromise process control.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the controlled characteristics, acceptance criteria, and responsible function for verification.

| Characteristic | Acceptance criteria | Responsible function |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 as specified on purchase order and material certificate | Purchasing / Receiving |
| Hardness (throughout critical cross section) | 25-31 HRC | Heat treat / Quality |
| Bore diameter | Within drawing nominal plus or minus ±0.03 mm | Machining / Quality |
| Surface condition | Free of defects that affect function; no visible cracks or severe laps | Machining / Quality |
| Forging weight (as-delivered) | Not to exceed maximum forging weight 97.2 kg | Forging / Production |
| Final visual and functional check | Conforms to drawing and assembly requirements | Quality / Assembly |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Verify material certificate matches procurement specification and that material grade is 4140. Record the certificate reference in the job lot file.
  - Confirm forging gross mass is not above maximum forging weight 97.2 kg by cross reference to the forging work order and handling documentation. If forging mass is unspecified on the work order, use scale ticket supplied by forging operations and attach to the lot record.
- In-process inspection
  - Hardness control: perform hardness verification on representative locations identified in the inspection plan. Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Measurements must confirm hardness within 25-31 HRC across the critical cross section. Document all readings in the heat treat record. If readings trend toward the limits, notify heat treat process owner to evaluate process settings and quench/temper procedure.
  - Bore verification: measure bore diameter using the measurement method specified on the drawing or inspection plan. Measurements must be within ±0.03 mm of the nominal drawing diameter. Record measurements on the dimensional inspection sheet and attach to the lot passport.
  - Surface and visual inspection: inspect for forging laps, cracks, inclusions, scale, and other defects prior to machining. Critical defects require containment and escalation to quality engineering.
- Final inspection
  - Verify that all hardness values recorded during heat treat are within 25-31 HRC and that all bore measurements are within ±0.03 mm. Confirm surface condition and that no nonconformances remain open. Complete final inspection checklist and file with process records.
- Calibration and equipment
  - Ensure hardness tester and bore measuring equipment are within valid calibration. Calibration certificates must be referenced in the inspection record. If an instrument is found out of calibration, quarantined lot measurements must be re-established with a calibrated instrument and documented.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and containment
  - Any part or lot that fails to meet hardness criteria 25-31 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.03 mm, or exceeds maximum forging weight 97.2 kg shall be identified, segregated, and tagged as nonconforming. Segregation must prevent inadvertent use.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - Quality shall evaluate the root cause and propose a disposition: rework, repair, use-as-is with acceptance by engineering, or scrap. Evaluation shall include review of process data from forging, heat treat, and machining.
  - Rework examples: if bore is marginally out of tolerance and material remains within drawing allowance, machining to an alternate size with appropriate mating parts or use of approved oversize bearing may be considered only after engineering approval and with traceability recorded. If hardness is out of range due to reversible processing, reheat and temper or re-quench may be considered only if metallurgical assessment supports the action and records are maintained.
  - Scrap: parts that exhibit critical defects such as through-thickness cracks, excessive decarburization, or damage incompatible with repair shall be scrapped and documented.
- Records and traceability
  - For every nonconformance, maintain a nonconformance report in the lot file that includes part identification, time and source of discovery, measured deviation from requirement, immediate containment action, root cause analysis summary, disposition decision, and corrective actions. Attach relevant process data: heat treat records, hardness readings, bore measurement sheets, forging weight documentation, and calibration certificates.
  - Retain records in the job lot file and the quality management system in accordance with company retention rules.
- Corrective action and prevention
  - If nonconformances repeat or indicate systemic process issues, initiate corrective action. The corrective action shall include containment verification, root cause analysis, process parameter review, training if required, and monitoring to confirm effectiveness. Quality shall track corrective actions until closure and include evidence demonstrating that risk of recurrence has been reduced.

Examples and notes
- Example situations are provided for clarity. If a lot exhibits hardness values just outside 25-31 HRC at the outer surface but passes internal measurements, engineering metallurgical evaluation is required before disposition. If a single part bore measurement exceeds ±0.03 mm while the remainder of the lot is within tolerance, evaluate whether machining recovery is feasible and document the decision and method.
- Maintain clear linkage between forging batch, heat treat load, machining batch, and final lot to ensure traceability from forging through final inspection.

Records to keep
- Material certificate for 4140
- Forging weight documentation referencing maximum forging weight 97.2 kg
- Heat treat records with hardness readings showing 25-31 HRC
- Dimensional inspection sheets showing bore measurements within ±0.03 mm
- Calibration certificates for measurement equipment
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation

End of specification.
title: Quality specification - axle hub CFW-2573-68 (4140)

# QS-CFW-7661-91 - Quality specification - track link CFW-7661-91 (15B37)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Part(s): CFW-7661-91

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the track link CFW-7661-91 (CFW-7661-91). It applies to forgings delivered to P1 and to all in-plant operations that affect final hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life consistent with design requirements for the CFW-7661-91 family.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory quality attributes and acceptance criteria for CFW-7661-91.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Through-hardness | 39-42 HRC | All finished inspection points must fall within 39-42 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.02 mm | Measured bores must be within nominal dimension ±0.02 mm |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg | Any forging exceeding 28.0 kg is rejected for this part number |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Purpose: Verify through-hardness distribution meets the requirement 39-42 HRC for CFW-7661-91.
- Method: Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and apply the manufacturer’s standard procedure for HRC measurement on steel forgings. Measurements shall be taken at locations representative of service-critical sections including the girth area and the bore collar. For each inspected part, record the highest and lowest hardness values measured and compare to the requirement 39-42 HRC.
- Rationale: Through-hardness directly correlates with wear resistance and fatigue life in track link applications. Establishing a representative measurement practice ensures that variations from heat treatment or material chemistry are detected before assembly.

Bore diameter
- Purpose: Confirm bore concentricity and size meet functional fit for mating pins and rollers.
- Method: Measure bore diameter using a calibrated internal micrometer or plug gauge suitable for the nominal bore size. Measure along at least two orthogonal axes at the mid-length of the bore and at the bore entrances to detect taper. Record the measured values and calculate deviation from nominal. Acceptance criterion is ±0.02 mm as specified in the requirements table.
- Rationale: Bore tolerance ±0.02 mm is required to ensure proper press fit and dynamic clearance. Excess deviation can produce accelerated wear or assembly issues; undersized bores impede assembly.

Forging weight
- Purpose: Ensure forgings are within process control limits for charge weight and flash removal, and to verify material distribution.
- Method: Weigh the cleaned, de-flashed forging on a calibrated scale. Record the weight on the inspection record. Any part with weight greater than the specified maximum forging weight 28.0 kg shall be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg ensures compatibility with downstream handling equipment and heat-treat batch limits. Forgings above this limit indicate an out-of-control forming or trimming process.

Sampling and inspection coverage
- Inspectors shall follow production control schedules and sampling plans defined in site quality procedures. For each production lot of CFW-7661-91, maintain a minimum set of records that includes hardness readings, bore measurements, and forging weight for representative units and any units inspected 100 percent as a condition of corrective actions.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system for each lot of CFW-7661-91:
- Hardness inspection log including part identifier, measurement locations, and values compared against 39-42 HRC.
- Bore measurement records showing measured values and confirmation of tolerance ±0.02 mm.
- Forging weight record indicating measured weight and comparison to maximum forging weight 28.0 kg.
- Heat-treatment batch record and furnace charge list as applicable.
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions when defects or out-of-tolerance conditions are found.
Records must be retained per site retention policy and must be available for review during audits and customer inquiries.

Nonconformance handling
Definition and segregation
- Any part that fails to meet the hardness requirement 39-42 HRC, the bore diameter tolerance ±0.02 mm, or that exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.0 kg is nonconforming and must be segregated immediately from conforming material.

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.
- Repair by engineering: Where engineering assessment determines a repair that preserves function and safety is possible, Quality must approve a repair instruction and all repaired parts must be re-inspected to the original requirements.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be returned to conformance, including those exceeding maximum forging weight 28.0 kg or those with through-hardness outside 39-42 HRC that cannot be corrected, shall be designated scrap and processed per site scrap control procedures.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Audit and corrective action
- Quality shall track occurrences of nonconformance by characteristic and require root cause analysis for repeated failures against hardness 39-42 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.02 mm, or weight exceedance 28.0 kg. Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the failure mode and documented in corrective action records.

Revision and configuration
- This specification applies to part CFW-7661-91 as identified above. Changes to the requirements must be approved through the plant configuration control process.

# QS-CFW-8165-49 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-8165-49 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-8165-49

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for flange blank CFW-8165-49 manufactured from alloy 4140 at Plant P2. It applies to all production lots and to material released for machining operations. The intent is to ensure the flange blank meets metallurgical and dimensional conditions necessary for downstream processing and final part performance.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria / Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4140 | Verify mill test report matches order. |
| Hardness | 36-42 HRC. | Hardness to be measured on machined or flat ground surface representative of forged condition. Accept if hardness falls within range. If readings border tolerance limits, verify with an additional measurement at an adjacent location. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.06 mm. | Verify bore diameter with calibrated bore gage or plug gage compatible with specified nominal bore. Accept if measured diameter falls within tolerance band. |
| Maximum forging weight | 25.2 kg. | Reject any individual forging that exceeds maximum forging weight at time of part release. Weigh on calibrated scale; record mass on inspection report. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cracks, and cold shuts that would affect machining or final integrity. | Localized surface imperfections that can be removed by normal machining and do not materially change the geometry are acceptable after documented disposition. |

Inspection method
- Sampling and frequency: Inspect representative parts from each production lot prior to release for machining. Use risk-based sampling consistent with quality system practice. When process changes occur, include full dimensional and hardness verification on first shipment after change.
- Hardness measurement: Prepare a flat area free of scale and heavy flash. Use a Rockwell hardness tester capable of reading Rockwell C scale. Apply test load according to equipment procedure and record values in the inspection record. Take a minimum of two readings on each part in locations representative of bulk material, avoiding edges and features. If the two readings differ materially, take a third reading and record all values with location notes. Final acceptance requires the recorded readings to be within 36-42 HRC.
- Bore measurement: Clean bore to remove scale and any burrs. Measure using a calibrated bore gage or calibrated go/no-go plug gage appropriate for the nominal bore dimension. Report measured diameter and note measurement instrument and calibration identifier. Acceptance is based on the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm.
- Weight verification: Use a calibrated industrial scale. Place part on scale in a stable orientation that does not add fixtures or supports that contribute measurable mass. Record the mass and ensure value does not exceed 25.2 kg. If a part exceeds 25.2 kg, segregate and tag for disposition.
- Visual inspection: Use adequate lighting and magnification as needed. Document any surface anomalies with photographs and descriptive notes. For discontinuities that are not clearly acceptable, perform supplementary evaluation per nonconformance handling below.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification: Segregate nonconforming parts immediately and tag with a unique nonconformance identifier. Record the nature of the nonconformance, measurement data, inspection instruments used, inspector name, and date.
- Examples and disposition rationale:
  - Example: A flange blank measures 35 HRC on two hardness readings and 36 HRC on a third. Because 35 HRC is outside the requirement of 36-42 HRC., the part is nonconforming. Disposition options include reheat/heat treatment to achieve the required hardness band, scrap if further processing is impractical, or use as scrap material. Any heat treatment disposition must be approved by engineering and documented.
  - Example: A bore measurement shows a deviation greater than ±0.06 mm. The part is nonconforming for dimensional tolerance. Disposition may include rework if machining allowance exists and the feature can be brought into tolerance without violating other requirements. If rework is not viable, the part shall be rejected.
  - Example: A forge weighing 25.4 kg is over the maximum forging weight of 25.2 kg. The part is rejected and segregated. Investigate process variables that allowed excess mass and take corrective action.
- Disposition process: Fill out the nonconformance report and notify quality engineering. For potential rework or repair, provide an engineering evaluation that documents the corrective action method, verification steps, and final acceptance criteria. Only quality engineering may authorize return to production.
- Records and traceability: Maintain the following records for each lot and for any nonconforming disposition:
  - Mill test report or material certificate for the lot.
  - Hardness readings with instrument identification and calibration status.
  - Bore diameter measurements, instrument identification, and calibration status.
  - Weight measurement with scale identifier and calibration status.
  - Visual inspection notes and photographs where applicable.
  - Nonconformance reports and final disposition documentation including engineering approvals.
- Corrective actions: For repeated nonconformances, perform root cause analysis, implement corrective actions, and track effectiveness. Document corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification results in the lot history.

Records to keep
- Inspection records for each lot shall be retained in the document control system and include all items listed under Records and traceability. Records shall be sufficient to allow trace-back to raw material batch and individual part where practical. Maintain photographic records for visual defects that require engineering disposition.

Background and rationale
- The hardness requirement of 36-42 HRC. is selected to ensure the forged microstructure and mechanical properties are suitable for subsequent machining, heat treatment, and service loading for parts machined from flange blank CFW-8165-49. The bore diameter tolerance of ±0.06 mm. ensures the feature can be machined to final drawing dimensions without excessive stock removal or rework. The maximum forging weight of 25.2 kg. is set to confirm forging press capacity, handling limits, and tooling compatibility in Plant P2 operations.

Revision control
- This is Revision Rev C of QS-CFW-8165-49. Implement changes as directed by quality management and record revision history in the document control log.
title: Quality specification - flange blank CFW-8165-49 (4140)

# QS-CFW-9184-50 — Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (4340)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9184-50

Scope
This document defines quality acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the crankshaft blank identified as CFW-9184-50, manufactured from steel grade 4340, produced at Plant P3. The intent is to establish mandatory material and dimensional acceptance criteria, outline the inspection methodology to demonstrate conformity, and provide a consistent process for handling nonconforming items. This specification applies to raw forged blanks prior to finish machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks for high-cycle rotating assemblies require controlled hardness and accurate bore location to ensure final machining yield and finished-component performance. The values stated in this document reflect metallurgical and machining constraints established by design engineering. Inspectors and quality engineers must verify the stated requirements on incoming and in-process forgings to avoid downstream scrap, rework, and latent field failures. The inspection methods described favor traceable, instrumented measurements and documented records to support first article verification and routine production checks.

Requirements table
| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4340 (as specified on part drawing) |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and separation defects that would affect machinability or structural integrity (visual and tactile inspection). |
| Traceability | Each forging must be legibly stamped or tagged with the part identifier and a batch or heat number that links to mill certificates. |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections are performed using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. The emphasis is on objective data capture, clear acceptance criteria, and retention of records that enable traceability to the production batch.

Hardness verification
- Perform hardness testing at locations representative of crank web and journal regions to assess bulk condition prior to finish heat treatment. Use a calibrated portable hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and following the instrument manufacturer's procedure.
- Record measured values and compare against the requirement: The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 32-38 HRC. Any measured value outside this stated range is a basis for nonconformance.

Bore diameter verification
- Measure the bore diameter using an appropriate bore gauge or inside micrometer capable of the required resolution. Verify measurements at nominal bore locations specified on the engineering drawing.
- Document measured values and verify compliance with the tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is ±0.02 mm. Records must show measured dimension, instrument used, and the inspector's identification.

Weight verification
- Weigh the forging on a calibrated scale capable of handling the part mass. Compare the measured weight to the maximum forging weight requirement: The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (CFW-9184-50) is 80.8 kg.
- If weight is at or below the stated value, the forging meets the weight requirement; weigh and record per lot.

Surface and defect inspection
- Perform visual inspection under appropriate lighting with supplemental tactile examination. Reject parts exhibiting forging defects that compromise machinability or fatigue integrity, and record defect type and location.

Sampling and acceptance note
- The inspection methods described are intended for first article and routine production verification. When sampling is employed, ensure the sampling plan is documented and justified in the inspection record. The acceptance or rejection of items always references the stated requirements in the requirements table.

Examples and illustrative scenarios
- Example: A forging measured during first article has hardness readings of values within the specified HRC band; record entry shows tester identification and instrument calibration identifier. The item proceeds to the next operation.
- Example: A forging measured for bore diameter shows deviation beyond the stated bore tolerance; the forging is segregated and the nonconformance process is invoked.

Records to keep
- Inspection checklist showing item identifier, part number CFW-9184-50, batch or heat number, measured hardness values, instrument identification, instrument calibration references, measured bore diameters, measured weight, inspector name, and date.
- Nonconformance report for any item failing to meet the requirements in the requirements table, including disposition and corrective action.
- Traceability records linking each forging to its mill certificate and heat lot.
- First article inspection report for initial production lots and any process change affecting material, tooling, or heat treat practice.

Nonconformance handling
Disposition process
- Any forging that does not meet the requirements listed in the requirements table is to be segregated and clearly identified. The nonconforming item must not proceed to downstream operations until disposition is approved by quality engineering and any required corrective actions are completed.
- Nonconformance reports shall include the observed deviation, reference to the applicable requirement (for example, the exact text for hardness, bore tolerance, or maximum weight), the lot identity, and a proposed disposition.

Root cause and corrective action
- Quality engineering will lead or coordinate a root cause evaluation for systemic deviations. Corrective actions may include process adjustments, additional inspection steps, or supplier escalation. Records of the root cause analysis and corrective action implementation are to be retained with the nonconformance file.

Returns to service
- Authorized rework or acceptance by concession must be documented and include verification steps that confirm the forging now meets the stated requirements. Re-inspection records must reference the original nonconformance report.

Related documents
- None

Revision history
- Revision: Rev C (current document control designation).
title: Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-9184-50 (4340)

# QS-CFW-2490-88 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (1045)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-2490-88

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treatment verification, machining interface inspection, and final release inspection for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 produced at Plant P1.
- The document defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore geometry, and maximum forging mass, and establishes inspection methods, record requirements, and nonconformance handling for those attributes.
- This specification is intended for use by production, quality, heat treat, and machining personnel as the controlling acceptance standard for CFW-2490-88.

Requirements table
- Attribute: Material
  - Requirement: Medium carbon steel nominally supplied as specified for CFW-2490-88 connecting rods.
  - Evidence: Mill test report and incoming material verification record.
- Attribute: Hardness
  - Requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is 22-27 HRC.
  - Evidence: Hardness test log entries showing location and reading; equipment calibration certificate traceable to calibration system.
  - Acceptance rule: All measured production samples must fall within the stated hardness range.
- Attribute: Bearing bore diameter
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is ±0.02 mm.
  - Evidence: Dimensional inspection reports showing measured bore diameters and tool calibration records.
  - Acceptance rule: Gauged and measured diameters must be within the nominal drawing dimension plus or minus the stated tolerance.
- Attribute: Forging mass
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is 50.1 kg.
  - Evidence: Batch mass report and individual forging weight record.
  - Acceptance rule: Any forging exceeding the stated maximum forging weight must be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.
- Attribute: Visual and surface condition
  - Requirement: Free from cracks, laps, major laps, and other surface discontinuities that affect fit, function, or safety.
  - Evidence: Visual inspection checklist and NDT records where performed.

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Verify incoming material documentation and perform visual check for shipment damage. Record material certificates on the incoming material form.
- Hardness verification
  - Location: Verify hardness at specified locations on the rod that represent the critical bearing and shank regions. Use a portable or bench hardness tester validated for HRC scale; record each reading on the hardness test log.
  - Procedure rationale: Hardness control ensures appropriate strength and toughness balance after heat treatment. Sampling should cover representative pieces from each heat to detect process drift.
  - Example entry: Record equipment ID, operator initials, test points, and raw HRC values. If a reading is outside the stated hardness range, follow nonconformance handling.
  - Calibration: Verify tester calibration status prior to use and record calibration reference on the test log.
- Dimensional inspection of bore diameter
  - Measurement method: Measure bore diameters using calibrated internal micrometers, bore gauges, or air gauging where applicable. Verify instruments are within their calibration cycle prior to inspection and document instrument ID.
  - Rationale: The specified bore diameter tolerance directly controls clearance at assembly; adherence prevents premature wear and ensures proper fit to mating components.
  - Example entry: Record nominal drawing diameter, measured value, instrument used, and inspection operator.
  - Acceptance: Values must conform to the stated bore diameter tolerance.
- Forging mass verification
  - Measurement method: Weigh each forging on a calibrated industrial scale and record the mass on the forging mass record.
  - Rationale: Mass control confirms correct material volume and identifies potential leftover flash or incomplete forgings that could affect machining allowance and properties.
  - Acceptance: Any forging exceeding the maximum forging weight must be segregated and evaluated per nonconformance handling.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part that fails to meet the hardness range, bore diameter tolerance, or maximum forging mass shall be clearly identified and isolated from conforming product. Marking and segregation shall be sufficient to prevent inadvertent use.
- Containment actions
  - Stop shipment of suspect lots. Notify quality control and production supervision immediately. Document the nonconformance on the nonconformance report form and attach supporting inspection records.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - Quality personnel shall evaluate the root cause and extent of nonconformance using available inspection data, process records, and operator interviews. Disposition options include rework if feasible, acceptance with concession following engineering approval, or scrap. The disposition decision must be recorded and signed by authorized personnel.
  - Example scenarios: A hardness value below the specified range may indicate heat-treat cycle deviation; corrective actions may include retest of the batch, adjustment of heat-treat parameters, and reheat where metallurgically acceptable. A bore diameter outside tolerance may be returned to machining if material allowance permits; otherwise, follow scrap disposition.
- Records and corrective action tracking
  - Maintain nonconformance reports, inspection logs, calibration certificates, and disposition records in the document control system. Records shall include a description of the issue, affected quantities, investigation summary, root cause, corrective actions taken, and verification of effectiveness.
  - Rationale: Retaining complete records ensures traceability and supports continuous improvement activities.

Records to keep
- Hardness test logs with equipment identification and operator initials.
- Dimensional inspection reports showing measured bore diameters and instrument calibration references.
- Forging mass records showing individual part weights.
- Incoming material certificates and mill test reports.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records.

Notes and rationale
- The specified hardness, bore tolerance, and maximum forging mass are primary acceptance criteria for CFW-2490-88 given their direct impact on performance and interchangeability. The inspection methods are selected to provide objective, verifiable evidence for acceptance decisions. Records generated during inspection and nonconformance handling are mandatory for traceability and corrective action verification.
title: Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (1045)
