# QS-CFW-4922-70 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-4922-70 (8620)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4922-70

Scope

This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection practices for gear blank CFW-4922-70 manufactured from material grade 8620 at Plant P2. The document applies to all forgings identified by the part designation CFW-4922-70 from receipt of forged blanks through final release for downstream machining. It is intended for use by quality inspectors, production supervisors, and material handling personnel to ensure conformity to key functional and safety-related attributes of the gear blank prior to machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale

CFW-4922-70 is a finished blank geometry intended for carburizing and finishing as a power-transmission gear. Dimensional integrity, bore concentricity, and core hardness are primary drivers for part performance and fit in downstream processes. The acceptance criteria in this document isolate critical attributes that must be verified on each lot to reduce rework, scrap, and assembly issues. The specified hardness band balances machinability for pre-machining operations with sufficient core strength to endure subsequent heat treatment and service loads. The bore tolerance controls runout and fit with mating assemblies; the maximum forging weight controls handling, tooling selection, and process capability of forging equipment.

Requirements table

- Attribute: Hardness
  - Requirement: The hardness range for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 38-42 HRC.
  - Applicability: All forgings prior to final release.
  - Acceptance: Within stated hardness range on cross section at the core location specified in drawing.

- Attribute: Bore diameter tolerance
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is ±0.03 mm.
  - Applicability: Bore features intended for press fit or bearing fit as shown on the part drawing.
  - Acceptance: Measured bore diameter must be within nominal dimension plus or minus the stated tolerance.

- Attribute: Forging weight
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-4922-70 (CFW-4922-70) is 69.8 kg.
  - Applicability: Individual blank weight as-recorded on material disposition documentation.
  - Acceptance: Any forging exceeding the stated maximum must be segregated and dispositioned as nonconforming.

Inspection method

General

Inspectors shall employ calibrated measurement equipment and documented methods to verify each attribute. All instruments used shall have valid calibration status traceable to the laboratory control system. For each lot, record the instrument identification and operator initials on the inspection record.

Hardness testing

Perform hardness verification on an as-forged cross section representative of the bulk material. Use a hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale with a correctly specified indenter for steel substrates. Prepare the test surface to remove scale and to provide a flat, smooth area sufficient for an accurate indenter reading. Take readings at the core location defined on the engineering drawing for CFW-4922-70. Document individual readings and calculate the observed range for the part sampled. Compare to the requirement in the requirements table. If the sample reading approaches the limits of the range, take additional independent measurements on the same part and on additional parts from the lot to confirm conformance.

Bore diameter measurement

Measure bore diameter using a bore gauge or internal micrometer with calibration certificates on file. Ensure the measuring instrument is zeroed and the part is stabilized at ambient shop conditions prior to measurement. When measuring, take multiple cross-sectional readings at normal intervals around the bore to detect out-of-round conditions. Record the nominal drawing diameter and each measured value on the inspection record. Calculate the deviation from nominal and verify the deviation is within the tolerance stated in the requirements table. For a bore with nonuniform geometry, follow the drawing callouts for the inspection location.

Weight verification

Verify forging weight using scales appropriate for the stated maximum weight. Record the measured weight on the inspection record and compare to the requirement. If the measured weight equals or is less than the stated maximum, forward the part for normal processing. If the measured weight exceeds the stated maximum, follow nonconformance handling procedures.

Records and examples

Inspection records shall include the following for each lot: part designation CFW-4922-70, lot identifier, inspector name or initials, instrument identification and calibration status, hardness readings and locations, bore measurements with locations, measured weight, and final disposition. Example entries are provided in the QMS inspection form template. All records shall be retained in the document control or quality records repository in accordance with company retention policy for traceability to the lot.

Nonconformance handling

Segregation

Any forging that fails to meet a requirement in the requirements table shall be immediately segregated and clearly labeled as nonconforming. Segregated stock shall be stored separate from conforming inventory and access limited to authorized personnel.

Disposition

The quality engineer or designee shall review nonconforming material and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, return to supplier, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. Disposition decisions shall be documented on the nonconformance report and include the specific attribute(s) that failed, measured values, and justification for the selected disposition.

Containment and root cause

For process escapes or repeated nonconformances, containment actions must be initiated to prevent additional nonconforming parts from entering downstream operations. Conduct a root cause analysis involving production, tooling, and materials personnel to identify corrective actions. Implement corrective actions and verify effectiveness with additional inspection records showing compliance to the stated requirements.

Notification and records

Notify affected stakeholders when a lot is dispositioned as nonconforming, including production scheduling and downstream process owners. Maintain nonconformance records including disposition rationale, corrective action plan, and verification evidence in the quality system. The inspection records described above shall be appended to the nonconformance report when applicable.

This specification is the governing acceptance standard for part CFW-4922-70 at Plant P2. Compliance with the stated requirements is mandatory prior to releasing forgings for subsequent processing.
title: Quality specification - gear blank CFW-4922-70 (8620)

# QS-CFW-4068-79 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (52100)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-4068-79

Scope
This quality specification defines mandatory acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 forged from steel grade 52100. It applies to all forgings produced at Plant P3 for this part number and to any subcontracted forging operations performed on behalf of Cascade Forge Works. The intent is to ensure consistent hardness, dimensional control, and safe forging mass prior to subsequent machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Bearing rings for this product are critical components in rotating assemblies. Control of hardness and bore geometric stability entering the machine shop reduces scrap and rework, improves bearing life, and lowers total cost. The specified hardness range balances wear resistance and toughness for the selected steel grade. The specified bore tolerance ensures proper running clearance after finishing operations. The maximum forging weight is defined to ensure safe handling and to match the capabilities of in-plant forging and handling equipment.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory acceptance criteria to be verified for each production lot. Any item not clearly conforming to the stated requirement must be recorded and handled per the nonconformance handling section.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material grade | 52100 |
| Part identification | CFW-4068-79 |
| Hardness (as-formed or after specified heat operation prior to final machining) | 35-40 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.07 mm |
| Maximum forging weight | 91.7 kg |
| Surface condition | Free of seams, laps, and forging defects that jeopardize machinability or integrity; machining allowance maintained where applicable |
| Identification marking | Legible part and heat traceability marking per plant marking standard |

Inspection method
General principles
Inspections shall be carried out by trained quality personnel or designated inspectors. Inspectors shall use calibrated equipment traceable to applicable calibration standards maintained by Plant P3. When sampling is used, samples shall be representative of the production lot and the sampling rationale shall be documented in the inspection record.

Hardness verification
Hardness shall be measured on the forged ring at locations that are representative of the bore region and the ring cross section. Measurements shall be made using an instrument appropriate for HRC scale. The measured hardness values must fall within the specified hardness range of 35-40 HRC. If initial measurements are outside of this range, additional discrete measurements shall be made across the ring to assess the extent of deviation. Records shall state measured locations, measured values, instrument identification, and operator identification.

Bore tolerance verification
Bore diameter shall be measured using an appropriate internal sizing method capable of resolving the required tolerance. Measurement shall confirm the bore is within the specified tolerance of ±0.07 mm relative to the nominal drawing dimension. For rings with interrupted or out-of-round conditions, multiple measurements in different radial positions shall be recorded. The measurement technique and instrument used shall be recorded on the inspection record.

Mass verification
The forging weight shall be checked to ensure the forging does not exceed the maximum forging weight of 91.7 kg. Scales used for mass verification must be calibrated and traceable to plant calibration records. Where a forging is found above the maximum forging weight, it shall be segregated and processed through the nonconformance workflow.

Surface and visual inspection
All forgings shall be visually inspected for surface discontinuities, laps, cracks, and foreign material that may affect subsequent processing. Inspectors shall verify machining allowance areas are intact and that no scarfing removed required stock. Visual inspection findings shall be annotated in the inspection record and supported with photographic evidence for any indication graded as potentially consequential.

Sampling and documentation
When full inspection of each item is impractical, a documented sampling justification must be attached to the lot inspection record. The sampling justification shall include the lot definition and the rationale for the selected sample items. For each inspected item, the inspection record shall include identification of the part, material heat number, measured values for each characteristic, instrument identifiers, inspector initials, and disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Any forging that fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table shall be marked and segregated immediately from conforming material. Segregation shall prevent inadvertent use of nonconforming forgings in production.

Disposition options
Disposition of nonconforming forgings shall follow one of the documented options: rework, scrap, or use as-is under authorized concession. Rework proposals must include a documented method and verification steps demonstrating the final part will meet all specified requirements. Scrap must be processed per plant material control procedures. Use-as-is concessions require formal engineering authorization and must reference the specific deviation and the risk mitigation plan.

Documentation and records
All nonconformances shall be recorded in the plant quality system with a description of the nonconformance, measured evidence, photographs where applicable, proposed disposition, and final approval. Records shall include the inspector name, date of discovery, associated heat number, and disposition authority. For any concession granted, the record shall include the justification, engineering approval, and any applicable customer notification.

Examples
Example 1: A forging shows local hardness readings below the specified range. The inspector documents measurement points and values, segregates the lot, and initiates an investigation. If heat treatment correction is feasible and documented to restore hardness into 35-40 HRC, rework may be permitted with verification testing.

Example 2: A forging measures outside the bore tolerance of ±0.07 mm in one radial position. The inspector records multiple radial measurements, marks the part as nonconforming, and proposes corrective machining. Corrective machining shall be evaluated to ensure final geometry will meet drawing requirements and is documented prior to release.

Records to keep
- Lot inspection report including part identification CFW-4068-79 and material 52100.  
- Hardness measurement log with instrument identifiers and measured values.  
- Bore measurement records with instrument identification and measured locations.  
- Mass verification record showing measured mass versus maximum forging weight 91.7 kg.  
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records, including photographic evidence and engineering approvals.

Approval and implementation
This specification is effective at Plant P3 for all production and subcontract forgings of CFW-4068-79. Compliance with the listed requirements is mandatory; deviations require formal engineering concession and documented approval.
title: Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (52100)

# QS-CFW-7855-84 Quality specification - valve body CFW-7855-84 (F316)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-7855-84

Scope
This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) forged in F316 material at Plant P1. It applies to all incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and final machined valve bodies delivered to internal assembly or customer shipment. Background and rationale: valve body sealing and mechanical performance are driven by material hardness, internal bore geometry, and control of forging mass. The requirements herein are chosen to balance machinability, toughness, and dimensional stability for this geometry and alloy.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the part. Values are batch-level pass/fail limits to be used by production and quality control.

- Characteristic: Hardness (post-forge, prior to final machining)  
  Requirement: The hardness range for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 32-36 HRC.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter tolerancing (as-forged or after rough bore operation where specified on the print)  
  Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is ±0.05 mm.

- Characteristic: Forging mass (as cast/forged blank condition, prior to finish machining)  
  Requirement: The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 105.0 kg.

Notes on table application
- Hardness is specified on the as-forged or heat-treated condition referenced on manufacturing travelers. The range is intended to prevent excessive hardness that would impede machining and to retain sufficient strength for service. Hardness outside the range is treated as nonconforming unless dispositioned per the nonconformance handling section.
- Bore diameter tolerance applies to specified bores identified on the engineering drawing for this part. For assemblies requiring interference or clearance fits, the drawing overrides this table and must be consulted first. The tolerance is a final-inspection acceptance band; process controls should target a centered nominal value to reduce scrap.
- Maximum forging weight is used to screen incoming blanks and to control forging die life and handling capacity. Shipments of blanks heavier than the stated maximum must be rejected or returned unless an approved deviation is issued.

Inspection method
General principles
Inspections shall be performed by trained quality personnel using calibrated equipment traceable to the plant calibration program. Records listed below must be retained in the document control system and linked to each lot or serial number.

Hardness inspection
- Location: Hardness shall be measured at the locations defined on the inspection drawing or on representative surfaces that are not affected by machining or scale removal. Where multiple readings are required per part, follow the sampling pattern on the inspection traveler.
- Equipment: Use Rockwell hardness testers configured for the Rockwell C scale. Ensure indenter and load are appropriate for HRC measurements and that the unit is within current calibration.
- Acceptance: Report each reading and the lot average. Compare results against the requirement: The hardness range for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 32-36 HRC. Parts or lots with readings outside this range require disposition.

Bore diameter inspection
- Location: Measure the bore at the intended functional surfaces and at locations specified on the drawing. Take measurements after any rough-boring operation and again after final machining as required by the process step.
- Equipment: Use calibrated bore gauges or internal micrometers suitable for the bore geometry. Surface finish and geometry may require specialized gauges; use non-deforming contact methods for soft or unfinished surfaces.
- Acceptance: Each measured bore must meet the tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is ±0.05 mm. Record individual measurements, the nominal target dimension from the drawing, and whether the measurement lies within the allowable band.

Forging weight inspection
- Location: Weigh the forging blank after derusting and prior to major machining operations that remove significant mass.
- Equipment: Use calibrated scales or load cells consistent with plant calibration practice.
- Acceptance: Verify that the blank does not exceed the stated limit: The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) is 105.0 kg. If a blank exceeds this mass, segregate and notify quality and production engineering for investigation.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A lot of blanks shows a hardness average near the lower bound but with occasional readings below the range. These parts should be quarantined and a root cause analysis conducted to determine whether heat treatment or cooling variations caused the deviation. Rework by approved heat treatment may be considered if metallurgical evaluation supports it.
- Example: A bore measured at final inspection is outside the ±0.05 mm band on one axis due to ovality. The part should be evaluated for machining correction if the drawing allows material removal; otherwise, designate as scrap or reworkable per disposition.

Records to keep
- Hardness test reports with individual readings and equipment calibration identifier.  
- Bore measurement records including gauge identifier, nominal dimension, and measured values.  
- Weight records for each blank with scale identifier.  
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions when a requirement is not met.  
- Traveler or process sheet linking inspection records to the batch or serial number.

Nonconformance handling
Initial screening and quarantine
- Any part or lot failing to meet the hardness, bore tolerance, or forging weight requirements must be clearly marked and segregated from conforming material. Do not proceed to assembly or shipment.

Investigation and disposition
- Quality shall initiate an investigation to determine the root cause of the nonconformance. Actions may include review of heat-treatment records, operator logs, tooling condition, and incoming raw material certificates. Where corrective heat treatment, machining, or other rework is feasible and documented, a formal disposition must be issued before returning parts to production.
- Dispositions must be documented and retained with the inspection records. Records must state the corrective action taken and the verification method to confirm acceptance after rework.

Customer notification and reporting
- If nonconformance affects material previously shipped or is a systematic process failure, notify the customer per plant communication procedures and retain copies of the notification and corrective action report.

Final note
Adherence to this specification ensures consistent part performance and reduces downstream rework. All personnel performing inspections or dispositions on valve body CFW-7855-84 (CFW-7855-84) must be familiar with this document and the associated inspection travelers and drawings.

# QS-CFW-4713-78 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-4713-78 (4140)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4713-78

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the manufactured axle hub identified as CFW-4713-78, forged from material designated 4140 at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, mandatory inspection methods, records to retain, and the nonconformance handling process for production, finishing, and final inspection prior to release to shipping or assembly.
- The intent is to ensure consistent mechanical properties and dimensional conformity for service use. Background rationale: the chosen hardness and bore tolerance reflect required performance for fitment and wear life while the maximum forging weight limit is to ensure safe material handling and appropriate process controls during forging and heat treatment.

Requirements table
- The following table lists mandatory acceptance criteria. These criteria are to be applied to every lot presented for final inspection. Where values are stated, they are mandatory and testing or measuring equipment shall be calibrated to national or internal standards; records of calibration shall accompany inspection records.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material | 4140 (as specified on part drawing and heat treat route) |
| Hardness (post-process) | The hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 29-32 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, cracks, and foreign inclusions that affect function (visual and tactile confirmation) |
| Threaded features and mating faces | Must meet drawing geometry and be free of galling and burrs that prevent assembly |

Inspection method
- Visual inspection
  - Perform a visual assessment under standard shop lighting to detect surface discontinuities, laps, scale, or other defects. Use magnification when necessary to clarify questionable features. Record observations on the final inspection form.
- Dimensional inspection
  - Measure bore diameter using a calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Verify conformity to the bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm. When measuring, ensure gauge contact surfaces are clean and gauge temperature has stabilized to ambient shop conditions.
  - Measure other drawing-controlled dimensions as applicable to confirm fit. Use calibrated instruments and capture raw readings and instrument identification on the inspection record.
- Hardness testing
  - Test hardness in the machined, finished condition at locations specified on the part drawing. The hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 29-32 HRC. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and follow standard test practice for the chosen indenter. Document test locations, instrument ID, operator, and individual hardness readings on the inspection record.
- Weight verification
  - Confirm forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg. Use calibrated scales and include scale ID and weight reading on the material handling record. If the forging weight approaches the maximum, tag and segregate the part pending engineering disposition.
- Sampling and acceptance
  - Inspection shall follow the inspection plan for the part. When sampling is used for lot acceptance, ensure the sampling rationale and results are documented and justified in the lot record. Any measured value outside the stated requirement is a nonconformance.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any unit that fails to meet the hardness range, bore diameter tolerance, maximum forging weight, or other drawing requirement must be clearly identified and physically segregated from conforming product. Use the nonconforming product tag and store in a designated quarantine area.
- Documentation
  - Complete a nonconformance report that includes part identification, manufacturing lot or heat number, description of nonconformance, measured values, inspection records, and photographs where useful. Reference the inspection record and equipment calibration entries that produced the measurement.
- Disposition options
  - Notify quality engineering and production supervision immediately for review. Disposition may include rework where permitted by engineering, return to heat treatment or machining if allowed by the process control plan, use-as-is only with documented customer approval, or scrap. Any rework must be carried out per documented procedures and followed by reinspection.
- Root cause and corrective action
  - For confirmed nonconformances, perform a root cause analysis and document corrective actions. Include process step controls or inspection additions intended to prevent recurrence. Record effectiveness checks in the quality system records.

Records to keep
- Final inspection report with instrument IDs, operator initials, and actual hardness readings at each test location. Ensure the hardness range for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is clearly referenced.
- Dimensional inspection records showing bore measurements and confirmation that the bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is ±0.04 mm.
- Material and forging weight records including scale ID and verification that the maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-4713-78 (CFW-4713-78) is 106.1 kg.
- Calibration certificates for all measuring equipment used and operator training records for inspection personnel.
- Nonconformance reports and corrective action records associated with this part number.

Examples and step rationale
- Example: a hub presented with a bore measurement outside the stated tolerance must be tagged and held. Rationale: bore fit affects bearing seating and axial runout; immediate segregation avoids downstream assembly failures.
- Example: a hardness test yielding a reading below the specified range requires review of heat treat records. Rationale: hardness correlates to strength and fatigue life; correcting the thermal process or segregating the material prevents field failures.
- Example: a forging exceeding the maximum forging weight is handled as a handling and process control risk. Rationale: tooling and material flow are validated up to the stated maximum; heavier forgings may not meet process assumptions and can cause tool damage or process variability.

Approval and responsibilities
- Production is responsible for initial inspection and identification. Quality is responsible for final disposition and record retention. Engineering provides dispositions for rework and approves any deviations.

End of document.

# QS-CFW-1159-60 - Quality specification - track link CFW-1159-60 (15B37)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-1159-60

## Scope
This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection practices, and nonconformance handling for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) produced at Plant P3. It applies to all forged, heat treated, and machined track links delivered under part number CFW-1159-60 for customer orders and internal inventory. The document defines required measurements, allowable tolerances, inspection methods, documentation to be retained, and disposition instructions for nonconforming material.

Background and intent: track links are safety-critical wear components. The controls in this specification are intended to ensure dimensional accuracy, material condition, and hardness consistent with design requirements and downstream assembly fitment. Where measurement choices require judgment, the inspection method section provides examples and rationale to support consistent application by quality and production personnel.

## Requirements

| Item | Requirement | Acceptance |
|------|-------------|------------|
| Hardness | The hardness range for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 36-40 HRC. | Must be within stated range across inspected locations. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is ±0.03 mm. | Measured bore diameter must be within nominal plus or minus stated tolerance. |
| Forging weight | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-1159-60 (CFW-1159-60) is 80.0 kg. | Raw forging weight must not exceed stated maximum. |

Notes on table application: Acceptance applies to sampled or 100 percent inspected parts as specified in the production routing and as required by the purchase order. References to "nominal" in the bore entry refer to the drawing nominal diameter called out on the engineering drawing for CFW-1159-60.

## Inspection method

General approach: Inspection shall verify each requirement in the table using calibrated instruments and documented procedures. Inspectors shall be trained on the equipment and methods used and shall follow practices that minimize measurement variation.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness shall be verified using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the HRC scale and operated per the instrument manufacturer's procedure. Impact of surface finish and case depth shall be considered; measures shall be taken to ensure a representative test surface (for example, removal of heavy scale, light surface grinding to reveal base material if required). When testing multiple locations, select points representative of typical load-bearing areas and areas away from heavy machining features. Record individual readings and calculate the observed range for the part lot. The acceptance criterion is the stated requirement in the requirements table.

Bore diameter measurement
- Bore diameter shall be measured using appropriately calibrated bore gauges, internal micrometers, or coordinate measuring machines capable of resolving the stated tolerance. When using manual plug gauges for quick checks, they are suitable only for go/no-go acceptance and must be supplemented by dimensional measurement during initial lot qualification or when process variation is suspected. For CMM measurement, use a probing strategy that avoids runout artifacts and records the measured nominal diameter for each bore. The stated tolerance is applied directly to the nominal drawing dimension.

Forging weight verification
- Forging weight shall be established at the forging operation by weighing the forged blank on calibrated scales. The maximum forging weight is the limit for feedstock and die charges. Record the weight for each heat or batch as part of the batch manufacturing record. If trimming operations remove material before subsequent operations, ensure the raw forging weight at release does not exceed the stated maximum.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A batch of track links with hardness readings of 37 HRC, 38 HRC, and 36 HRC is acceptable because all readings fall within the stated hardness range. An isolated reading below the stated range requires disposition per nonconformance handling.
- Example: A bore measured at nominal plus 0.02 mm is acceptable; a bore measured at nominal plus 0.04 mm is not acceptable against the stated tolerance.

Calibration and equipment
- All measuring equipment used to verify the requirements must be in calibration and traceable to internal calibration records. Calibration records and equipment identification must be retained in the quality record for the lot.

Records to keep
- Heat/batch manufacturing record including forging weight for each forged blank.
- Hardness test records showing individual readings, test locations, test instrument identification, and operator initials.
- Dimensional inspection report for bore diameters with instrument identification and measurement method.
- Calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore measurement devices, scales, and CMM probes used for the inspections.

## Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation
- Any part or lot that fails to meet a requirement in the requirements table shall be clearly marked and physically segregated to prevent unintended use. Segregation shall be maintained until a disposition decision is recorded.

Disposition process
- The case shall be documented with the observed nonconformance, measured values, inspection evidence, and batch manufacturing records. The responsible quality engineer shall initiate a formal disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, repair, use-as-is with approval, or scrap. Rework or repair must be evaluated to ensure no compromise to material integrity or part function.

Required documentation
- Nonconformance reports shall include batch identity, forging weight record, hardness test records, dimensional inspection records, and photographs where applicable. The report shall describe containment actions and recommended disposition. The final disposition must be recorded and signed by the authorized quality representative.

Containment and corrective actions
- For process deviations that produce out-of-specification characteristics, containment measures shall include additional inspection of suspect lots and review of upstream process steps. Root-cause analysis and corrective actions shall be documented and retained with the nonconformance record.

Retention and audit
- All records described under Records to keep and nonconformance documentation shall be retained per the plant document control policy and made available for internal audit and customer review on request.

Revision control
- Changes to this specification shall be controlled through the plant document control process.
title: Quality specification - track link CFW-1159-60 (15B37)

# QS-CFW-9497-56 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-9497-56 (4140) Rev A

Scope
- This quality specification applies to raw forged flange blanks identified as CFW-9497-56 produced at Plant P1. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for material, dimensional tolerance, hardness, and weight control for the stated part.
- The document covers incoming material verification from the heat treatment supplier, production forging release inspection at P1, and final inspection prior to delivery to the machining cell. It does not supersede customer drawing notes; where customer drawing and this specification conflict, escalate to engineering for disposition.

Requirements table
- Part: CFW-9497-56
- Material: 4140 (as specified on purchase order)
- Hardness: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 31-34 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg.
- Surface condition: Forged surfaces shall be free from scale, laps, cracks, and other discontinuities that would prevent machining or cause rejection under visual acceptance criteria.
- Identification: Each blank shall be identified with batch and heat information legibly marked or tagged to support traceability to mill test reports and heat treatment records.

Inspection method
Background and rationale
- Inspection steps prioritize traceability and prevention of downstream rejection. Hardness is verified on the forging as received to confirm heat treatment stability prior to machining. Bore dimensional control is critical for assembly fit; therefore, inspection uses calibrated gauges and measurement procedures that target the bore specified on the drawing. Weight control ensures die wear or fill issues are identified early; a maximum forging weight limit is specified to prevent overfilled impressions that could hide defects or exceed handling constraints.

Measurement procedures
- Hardness verification: Select at least two locations on each blank representative of the region specified on the drawing. Perform hardness testing using a calibrated portable hardness tester following the manufacturer procedure and accepted method in the plant quality manual. Record each reading and the location on the part. If readings fall within the specified range, mark the part as inspected. If any reading is outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling.
- Bore measurement: Measure the bore using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment set up to measure the feature specified on the customer drawing. The bore will be accepted only if measured values fall within the nominal dimension plus or minus the specified tolerance. The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm. Record measurement device identification, calibration status, operator, and measurement results in the inspection record.
- Weight verification: Weigh each blank on a calibrated scale and record the value. The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg. If the measured weight exceeds that value, quarantine the part and initiate nonconformance handling.
- Visual and dimensional inspection: Conduct a visual inspection for surface defects and a dimensional check of key features as specified on the drawing. Use calibrated instruments for critical dimensions. Document the inspector, date, and inspection station.

Examples and acceptance rationale
- Example acceptance scenario: A blank with hardness readings of values within the stated hardness range, a bore measurement within the specified bore diameter tolerance, and a weight below the maximum forging weight is released to machining. The combination of checks ensures metallurgical properties and dimensional conformity prior to further processing.
- Example rejection scenario: A blank with a hardness reading below the lower limit of the specified hardness range or above the upper limit, or with a bore measurement falling outside the specified bore diameter tolerance, or with a measured weight above the maximum forging weight shall be treated as nonconforming.

Records to keep
- Maintain a traceable inspection record for each batch that includes:
  - Part identifier and batch or heat number.
  - Material certificate reference from the mill.
  - Hardness test locations, individual readings, device identification, and calibration status.
  - Bore measurement results, measurement device identification, calibration status, operator, and date.
  - Measured weight and scale identification and calibration status.
  - Visual inspection findings and disposition.
  - Inspector name or identifier and date of inspection.
- Store records in the plant document control system for retention according to Plant P1 retention policy and to support customer or internal audits.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any blank that fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table shall be immediately identified as nonconforming, tagged, and moved to the nonconforming material area. Do not return nonconforming blanks to inventory or machining without formal disposition.
- Notification and documentation: The inspector shall complete a nonconformance report that describes the failed characteristic, reference to this specification, measured values, and any immediate containment actions. Include supporting records such as hardness printouts, bore measurement records, and weight records.
- Disposition options: Engineering or quality shall review the nonconformance report and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, use-as-is with documented concession, return to supplier, or scrap. Rework must have a documented method and acceptance criteria and shall be approved by engineering before execution.
- Example disposition rationale: If a blank exceeds the maximum forging weight, engineering may determine that the excess indicates overfill and potential internal defects; return to supplier or scrap may be appropriate. If a hardness reading is marginal and consistent across the batch, engineering may require full batch testing or heat-treatment rework.
- Final verification: Any product released from nonconforming status must be re-inspected and documented. The re-inspection record shall reference the original nonconformance report and show evidence that the disposition criteria have been met.

Revision control
- This revision applies to flange blanks CFW-9497-56 produced at Plant P1 and is Rev A. All inspectors and engineers working with this part shall follow the procedures and recordkeeping detailed above.
title: Quality specification - flange blank CFW-9497-56 (4140)

# QS-CFW-7185-40 Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (4340)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-7185-40

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (4340) produced at Plant P2. It applies to all incoming forgings, in-process blanks, and finished blanks identified as CFW-7185-40. The objective is to ensure material, dimensional, and hardness requirements meet downstream machining and performance expectations.

Background and rationale
- CFW-7185-40 is a 4340 alloy crankshaft blank that must meet tight hardness and bore tolerance requirements to control machining performance, crankshaft balance, and fatigue life after subsequent heat treatment and finish operations. The specified hardness range limits the amount of hardenability and work hardening introduced during forging and prior handling. Bore dimensional control ensures fitment accuracy in downstream operations and alignment of main bearing journals. Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure handling equipment and heat treatment loads remain within certified capacities for plant P2 tooling and furnaces.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the controlled attributes and acceptance criteria for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40).

| Attribute | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Hardness range | The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is 39-42 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is ±0.07 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40) is 117.8 kg. |

Inspection method
- Material verification
  - Verify raw material certification and traceability for each heat lot against purchase documentation and mill test report. Confirm alloy designation matches 4340 and associated chemical compliance per incoming material procedures. Record material heat identifiers with the production lot record.
- Visual inspection
  - Inspect each blank for surface discontinuities, laps, and forging defects using daylight and clean surface conditions. Remove light scale if necessary to reveal surface indications before acceptance evaluation. Document any visible defects on the inspection record and photograph defects that are unclear or borderline for review.
- Dimensional inspection (bores and critical features)
  - Establish a dedicated inspection setup for measuring bore diameters using calibrated measuring equipment appropriate for the feature size and geometry. Verify operator competence and calibration status are recorded on the measurement log. Measure the bore(s) and record the nominal measurement and deviation. Acceptance is based on meeting the bore diameter tolerance.
  - Example: If the measured deviation is within the bore diameter tolerance for the part, accept the blank and proceed to process control records. If the deviation exceeds tolerance, follow the nonconformance handling procedure below.
- Hardness inspection
  - Perform hardness testing on specified locations on the blank using a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC measurement. Ensure surface preparation meets testing equipment requirements to obtain reliable readings. Record individual hardness readings and the location for traceability. Acceptance requires the measured hardness to fall within the specified hardness range.
  - Example: If hardness measurements are within the hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40), log results in the inspection report and release the part for downstream operations.
- Weight verification
  - Confirm forging weight by comparing shop floor scale records against the maximum forging weight requirement. Record the measured weight on the production traveler.
  - Example: If the measured forging weight is equal to or less than the maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40), continue normal processing. If the measured weight exceeds the maximum forging weight, initiate the nonconformance handling steps below.

Inspection records to keep
- Material heat certificate and traceability record for each lot.
- Visual inspection log including defect descriptions and photographs for atypical findings.
- Dimensional inspection log showing nominal measurements, deviations, measurement locations, and inspector identification.
- Hardness test log showing test locations, individual readings, equipment identification, and calibration status.
- Forging weight record from the shop floor scale with operator initials.
- Final disposition record for each blank indicating accept, rework, or scrap, with justification and reviewer signature.
- Retain inspection records in the document control system according to Plant P2 retention policy and make available to quality audits and customer requests.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any blank failing to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be clearly identified as nonconforming and segregated from conforming inventory to prevent unintended use. Use visual tags and physical separation at the point of discovery.
- Initial containment and notification
  - The inspector records the nonconformance on the nonconformance report and notifies the production lead and quality engineer. Provide complete measurement data, photographs, and material traceability to support disposition.
- Disposition options
  - Accept: Only allowed if an approved engineering deviation exists. The deviation must reference the affected attribute and provide clear justification and approval by authorized engineering personnel.
  - Rework: If the nonconformance is judged remediable (for example, machining to correct bore within tolerance), document the rework instructions, responsible party, and reinspection requirements. Reinspection must confirm compliance with the original requirement before release.
  - Scrap: When rework is not feasible and no deviation is approved, the blank is to be scrapped. Document scrap reason and record material disposition.
- Example disposition scenarios
  - Example: A blank exhibits hardness below the hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40). If engineering authorizes reheat and quench corrective action, the reheat process must be documented and the blank requalified via hardness testing and dimensional inspection before release. If no corrective action is authorized, scrap the blank and record the decision.
  - Example: A bore measurement deviates beyond the bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (CFW-7185-40). If machining allowance remains and rework can restore the feature to within tolerance without compromising part integrity, document the rework and reinspection. If not, disposition as scrap or request an engineering deviation.
- Corrective action and records
  - For all nonconformances, initiate corrective action as appropriate to prevent recurrence. Document root cause analysis, containment actions, corrective steps, responsible owners, and completion evidence in the corrective action record. Link corrective actions to the affected production lot and retain records for audit.
- Escalation
  - For production impacts or repeated nonconformances with the same characteristic, escalate to plant quality management for further review and potential process changes.

Notes
- All measurement equipment used for acceptance testing must be calibrated and traceable. Calibration records are maintained with inspection equipment documentation.
- Any approved engineering deviations or special dispositions must be recorded and attached to the lot’s quality records.
title: Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-7185-40 (4340)

# QS-CFW-4516-94 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (1045)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4516-94

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for the forging and finishing of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94) manufactured in Plant P3 from 1045 material. The document applies to all incoming forgings, in-process operations, and final functional inspections prior to release to assembly or external shipment. It covers metallurgical hardness, critical bore geometry, forging weight limits, visual and dimensional requirements where they affect fit or function, and the required records to demonstrate compliance.

Background and rationale
Connecting rod performance is controlled by core material properties and tight geometry at critical features. Hardness is used as a proxy for heat treatment and tensile properties; observed service and qualification testing require the rod to achieve a specific hardness band to ensure fatigue performance and bearing compatibility. Bore diameter tolerance is critical for journal fit and bearing clearance after machining; controlling bore tolerance at the forging stage minimizes downstream machining risk and ensures consistent wall thickness. Forging weight is controlled to manage die fill, internal soundness, and to limit defects associated with over- or under-filled impressions.

Requirements table
The following table lists the mandatory acceptance criteria for the part. These are minimum inspection limits and must be met for release.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes / Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (through or core, as applicable) | 28-32 HRC | Measured per inspection method below. Parts outside this band are rejected. |
| Bore diameter tolerance (unmachined forging ID) | ±0.10 mm | Measure at specified inspection locations; see Inspection Method. |
| Maximum forging weight (as-forged, prior to trim) | 28.4 kg | Weigh part on calibrated scale; parts over limit are rejected and investigated. |

Inspection method
General
Inspections shall be performed by qualified personnel using calibrated instruments. Calibration certificates for measurement equipment must be retained with the inspection records. Environmental conditions that materially affect measurement must be recorded in the inspection log.

Hardness measurement
Hardness testing shall be performed on representative locations that reflect core and critical cross-section properties. Use a method appropriate to HRC scale; ensure the test impression is placed where it will not be removed in subsequent processing or affect fit. Record the reading and the measurement location. If a part yields a reading outside 28-32 HRC, perform two additional measurements at other representative locations; if any measurement remains outside the requirement, the part lot is nonconforming.

Bore diameter measurement
Measure the unmachined forging internal diameter at the bore midspan and at a near-end location to verify uniformity. Use calibrated bore gauges or a coordinate measuring device to achieve sufficient resolution. Acceptance is based on the unmachined bore being within ±0.10 mm of the nominal drawing size supplied with the part release. Document all readings, gauge identification, and operator.

Weight measurement
Weigh each forging on a calibrated industrial scale. Record the net as-forged weight and scale calibration ID. Any forging exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg must be quarantined and evaluated for die fill issues, trimming errors, or potential internal anomalies. For lots where multiple parts exceed the limit, initiate an investigation per Nonconformance Handling.

Additional inspections and sampling
Visual inspection for surface defects that would impair fit or fatigue life shall be performed on all parts. Metallurgical sampling or nondestructive testing may be required based on prior history or when anomalies are detected during dimensional or hardness inspection. All sampling plans and subsequent results must be recorded.

Inspection records to keep
- Hardness readings with location and tester ID.  
- Bore diameter measurements with gauge/coordinate device ID.  
- Individual part weight records with scale calibration reference.  
- Visual inspection checklist and imagery for any nonconforming indications.  
- Traceability linking the forging to the heat lot and process route.  
All records must be retained according to Plant P3 document retention policy and be available for internal audit and customer review.

Nonconformance handling
Initial disposition
Any part or lot that fails to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be segregated and marked as nonconforming immediately. Do not release nonconforming parts for assembly or shipment.

Containment and evaluation
Perform containment to prevent further processing of affected material. Evaluate the extent of the nonconformance by determining if it is isolated to individual forgings or systemic across a production run. For hardness and bore tolerance failures, review the associated heat lot and die set run records to identify potential root causes. For parts exceeding the maximum forging weight of 28.4 kg, inspect the die trim and flash removal process and verify die maintenance records.

Disposition options and rationale
Acceptable dispositions include rework that demonstrably returns the part to conformance and is allowed by engineering drawing notes; controlled segregation for noncritical internal uses only if approved by engineering; or scrap. Rework that would alter the metallurgical condition (e.g., heat treatment) must be documented and validated by engineering prior to implementation. Parts that fail hardness criteria are generally not eligible for rework to meet mechanical property requirements without a documented and approved heat treatment plan. Parts exceeding the forging weight limit are often indicative of overfill and potential internal defects and must be evaluated for soundness before any rework decision.

Examples
Example of hardness failure response: a single forging reads outside 28-32 HRC at two locations. The lot is quarantined; three additional forgings from the same heat are sampled. If multiple parts are out of range, halt production, notify metallurgy, and coordinate a corrective action that may include hold, rework approval, or scrap. Record decisions and supporting test data.

Example of bore tolerance failure response: if an unmachined bore is outside ±0.10 mm, perform inspection of adjacent forgings in the run. If the issue is isolated, scrap or rework per engineering discretion; if systematic, review die fit, mandrel condition, and process parameters.

Records and corrective action
All nonconforming reports, investigation findings, root cause analyses, and corrective actions must be documented and retained with the lot quality file. Corrective actions should address immediate containment and long-term prevention, and shall include verification steps to confirm effectiveness.

Revision and control
This specification supersedes prior versions for Plant P3 production of connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (CFW-4516-94). Any deviations from this document require written engineering approval and must be recorded with justification and sign-off.
title: Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4516-94 (1045)

# QS-CFW-6874-71 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-6874-71 (8620)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6874-71

Scope
This quality specification applies to gear blank CFW-6874-71 manufactured at Plant P1. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for raw forged blanks of material grade 8620. The intent is to ensure consistent mechanical and dimensional characteristics for downstream machining and heat treat operations while providing traceable records for quality assurance and production control.

Requirements table
- Part identification: CFW-6874-71
- Material grade: 8620
- Hardness range for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 38-42 HRC
- Bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): ±0.07 mm
- Maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 113.4 kg
Notes on requirements table:
- The hardness parameter is measured on the as-forged blank prior to any heat treatment or machining. The specified hardness range for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) is intended to verify material condition consistent with forging practice for grade 8620 and to provide a baseline for subsequent processing.
- The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) applies to the principal bore used for fixture and concentricity reference during machining. Acceptance is based on final measured diameter relative to the nominal drawing callout.
- The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) is a handling and process constraint for the forging cell and material handling equipment. Blanks exceeding this weight are to be quarantined and dispositioned.

Inspection method
General approach:
- Visual and dimensional inspections are performed on every shipment lot at receipt and again at the forging cell as part of in-process inspection. Sampling for hardness testing uses a targeted approach to validate process consistency across a production run.
Hardness verification:
- Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Test locations shall be taken at representative positions on the as-forged surface, avoiding scale, heavy decarburized areas, and fillet transitions. Report measured values and verify that the hardness for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) falls within 38-42 HRC. If any reading is outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling below.
Dimensional verification:
- Inspect the bore diameter for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) using calibrated bore gauges or equivalent measurement equipment capable of resolving the specified tolerance. Record the measured bore diameter and compare to nominal. Acceptance requires the bore diameter to be within ±0.07 mm of nominal. Measurements should be taken after any required cleaning of the bore to remove scale or debris.
Weight verification:
- Confirm the forging weight for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71) at the forging cell using calibrated scales or documented weight records from the forging operation. Ensure the forging weight does not exceed 113.4 kg. Blanks stamped or otherwise marked with weight shall be cross-checked to the measured weight where discrepancies are suspected.
Sampling and frequency rationale:
- Sampling aims to balance production flow with statistical confidence in process control. Representative hardness testing across a production run provides timely detection of process drift. Dimensional checks on initial pieces and periodic audit pieces ensure tooling and die wear do not push parts out of tolerance. Weight checks validate charge and handling processes.
Records to keep:
- Inspection report for each lot containing part identification CFW-6874-71, measured hardness values, measured bore diameters, measured forging weight, inspector initials, and any deviations noted.
- Calibration certificates for hardness tester, bore gauge, and scale used for measurements.
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions as required by nonconformance handling.
- Work instructions or tooling change notices that affect bore dimensions or forging charge weight.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation:
- Any blank that fails to meet the hardness range for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 38-42 HRC, the bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): ±0.07 mm, or the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 113.4 kg shall be identified, tagged, and physically segregated from conforming material. Tags must reference the inspection report and note the failed characteristic.
Disposition process:
- Document the nature of the nonconformance in a nonconformance report. Include measured values, photos where applicable, and the location of the part in the process flow.
- Evaluation for rework or repair must consider downstream processing steps and final part function. For dimensional variance of the bore, assess whether machining allowances and fixture strategies can recover the part without compromising net geometry. For hardness excursions, consult metallurgical input to determine if heat treatment or other corrective action is appropriate and whether the part is fit for intended machining and service.
- For weight overage, review forging records to determine cause. Parts exceeding the maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 113.4 kg are typically rejected from the standard production flow and require disposition for special handling or reduction processes.
Examples and rationale:
- Example scenario for hardness: a measured hardness below the range for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): 38-42 HRC may indicate over-tempering or improper cooling. Metallurgical assessment can determine if the part can proceed to heat treat or must be scrapped.
- Example scenario for bore diameter: a bore measurement beyond the tolerance for gear blank CFW-6874-71 (CFW-6874-71): ±0.07 mm may prevent proper fixture seating and result in concentricity errors through machining. Such a part should be evaluated for rework feasibility.
Disposition recording and closure:
- All dispositions must be recorded and closed with documented evidence of final action. Records include the original inspection report, the nonconformance report, disposition decision, corrective action taken, and final verification measurements where applicable. Maintain records in the quality system for traceability to production lots and customer orders.

End of specification.
title: Quality specification - gear blank CFW-6874-71 (8620)

# QS-CFW-6476-89 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-6476-89

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100) manufactured at Plant P2. It applies to forgings and finished rings produced to drawing CFW-6476-89 and to all incoming raw forgings that will be processed and finished under this specification.
- Background and intent: the bearing ring is intended for use in high-cycle radial applications. The requirements reflect material and geometric controls necessary to ensure service life and interchangeability. The controls emphasize hardness, bore geometry, and mass limitations to manage forging integrity and subsequent heat treat response.

Requirements table
- The table below captures the mandatory acceptance criteria. Values in the table are measured as produced and after heat treatment where indicated.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Material designation | 52100 per part drawing CFW-6476-89 |
| Hardness (post heat treat) | The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 29-32 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance (final machined) | The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is ±0.04 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight (as forged) | The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 119.0 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and subsurface discontinuities that would impair machining or final part performance. |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Inspect incoming forgings for conformance to the maximum forging weight requirement by recording the forging mass from the shipping documentation and verifying mass against the forging. If doubt exists, confirm mass on calibrated weighing equipment and record results in the inspection record.
  - Visually inspect for gross forging defects that would prevent machining or heat treatment. Document any findings on the incoming inspection form.
- Dimensional inspection
  - Bore diameter: verify final machined bore conforms to the bore diameter tolerance by measuring at multiple axial locations using a calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer. Measurements must be taken after final machining and before any press-fit operations or heat treatment that could alter the bore. Record the measured bore diameters and note deviations from nominal within the inspection record.
  - Rationale: multiple axial measurements detect taper and localized out-of-round conditions that a single measurement would not capture, reducing risk of assembly issues.
- Hardness verification
  - Hardness shall be measured on the finished bearing ring after final heat treatment and stable temper. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale for HRC. Perform a minimum of three indents in the bearing race area on representative rings across a production run to confirm uniform hardness within the specified range. Ensure indent locations avoid machined surfaces and include areas representative of service loading.
  - Rationale: confirming hardness post heat treat ensures proper transformation and temper; the specified range controls wear resistance and toughness balance for 52100.
- Weight confirmation
  - Verify the forging mass does not exceed the maximum forging weight by reviewing forging records and mass documentation provided by the forging supplier. If forging mass equals or exceeds the maximum forging weight, initiate the nonconformance process.
  - Rationale: controlling forging mass limits flash, nonmetallic inclusion distribution, and material flow during forging, which can affect final microstructure and dimensional accuracy.
- Sample and frequency guidance
  - Inspection frequency and representative sampling shall follow plant inspection practice and known process capability. For routine production, periodic verification of hardness and dimensional stability must be maintained and documented to demonstrate control.
- Measurement equipment and calibration
  - All measurement devices used for verifying the listed requirements must be in a current calibration status traceable to the plant calibration system. Calibration certificates and the equipment identification shall be recorded in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part or forging found outside the requirements table shall be identified, segregated from conforming material, and labeled with a nonconformance tag. The tag shall reference this specification and include a brief description of the nonconformance.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - The responsible quality engineer shall evaluate nonconforming items to determine acceptability for use, rework, or scrap based on root cause and impact to performance. Where hardness is out of range, disposition may include reheat and controlled temper only if metallurgical analysis supports restoration to the specified hardness range. Where bore diameter exceeds tolerance, rework by machining back to draw-on dimensions may be considered only if sufficient material remains and functional geometry can be met without violating drawing limits.
  - Examples of disposition rationale:
    - A ring with hardness below the specified range may indicate under-hardening; reheat followed by a controlled quench and temper may restore properties if microstructure analysis confirms absence of tempering-induced defects.
    - A ring with bore out of tolerance due to machining error may be reworked if final geometry and surface integrity can be restored; otherwise scrap is required.
- Documentation and approval
  - All disposals, rework steps, and final dispositions must be documented on the nonconformance report and approved by the quality engineer. Records must include the nature of the nonconformance, measurements, root cause analysis, corrective actions, authorization for rework or use-as-is, and final disposition.
- Records to keep
  - Maintain the following records in the document control system:
    - Incoming inspection records and forging mass documentation.
    - Final dimensional inspection reports including bore measurements and instrument identification.
    - Hardness test records including tester identification, readings, and locations of indents.
    - Calibration certificates for measuring equipment used.
    - Nonconformance reports with dispositions and approvals.
    - Process change or corrective action records tied to recurrence prevention.
  - Retain records in accordance with plant retention policy and make available for audits and customer review upon request.

Notes
- This specification is authoritative for the listed part at Plant P2. Any deviations or concessions require written approval from quality engineering and operations management.
title: Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100)

# QS-CFW-4376-34 Quality specification - valve body CFW-4376-34 (F316)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4376-34

Scope

This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) machined from F316 forging stock at Plant P3. It defines critical quality requirements that must be met prior to release for assembly and shipment, and it establishes the accepted inspection methods, example acceptance criteria, and required records. Background information is provided to explain the rationale for each requirement and to aid inspection planning and nonconformance disposition.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 31-34 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is ±0.10 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 46.2 kg. |

Inspection method

Overview
- Inspectors must verify each item in the requirements table against the part and associated certification. The inspection sequence should ensure traceability from forging material to final inspected part. The inspection method described here explains equipment selection, calibration requirements rationale, measurement approach, and sample-record examples to be retained.

Hardness verification
- Rationale: Hardness is a proxy for microstructure and heat treatment effectiveness in F316 forgings. The specified hardness controls machinability and wear characteristics while ensuring the material has not been over-tempered.
- Method: Verify hardness using a Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to the appropriate scale for HRC readings. Test locations must be representative of critical wall sections and machined surfaces. Document test locations and results on the inspection record.
- Acceptance: The hardness must meet the hardness range for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 31-34 HRC. Any reading outside this range requires immediate hold of the affected lot and initiation of nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter verification
- Rationale: Bore form and tolerance affect sealing and assembly fit. The process capability of machining and finishing operations must produce bores within the stated tolerance to ensure functional performance.
- Method: Measure the bore using an appropriate bore gauge or plug gauge with calibration traceability. Report the measured diameter and directly compare to the nominal drawing dimension plus or minus the bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is ±0.10 mm. Record the measurement instrument ID and calibration reference on the inspection record.
- Examples: If a measured diameter deviates such that it exceeds the ±0.10 mm tolerance relative to the drawing nominal, flag the part as nonconforming and follow the nonconformance handling procedure in this document.

Forging weight verification
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight is controlled for material procurement, forging die capability, and handling equipment limits. Conformance prevents overloading of equipment and ensures process consistency.
- Method: Verify forging weight using the supplier certificate of conformance and cross-check with the receiving scale report. Confirm that the maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-4376-34 (CFW-4376-34) is 46.2 kg is not exceeded for any unpackaged forging intended for this part number.
- Notes: If a forging exceeds the specified maximum, segregate the material and initiate nonconformance handling.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement instruments used for verification must have up-to-date calibration certificates traceable to an accredited calibration laboratory. Record instrument ID, calibration date, and next-calibration status on the inspection form. Maintain a copy of the calibration certificate with inspection records.

Inspection records to keep
- Retain the following for each inspected lot: part identifier, heat/lot number, hardness readings with locations, bore measurements with instrument ID, forging weight verification notes and certificates, inspector name, and final disposition statement. Ensure records are stored in the document control system and linked to part CFW-4376-34 traceability files.

Nonconformance handling

Detection and immediate actions
- When a nonconformance is detected against any requirement in the requirements table, the inspector shall stop progression of the affected parts and mark the items clearly with a hold status. Provide a written hold tag referencing this document and the failed requirement.

Containment and segregation
- Segregate nonconforming parts from conforming inventory to prevent inadvertent use. Document the location and count of segregated items on the inspection record.

Evaluation and disposition
- Evaluate the nature and extent of the nonconformance through root-cause analysis. Consider rework options only if the corrective action will result in full compliance with the original specification without introducing other defects. Examples of acceptable dispositions include rework to an inspected and documented corrective process that restores compliance, acceptance under a documented engineering deviation, or scrap if recovery is not feasible.

Documentation and approval
- Document the nonconformance, evaluation, proposed disposition, and final approval in the quality system. Include supporting evidence such as hardness test plots, bore measurement logs, supplier certificates, and photographs where applicable. Approval for disposition must be recorded with signatory authority consistent with Plant P3 procedures.

Feedback and corrective action
- For systemic issues, initiate a corrective action to address root causes in forging, heat treatment, or machining processes. Track corrective actions until effectiveness is demonstrated and documented.

Retention of records
- Maintain nonconformance records with the inspection records tied to the affected part number CFW-4376-34 and reference this document identifier. Records must include the initial detection data and final disposition rationale.

Related documents
- None.
title: Quality specification - valve body CFW-4376-34 (F316)
