# QS-CFW-1140-78 Quality specification - axle hub CFW-1140-78 (4140)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1140-78

Scope
This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of the axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) forged from 4140 material in Plant P1. It defines the acceptance criteria for mechanical condition and dimensional features important to fit, function, and downstream machining. This document is mandatory for all production lots and for any rework intended to return parts to saleable condition.

Background and rationale
Axle hubs for heavy equipment require controlled hardness for wear resistance and sufficient toughness for fatigue performance. The bore fits critical mating components; therefore, dimensional tolerance is controlled tightly to ensure consistent assembly and to minimize scrap during finish machining. The maximum forging weight is limited to ensure die life and press capacity, and to control cooling and microstructure uniformity. The specific values in this document reflect validated process capability and incoming material characteristics for the 4140 grade used in Plant P1.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Material | 4140 per procurement specification | Certificate required with each lot |
| Hardness (through radial section after heat treatment) | The hardness range for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 27-32 HRC. | Measured values must fall within the range across inspection locations; statistical trending required for outliers |
| Bore diameter | Machined bore tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is ±0.08 mm. |
| Forging weight | Casting/forging process control | The maximum forging weight for axle hub CFW-1140-78 (CFW-1140-78) is 93.3 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of laps, seams, and forging cracks | Visual and penetrant inspection per Inspection Method below |
| Documentation | Material certificate, process travelers, inspection records | Must be retained per Records to keep below |

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections are performed on a sampling basis defined by the plant quality plan; however, the inspection methods below represent the mandatory tests and measurements that must be performed on initial production pieces, after process changes, and for any suspect lot.

Hardness measurement
- Hardness testing shall be performed on production parts after final heat treatment and prior to finish machining operations. Portable or bench Rockwell testers selected must be calibrated and traceable to calibration standards. Test locations should represent radial distribution and include the bore region and spoke/web area to detect local variations.
- Acceptance criteria are based on the hardness range above. If any measured point falls outside the specified range, follow the Nonconformance handling section.

Bore diameter inspection
- Bore diameter shall be inspected using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measurements must be taken at multiple axial locations and averaged for reporting.
- Report results in the inspection record and mark parts only when within the tolerance specified above. For assemblies where rework is necessary, refer to Nonconformance handling.

Visual and non-destructive examination
- Perform a visual inspection under adequate illumination to identify surface defects. Penetrant inspection shall be used where surface-breaking discontinuities are suspected or where required by process travelers.
- Any discontinuity identified that could affect fit, function, or fatigue life must be evaluated per Nonconformance handling.

Sampling and statistical trending
- Document all inspection results in the lot inspection report. Track hardness and bore measurements for trending. Continuous drift or repeated border-line results should trigger process review even if individual parts meet the literal acceptance criteria.

Calibration and equipment
- All measurement tools used for hardness and bore inspection must be calibrated against traceable standards. Records of calibration must be available in the inspection folder for each lot.

Inspection records and examples
- Example entry: Lot identifier, part number CFW-1140-78, measured hardness locations and values, bore location measurements with mean and deviation, inspector initials, equipment ID, and calibration reference. Use the plant inspection form for format consistency.
- Records to keep: material certificates, heat-treatment records, inspection reports, calibration certificates, process travelers, and nonconformance reports. Retain according to Plant P1 retention policy.

Nonconformance handling
Detection and immediate action
- If a part fails to meet any requirement in the Requirements table, the part must be segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Notify quality lead and document the nonconformance in the lot file.

Disposition options
- Conditional rework: Parts failing bore tolerance may be eligible for machining rework if adequate stock and design allow, and if rework will restore the part to full conformance. Rework must be documented and approved by engineering and quality prior to execution.
- Material or process failure: Parts that exhibit hardness outside the specified range, or any crack-like discontinuity, are considered suspect for structural performance and may require full scrap or metallurgical investigation. Do not return parts that fail hardness limits to service without a documented engineering disposition.
- Root cause and corrective action: For any repeated nonconformance, initiate a root cause analysis and corrective action plan. Document findings and corrective measures in the lot file.

Records and reporting
- The lot nonconformance report shall include: description of nonconformance, affected part(s) identified as CFW-1140-78, inspection data demonstrating failure, proposed disposition, and final approval by authorized personnel. Maintain these records with the inspection records described above.

Examples and clarifications
- Example of a permitted action: If a bore measurement is outside the ±0.08 mm. tolerance but machining stock is available and engineering approves, rework to required dimension is allowed with documented sign-off.
- Example of prohibited action: Cooling or tempering adjustments intended to alter hardness post-final inspection without engineering approval are not permitted. Any attempt to alter heat-treatment outcomes must follow a documented process-change procedure and be requalified.

End of document.
title: Quality specification - axle hub CFW-1140-78 (4140)

# QS-CFW-5753-95 Quality specification - track link CFW-5753-95 (15B37)

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5753-95

Scope
- This quality specification applies to forged track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) produced at Plant P2 and is the controlling document for final acceptance of material, dimensional conformity, hardness, and weight prior to release to assembly or inventory.
- The document covers acceptance criteria, inspection methods, rationale for test choices, examples of typical nonconformances, and records to be retained in the document control system for traceability.
- It is intended for use by quality engineers, inspectors, forging operations, heat treat, and shipping personnel when verifying and releasing track links.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (through hardened area) | 34-37 HRC | Accept only parts with hardness within 34-37 HRC across specified measurement locations. |
| Bore diameter | Per drawing with bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm | Accept only parts where measured bore diameter is within drawing specification and the stated tolerance of ±0.03 mm. |
| Forging weight (maximum) | Maximum forging weight 28.3 kg | Reject parts that exceed the maximum forging weight of 28.3 kg as received from the forge operation. |

Notes on table
- The hardness range for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is critical to wear life and must be verified after applicable thermal processing. Hardness readings outside the range indicate a process deviation requiring containment and investigation.
- The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is ±0.03 mm and must be confirmed against the nominal dimension shown on the controlled drawing referenced in the work order.
- The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is 28.3 kg; material exceeding this mass suggests an overforge condition or material inclusion and must not be released.

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Inspect each part for forging defects that could affect fit or function, such as laps, cold shuts, cracks, and significant surface inclusions. Use magnification as required to confirm suspected discontinuities. Parts with suspected internal discontinuities shall be segregated pending further nondestructive evaluation.
- Dimensional inspection: Verify bore diameter at specified locations using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measuring equipment capable of reading to the specified drawing resolution. Compare measurements directly to the nominal drawing dimension and the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm. Record measured values on the inspection record.
- Hardness testing: Perform hardness testing on the through-hardened area using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale. Take measurements at the specified locations detailed on the inspection drawing. The hardness range for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is 34-37 HRC; parts must exhibit values within this range. If hardness readings vary across locations, record all readings and hold the lot until disposition is determined.
- Weight verification: Weigh each forging on a calibrated scale to confirm the forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg. For batches where full-piece weighing is not practical, perform representative checks and escalate to 100 percent weighing if any sample exceeds the maximum.
- Nondestructive testing: Where indicated by process control or suspect indications from visual inspection, perform magnetic particle inspection or ultrasonic testing per the applicable procedure. Record results and attach to the inspection log.

Rationale and examples
- Hardness rationale: Maintaining hardness within 34-37 HRC ensures a balance between wear resistance and fracture toughness. For example, a part hardened above the specified range may be brittle under impact; a part below may wear prematurely in service.
- Bore tolerance rationale: The bore tolerance of ±0.03 mm controls fit with mating pins and affects assembly preload and track articulation. An out-of-tolerance bore can produce premature wear or assembly interference.
- Weight rationale: The maximum forging weight 28.3 kg guards against excessive material that can indicate incorrect die fill, excessive flash, or material defects. For example, an over-weight forging may not properly heat treat or may contain hidden inclusions that compromise integrity.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Immediately segregate any part or lot that fails to meet any requirement in the table. Mark segregation tags with the part number, lot identifier, and the failed feature(s).
- Containment: Halt release of the affected lot. Notify quality engineering and production supervision. Suspend downstream process operations for affected serials or batches until disposition is set by quality engineering.
- Investigation: Quality engineering will review production records, heat treat records, tool maintenance logs, and inspection records to determine root cause. For hardness deviations, review heat treat cycle data and quench medium condition. For bore deviations, review die maintenance and machining records. For weight exceedance, review forging parameters and die design confirmation.
- Disposition: Options include rework if technically feasible, reheat/temper only when approved by engineering, scrapping, or use-as-is with engineering acceptance for minor deviations that do not affect safety or function. Any use-as-is disposition requires written engineering approval filed with the inspection record.
- Examples of disposition scenarios:
  - A single part with a bore out of tolerance due to machining error may be reworked if material and geometry permit; reworked parts must be re-inspected to confirm compliance with bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm.
  - A lot with hardness below the specified range across multiple samples requires suspension of release and corrective action in the heat treat process; parts are not released until hardness is within 34-37 HRC.
  - Overweight forgings discovered at receipt from the forge should be quarantined and returned to forging operations for evaluation when weight exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg.

Records to keep
- Inspection log showing measured bore diameters and individual hardness readings for each inspected location, with identifiers linking parts to production lot and heat lot.
- Weight records from calibrated scales indicating measured forging weight versus the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg.
- Visual and nondestructive testing reports, including photographs of any suspect defects.
- Nonconformance reports, containment records, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and disposition approvals signed by quality engineering and production supervision.
- All records shall be retained in the document control system under the part identifier CFW-5753-95 for traceability and audit.

Revision control
- Maintain this document under version control. Any procedural changes that affect inspection methods or acceptance criteria for CFW-5753-95 must be approved by quality management and documented in the revision history.
title: Quality specification - track link CFW-5753-95 (15B37)

# QS-CFW-8404-30 Quality specification - flange blank CFW-8404-30 (4140)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-8404-30

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and disposition procedures for flange blank CFW-8404-30 produced from material grade 4140 at Plant P3. The document applies to incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and finished blank releases intended for machining and assembly. It is intended for use by operations, quality, and production engineering personnel responsible for manufacturing and inspection.

## Background and rationale
CFW-8404-30 is a critical forging blank that will be machined to final geometry in subsequent operations. Controlling hardness, bore tolerance, and forging weight is necessary to ensure machinability, dimensional conformity, and material integrity. The specified hardness range provides a balance between strength and machinability for 4140 material in this supplied condition. The bore diameter tolerance ensures adequate fit and concentricity at machining setup. Maximum forging weight is controlled to ensure die life, handling capability, and process consistency.

## Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material | 4140 | Per purchase order and material certificate |
| Hardness (as-supplied) | The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. | Hardness measured on heat-affected cross section representative of production lot |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm. | Tolerance applies to nominal bore dimension on drawing prior to finish machining |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 15.0 kg. | Weight measured after trimming and flash removal |

## Inspection method
Inspection shall be performed by certified quality personnel using calibrated equipment and documented practices.

Hardness
- Sampling: Select representative pieces from each production lot. For small lots, select a representative sample consistent with shop standard sampling practice to demonstrate lot conformity.
- Location: Perform hardness readings on the face and rim area representative of the bulk material, avoiding scant flash and heavily worked zones. Multiple indentations may be taken to establish a representative mean and range.
- Equipment: Use Rockwell hardness tester calibrated to appropriate scale and verified with certified reference blocks prior to use.
- Acceptance: Verify that readings fall within The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. If any measured location falls outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter tolerance
- Measurement: Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer capable of reading to the required tolerance. Measurements shall be taken at multiple axial positions and at two orthogonal diameters to detect out-of-round.
- Datum and orientation: Measure relative to drawing datums; ensure part is free of burrs and debris that could affect measurement.
- Acceptance: Verify that measured bore diameter conforms to nominal plus or minus The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm. Document all measurements.

Weight
- Procedure: Determine forging weight after trimming and flash removal using calibrated scales placed on a stable surface. Remove loose debris and any packaging prior to weighing.
- Acceptance: Confirm weight does not exceed The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 15.0 kg. Parts exceeding this value must be segregated and dispositioned.

Surface condition and visual inspection
- Conduct a visual inspection for defects such as laps, folds, cracks, piping, excessive oxide, and unacceptable scale. Document defects and severity to support disposition decisions.

Calibration and equipment
- Use only calibrated measuring and hardness testing equipment. Calibration records shall be current and available in the quality record package.

## Nonconformance handling
When inspection identifies nonconforming conditions, follow the process below to ensure consistent and traceable disposition.

Identification and segregation
- Immediately tag and physically segregate nonconforming parts from conforming inventory. Use clear labeling to prevent inadvertent use.

Containment and notification
- Notify production supervision and quality engineering of nonconforming findings. Provide documented measurement data and relevant heat or lot information from material certificates.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the nonconformance is dimensional and can be corrected by machining without violating design intent or downstream processes, prepare a rework plan. Rework must be reviewed and approved by quality engineering prior to execution.
- Use-as-is with concession: For certain deviations that do not affect function, quality engineering may approve a concession. Concessions require documented justification, affected quantity, and authorization signature.
- Scrapping: Parts that cannot be safely reworked or used shall be scrapped in accordance with scrap control procedures and documented.

Root cause and corrective action
- For recurring nonconformances, initiate a containment and corrective action investigation. Include process review, tooling condition, material certificate verification, and supplier communication where applicable. Implement corrective actions and verify effectiveness before resuming normal production.

Examples
- Example: A sample piece measures a hardness slightly below the lower bound specified by The hardness range for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is 33-38 HRC. Quality will segregate the lot, review heat treatment records, and either reheat or request supplier corrective action depending on root cause analysis.
- Example: A bore measurement reads beyond The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-8404-30 (CFW-8404-30) is ±0.08 mm at multiple positions. The lot is segregated and reviewed for die wear; parts may be reworked if material remains within machining allowance and quality approves.

## Records to keep
Maintain QA records for each lot and retained documentation in the document control system. Required records include:
- Incoming material certificate and traceability to forging heat
- Hardness test reports and calibration verification for hardness equipment
- Bore diameter measurement logs with gauge identification and calibration status
- Weighing records showing measured weight and scale calibration
- Nonconformance reports, disposition documents, and corrective action records
- Final release authorization

Retention of records shall follow plant archival practice and be available for audit.

# QS-CFW-1392-34 - Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (4340)
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-1392-34

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) forged from 4340 material at Plant P1.  
- Applies to finished forging delivery from the heat of forge to final pack off prior to release to machining.  
- Purpose is to ensure mechanical properties and critical dimensional features meet downstream machining and functional requirements.

Requirements table
- Material: 4340 forging material per internal material control.  
- Hardness: The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 34-37 HRC. This applies to the forged and normalized or quenched and tempered condition as supplied. Hardness shall be measured on machined faces or ground witness coupons as described in Inspection method.  
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is ±0.06 mm. Acceptance requires all bores measured to be within tolerance prior to release. Critical bores that are out of tolerance shall be managed via the Nonconformance handling section.  
- Forging weight: The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (CFW-1392-34) is 5.8 kg. Forgings exceeding this weight shall be segregated and dispositioned per Nonconformance handling.  
- Surface condition: Forged surfaces shall be free of forging laps, cold shuts, and surface cracks in areas that cannot be removed in normal machining. Any surface indication requiring removal beyond normal machining allowance shall follow Nonconformance handling.  
- Internal soundness: Indications of internal defects detected by routine acceptance testing shall be dispositioned per Nonconformance handling.

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Conduct visual inspection of each forging for surface defects immediately after final cooling and cleaning. Use appropriate lighting and surface preparation to reveal laps, folds, and cracks. Document findings on the forge inspection record.  
- Hardness testing: Hardness testing shall be performed using a calibrated Rockwell tester on HRC scale. Test locations shall be selected on witness areas representative of core microstructure or on machined faces when witness areas are not available. Record actual hardness readings and average where multiple indentations are used. Acceptance is based on the hardness range specified above. If hardness readings fall outside the specified range, follow Nonconformance handling.  
- Dimensional inspection: Measure bore diameters using calibrated plug gauges or bore micrometers suitable for the feature form. Measurement technique shall include measuring at multiple circumferential positions to detect out-of-round conditions. Record each measured value and compare to the tolerance specified above. Features requiring post-forge machining shall still meet the bore diameter tolerance prior to release when the drawing calls for forged-to-size bores.  
- Weight verification: Weigh each forging or a representative sample batch on calibrated scales. Compare the measured mass to the maximum forging weight specified above. Record weight values on inspection records and tag or label forgings accordingly.  
- Non-destructive testing: When required by order or suspicion of subsurface defects, perform applicable NDT such as ultrasonic testing following standard plant procedures. Record NDT findings and attach to the lot inspection report.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A forging returns a hardness reading of a value below the lower bound of the specified hardness range. The rationale is that hardness below the specified range may indicate improper heat treatment or cooling rate and could lead to reduced fatigue life in service. Follow Nonconformance handling to ensure appropriate corrective action and root cause analysis.  
- Example: A bore measures at a size that violates the bore diameter tolerance. The rationale is that bore tolerance affects journal alignment and bearing fit after machining. Forgings that cannot be corrected by authorized rework must not be released to machining and require disposition.

Records to keep
- Maintain the following records in the document control system and attach to the shipment lot record: forge inspection report, hardness test logs showing raw readings, dimensional measurement sheets for bores showing individual measurement points, weight verification record, and any NDT reports generated.  
- Records shall include traceability to the heat lot and forging serial or identification marks so that individual forgings can be traced to their inspection results.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Any forging found outside the acceptance criteria in the Requirements table shall be segregated physically and clearly labeled as nonconforming.  
- Notification: Notify quality engineering and production supervision immediately upon discovery of a nonconformance. Provide associated inspection records and heat lot traceability.  
- Disposition: Quality engineering will review inspection data and determine disposition which may include rework, reheat treatment and retest, scrap, or concession with documented risk assessment. Disposition decisions and justification shall be documented and appended to the lot record.  
- Root cause and corrective action: For confirmed process or material causes leading to nonconforming forgings, open a corrective action record and implement steps to prevent recurrence. Include changes made to process controls, operator instructions, or supplier controls as applicable.  
- Example disposition actions: If a forging exceeds the maximum forging weight, options include segregation for scrap or return to melting per plant scrap procedure. If hardness is outside range, options include authorized reheat and temper per plant heat treatment procedure followed by retest. Any concession granted must document functional risk and require authorization by quality engineering.

Annex
- Retain inspection records for the life cycle required by customer contract and internal records policy. Ensure accessibility for audits and traceability for field investigations.
title: Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-1392-34 (4340)

# QS-CFW-4919-21 - Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (1045)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4919-21

Scope
This quality specification applies to the connecting rod CFW-4919-21 produced by Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forged, machined, and heat-treated connecting rods identified as CFW-4919-21. The scope covers dimensional, metallurgical, and mass requirements as they relate to final inspection prior to release for assembly. Use this document as the controlled reference for quality decisions and for generation of inspection records for each lot or material flow.

Requirements table
The following characteristics are required for acceptance of CFW-4919-21. Values are mandatory and must be used exactly as specified.

- Characteristic: Hardness (post heat-treat, machined bearing surfaces)  
  Requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is 29-32 HRC.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter (main bearing bores, final machined)  
  Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is ±0.10 mm.

- Characteristic: Forging mass (raw forging weight before trimming)  
  Requirement: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is 8.0 kg.

Notes on requirements:
- Hardness applies to the machined bearing contact surfaces and to any specified journal faces; atypical heat-treat variations must be resolved per the nonconformance handling section.
- Bore diameter tolerance is relative to the drawing nominal dimension; the tolerance value above is the allowable deviation after final machining and finish processes.
- Maximum forging weight applies to the raw forging condition; any forging exceeding the specified mass must be segregated and dispositioned.

Inspection method
General:
All inspections shall be carried out by trained inspection personnel using calibrated equipment. Calibration certificates must be traceable and available in inspection records. Visual inspection is a prerequisite before dimensional and hardness testing; parts exhibiting visible defects must be flagged and processed per nonconformance handling.

Hardness measurement:
- Measure hardness on the designated machined bearing surfaces using a Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale compatible with the requirement. Indent locations shall avoid edges, holes, and fillets and be in flat, representative surface areas.
- Record the measured values on the inspection record for each part. If a reading falls outside the specified range, perform a verification check at an adjacent location. If verification confirms out-of-specification, tag the part for nonconformance review.

Bore diameter measurement:
- Use bore gauges or internal micrometers appropriate for the bore geometry to determine the final bore diameter. Measurements shall be taken at multiple radial positions around the bore to detect out-of-round conditions and at multiple positions along the bore length to detect taper.
- Report measurements as nominal dimension plus or minus the specified tolerance. Parts with any measured value outside the tolerance shall be marked and moved to nonconformance handling.

Forging mass verification:
- Verify forging mass using calibrated industrial scales placed on a stable, level surface. Record the mass of each forging prior to trimming.
- Any forging mass recorded greater than the stated maximum shall be segregated and flagged for engineering disposition.

Sampling and records:
- Each inspected part shall have an inspection record that includes identification of the part, the inspector's initials, equipment identifiers, the measured values for hardness and bore diameter, and the forging mass. Records shall also include a brief description of any observed surface condition that could affect measurement validity.
- Maintain inspection records in the document control system under the part identifier CFW-4919-21. Inspection records are the primary evidence for acceptance and must be available for quality audits.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A connecting rod presents a hardness measurement at the bearing face of 31 HRC and a bore measurement within the handheld gauge readout that aligns with the nominal plus the stated tolerance. This part meets the hardness and bore criteria and may proceed to assembly staging.
- Example: A forging weighs 8.05 kg when placed on the calibrated scale prior to trimming. Because the mass exceeds the maximum forging weight specified, the forging is segregated and placed on hold for disposition; record the scale identifier and inspector notes.
- Rationale: Hardness band and tight bore control are critical for bearing fit and fatigue life. Forging mass control ensures the die and material usage conform to designed blanks and prevents downstream machining burden that could affect dimensional stability.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation:
- Any part or forging found not to meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be immediately identified, segregated from conforming material, and marked to prevent accidental use.

Disposition:
- The quality engineer or authorized disposition authority shall review nonconforming items using available inspection data and process records. Options include rework, reheat, scrap, or return to supplier as applicable.
- Decisions shall be documented on the nonconformance record for the affected part or lot, including the reason for disposition, any rework instructions, and the identity of the approver.

Rework controls:
- Where rework is allowed to correct a nonconformance, the rework instruction must include the required verification method and acceptance criteria, which are those stated in this specification. Reworked parts must be reinspected and recorded before release.

Root cause and corrective action:
- For recurring nonconformances, perform a root cause analysis and document corrective actions. Corrective actions may include process adjustment, tool maintenance, or additional operator training. Maintain records linking corrective actions to the nonconformance events.

Records to keep
- Inspection records for each part, including hardness readings, bore dimension measurements, forging mass measurements, equipment identifiers, and inspector identification.
- Calibration certificates for measurement equipment used for hardness, bore, and mass verification.
- Nonconformance records for all parts that failed acceptance, including disposition decisions and approvals.
- Corrective action records where applicable.

This document is the controlled quality specification for CFW-4919-21 at Plant P2. Follow documented procedures and recordkeeping to ensure traceability and repeatability of inspection outcomes.
title: Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (1045)

# QS-CFW-9335-36 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9335-36

Scope

This quality specification establishes acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) manufactured of 8620 material at Plant P3. It applies to finished forging blanks delivered to machining and heat treatment operations. The intent is to ensure dimensional accuracy and material condition sufficient for downstream transformation into final gears while minimizing rework and scrap.

Requirements table

- Part identification
  - Part: CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36)
  - Material: 8620

- Hardness
  - The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC.

- Bore
  - Bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.09 mm.

- Weight
  - The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg.

- Surface condition
  - Forging surfaces shall be free of forging laps, cold shuts, and open defects that would impair safe machining to final geometry. Surface blemishes that can be removed by normal clean-up passes are acceptable.

- Identification and traceability
  - Each lot shall be accompanied by a material test report and a forging traveler that links heat lot to individual blanks. The traveler shall reference this document id QS-CFW-9335-36.

Inspection method

General approach
Inspections shall be performed by trained quality personnel following documented procedures in the plant quality system. The objective is to verify that forgings meet the requirements table. Inspectors shall record findings on the forging traveler and retain records as described in Records to keep.

Hardness verification
Surface hardness checks shall be taken at representative locations on the blank where machining will not remove the test area. Measurements shall be taken on the forged surface after any planned stress relief but prior to final machining. The measured hardness shall fall within the specified range. The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC. When portable hardness testers are used, calibration of the instrument shall be verified against certified blocks prior to use.

Bore measurement
Bore diameters shall be measured using plug gauges or calibrated bore gauges appropriate for the nominal bore geometry. The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.09 mm. When using gauging methods that produce a go/no-go decision, the go/no-go limits shall be set to the nominal bore plus and minus the tolerance. When using direct-reading instruments, recorded values shall be entered on the traveler and compared to tolerance limits.

Weight check
Each forging shall be weighed on a calibrated scale capable of the expected mass range. The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg. Any blank that exceeds this weight shall be held for engineering disposition to evaluate material distribution, potential flash, or excess stock that could affect downstream processes.

Visual and surface inspections
Conduct a systematic visual inspection under adequate lighting. Look for laps, cracks, cracks circumferentially, and other discontinuities. Minor surface irregularities that are fully machined away are acceptable if they do not compromise part integrity or material traceability. Document any anomalies on the traveler with photographs where helpful.

Sampling and lot acceptance
Sampling shall be based on process capability and risk; inspect representative pieces from each furnace lot and die set combination. When an out-of-tolerance condition is found within a lot, escalate to 100 percent inspection of the lot until root cause and corrective actions are implemented.

Records to keep
- Completed forging traveler with inspector signature and dates of inspections.
- Hardness test records including instrument identification and calibration reference.
- Bore measurement records with instrument identification and calibration reference.
- Scale weight records showing the measured weight for each blank or lot summary.
- Photographic records for any nonconforming surface conditions.
All records shall be retained in accordance with plant document retention policy and shall be made available for customer or internal audits upon request. The traveler shall reference this document id QS-CFW-9335-36 to maintain traceability.

Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation
Any forging that fails to meet the requirements table shall be tagged and segregated from conforming material immediately. The tag shall reference the specific failing characteristic and the forging traveler.

Containment and notification
Quality shall notify manufacturing supervision and engineering when a nonconformance is discovered. A containment action shall be initiated to prevent further shipment or use of affected forgings.

Disposition
Disposition options include rework, repair, or scrap. Examples of allowed dispositions:
- Minor surface blemishes that can be removed by standard clean-up machining passes may be approved for machining after engineering review.
- Forgings exceeding the maximum mass shall be evaluated for removal of excess flash or machining allowance; if removal is not feasible or would compromise part integrity, scrap shall be issued.
All dispositions that constitute a deviation from this specification require engineering documentation and approval. The disposition record shall be attached to the forging traveler.

Root cause and corrective action
For any lot with a confirmed nonconformance, perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions. Document findings, actions taken, and verification steps on the corrective action record linked to the traveler.

Audit and continuous improvement
Quality shall review inspection results periodically to identify trends. Process improvements and tooling adjustments shall be prioritized when recurring issues are identified. Continuous improvement actions and their verification shall be documented and retained with related records.

Related documents
None cited.

Revision history
Rev E entered to reflect current requirements for Plant P3 and parts CFW-9335-36.
title: Quality specification - gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620)

# QS-CFW-6417-61 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (52100)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6417-61

Scope
This quality specification governs acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 manufactured from material grade 52100 at Plant P1. It applies to forged rings delivered to machining and assembly and to in-process forgings held for inspection prior to heat treatment or finishing. The intent is to ensure functional hardness, dimensional accuracy of the bore, and compliance with forging weight limits for safe handling and traceability.

Requirements table
The table below lists mandatory acceptance criteria that constitute final quality requirements for CFW-6417-61.

- Part identification: CFW-6417-61
- Material: 52100
- Hardness: The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 29-35 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is ±0.07 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 9.4 kg.
- Visual and surface: Forgings must be free of cracks, laps, and other discontinuities that could impair machining or performance. Light scale and surface oxides are acceptable provided they are removed in subsequent operations without loss of nominal material.
- Identification and traceability: Each forging must be marked or tagged to allow linkage to the associated heat lot and inspection record through the plant document control system.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspectors shall verify requirements listed in the requirements table at designated inspection points: incoming inspection for received forgings, in-process inspection post-forge and pre-heat treatment, and final inspection after finishing operations that affect the bore or hardness. Record results on the part inspection record and file with the part history record for the heat lot.

Hardness verification
Hardness shall be measured using a calibrated portable Rockwell hardness tester set for HRC scale. Measurement locations shall be on the forged surface and representative of the ring wall without crossing machined areas. Take multiple measurements distributed circumferentially and axially to represent variability. Document each reading on the part inspection record and calculate the range observed; the hardness values must be within the specified range above. If readings cluster near either limit, perform additional measurements and attach notes describing locations sampled and any anomalies.

Bore diameter verification
Measure the bore using a calibrated bore gauge or inside micrometer suitable for the part geometry. Ensure the gauge contacts clean, representative surfaces and that measurements are taken at multiple angular positions and along the axial length to detect taper and out-of-round conditions. Record each measurement on the part inspection record. The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is ±0.07 mm; acceptance requires all relevant measurements to be within that tolerance relative to the nominal diameter on the manufacturing drawing.

Weight verification
Weigh forgings on a calibrated scale to confirm they do not exceed the allowed forging mass. The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (CFW-6417-61) is 9.4 kg. Record the weight on the part inspection record. If the weight is below expected nominal mass due to excessive flash removal or other causes, document and investigate for potential missing material.

Sampling and frequency
For lot-based inspection, select samples per the plant sampling plan and for critical features perform 100 percent inspection as directed by the part family risk assessment for this product class. For single-piece releases, perform full verification of all listed requirements on each piece.

Instrument calibration and acceptance
Use instruments with valid calibration status. Attach instrument identifiers and calibration dates to the inspection record. Reject readings from instruments found out of calibration and repeat measurements with a calibrated instrument; note the cause and corrective action in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
Identification
Any forging that fails to meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be segregated clearly and tagged as nonconforming. Establish a nonconformance tag linking the piece to its inspection record, heat lot, and the responsible inspector.

Disposition options
Disposition decisions include use-as-is, rework, scrap, or return to supplier as applicable under plant nonconformance procedures. Rework proposals must include method statements describing how the affected feature will be corrected without introducing new risks to functionality. For bore deviations, approved machining operations can be used to bring dimensions into tolerance if sufficient allowance exists and if the proposed correction is documented and approved by engineering prior to execution. For hardness deviations, submit a corrective heat-treatment plan and secure approval before proceeding. For weight deviations, investigate root cause and evaluate whether rework or scrap is appropriate.

Containment and corrective action
When a nonconformance is discovered that potentially affects previously released or in-process assemblies, apply immediate containment by locating all suspect parts, halting shipments if applicable, and notifying the quality manager. Document containment actions and propose corrective actions, including any changes to forging process controls, tooling, or inspection points. Maintain records of root cause analysis, corrective actions implemented, and verification of effectiveness.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the plant document control and quality records system for each heat lot and part number:
- Part inspection record containing individual hardness readings, bore measurements, and weight entries.
- Instrument calibration certificates or identifiers for the instruments used.
- Nonconformance tags and disposition reports where applicable.
- Engineering approvals for any rework or deviation requests.
- Traceability records linking the forging to the heat lot and manufacturing operations.

Examples and rationale
Example: A forging measures outside the bore tolerance at one axial station but within tolerance elsewhere. The inspector documents all measurements, segregates the part, and initiates an engineering review. If machining allowance exists, machining to size with appropriate quality controls may be approved. Rationale: Multiple-point measurement detects localized defects such as nonuniform cooling or die wear that single measurements could miss.

Example: Hardness readings show a regional trend toward the lower bound of the allowed range. The inspector increases sampling density and notifies heat-treatment personnel for process review. Rationale: Early detection prevents release of parts with out-of-spec hardness and limits rework.

Audit and review
Quality shall periodically review inspection records and nonconformance trends for CFW-6417-61 to determine ongoing process capability and identify opportunities for process control improvements. Maintain records as described for audit and continuous improvement purposes.
title: Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6417-61 (52100)

# QS-CFW-2117-10 Quality specification - valve body CFW-2117-10 (F316)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-2117-10

Scope
This quality specification applies to valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10), forged from F316 grade material, manufactured at Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forging, heat treat, and final machining handoff. Background and rationale are provided to ensure consistent evaluation and traceable records for customer quality and internal continuous improvement.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness | 39-44 HRC | Measured after final heat treat and stabilization |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.09 mm | Applies to final machined bore; measurement at part datum surfaces |
| Maximum forging weight | 14.5 kg | Weight measured after finishing flash removal, prior to machining |

Inspection method
General
- Inspectors shall verify each requirement listed in the Requirements table prior to release to machining or assembly. Rationale: early detection of deviations reduces scrap and rework and preserves heat treat control.

Hardness verification
- Method: Use a calibrated portable hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Measure on representative locations that are accessible without further machining and away from surface anomalies. Rationale: portable testers enable in-line verification while minimizing handling.
- Sampling and measurement protocol: For each part presented for hardness verification, take at least two readings on opposite faces or equivalent locations. If readings differ beyond allowed spread, perform a confirmatory test on a metallurgical coupon or a secondary location on the same part. Rationale: multi-point verification reduces false failures due to localized work hardening or surface condition.
- Acceptance: Part is acceptable only if readings fall within 39-44 HRC across verified locations. Record all readings in the inspection record.

Bore diameter verification
- Method: Use calibrated bore gauge equipment or coordinate measuring equipment capable of resolving the stated tolerance. Measure at a nominally mid-depth location along the bore and at defined datum references. Rationale: bore tolerance is critical for fit and sealing; measurement must reference the same datums used by machining.
- Acceptance: The measured bore diameter must be within ±0.09 mm of nominal drawing size. If the bore is out of tolerance, part shall be segregated and processed as nonconforming.
- Example: If a gauge indicates deviation beyond ±0.09 mm at any evaluated plane, record measurement and follow nonconformance handling.

Forging weight verification
- Method: Weigh each forging after flash removal and trimming using calibrated scales. Record weight on the material traveler and inspection form.
- Acceptance: Weight must not exceed 14.5 kg. Parts under the maximum are acceptable provided all other requirements are met. Rationale: maximum forging weight controls cycle loads and material use and confirms correct batch processing.

Surface condition and visual
- Method: Visual inspection for defects that could affect function or machinability. Remove loose scale prior to inspection. Rationale: superficial defects may mask subsurface issues; visual checks help prevent tooling damage.
- Acceptance: Defects that compromise intended use or prevent attainment of dimensional features shall be documented and treated as nonconformance.

Records to keep
- For each inspected part, retain the following records in the document control system and on the material traveler:
  - Hardness readings with tester identification and calibration status.
  - Bore diameter measurements with instrument identification and calibration status.
  - Weighing result and scale identification.
  - Visual inspection notes and photographic evidence where anomalies exist.
  - Inspector name or badge identifier and timestamp of inspection.
- Rationale: complete records ensure traceability for customer inquiries, warranty claims, and process improvement.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part failing to meet the requirements in the Requirements table shall be immediately tagged and segregated from conforming material. Rationale: prevents inadvertent use and facilitates root cause analysis.

Disposition options
- Rework: If a nonconformance is deemed recoverable by authorized engineering, a rework instruction shall be issued and the part shall be re-inspected following the rework. Re-inspection must include all applicable checks from this specification.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be restored to meet requirements or that exceed safe material limits shall be scrapped in accordance with Plant P2 scrap procedures.
- Return to process owner: For issues originating in forging or heat treat, parts may be returned to the originating operation for containment and corrective action.

Reporting and corrective action
- All nonconformances shall be recorded in the nonconformance report system with supporting data from Records to keep. Rationale: structured reporting enables trending and process improvement.
- Engineering review is required for repeated failures against any single requirement to determine root cause and necessary process controls or design reviews.

Examples
- Example nonconformance scenario: A forging measures 41 HRC at one location and 45 HRC at another location. Action: segregate part, perform confirmatory hardness testing, initiate nonconformance report, and quarantine similar parts from the same heat for inspection.
- Example disposition: A bore found beyond ±0.09 mm may be evaluated for undersize salvage via insert or sleeve only after engineering approval. If no restorative path is approved, designate part as scrap.

Roles and responsibilities
- Quality inspectors: execute inspections and maintain records.
- Process owners: implement containment for detected deviations and coordinate corrective actions.
- Engineering: review nonconformance trends and approve dispositions that alter part geometry or material condition.

This specification is mandatory for all valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) production at Plant P2. Compliance ensures fit, function, and service life consistent with customer expectations.
title: Quality specification - valve body CFW-2117-10 (F316)

# QS-CFW-5010-61 - Quality specification - axle hub CFW-5010-61 (4140) Rev A

## Scope
This quality specification applies to finished axle hub CFW-5010-61 forgings produced at Plant P3 for part CFW-5010-61. It defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore dimensional tolerance, and forging weight, and documents inspection methods, rationale for acceptance criteria, examples of acceptable and nonconforming conditions, and required records. This document is intended for use by production, heat treatment, quality assurance, and shipping.

## Requirements

| Parameter | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Material/part | CFW-5010-61 (4140) | Part identification must match supplied order |
| Hardness (after final process) | 22-28 HRC. | Hardness across critical surfaces must be within range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.10 mm. | Measured at specified bore feature for fit accuracy |
| Maximum forging weight | 5.4 kg. | Includes any machining stock retained for finish operations |

Background and rationale:
- Hardness range 22-28 HRC. is specified to ensure required combination of wear resistance and toughness for axle application while remaining compatible with downstream machining operations.
- Bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm. is specified to control press-fit/interference characteristics with mating shafts and to ensure consistent assembly performance.
- Maximum forging weight 5.4 kg. limits material handling risk and ensures compatibility with established tooling and heat treatment fixtures.

## Inspection method

General statements:
- Inspection is performed by Quality Assurance personnel following established receiving and in-process inspection workflows. Measurements are recorded to permit traceability to production lot and furnace/heat batch identifiers.
- Inspectors shall confirm part identification marking or packaging to match the production order before dimensional or hardness checks.

Hardness inspection:
- Hardness readings shall be taken on representative features and potential critical faces identified on the engineering print. Indent locations shall be on clean, flat surfaces free of scale, heavy oxide, or painted surfaces that could affect reading quality.
- For parts exhibiting a hardness outside 22-28 HRC., additional measurements surrounding the initial indication are recommended to determine if the condition is localized or systemic.
- Instrument calibration status shall be verified prior to use. Calibration records for hardness testing equipment must be maintained.

Dimensional inspection (bore):
- Bore diameter shall be checked using an appropriate bore measuring instrument consistent with the feature geometry. The measured value must fall within ±0.10 mm. of the nominal bore callout on the drawing.
- For features that will be machined after forging, inspectors shall verify that the measured bore leaves sufficient machining allowance compatible with downstream operations. If doubt exists regarding allowance, consult process engineering.

Weight verification:
- Forging weight shall be verified against shop traveler or casting/forging ticket. The final forging must not exceed 5.4 kg. for handling and tooling compatibility.
- If a part exceeds 5.4 kg., stop production of that lot and initiate nonconformance handling per this document.

Examples:
- Example acceptable condition: hardness readings of 24 HRC. and 26 HRC. on opposing faces, bore measured within ±0.10 mm. of nominal, and forging weight recorded as less than or equal to 5.4 kg.
- Example nonconforming condition: single reading of 20 HRC. on a critical face, bore out of tolerance beyond ±0.10 mm., or forging weight greater than 5.4 kg.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test reports showing location, readings, tester ID, and calibration status.
- Dimensional inspection reports showing measured values for the bore feature, inspector ID, and instrument used.
- Forging weight records tied to lot/heat numbers and the shop traveler.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records when applicable.
All records shall be retained in the document control system and made available for internal review and customer audits.

## Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation:
- Any part or lot found to be outside the requirements in the Requirements table must be immediately identified and segregated from conforming material. A visible tag indicating quarantine status is recommended to prevent inadvertent use.

Notification and containment:
- Quality shall notify production and process engineering of nonconforming findings promptly. Production of similar parts should be halted until containment and root cause are assessed.

Disposition:
- Disposition options include rework, repair, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. The selected disposition must be documented and approved by authorized personnel.
- For hardness values outside 22-28 HRC., disposition must consider potential impacts on mechanical performance. Options may include reheat/tempering if process capability and material condition permit, or rejection if material integrity is suspect.
- For bore dimensions outside ±0.10 mm., options may include corrective machining where drawing tolerances and material condition allow, or rejection if the bore cannot be brought into tolerance without violating design requirements.
- For forgings exceeding 5.4 kg., the lot must be evaluated for tooling and handling implications. Unless approved disposition exists, excess-weight forgings shall be rejected.

Root cause and corrective action:
- A root cause investigation should document process step(s) leading to nonconformance, corrective actions taken to prevent recurrence, and verification of effectiveness.
- Corrective actions may include changes to forging charge, trim parameters, heat treatment procedures, or tooling maintenance, as applicable.

Final disposition and release:
- Only authorized personnel shall sign off on final disposition. Released parts must have all inspection records and dispositions attached to the lot's quality file prior to shipment.

Audit and review:
- Nonconformance trends shall be periodically reviewed by quality leadership to identify systemic issues. Corrective measures shall be implemented where trends indicate repeat occurrences.

Appendix (records examples):
- Typical record set for a conforming lot: hardness test report, dimensional inspection report with bore readings, forging weight ticket, and inspection release sign-off.
- Typical record set for a nonconforming lot: all of the above plus quarantine tag, nonconformance report, root cause analysis, corrective action documentation, and final disposition approval.

End of document.

# QS-CFW-5349-60 Quality specification - track link CFW-5349-60 (15B37)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-5349-60

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the manufactured track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) produced at Plant P1. It applies to forged parts delivered to assembly, parts returned from heat treatment, and finished parts submitted for final inspection. The document covers material condition, dimensional control of the bore, hardness acceptance, inspection procedures, sampling rationale, and controls for nonconforming items. This specification is intended for use by production, quality, and metallurgical personnel.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material hardness | 31-35 HRC | Hardness applies to working surface and cross section representative of the bore area. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.03 mm | Applies after final machining and before assembly processes. Measurement method is described below. |
| Maximum forging weight | 58.0 kg | Maximum weight per individual forged blank prior to machining. Exceeding items are processed as nonconforming. |

Rationale: The hardness band is selected to ensure adequate wear resistance while maintaining toughness for the dynamic loading environment of the track link. The bore tolerance is dictated by mating component fit and lubrication retention requirements. The maximum forging weight reflects handling and die capacity constraints at Plant P1.

## Inspection method
General approach
- Inspectors shall verify each characteristic in the Requirements table prior to release to the next operation. Records must document the inspector identity, inspection equipment used, and results observed.
- Calibration status of all measuring equipment shall be verified against the calibration control system prior to use. Use equipment with appropriate resolution and repeatability for the characteristic measured.

Hardness verification
- Hardness shall be measured on a minimum of one location representative of the bore region on every finished part. If part geometry prevents direct indentation in the bore, an adjacent location that has undergone identical heat treatment and machining shall be used. When a part is measured, record the instrument identifier and reading. Acceptance is granted only when the measured value falls within 31-35 HRC.
- If a measured value is outside the specified range, follow the nonconformance handling section below.

Bore diameter measurement
- Measure the bore diameter after final machining using a bore gauge or coordinate measuring system capable of resolving the specified tolerance. Record the nominal dimension and deviation. Acceptance requires the measured diameter to be within ±0.03 mm of the specified nominal bore dimension as provided on the drawing for part CFW-5349-60.
- For runs with multiple pieces, apply a sampling rationale consistent with Plant P1 sampling procedures. If any sampled piece exceeds the tolerance, expand inspection to the entire lot and hold the lot pending disposition.

Forging weight control
- Weigh every forged blank prior to machining and confirm it does not exceed 58.0 kg. Weighing shall be performed on calibrated scales. If a blank exceeds the maximum, segregate and label it as a potential nonconforming blank and notify production supervision for evaluation.

Surface and visual checks
- Perform a visual inspection to detect forging defects, cracks, excessive laps, or surface contamination that could affect subsequent machining or performance. Any visual anomalies that may compromise fit, function, or fatigue life shall be recorded and processed under nonconformance handling.

Records to keep
- For each batch, retain an inspection record that includes: part identifier, serial or lot identifier, inspector initials, caliper or instrument identifiers, hardness readings, bore measurement results, forging weight records, visual inspection notes, and disposition decisions. Maintain these records in the document control system and on the shop floor for traceability.
- Keep hardness test block comparisons used to verify hardness tester performance with the inspection data for that shift.

Examples
- Example of acceptable condition: A finished link with a recorded hardness of thirty-two point five HRC within the range 31-35 HRC, bore measurements recorded within ±0.03 mm relative to nominal, and forging weight recorded below 58.0 kg is acceptable for release.
- Example of reject condition: A forged blank measured at a weight exceeding 58.0 kg, or a machined part with a bore outside ±0.03 mm, or a hardness reading outside 31-35 HRC, is subject to the nonconformance process and may require rework, segregation, or scrap.

## Nonconformance handling
Segregation and hold
- Any item that fails to meet the Requirements table shall be immediately segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Do not release nonconforming items to downstream operations without documented disposition.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the deviation is something that can be corrected by defined machining or heat treatment processes without compromising part integrity, a controlled rework plan may be approved by quality engineering. Reworked parts must be re-inspected to demonstrate compliance with the Requirements table.
- Use-as-is: Rare dispositions for use-as-is must be supported by engineering analysis demonstrating that functional performance is not compromised and must be approved by authorized engineering personnel. The basis for approval must be documented and retained.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be reworked or approved for use-as-is shall be scrapped and recorded.

Investigation and corrective action
- For any recurring nonconformance, initiate a root cause investigation. Document findings, corrective actions, and verification steps. Implement corrective action to prevent recurrence and verify effectiveness through subsequent inspection results.

Notifications and records
- Notify production supervision and quality management of any nonconformance that affects delivery or safety. Maintain records of nonconformance forms, dispositions, investigation reports, and corrective action records in the document control and quality management systems.

Audit and review
- Quality shall periodically review inspection records to confirm continued conformance to this specification and to identify any trends. Findings and corrective actions shall be recorded and retained as part of the plant quality records.

End of specification.

# QS-PROC-01 Forging temperature control (P1)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Scope
This quality specification establishes requirements for temperature control and coil condition monitoring for the induction billet heater identified as EQ-P1-L1-IH03 on line P1-L1 in Plant P1. The document addresses acceptance criteria, inspection frequency, inspection methods, records, and nonconformance handling for the coil and its observed effects on forging temperature control. Follow related maintenance and operational procedures cited in related documents for detailed tasks and safe work practices: MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-01, SOP-P1-L1-04.

Background and rationale
Consistent heater coil condition is a primary contributor to stable heating profiles and repeatable forging temperatures. Coil degradation, partial shorting, turn separation, or insulation breakdown will manifest as drift in heating uniformity, increased electrical losses, and potential safety hazards. Regular coil inspections reduce unplanned downtime and prevent unacceptable forging temperature variation that can produce out-of-spec parts. The coil inspection interval is selected to balance operational availability and early detection of degradation, based on historical degradation patterns and supplier guidance documented in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Requirements table
| Item | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coil inspection interval | The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. | Inspection completed at or before interval; documented completion entry in equipment log; no unresolved findings older than the next scheduled inspection. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Coil visual integrity | Coil surfaces free of visible insulation cracks, charring, or exposed conductors that could affect field uniformity. | No exposed conductors; no insulation delamination requiring immediate shutdown per SOP-P1-L1-01. | SOP-P1-L1-01 |
| Electrical connections | Terminal lugs and leads secured, no discoloration indicative of overheating. | Connections torque and condition per MM-P1-L1-IH03; no loose or oxidized terminals. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Cooling path | Cooling channels and flow connections free of blockage and corrosion that could alter coil operating temperature. | Visual confirmation of flow integrity; no deposits obstructing flow. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Heater-to-process performance | Forging inlet temperature stability within process capability as monitored in SOP-P1-L1-04. | Process monitoring shows stable inlet temperature profile after inspection; deviations logged and addressed. | SOP-P1-L1-04 |

Inspection method
- Preparation and safety
  - Review applicable steps in SOP-P1-L1-01 and MM-P1-L1-IH03 before beginning the inspection. Lockout and tagout per SOP-P1-L1-01 and ensure electrical isolation of EQ-P1-L1-IH03.
  - Allow the coil and surrounding structure to reach a safe condition as defined in SOP-P1-L1-01 before performing hands-on inspection.

- Visual inspection
  - Perform a systematic visual sweep of the coil exterior visible from the access point. Inspect for cracks, discoloration, deformation, insulation separation, and any foreign material adhering to coil surfaces.
  - Inspect mechanical supports and clamp points for wear or movement that could cause coil displacement.

- Electrical interface check
  - With the equipment isolated, examine terminal connections and cable entry points for signs of arcing, discoloration, or mechanical loosening. Follow connection checks in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

- Cooling inspection
  - Inspect cooling lines and fittings for signs of leakage, corrosion, or blocked passages where accessible. Confirm seals and hose conditions per MM-P1-L1-IH03.

- Functional verification
  - After reassembly and removal of lockout/tagout, perform controlled start-up per SOP-P1-L1-04. Monitor process temperature behavior and compare to expected heating profile. Document any transient anomalies.

- Use of non-destructive aids
  - Where available, employ infrared imaging or borescope inspection to reveal subsurface hot spots or internal coil defects not visible externally. Record findings in the inspection report.

Examples and interpretation
- Example: If visual inspection finds localized insulation charring without exposed conductor, clean area and schedule follow-up per MM-P1-L1-IH03. Record cleaning action and monitor at the next scheduled coil inspection.
- Example: If terminal discoloration and looseness are found, do not return the heater to service until connections are repaired and verified per MM-P1-L1-IH03. Document repair and attach post-repair verification evidence.
- Example: If cooling passage restriction is detected, isolate the cooling loop and remediate blockage. Confirm restored flow and monitor heater temperature response during the next start-up sequence.

Records to keep
- Maintain an equipment inspection log entry for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 that includes inspector name, date of inspection, scope of inspection, and a statement confirming the coil inspection interval condition: The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Attach supporting images, infrared scans, and repair orders as applicable.
- File all corrective maintenance records per MM-P1-L1-IH03 and link start-up verification records to the entry as referenced in SOP-P1-L1-04.
- Retain inspection reports and related records in the document control system in accordance with plant retention practices referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate actions
  - If any condition is found that presents an immediate safety risk or clear electrical hazard, stop operation and place EQ-P1-L1-IH03 into an out-of-service state following SOP-P1-L1-01.
  - Initiate a nonconformance record and notify maintenance and quality leads.

- Evaluation and disposition
  - Classify findings according to severity per MM-P1-L1-IH03. For defects that may impact forging temperature control, perform containment actions such as process hold or quarantining affected lots until heater condition is verified.
  - Repair or replace defective components following MM-P1-L1-IH03 procedures. Perform re-inspection and start-up verification per SOP-P1-L1-04.

- Verification and closure
  - Document corrective actions and verification results in the EQ-P1-L1-IH03 equipment log. Nonconformance records must include reference to related repair orders and verification steps. Close nonconformances only after successful verification that heater performance and coil condition meet the acceptance criteria listed in this document.

Related documents
- MM-P1-L1-IH03
- SOP-P1-L1-01
- SOP-P1-L1-04
