# QS-PROC-02 Quench and temper process window (P1)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-IH02

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptable process window and associated controls for quench and temper operations for billets fed from Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 at Plant P1, line P1-L2. It applies to all billets processed using EQ-P1-L2-IH02 and is used to set control limits, inspection criteria, and records retention for downstream ring rolling and heat treat operations. This document supplements operating procedures listed in the Related Documents section and is intended for production, quality, and maintenance staff responsible for process control and conformance.

Requirements table
| Parameter | Requirement | Rationale | Reference procedure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Induction billet heater setpoint for EQ-P1-L2-IH02 | The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 1230 °C. | Establishes metallurgical starting condition for quench and temper to achieve required microstructure and hardness after ring rolling. | SOP-P1-L2-01 |
| Billet tracking and identification | All billets entering the quench and temper line shall retain unique heat and lot identity through processing and inspection records. | Traceability for nonconforming material and root cause analysis. | SOP-P1-L2-03 |
| Process parameter recording | Heater setpoint, measured billet temperature at transfer point, and operator confirmation shall be recorded for every production run. | Demonstrates control of the thermal process and provides data for trend analysis. | SOP-P1-L2-01 |
| Calibration and equipment verification | Temperature measurement devices and EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control sensors shall be verified per calibration plan and documented. | Ensures measurement accuracy for compliance to the target billet temperature. | SOP-P1-L2-05 |
| Hold and release criteria | Billets not meeting identification or recording requirements shall be segregated and held from production release until disposition. | Prevents use of unverified material and protects final product quality. | SOP-P1-L2-03 |

Inspection method
Background and rationale
The target billet temperature is set to provide a repeatable starting condition for quench and temper that aligns with alloy heat treat response and the expectations of downstream ring rolling. Measured billet temperature at the transfer point provides the most representative value for the mass entering the quench medium; therefore, control and inspection focus on the transfer point reading and the documentation of heater control output. Records serve both immediate inspection and longer term process capability assessment.

Procedure
- Verify that EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control displays the setpoint described in this document prior to starting a run per SOP-P1-L2-01.
- Measure billet temperature at the transfer point using the facility approved pyrometer or thermocouple method referenced in SOP-P1-L2-01. Record the measured value in the process log with the billet heat/lot identification from SOP-P1-L2-03.
- For each production run, confirm that calibration status for temperature sensors used on EQ-P1-L2-IH02 is current and documented per SOP-P1-L2-05. Attach calibration evidence to the run packet.
- When inspecting billets, record visual condition notes and any deviations from expected surface appearance. Note any indications that could affect quench performance and include these observations in the run log.

Examples
- Example inspection entries should include the billet heat/lot id, the measured transfer point temperature, the operator initials, and a link to the EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control log. Use the forms prescribed in SOP-P1-L2-03.
- If multiple billets are processed in a single heater cycle, record a representative transfer point temperature for the cycle and list the billet identifiers covered by that cycle in the run log.

Records to keep
- Process run log with heater setpoint confirmation, transfer point temperature readings, billet heat/lot identifiers, and operator confirmation; retain with production records per SOP-P1-L2-03.
- Calibration certificates and verification records for temperature measurement devices used with EQ-P1-L2-IH02; file per SOP-P1-L2-05.
- Disposition records for any segregated or reworked billets, including nonconformance reports and corrective action documentation.

Nonconformance handling
Detection and initial containment
- Any billet or run that lacks the required identification, measurement, or documentation shall be segregated and held. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-03 for segregation tagging and immediate containment measures.
Investigation and disposition
- Conduct investigation to determine root cause using process records, EQ-P1-L2-IH02 control logs, calibration records, and operator interviews. Document findings in the run packet.
- Disposition options include reheat under controlled conditions, rework per applicable procedures, or scrap. The disposition must be approved by quality and production leads and recorded with the billet heat/lot id.
Corrective action and prevention
- Implement corrective actions based on root cause. Actions may include adjustments to SOP steps, retraining of operators, or equipment maintenance on EQ-P1-L2-IH02. Record corrective actions and their verification.
- Review related process controls and update references to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-03, and SOP-P1-L2-05 as required to prevent recurrence.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L2-01
- SOP-P1-L2-03
- SOP-P1-L2-05

Revision control
Maintain this document and associated records in the document control system. Changes to the target or procedural controls require approval through the formal revision process.

# QS-PROC-03 Ring rolling dimensional control (P1)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
-------
This quality specification defines dimensional control requirements for ring rolling operations at Plant P1, line P1-L2, with emphasis on heat treat integration and final dimensional verification for rings processed on the Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03. It applies to production and inspection personnel responsible for rolling, heat treating, and final measurement activities for parts routed through the line. It does not replace process control plans or maintenance procedures; it is intended to be used in conjunction with MM-P1-L2-HT03, SB-1035, and SOP-P1-L2-04.

Background and rationale
------------------------
Dimensional stability of forged rings is controlled by a combination of forming practices and heat treatment. The austenitizing temperature used in the furnace prior to quench and temper has a direct effect on final microstructure and resultant dimensional change during post-heat-treat stabilization. To minimize variability, operators must follow fixed setpoints, documented transfer conditions, and prescribed inspection methods. This specification documents the critical setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and defines inspection and nonconformance handling steps to ensure consistent ring geometry at final inspection. Related maintenance and equipment calibration information is contained in MM-P1-L2-HT03; metallurgical acceptance criteria are referenced in SB-1035; operation sequence and operator actions are specified in SOP-P1-L2-04.

Requirements table
------------------
| Requirement | Acceptance / Instruction | Record to retain |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| Furnace austenitizing setpoint | The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. | Furnace log entry from EQ-P1-L2-HT03 showing setpoint and operator initials; cross-reference to SOP-P1-L2-04 operation step. |
| Post-heat-treat dimensional tolerance verification | Final ring dimensions shall meet drawing requirements as specified on work order; if drawing requires additional metallurgical exceptions, follow SB-1035. | Final inspection report linked to work order and SB-1035 disposition notes. |
| Transfer conditions between rolling and heat treat | Parts must be handled in accordance with SOP-P1-L2-04 to avoid mechanical distortion during transfer. | Transfer checklist signed by sender and receiver. |
| Measurement method and gauge control | Use calibrated gauges referenced to MM-P1-L2-HT03 and recorded per plant gauge control practice. | Calibration certificates and measurement records filed per MM-P1-L2-HT03. |

Inspection method
-----------------
Overview
This section describes the method for verifying ring dimensions after heat treat and prior to shipment. The purpose is to identify dimensional shifts attributable to heat treatment or handling and to document compliance.

Preparation
- Verify the furnace austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 is set as specified in this document prior to processing. Confirm the setpoint entry in the furnace log and sign the process step as required by SOP-P1-L2-04.
- Ensure measuring equipment is within calibration according to MM-P1-L2-HT03. Reject any out-of-calibration gauge before use and notify quality control.

Measurement procedure
- Stabilize the part per the handling instructions in SOP-P1-L2-04 to eliminate residual handling distortion.
- Measure the ring dimensions defined on the drawing using the controlled gauges. Record measured values on the final inspection report field provided on the work order.
- For any dimension approaching drawing limits, perform a secondary verification using an alternative calibrated instrument and document both measurements and operator initials.

Example scenarios and interpretation
- If a measured diameter deviates from the drawing beyond allowable drawing limits, tag the part for nonconformance review and follow the nonconformance handling section below. Record the condition with photographs and measurement records.
- If repeated parts from the same heat exhibit a trend toward the same deviation, stop production and initiate the hold and review process with process engineering, referring to MM-P1-L2-HT03 for furnace checks and SB-1035 for metallurgical assessment.

Records to keep
- Furnace setpoint log for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 showing the austenitizing setpoint entry and operator initials.
- Final inspection report for each part processed through P1-L2 line, including measurement entries and gauge identifiers.
- Transfer checklist between rolling and heat treat, signed by responsible personnel.
- Calibration certificates and evidence of gauge checks per MM-P1-L2-HT03.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records linked to SB-1035 when applicable.

Nonconformance handling
-----------------------
Detection and immediate actions
- When a dimensional nonconformance is detected, isolate affected parts and clearly tag them with a unique hold identifier. Record the finding on the final inspection report and notify quality control immediately.
- If the nonconformance is suspected to be related to heat treatment, suspend further runs to the furnace EQ-P1-L2-HT03 pending investigation. Consult MM-P1-L2-HT03 for furnace performance checks and SOP-P1-L2-04 for any operator action history.

Investigation and root cause
- Initiate a documented investigation that reviews furnace setpoint logs for EQ-P1-L2-HT03, transfer checklists, measurement records, and recent maintenance activity. Use SB-1035 for guidance on metallurgical examination when dimensional change could be microstructure related.
- Gather evidence: furnace log showing the austenitizing setpoint, measurement records, handling checklists, and calibration certificates. Preserve sample parts for metallurgical evaluation if required.

Disposition and corrective action
- Determine disposition using SB-1035 criteria for metallurgical acceptance and drawing limits for dimensional acceptance. Document the final disposition on the nonconformance report and link to the work order.
- Implement corrective actions proportionate to root cause. Examples include confirming the austenitizing setpoint on EQ-P1-L2-HT03, reinforcing SOP-P1-L2-04 transfer procedures with operators, or addressing gauge calibration gaps per MM-P1-L2-HT03.
- Record corrective actions, responsible parties, and verification steps. Close the nonconformance once all verification measures confirm compliance.

References
----------
See MM-P1-L2-HT03 for maintenance and calibration requirements; SB-1035 for metallurgical acceptance and test methods; SOP-P1-L2-04 for operation and transfer steps.
title: Ring rolling dimensional control (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-04 Shot peening coverage (P1)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Scope
- This quality specification describes requirements, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for shot peening coverage applied to components processed on line P1-L3 in Plant P1 using EQ-P1-L3-IH01. It applies to all production and rework parts that call out shot peening coverage control in the part drawing, purchase order, or process route. Related documents: ECN-2026-029, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05.

Background and intent
- Shot peening is used to impart controlled compressive residual stress and to improve fatigue life. This specification defines acceptance criteria, establishes inspection methods that are reproducible on the plant floor, and prescribes handling for observed nonconformance. The intent is to ensure consistent peening across part families processed at line P1-L3, with traceability and records that support root cause analysis and corrective action when required.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Description | Responsible |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| Process control | Shot peening parameters shall be set and recorded per the applicable process sheet and SOP-P1-L3-05. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. | Process engineer / Operator |
| Coverage documentation | Each peened part shall have a coverage inspection record completed and attached to the lot traveler. Coverage areas and exceptions shall be annotated. | Inspector |
| Media condition | Media lot identifier and media condition verification shall be recorded on the media log prior to production. | Maintenance / Quality |
| Equipment status | Equipment deviations that may affect peening uniformity shall be logged and held out of service until cleared. | Maintenance |
| Traceability | Part numbers, heat numbers, lot identifiers, operator initials, and shift identifier shall be recorded in the process record for each lot. | Operator / Quality |

Inspection method
- Visual sampling and documented measurement shall be used to verify peening coverage. Inspectors shall follow SOP-P1-L3-05 for detailed inspection steps and use calibrated tools listed in SB-1026. Use the following floor-level method to assess coverage:
  - Identify coverage zones per the part drawing and mark on the inspection form.
  - For each coverage zone, perform a surface appearance assessment per the acceptance criteria referenced in ECN-2026-029 and record as acceptable or not acceptable.
  - Capture a photographic record of representative zones for each lot and attach to the lot traveler.
- Rationale: Visual assessment combined with photographic evidence provides repeatable verification that can be reviewed during audits and correlates with fatigue performance when performed per the referenced engineering change and specification documents.
- Examples:
  - Example A: For a multi-feature component with overlapping arcs and flat faces, document inspection for each face and each arc, with photos showing boundary marks.
  - Example B: For a tubular configuration, document inspection on the inner bore and both external surfaces, noting any shadowed areas and corrective action taken to achieve coverage.

Calibration and tools
- Use only inspection tools and gauges referenced in SB-1026. Ensure tools are within calibration status prior to inspection. If tool calibration status is unknown, the lot shall be held pending verification.

Records to keep
- Lot traveler with completed coverage inspection form (attached).
- Photographic evidence files stored in the electronic process archive and referenced on the lot traveler.
- Media lot and condition log from the media storage area.
- Equipment status log for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 during the lot run.
- Calibration certificates for inspection tools used (as referenced in SB-1026).
- Any deviation reports or nonconformance records generated during the lot.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification: Any part or zone failing coverage inspection shall be segregated and tagged as nonconforming. The tag shall reference the lot traveler and inspection record.
- Containment: The affected lot shall be quarantined and production held until disposition is approved by Quality.
- Disposition options:
  - Rework: If re-peening is selected, document corrective actions to address root cause and perform a follow-up inspection per SOP-P1-L3-05. Record media and equipment checks performed prior to rework.
  - Use-as-is with concession: If allowed by the engineering authority under ECN-2026-029, a formal concession shall be recorded and attached to the lot traveler.
  - Scrapping: If neither rework nor concession is acceptable, the lot shall be scrapped per plant scrap procedure and documented.
- Root cause and corrective action: Perform root cause analysis using available records (equipment logs, media logs, operator notes). Document corrective actions and preventive measures in the nonconformance report. Link corrective action to the maintenance work order or engineering change as applicable.

Step rationale
- Segregation and documentation preserve traceability and allow retrospective analysis. Photographs and media logs provide objective evidence of process performance. Referencing ECN-2026-029 ensures any approved deviations or design-specific acceptance criteria are applied consistently. SOP-P1-L3-05 contains the operative floor procedures to ensure inspections are repeatable and auditable.

Audit and review
- Quality shall perform periodic reviews of coverage inspection records and nonconformance trends. Findings that indicate systemic issues require escalation to the process owner and may trigger an engineering review per ECN-2026-029.

References
- ECN-2026-029
- SB-1026
- SOP-P1-L3-05

Distribution and retention
- Retain coverage inspection records and associated attachments as specified in the plant document retention policy. Records shall be available for review during internal and external audits.

text:
# QS-PROC-05 Machining surface finish (P1)
Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Scope
This quality specification defines the surface finish acceptance criteria, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for machined forgings produced on line P1-L4 and processed through the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03). It applies to all incoming forging blanks and finished machined components routed through Plant P1 where machining surface finish affects functional fit, wear life, and downstream processing. The document supplements operational procedures and change notices; refer to ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-01, and SOP-P1-L4-02 for process setup, batch handling, and heat treat workflow.

Requirements table
| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Evidence to record |
|---|---|---|
| Surface finish after final machining | Conforms to drawing surface finish callouts and functional fit for mating parts | Final inspection report with measured locations and inspector initials; include referenced drawing revision |
| Machine setup | Tools and machine parameters set per SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 | Setup checklist completed and retained with job traveler |
| Post-heat treat timing for quench | The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. | Heat treat batch log indicating furnace ID, timer start/stop, and operator signature |
| Visual surface integrity | No visible machining tears, deep gouges, or foreign material embedded in critical surfaces | Visual inspection record and photographs where nonconformances are observed |
| Debris removal prior to inspection | Component clean and free of cutting fluids and chips per SOP-P1-L4-02 | Cleaning verification on inspection form |

Inspection method
Background and rationale
Surface finish is a primary determinant of part function where contact, sealing, or bearing surfaces are employed. Machining steps can introduce fine irregularities, tool marks, or embedded debris that compromise assembly and performance. This inspection method describes procedures to verify finish and to capture timing with the heat treat step, since surface characteristics can change when parts are quenched or otherwise processed thermally.

Preparation
- Confirm the job traveler and referenced drawing are present. Cross-reference with SOP-P1-L4-01 for machine set up and SOP-P1-L4-02 for cleaning and handling.
- Verify heat treat records for the lot processed through EQ-P1-L4-HT03. Ensure the quench delay timing is recorded as required.

Measurement points and instrumentation
- Identify critical surfaces as called out on the drawing. When no explicit callout exists, inspect functional mating surfaces and visible bearing interfaces.
- Use calibrated surface finish measuring instruments and visual aids as specified in SOP-P1-L4-01. Calibration status must be current and recorded.

Procedure
- Clean the part in accordance with SOP-P1-L4-02 before any measurement.
- Measure surface finish at the designated locations. Record instrument used and reading for each point.
- For batches processed in the furnace identified as EQ-P1-L4-HT03, verify the quench delay in the heat treat batch log. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Record the logged time next to inspection measurements to maintain traceability between thermal processing and surface condition.
- Document any surface anomalies with high-resolution photographs and annotate the location on the drawing or a copy of the inspection form.
- Complete the final inspection report, sign, and attach the heat treat batch log extract.

Examples and interpretation
- Example: If a mating surface shows higher than expected roughness readings but the heat treat batch log indicates a quench delay within the required maximum for EQ-P1-L4-HT03, the deviation is likely machining related. Follow nonconformance handling below.
- Example: If roughness readings are acceptable but visual inspection reveals embedded debris, the cause may be inadequate cleaning post-machining. Recleaning and reinspection are required per SOP-P1-L4-02 and records must show corrective action.
- Record linkage: For any condition that may relate to thermal processing, include the EQ-P1-L4-HT03 identifier and the quench delay value exactly as logged to facilitate later root cause analysis.

Records to keep
- Final inspection report with surface finish readings and annotated drawing.
- Heat treat batch log extract showing furnace ID and quench delay for EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
- Machine setup checklist per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Cleaning verification per SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Photographic evidence of any nonconformance.
All records shall be retained in the document control system under the job traveler and referenced by job number and lot for traceability.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and containment
- Any part that fails to meet the acceptance criteria in the requirements table shall be segregated and clearly labeled until disposition.
- For conditions possibly linked to heat treat timing, include the EQ-P1-L4-HT03 batch log and the recorded quench delay. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds; verify compliance before further disposition.

Disposition options
- Rework: If deviation is limited to machinable defects (for example, tool marks beyond acceptable limits), machine rework is permitted if rework does not affect material integrity or functional dimensions. Re-inspect and record results.
- Repair: For surface defects that can be corrected by controlled processes defined in SOP-P1-L4-02, follow repair procedure and document operator and inspection approval.
- Reject: If defects compromise function or safety and cannot be corrected without altering the part beyond allowed limits, move to reject and document per plant rejection workflow.

Root cause and corrective action
- Initiate an investigation for recurring defects or any case where the quench delay log for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 shows a value exceeding the specified maximum. Reference ECN-2026-002 when proposed process changes are required.
- Document root cause analysis and corrective actions. Update SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-02 only after authorization and align with ECN-2026-002 as needed.

Review and approval
- Inspectors, heat treat operators, and process engineers shall review combined inspection and heat treat records for conformity. Any change to acceptance criteria or measurement methods must be controlled through ECN-2026-002.

End of document.
title: Machining surface finish (P1)

text:
# QS-PROC-06 Forging temperature control (P2)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
- This quality specification defines mandatory requirements and inspection methods for forging temperature control related to Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) on line P2-L1 at Plant P2. It applies to operations, maintenance, and quality personnel responsible for set up, monitoring, and corrective action for induction heating and associated coil cooling systems. Refer to change control and operating procedures listed in References.

Background and rationale
- Consistent temperature control of billets during induction heating is critical to forging quality and die life. Induction heater coil cooling directly affects heater performance and reliability. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Maintaining this minimum prevents coil overheating, reduces risk of equipment damage, and stabilizes heat transfer to the billet. This specification implements a single-point requirement for coil cooling flow and defines inspection and nonconformance handling to ensure traceability and timely corrective action.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| Coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 | The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. | Production lead, Maintenance lead |
| Flow sensing and recording | Flow sensing devices must be functional and provide readable output to the operator interface; records of flow readings associated with each heating batch must be retained as specified in Records. | Instrumentation technician |
| Preventive maintenance interaction | Preventive maintenance activities that affect coil or water circuits must follow SOP-P2-L1-02 and SOP-P2-L1-03 and be documented in maintenance logs. | Maintenance planner |
| Change control | Any modification to heating or cooling circuits must be initiated via ECN-2026-039 or successor change notice processes and approved prior to implementation. | Engineering |

Inspection method
- Purpose: Verify that coil cooling flow meets the minimum requirement and that sensing/recording systems are competent for quality records.

- Pre-inspection check: Confirm continuity of the water circuit and that instrumentation is powered and communicating. If instrumentation is nonfunctional, follow nonconformance handling below; do not proceed without initiating corrective steps.

- Measurement: For each operational shift or production batch, observe the flow instrument associated with EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and confirm the recorded value meets the requirement. When automated logs are available, extract the flow record corresponding to the heating event and include it with the production run documentation.

- Acceptance decision: A flow record that meets the requirement is acceptable. A flow reading below the minimum is nonconforming; take immediate action per Nonconformance handling.

- Examples and rationale:
  - Example of acceptable record: an operator log entry or automated record indicating the flow at or above the minimum during the heating event. This validates cooling adequacy for that event.
  - Example of nonconforming record: any record showing flow below the minimum during a heating event, or missing flow data for a heating event where verification cannot be established. Missing data is treated equivalently to below-minimum flow for disposition purposes because it prevents verification of cooling adequacy.

- Records to keep: Retain the flow reading or automated log extract associated with each heating batch, the operator verification checklist, and any corrective action records generated for the event. These records support quality investigations and must be available for audits and for any ECN invoked.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate actions:
  - If coil cooling flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is found below the minimum, stop billet feed to the heater and notify maintenance and production supervision immediately.
  - Isolate the heater per safe work practices and secure the process to prevent further heating events until documented corrective action is completed.

- Troubleshooting steps and documentation:
  - Verify instrument function and wiring. If instrumentation is failed, document failure and initiate repair under SOP-P2-L1-02 or SOP-P2-L1-03 as applicable.
  - Inspect supply circuits and valves for obvious restriction or isolation. Record findings in the maintenance log and in the unit incident report.

- Disposition and corrective action:
  - Do not release any forgings processed during intervals where coil cooling flow could not be verified as meeting the minimum, until an engineering disposition is issued.
  - Document corrective actions taken, root cause analysis, and verification of restoration of compliant flow. Include flow records demonstrating sustained compliance before returning the heater to normal production.

- Escalation and change control:
  - If the root cause implicates design, materials, or recurring failures, initiate ECN-2026-039 to propose engineering changes. All modifications must be approved and documented before implementation.

Records and retention
- Maintain the following records linked to each heating event or batch: flow reading or automated log extract for EQ-P2-L1-IH02, operator verification checklist, maintenance incident reports, corrective action documentation, and any related ECN documentation. Retain records per the plant records retention policy and make available for quality audits.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-039
- SOP-P2-L1-02
- SOP-P2-L1-03

Revision control
- This specification is Rev E. Amendments to this document must be processed through the plant document control workflow and cross-referenced to ECN-2026-039 when applicable.
title: Forging temperature control (P2)

text:
# QS-PROC-07 Quench and temper process window (P2)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Scope
- This quality specification defines the acceptable process window for quench and temper operations performed on parts processed on line P2-L2 in plant P2, with emphasis on operations that reference Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01). It establishes requirements, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for process variables and records that determine heat treatment outcome and part integrity. This document applies to finished forgings and to in-process billets that proceed to subsequent machining or assembly operations. Related procedural controls and setup steps are documented in SB-1024, SOP-P2-L2-02, and SOP-P2-L2-04.

Background and rationale
- Heat treating by quench and temper produces microstructure and mechanical properties sensitive to heating uniformity, quench media condition, and tempering profiles. The intent of this specification is to reduce variability originating at the induction heater, quench station, and tempering furnace by identifying critical requirements and inspection points. Equipment-specific considerations for EQ-P2-L2-IH01 are included to ensure lubricant application and heater condition do not compromise surface quality or dimensional stability. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938. Inclusion of lubricant identification allows consistent procurement and application during billet preheat and handling.

Requirements table
- The table below lists process elements, acceptance criteria, rationale, and required records. Acceptance criteria are qualitative where numerical specifications are governed by separate controlled documents; refer to SB-1024 and SOP-P2-L2-02 for measurement procedures.

| Process element | Acceptance criteria | Rationale | Records to keep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Induction heater condition (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) | Heater surfaces clean, intact, and free of deposits; lubricant applied per equipment maintenance reference; visual confirmation of no arcing or smoke during run | Surface condition affects heat transfer uniformity and surface appearance of billets; lubricant selection prevents sticking and minimizes contamination | Equipment maintenance log; visual inspection checklist; lubricant usage record |
| Preheat and soak uniformity | Billet shows no visible thermal gradients or discoloration bands; operator notes uniform coloration and consistent surface appearance across length | Uniform heating is critical to avoid quench distortion and inconsistent microstructure | Process log; operator preheat verification entry |
| Quench medium condition | Quench media clarity and agitation as specified in SOP-P2-L2-04; no visible contamination, foaming, or film at surface | Contaminated or degraded quench medium alters cooling rate and may cause nonuniform hardness or surface defects | Quench media test record; daily media inspection form |
| Tempering stage | Parts exhibit uniform temper color or appearance consistent with reference samples; no temper embrittlement indicators | Tempering restores toughness and relieves residual stress; visual and mechanical indications guide accept/reject | Tempering cycle completion record; temper verification inspection |
| Surface quality after quench | Surface free of quench-related scale, deposits, or fluid retention; any residue removed per cleaning procedure prior to final inspection | Surface defects can mask defects and impede downstream processes | Post-quench cleaning record; final surface inspection report |
| Documentation and traceability | Each heat event documented with unique heat identifier and cross-reference to SB-1024; operator initials and review required | Traceability enables root cause analysis and supplier audits | Heat event log; traceability ledger; sign-off sheet |

Inspection method
- Visual inspection is the primary method for initial acceptance at the induction heater, quench, and temper stages. Inspectors must be trained to recognize the acceptance criteria listed in the requirements table and to use reference samples kept at the line for color and surface condition comparisons. For items where nondestructive testing is specified in SB-1024, inspectors shall follow the method and acceptance criteria in that document. When doubt exists regarding heating uniformity or surface condition, escalate for metallographic cross-sectioning or hardness testing as directed in SOP-P2-L2-02.
- Inspection steps, performed in the sequence below, form the minimum required checks for each heat event:
  - Verify equipment readiness and confirm lubricant CFW-LUB-938 is available and applied per maintenance practice for EQ-P2-L2-IH01.
  - Perform visual verification of billet heating uniformity at the induction heater exit using reference coloration samples.
  - Inspect quench medium condition prior to immersion; document any deviation and do not proceed if contamination or abnormal behavior is observed.
  - After quench, inspect surface condition and ensure cleaning procedures are applied before tempering.
  - During temper, compare part appearance to temper reference samples; document completion and any anomalies.
- Sampling and additional inspection follow the guidance in SB-1024; coordinate with quality engineering if destructive testing is required. Records from each inspection step must be retained in the process log and made available for audit.

Nonconformance handling
- Any condition that fails to meet the acceptance criteria in the requirements table constitutes a nonconformance. Examples include visible heater deposits, quench medium contamination, nonuniform heating signs, or tempering anomalies. Handling steps:
  - Contain affected lots by tagging parts and halting downstream flow until disposition is determined.
  - Notify line supervision and quality engineering immediately, providing heat event identifier and a summary of observed condition.
  - Perform root cause evaluation referencing SB-1024 and SOP-P2-L2-02; include review of maintenance logs for EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and confirmation of lubricant CFW-LUB-938 usage where relevant.
  - If rework is feasible and permitted by specification, define corrective action in writing and record all steps taken. Examples of permissible corrective actions include controlled temper adjustments or surface cleaning when allowed by applicable product specification.
  - When disposition requires scrapping or segregation, record the decision and notify procurement if lubricant or equipment condition contributed to failure.
  - Implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence and document verification activities and effectiveness checks in the process log.
- All nonconformance records shall reference SB-1024 and include links to any applicable work instructions in SOP-P2-L2-02 and SOP-P2-L2-04. Retain nonconformance reports, inspection checklists, and corrective action documentation in the quality system for review during audits.

Records and examples
- Maintain a complete file per heat event containing: heat event log, equipment maintenance log for EQ-P2-L2-IH01, lubricant usage record for CFW-LUB-938, quench media inspection records, temper verification, and any nonconformance reports. Example entries and templates are provided in SOP-P2-L2-02. Records are required for traceability and to support continuous improvement activities outlined in SB-1024.

End of specification.
title: Quench and temper process window (P2)

text:
# QS-PROC-08 Ring rolling dimensional control (P2)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Scope
- This quality specification defines dimensional control requirements for ring rolling operations on line P2-L2 and associated heat treat staging at EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Applies to all ring rolling billets and forgings processed on P2-L2 that will be heat treated using EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and subsequently inspected for dimensional conformance.
- Excludes operations outside of P2-L2 and heat treat furnaces not identified as EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Cross-reference change notices and procedural instructions are provided in ECN-2026-028, ECN-2026-031, and SOP-P2-L2-04.

Background and rationale
- Dimensional drift during ring rolling and handling to heat treat can cause downstream nonconformance that impacts machining yield and final assembly acceptance. This specification consolidates inspection points, acceptance rationale, and corrective actions to protect product geometry and traceability.
- The lubricant specified for furnace staging and contact surfaces for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376. Using the specified lubricant mitigates surface upset and localized galling during handling between rolling and heat treat staging; lubricant selection is controlled to maintain metallurgical and dimensional integrity per ECN-2026-028 and SOP-P2-L2-04.

Requirements table

| Requirement ID | Description | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| R-A | Dimensional inspection at final roll exit | Measured geometry shall match drawing intent and specified tolerances documented in customer drawing or job traveler; measurement plan shall reference the drawing noted on the traveler |
| R-B | Inspection immediately prior to heat treat staging at EQ-P2-L2-HT02 | Parts shall be assessed for handling damage, burrs, and witness marks; parts with handling damage that could affect final machining are segregated |
| R-C | Lubricant control for staging and contact surfaces | Only lubricant CFW-LUB-376 is authorized for use on surfaces that contact parts staged for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 |
| R-D | Measurement instrument calibration and traceability | Instruments used for dimensional checks shall be listed on the job traveler; calibration status shall be available in records; measurements without instrument status are not accepted |
| R-E | Record retention and traceability | Dimensional reports, traveler sign-off, and lubricant lot used shall be retained with the job file in accordance with shop quality retention rules defined in ECN-2026-031 |

Inspection method
- Sampling and measurement plan:
  - Inspection locations and measurement features shall be derived from the customer drawing referenced on the job traveler. Inspectors shall follow the sequence in SOP-P2-L2-04 for handling and measurement to minimize handling-induced variation.
  - Measurement devices shall be confirmed as calibrated and suitable for the feature type. Record device identifier and calibration status on the dimensional report.
- Measurement procedure overview:
  - Clean the feature per SOP-P2-L2-04 and remove transient debris using approved wipes and, where staging contact is required, use only CFW-LUB-376 as the contact lubricant. Document lubricant lot in the dimensional report.
  - Orient the part using datum features specified on the drawing. Apply measurement devices according to instrument manufacturer guidance and good metrology practice. Record each reading and the instrument identifier.
  - For features with tight form or concentricity intent, perform comparative checks against the master fixture or reference standard recorded in the job file.
- Examples and clarifications:
  - Example scenario: a ring leaving the final roll shows a surface nick at a noncritical location. Inspector segregates part per R-B and records the condition; part disposition follows Nonconformance handling below.
  - Example scenario: a measurement device is found with expired calibration status. Measurements made with that device are invalid. Re-measure the part with a calibrated device and note the corrective action on the dimensional report.
- Records to keep:
  - Dimensional report for each work order with part identifier, feature measurements, instrument identifiers, lubricant lot used (CFW-LUB-376), inspector initials or electronic signature, and reference drawing noted.
  - Job traveler sign-off showing inspection points completed.
  - Instrument calibration certificates or traceable identifiers supporting the measurement devices used.
  - Segregation tags and disposition records for any parts placed on hold.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate actions:
  - Any part failing to meet the drawing intent or showing handling damage that could affect downstream processing shall be segregated and tagged with a hold status. The hold tag shall reference the part identifier and the reason for hold.
  - Notify the shift quality lead and the rolling supervisor. Reference ECN-2026-028 for engineering notification requirements when part geometry deviates from baseline expectations.
- Investigation and disposition:
  - Perform root cause assessment focusing on process steps from final roll through staging at EQ-P2-L2-HT02, including handling, fixturing, and lubricant application. Include review of the dimensional report, instrument calibration records, and the lubricant lot recorded for CFW-LUB-376 usage.
  - Disposition options include rework, repair, use-as-is with concession, or scrap, as permitted by customer agreements and internal engineering authorization. Document disposition decision and responsible approver in the job file.
- Corrective actions and preventive measures:
  - For repeated incidents tied to handling or fixturing, implement containment and process changes; update SOP-P2-L2-04 when changes to handling or measurement sequences are required.
  - When lubricant-related issues are suspected, verify lubricant lot and shelf condition for CFW-LUB-376 and suspend use pending investigation. Record findings and corrective actions in the nonconformance record.
- Records and closure:
  - All nonconformance records, investigation notes, disposition approvals, and verification results are retained with the job file and cross-referenced to ECN-2026-031 where change documentation is required.
  - Closure of nonconformance requires verification that corrective actions are implemented and that affected lots are either reworked to meet drawing intent or properly disposed.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-028
- ECN-2026-031
- SOP-P2-L2-04

Revision control and approvals
- Maintain this specification under document control. Approval block and revision history are stored in the document control system with links to the job files and related ECN records.
title: Ring rolling dimensional control (P2)

text:
# QS-PROC-09 Shot peening coverage (P2)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-HT02

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance and verification requirements for shot peening coverage applied to machined forgings processed on P2, line P2-L3 and associated operations that affect peened surfaces. It applies to production and rework where shot peening is used to achieve fatigue-strength improvements and residual compressive stress profiles prior to final machining or hardening processes. This document supplements process maintenance and operation procedures and is to be read in conjunction with MM-P2-L3-HT02, MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3, and SOP-P2-L3-03.

Requirements table
- Purpose: Record minimum coverage goals, critical control points, and referenced equipment conditions that are required for acceptance of peened components.
- Table entries:
  - Process step: Shot peening on parts routed from P2-L3 line
  - Acceptance criteria: Visual and nondestructive evidence of consistent coverage of targeted feature surfaces, no damage or deformation attributable to peening that would impair fit, function, or downstream processing
  - Critical control point: Equipment setup, media condition, nozzle patterning, and masking integrity
  - Related equipment condition: The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C.
  - Records to retain: Peening cycle log, media lot ID, operator identifier, masking verification checklist, post-peen inspection images, and disposition notes

Inspection method
- Rationale: Shot peening alters surface topology and residual stress. Inspection focuses on confirming a consistent and adequate peened surface while preserving part geometry and identifying any overpeening or media damage.
- Method overview: Inspectors perform a systematic surface survey of all peened faces using visual magnification and comparison to reference surface condition samples. Nondestructive checks such as surface topology imaging and adherence to referenced setup parameters documented in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and SOP-P2-L3-03 are used to corroborate visual findings.
- Steps:
  - Verify documentation from the peening operation: operator signature, media lot, blast cabinet or nozzle setup description, and masking checklist. Confirm that the peening operation was performed under the machine and process setup identified for parts from P2-L3 as recorded in MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.
  - Perform visual survey under appropriate illumination. Inspectors look for uniform matte appearance and absence of concentrated burnishing, gouges, or embedded media. Compare to reference images maintained in the quality system.
  - Use magnification to inspect feature edges, fillets, and radii for peen-induced distortion or fracture initiators. Document findings with annotated images attached to the inspection record.
  - Where surface residual stress or coverage mapping is required by engineering, coordinate with quality engineering to perform the specified nondestructive testing and report results per SOP-P2-L3-03.
- Examples to illustrate judgment:
  - A uniform appearance over an exposed bearing journal that matches the approved reference image is considered acceptable when all documentation and masking evidence are in order.
  - Localized deformation adjacent to a masked edge that indicates masking slip or incorrect nozzle angle requires containment and disposition per the nonconformance handling section.
- Records and traceability:
  - Maintain peening cycle logs and media lot identification with the part route card. Attach inspection images and the inspector checklist to the part history file.
  - Retain traceable links to setup sheets and maintenance records referenced in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3.

Nonconformance handling
- Objective: Provide clear, auditable steps to identify, quarantine, evaluate, and disposition parts exhibiting unacceptable peening results.
- Detection: Nonconforming conditions are identified through in-process inspection, final inspection, or field return. Examples of nonconformance include localized overpeening that reduces section integrity, visible media embedding not removed by cleaning, or peening on surfaces that should have been masked.
- Immediate actions:
  - Quarantine affected parts and mark routing to prevent unintended processing.
  - Notify the process owner and quality engineer. Preserve the peened part and associated fixture or masking sample to enable root cause analysis.
- Investigation and disposition:
  - Perform root cause analysis using documented media condition, operator setup, and machine state logs. Review applicable entries in MM-P2-L3-HT02 and MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3 for maintenance and setup history that may have contributed.
  - Evaluate whether the condition is correctable by rework without compromising part integrity. If rework is undertaken, document the corrective process, operators involved, and post-rework inspection evidence.
  - If the part is not suitable for rework, record rejection and scrap in the production and quality records.
- Preventive actions:
  - Where recurring causes are identified, update SOP-P2-L3-03 and the MM documents cited to reflect improved controls, additional operator training, or updated masking methods.
  - Implement changes to the peening setup or media handling only after verification and approval by process engineering and quality; document the verification results and update the records referenced in the requirements table.
- Records to keep for each nonconformance:
  - Quarantine tag and routing identifier, root cause analysis summary, corrective and preventive actions taken, disposition decision, and post-action inspection evidence. Link all records to the part history and the MM and SOP documents cited above.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-HT02
- MM-P2-L3-HT02-S3
- SOP-P2-L3-03

Notes
- This specification is intended to be applied in concert with the machine maintenance and standard operating procedures referenced above. Use the records listed to maintain process traceability and to support continuous improvement activities.
title: Shot peening coverage (P2)

text:
# QS-PROC-10 Machining surface finish (P2)
Revision: Rev E
Plant: P2, line P2-L3
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This quality specification defines the surface finish requirements, monitoring, and controls for machined forgings processed at P2, line P2-L3 using Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03). It applies to all machining operations where the induction heater conditions influence billet temperature homogeneity and resultant surface finish. The intent is to ensure consistent surface condition for downstream processing and customer requirements.

Background and rationale
- Surface finish of forgings is influenced by initial billet condition, machining parameters, and billet heating uniformity. The induction billet heater provides thermal conditioning that affects material ductility and chip formation. Cooling of the heater coils is critical to maintain stable coil impedance and field distribution; inadequate coil cooling correlates with irregular heating and surface anomalies. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Maintaining this minimum is a preventive control to reduce the likelihood of thermal-induced surface defects.

Requirements table
| Item | Requirement | Responsible |
|---|---|---|
| Coil cooling water flow | Coil cooling water flow must be maintained at or above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03): 72 L/min. | Maintenance / Production |
| Visual surface condition | Finished machined surfaces shall be free of burn patterns, discoloration, or surface tearing attributable to heating irregularities. | Production |
| Process adherence | All operators shall follow SOP-P2-L3-02 and SOP-P2-L3-05 for setup and machining sequences. Deviations that could affect surface finish must be documented and approved by Quality. | Production / Quality |
| Monitoring and records | Continuous recording of coil cooling water flow and visual inspection records shall be retained per MM-P2-L3-IH03 guidance. | Operations / Quality |

Inspection method
- Pre-shift verification
  - Confirm equipment readiness per SOP-P2-L3-02 and SOP-P2-L3-05 before initiating production. Verify that the coil cooling system is operating and that the flow indicator shows stable flow. Acceptance is based on the requirement in this document.
- Flow verification
  - Verify the coil cooling water flow against the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03): 72 L/min. Use the institutionally approved flow meter or monitoring device calibrated per MM-P2-L3-IH03. If the flow instrument indicates below the stated minimum, follow nonconformance handling steps before machining resumes.
- Visual surface inspection
  - Inspect a representative sample of machined surfaces immediately after machining for signs of thermal damage: burn marks, discoloration, or irregular chip morphology. Record findings on the operation's inspection log. If borderline conditions are detected, quarantine affected pieces and escalate to Quality.
- Follow-up verification
  - When any adjustment to coil cooling or heater operation is made, verify return to acceptable flow and perform a targeted surface inspection on subsequent machined billets to confirm issue resolution.

Examples and interpretation
- Example scenario: If visual inspection reveals localized discoloration on the machined surface concurrent with a recorded drop in coil cooling flow below the specified minimum, this suggests heater instability contributed to the defect. The immediate action is to stop production, implement containment, and escalate per nonconformance handling.
- Example scenario: If surface tearing is noted but recorded coil cooling flow meets the minimum, the issue may originate from tooling condition or machining parameters. Follow SOP-P2-L3-02 and SOP-P2-L3-05 for tooling and process checks and document findings.

Records to keep
- Coil cooling flow logs obtained from the installed monitoring device. Retain according to MM-P2-L3-IH03 guidance.
- Pre-shift equipment checklist completed per SOP-P2-L3-02.
- Machining setup and parameter records per SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Visual inspection logs and nonconformance reports. Include photographs when applicable.
- Corrective action and containment records including root cause analysis and validation of corrective measures.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate containment
  - Stop processing when a confirmed nonconformance related to heater cooling or surface finish is identified. Segregate affected material to prevent inadvertent shipment or further processing.
- Notification and escalation
  - Notify Production Lead and Quality immediately. Reference this document and associated guidance in MM-P2-L3-IH03, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-05 in communications and reports.
- Investigation
  - Conduct a structured investigation to determine root cause. Consider coil cooling system performance relative to the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03): 72 L/min., heater control stability, tooling wear, and adherence to machining procedures.
- Corrective action
  - Implement corrective actions based on investigation findings. Actions may include repairing cooling system components, updating procedures, retraining operators, or replacing tooling. Validate corrective action effectiveness by monitoring subsequent production for absence of recurrence and by reviewing records listed above.
- Disposition
  - Quality will determine disposition of affected material. Criteria for release include demonstrable process stability and inspection evidence that surface finish meets customer and internal acceptance criteria.
- Documentation
  - Maintain a nonconformance file that includes the initial report, investigation findings, corrective actions taken, verification of effectiveness, and any procedural changes. Cross-reference MM-P2-L3-IH03, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-05 where relevant.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-IH03
- SOP-P2-L3-02
- SOP-P2-L3-05

Revision control and approvals
- Maintain this quality specification under document control. Record approvals and revision history in the document control system entry for QS-PROC-10.

# ECN-2026-001 Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a formal change to the heat treat process control limits for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). Background: recent in-process inspection findings and a review of process capability records identified excursions in quench timing that have a plausible link to surface condition variability on forged components. A cross-functional review including Production, Heat Treat, Metallurgy, Maintenance, and Quality concluded that the control of quench initiation must be clarified and enforced to reduce variability and support downstream process consistency.

Change rationale: the change establishes a firm maximum permitted quench delay to minimize microstructural divergence caused by inconsistent thermal exposure prior to quench. The change is preventive and intended to reduce rework, nonconforming product incidents, and metallurgical uncertainty. The change aligns with procedural controls in SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05 and permits a single, auditable process limit to be referenced by operators, maintenance personnel, and quality auditors.

Affected items
- Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) process control documentation and operator checklists.  
- All heat treat work orders specifying furnace EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Control software alarm set points, HMI prompts, and maintenance lubrication work items that reference quench timing.  
- Training materials and operator qualification records for personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02.

Process limit to be implemented
The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds.

Implementation
Scope and applicability: this limit applies to all parts processed in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 when the furnace is used in its normal heat treat cycles as identified in the plant routing. The limit is to be applied from the established quench initiation point defined in the furnace HMI sequence to the actual commencement of quench flow. Operators will be required to follow the updated sequence in the furnace HMI and to log events according to the revised checklist.

Steps for implementation:
- Update process documents: revise the EQ-P3-L4-HT02 process sheet and the operator checklist to include the quench delay maximum statement. Reference and update SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05 as required for consistency; changes to the SOPs will be coordinated through document control.  
- HMI and alarm configuration: configure the furnace HMI to display the quench delay target and to alarm when the elapsed time approaches the maximum. Configure the event log to capture the timestamp of quench initiation and the timestamp of quench command for audit traceability.  
- Maintenance verification: perform a mechanical and control verification to ensure the quench valve actuation and sensing are functioning to support the limit; record verification results in the equipment maintenance record.  
- Training: train all operators and maintenance staff assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 on the revised process limit, HMI changes, and the requirement to log quench initiation events. Training completion will be recorded in personnel training records.  
- Verification runs: perform production verification runs using scrap or designated verification lots to demonstrate process stability under the new limit. Record outcomes, including any out-of-limit events and corrective actions, in the furnace process log.

Examples and expected responses
- Example operator response: when the HMI indicates a pending quench command, the operator verifies that the quench flow is initiated immediately. If the HMI alarm for delay is triggered, the operator follows the abnormal procedure to stop the cycle and notify Heat Treat supervision.  
- Example maintenance response: if a repeated alarm indicates inability to meet the quench delay maximum, maintenance isolates the quench valve, inspects actuators and sensors, and repairs or replaces defective components. Maintenance documents the work performed and returns the equipment to service only after a verification run is successful.

Records to keep
- Updated process sheet and operator checklist for EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- HMI event logs capturing quench command timestamp and quench initiation timestamp for each cycle processed in EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Maintenance verification records and any corrective maintenance work orders related to quench actuation components.  
- Training completion records for all personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Verification run records showing process outcomes and any investigations for out-of-limit events.  
All records will be retained in the plant document control system and made available for internal audits and process reviews. The SOPs cited for procedural alignment are SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05.

Approvals
The change requires sign-off from Heat Treat Management, Quality Engineering, Plant Operations, and Maintenance Management. Approval acknowledges review of background data, acceptance of the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and commitment to implement the actions described under Implementation. Post-implementation, Quality Engineering will schedule a process compliance audit to review records and to validate that the change has achieved the intended reduction in process variability.

This ECN becomes effective upon completion of approvals and staged implementation as described above.
title: Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

# ECN-2026-002 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Reason for change
- Background: During a recent review of heat treat process capability and post-process metallurgical data for parts processed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03, process engineering and quality identified a variance between intended austenitizing energy input and the furnace control setpoint history. The variance correlated with marginal case depth consistency on a segment of production parts subjected to the existing control strategy. The change is intended to tighten metallurgical consistency and bring process documentation and control setpoints into alignment with current metallurgical requirements.
- Rationale: Consolidating the documented austenitizing setpoint with the furnace control configuration reduces ambiguity for operators and maintenance staff, and reduces risk of downstream nonconformance. The specific actionable change is the formal specification of the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 as the single authoritative value used in process control, machine setup, and shop floor documentation.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P1-L4-HT03 (Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3) is the only equipment affected by this notice.
- Procedures and work instructions: SOP-P1-L4-03 will be updated to reflect the new authoritative austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and to include verification steps for setpoint confirmation during startup and before each production run.
- Maintenance documents: MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 will be revised to include check procedures that confirm controller parameters for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 match the authoritative setpoint and to record the results of setpoint confirmation after maintenance actions that impact the control loop.
- Quality processes: QS-PROC-05 will be annotated to indicate that quality verification for heat treat acceptance includes confirmation of the austenitizing setpoint recorded in furnace controller logs and operator pre-run checklists.
- Inventory items and product families processed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 are indirectly affected; operators will be required to follow the updated SOP-P1-L4-03 checklist for any job scheduled on EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

Implementation
- Authoritative setpoint: The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. This value is the single authority for controller configuration, process documentation, and acceptance criteria for parts processed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
- Controller update and verification: Process engineering will update the furnace control configuration to reflect the authoritative setpoint. After update, a verification sequence will be executed to confirm that the controller displays and logs the setpoint accurately and that operator pre-run checklists capture the displayed value.
- Procedure updates: SOP-P1-L4-03 will be revised to include explicit steps for setting and verifying the austenitizing setpoint on EQ-P1-L4-HT03, instructions for documenting the displayed setpoint in the operator log, and actions to take if the displayed setpoint does not match the authoritative setpoint.
- Maintenance checks: MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 will be revised to require technicians to confirm controller parameter integrity following any maintenance that affects thermal control elements, with a mandatory entry into the maintenance record that states the controller setpoint matches the authoritative setpoint.
- Quality actions: QS-PROC-05 will be updated to include a requirement that quality inspection records for heat-treated parts include the furnace controller log printout or digital export demonstrating the applied austenitizing setpoint for the batch, and that any deviation triggers the existing nonconformance workflow referenced in QS-PROC-05.
- Training and communication: A short training brief will be issued to affected operators, maintenance technicians, and quality inspectors that explains the change, the location of the authoritative setpoint in process documentation, and the verification steps to be performed. Training attendance and acknowledgment will be recorded in the training management system and referenced in the ECN closure package.
- Examples and expected records: Example artifacts to be created and retained include the revised SOP-P1-L4-03 page with the setpoint confirmation checklist filled out, the MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 maintenance entry confirming controller parameter integrity, and the QS-PROC-05 inspection record containing the furnace controller log or digital export showing the 880 °C setpoint. All artifacts will be retained in the document control system under the existing record retention location for heat treat process documentation.
- Change control and verification: After implementation, a process audit will be performed to verify adherence to the revised SOP-P1-L4-03 and to confirm that operating logs for a representative set of runs on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 reflect the authoritative setpoint. Any nonconformances discovered during the audit will be handled through the corrective action process defined in QS-PROC-05.

Approvals
- Responsible engineering approver: Process engineering signoff is required to finalize the control configuration change for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and to approve the revised SOP-P1-L4-03 and MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 content prior to release.
- Quality approver: Quality management must approve the updates to QS-PROC-05 and the acceptance criteria that reference the 880 °C setpoint as part of heat treat verification.
- Maintenance approver: Maintenance management must approve the MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3 revisions and confirm training requirements for technicians.
- Closure requirements: For ECN closure, submit the following package referencing this ECN: revised SOP-P1-L4-03, revised MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3, revised QS-PROC-05 annotations, controller configuration export for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 showing the authoritative setpoint, representative operator pre-run checklists, maintenance entries showing post-maintenance verification, and training attendance records. The change will be closed when all approvers have signed and the closure package is accepted for retention by document control.

Related documents: MM-P1-L4-HT03-S3, QS-PROC-05, SOP-P1-L4-03

# ECN-2026-003 - Change notice - Hot Forge CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-CN02

Reason for change
- Background: During the quarterly maintenance review of EQ-P1-L1-CN02, maintenance and production teams identified inconsistent spindle lubrication reports and an increase in minor bearing noise events documented in the maintenance log. Field inspection found multiple lubricant containers in use with inconsistent labeling and no single approved supplier record for this asset in the equipment master. To standardize lubrication practice and reduce variability in preventive maintenance outcomes, a single approved lubricant part number is being adopted for EQ-P1-L1-CN02.
- Objective: Establish and document the approved lubricant for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 to ensure consistent procurement, storage, application, and recordkeeping across P1-L1.
- Scope: This ECN standardizes lubricant selection only. It does not alter machine settings, cycle parameters, or SOP machining steps covered in SOP-P1-L1-02 and SOP-P1-L1-04 beyond lubrication application steps specified below.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-CN02 (Hot Forge CNC turning center #2).
- Consumable: Lubricant for spindle and guideways for EQ-P1-L1-CN02.
- Documentation: Update equipment master entry and maintenance task cards referenced in MM-P1-L1-CN02 to reflect the approved lubricant part number.
- Procedures: Revise the lubrication steps in SOP-P1-L1-02 and SOP-P1-L1-04 where they refer to lubricant selection or procurement. Changes will be limited to lubricant identification and storage instructions; machine operation steps remain unchanged.
- Inventory and procurement: Update procurement catalog and bin labeling in storeroom to show the approved part number for EQ-P1-L1-CN02.

Approved lubricant
- The lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508 (part number).

Implementation
- Procurement and inventory
  - Update the storeroom inventory and procurement system entries for all P1-L1 lubricant stock that can service EQ-P1-L1-CN02 to include CFW-LUB-508 (part number). Place a reorder flag on existing stock of CFW-LUB-508 to maintain continuity of supply.
  - Remove unapproved lubricant containers from the immediate maintenance staging area for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and quarantine them with labeling indicating "Not for EQ-P1-L1-CN02" until disposition per MM-P1-L1-CN02.
- Labeling and storage
  - Label the lubricant cabinet and spares bin that support EQ-P1-L1-CN02 with the approved part number CFW-LUB-508 (part number). Include date received and batch/lot information on each container at time of receipt to support traceability.
- Maintenance procedure updates
  - Modify the lubrication line items in MM-P1-L1-CN02 to list CFW-LUB-508 (part number) as the required consumable for any lubrication tasks on EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Retain existing task intervals and task descriptions as documented in MM-P1-L1-CN02; only the consumable reference is updated.
  - Amend SOP-P1-L1-02 and SOP-P1-L1-04 sections that instruct operators or technicians to identify or top up lubricant to explicitly require CFW-LUB-508 (part number) for EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Add an instruction to verify part number on the container prior to application.
- Training and communication
  - Conduct a short training brief for maintenance technicians and relevant operators covering the change to CFW-LUB-508 (part number). Training will include: how to verify part number, storage/handling notes, and updates to MM-P1-L1-CN02, SOP-P1-L1-02, and SOP-P1-L1-04 references.
  - Issue a change communication bulletin to affected personnel that references MM-P1-L1-CN02, SOP-P1-L1-02, and SOP-P1-L1-04.
- Field implementation steps (example)
  - Example record entry when applying lubricant: record asset EQ-P1-L1-CN02, task per MM-P1-L1-CN02, lubricant applied CFW-LUB-508 (part number), container lot/batch, date, technician initials, and reason code if application deviates from scheduled maintenance. Use the existing maintenance log format; add a single line field for "Lubricant PN" where CFW-LUB-508 (part number) is entered.
  - Example storeroom action: upon receipt of new shipment, label each container with "CFW-LUB-508" and enter lot/batch in the storeroom ledger. Reconcile existing inventory against newly updated procurement entries.
- Timing and cutover
  - Implementation will occur during the next scheduled maintenance window for EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Until cutover, do not change current maintenance intervals or tasks in MM-P1-L1-CN02; only transition consumables to CFW-LUB-508 (part number) when new stock is available.

Records to keep
- Update and retain records in accordance with MM-P1-L1-CN02 retention requirements. Minimum records to capture for each lubrication event on EQ-P1-L1-CN02:
  - Equipment identifier: EQ-P1-L1-CN02.
  - Lubricant part number: CFW-LUB-508 (part number).
  - Container lot/batch and receiving date.
  - Technician name/initials and date of application.
  - Reference to maintenance task as per MM-P1-L1-CN02.
- Maintain procurement and receipt records for CFW-LUB-508 (part number) in the storeroom system for audit and quality traceability.
- Retain change training attendance records and the issuance log for the communication bulletin referencing SOP-P1-L1-02 and SOP-P1-L1-04.

Approvals
- The following approvals are required to enact this ECN:
  - Maintenance Manager (approval to update MM-P1-L1-CN02 and storeroom entries).
  - Production Supervisor (approval for operator-facing SOP updates SOP-P1-L1-02 and SOP-P1-L1-04).
  - Quality Assurance (approval to accept CFW-LUB-508 (part number) as the controlled consumable and to update audit checklists).
- Documentation updates to MM-P1-L1-CN02, SOP-P1-L1-02, and SOP-P1-L1-04 must be completed and recorded prior to the full cutover to CFW-LUB-508 (part number). Signatures and dates for each approval shall be recorded on the ECN approval page and attached to the ECN record in the document control system.

Related documents
- MM-P1-L1-CN02
- SOP-P1-L1-02
- SOP-P1-L1-04

End of ECN-2026-003 Rev E.
