# ECN-2026-004 Change notice - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Reason for change
- Background: Routine maintenance reviews and field observations identified inconsistent performance of the media containment seals and accelerated wear of rotating elements in Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02). An evaluation of current lubricants and service records showed the installed lubricant specification did not match the vendor recommendation for this cabinet's bearing assemblies and rotary feed mechanisms as referenced in maintenance history and operator logs.
- Purpose: This change aligns the lubrication specification for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 with the verified part approved for Hot Forge shot blast service to improve reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, and standardize spare stocking for P3, line P3-L1.
- Scope: The change updates the lubricant part number used on EQ-P3-L1-SB02 only. Related procedural adjustments to lubrication verification steps are provided for operator and maintenance teams and will be incorporated into the cited operating procedures.

Affected items
- Equipment impacted: EQ-P3-L1-SB02 (Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2).
- Parts affected: The lubricant part number currently referenced in local records and maintenance checklists for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 will be replaced by the approved lubricant part number CFW-LUB-278.
- Documents to be updated: SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05 will be revised to reflect the new lubricant specification and the required verification step for incoming lubricant labeling. Maintenance checklist entry and spare parts lists associated with EQ-P3-L1-SB02 will be revised to show CFW-LUB-278. Cite related engineering specification SB-1033 for baseline equipment requirements when confirming compatibility.
- Inventory: Existing stocks currently staged for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 must be quarantined and dispositioned per parts control until they are either reused on other compatible assets or returned to suppliers. Replacement stock orders should reference CFW-LUB-278.

Implementation
- Rationale and approach: Selection of CFW-LUB-278 follows supplier compatibility verification and in-house compatibility testing against media and seal materials used in EQ-P3-L1-SB02. The objective is to ensure lubricant chemistry reduces wear on bearing surfaces and minimizes contaminant interaction with shot media and containment seals.
- Stepwise implementation:
  - Update documentation: Revise SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05 to include CFW-LUB-278 as the approved lubricant for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and add a verification checkpoint for lubricant lot and label at the point of use. Update SB-1033 references where lubricant compatibility is discussed.
  - Field change: Apply CFW-LUB-278 to lubrication points on EQ-P3-L1-SB02 during the next scheduled maintenance opportunity. Technicians will follow the procedural steps in the revised SOPs for application and verification.
  - Training: Conduct a targeted briefing for P3, line P3-L1 maintenance and operations personnel covering the change, focusing on correct lubricant identification, application location, and contingency steps if unlabeled or suspect lubricant is encountered.
  - Verification: After the first application of CFW-LUB-278, technicians will complete a verification checklist and photographic record of labeled lubricant containers and application points. These verification records will be retained per records requirements below.
- Examples of application context: When servicing the rotary feeder bearings and media conveyor drive bearings on EQ-P3-L1-SB02, technicians will withdraw the labeled container of CFW-LUB-278 and perform the lubrication step specified in SOP-P3-L1-02. If an unlabeled container or a container not marked CFW-LUB-278 is found in the immediate work area, the technician will stop work and notify the maintenance lead for disposition per parts control.
- Contingencies: If an incompatibility is suspected following application, operations will use containment procedures from SB-1033 to isolate the cabinet and initiate joint maintenance–engineering review. Any field findings will be captured in the change record and used to adjust SOP notes as needed.

Records to keep
- Maintain an ECN implementation log that records revision markers and the personnel performing the updated lubrication application on EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Include photographs of lubricant labels showing CFW-LUB-278 at point of use.
- Retain completed verification checklists from SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05 that demonstrate correct lubricant identification and application for each service event post-implementation.
- Log any product returns or quarantine actions for previously stocked lubricant and record final disposition in the spare parts system.
- Archive all related test reports and compatibility assessments referenced during selection of CFW-LUB-278 alongside SB-1033 in the engineering document repository.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Required to authorize revision of SB-1033 references and confirm compatibility rationale.
- Maintenance approval: Required to authorize field application and update SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-05 maintenance steps.
- Operations approval: Required to confirm operator training and update operator checks within SOP-P3-L1-05.
- Approval actions will be documented on the ECN approval log and retained with the ECN record. Sign-off indicates acceptance of CFW-LUB-278 as the approved lubricant for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and acknowledgment of the required updates to SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-05, and references to SB-1033.

# ECN-2026-005 Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

## Reason for change

Background: An operational review and reliability analysis of the machining induction billet heater EQ-P1-L3-IH01 identified recurring thermal imbalance events correlated with cooling water flow fluctuations. Inspection findings and vendor consultation concluded that the existing documented minimum coil cooling water flow did not reflect observed required flow rates to maintain safe coil temperatures under typical machining duty cycles. The change updates the documented minimum coil cooling water flow for the coil circuit to the value required to restore acceptable thermal margins and reduce unscheduled thermal trips and associated production disruptions.

Rationale: The change establishes a clarified minimum coil cooling water flow value to align maintenance, commissioning, and process control activities. Specifying the minimum flow in the equipment documentation removes interpretive variability between operations and maintenance teams, supports consistent alarm setpoints in the local control system, and provides a single source of truth for post-modification validation and future audits. This will reduce risk of coil overheating, early insulation degradation, and unplanned downtime.

Related documents: ECN-2026-046, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05

## Affected items

Scope: This change applies to EQ-P1-L3-IH01 and to records and procedures that reference coil cooling water flow for that equipment. Affected items include the equipment specification sheets, the local control logic documentation, the preventive maintenance checklist referenced in SOP-P1-L3-05, and the spare parts verification procedure referenced in SB-1026. Technical drawings and tag lists that include coil cooling water requirements must be revised to reflect the updated minimum flow.

Items to be revised:
- Equipment documentation and nameplate data for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Maintenance work orders and checklists that cite coil cooling water minimums.
- Control system alarm and interlock setpoints that enforce coil cooling flow.
- Operator procedure steps in SOP-P1-L3-05 that refer to acceptable cooling conditions.

Examples of impacted activities:
- Commissioning and start-up verification where acceptance criteria rely on coil cooling flow.
- Shift handover checks that require operators to confirm cooling water adequacy.
- Troubleshooting guides used by maintenance that specify corrective actions for low flow conditions.

Records to keep:
- Updated equipment specification sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 with the revised minimum flow incorporated.
- Revised activity sheets and checklists from SOP-P1-L3-05 showing the updated acceptance criteria.
- As-built control logic printouts showing alarm and interlock settings changed to reflect the new minimum.
- Field verification records and test logs demonstrating compliance during implementation.
- Affected work order change logs and maintenance history entries linked to ECN-2026-005.

Mandatory note: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min.

## Implementation

Change actions:
- Revise the equipment specification sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to include the updated minimum coil cooling water flow. Ensure the mandatory note above appears verbatim in the specification and nameplate references.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-05 to reflect the new acceptance criteria and any operator checks that reference coil cooling water. Replace or annotate affected pages and ensure effective distribution to operations staff.
- Update control system documentation and implement the revised alarm and interlock setpoints in the control logic. Ensure the logic changes are reviewed and signed off per control change procedures.
- Modify maintenance checklists and preventive maintenance instructions to include flow verification against the specified minimum. Cross-reference SB-1026 where procedures require confirmation of flow-related spare parts or diagnostic steps.
- Conduct field verification testing after changes are applied. Document flow measurements and demonstrate that system performance is within acceptable ranges when coil cooling flow meets or exceeds the specified minimum. Record results in the equipment test log.
- Provide targeted training for operations and maintenance personnel that covers the reason for the change, the new documented minimum, how to verify flow, and steps to take if flow is below the specified value. Update training records to reference ECN-2026-005.

Implementation sequence:
- Issue revised documentation and circulate to affected groups referenced in SOP-P1-L3-05 and SB-1026.
- Schedule control logic change and maintenance checklist update during a planned access window to avoid unplanned production impact.

# ECN-2026-006 Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change

Background: During routine thermal performance trending and maintenance inspections it was observed that coil surface temperatures and dielectric insulation condition on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 were degrading at a rate higher than expected. Review of historical maintenance records and comparison to similar assets indicated that periods of marginal cooling water flow correlated with accelerated coil wear and reduced heater efficiency. A recent engineering assessment recommended establishing a formal minimum coil cooling water flow requirement to reduce thermal stress, mitigate premature coil failure, and stabilize process performance.

Change rationale: Establishing a documented minimum coil cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 reduces risk of coil overheating, insulation breakdown, and unplanned downtime. The minimum flow requirement provides a clear threshold for operational monitoring, maintenance acceptance criteria, and SOP alignment. This ECN implements that threshold and updates affected procedures and records to ensure consistent compliance and traceability. This change aligns with findings and actions described in related review ECN-2026-027 and requires updates to SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 to reflect new acceptance criteria and monitoring steps.

Affected items

Primary asset: EQ-P3-L1-IH03 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #3) — coil assembly, cooling water inlet and return piping, flow monitoring points, and associated instrumentation used to verify cooling performance.

Procedures: SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 require revision to incorporate the new minimum coil cooling water flow threshold, criteria for action when flow is below threshold, verification steps for corrective actions, and recordkeeping requirements.

Documentation and records: Operational logs, preventive maintenance checklists, calibration records for flow-measuring instruments, and incident reports where coil cooling was implicated in degraded performance shall reference this ECN and include the measured flow values against the established threshold.

Suppliers and spare parts: Any orders or acceptance criteria for coil assemblies or flow control devices used on EQ-P3-L1-IH03 shall include reference to this ECN and the minimum flow requirement to ensure compatibility and verification at installation.

Implementation

Specification: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This value shall be used as the operational acceptance threshold for normal production and for return-to-service after maintenance.

Operational verification: Operators shall verify coil cooling water flow at the designated measurement point for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 during startup, shift checks, and after any cooling system intervention. If measured flow is below the specified minimum, the heater shall be taken to a safe state as defined in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 and maintenance shall be notified.

Maintenance actions: Maintenance shall inspect inlet strainers, valves, piping, heat exchangers, and flow-sensing instrumentation when flow is found to be below the specified minimum. Corrective actions include cleaning, valve adjustment to remove unintended throttling, repair of leaking joints, and verification of pump performance per existing maintenance practice. After corrective action, the flow measurement shall be repeated and recorded prior to returning EQ-P3-L1-IH03 to service.

Instrumentation and calibration: Existing flow-measuring devices used to verify coil cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be within their calibration cycle and proven accurate for the range around the established minimum. If existing instrumentation cannot reliably resolve the specified minimum, replacement or supplemental verification methods shall be implemented. Calibration records shall be attached to the maintenance record for the action.

Procedure updates: Revise SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 to include:
- The specified coil cooling water flow minimum.
- Stepwise actions for operators and maintenance when flow is below the threshold.
- Forms and log entries required to document flow measurements, corrective actions, and approval to return to service.
- Roles and responsibilities for confirming the flow meets the minimum after corrective work.

Examples of application: If an operator observes reduced heating efficiency on EQ-P3-L1-IH03, the operator follows SOP-P3-L1-01 to measure coil cooling water flow. If the recorded flow is below the specified minimum, the operator initiates the response sequence in SOP-P3-L1-03, places the heater in a safe state, and notifies maintenance. Maintenance records the observed flow, corrective steps taken, calibration status of the measuring device, and final measured flow upon restoration. These entries are retained in the maintenance log and referenced for trending.

Records to keep

- Operational flow check entries for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 with the measured value and the action taken when below the specified minimum.  
- Preventive maintenance reports documenting inspections related to coil cooling and any corrective interventions performed.  
- Calibration certificates or verification records for flow-measuring devices used for compliance checks.  
- ECN trace file linking maintenance and operations records to this ECN and to related ECN-2026-027.  
- Revised procedure versions for SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03 with visible change markers and an index entry referencing this ECN.

Approvals

Engineering: review and acceptance of the technical basis for the specified minimum flow and verification that implementation steps are consistent with safe operation and design margins.

Maintenance: acceptance of revised maintenance actions, confirmation of capability to verify and restore coil cooling flow to the specified minimum, and commitment to update maintenance checklists and records.

Operations: acknowledgement of procedural updates, training plan to ensure operators can measure and respond to low flow conditions per SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-03, and confirmation of incorporation into shift handover practices.

Quality and Plant Management: final approval for change implementation at P3, line P3-L1, and confirmation that records will be maintained in the document control system and referenced in future audits. All approvals shall be recorded in the ECN approval form and retained with the ECN file.

Related documents

- ECN-2026-027  
- SOP-P3-L1-01  
- SOP-P3-L1-03

End of document.

# ECN-2026-007 - Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

## Reason for change
This engineering change updates the specified main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) and aligns maintenance practice and records with inspection findings and supplier recommendations. During a recent inspection and teardown referenced in maintenance records, evidence of bolt relaxation and uneven clamping of the main ram assembly was identified. The change is intended to restore and maintain clamp load uniformity, reduce fretting and wear at the ram-to-housing interface, and mitigate risk of ram misalignment that can lead to premature component failure or safety hazards.

Root-cause analysis found that prior torque practice and documentation were inconsistent with the fastener specification and the press manufacturer’s guidelines. This ECN consolidates the torque requirement into the controlled documentation set and updates work instructions and maintenance checks to ensure reproducible application of the specified clamp load.

The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.

Related documents: MM-P1-L4-HP02, SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-05

## Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2).  
- Maintenance procedures: SOP-P1-L4-05 (work instruction updates required to reflect new torque value).  
- Maintenance history and asset records: MM-P1-L4-HP02 (to be updated to capture torque application and verification entries).  
- Service bulletin: SB-1034 (incorporate applicable inspection findings and recommendations into routine checks).

Affected components and records to be revised:
- Main ram bolt torque specification in the EQ-P1-L4-HP02 equipment file. Include torque application method and verification acceptance criteria.
- SOP-P1-L4-05: revise step sequence for main ram removal/installation to require torque verification and a specified verification record.
- MM-P1-L4-HP02: create a maintenance log entry template for torque application and verification sign-off.
- Training records for technicians performing ram bolt torque application: update to include competency check against the revised SOP.

Note: This ECN does not change hydraulic pressures, operational setpoints, or component part numbers. See SB-1034 for historical inspection detail and MM-P1-L4-HP02 for original maintenance context.

## Implementation
Summary: Apply the specified torque value to the main ram bolt on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and revise controlled documents and records to ensure repeatable application and traceability.

Implementation steps (high level):
- Document update: Revise SOP-P1-L4-05 to include the torque value and associated verification steps. Add a required signature block and reference to MM-P1-L4-HP02 for record retention. Cross-reference SB-1034 for inspection checkpoints.
- Tooling and method: Use a calibrated torque tool appropriate for the required torque range and fastening geometry. Calibrate torque tools according to the calibration schedule documented in MM-P1-L4-HP02. Record serial numbers of tools used in maintenance logs.
- Procedure for torque application:
  - Prepare the main ram assembly per SOP-P1-L4-05 revision. Clean mating surfaces and threads, inspect fastener condition, and replace any fasteners showing damage. Apply torque following the sequence specified in SOP-P1-L4-05.
  - Apply the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.
  - Verify applied torque using independent verification method (secondary torque tool or torque verification witness). Document verification in MM-P1-L4-HP02 maintenance entry.
- Records to keep:
  - Completed SOP-P1-L4-05 checklist with technician and supervisor signatures.
  - MM-P1-L4-HP02 maintenance entry with torque value, tool identifier, verifier signature, and any observations.
  - Calibration certificate reference for the torque tool used (attach or reference in MM-P1-L4-HP02).
  - Any deviation reports and follow-up corrective actions if achieved torque differs from the specified value.
- Training:
  - All technicians performing main ram work on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 must complete the updated SOP-P1-L4-05 training and demonstrate competency. Document training completion in personnel records and in MM-P1-L4-HP02.
- Example entries (for illustrative style; exact form to be placed into MM-P1-L4-HP02):
  - Tool ID: [tool serial]; Applied torque: 970 N·m; Verifier: [name]; Notes: [inspection observations]
  - Calibration certificate: [ref]; SOP revision used: SOP-P1-L4-05 Rev B; Maintenance record link: MM-P1-L4-HP02

Quality control and verification:
- After torque application, perform a follow-up inspection per SB-1034 checkpoints to confirm ram alignment and absence of fretting or movement under static load.
- Maintain records in MM-P1-L4-HP02 and make them available for engineering review and audits.

## Approvals
- Engineering approval: Required to accept the change into the equipment file. Engineering will review revisions to SOP-P1-L4-05 and MM-P1-L4-HP02 entries for conformance.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance management to confirm readiness of personnel, calibration status of torque tools, and ability to implement the revised procedure on EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
- Safety review: Safety representative to confirm the implementation method does not introduce new hazards and that required lockout/tagout and guarding practices are followed during the procedure.

Approval signatures shall be recorded on the ECN form and attached to the SOP-P1-L4-05 revision package. Retain completed ECN, updated SOP-P1-L4-05, updated MM-P1-L4-HP02 entries, and any referenced SB-1034 inspection notes in the document control system archive.

Related documents: MM-P1-L4-HP02, SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-05

Notes:
- Implement this change only on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 as specified in this ECN. If similar upgrades are proposed for other presses, initiate separate ECN actions referencing the approach and lessons learned from this implementation.
- Maintain traceability between ECN-2026-007 Rev B, the revised SOP, and the maintenance records for future audits and failure investigations.

# ECN-2026-008 - Change notice - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line: P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: During a recent preventive maintenance review and spindle rebuild on Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03), maintenance personnel discovered inconsistent clamp preload on the chuck jaws after routine reassembly. The root cause analysis identified that the previous standard referenced an incorrect torque value for the chuck jaw bolts in the equipment-specific maintenance checklist. The incorrect torque resulted in uneven jaw seating, intermittent concentricity loss on turned parts, and increased wear on the collet and jaw interface. To mitigate the risk of part nonconformance, reduced tool life, and potential safety hazards from loose hardware, the chuck jaw bolt torque specification is being corrected.

Change summary: Update the specified chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to the correct value: 95 N·m. This ECN updates applicable maintenance procedures, inspection checkpoints, and training material references to reflect the corrected torque value and adds a verification step in the reassembly sign-off process.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03 (Machining CNC turning center #3) — torque specification for chuck jaw bolts.  
- Documentation: Maintenance checklist and work instructions that reference chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03. Refer to SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-03 for linked procedures and baseline records.  
- Spare parts handling: Any spare chuck jaw bolt replacements used during maintenance must be torqued to 95 N·m when installed on EQ-P1-L3-CN03.  
- Quality inspections: In-process first-article checks and in-shift chuck verification routines that sample turned parts from EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: Applies to all maintenance and assembly activities on EQ-P1-L3-CN03 at plant P1, line P1-L3. The new torque specification replaces the previous value in all equipment-specific documentation and in maintenance task instructions.

Actions:
- Documentation update: Revise the maintenance checklist and torque table entries within SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 to state the chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 as 95 N·m. Add a cross-reference note to SB-1014 for spindle rebuild best practices.
- Tooling: Ensure calibrated torque wrenches used for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 are capable of and set to 95 N·m when performing chuck jaw bolt installation. Record calibration status in the tool log for the wrench used.
- Rework and verification: For any unit of EQ-P1-L3-CN03 that has undergone chuck or jaw replacement since the previous specification, perform a re-torque and verification to 95 N·m at the next available maintenance opportunity. Log the re-torque action per the record procedure below.
- Training: Conduct a focused operator and maintenance briefing covering the revised torque requirement and the rationale. Include a hands-on session during which personnel practice the re-torque and verification steps using the documented checklist.
- Sign-off procedure: Add a mandatory sign-off line to the maintenance work order that records: technician name, torque applied (95 N·m), torque tool identifier, and witness inspector initials. The witness inspector must be a qualified maintenance lead or quality engineer.
- Inspection sampling: Increase first-piece inspection attention after reassembly. Typical checks include concentricity and runout assessments as defined in SB-1014 and related SOPs. If out-of-spec conditions are found, retain the assembly and follow nonconformance procedures.

Step rationale and examples:
- Rationale: Achieving uniform preload on all chuck jaw bolts ensures even jaw seating and consistent clamping force. This reduces part runout and vibration, preserves jaw and spindle interfaces, and minimizes risk of bolt loosening. A comparative example: an assembly torqued uniformly to the specified value produced repeatable concentricity across multiple part families, whereas assemblies with variable torque showed intermittent high runout on semi-critical diameters.
- Example work step: After cleaning mating surfaces and applying thread lock where specified in SB-1014, hand-start all chuck jaw bolts, then tighten in the manufacturer-recommended sequence to bring them up evenly. Final torque each bolt to 95 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench while a witness observes and signs the work order.

Records to keep
---------------
Maintain the following records in the equipment maintenance folder and the electronic document control system:
- Updated copies of SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 with the 95 N·m entry.  
- Maintenance work orders showing re-torque actions to 95 N·m, including technician and witness signatures and torque tool identifier.  
- Torque wrench calibration certificate for the tool used, retained per calibration schedule and linked to the work order.  
- Post-reassembly inspection reports and first-article inspection records referencing SB-1014 where applicable.  
- Training attendance and competency sign-off records for personnel who performed or supervised the re-torque work.

Approvals
---------
The following approvals are required to close this ECN and implement the change in production:
- Maintenance Manager approval for revision of SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 to include the 95 N·m value.  
- Quality Manager approval for updated inspection checkpoints and first-article criteria referencing SB-1014.  
- Operations Manager acknowledgement of the updated sign-off and training requirements for EQ-P1-L3-CN03.

Post-implementation review
--------------------------
After implementation, conduct a focused review to confirm effectiveness: review maintenance logs and inspection results for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 for at least one production cycle following the change, verify that all re-torque records to 95 N·m are complete, and ensure no related part nonconformances are reported. If issues persist, escalate per SB-1014 and update SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 as required.

Related documents
-----------------
SB-1014  
SOP-P1-L3-02  
SOP-P1-L3-03

Prepared by: Maintenance Engineering  
Distribution: Plant P1 maintenance, quality, and operations records systems

# ECN-2026-009 - Change notice - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: During routine maintenance and a targeted reliability review of the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01), maintenance staff identified inconsistent clamp behavior on the mandrel assembly. Investigation cross-referenced the maintenance manual MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 and operational procedure SOP-P1-L2-03. The investigation determined that a clarification and formal change to the mandrel clamp fastener requirement is necessary to ensure consistent clamp preload, reduce cycle variation, and prevent premature wear of the mandrel clamp components.

Change rationale: The change standardizes the fastening requirement for the mandrel clamp bolt on EQ-P1-L2-RR01 to eliminate ambiguity that led to variable manual torqueing practices. Standardization reduces maintenance error, improves repeatability of radial positioning, and aligns field practice with the design intent captured during commissioning. This ECN updates the documented torque requirement and prescribes implementation and verification steps for maintenance and operations personnel.

Affected items
--------------
- Technical documentation: Update MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 to incorporate the standardized mandrel clamp bolt torque specification and to add the verification checklist reference.  
- Operating procedure: Update SOP-P1-L2-03 to reflect the mandated verification step after clamp torqueing and to include the acceptance criteria language that references inspection records.  
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01 mandrel clamp bolt fastening practice; maintenance and inspection regimes for the mandrel clamp assembly.  
- Spare parts handling: Include inspection and re-torque verification when installing replacement mandrel clamp bolts or housing components, and document in parts installation records.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: This change applies to all maintenance actions affecting the mandrel clamp of EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and to any operation that requires removal and reinstallation of the mandrel or its clamp bolt. It is effective immediately upon approval.

Mandatory specification: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m. This value is to be used for all reassembly and verification activities for the mandrel clamp bolt on EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

Work steps:
- Before applying torque, consult MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 for bolt condition acceptance criteria and replacement guidance.  
- Use a calibrated torque tool capable of achieving the required value and record the tool serial number on the maintenance record. Calibration traceability must be recorded per the existing calibration program referenced in MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.  
- Apply torque to the mandrel clamp bolt to the specified value of 395 N·m. Follow the tightening sequence and technique documented in MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.  
- After torque application, perform the verification checks required by SOP-P1-L2-03, including functional clamp engagement and a run-in check under the conditions described in SOP-P1-L2-03. Record observations and any deviations.  
- If replacement of the clamp bolt or related clamp components occurred, attach the part change note to the maintenance record and reference MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 for installation acceptance criteria.

Examples and expected outcomes:
- Example A: During a scheduled bearing housing replacement on EQ-P1-L2-RR01, the mandrel clamp bolt was removed. Reassembly followed the procedure above and the bolt was torqued to 395 N·m. Post-assembly verification per SOP-P1-L2-03 showed no axial movement and acceptable concentricity without additional adjustment. Record indicated no unusual vibration during initial production cycles.  
- Example B: A field incident where the bolt had been torqued using an uncalibrated tool resulted in a loose clamp. After rework and application of 395 N·m with a calibrated tool, clamp performance returned to expected parameters. The maintenance record documented the torque value, tool ID, and post-torque verification results.

Records to keep
----------------
- Maintenance action record: Include equipment tag EQ-P1-L2-RR01, description of action, technician name, tool serial number, applied torque value 395 N·m, and verification outcome. Attach any photograph evidence of torque tool reading and clamp assembly orientation.  
- Calibration record: Maintain calibration certificate for the torque tool used; reference in the maintenance action record.  
- Inspection checklist: Update and retain the checklist per SOP-P1-L2-03 and file with the work order history for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.  
- Change trace: Record ECN-2026-009 in the equipment history log and note linkage to ECN-2026-041 where applicable.  
All records must be filed in the document control system under the equipment history for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and be retrievable for audits aligned to MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.

Training and communication
--------------------------
- Briefing: Conduct a targeted briefing for maintenance and operations teams covering the new mandatory torque requirement and updated verification steps. Reference MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 for technical details and SOP-P1-L2-03 for operational checks.  
- Competency: Only personnel trained on the updated procedure and authorized to use calibrated torque tools shall perform the torque application and verification.

Approvals
---------
- The change requires documented approval from the plant maintenance manager and the operations manager for P1, line P1-L2. Signatures and dates shall be recorded on the ECN approval page and stored with the ECN file.  
- Post-implementation review will reference ECN-2026-041 for related system changes and to confirm that the updates in MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 and SOP-P1-L2-03 have been completed and published.  
- A one-time verification audit will be scheduled following implementation to confirm records and to validate that the mandated torque value of 395 N·m has been consistently applied and recorded.

Related documents
-----------------
ECN-2026-041  
MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1  
SOP-P1-L2-03

# ECN-2026-010 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: During routine inspections and operational trend review for EQ-P3-L1-IH03, cooling system performance was identified as a recurring contributor to heater trips and premature coil wear. Field verification and hydraulic assessment indicated the coil cooling water flow threshold used in operational checks and interlock settings was below the level required to maintain stable coil temperature and to prevent accelerated insulation degradation. This change clarifies the minimum flow requirement that must be enforced in controls, SOPs, and maintenance checks.
- Rationale: Standardizing a documented minimum coil cooling water flow consolidates corrective actions already implemented in the field and eliminates ambiguity between operators, maintenance, and controls engineering. A clear minimum reduces variation in start-up and run procedures, decreases risk of thermal stress to the coil assembly, and supports longer coil life and more reliable production availability. This change is consistent with corrective recommendations referenced in ECN-2026-006 and aligns with normal operating expectations captured in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P3-L1-IH03 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #3). All physical coils, their flow measurement and control subsystems, flow interlock logic, operator displays, and maintenance documentation for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 are within scope.
- Procedures affected: SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 require update to reference the clarified coil cooling water flow minimum and to align step wording and interlock verification steps with the new requirement.
- Control and instrumentation: Flow transmitter scaling, alarm thresholds, and interlock setpoints for coil cooling on EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be updated to reflect the minimum flow requirement. Operator HMI text and alarm descriptions must be revised where they reference coil flow limits.
- Training and records: Operator and maintenance training materials specific to EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must be amended. Change training attendance and competency records must be retained in the maintenance document control folder for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

Implementation
- New minimum flow requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This value will be used as the definitive minimum for control interlocks, alarm thresholds, operator checklists, and maintenance acceptance criteria for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Control updates: Controls engineering will update flow transmitter scaling and interlock setpoints on the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 control system to reference 65 L/min. Alarm text will state the minimum explicitly and reference this ECN where interlock logic or manual override justification is required.
- Procedure updates: SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 will be revised to incorporate the coil cooling water flow minimum. The relevant procedure sections will be rephrased to instruct operators to verify that flow meets or exceeds the documented minimum before heater energization and to document flow readings in the shift log. Procedure update shall include guidance for actions when flow is below the minimum, consistent with safe shutdown and notification steps.
- Maintenance actions: Maintenance inspection checklists for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 will add a dedicated step to confirm measured flow against 65 L/min during post-repair commissioning and periodic verification tasks. Flow metering calibration checks will be scheduled and recorded following any instrumentation work.
- Training: A targeted briefing will be delivered to operations and maintenance teams responsible for EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Briefing will cover the reason for the change, how to interpret the flow reading, control behavior when flow is below the minimum, and documentation expectations. Attendance will be recorded and training materials attached to the equipment file.
- Examples and expected behavior: Example scenarios will be provided in the procedure updates. Example text will show an operator verifying coil cooling water flow on the local HMI and documenting the reading in the shift log prior to heater energization. Another example will describe steps to take when flow drops below the minimum during operation, including safe ramp down and notification of maintenance and engineering.
- Records to keep: The following records will be created and retained in the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 document folder: control change log documenting setpoint updates referencing this ECN, updated versions of SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02, flow verification checklist entries demonstrating compliance with 65 L/min during commissioning or after repairs, training attendance records for affected personnel, and a brief incident log for any events where flow fell below the minimum after implementation.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Responsible process and controls engineers will sign to confirm control updates and procedural wording are complete and that the change achieves the intended operational objective for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Operations approval: Operations management will confirm procedural updates and training satisfy operational readiness for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and that operator materials are aligned with plant practice.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance leadership will confirm additions to maintenance checklists and recordkeeping practices for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Document references: Implementers must consult ECN-2026-006 for preceding corrective details and follow procedural change control steps in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-02 when updating and releasing revised procedures.

Change control note
- This ECN establishes the authoritative minimum coil cooling water flow for EQ-P3-L1-IH03. All stakeholders must reference this ECN when performing work, updating documentation, or assessing operational events related to coil cooling on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3.

# ECN-2026-011 Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: Recent inspection and trending of heater performance identified repeated low coil cooling water flow events that correlate with control trips and degraded billet heating uniformity on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03). The investigation determined that the effective minimum flow required to prevent coil overheating and to maintain stable power coupling is higher than the conservative operational threshold currently documented in maintenance checklists.
- Safety and quality rationale: Maintaining sufficient coil cooling water flow prevents premature insulation degradation, reduces electrical arcing risk, and supports stable process control that affects billet microstructure consistency. The change aligns minimum flow requirements with observed operational limits to reduce unplanned downtime and nonconforming forged parts.
- Regulatory and procedural alignment: This ECN implements the engineering change mandated by the equipment reliability review and ensures related maintenance and operational procedures are updated in accordance with MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 and QS-PROC-01. A service bulletin is issued for immediate field awareness (see SB-1009).

Affected items
- Equipment: Induction billet heater identified as EQ-P1-L1-IH03 (Hot Forge induction billet heater #3).
- Documentation: Maintenance procedures and operator checklists in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3; process control and nonconformance handling in QS-PROC-01; plant service bulletin SB-1009.
- Controls and alarms: Pump interlock and flow indication logic related to coil cooling water for EQ-P1-L1-IH03. Control system setpoints and alarm thresholds shall be reviewed and adjusted to reflect the new minimum flow requirement.
- Records and logs: Flow verification records, maintenance intervention reports, and corrective action records will be updated and maintained as described in the Implementation section.

Implementation
- Change description: Establish the coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 as 72 L/min and update all relevant control setpoints, operator instructions, and maintenance documentation to reference this value exactly as written.
- Procedure updates: Revise MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 to include:
  - A mandatory flow verification step at shift handover and after pump maintenance that records measured flow versus the specified minimum of 72 L/min.
  - A procedural pause and escalation path if measured flow is below 72 L/min, including immediate notification of maintenance and process engineering and placement of the heater into a safe state per QS-PROC-01.
- Control system changes: Update the programmable logic controller and human-machine interface alarm thresholds so that low-flow alarm annunciates when measured flow falls below 72 L/min. Alarm response text must direct operators to follow the updated steps in MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Physical work: Inspect the cooling circuit hardware, clean strainers, and verify pump performance where indicated by troubleshooting. If corrective hardware work is required, document findings and actions in maintenance records and reference SB-1009 for guidance on interim operating limits and field advisories.
- Training and communication: Conduct targeted training sessions for operators and maintenance technicians covering the new minimum flow requirement of 72 L/min, revised control behavior, and the procedural steps from MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3. Maintain attendance records and competency confirmation as required by QS-PROC-01.
- Examples of application: 
  - Example scenario A: During a routine shift check, the operator measures coil cooling water flow below the required minimum. The operator places EQ-P1-L1-IH03 in standby per MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3, records the measured value, notifies maintenance and process engineering, and follows SB-1009 for interim safety measures until flow is restored to at least 72 L/min.
  - Example scenario B: Post-pump maintenance, the technician performs a verification run and documents a measured flow meeting or exceeding the minimum. The technician completes the post-maintenance checklist and signs off in the maintenance log as prescribed by MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3.
- Verification and acceptance: After changes are implemented, perform a validation run to demonstrate stable heater operation with recorded coil cooling water flow at or above 72 L/min and normal power coupling behavior. Document results in the equipment validation record and attach to the ECN closure package.

Records to keep
- Updated MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3 with revision history noting this ECN.
- Control system change request and implementation log showing updated alarm thresholds tied to the 72 L/min minimum.
- Training attendance roster and competency confirmations as required by QS-PROC-01.
- Post-change validation report and trend data demonstrating heater stability at or above 72 L/min.
- Maintenance logs and any corrective action reports generated as a result of low-flow events, with reference to SB-1009 when interim measures were applied.

Approvals
- Engineering review: Approval required to implement control logic and documentation changes.
- Maintenance authorization: Approval required for any hardware interventions and for release of the equipment to operations following repairs.
- Operations acceptance: Sign-off required confirming operator training completion and adherence to revised procedures.
- Quality oversight: Quality assurance verification that changes comply with QS-PROC-01 and that records meet system retention requirements.

References
- MM-P1-L1-IH03-S3
- QS-PROC-01
- SB-1009

Document control
- ECN identifier: ECN-2026-011 Rev B
- Affected equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03
- Plant location: P1, line P1-L1

End of change notice.

# ECN-2026-012 - Change notice - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Production and quality reviews identified drift in billet surface condition and inconsistent ring geometry downstream of the ring rolling cell fed by EQ-P2-L2-IH01. Investigation traced the primary causal vector to uncontrolled variation in billet core temperature at transfer into the ring rolling mandrel zone. Measured variability correlated with process nonconformances recorded against QS-PROC-07 and with operator entries in SOP-P2-L2-04. The engineering change narrows acceptable billet thermal condition to reduce metallurgical variability and improve first-pass yield.

Change summary: The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. This ECN formalizes heater operating setpoint verification, introduces procedural updates to SOP-P2-L2-04 for transfer gating, and mandates maintenance actions referenced in MM-P2-L2-IH01 to support stable control of the heater process.

Rationale: Holding the billet at the specified target reduces the frequency of corrective heat work at the mandrel and limits microstructural heterogeneity in wrought sections. The change aligns heater control expectations with metallurgical acceptance criteria captured in QS-PROC-07 and provides a traceable means to demonstrate compliance for customer audits.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: All operating procedures and operator training linked to EQ-P2-L2-IH01.  
- Procedures: SOP-P2-L2-04 will be revised to include explicit verification steps for the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C and to document the acceptance criteria at transfer.  
- Maintenance records: MM-P2-L2-IH01 preventative and corrective work orders will be updated to include heater element and sensor validation tasks that support maintaining the specified target.  
- Quality documentation: QS-PROC-07 will reference this ECN as the source controlling allowable billet thermal input for ring rolling feedstock.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: Apply to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 on line P2-L2 and to all associated written work instructions, calibration records, operator checklists, and maintenance task lists. Implementation will follow the steps below.

Steps:
- Update SOP-P2-L2-04 to include a clear verification routine that confirms the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C prior to transfer from the heater to the ring rolling cell. The revision will replace any ambiguous language with a firm acceptance statement and required entries in the operator log.
- Modify MM-P2-L2-IH01 maintenance workflows to incorporate heater control sensor checks and validation steps that ensure the heater can reliably achieve and maintain the specified target. Maintenance closures must include the updated sign-off template.
- Revise QS-PROC-07 cross-references to point to this ECN and to require quality hold and verification steps whenever operator records show deviation from the specified target. Nonconforming product flows shall follow the disposition routes described in QS-PROC-07.
- Train all affected personnel on revised SOP-P2-L2-04 and the implications for feedstock staging and ring rolling acceptance. Training records will be maintained in the document control system and referenced to this ECN.

Examples of application:
- Example entry in the operator log (as required by the revised SOP-P2-L2-04): Record the confirmation that the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C and note any hold actions taken.  
- Example maintenance closure in MM-P2-L2-IH01: Record the sensor verification outcome and reference the heater element service performed to support consistent attainment of the specified target.

Records to keep
---------------
- Operator logs and checklists updated under SOP-P2-L2-04 showing verification that the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C at transfer.  
- Maintenance task completion records and validation checklists under MM-P2-L2-IH01 demonstrating sensor and heater element condition supporting the specified target.  
- Quality control verification records and any disposition documentation created under QS-PROC-07 when billets are found outside the acceptance criteria.  
- Training attendance and competency sign-offs for personnel who operate or maintain EQ-P2-L2-IH01.

Approvals
---------
This change requires concurrence from the following functions before release into controlled documents:
- Plant operations management for line P2-L2 to confirm operational readiness and staffing for the revised verification steps.  
- Maintenance supervision responsible for MM-P2-L2-IH01 to confirm updates to maintenance workflows and tooling.  
- Quality assurance to update QS-PROC-07 references and disposition criteria.  
- Document control to issue the revised SOP-P2-L2-04 and to archive prior revisions.

Post-implementation review
--------------------------
Post-implementation, a targeted review will be conducted to assess the effectiveness of the change. The review will use records listed above to verify adherence and to evaluate any reduction in downstream nonconformances referenced in QS-PROC-07. Findings will be used to refine SOP-P2-L2-04 and maintenance activities in MM-P2-L2-IH01 as needed.

Related documents
-----------------
See: MM-P2-L2-IH01, QS-PROC-07, SOP-P2-L2-04

Distribution
------------
Electronic distribution to plant P2 operations, maintenance, quality, and document control libraries. Hard copy available upon request to the plant document owner.

# ECN-2026-013 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

## Reason for change
Background: Recent preventive maintenance and operational trend analysis for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 identified recurring coil overheating events and intermittent flow alarms that correlate with reduced cooling performance. Root cause analysis determined that coil thermal stress and marginal cooling capacity at low flow conditions increase the risk of coil insulation breakdown and downstream components being exposed to elevated temperatures. Risk assessment concluded that a formal change to the minimum allowable coil cooling water flow specification and associated verification steps is required to maintain safe operation and prolong coil life.

Change objective: Update the minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and implement revised procedural controls, verification, and records to ensure continued compliance and risk mitigation.

Mandatory value update: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min.

Rationale: Establishing a clearly documented minimum flow value reduces false negatives in alarm interpretation, aligns operator actions with actual equipment capability, and informs maintenance acceptance criteria following component replacement or system restoration.

Related documents: MM-P2-L1-IH02, SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-03

## Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is directly affected by the updated minimum coil cooling water flow requirement and related verification steps.
- Procedures: SOP-P2-L1-03 will be revised to include the updated minimum flow value and step-by-step verification requirements for pre-start checks, start-up, and emergency restart after a cooling system intervention.
- Maintenance plan: MM-P2-L1-IH02 will be updated to include acceptance criteria for cooling system servicing, including component handover checklists that reference the updated minimum flow.
- Safety bulletin: SB-1001 will be referenced in operator briefings to highlight the operational risk mitigations and emergency response implications tied to the cooling flow minimum.
- Training: Operations and maintenance training materials and competency checklists will be updated to reflect the value and associated verification actions.

## Implementation
Scope: The change applies to all activities that affect the cooling circuit, coil assembly, flow measurement devices, and control logic related to EQ-P2-L1-IH02 on line P2-L1.

Actions:
- Update SOP-P2-L1-03 to include the mandatory minimum cooling flow value and explicit acceptance criteria for pre-operational checks. The SOP will require operators to verify that measured flow meets or exceeds the specified minimum before generating a billet heat cycle.
- Update MM-P2-L1-IH02 to add post-service verification steps where maintenance personnel confirm that flow instrumentation is calibrated and that measured flow meets the minimum before returning the heater to service.
- Revise control system alarm setpoints and interlocks to align with the minimum flow requirement. Document the rationale for each setpoint change in local control system change records, and reference SB-1001 for temporary bypass procedures and required authorization when alarms inhibit production.
- Implement a verification checklist to be completed and signed by qualified personnel after any cooling system intervention. The checklist will be retained with equipment maintenance records and referenced in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Conduct a focused training session for operations and maintenance on the updated requirement, its implications, and the new verification checklist. Training attendance and assessment results will be recorded and filed with personnel training records.
- Initiate an initial compliance audit after implementation to confirm that SOP, maintenance documentation, control logic, and training updates are in place and that field verification demonstrates the cooling flow meets the specified minimum during representative operating conditions.

Examples of application:
- Pre-start sequence: Operators will consult SOP-P2-L1-03, perform the flow verification, and sign the pre-start checklist before energizing the heater. If measured flow is below the minimum, the operator will follow the escalation path defined in SB-1001.
- Post-maintenance handover: Maintenance will use the updated MM-P2-L1-IH02 acceptance checklist, demonstrate that flow instrumentation is within calibration and that measured flow meets the minimum, and annotate the maintenance record prior to releasing EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to operations.

Records to keep:
- Revised SOP-P2-L1-03 version and change log entry.
- Updated MM-P2-L1-IH02 maintenance procedure and service acceptance checklists.
- Completed verification checklists associated with any cooling system work on EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Training attendance rosters and competency assessments for personnel who received the update.
- Control system change records and alarm setpoint rationales that reference SB-1001 where applicable.
- Initial compliance audit report and any corrective action records generated from the audit.

Retention and storage: All records listed above will be stored in the document control system and equipment maintenance folder for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Records will be referenced during routine audits and when investigating future cooling-related incidents.

## Approvals
Approval matrix: The engineering change requires documented approval by the responsible equipment engineer, maintenance manager, operations manager for line P2-L1, and safety/compliance representative.

Sign-off deliverables:
- Engineering approval of the revised minimum cooling flow value and supporting technical justification.
- Maintenance approval of MM-P2-L1-IH02 updates and acceptance checklist.
- Operations approval of SOP-P2-L1-03 updates and training plan.
- Safety approval referencing SB-1001 for emergency procedures and temporary bypass authorization.

Post-approval actions:
- Release the revised SOP-P2-L1-03 and MM-P2-L1-IH02 documents through the document control system.
- Schedule and complete training for affected personnel.
- Implement control system changes and complete verification checks documented in the records to keep.

Related documents for reference: MM-P2-L1-IH02, SB-1001, SOP-P2-L1-03

Notes: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Compliance with this requirement is mandatory and will be enforced through procedural checks, maintenance acceptance criteria, and control system interlocks.

# ECN-2026-014 Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and audit of Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), inspection records and maintenance rounds identified recurring fastener seating anomalies at the main ram assembly. Previous corrective actions documented under ECN-2026-024 addressed related interface components but did not finalize the required target torque value for the main ram retaining bolt. Field technicians reported episodic joint relaxation and evidence of micro-movement at the ram flange interface. Root cause analysis identified an under-specified assembly torque as a contributing factor.
- Purpose: This engineering change establishes the required main ram bolt torque for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to ensure joint integrity, reduce fretting at the ram flange, and improve dimensional stability of the ram position during production runs in Heat Treat operations. The change aligns assembly practice with mechanical fastener retention best practices and complements procedural updates in SOP-P1-L4-03 and maintenance task updates in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.

Affected items
- Equipment: Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2, EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The change applies to the main ram bolt at the ram to cylinder flange interface.
- Documents and procedures: SOP-P1-L4-03 is affected for assembly and startup checks; reference updates are required to include the specified torque. Maintenance work instructions MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 are affected to reflect the revised bolting requirement and to capture acceptance criteria for post-torque inspection. ECN-2026-024 remains a related change and should be consulted for component-level modifications that led to this torque determination.
- Records: Torque application records, bolted joint inspection checklists, and post-maintenance run-in logs must be updated to include the new torque entry for the main ram bolt.

Implementation
- Engineering determination: After mechanical analysis and review of the ram flange geometry and bolt class compatibility, the required main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. This value is provided to establish a repeatable target for assembly and verification.
- Procedure updates: Update SOP-P1-L4-03 to add a step requiring application of the main ram bolt torque value and to require torque verification stamping in the maintenance completion section. MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 shall be revised to include a dedicated torque step and to document torque tool calibration status at the time of work execution. Include a pass/fail acceptance criterion tied to complete seating and absence of visible gap or movement at the ram flange after torque application.
- Tools and calibration: Use calibrated torque wrench tooling appropriate for the specified torque. Prior to implementation, verify calibration records for torque application tools and capture calibration identifiers in the maintenance record entry for each torque event.
- Work control and sequencing: Implement the torque change during the next scheduled preventive maintenance window for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 or before the next hot cycle after the ECN is released, whichever occurs first. Coordinate with production planning to minimize impact on the Heat Treat schedule. Execute a dry-run bolting sequence on the ram assembly with the updated torque to verify ergonomics and access for technicians.
- Verification and validation: After torque application, perform a visual and tactile check for joint seating and confirm no excess gap. Perform functional checks required by SOP-P1-L4-03. Capture the torque reading from the calibrated tool in the maintenance record and sign off per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2. Monitor the joint during the subsequent production cycles and record any evidence of loosening or movement. If loosening is observed, halt operation and initiate the escalation matrix documented in ECN-2026-024.
- Training: Provide a brief instruction and sign-off for maintenance staff performing the torque application. Training shall cover the new torque value, the updated steps in SOP-P1-L4-03 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, tooling selection, and recordkeeping expectations. Training attendance and competency confirmation shall be retained with the maintenance records for EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
- Examples: Example entries in the maintenance log should include the equipment id, the applied torque value, tool calibration id, technician initials, and a remark field noting joint condition post-torque. Use the format specified in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 for consistency across records.

Records to keep
- A copy of the revised SOP-P1-L4-03 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, with revision reference and change summary.  
- Torque application records for each execution on EQ-P1-L4-HP02, including the applied value and torque tool calibration reference.  
- Post-torque inspection checklist completed and signed per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.  
- Training attendance and competency records for personnel authorized to apply the main ram bolt torque.  
- Any follow-up observations or corrective action entries referencing ECN-2026-024 where applicable.

Approvals
- Engineering: Approval required to confirm the mechanical basis for the specified torque and to authorize changes to SOP-P1-L4-03 and MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.  
- Maintenance management: Approval required to schedule implementation and to confirm tool availability and calibration compliance.  
- Operations supervision: Approval required to accept the implementation plan and to coordinate production impact mitigation.  
- Records of approval signatures and dates shall be filed with the ECN and retained in the document control system alongside the updated procedural documents.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-024  
- MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2  
- SOP-P1-L4-03

Note: The single explicit assembly torque requirement for this change is recorded as the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. All execution and verification steps shall reference that value exactly as documented above.

# ECN-2026-015 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Related documents: ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-04

Reason for change
-----------------

This engineering change notice documents a modification to the operational control for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, EQ-P1-L4-HT03. The change corrects an identified risk condition in the post-soak transfer-to-quench sequence that can result in unacceptable microstructural variability for affected forgings. Root-cause analysis referenced in ECN-2026-002 identified a timing allowance in the control recipe that exceeded the process window validated in initial qualification. The immediate objective is to impose a firm maximum on the delay between furnace extraction and immersion quench to align operation with metallurgical acceptance criteria and to close the procedural gap in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04.

The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.

Background and rationale
------------------------

During routine quality trend reviews and verification sampling, a pattern of elevated hardness scatter was traced to inconsistent heat transfer during the transfer-to-quench interval. Metallurgical evaluation showed that delays beyond the validated transfer window increase the risk of undesirable transformation products. The control change is limited to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and targets the control logic, operator procedures, and acceptance criteria recorded on shift logs and process control records.

This change follows the scope and intent of ECN-2026-002 and supplements procedural revisions in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04. The approach balances production continuity against the need to mitigate nonconforming output: hardware remains unchanged; software and procedural constraints are adjusted to enforce the revised timing limit.

Affected items
--------------

- All work orders processed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 while performing heat treat recipes that require immersion quench.  
- Operator checklists and control-panel prompts associated with SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04 when executed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Shift logs, nonconformance logs, and process control records generated during the transfer-to-quench operation for EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

Affected deliverables that must be updated in the document control system:
- SOP-P1-L4-02 (operational sequence) — update to incorporate enforced transfer-to-quench timing and revised operator actions when the limit is reached.
- SOP-P1-L4-04 (sampling and verification) — update to include additional sampling triggers and disposition steps when transfer delay exceeds the allowable maximum.

Implementation
--------------

Scope of implementation
- The change applies only to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 in Plant P1, line P1-L4 and to operators and technicians authorized on that equipment.

Control logic update
- Update the furnace control recipe to enforce the maximum transfer-to-quench delay as specified above. The control system shall inhibit further soak timer progression that would permit a transfer delay beyond the stated maximum and shall generate an alarm and hold the workflow for operator intervention if the limit is reached.

Operator procedure updates
- Revise SOP-P1-L4-02 to include: pre-transfer confirmation steps, real-time monitoring of transfer initiation, actions to take when an alarm is triggered, and required notifications to supervision.
- Revise SOP-P1-L4-04 to include: sampling frequency adjustments for the first production run after implementation, the required hardness and microstructure verification samples to validate the effect of the change, and disposition paths for suspect material.

Training and competency
- Conduct targeted training on the revised SOPs and control actions for all personnel assigned to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 prior to the change going live. Training records must be retained in the training management system and cross-referenced to the shift coverage record.

Operational exceptions and contingencies
- If the control alarm is received indicating the delay limit is reached, operators shall follow the exception workflow in SOP-P1-L4-02, secure the affected load, and initiate the corrective sample sequence per SOP-P1-L4-04. No product shall be released from EQ-P1-L4-HT03 without completion of the disposition path specified in SOP-P1-L4-04.

Verification and validation
- Execute one monitored production run under the revised control with full metallurgical verification per SOP-P1-L4-04. Maintain verification records, including the transfer-to-quench timing capture, process parameters, and sample results, in the process control folder for the lot.

Records to keep
---------------

Maintain the following records in the equipment file and quality system for traceability:
- Control system configuration change log for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 (including reason for change and person authorizing the change).
- Operator training sign-off records for the revised SOPs.
- Alarm and event logs showing any instances where the transfer-to-quench delay reached the maximum and subsequent actions taken.
- Process verification records and metallurgical sample results created during the initial implementation run and for subsequent verification runs as required by SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Disposition records for any affected forgings that fail verification.

Examples of documented entries
- Example entry in the shift log: description of alarm condition, start of hold, sample initiation per SOP-P1-L4-04, supervisory notification, outcome of verification testing, and final disposition.
- Example entry in the nonconformance log: reference to work order, identification of failed sample, corrective action taken, and link to control configuration change.

Approvals
---------

Approval of this ECN authorizes the changes described herein for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and requires coordinated updates to SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04 prior to live operation. Approval signatories shall confirm completion of control changes, training, and initial verification records before the revised process is placed back into production.

Related documents: ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-04

(End of document)

# ECN-2026-016 - Change notice - Machining shot blast cabinet #1
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Reason for change
- Background: During the P3-L3 machining process audit (see SB-1010) and subsequent corrective maintenance reviews, maintenance staff identified recurring lubricant compatibility issues in the shot blast cabinet drive and pivot assemblies on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Inspection records indicate increased deposition in splash shields and premature buildup on exposed bearings affecting access and cleaning efficiency. The current preventive maintenance approach did not fully address residue characteristics or handling records.
- Purpose: Standardize the lubricant for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) to a single approved part and update routines, work instructions, and records to reduce residue buildup, simplify procurement, and ensure consistent maintenance execution across line P3-L3. The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709.
- Rationale: Using a defined, approved lubricant removes ambiguity from maintenance steps in SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04, improves traceability of consumables, and aligns with material control objectives in SB-1010. The selected part has been evaluated by maintenance engineering for compatibility with cabinet materials and containment methods; field trials on a sister unit showed reduced tenacity of deposited residues and easier removal during scheduled cleaning.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01 (Machining shot blast cabinet #1) — all lubrication points identified in existing schematics and SOPs for this unit.
- Documents and procedures:
  - SOP-P3-L3-03 (weekly and monthly lubrication and cabinet inspection tasks) — updated to specify CFW-LUB-709 at each lubrication step and to add handling notes.
  - SOP-P3-L3-04 (cabinet cleaning and abrasive handling) — updated to include post-lubrication residue checks and disposal/kitting requirements.
  - SB-1010 (equipment specification and audit checklist) — cross-reference table to be updated to show CFW-LUB-709 as the specified lubricant for EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
- Parts and storeroom: Parts catalog entry for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 maintenance kit; stock record to include CFW-LUB-709 as the designated lubricant for this cabinet.
- Training: Maintenance technicians assigned to P3-L3 and operators interfacing with EQ-P3-L3-SB01 who perform minor maintenance will require training on the updated SOPs and handling precautions related to CFW-LUB-709.

Implementation
- Effective date: Implementation of the change will begin on the date of approval by the signatories in the Approvals section and will be phased into routine maintenance per the steps below.
- Steps:
  1. Documentation updates: Revise SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 to include explicit call-outs for CFW-LUB-709 and updated work-step notes. Revise SB-1010 cross-reference table. Issue redline and controlled copies.
  2. Parts provisioning: Create a stocked item entry for CFW-LUB-709 in the P3 storeroom and add to the preventive maintenance kit contents for EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Tag current lubricant stock to be used only after confirmation of compatibility or returned to vendor.
  3. Pilot application: Perform a controlled application of CFW-LUB-709 on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 during a scheduled maintenance window. Document pre- and post-application condition with photos and checklist items from SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04.
  4. Verification and acceptance: Maintenance engineering to review pilot records and, if acceptable, sign off to proceed with full roll-out.
  5. Full roll-out: Replace ad hoc lubricants in the cabinet with CFW-LUB-709 during the next scheduled maintenance tasks, following updated SOP steps.
- Work-step examples to be added to SOPs:
  - Example 1: Apply CFW-LUB-709 to the outer pivot pin using a clean dispenser until shop-recommended indication (see SOP-P3-L3-03 for dispenser handling). Wipe excess and inspect splash shield per SOP-P3-L3-04 checklist.
  - Example 2: After cabinet cleaning, record lubricant lot and dispenser ID in the maintenance log entry for traceability.
- Records to keep:
  - Maintenance log entries on the EQ-P3-L3-SB01 equipment history: technician name, date, lot number of CFW-LUB-709, dispenser ID, observations pre/post-application, and link to photo records.
  - Pilot trial report and acceptance sign-off retained in the equipment file.
  - Updated SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 controlled copies and redline histories.
  - Storeroom transaction logs showing receipt and issue of CFW-LUB-709 for EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
  - Audit trail in SB-1010 showing the change and sign-off for traceability.
- Safety and environmental notes: Add handling and spill containment steps for CFW-LUB-709 to SOP-P3-L3-04. Ensure Material Safety Data Sheet for CFW-LUB-709 is filed with plant safety and referenced in the updated SOPs.

Approvals
- Review path: Maintenance Engineering → Process Engineering → Quality Assurance → Plant Management.
- Required approval elements:
  - Confirmation that CFW-LUB-709 is stocked and traceable in the P3 storeroom.
  - Sign-off on updated SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 controlled copies.
  - Entry in SB-1010 noting the change and linking to the revised SOPs.

  - Process Engineering: name / signature / date
  - Quality Assurance: name / signature / date
  - Plant Management: name / signature / date

Related documents

- SOP-P3-L3-03
- SOP-P3-L3-04

Change control notes
- Revision: Rev C applies to this document; record the revision in the ECN log and attach redline to the prior revision.
- Rollback: If field performance of CFW-LUB-709 is unsatisfactory during pilot or roll-out, revert to prior lubricant only after documented QA concurrence and disposal or quarantine of CFW-LUB-709 stock as required. All deviations to be recorded against the ECN number.
- Post-implementation review: Schedule a 30-day field review after full roll-out to assess residue characteristics, cleaning time impact, and record completeness; capture findings in the equipment history under ECN-2026-016.
