# ECN-2026-017 - Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Reason for change
- Background: Routine review of heat treat process control for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) identified that the documented austenitizing setpoint in maintenance and operating records did not match the furnace controller setpoint. The discrepancy was discovered during a process audit and corroborated by cross-checking operator logs and controller history.
- Purpose: Align documented procedure and maintenance documentation with the verified process setpoint to eliminate ambiguity, prevent unintended parameter changes, and ensure consistent metallurgical results for downstream ring rolling operations.
- Change summary: The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C. This ECN standardizes that value across the equipment controller, the preventive maintenance package, and the standard operating procedure references cited below.

Affected items
- All copies of the preventive maintenance document for EQ-P3-L2-HT03: MM-P3-L2-HT03 will be updated to reflect the specified austenitizing setpoint.
- The specific service procedure supplement MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 will be revised to include verification steps that confirm controller setpoint matches the documented austenitizing setpoint prior to any production heat cycle.
- The standard operating procedure SOP-P3-L2-02 will be revised to include a mandatory pre-heat checklist line that references verification of the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
- Operator training records and shift handover logs that reference austenitizing conditions for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 must be reviewed and updated to reflect the approved setpoint.
- Historical furnace run records where the documented setpoint differs from the approved setpoint will be flagged for metallurgical review as part of the implementation.

Implementation
- Documentation updates: Revise MM-P3-L2-HT03, MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3, and SOP-P3-L2-02 to include the confirmed austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 as 870 °C and the verification steps described below. The revised documents will be issued through document control and placed on the plant document server with controlled revision status.
- Controller verification: Technicians will compare the controller display and configuration for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 to the documented austenitizing setpoint. If the controller does not read the specified austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L2-HT03, the technician will follow MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 to locate and correct the discrepancy before release for production.
- SOP sequence addition: SOP-P3-L2-02 will be modified to include a pre-heat verification step requiring the operator to confirm that the controller setpoint for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 equals the documented austenitizing setpoint. Operators will initial and date the pre-heat checklist entry to provide an auditable record.
- Training and communication: All operators and maintenance personnel assigned to line P3-L2 and EQ-P3-L2-HT03 will receive a briefing on the change. The briefing will cover background, the revised verification step in SOP-P3-L2-02, and how to use MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 to reconcile controller/document discrepancies.
- Nonconformance handling: Any production heat cycles on EQ-P3-L2-HT03 performed with a controller setpoint that does not match the documented austenitizing setpoint will be documented as a process deviation. Affected batches will be quarantined and referred to metallurgical engineering for disposition, using the process referenced in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Examples: Example documentation entries will be included in MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3 showing a completed pre-heat verification for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 where the operator initials the checklist and records the controller readout value as matching the documented austenitizing setpoint of 870 °C.
- Records to keep: Maintain the following records in the equipment file for EQ-P3-L2-HT03: the ECN form for ECN-2026-017, the revised MM-P3-L2-HT03, the revised MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3, the revised SOP-P3-L2-02 excerpt, completed pre-heat checklists for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 showing verification of the austenitizing setpoint, any controller configuration printouts used during verification, training acknowledgment forms for operators and maintenance personnel, and a log of any deviations discovered and their dispositions.

Approvals
- Authorization: This change is approved for implementation in plant P3, line P3-L2 for EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Implementation must follow the revision and issuance process in the document control system and include updates to MM-P3-L2-HT03, MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3, and SOP-P3-L2-02 as cited.
- Approver responsibilities: Approvers will confirm that the documentation updates correctly reference the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and that the implementation actions listed under Implementation have been completed. Approvers will ensure that training acknowledgments and pre-heat verification records are present in the equipment file prior to releasing the revised procedures for production use.
- Record retention: All records generated as part of this ECN will be retained in the equipment file for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 and available for audit in accordance with plant P3 record retention practice and the document control requirements referenced in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
- Related documents: See MM-P3-L2-HT03, MM-P3-L2-HT03-S3, and SOP-P3-L2-02 for the procedural details and forms to be used in implementation.

Prepared by: Engineering Change Control  
For inquiries related to this ECN, contact the document owner listed in MM-P3-L2-HT03.
title: Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

# ECN-2026-018 Change notice - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Related documents: MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1, SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-05

## Reason for change

Background: During a routine maintenance review and after an incident that produced excessive runout on a finished ring, the maintenance and reliability teams performed a focused investigation of the mandrel clamp assembly on EQ-P2-L3-RR01. The existing maintenance documentation referenced in MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 lacked a mandatory, documented clamp bolt torque value for the mandrel clamp. Field verification found inconsistent clamp bolt tensioning practices among technicians, which contributed to clamp slippage and repeat set-up adjustments during machining.

Engineering assessment determined that establishing a single validated clamp bolt torque will reduce clamp slippage, improve concentricity on first-pass machining, and reduce rework. The new torque value is also required to align SOP practice language between SOP-P2-L3-01 and SOP-P2-L3-05 and to provide clear acceptance criteria for maintenance and operations crews.

Change objective: Issue a controlled change to maintenance and operating procedures to mandate the verified mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 to ensure consistent clamp preload, reduce part rejects, and improve process capability.

Mandated value: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 470 N·m.

## Affected items

Scope: This change affects the mandrel clamp assembly and associated fasteners on EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and all work instructions, maintenance checklists, and operator setup procedures that reference clamp torque for that equipment.

Documents to be revised:
- MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 — update maintenance procedure section to include the mandated torque and acceptance criteria.
- SOP-P2-L3-01 — update machine setup steps to require verification of clamp torque prior to cut.
- SOP-P2-L3-05 — update maintenance verification and handover criteria to include post-torque inspection and recordkeeping.

Affected personnel and roles:
- Maintenance technicians assigned to EQ-P2-L3-RR01 must apply the mandated torque and document the action in the maintenance record.
- Machine operators must verify presence of the maintenance record before commencing production and confirm clamp integrity as specified in SOP revisions.
- Reliability engineers will monitor clamp-related defects and trend results after implementation.

Excluded items:
- Other radial ring rolling mills and other clamps not explicitly identified as part of EQ-P2-L3-RR01 are not included in this ECN; any adoption on other equipment requires separate ECN and validation.

## Implementation

Procedure updates: The maintenance procedure in MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 will be revised to add a dedicated step for mandrel clamp bolt torque. The step will identify the required torque value, acceptable evidence of torque application, and acceptance checks for clamp seating and thread engagement. SOP-P2-L3-01 and SOP-P2-L3-05 will be updated to reference the revised maintenance document and to require verification of the maintenance entry prior to machine start.

Work instruction excerpt (for insertion into MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 and SOPs):
- Clean clamp bolt threads and seating area; inspect for damage or contamination.
- Apply specified torque to clamp bolts using a calibrated torque wrench.
- The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 470 N·m.
- Record torque application in the equipment maintenance log with technician initials and torque wrench serial number.
- Perform visual check for proper clamp seating and confirm no gap exists between clamp face and mandrel flange.

Tools and calibration: Only calibrated torque wrenches with valid calibration tags are to be used. Calibration records will be checked during the first implementation audit.

Training and competence: Conduct focused training for affected maintenance technicians and operators covering the change rationale, the new mandatory torque value, correct torque application technique, and record requirements. Training attendance and competence checks will be documented.

Implementation steps and timeline: The revised documents will be issued as controlled revisions and distributed through document control. Maintenance for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 will incorporate the new step at the next scheduled downtime window. During the first applications after implementation, a reliability engineer will perform a verification of clamp torque and seating.

Examples of acceptable records:
- Maintenance log entry that states the torque value applied, technician initials, date, and torque wrench identifier.
- Post-maintenance checklist item in SOP-P2-L3-05 confirming torque verification and clamp inspection.
- A photo of the clamp with visible seating and torque wrench in-station where applicable.

Monitoring and metrics: Reliability will track clamp-related defects and first-pass machining yield for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 after implementation. Trend analysis will reference the maintenance records and SOP signoffs. If clamp slippage or related defects persist, further engineering evaluation and possible hardware redesign will be initiated.

Document control actions: MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1, SOP-P2-L3-01, and SOP-P2-L3-05 will receive revision updates citing ECN-2026-018. The controlled copies on the plant network will be updated and superseded copies archived per document control policy.

## Approvals

Required approvals:
- Maintenance Manager: approves update to MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 and confirms technicians will be trained.
- Operations Manager: approves SOP updates and confirms operator verification requirement.
- Reliability Engineer: approves the torque validation method and will monitor post-implementation results.
- Document Control: issues controlled revisions and records the ECN in the change log.

Approval records to be kept:
- Signed ECN approval sheet archived in the document control system.
- Revision history entries in MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1, SOP-P2-L3-01, and SOP-P2-L3-05 referencing ECN-2026-018.
- Training rosters and competency checklists showing attendance and successful demonstration.
- Calibration certificates for torque wrenches used, linked to maintenance log entries.
- Maintenance log entries and photographic evidence where applicable.

References: MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1, SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-05

Change owner: Maintenance Engineering lead for line P2-L3

Document distribution: Controlled electronic copies will be issued to maintenance, operations, reliability, and document control. Physical copies will be posted at the EQ-P2-L3-RR01 maintenance station as referenced in the revised SOPs.

# ECN-2026-019 - Change notice - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Reason for change
- Background: Routine audits and operator feedback identified variability in surface quality of ring-rolled components processed in the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet identified as EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Inspection records and process reviews indicated that media wear and contamination were contributing factors influencing blast effectiveness and repeatability.
- Purpose: This change updates the preventive maintenance practice specific to shot media replenishment for EQ-P3-L2-SB01 to improve consistency of blast results, reduce rework, and align maintenance activity with actual process demands while minimizing production interruptions.
- Root cause rationale: Analysis showed that media degradation and gradual size distribution shift reduce kinetic efficiency and change abrasive behavior over time. Top-up frequency was observed to lag behind the rate of effective media loss and contamination accumulation. Adjusting the media top-up cadence addresses the root cause by restoring media mass and abrasive profile before process drift becomes measurable.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P3-L2-SB01 (Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1) only. No changes to other shot blast cabinets or different processes in plant P3 are covered by this ECN.
- Procedures impacted: Operators and maintenance personnel shall follow updated instructions and recordkeeping practices in SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 where those procedures reference shot media handling, cabinet operation, and quality acceptance criteria. Cross-reference check: these SOPs remain the governing documents for routine operation and quality checks; this ECN modifies how often media is topped up for the listed equipment and documents required to capture.
- Spare parts and consumables: Existing approved shot media type and vendor remain unchanged. This ECN does not change material specifications or introduce new consumables.

Implementation
- Change detail: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. This interval is the new standard cadence for adding fresh shot media to the cabinet hopper to maintain target media mass and abrasive performance between scheduled full media maintenance events.
- Implementation steps:
  - Supervisors will update the maintenance schedule in the local planning board and electronic maintenance system to reflect the new top-up cadence for EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
  - Operators will perform a media level and contamination check at shift turnover and log the check in the cabinet log. If media shows abnormal contamination or degradation outside expected conditions, escalate per SOP-P3-L2-03.
  - Maintenance technicians will perform the media top-up action per the cabinet handling instructions in SOP-P3-L2-02. Top-up actions will replenish media to the nominal fill point specified in existing cabinet documentation; no change to fill point is authorized by this ECN.
  - Quality engineering will sample processed parts at normal inspection gates and track surface uniformity trends for a baseline period following implementation to confirm effectiveness.
- Examples and acceptance criteria:
  - Example scenario: If, during a production run, an operator notes increased dusting or reduced finish uniformity, the operator will document the observation and perform the prescribed media check. If the observation correlates to media level below acceptable visual range or visible contamination, a top-up action in accordance with the new interval statement will be executed immediately and recorded.
  - Acceptance criteria: Post-implementation data should show reduced incidence of rework related to surface finish, stable inspection metrics, and reduced variance in acceptance decisions at quality gates. Any deviation will trigger a review and possible adjustment in execution fidelity rather than further change to hours interval.
- Records to keep:
  - Cabinet media log entries for EQ-P3-L2-SB01 showing date, shift, operator initials, media top-up confirmation, and any noted anomalies.
  - Maintenance service call records and work orders referencing the top-up action and linking to the cabinet log.
  - Quality inspection records and trend analysis reports for the ring-rolled product family processed through EQ-P3-L2-SB01, maintained per plant retention policy and referenced in follow-up reviews.
- Training and communication:
  - Operators, maintenance, and quality personnel assigned to P3-L2 will receive briefing on the top-up interval change and the required log practices. Briefing materials will reference SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 for operational and quality criteria.
  - Supervisors are responsible for ensuring briefing completion and for initial verification of record entries for a monitoring period following rollout.

Approvals
- Authorization path: Implementation requires signatures from plant maintenance management, operations management for line P3-L2, and quality engineering. The approval package will include a signed copy of this ECN, updated maintenance schedule entries for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, and evidence of personnel briefing.
- Post-implementation review: A coordinated review among maintenance, operations, and quality will be conducted after the initial monitoring period to verify that the shot media top-up practice yields the intended reduction in process variability. The review will reference the records described above and the governing SOPs SOP-P3-L2-02, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-05 to ensure compliance.
- Document control: This ECN is Rev D and will be attached to the EQ-P3-L2-SB01 asset file and the revision history for the related SOPs where applicable. All relevant local work instructions will be updated to reflect the new top-up cadence and recordkeeping requirements.

Notes
- This change does not alter approved media specifications, part numbers, or the physical configuration of EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Any proposed variation beyond the scope of media top-up cadence must be addressed via a separate engineering change process.
title: Change notice - Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1

# ECN-2026-020 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Routine maintenance reviews and recent audit findings identified inconsistent tracking of thermocouple drift on Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02). Calibration records in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 indicated variable intervals between verifications, and operators reported uncertainty about when the next verification was due. To reduce process variability and ensure metallurgical conformance for parts processed on line P2-L4, a formal standardized calibration interval is required for the furnace thermocouples.

Rationale: Establishing a documented thermocouple calibration interval reduces risk of undetected measurement drift, improves repeatability of heat treat cycles, and aligns maintenance activity with procedural expectations referenced in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02. The chosen interval balances equipment reliability and workload on the maintenance team while being short enough to detect drift before it impacts product quality. This change closes a gap observed during the recent maintenance review and supports traceability of calibration activities.

Affected items
--------------
Scope: This change applies to the thermocouple sensor array and associated calibration records for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Affected records include the on-equipment calibration log, the maintenance master record MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and any process run sheets that reference thermocouple verification status in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02.

Specifics: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days. All calibration events recorded for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 must reference MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and be cross-referenced on the daily control log used by operators under SOP-P2-L4-01. Any nonconforming readings discovered during calibration must be dispositioned according to the escalation path in SOP-P2-L4-02.

Implementation
--------------
Overview: Implementation will be coordinated between Maintenance, Heat Treat Operations, and Quality. The change will be applied to the calibration scheduling system, the maintenance master record MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and to the procedural steps in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02 where calibration status is checked prior to processing.

Stepwise actions:
- Update MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 to include the new thermocouple calibration interval and to include a field for next due date. Maintenance planners will populate the next due date at the time of each calibration event.
- Update the pre-run checklist in SOP-P2-L4-01 to require verification of calibration status for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 before authorizing the start of any heat treat cycle. Include instruction that the on-equipment log must be present and that the last calibration entry must reference MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.
- Update the escalation and disposition steps in SOP-P2-L4-02 to define actions when a thermocouple fails calibration. Required actions include tagging affected thermocouples, logging the event, and notifying Quality for potential hold on affected lots.
- Configure the electronic maintenance scheduling tool to generate reminders aligned with the calibration interval for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Maintenance will acknowledge reminders and attach a completed calibration certificate to MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.
- Conduct a short training brief for Maintenance and Operations staff to review the new interval and the updated checklist items in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SOP-P2-L4-02. Training attendance will be recorded and retained with change implementation records.

Examples of expected behavior:
- When a calibration is completed on EQ-P2-L4-HT02, the technician will enter the calibration result in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, sign the entry, and schedule the next calibration according to the interval specified above. Operators will confirm calibration status during pre-run checks per SOP-P2-L4-01.
- If a thermocouple is found out of tolerance during calibration, Maintenance will tag the sensor as out of service, document the corrective action in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2, and follow the hold and disposition steps in SOP-P2-L4-02 before returning the furnace to production.

Records to keep
---------------
Retention: All calibration records for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 must be filed in MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 and maintained in the quality record system referenced by SOP-P2-L4-02. Records from the pre-run verification in SOP-P2-L4-01 shall be retained with the affected job traveler and linked to the lot history.

Minimum documentation for each calibration event:
- Completed calibration certificate attached to MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2.
- Technician name and signature on the calibration entry.
- Date of calibration and the next due date populated per the interval.
- Any deviation or corrective action noted and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L4-02 when applicable.
- Training acknowledgment for personnel performing or verifying calibration checks.

Audit and verification
----------------------
Quality will include verification of compliance with the new calibration interval during planned audits and when reviewing process capability data for heat treat operations on line P2-L4. Audit checks will include review of MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 entries and cross-reference to pre-run checks in SOP-P2-L4-01. Discrepancies will be handled following SOP-P2-L4-02.

Approvals
---------
Requested approvers: Maintenance Supervisor, Heat Treat Operations Manager, Quality Manager, and Plant Manager for P2, line P2-L4.

Approval actions:
- Maintenance Supervisor to confirm MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2 has been updated and scheduling configured.
- Heat Treat Operations Manager to confirm SOP-P2-L4-01 pre-run checklist has been updated and the team briefed.
- Quality Manager to confirm SOP-P2-L4-02 escalation paths are clear and record retention meets audit requirements.
- Plant Manager for P2, line P2-L4 to authorize the change and confirm resources for training and any tooling support.

Related documents
-----------------
MM-P2-L4-HT02-S2  
SOP-P2-L4-01  
SOP-P2-L4-02

Change control notes
--------------------
This ECN captures the formal change to calibration practice for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Implementation will be monitored and reported in the next maintenance review cycle. Any need to adjust the interval or related procedures must be submitted as a follow-up ECN with supporting data from calibration trends and process capability analyses.
title: Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

# ECN-2026-021 - Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

Related documents: ECN-2026-035, SB-1029, SOP-P1-L3-01

Reason for change
- Background: During routine inspection and feedback from machining operations, documentation and safety review identified a need to formally revise the operational envelope and maintenance handling instructions for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02). The change clarifies the system pressure limit and aligns operational references with current preventive maintenance practice and safety bulletin content.
- Safety rationale: The primary driver is to ensure all operators, maintenance technicians, and engineering staff have an unambiguous maximum hydraulic system pressure for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 to prevent overpressure events and reduce risk of component failure. This revision provides the single authorized pressure limit for the system: the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. This value supersedes any informal or legacy references to pressure values that lack formal control.
- Process rationale: Standardizing the pressure limit reduces variability in set point configuration, pressure gauge interpretation, and calibration targets. It supports consistent procurement of pressure control components and a harmonized approach to troubleshooting pressure-related faults.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02, including hydraulic power unit, pressure relief and control valves, pressure transducers, hoses, fittings, and the machine control interface.
- Documentation: SOP-P1-L3-01 must be updated to reference the authorized system pressure limit for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 and to include verification steps aligned with this change. Related change ECN-2026-035 and safety bulletin SB-1029 are cited for additional procedural and safety context and must be cross-referenced in updated materials.
- Records and labels: Pressure set point records, calibration certificates, and in-situ pressure gauge labels on EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must reflect the new limit. Maintenance logs and inspection checklists for the equipment are affected to ensure recorded readings and tolerances are evaluated against the stated system pressure limit.
- Training: Operator and maintenance training materials that reference system pressure limits or pressure-related troubleshooting for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must be revised. Practical training sessions and assessment checklists should incorporate verification that personnel understand and can demonstrate compliance with the stated system pressure limit.

Implementation
- Scope: The implementation applies exclusively to EQ-P1-L3-HP02 and its supporting documentation and records within Plant P1, line P1-L3. No changes to other presses are authorized by this notice unless those items are specifically captured in a separate ECN.
- Procedure updates: Update SOP-P1-L3-01 to show the system pressure limit for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 as the definitive value. Add a verification step to pre-operational checks: confirm pressure displays and gauges read no greater than the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar and document the result.
- Labeling: Apply new durable decals at the hydraulic power unit and at the operator control panel stating the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Existing adhesive labels that state any other pressure value must be removed or obscured.
- Controls and set points: Maintenance personnel must set and lock any adjustable pressure relief or control devices so that system pressure cannot be increased above the authorized limit. Where mechanical locks or tamper-evident seals are used, documentation must record seal identifiers and the authorizing approver.
- Verification and calibration: Pressure transducers and portable pressure measuring devices used for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must be verified against calibration records and confirmed to be within acceptable accuracy for the stated system pressure limit. Calibration certificates referenced in maintenance logs should cite the device identifier and test result; any device lacking a valid certificate must be removed from service until recalibrated.
- Acceptance criteria: Successful implementation requires that all updated documentation is published to the document control system, that labels are installed on EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and that a three step verification is completed by maintenance and operations: physical label check, control set point confirmation, and a recorded gauge reading that does not exceed the published limit. Completion of these steps must be recorded in the equipment maintenance log and attached to the ECN closure package.
- Records to keep: Maintain the following records in the equipment file: updated SOP-P1-L3-01 excerpt showing the new limit, pressure gauge calibration certificates, pressure transducer test data, label installation confirmation, control set point lock documentation, and the completion record from the verification steps. Also include cross-references to ECN-2026-035 and SB-1029 as they relate to procedural or safety updates.
- Example scenarios: For a planned maintenance task involving replacement of a pressure relief valve on EQ-P1-L3-HP02, use the new limit as the acceptance target when adjusting the replacement valve. During pre-operational start-up after maintenance, confirm that live system readings do not exceed the declared limit and record the check in the maintenance log.

Approvals
- Approval process: This ECN requires approval by responsible engineering authority, maintenance management, and operations supervision before implementation. Approvals shall be recorded in the document control system and linked to the ECN record.
- Responsibilities: Engineering is responsible for updating SOP-P1-L3-01 and coordinating label content. Maintenance is responsible for performing mechanical set point control actions, locking set points, and performing verification checks. Operations is responsible for updating operator checklists and completing operator verification of label presence and pre-operational pressure checks.
- Cross references: Implementing parties must review ECN-2026-035 and SB-1029 for related changes and safety guidance and ensure SOP-P1-L3-01 reflects both the procedural and safety context.
- Closure requirements: The ECN will be closed when all affected items are updated, required records are filed, and approvers have signed off in the document control system. The closure package must include the records listed above and a brief implementation report summarizing actions taken on EQ-P1-L3-HP02.

Document control note
- This change notice modifies the authorized operating documentation for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 and must be referenced in future maintenance and engineering actions affecting the hydraulic system. See SOP-P1-L3-01 for day to day operational steps and ECN-2026-035 and SB-1029 for supplementary instructions and safety context.

# ECN-2026-022 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

## Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a required update to the documented minimum coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01). Field verification and vendor guidance revealed that previous documentation and control setpoints allowed flows below the safe operating value for the heater coil cooling circuit. Operating at lower flow has repeatedly produced coil outlet temperatures and diagnostics that indicate elevated risk of localized overheating and accelerated insulation degradation. The change aligns operational controls and maintenance acceptance criteria with the verified minimum flow requirement to preserve coil life and to maintain safe and reliable heater performance.

Related guidance and background from recent change activity and procedures are recorded in ECN-2026-029 and in the operational procedures SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-04. This ECN updates machine-specific requirements only; procedural updates to operator checklists and SOPs are tracked in the related documents cited above.

Rationale:
- Remove ambiguity between machine wiring diagrams, the unit PLC interlocks, and the maintenance acceptance criteria.
- Reduce unplanned heater outages attributed to coil overheating and insulation faults.
- Standardize entry criteria for planned maintenance and for run-permit interlocks.

## Affected items
- Machine: Machining induction billet heater #1, equipment tag EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Operator checklists and pre-start verification items used on line P1-L3, referenced in SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-04.
- PLC analog input mapping and alarm thresholds that govern the coil cooling water flow permissive and associated inhibit logic.
- Maintenance acceptance criteria and torque verification steps that reference coil cooling performance.

Specific change to be recorded on equipment nameplate and in the equipment record: the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. This value is to be treated as the minimum allowable flow for normal operation and will be used for commissioning, acceptance, and alarm limits.

Examples of scenarios to which the change applies:
- During start-up, the cooling water flow reading must be verified against the minimum value prior to establishing heater drive enable.
- During preventative inspections, if measured flow is at or below the minimum, tagging and corrective action are required prior to return to service.
- When troubleshooting coil-related alarms, flow verification to this minimum is a first-line diagnostic step.

## Implementation
Scope:
- Update equipment record and drawing notes for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to include the specified minimum coil cooling water flow.
- Update PLC alarm and interlock thresholds associated with the flow permit so that a below-minimum condition generates a visible alarm and inhibits heater enable.
- Revise the pre-start checklist in SOP-P1-L3-01 and the maintenance acceptance checklist in SOP-P1-L3-04 to include explicit verification of the minimum flow value for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.

Actions and sequence:
1) Engineering will issue an updated equipment data sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 reflecting the required flow minimum and attach it to the equipment file.
2) Controls will change the flow permissive setpoint and the alarm setpoint in the PLC to reference the minimum. Controls will document the ladder or function block changes in the control change log.
3) Operations will receive a brief awareness briefing covering the revised pre-start checks and the location of the equipment nameplate stating the minimum flow.
4) Maintenance will incorporate the minimum flow verification into the standard maintenance checklist for coils and circulation systems. Records of measured flow will be retained as maintenance evidence.
5) Commissioning verification will demonstrate that with the revised interlock in place the heater will not enable when measured flow is below the minimum. Results will be recorded in the commissioning record.

Records to keep:
- Updated equipment data sheet for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 with the minimum coil cooling water flow note.
- Controls change log entries showing the PLC modifications and justification.
- Commissioning test report demonstrating interlock functionality and alarm behavior.
- Operator pre-start checklist entries showing flow verification for an agreed number of consecutive starts following implementation.
- Maintenance inspection reports showing periodic verification of actual flow against the minimum value.

Examples of acceptable records entries:
- A maintenance report entry shall state the measurement method, the measured value, and confirmation that the measured flow meets or exceeds the minimum as referenced on the equipment data sheet.
- Controls log entries shall include the file and function block names revised, a brief rationale, and the signature of the responsible engineer.

Note on measurement method:
Use the method specified in SOP-P1-L3-04 for measuring coil cooling water flow and record instrument identification as part of the evidence. If temporary flow measurement equipment is used for verification, the instrument serial or tag used must be recorded in the maintenance report.

Change timing and coordination:
- Implementation requires coordination between Engineering, Controls, Operations, and Maintenance to schedule PLC updates and operator training without disrupting production continuity. Controls will coordinate an installation window with Operations.

## Approvals
- Engineering: approval required to update equipment data sheet and issue ECN.
- Controls: approval required for PLC interlock and alarm changes.
- Operations: acknowledgment of revised pre-start procedures and acceptance of training.
- Maintenance: acknowledgment of revised maintenance acceptance criteria and recordkeeping requirements.

Approvals shall be recorded in the ECN approval block and in the equipment file. Reference related documents ECN-2026-029, SOP-P1-L3-01, and SOP-P1-L3-04 for procedural detail and for any follow-up tasks that propagate to standardized procedures.

# ECN-2026-023 Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and reliability reviews of Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01), lubrication performance deviations were observed in the main radial bearing lubrication system. Condition monitoring records indicated increased vibration and bearing temperature trends that were traced to inconsistent lubricant supply and a change in vendor performance of the legacy lubricant. An engineering evaluation recommended a controlled change to the approved lubricant to address contamination control, film stability, and compatibility with existing seals and metering devices.
- Objective: Standardize the lubricant in the primary radial bearing circuit to an approved Cascade Forge Works lubricant identified by part number CFW-LUB-724 in order to restore consistent lubrication performance, reduce unplanned stoppages, and simplify inventory and procurement for P2, line P2-L1.
- Rationale: CFW-LUB-724 was selected after laboratory compatibility testing with machine elastomers and materials, bench tribology testing representative of the ring rolling mill service, and supplier quality assurance review. The lubricant meets internal acceptance criteria documented in SB-1030 and is compatible with the machine's existing filtration and metering hardware described in SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02. Adopting a single, specified lubricant reduces cross-contamination risk and streamlines parts and materials traceability.

Affected items
- Equipment effected: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1, asset tag EQ-P2-L1-RR01, including main radial bearing lubrication circuits, refill reservoirs, and associated supply lines identified in the equipment lubrication schematic.
- Procedures: Lubrication procedures and reservoir refill steps in SOP-P2-L1-01 and the inspection and sampling steps in SOP-P2-L1-02 require update to reference CFW-LUB-724 as the approved lubricant for EQ-P2-L1-RR01.
- Inventory: Plant storeroom inventory for P2, line P2-L1 must be updated to include CFW-LUB-724 as the designated stock item for radial bearing lubrication for EQ-P2-L1-RR01. Existing stocks of other lubricants previously used on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 must be quarantined and dispositioned per SB-1030.
- Training and competence: Maintenance personnel performing lubrication tasks on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 are affected; training records must reflect the change and updated procedural steps.

Implementation
- Approval boundary: This change is limited to Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) at Plant P2, line P2-L1. No other equipment is affected unless explicitly listed in a separate ECN.
- Procurement and supply: All future purchases for radial bearing lubricant for EQ-P2-L1-RR01 must use the part number CFW-LUB-724. Procurement will only accept material tagged with this part number for the affected asset. Incoming material shall be checked against the supplier certificate of analysis and lot identification per SB-1030.
- Preparation: Prior to first fill with CFW-LUB-724, the lubrication reservoir and supply lines shall be drained and flushed to remove residual lubricant from prior fills. Flushing agents and methods shall follow the guidance in SOP-P2-L1-01 to ensure material compatibility with CFW-LUB-724 and system elastomers. Flush waste and cleaning records must be retained with the work order.
- First-fill execution: Maintenance shall perform the first-fill sequence under a planned maintenance work order. The work order shall reference ECN-2026-023 and include the following required records: batch/lot number of CFW-LUB-724 used, supplier certificate of analysis, pre- and post-fill condition readings, and a signed verification by the maintenance supervisor that flushing and fill steps conformed to SOP-P2-L1-01.
- Post-change monitoring: After implementation, the reliability team will monitor EQ-P2-L1-RR01 using existing condition monitoring processes documented in SOP-P2-L1-02. Trending records, bearing vibration readings, and any abnormal alarms shall be reviewed and retained in the maintenance record for the asset. Any deviation from expected performance shall trigger immediate inspection and corrective action, with records updated under the associated work order.
- Examples of acceptable records: a completed work order packet containing the CFW-LUB-724 lot number, supplier certificate of analysis, signed procedural checklists referencing SOP-P2-L1-01, and post-fill condition monitoring logs pulled per SOP-P2-L1-02.
- Change to documentation: SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02 shall be revised to list CFW-LUB-724 as the approved lubricant for EQ-P2-L1-RR01. The revisions shall be controlled updates coordinated through document control and linked to this ECN. Operators and maintenance staff will receive the updated procedures and a briefing prior to first-fill.
- Inventory disposition: Existing lubricant stocks previously assigned to EQ-P2-L1-RR01 must be quarantined, labeled, and processed following SB-1030 for disposition. Records of disposition shall be attached to the ECN closeout package.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: The responsible mechanical engineering reviewer must sign to confirm laboratory compatibility testing and bench testing support the use of CFW-LUB-724 for EQ-P2-L1-RR01. The approval shall reference SB-1030 evidence and link to updated SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance management must sign to authorize implementation of the drain, flush, and first-fill activities and to confirm training and resources are scheduled. Maintenance must ensure that work orders capture required records and that the maintenance planner updates inventory masters to include CFW-LUB-724 for the asset.
- Quality assurance approval: QA shall confirm receipt and review of supplier certification for CFW-LUB-724 batches used on the asset and approve final release of the ECN upon satisfactory completion of first-fill and initial monitoring.
- Records to keep: Attach to the ECN closeout package the following items: supplier certificate of analysis for each CFW-LUB-724 lot used, completed work order with signed checklists, pre/post condition monitoring logs produced per SOP-P2-L1-02, inventory change notifications, and revised procedure documents SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-02 with change markings.
- Closure criteria: ECN will be closed after engineering, maintenance, and QA approvals are documented and post-change monitoring demonstrates restored and stable lubrication performance for EQ-P2-L1-RR01 per the acceptance process in SB-1030. The closeout package must be submitted to document control and filed against the asset record.

Related documents
- SB-1030
- SOP-P2-L1-01
- SOP-P2-L1-02

Approved by:
- Engineering (name/signature)
- Maintenance (name/signature)
- Quality Assurance (name/signature)

Note: The specified lubricant part number for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 is CFW-LUB-724 and must be used in all implementation and procurement actions for EQ-P2-L1-RR01.

# ECN-2026-024 Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Reason for change

This engineering change modifies the documentation and maintenance baseline for the main ram bolt of the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02). Background: during a planned disassembly for component inspection, maintenance technicians observed variable preload and fretting at the main ram bolt connection. Investigation confirmed that assembly practice varied between shifts and that existing maintenance procedures did not explicitly specify a final main ram bolt torque for EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The change establishes and documents the required main ram bolt torque and updates affected procedures and records to ensure repeatable assembly and to reduce the risk of loosening, fatigue damage, or misalignment of the ram assembly.

The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.

Rationale

Establishing a single, documented torque value ensures consistent preload and clamp load across maintenance activities and between crews. Consistent preload reduces relative motion at the bolted joint, decreasing fretting wear and the likelihood of fatigue cracks initiating at the bolt or mating components. Explicit torque specification also supports traceability of assembly and simplifies troubleshooting when vibration or alignment anomalies occur. This change aligns the maintenance and operating documentation for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to support safe, reliable operation during production and planned maintenance.

Affected items

- Maintenance procedure revisions: update the technical maintenance document referenced as MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 to include the specified main ram bolt torque and associated assembly notes.
- Standard operating procedures: update SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-05 to reference the new torque requirement where they direct ram removal, installation, or bolt inspection sequences.
- Maintenance records and checklists: update maintenance checklists and electronic work orders to include a field for recorded torque confirmation for the main ram bolt of EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
- Training and qualifications: maintenance technicians who perform ram assembly/disassembly on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 must be briefed on the revised torque requirement and the associated verification process.
- Spare parts handling: during reassembly after any replacement of ram-related components, the main ram bolt torque value must be applied and recorded per the revised MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.

Implementation

Scope: apply to all maintenance actions that require removal or reinstallation of the main ram bolt on EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and to routine inspections where bolt torque verification is specified.

Procedure updates
- MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2: add a new section immediately following the ram installation sequence titled "Main Ram Bolt Final Torque." This section will state the required torque value verbatim: 970 N·m. It will include the requirement to use a calibrated torque wrench and to apply torque in the specified bolt seating configuration described elsewhere in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2. Cross-reference SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for safety and lockout procedures prior to assembly.
- SOP-P1-L4-01 and SOP-P1-L4-05: insert a single-line callout where ram work is invoked to ensure the technician verifies the main ram bolt torque per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 and documents the result on the work order.

Assembly and verification steps (summary)
- Prior to torque application, verify bolt and mating surfaces are clean and free of debris as described in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.
- Use a calibrated torque wrench appropriate for the required torque range, and verify calibration status against calibration records.
- Apply the final torque to the main ram bolt and record the measured torque value on the maintenance record.
- Perform a visual inspection for correct seating and apply any mechanical retention method called out in MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2.
- Document the technician’s name, tool identifier, and reference to the work order on the maintenance record.

Examples of acceptable records to retain
- Completed maintenance work order with explicit entry: "Main ram bolt torque applied per MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2: 970 N·m. Tool ID: [tool identifier]. Technician: [name]." (Bracketed items denote free-text fields that record personnel and tool identifiers.)
- Torque wrench calibration certificate or traceability record referenced by tool identifier used for the work.
- Photo record of the installed ram connection showing the final seating and any locking device applied, saved to the equipment maintenance folder for EQ-P1-L4-HP02.

Training and rollout
- Conduct a brief job safety and procedure briefing for maintenance staff assigned to EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The briefing will cover the torque requirement and verification steps, and direct staff to the updated MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, SOP-P1-L4-01, and SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Supervisors will ensure the first three maintenance actions performed against the revised procedure are co-signed by the supervisor to verify compliance and record retention.

Records to keep

Maintain the following documents in the equipment maintenance file for EQ-P1-L4-HP02:
- Updated MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 with the "Main Ram Bolt Final Torque" section.
- Work orders and checklists showing recorded application of 970 N·m to the main ram bolt.
- Torque tool calibration records referenced by tool identifier.
- Training acknowledgement records for personnel who received the briefing.
All records will be retained according to plant document control policy and made available for review during inspections and audits.

Approvals

This ECN requires approval by maintenance engineering, shop supervision, and quality assurance prior to issuing revised MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, SOP-P1-L4-01, and SOP-P1-L4-05. Approval signatures will be appended to this ECN and copies of the approved revision will be distributed to maintenance planners, supervisors, and the document control system.

Related documents

See the following documents for procedure details and safety steps:
- MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2
- SOP-P1-L4-01
- SOP-P1-L4-05

Implementation note: do not perform torque work on EQ-P1-L4-HP02 until revised MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2, SOP-P1-L4-01, and SOP-P1-L4-05 have been issued and the assigned maintenance personnel have completed the briefing.

# ECN-2026-025 Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: Recent maintenance audits and lubricant analysis samples identified accelerated wear signatures on the main roll bearings of the Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01). Trending in vibration and oil particle counts, reviewed against the existing maintenance practice, indicates that lubrication frequency is a principal contributor to the observed condition. Laboratory commentary recommended shortening the time between replenishment to reduce contamination loading and restore hydrodynamic film integrity.
- Objective: Standardize the main roll bearing lubrication to a defined interval to reduce wear rates, extend component life, and reduce unplanned downtime risk. This change aligns maintenance practice with the findings in related engineering notices and standard operating procedures to ensure consistent application across the line and supporting documentation.
- Rationale: Implementing a documented, shorter lubrication interval provides a simple, auditable action that directly addresses the root-cause indicators from oil analysis and bearing inspections. The interval decision was selected to balance operational availability with lubricant contamination control, minimize bearing metal-to-metal contact risk, and provide a repeatable baseline for future trend analysis and corrective actions.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01).  
- Components affected: Main roll bearings and associated lubrication system components (feed lines, reservoirs, strainers, and gauge points used for sampling).  
- Documentation affected: Maintenance task lists and log templates for EQ-P1-L1-RR01; operator shift handover checklists that include bearing condition notes; lubrication consumption and inventory records; oil analysis sampling schedule records used for trend tracking. See related documents ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for prior condition assessments and supporting analysis, and SOP-P1-L1-02 for operating interface and handover requirements.

Implementation
- New requirement: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. This interval supersedes prior informal practice and becomes the controlled interval to be recorded in maintenance execution and equipment history records.
- Tasks and responsibilities:
  - Maintenance planners: Update the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) task for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to reflect the new interval. Ensure work order templates include fields for lubricant type, quantity added, sight/level confirmation, and initial oil cleanliness check result.
  - Maintenance technicians: Perform lubrication per the updated work order. Record lubricant batch identifier, amount added, and any abnormal findings. Attach an oil sample label when contamination is suspected and route sample to the laboratory per existing sampling protocol in SOP-P1-L1-02.
  - Operators: Perform pre-lubrication checks at shift handover and log any visible leaks, unusual noise, or temperature anomalies to the maintenance queue as required by SOP-P1-L1-02.
  - Reliability engineers: Monitor trend data after implementation, comparing vibration and oil analysis results against pre-change baseline from ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040. Provide a summary of trend performance at the next scheduled review.
- Procedure details and examples:
  - Use approved lubricant specified in the current equipment lubrication matrix; confirm compatibility with reservoir and seals before addition. If label or batch is unclear, escalate to the reliability engineer.
  - Example record entries: work order reference, technician initials, main roll bearing lubrication interval confirmation (entered as 120 hours), lubricant batch ID, liters added, and oil sample taken Y/N. Maintain a physical copy of the work order on the equipment maintenance binder for shift access and attach the electronic record in the CMMS.
  - Sampling: When oil appears discolored or particle counts exceed guideline threshold, collect a routed sample and reference ECN-2026-034 for prior sample context. Mark sample with equipment id EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and work order reference.
- Training and communication:
  - Conduct a focused briefing with maintenance and operations covering the new interval, recording expectations, and escalation paths. Use SOP-P1-L1-02 as the operator interface reference for shift responsibilities.
  - Post visible change notices at the equipment and in the maintenance office summarizing the new lubrication requirement and referencing this document and related documents ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for background.

Records to keep
- Maintain work order copies and CMMS entries showing lubrication performed at the new interval for EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Records should include lubricant batch IDs and any abnormal findings.
- Preserve oil analysis results and trend charts used to justify the interval, referencing the prior notices ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for continuity.
- Training attendance logs and signed acknowledgements from personnel briefed on the change, retained according to document control practice.

Approvals
- Approval chain must include maintenance manager, reliability engineer, operations supervisor, and document control. Approvers shall reference this ECN id in approval records and ensure CMMS entries are updated after approval.
- Post-implementation review: Reliability engineering to perform a review of lubricant consumption and condition trends after a sustained period of lubrication at the specified interval and provide recommendations for further adjustment if necessary. Refer to ECN-2026-034 and ECN-2026-040 for comparative analysis and SOP-P1-L1-02 for operator interaction during review cycles.
title: Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

# ECN-2026-026 Change notice - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3 (plant)  
Line: P3-L4 (line)  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03 (equipment)

Related documents: MM-P3-L4-SB03, SOP-P3-L4-03, SOP-P3-L4-05

Reason for change
- Background: Preventative maintenance and production feedback identified accelerated wear and lubricant contamination pathways in Heat Treat shot blast cabinet number three, EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Inspection findings and maintenance records showed recurrent bearing and seal degradation linked to lubricant selection and application practice. The change clarifies the approved lubricant, updates lubrication application method, and formalizes records and verification steps to reduce unscheduled downtime and extend component life.
- Root cause summary: Investigation determined the existing field-applied lubricants in use were inconsistent with vendor recommendations for the cabinet drive bearings and were permitting airborne media carryover into lubrication points. Additionally, application practice did not ensure complete coverage of serviceable points and left residue that trapped abrasive material. Corrective action requires a controlled lubricant specification, revised lubrication procedure, and verification by maintenance checks described here.
- Objective: Standardize lubricant to CFW-LUB-526 (part number) for all lubrication points specified for EQ-P3-L4-SB03, update relevant SOPs, and implement inspection and recording steps to demonstrate compliance and efficacy.

Affected items
- Equipment scope: EQ-P3-L4-SB03 main turbine blast wheel bearings, pivot points, and accessible gear interfaces that currently accept non-sealed grease fittings as identified in MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Documentation: This ECN modifies maintenance and operations practice by directing amendments to MM-P3-L4-SB03 and the following operating procedures: SOP-P3-L4-03 and SOP-P3-L4-05. These documents shall be updated to reference CFW-LUB-526 (part number) and the new application method.
- Consumables: All future purchases and on-site spares for lubricants to be listed and stocked as CFW-LUB-526 (part number). Existing stocks not labeled as CFW-LUB-526 must be quarantined and dispositioned per stores policy prior to their use on EQ-P3-L4-SB03.
- Personnel: Maintenance technicians assigned to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and shift leads in P3-L4 shall be trained on the revised SOP content and sign acknowledgement forms retained with the maintenance records.

Implementation
- Specification change: Effective upon approval of this ECN, CFW-LUB-526 (part number) is the only approved lubricant for the specified lubrication points on EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Procurement, stores, and maintenance supervisors will update master parts lists and work orders to reflect this change.
- Procedure revision: Update SOP-P3-L4-03 and SOP-P3-L4-05 to include:
  - Explicit identification of each lubrication point on EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and the recommended application quantity phraseology for technicians.
  - Pre-application cleaning steps to remove trapped abrasive material and old lubricant residues.
  - Acceptance criteria for completed lubrication (visual and tactile).
  - Use of clean dispensing tools and dedicated application containers to minimize contamination risk.
  - Steps for returning replaced parts to inspection when required by MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Training and roll-out: Conduct a training session for maintenance and operations staff on the revisions to SOP-P3-L4-03 and SOP-P3-L4-05 and on the handling and application of CFW-LUB-526 (part number). Attendance rosters and signed acknowledgements will be retained by the maintenance supervisor.
- Example application scenario: During scheduled preventive maintenance for EQ-P3-L4-SB03, technicians shall:
  - Isolate the cabinet, follow lockout procedures, and remove guards to expose lubrication points.
  - Clean each fitting area per the revised SOP, apply CFW-LUB-526 (part number) using a clean dispenser, wipe excess, and record completion in the maintenance log as specified by MM-P3-L4-SB03.
  - Where evidence of media intrusion is found, document as a nonconformance and follow corrective steps in MM-P3-L4-SB03 before returning the equipment to service.
- Verification and monitoring: Post-implementation, maintenance leadership will perform verification audits of lubrication logs and physical inspections on EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Audit frequency and specific checklist items will be appended to MM-P3-L4-SB03 to ensure consistent verification against the new standard.
- Inventory control: Stores will flag existing lubricant inventory that does not match CFW-LUB-526 (part number) and will not release nonconforming items for use on EQ-P3-L4-SB03. A reconciliation record of existing stocks shall be maintained and attached to the purchase order history.

Records to keep
- Updated MM-P3-L4-SB03, SOP-P3-L4-03, and SOP-P3-L4-05, with revision notes indicating this ECN.
- Training attendance rosters and signed acknowledgement forms for personnel trained on the new lubricant and procedures.

text:
# ECN-2026-027 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: During recent production observations and predictive maintenance reviews, the induction billet heater designated EQ-P3-L1-IH03 exhibited intermittent temperature control excursions that tracked to variations in coil cooling water flow. The current maintenance and operating guidance did not specify a measurable minimum flow value for continuous safe operation of the coil assembly. To eliminate ambiguity in operator response and maintenance thresholds, this change establishes a firm minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Purpose: Set a clear minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 to prevent coil overheating, reduce unscheduled downtime, and align operator actions with maintenance acceptance criteria. This change clarifies responsibilities, the threshold that triggers operator intervention, and the acceptance criteria for returning the heater to service following a flow alert.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03 — coil assembly and associated cooling water circuit.  
- Procedures: Update SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03, and SOP-P3-L1-05 to incorporate the new minimum coil cooling water flow requirement, associated alarm conditions, and restart checks. Each cited SOP must be revised to reference the new ECN and to include the flow minimum as an operating parameter.
- Training: Operations and maintenance personnel assigned to P3-L1 who interact with EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must receive a revision briefing and demonstration of required checks and records.
- Spare parts and inspection checklists: Inspection checklists for coil cooling circuit verification must be updated to include the flow confirmation step and acceptance criteria tied to this ECN.

Implementation
- New operating requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This value is the operational lower limit; operation below this value is not permitted unless supervised shutdown or controlled cooldown is in effect.
- Alarm and interlock behavior: Configure local display and control logic to clearly show current flow status and produce a visible alarm when flow is below the stated minimum. Where control logic prevents heater power application below the threshold, document the conditions that allow manual override for controlled cooldown, per SOP updates.
- Operator actions on alarm:
  - Immediately take the heater to a safe hold condition following the steps specified in the revised SOPs. Confirm the cause of low flow by checking upstream valve positions, visible leaks, and pump status as described in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.
  - If flow recovers to at least the stated minimum and there is no indication of coil damage or abnormal electrical signatures, follow the restart checklist in SOP-P3-L1-05 before returning the heater to full production service.
- Maintenance response:
  - If flow does not recover to the stated minimum after basic operator checks, initiate maintenance troubleshooting for the cooling circuit, including pump capacity verification, strainer inspection, and sensor calibration as relevant. Record observations and corrective actions in the equipment maintenance history.
  - Before returning the heater to production after corrective action, perform a coil visual inspection and verify flow stability at or above the stated minimum while monitoring the heater for normal electrical behavior.
- Examples:
  - Example scenario A: During batch ramp, local display indicates flow below the minimum. Operator follows SOP-P3-L1-02 steps, isolates heater power per procedure, confirms a partially blocked strainer, cleans the strainer, verifies flow restored to the stated minimum, and completes restart per SOP-P3-L1-05.
  - Example scenario B: Flow alarm persists; operator escalates to maintenance. Maintenance identifies a failing circulation pump, replaces the component, verifies flow at or above the stated minimum, and documents repair before restart.
- Records to keep:
  - Alarm log entry for any flow alarm event that includes timestamp, observed flow value, operator steps taken, and outcome. Include the phrase "coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min" in the event narrative.
  - Maintenance work order documenting troubleshooting steps, parts used, corrective actions, and verification that flow meets or exceeds the stated minimum prior to closure.
  - Restart checklist completion record per SOP-P3-L1-05, including signed acknowledgement by operations and maintenance personnel verifying that the stated minimum is met and that no coil damage is suspected.
  - Training attendance records for personnel briefed on this ECN and the updated SOP content.
- Documentation updates:
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-02 to include detection, operator immediate actions, and logging requirements tied to the stated minimum.
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-03 to include maintenance troubleshooting steps and acceptance criteria referencing the stated minimum.
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-05 to include the restart acceptance checklist and requirement to verify the stated minimum before full power application.
  - Append this ECN to the equipment file for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and include cross-reference entries in the affected SOPs.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Required before procedural changes are published and before control logic updates are implemented.
- Operations approval: Required for procedural acceptance and training closure for P3-L1 operators.
- Maintenance approval: Required for any control logic or hardware changes and for maintenance procedure updates.
- Document control: Upon approval, this ECN will be released to the controlled document system and referenced in SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03, and SOP-P3-L1-05.

Notes
- This ECN does not change any other equipment setpoints or introduce new hardware beyond required sensors or indicators to enforce and display the stated minimum. All implementation steps must be carried out in coordination with affected stakeholders and in accordance with applicable safety and lockout/tagout practices described in the referenced SOPs.
title: Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

text:
# ECN-2026-028 Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Related documents: MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, SOP-P2-L2-01

Reason for change
This engineering change notice is issued to document and formalize an adjustment to the quench delay control logic for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). Field incident reports and subsequent investigation identified inconsistent quench initiation during parts handling transitions, producing variability in hardness outcomes and increasing rework rates on affected ring geometries. Root cause analysis determined the control sequence allowed the quench actuator to engage before the part verified position and after a variable operator hold, producing an inconsistent hold-to-quench interval.

Corrective action requires a definitive, measurable limit on the allowable delay between the verified part ready state and initiation of the quench operation in the furnace control program. The new control parameter will reduce process variability, align equipment behavior with metallurgical expectations, and reduce rework and scrap.

The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

Affected items
- Control program parameter on EQ-P2-L2-HT02 that governs delay from part ready confirmation to quench initiation.
- Associated human-machine interface screens and operator guidance that reference the previous unspecified delay behavior.
- Maintenance checklists and preventive maintenance tasks that reference quench timing in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.
- Standard operating procedure steps in SOP-P2-L2-01 that describe the quench sequence and operator confirmations.

Affected stakeholders: production operators for line P2-L2, furnace maintenance technicians, process engineering, quality assurance, and metallurgical engineering. The change applies to in-process lots currently staged for processing in EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and to all future production until superseded by another controlled change.

Implementation
Scope
Implement the updated quench delay parameter in the PLC and furnace controller for EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Update operator interface text to display current measured delay and an alert when delay approaches the limit. Revise maintenance and SOP documentation to reference the new maximum delay requirement and to provide steps for verification and corrective action.

Steps
- Modify controller parameter: set the quench delay limit in the control program to the value specified above. Ensure limit is enforced as a hard constraint so that quench initiation is inhibited if the delay exceeds the limit until manual override is authorized and logged.
- Update HMI: add a visible indicator showing the real-time measured delay for each cycle and a status flag that transitions to alarm state when the measured delay reaches a threshold indicative of imminent violation.
- Update MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1: add a procedural check entry to verify the quench delay parameter and HMI indicator during functional checks. Reference the new limit explicitly in the maintenance steps so that calibrations and diagnostic tests validate the control logic.
- Update SOP-P2-L2-01: revise the operator sequencing description to include the requirement to observe the HMI delay indicator and to follow the documented steps if the indicator reports a delay approaching or exceeding the allowed maximum. Include guidance on permissible use of documented override procedures and subsequent verification steps.
- Commissioning and validation: conduct a controlled validation run sequence to demonstrate that the controller enforces the quench delay limit under typical loading and handling conditions. Record measured delay values and corresponding part hardness or process monitor outputs as evidence of compliant operation.
- Training: deliver an operator and maintenance briefing covering the change rationale, how to read the HMI delay indicator, the required actions when an alarm occurs, and reporting expectations. Training records will be retained in accordance with plant practice.

Examples and rationale
Example scenarios are provided to clarify expected behavior:
- Where a normal pick-and-place cycle results in timely verification of part readiness, measured delay should remain well below the limit. The controller permits automatic quench initiation and the batch proceeds without intervention.
- If a handling anomaly or test hold causes delay near the allowable maximum, the HMI indicator will show the approaching limit and the operator will be required to follow the procedural steps in SOP-P2-L2-01, including pausing further cycles and notifying maintenance if the condition repeats.
- If the delay exceeds the limit, the controller will inhibit automatic quench initiation. The operator will follow documented override and verification steps, and a maintenance ticket will be generated to investigate mechanical or sensor faults.

Records to keep
Maintain records of:
- Controller configuration change log for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 showing the parameter update and the implementing engineer.
- Commissioning validation records including measured delay traces and companion process data that demonstrate compliance to the maximum delay requirement.
- HMI alarm logs and any manual override entries related to quench delay events.
- Updated maintenance checklists and signoffs in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 showing completed verification steps.
- Operator training attendance and acknowledgement that SOP-P2-L2-01 revisions were reviewed.

Approvals
Approval of this change requires signoff from process engineering, maintenance management, operations management for line P2-L2, and quality assurance. Upon approval, the change will be implemented and the related documents MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-01 will be revision-controlled to reflect the required updates.
title: Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2
