# ECN-2026-029 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Reason for change
- Background: During routine review of process capability and furnace performance logs, machining downstream feedback indicated variability in billet hardening and surface finish attributed to inconsistent feed temperature at the machining cell. Analysis of heater control logs and metallurgical reports identified that the setpoint for the induction billet heater did not match the metallurgical profile used for forging and machining acceptance. To align the thermal input with metallurgical specification and reduce rework, the heater setpoint is being standardized.
- Objective: Establish a verified target billet temperature for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to reduce process variability, improve dimensional stability at machining, and reduce downstream scrap and rework events.
- Change statement: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. This replaces the previous undocumented practice of operator-adjusted setpoints and moves the setting into controlled documentation and automated control limits.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01 (Machining induction billet heater #1) control setpoint and associated control logic parameters.
- Process: Billet feed into P1-L3 machining cell, heat soak and transfer procedures upstream of machining operations.
- Procedures and records: SOP-P1-L3-01, SOP-P1-L3-02 require revision to capture the new target temperature, verification steps, and acceptance criteria. Training records and calibration logs associated with EQ-P1-L3-IH01 must be updated.
- Materials: Billets processed for the P1-L3 line while EQ-P1-L3-IH01 is operating under the new setpoint; traceability records must reference the setpoint change for affected production lots.

Implementation
- Control change: Update the control system setpoint for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to the specified target. Configure the heater control profile such that the billet temperature at transfer is validated against the target. Logging must capture setpoint, measured billet temperature, and operator acknowledgement on each charge.
- Procedure updates: Revise SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 to include:
  - The target billet temperature for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 is 1235 °C as the required setpoint for billets entering the machining cell.
  - Pre-transfer verification method and acceptable variance description (refer to metallurgical acceptance criteria in related documentation).
  - Operator steps for initiating the controlled setpoint, monitoring temperature, and recording the measured value in the production log.
  - Escalation and hold procedures when measured temperature does not meet the documented acceptance criteria.
- Verification and validation: Prior to full production use, perform a controlled validation run with documented measurements demonstrating stable approach to the target temperature and consistent transfer temperature at the machining interface. Document metallurgical test results and machining sample inspections to demonstrate reduced variability.
- Training: Conduct targeted training for operations and maintenance personnel covering:
  - Rationale for the setpoint change and expected impact on machining quality.
  - How to engage the updated control logic for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
  - Required logging and deviation reporting steps per the updated SOPs.
  - Maintenance response for control alarms related to temperature deviation.
- Maintenance and calibration: Ensure temperature sensors and control loops associated with EQ-P1-L3-IH01 are within calibration and that any drift is corrected before adoption. Record sensor calibration status in equipment maintenance records.
- Records to keep:
  - Control system change log documenting the setpoint change entry for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 and approval traceability.
  - Validation run report including measured billet temperatures, process conditions, and machining inspection results.
  - Revised SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 versions showing incorporation of the target temperature and new verification steps.
  - Training sign-off sheets for all affected operators and maintenance staff.
  - Production logs showing ongoing compliance with the target billet temperature for each shift or charge as required by the revised SOPs.
  - Any deviation reports and corrective action records if billets are processed outside the acceptance window.
- Examples:
  - Example entry in the production log must show the equipment id, the setpoint reference, measured billet temperature at transfer, and operator initials as required by the revised SOPs.
  - Example validation documentation should include metallurgical sample id, measured hardness or microstructure notes, and reference to the production lot processed under the new setpoint.

Approvals
- Engineering: Approval required for configuration changes to the heater control logic and for acceptance of validation test results.
- Operations: Approval required to update SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 and to commence production under the new target.
- Quality: Approval required for metallurgical acceptance criteria and sign-off on validation demonstrating reduced variability at machining.
- Maintenance: Approval required to confirm calibration and readiness of sensors and actuators before change implementation.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-022
- SOP-P1-L3-01
- SOP-P1-L3-02

Change authority and sign-off dates must be recorded in the document control system with references to the above related documents. All implementation actions shall be tracked against the approvals listed and retained in the permanent engineering change record for audit and continuous improvement purposes.
title: Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

# ECN-2026-030 - Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

Related documents: MM-P1-L3-HP02, SB-1029, SOP-P1-L3-01

Reason for change
This engineering change notice updates the specified lubricant for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) and clarifies maintenance and recordkeeping actions required during transition and after implementation. The existing lubrication practice has produced inconsistent replenishment documentation and occasional pump inlet cavitation events traced to a mismatch between lubricant packaging and plant dispensing method. The change standardizes the lubricant to a single approved part number to improve supply chain clarity, reduce cross-contamination risk, and simplify maintenance procedures. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497.

Background and technical rationale
EQ-P1-L3-HP02 is a high-duty hydraulic forging press used on line P1-L3 for machining operations. Maintenance records reviewed under MM-P1-L3-HP02 and corrective maintenance reports referenced in SB-1029 showed multiple instances where field personnel used alternate lubricants from general floor stock when the original dispensing container was not immediately available. Laboratory viscosity checks associated with those incidents indicated variance from specification limits documented in SOP-P1-L3-01. Those variances correlated with transient performance issues and increased housekeeping for hydraulic filtration.

Standardizing to CFW-LUB-497 addresses three primary issues:
- Single-source identification: Use of a unique plant lubricant part number reduces misidentification and accidental substitution.
- Packaging compatibility: CFW-LUB-497 is supplied in containers compatible with the existing dispensing hardware used for EQ-P1-L3-HP02, eliminating occasional transfer contamination.
- Maintenance clarity: Maintenance procedures in SOP-P1-L3-01 can reference CFW-LUB-497 directly, removing ambiguous instructions that previously allowed alternative products.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02 — lubrication circuit, reservoir top-up procedures, and associated filtration changeover tasks.
- Documentation: MM-P1-L3-HP02 maintenance master record — update lubricant field and replenishment instructions; SOP-P1-L3-01 — update lubrication section to reference CFW-LUB-497 and describe approved handling steps; SB-1029 — include a reference to revised approval rationale where SB-1029 records the laboratory testing that supported initial lubricant selection.
- Spares and consumables: All active stock locations supplying EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must transition to using only CFW-LUB-497 for top-up and reservoir replacement activities. Any legacy lubricant stock identified for this press must be quarantined and dispositioned per existing stock control processes.

Implementation
Phased implementation will be executed in coordinated maintenance windows to avoid production disruption. Implementation steps:
- Inventory review: Conduct a physical inventory of lubricants currently assigned to line P1-L3 storerooms servicing EQ-P1-L3-HP02. Quarantine any units not bearing the part number CFW-LUB-497 and tag per inventory control procedures. Record inventory actions in the MM-P1-L3-HP02 log.
- Procurement and supply: Place supply orders to ensure a common supply of CFW-LUB-497 is available at primary and secondary storerooms serving P1-L3 before field changeover. Receive and verify shipments against part number CFW-LUB-497.
- Training and procedure update: Revise SOP-P1-L3-01 lubrication steps to reference CFW-LUB-497 explicitly and to add handling notes for container compatibility. Conduct a toolbox session for operators and maintenance staff assigned to EQ-P1-L3-HP02. Training attendance and acknowledgement will be recorded and appended to the maintenance file for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
- Changeover activity: Scheduled maintenance personnel will drain and replace residual lubricant in EQ-P1-L3-HP02 reservoirs following the sequence in SOP-P1-L3-01, now updated to cite CFW-LUB-497. During changeover, filtration elements will be inspected and replaced if contamination is present. All replacement actions and serial identifiers for filters (where applicable) will be logged in MM-P1-L3-HP02.
- Verification: Post-changeover performance verification will follow the acceptance checks outlined in MM-P1-L3-HP02. Any deviations observed will be recorded and referenced against SB-1029 laboratory testing guidance for troubleshooting.
- Disposal: Residual stock of legacy lubricants removed from service for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 will be handled under normal waste and reclamation procedures and documented in the maintenance file.

Records to keep
- MM-P1-L3-HP02: Update entries to show lubricant part number CFW-LUB-497 for EQ-P1-L3-HP02 and log all physical inventory adjustments, changeover actions, filter replacements, and post-changeover verification results.
- SOP-P1-L3-01: Maintain a revision note indicating the change to CFW-LUB-497 and include a record of training session attendance and acknowledgements.
- SB-1029: Retain laboratory reports and test data used during selection and verification, and append notes explaining how SB-1029 test criteria informed acceptance thresholds used in MM-P1-L3-HP02 checks.
- Quarantine records: Maintain tags and disposition forms for any removed or obsolete lubricant stock originally intended for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.

Examples and expected outcomes
- Example entry for MM-P1-L3-HP02: “Lubricant top-up material: CFW-LUB-497 installed; filter inspected and replaced; post-fill checks nominal per SOP-P1-L3-01.” Such entries will standardize future troubleshooting and audit trails.
- Expected performance: Reduction in mis-lubrication incidents and clearer supply chain traceability for lubrication of EQ-P1-L3-HP02. Improved alignment between field practice and the technical acceptance criteria referenced in SB-1029.

Approvals
Signatures and approval routing will follow standard plant change control. Approval records will be filed with MM-P1-L3-HP02 and a copy appended to SOP-P1-L3-01 revision history. Approval routing includes maintenance supervision, engineering lead for line P1-L3, and plant operations authorization.

Related documents for reference
MM-P1-L3-HP02  
SB-1029  
SOP-P1-L3-01

Lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02): CFW-LUB-497
title: Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

text:
# ECN-2026-031 Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Reason for change
- Background: During routine operation and post-implementation review of the previous control update (see ECN-2026-028) operators and maintenance noted inconsistent quench initiation timing on EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Analysis of event logs and furnace control sequences found variable delay between the quench command and actual quench start that could exceed acceptable process variability limits for ring rolling heat treat cycles.
- Purpose: The change standardizes the maximum allowable delay between quench command and quench initiation for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 to ensure repeatable metallurgical outcomes and reduce rework. The updated maximum quench delay value is set to 16 seconds. This is a process control limit required to maintain hardness and microstructure results within the established acceptance criteria referenced in QS-PROC-08.
- Rationale: Consistent quench timing is critical for ring rolling forgings to achieve target mechanical properties. The furnace control hardware and the quench system response have adequate capability to meet a stricter maximum delay; formalizing the limit and updating procedures eliminates ambiguity in operator response and maintenance diagnosis.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02 control logic and operator guidance are affected. Physical hardware requiring inspection is the quench actuation circuit and associated interlocks as identified in MM-P2-L2-HT02.
- Documents: Update MM-P2-L2-HT02 maintenance checklist and procedures to include verification steps for the new quench delay limit and record-keeping requirements. Update operator work instructions under the P2 line to include the 16 seconds quench delay maximum and related monitoring actions. Ensure QS-PROC-08 references the revised operational control verification for EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Training: Operators and maintenance personnel assigned to P2-L2 must be notified and trained on the change. Training shall cover the impact of quench delay on product quality, how to monitor and record quench timing, and escalation steps if the limit is exceeded.

Implementation
- Control change: Modify EQ-P2-L2-HT02 PLC sequence to implement a hard alarm when measured delay from command to quench initiation exceeds 16 seconds. The sequence change will also log the measured delay value in the furnace event log for each heat treat cycle.
- Operator procedure updates: Revise the furnace start-up and cycle monitoring checklist to require the operator to verify quench initiation within the 16 seconds maximum after the quench command is issued. If the alarm occurs, the operator will follow the escalation steps defined in MM-P2-L2-HT02 and notify maintenance per plant communication protocol.
- Maintenance actions: Add an item to MM-P2-L2-HT02 requiring verification of quench actuator response time during scheduled maintenance and after any control changes or actuator repairs. Maintenance records must include the measured response verification outcome and any corrective actions taken.
- Example scenarios:
  - Normal cycle: Operator issues quench command; PLC measures delay and logs value; no alarm if value is within 16 seconds; record entry appended to the cycle log.
  - Alarmed cycle: PLC measures delay greater than 16 seconds; system generates alarm, logs the delay value and timestamp, and inhibits loading of subsequent work until maintenance review is completed per MM-P2-L2-HT02. Operations will quarantine affected parts per QS-PROC-08 until disposition.
- Records to keep:
  - Furnace cycle log entries containing measured quench delay and outcome for each cycle.
  - Maintenance verification records from MM-P2-L2-HT02 showing quench actuator response checks and corrective actions.
  - Training attendance and competency acknowledgment for operators and maintenance staff covering the new 16 seconds maximum quench delay requirement.
  - Nonconformance records and dispositions processed under QS-PROC-08 for any parts impacted by quench delay exceedance.
- Timing and coordination: Implementation will be coordinated between process engineering, controls, operations, and maintenance to minimize production disruption. Changes to PLC code and MM-P2-L2-HT02 documentation shall be version controlled and tested in a controlled environment before deployment to EQ-P2-L2-HT02.

Approvals
- Required approvals: Process Engineering, Controls Engineering, Maintenance Management, Quality Assurance, and Operations Management must review and sign off on the change prior to deployment.
- Quality review: QA will confirm the change documents cross-reference QS-PROC-08 and that the 16 seconds maximum quench delay is reflected in inspection and disposition workflows.
- Post-implementation review: After deployment, a follow-up review will examine furnace cycle logs and maintenance verification records for at least one production run to confirm compliance with the 16 seconds limit and evaluate any residual process variability. Findings will be documented and, if necessary, addressed via subsequent ECN referencing ECN-2026-028.
- Related documents: This change implements and references maintenance and procedure updates in MM-P2-L2-HT02, follows the corrective thread begun under ECN-2026-028, and aligns with quality handling per QS-PROC-08.

Distribution list and records retention
- Distribution: Process Engineering, Controls, Maintenance, Operations P2-L2, Quality Assurance.
- Retention: All records related to this change including PLC change logs, furnace cycle delay logs, maintenance verification, and QA dispositions will be retained per plant records practice and made available to Quality and external auditors upon request.

End of notice.
title: Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

text:
# ECN-2026-032 - Change notice - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

Reason for change
- Background: During a recent review of maintenance and measurement accuracy for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02), traceability gaps were identified between field calibration activities and the calibration records retained in the document control system. Field technicians reported inconsistent reminder scheduling for thermocouple calibrations; maintenance work orders referenced different intervals across MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1. The inconsistency increases risk of out-of-tolerance thermocouples being used in production, which can affect furnace control and part quality.
- Purpose: Standardize the thermocouple calibration interval and the procedural flow for scheduling, performing, and recording calibrations on EQ-P2-L2-HT02 to ensure measurement integrity and audit readiness.
- Rationale: A single, documented calibration interval removes ambiguity for maintenance scheduling, improves consistency of measurements used by furnace control systems, and streamlines records management. Aligning the work instructions and maintenance task lists reduces duplicate entries and missed calibrations.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02 (Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2) — applies to all thermocouples installed on the equipment control loops and any portable thermocouple probes used for verification on this asset.
- Procedures and maintenance documents: MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, SOP-P2-L2-04 are to be updated to reflect the revised calibration control flow and the standardized thermocouple calibration interval.
- Records: Calibration certificates, maintenance task completion records, calibration reminder logs, and calibration verification checklists associated with EQ-P2-L2-HT02.

Change detail and implementation
- Specification update: The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 40 days. This interval is the required scheduling cadence for all calibrated thermocouples assigned to EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and is to be entered verbatim into maintenance planning systems and checklists.
- Procedure alignment:
  - MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 will be revised to contain a single, clear maintenance task item specifying the calibration interval as 40 days for thermocouples used on EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Task descriptions will include acceptance criteria, required tools, and the referenced calibration method in SOP-P2-L2-04.
  - SOP-P2-L2-04 will be updated to include the method for performing thermocouple calibration checks for EQ-P2-L2-HT02, references to the calibration interval of 40 days, and the documentation requirements listed below.
- Scheduling and notification:
  - Maintenance planners shall schedule thermocouple calibration tasks for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 to occur with the cadence of 40 days, using the electronic maintenance system. Work orders must cite MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 as the controlling maintenance procedures and SOP-P2-L2-04 as the calibration method.
- Execution steps (summary):
  - Verify identity of the thermocouple or probe against the equipment tag on EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
  - Perform calibration per SOP-P2-L2-04. Use the acceptance criteria in MM-P2-L2-HT02.
  - If the thermocouple passes, complete the calibration certificate and upload to the calibration database, citing the calibration interval of 40 days and referencing MM-P2-L2-HT02.
  - If the thermocouple fails, follow the disposition steps in MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 and initiate replacement or rework. Record the nonconformance and the corrective action taken.
- Examples:
  - Example maintenance task entry: "Thermocouple calibration – EQ-P2-L2-HT02 – Interval: 40 days – Procedure: MM-P2-L2-HT02 – Method: SOP-P2-L2-04."
  - Example record notation: "Calibration result: PASS; Interval cited: 40 days; Source procedure: MM-P2-L2-HT02; Method: SOP-P2-L2-04."
- Records to keep:
  - Calibration certificates for each thermocouple on EQ-P2-L2-HT02, with explicit notation that the thermocouple calibration interval is 40 days.
  - Maintenance work order completion records that reference MM-P2-L2-HT02 and MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 as applicable.
  - Calibration reminder log or maintenance system task history showing scheduled and completed calibrations at the 40 days cadence.
  - Any nonconformance reports and corrective actions arising from failed calibrations, with linkage to the replacement part record for the thermocouple.
  - Signed review of procedure updates indicating the incorporation of the 40 days calibration interval into MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-04.

Transition plan and verification
- Effective implementation requires updates to the three cited documents. Document revisions will be issued to maintenance and operations prior to enforcement.
- A transitional audit will be performed after the first full cycle post-implementation to verify that scheduled tasks reflect the calibration interval of 40 days and that records are being completed and uploaded as specified.
- Any deviations discovered during the transition audit will trigger a corrective action referenced to MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1.

Approvals
- Approval signatures shall be recorded on this ECN and retained in the document control system. The approval package shall include confirmation that MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-04 have been updated to reflect the thermocouple calibration interval of 40 days and that training notices have been distributed to affected staff.
- Required approvers will include maintenance management, quality assurance, and the asset owner for EQ-P2-L2-HT02. Approved copies of the revised MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-04 must be attached to the ECN record.

Change control notes
- Do not alter the calibration interval for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 outside of an approved ECN. Any request to change the thermocouple calibration interval must reference this ECN and provide justification, impact assessment, and updated procedural text for MM-P2-L2-HT02, MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1, and SOP-P2-L2-04.
- Retain all prior calibration records for audit traceability and include cross-reference to this ECN in the file index.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L2-HT02
- MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1
- SOP-P2-L2-04

# ECN-2026-033 - Change notice - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and review of shot media consumption records for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 at Plant P2 line P2-L1, operations staff and maintenance engineering identified inconsistent media replenishment timing that contributed to variations in blast cleaning performance and nonconforming surface finish results. The existing replenishment practice relied on manual timing and operator judgment, which did not provide a consistent media condition for the downstream hot forge process.
- Purpose: To establish a consistent, auditable top-up interval for shot media in the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 to stabilize cleaning performance, reduce rework, and align maintenance activities with documented procedures. This change supports quality and process stability objectives and reduces reliance on ad hoc operator decisions.
- Rationale: Standardizing the top-up interval reduces variability in media size distribution and contamination levels entering the blast cabinet. A defined interval enables predictable inventory usage, clearer shift handover communication, and measurable maintenance workload. The selected interval is based on review of media consumption patterns, production duty cycle, and coordination with related procedures contained in SB-1031, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-04.

Affected items
- Equipment scope: This notice applies to Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3, identified as EQ-P2-L1-SB03, installed on P2, line P2-L1.
- Procedures and training: Existing operating and maintenance practices that reference media handling for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 shall be updated to reflect the specified top-up interval and associated recordkeeping. Referenced documents to be updated or consulted include SB-1031, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-04.
- Documentation: Work orders, maintenance logs, and process control checklists associated with EQ-P2-L1-SB03 shall include a field for media top-up events and media condition notes.
- Inventory and supply: Shot media supply procedures that service EQ-P2-L1-SB03 must account for the new interval so inventory planners can align supply deliveries and storehouse allocations accordingly.

Implementation
- New top-up interval: The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. This interval is the required cadence for adding shot media to maintain target media condition. Each top-up event must be recorded in the equipment log described below.
- Action items:
  - Update SOP-P2-L1-01 to include the required top-up interval and a step for completing the media top-up entry in the cabinet log. Cross-reference SB-1031 for acceptable media types and handling precautions.
  - Update SOP-P2-L1-04 to incorporate visual acceptance criteria to be observed at each top-up event and to define escalation steps if media contamination or degradation is detected.
  - Maintenance planners shall schedule media top-up tasks in the computerized maintenance management system for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 to ensure visibility and assignment.
  - Operators responsible for running EQ-P2-L1-SB03 shall be provided brief hands-on training that covers the top-up procedure, log completion, and recognition of media condition anomalies.
- Procedure for top-up event:
  - Verify safety lockout and follow SB-1031 handling precautions before accessing the media hopper.
  - Perform a visual inspection of media condition and document findings on the cabinet log and in the process control checklist referenced in SOP-P2-L1-01.
  - Add media to the hopper to restore the working level as indicated in the equipment setup diagrams; document the addition including time, operator initials, and media source lot identifier.
  - Observe blast performance on a representative workpiece and record any deviations; follow SOP-P2-L1-04 escalation if unacceptable cleaning results occur.
- Examples of documentation entries:
  - Cabinet log entry: time of top-up, operator identification, media lot identifier, visual condition code, observed blast performance note.
  - Maintenance work order note: top-up completed as scheduled, any abnormal observations, and follow-up actions if required.
- Records to keep:
  - The cabinet media log for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 shall be retained with the unit documentation and retained in the digital process log system per record retention policy.
  - All top-up events shall be traceable to a media lot identifier for incoming material traceability.
  - Any deviations or escalations shall be recorded as nonconformance reports and routed per SB-1031 and SOP-P2-L1-04 instructions.
- Monitoring and review:
  - Quality and maintenance leaders shall review media log entries for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 on a routine schedule to confirm adherence to the interval and to identify trends in media consumption or performance that might prompt additional action.
  - If repeated deviations from expected performance are recorded, a targeted investigation will be opened and referenced to this ECN for corrective steps.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Maintenance engineering must sign to acknowledge changes to EQ-P2-L1-SB03 procedures and implementation responsibility.
- Operations approval: Line management for P2-L1 must sign to accept the operational changes and training requirements for operators running EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
- Quality approval: Quality management must sign to confirm the change aligns with inspection and acceptance criteria and that records required by SB-1031, SOP-P2-L1-01, and SOP-P2-L1-04 will be maintained.
- Handover: After approvals, updates to SOP-P2-L1-01 and SOP-P2-L1-04 will be issued and distributed to affected staff and the revision history will reference ECN-2026-033.

Related documents
- SB-1031
- SOP-P2-L1-01
- SOP-P2-L1-04

Record of implementation and approvals will be attached to this ECN and filed in the document control system with the ECN execution notes.

# ECN-2026-034 Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Related documents: SB-1025, SOP-P1-L1-03, SOP-P1-L1-05

## Reason for change

This engineering change notice updates operating and inspection boundaries for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Background: recent production trials and nonconformance reviews identified rings with outer diameters approaching the current practical limits of the mill mechanical envelope and tooling clearances. Analysis of forming results, tooling wear patterns, and handling constraints concluded that a clarified maximum ring outer diameter limit is required to ensure consistent forming quality, protect drive and roll train components, and maintain safe handling practices in the hot forge environment.

The maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 1240 mm. This value is declared as the formal limit for all planning, scheduling, and quality acceptance for rings routed to this piece of equipment. The change is intended to reduce variability in forming, eliminate repeat adjustments that accelerate tooling wear, and align production schedules and handling procedures with documented equipment capability. This also reduces risk of unplanned downtime caused by interference in the roll path or improper handling of oversized blanks.

## Affected items

- EQ-P1-L1-RR01 operating instructions and job setup sheets that reference dimensional limits.  
- Work orders and process routings that assign rings with outer diameters to EQ-P1-L1-RR01.  
- Tooling selection lists and spare parts staging that support roll profiles used near the declared limit.  
- Material handling procedures used for transfer to and from EQ-P1-L1-RR01, including lift planning and ergonomic controls.  
- Quality acceptance criteria and inspection records that verify ring outer diameter prior to roll entry.

Affected process documents to be updated: SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05. Design bulletin SB-1025 should be referenced for engineering constraints and component drawings during any tooling changes or layout adjustments.

Examples of routing impact: rings with nominal outer diameters at or below the declared limit may proceed to EQ-P1-L1-RR01 following SOP-P1-L1-03. Rings with outer diameters beyond the declared limit must be routed to alternative forming assets or require engineering disposition per SB-1025 prior to scheduling.

## Implementation

Scope: enforce maximum outer diameter limit within planning, pre-rolling inspection, setup, and production execution for EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Key implementation steps follow.

- Update process documents: revise SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05 to include the declared maximum ring outer diameter for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and include checklist items for verifying ring outer diameter at incoming inspection. Reference SB-1025 for any required engineering evaluation if a part exceeds the limit.

- Pre-rolling inspection: inspectors shall verify incoming ring outer diameter against the declared maximum prior to release to the mill. Measurement records shall be captured on the job traveler and retained with the work order.

- Job setup and tooling: setup personnel shall confirm tooling selection and roll profiles are compatible with rings at the declared outer diameter. Any tooling degradation observed during initial forming of rings near the declared limit must be documented in the tooling log and reported to maintenance.

- Handling and transfer controls: material handling teams shall follow updated lift and transfer procedures for rings sized at or near the declared limit. Handling checks shall be recorded on the transfer checklist.

- Quality acceptance: final inspection shall verify formed ring outer diameter meets drawing specifications and confirm no damage attributable to exceeding equipment capability. Nonconformances shall be processed per quality procedures with reference to this ECN and SB-1025.

- Training: affected operators, inspectors, schedulers, and maintenance staff shall receive training on the revised SOP content and the declared maximum outer diameter. Training attendance and competency checks shall be recorded in employee training records.

- Scheduling and routing enforcement: production planning shall apply the declared limit as a hard constraint in job assignment tools. Any exception request shall follow an engineering disposition process that references SB-1025.

Records to keep: updated SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05 controlled copies; job traveler measurement records showing incoming outer diameter verification; tooling logs noting any wear or adjustment when processing rings near the declared limit; transfer and handling checklists; training attendance records; engineering disposition records when exceptions are granted referencing SB-1025.

Timeline: changes will be entered into the document control system and distributed to impacted teams. Implementation monitoring will occur for an initial run period to verify compliance and to capture any unforeseen impacts on throughput or tooling life.

## Approvals

Approvals required prior to implementation: operations manager for P1-L1, quality manager, maintenance manager, and the engineering owner listed in SB-1025. Final approval will confirm that SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05 have been revised and that training and record capture mechanisms are in place.

Approval records to be maintained with this ECN: signed approval sheet stored in the document control repository and cross-referenced to the revised SOPs and to SB-1025. Engineering disposition records for any approved exceptions must cite SB-1025 and be filed with the work order and quality records.

Signatures will confirm acceptance of the declared maximum ring outer diameter and that operations, maintenance, and quality are aligned on inspection, handling, and tooling practices for EQ-P1-L1-RR01.

# ECN-2026-035 Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-HP02

## Reason for change
Background: During a recent preventive maintenance review and field inspection of EQ-P1-L3-HP02, an inconsistency in reported ram preload and bolt condition was noted relative to OEM maintenance guidance. The inspection highlighted potential for gradual preload loss at the main ram retention interface that could affect dimensional stability of forged parts and increase wear on mating components. To address this risk and align shop practice with observed field conditions, the bolting requirement for the main ram retention assembly is being formalized and propagated into local procedures.

Root cause rationale: Variability in previous torque application practices, combined with differing interpretations of older documentation, resulted in inconsistent clamping at the main ram. Standardizing the torque to a controlled value reduces variability in clamping force and improves repeatability of ram axial position under load cycles. The controlled torque value complements existing inspection checkpoints and sharpening of procedural references.

Safety and quality drivers: Ensuring consistent clamping at the main ram retention reduces potential for sudden bolt loosening that could compromise operator safety and product dimensional control. This change lowers the likelihood of unplanned disruptions and the need for intrusive corrective maintenance.

Related procedure alignment: The change requires updates and cross-references to local operating procedures SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 to ensure that operating, maintenance, and inspection teams apply the same requirement and recordkeeping practices.

## Affected items
Scope: This change applies to the main ram retention bolting and associated maintenance and inspection steps on EQ-P1-L3-HP02 located at Plant P1, line P1-L3. Affected documents and records include SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P1-L3-05, the PM task list for the press, and the press maintenance log.

Affected personnel: Machining and maintenance technicians who perform torqueing and bolt inspections, shift supervisors who approve maintenance operations, and quality personnel who review process capability records.

Parts and consumables: Existing fasteners used on the main ram retention assembly remain unchanged; however, the approved torque value and the method of application are now mandatory as described in the implementation section.

Performance impact: The change is intended to stabilize ram axial retention and reduce component cyclic fretting. Operators should expect improved dimensional repeatability on forged parts produced by EQ-P1-L3-HP02.

## Implementation
Specified requirement: The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m.

Procedural changes: 
- Update SOP-P1-L3-02 to include a dedicated step for applying and verifying the specified torque during reassembly of the main ram retention. The step must reference the exact applied torque value and specify verification by torque-measuring equipment.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-04 to require a visual and torque-verified check after any operation that requires main ram disassembly or loosening of the retention fasteners. The procedure must require documenting the torque verification result in the equipment maintenance log.
- Update SOP-P1-L3-05 to add an inspection checkpoint during routine press checks that confirms the torque verification entry exists for the most recent maintenance event affecting the main ram retention.

Tooling and measurement: Use calibrated torque application tools capable of applying and recording the specified torque value. Verification may be manual reading from a calibrated torque wrench or electronic capture from a torque tool with data export capability. Calibration status of torque tools must be current and traceable in tool calibration records.

Step-by-step implementation example (high level):
- Prepare press for maintenance following existing lockout procedures as per SOP-P1-L3-04.
- Clean mating surfaces and fastener threads to ensure consistent seating.
- Apply the specified torque to the main ram bolt using an appropriate calibrated torque tool.
- Record the applied torque and tool identifier in the maintenance log entry for the task.
- Perform post-torque inspection for proper seating and absence of thread lubricant contamination that might alter effective torque.
- Resume press operation only after documentation is complete and verified by the shift supervisor.

Training and competency: Technicians assigned to EQ-P1-L3-HP02 must complete a short training brief on the new torque requirement and on proper use of torque-measuring tools. Training records must be retained in the local training file.

Records to keep:
- Maintenance log entries for each main ram retention task that include the applied torque value, technician identifier, torque tool identifier, and calibration sticker/reference.
- Calibration certificates for torque application tools used on EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
- Updated versions of SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 reflecting the change.
- Training completion records for affected technicians.

Verification and follow-up: Post-implementation monitoring will include review of maintenance log entries and a targeted audit of one maintenance event per shift in the first implementation period to confirm compliance with the specified torque requirement and documentation practice. Findings from these audits will feed back into procedural clarification or retraining as required.

## Approvals
Change prepared by: Maintenance engineering for Plant P1, line P1-L3.

Change reviewed by: Production supervision and quality engineering for the machining line.

Change authorized by: Maintenance manager for Plant P1.

Document control: This ECN is to be filed with the equipment maintenance records and linked to SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, and SOP-P1-L3-05 in the document control system.
title: Change notice - Machining hydraulic forging press #2

# ECN-2026-036 Change notice - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Related documents: SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, SOP-P2-L1-05

## Reason for change
This engineering change notice updates the maintenance specification for the blast wheel liner bolt tightening on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03). Field inspection and root cause analysis of recurring liner movement identified that inconsistent bolt preload was a contributing factor to premature liner wear and unexpected wheel imbalance. The change standardizes the bolt torque requirement to ensure consistent clamping force, reduce relative motion between liner and adapter, and improve component life and shot quality.

Key drivers:
- Eliminate variable operator practice observed during service records review.
- Reduce unscheduled downtime associated with liner rework and wheel balancing.
- Align the maintenance instruction with bolted-joint best practice for this assembly.

The approved bolt torque value to be applied to the blast wheel liner bolts on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is 50 N·m. This value supersedes any previous informal guidance and is the new controlled setting for the cabinet.

## Affected items
Primary affected equipment:
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03)

Affected maintenance procedures and records:
- Operation and maintenance activities in SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, and SOP-P2-L1-05 where blast wheel liner removal or reinstallation is performed. Technicians must follow the updated torque requirement when reassembling the liner.

Affected personnel:
- Maintenance technicians assigned to P2, line P2-L1
- Shift supervisors overseeing preventive and corrective maintenance on shot blast equipment
- Quality personnel who verify wheel balance and shot pattern after liner service

Note: No changes are made to any other fasteners, sealing interfaces, or structural components beyond the blast wheel liner bolts for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 under this notice.

## Implementation
Scope
- This ECN mandates application of the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for all maintenance events that involve liner removal and reinstallation on EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Tools and calibration
- Use a calibrated torque wrench appropriate for the head style of the liner bolts. Calibration status must be verified before use per existing calibration program referenced in SOP-P2-L1-03.

Procedure steps (summary)
- Remove access covers per SOP-P2-L1-03 and expose the blast wheel assembly.
- When reinstalling the liner, hand-start bolts to ensure proper thread engagement and alignment.
- Using a calibrated torque wrench, apply the specified torque to each liner bolt. The required setting is 50 N·m.
- Tighten bolts in a crossing pattern to distribute clamp load evenly and minimize liner distortion.
- After torquing, rotate the wheel by hand to verify free rotation and absence of interference.
- Perform a dynamic check of wheel balance and shot distribution per SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05.

Rationale for steps
- Hand-starting and a crossing pattern reduce the risk of cross-threading and uneven clamping, which directly addresses the root cause of liner micro-motion.
- Applying the controlled torque value provides predictable clamping force across assemblies, reducing variation in wear behavior.
- Rotation and dynamic checks verify that the applied torque yields a functional assembly without binding or imbalance.

Examples and nonconformance handling
- Example: If after torquing at 50 N·m the wheel exhibits unusual resistance during manual rotation, do not return the cabinet to service. Tag out the equipment and notify maintenance supervision for inspection. Record findings on the maintenance work order and follow corrective actions documented in SOP-P2-L1-04.
- Example: If a bolt cannot achieve the specified torque due to thread damage or stripped head, replace the affected fastener and associated captive hardware, then apply the specified torque. Record replacement details on the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order showing liner removal/reinstallation and confirming application of the specified torque value of 50 N·m for EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
- Torque wrench calibration certificate or sticker indicating current calibration status used for the task; attach or reference calibration ID per SOP-P2-L1-03.
- Post-service quality verification report documenting wheel rotation check and shot pattern verification performed under SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Any Nonconformance Report created due to inability to achieve the specified torque or detected assembly issues; include disposition and corrective actions taken.

Document updates
- Update the step in SOP-P2-L1-03 that references liner reassembly to cite the new torque requirement for EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
- Add a note in SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05 to reference the torque confirmation as a prerequisite for post-service verification tasks.

Training
- Brief maintenance teams on the change during the next scheduled toolbox meeting. Emphasize the 50 N·m requirement and the importance of using calibrated tools.
- Supervisors to verify the first three applications of the new torque setting on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and sign off on associated records.

## Approvals
Authorized changes under this ECN require sign-off by Maintenance Engineering, Operations, and Quality Assurance. Approval signatures shall be recorded in the ECN approval block and retained with the equipment maintenance file. Once signed, distribute this ECN to maintenance supervisors, shift leads, and the document control system; update SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, and SOP-P2-L1-05 references accordingly.

Document control note
- This ECN becomes the governing instruction for blast wheel liner bolt torque on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and must be referenced in future revisions of the cited SOPs.

# ECN-2026-037 - Change notice - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: During a routine review of machining and securing procedures for the mandrel assembly on Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01), maintenance and reliability teams identified variability in clamp preload and evidence of recurring fastener loosening after heavy machining cycles. Root cause analysis traced the issue to a discrepancy between previously applied clamp bolt torque and the clamping requirement needed to maintain mandrel positional stability under radial load and vibration.
- Objective: Standardize the mandrel clamp bolt tightening requirement and update controlled procedures and records to eliminate preload variability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve part quality and dimensional consistency coming out of EQ-P2-L3-RR01.
- Rationale: A single, specified clamp bolt torque value provides a repeatable preload target, reduces operator interpretation during maintenance, and aligns mechanical joint behavior with design intent. The chosen value balances joint clamp force with bolt yield and joint surface conditions, minimizing risk of fatigue or joint slip while maintaining maintainability.

Affected items
- Equipment: All mandrel clamp assemblies on Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) are affected. This includes the clamp bolts and their associated washers and threaded interfaces as assembled on the mandrel housing.
- Procedures: Existing standard operating procedures that reference mandrel clamp bolt tightening for P2 line radial ring rolling mill machining are affected. See SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 for related process steps and safety precautions that will be updated to reflect the new torque specification.
- Training and skill checks: Operator and maintenance qualifications that verify correct torque application on this mill will be modified to include demonstration to the new requirement.
- Records and logs: Preventive maintenance records, torque calibration records, and post-maintenance inspection checklists that capture mandrel clamp bolt torque will be updated to record the specified value.

Implementation
- New specification: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 470 N·m. This value is to be applied every time the mandrel clamp bolts are installed or re-torqued following disassembly or adjustment.
- Tools and calibration: Use calibrated torque wrenches and, where applicable, calibrated torque multipliers that are within their calibration cycle and traceable to the calibration laboratory. Operators must confirm the calibration sticker or record prior to applying torque. If a torque tool is out of calibration, do not proceed until a compliant tool is provided.
- Application method: Tighten clamp bolts in a controlled, incremental sequence to final torque, observing the manufacturer guidance for even seating of the clamp. After achieving specified torque, perform a verification pass to confirm torque retention. If any bolt does not retain torque, disassemble, inspect the bolt, washer, and threaded interface for damage or contamination, clean and reassemble, and reapply torque.
- Verification and inspection: Post-torque visual inspection of clamp seating and a functional run check of the mandrel assembly should be performed. If abnormal noise, movement, or vibration is observed, stop operation and perform a detailed inspection before resuming machining.
- Procedure updates: Revise SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 to incorporate the new torque value, the required tooling and calibration verification steps, the tightening sequence, the recheck methodology, and the criteria for nonconformance. Each updated SOP must include the exact torque value as shown above and cross-reference this ECN.
- Training: Implement a training brief for affected maintenance and operations staff. Training will cover the reason for the change, the new torque value, correct use of torque tools, and the updated verification steps. Successful completion must be documented in the training record system referenced by plant practice.
- Example scenarios: Provide technicians with realistic examples in the updated SOPs showing how to proceed if a bolt does not hold torque, including steps for inspection, cleaning, replacement of damaged components, and escalation to engineering when thread damage is found that affects clamping integrity.

Records to keep
- Torque application record: For each mandrel clamp bolt operation on EQ-P2-L3-RR01, record the applied torque value, the tool identification and calibration status, the name of the technician, and a statement confirming verification pass. Store this record in the machine maintenance folder and in the electronic maintenance system as required by plant policy.
- Calibration records: Maintain current calibration certificates for all torque tools used on this procedure. Link calibration records to the torque application record.
- Post-maintenance inspection: Keep inspection checklists and any vibration or run data collected after reassembly. If follow-up corrective action was required, attach the corrective action record and root cause notes.
- Training evidence: Document attendance and competency check results for all personnel trained on the new requirement. Include signed or electronically approved training completion evidence.
- SOP revision control: Keep a copy of the updated SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 showing revision history and the ECN reference.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Process engineering must review the change for mechanical integrity implications and accept the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L3-RR01. The engineering review shall include verification that the torque value is compatible with the clamp and bolt specifications on the mill.
- Maintenance approval: Maintenance management is responsible for confirming that tooling, spare parts, and calibration support are in place prior to implementation.
- Operations approval: Line operations management must confirm that the implementation plan is compatible with production scheduling and that trained operators will be available for any planned rework or verification runs.
- Document control: Update the configuration of SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 to reference this ECN and the mandated torque value. Ensure controlled copies are issued and superseded copies are archived.

Disposition and follow-up
- Implement the change after all approvals are recorded and required resources are in place. Monitor the first production runs after implementation for evidence of improved clamp stability and reduced rework or downtime. Capture lessons learned and feed them into continuous improvement channels.
- Reference SOP-P2-L3-01, SOP-P2-L3-02, and SOP-P2-L3-04 for procedural context and for any safety steps that accompany clamp handling and torque application.

# ECN-2026-038 Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Reason for change
- Background: During routine production reviews and cross-checks against process capability targets, the machining induction billet heater identified as EQ-P1-L3-IH01 demonstrated variability in billet surface condition at the machining station. This variability correlated with inconsistent billet thermal profiles entering the machining cell. The intent of this change is to stabilize the billet preheat setpoint used by EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to reduce downstream rework and improve machining tool life.
- Rationale: Analysis of production logs and metallurgical evaluations indicated that maintaining a consistent target billet temperature at the heater exit improves material ductility and dimensional stability during the machining operation. To address the root cause linked to thermal input variation, the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Setting and enforcing this target at the heater control and in associated SOPs will align thermal conditioning with machining requirements and reduce process variability.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01 control parameters and operator interfaces will be revised to reflect the new target billet temperature.
- Procedures: SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 are affected and will be updated to incorporate the new target temperature, adjusted acceptance criteria for incoming billets, and corresponding inspections to be performed by operators and quality technicians.
- Records: Production logs, heater control logs, and quality inspection records generated for billets processed through EQ-P1-L3-IH01 will be appended with a field indicating verification of the target billet temperature. Calibration records for any temperature sensing and control devices associated with EQ-P1-L3-IH01 must reference this change.
- Training: Operators assigned to the P1-L3 line and maintenance technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 will require briefing and competency sign-off on the revised SOPs and the operational implications of the new billet temperature target.

Implementation
- Control setpoint update: Update the heater control setpoint for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to the specified target billet temperature. Ensure the control system displays and logs the active setpoint and the measured billet exit temperature against that setpoint. Where manual verification is included in SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02, revise the checklists to show the required confirmation against the new target.
- Verification method: Use the existing temperature sensors and data acquisition linked to EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to verify that billet exit temperature meets the target billet temperature for each run. Calibration of sensors used for verification must be current and traceable in accordance with plant metrology practices. If the heater control operates with staged power, document how stages are adjusted to achieve the target billet temperature within process capabilities in the revised SOPs.
- Operator actions: Update SOP-P1-L3-01 to include explicit steps for confirming the heater has reached steady state at the new target before releasing billets to the machining station. Include guidance for actions to take when measured billet exit temperature deviates from the target, including hold and notify steps, and criteria for rework or reject per the updated SOPs.
- Maintenance actions: Update SOP-P1-L3-02 to reflect any required adjustments to maintenance checks that influence thermal performance. Specify inspections and acceptance criteria for heater elements, sensor mounting integrity, and insulation integrity that directly affect the ability to achieve the target billet temperature. Include instructions for logging corrective maintenance actions and documenting parts replaced or adjustments made.
- Records and traceability: Modify production log templates to include a field for target verification stating the target billet temperature and the measured value at release. Quality inspection records must capture the measurement method used and the operator or inspector initials. Equipment maintenance records must reference the change notice id and document any alterations to calibration or sensor replacement undertaken to support attainment of the target billet temperature.
- Pilot and rollout: Conduct a pilot run on the applicable shift(s) to validate that the updated target can be achieved consistently under normal production conditions. Collect process data, billet condition observations, and machining outcomes during the pilot. Based on pilot findings, finalize procedural text in SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 and proceed to full rollout across the P1-L3 line.

Examples and expected outcomes
- Example record entries: Production log entry should show the target billet temperature field populated with the target billet temperature and the actual measured exit temperature with an accompanying note if corrective actions were required. Maintenance logs should cite ECN-2026-038 when recording changes made to EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to support the new target.
- Expected process improvements: Stabilization of incoming billet thermal condition to the machining cell, reduction in machining rework attributed to thermal distortion, and improved predictability of tooling wear and maintenance scheduling. Quality inspections should show a reduction in surface and dimensional issues that are traceable to pre-machining billet temperature variation.

Approvals
- Approval routing: This change notice requires review and signature by production management, maintenance management, and quality engineering to confirm that SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 updates are complete and that the pilot validation has demonstrated acceptable performance.
- Document control: Update the controlled document list to reference ECN-2026-022, which contains the initial findings that prompted this change, and revise SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 to reflect the new target and associated procedures. Include cross-reference to ECN-2026-022 in the revised SOPs for traceability.
- Records to keep: Retain pilot run data, revised SOP-P1-L3-01 and SOP-P1-L3-02 revisions, operator training sign-offs, maintenance work orders related to EQ-P1-L3-IH01 calibration or repair, and production logs marked with target verification. All retained records must reference ECN-2026-038.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-022
- SOP-P1-L3-01
- SOP-P1-L3-02

End of notice.

# ECN-2026-039 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Operational trends and maintenance logs showed recurring thermal cycling events and longer cool-down periods on EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Investigation identified that coil cooling water flow was operating at or just below acceptable thresholds for prolonged periods during heavy duty cycles. Although no immediate damage was observed, risk analysis determined that ensuring a higher minimum flow reduces coil insulation stress, prevents localized overheating, and extends coil life. This ECN formalizes an update to the documented minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 and defines implementation and verification steps.

Root cause: Flow variability combined with marginal setpoints on flow monitoring allowed transient low-flow conditions to persist. Contributing factors included control hysteresis and intermittent valve stiction that were not captured under the prior preventive maintenance scheme. The change addresses the detection and control of flow to reduce risk of premature coil failure and unplanned downtime.

Change summary: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. This ECN updates operational limits, inspection criteria, and maintenance task acceptance to align documentation, control setpoints, and maintenance practices with the new minimum flow requirement.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02 mechanical cooling circuit, flow sensor, control valve, and associated interlock logic.
- Documentation revisions: Update MM-P2-L1-IH02 to reflect the new flow minimum in the mechanical maintenance procedures; update SOP-P2-L1-04 to include operational verification steps for the cooling circuit; update control narrative and tuning notes as required in MM-P2-L1-IH02.
- Process and quality checks: Update QS-PROC-06 references where part temperature stability criteria depend on coil thermal control.
- Spare parts: Any flow sensor or valve replacements must be checked against the updated acceptance criteria defined in MM-P2-L1-IH02.

Implementation
--------------
Scope: Implementation covers adjustment of control setpoints, calibration and testing of flow metering, validation of alarms and interlocks, and updates to preventive maintenance and operating procedures. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. All systems and documents listed under Affected items must be completed prior to returning the induction heater to full production.

Steps:
- Update the PLC setpoint and alarm thresholds to enforce the new minimum flow requirement for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Ensure alarm behavior is consistent with QS-PROC-06 requirements for process interruptions.
- Calibrate the flow sensor in place and bench-check spare sensors according to MM-P2-L1-IH02 calibration steps. Record calibration results and calibration certificate reference in the maintenance log.
- Replace or refurbish the control valve if mechanical inspection reveals sticking or drift beyond the acceptance criteria in MM-P2-L1-IH02. Validate valve travel and response under simulated loads.
- Implement a verification procedure in SOP-P2-L1-04 for operators to confirm coil cooling water flow meets the stated minimum prior to heater startup and during shift handovers. Include guidance for immediate actions on alarm and escalation to maintenance.
- Perform a validation run sequence to demonstrate stable operation with the new minimum flow. Log flow readings and control responses to show compliance during representative operating conditions.

Examples of actions:
- Example operator check: confirm display reading and alarm status as documented in SOP-P2-L1-04 before initiating a billet heat cycle for EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Example maintenance check: record post-calibration flow reading and attach calibration sticker to the flow meter housing per MM-P2-L1-IH02.

Records to keep
---------------
- Calibration certificate for flow sensor with signature and location reference recorded in the equipment file for EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Commissioning and validation report demonstrating that EQ-P2-L1-IH02 maintains the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min during test scenarios. Include raw logs and trending graphs archived in the department document control system.
- Revised procedure pages from MM-P2-L1-IH02 and SOP-P2-L1-04 showing redline and final text. Maintain change rationale archive and approval record.
- Alarm log extract showing historical occurrences and post-implementation suppression or elimination of low-flow events.
- Training records indicating personnel briefed on revisions to SOP-P2-L1-04 and any new operator checks related to cooling flow.

Rationale and expected outcome
------------------------------
Maintaining the coil cooling water flow at or above the stated minimum will reduce thermal stress on coil insulation, lower the probability of localized coil hot spots, and improve overall heater reliability. Alignment of control setpoints, sensor accuracy, and maintenance acceptance criteria will reduce unplanned outages and support quality stability for parts processed on line P2-L1 in the Hot Forge cell. This change is preventive in nature and intended to extend mean time between coil interventions.

References
----------
- MM-P2-L1-IH02
- QS-PROC-06
- SOP-P2-L1-04

Approvals
---------
Engineering approval, maintenance oversight, operations acceptance, and quality concurrence are required to close this ECN. Signatures and dates will be recorded in the document control system upon acceptance. Implementation shall not proceed past initial calibration steps until approvals are logged against this ECN record.

Contact
-------
For implementation coordination and to request copies of revised procedure pages, contact the plant engineering lead listed in the EQ-P2-L1-IH02 equipment file.

# ECN-2026-040 - Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

### Reason for change
This engineering change corrects and formalizes the maximum ring outer diameter allowed for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01). Recent production trials and maintenance inspections identified inconsistencies between operator practice, tooling documentation, and the machine controller parameter set. To eliminate ambiguity that has resulted in repeated setup delays and an increase in out-of-tolerance parts, the maximum permitted ring outer diameter is now specified as 1240 mm. This value aligns with the verified roll geometry and machine clearance confirmed during the verification activity documented in MM-P1-L1-RR01 and supports safe operation practices described in SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05.

Background and rationale
- During routine maintenance and a concurrent production verification, mill runout and edge contact margins were measured against tooling envelopes documented in MM-P1-L1-RR01. Measurements and clearances confirmed the safe operating envelope for the roll train and guard boundaries. To prevent recurrence of marginal setups that risk roll contact with guards and nonconforming rings, a single unequivocal outer diameter limit is required for all shift crews and engineering changes.
- Standard operating procedures SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 will be updated to reflect the controlled maximum outer diameter. This prevents ad hoc increases during rush orders and ensures consistent QA acceptance criteria.

### Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01 — operational parameter controlling maximum ring outer diameter.
- Procedures: SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 — operating and setup instructions that reference permissible workpiece sizes.
- Maintenance master record: MM-P1-L1-RR01 — machine verification and clearance documentation that supports the change.
- Operator setup sheets and inspection checklists used at P1-L1 — to be revised to include the specified maximum outer diameter and associated verification steps.

All references to maximum ring outer diameter within the above items must be revised to state exactly: 1240 mm. Any existing documents, labels, or digital parameter entries that currently show a different value must be corrected or annotated with a link to this ECN.

### Implementation
Scope
- Apply the change to the EQ-P1-L1-RR01 machine controller limits, setup templates, operator checklists, and departmental signage. Ensure the physical guarding and tooling envelope checks documented in MM-P1-L1-RR01 are appended to the machine's maintenance file.
- Update SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 to include the certified maximum outer diameter and the mandatory verification method prior to first run of a lot and after any tooling change.

Action items and responsibilities
- Engineering: update the controller parameter and parameter log for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to reflect the maximum permitted outer diameter of 1240 mm and record the change in MM-P1-L1-RR01. Verify that controller interlocks will prevent entry of dimensions exceeding 1240 mm.
- Operations: revise the operator setup sheets and ensure all operators acknowledge the change. Train operators on the verification procedure documented in SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05; training records must be retained.
- Maintenance: perform a verification inspection of roll clearance and guards per MM-P1-L1-RR01, and record measurements and findings in the machine history file. Apply physical labels at the machine ingress point indicating the maximum outer diameter as 1240 mm.
- Quality: update incoming inspection and final inspection checklists to reference the maximum permissible outer diameter and ensure sampling plans include verification against the new limit.

Verification and records
- Prior to production re-start, engineering will run a verification routine to confirm the machine enforces the 1240 mm limit. Results and the controller snapshot will be filed in MM-P1-L1-RR01.
- Operations training attendance and competency sign-off will be recorded against operator personnel files and a copy retained with the EQ-P1-L1-RR01 run folder.
- Maintenance inspection forms and any corrective actions shall be logged in the equipment maintenance record and cross-referenced to MM-P1-L1-RR01.
- SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 revision notes will cite this ECN and note the date of implementation.

Examples and practitioner notes
- Example scenario: For a workpiece scheduled with target outer diameter approaching tooling limits, the setup operator must verify the nominal outer diameter and final expected outer diameter do not exceed 1240 mm before mounting. If nominal or expected final metric exceeds 1240 mm, the job must be escalated to engineering for alternate processing.
- Example documentation practice: When a tooling change is performed that could affect the envelope, maintenance shall perform the clearance check and append the signed MM-P1-L1-RR01 inspection sheet to the machine history. This sheet must include a statement confirming clearance for a maximum outer diameter of 1240 mm.

Transition plan
- Affected documents SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 will be revised concurrently with this ECN and released with change notices linking to this ECN. MM-P1-L1-RR01 shall be updated with the verification evidence.
- Implementation start will be the date on which approvals below are completed and recorded. No production batches that have potential outer diameters exceeding 1240 mm shall be processed on EQ-P1-L1-RR01 after that approval.

### Approvals
- This ECN requires documented approval by engineering, operations management, and maintenance management. Approval signatures and dates will be recorded in the document control system and copies attached to MM-P1-L1-RR01 and the revised SOPs.

Referenced documents
- MM-P1-L1-RR01
- SOP-P1-L1-01
- SOP-P1-L1-05

Records to keep
- Controller parameter snapshot for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 reflecting the 1240 mm limit.
- MM-P1-L1-RR01 verification and clearance inspection sheets.
- Operator training sign-offs and updated setup sheets.
- Revised SOP-P1-L1-01 and SOP-P1-L1-05 with revision notes linking to this ECN.

End of notice.
