# ECN-2026-041 Change notice - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

Reason for change
- Background: A recent targeted inspection of equipment EQ-P1-L2-RR01 identified inconsistent clamp preload readings during mandrel setup checks. Investigation concluded that the current documented clamp bolt torque value and verification steps did not reflect the updated clamp assembly and tooling introduced during a prior retrofit. To eliminate variability in ring geometry and to reduce risk of clamp slippage during rolling, the mandrel clamp bolt torque specification is being standardized and propagated to operational and maintenance documentation.
- Objective: Update the assembly and maintenance practice to require a single, clear mandrel clamp bolt torque value for EQ-P1-L2-RR01, and align the mill maintenance procedure and standard operating procedures to that value. This change aims to improve repeatability of rolled ring dimensions and reduce rework caused by clamp underload or overconstraint.

Affected items
- Primary affected equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01, referred to in operator and maintenance tasks as the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 located at Plant P1, line P1-L2.
- Documents to be revised: MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1, SOP-P1-L2-02, SOP-P1-L2-05. These documents contain maintenance schedules, torque tables, and startup checklists that reference mandrel clamp bolt torque for the subject mill.
- Tools and records: Torque wrench calibration entries, mandrel setup check sheets, and rolling run logs that reference clamp torque will be updated to record the standardized value.
- Consumables or parts: No change to part numbers is made by this notice. Existing clamp bolts and mating hardware remain in service unless inspection identifies damage.

Implementation
- New specification: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m. This value is to be used for initial assembly, pre-production setup, and any clamp retorque actions following maintenance or mandrel changeover.
- Procedure updates: MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1 will be revised to replace any prior torque references with the specified value and to add a verification step to confirm torque application with a calibrated torque wrench. SOP-P1-L2-02 and SOP-P1-L2-05 will be revised to include the torque value in startup and production checklists and to specify the record method for each rolling shift and each mandrel change.
- Application method: Apply torque in stages using the calibrated torque tool following the sequence described in the revised MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1. Verify final torque on each clamp bolt and record results on the updated mandrel setup check sheet. If final readings deviate from the specified value, follow the acceptance criteria and corrective action steps in MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.
- Calibration and tools: Only torque measuring tools with current calibration status shall be used to apply and verify clamp bolt torque. Calibration records must be available at the time of maintenance or setup verification and attached to the maintenance action record.
- Training and communication: Operators and maintenance personnel assigned to EQ-P1-L2-RR01 will complete a focused briefing covering the new torque specification, the rationale for the change, the verification steps, and the location of revised documents. The training will be documented in personnel training records and referenced when revisions to SOP-P1-L2-02 and SOP-P1-L2-05 are implemented.
- Examples of application scenarios:
  - During mandrel installation, the technician will torque the clamp bolts to the specified value and sign the mandrel setup check sheet. The rolling run will not commence until the setup sheet is complete and the torque verification has been recorded.
  - After a scheduled clamp maintenance action, the maintenance lead will torque each clamp bolt to the specified value, record the measurement, and attach the torque verification printout to the maintenance job record per MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1.
- Records to keep:
  - Updated mandrel setup check sheets for each mandrel installation, annotated with the applied torque and the name of the individual who performed the verification.
  - Torque wrench calibration certificates used for the application and verification, filed with maintenance records and accessible during audits.
  - Revision-controlled copies of MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-05 showing the change to the mandrel clamp bolt torque specification and the date of implementation.
  - Training acknowledgement records for all personnel briefed on the change.

Approvals
- Approval process: The engineering change will be approved by the equipment owner and maintenance manager. Approval signatures will be captured on the ECN approval sheet and stored in the document control system. Implementation of the change to MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-05 will not proceed until approvals are complete and calibration resources are confirmed.
- Post-implementation review: A verification review will be performed after initial implementation runs on EQ-P1-L2-RR01. The review will examine mandrel setup records, rolling run dimensional data, and any anomalies recorded since implementation. Findings will be documented and attached to the ECN approval record.
- Audit trail: All changes to MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-05 will be logged in the document control system with links to the approval documentation and training records.

Related documents
- MM-P1-L2-RR01-S1
- SOP-P1-L2-02
- SOP-P1-L2-05

Notes
- This change notice standardizes a single clamp bolt torque value for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 to reduce process variability. Follow-up actions include verification of tooling condition and a post-implementation dimensional check sequence to confirm the intended benefit. All records specified above are required to demonstrate compliance during internal and external reviews.

# ECN-2026-042 Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and operational review, engineering identified a need to formalize and communicate the maximum allowable system pressure limit for the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). The intent is to reduce risk of hydraulic component stress that could lead to premature wear or failure, and to align lockout tagout, maintenance, and SOP references with operational controls. This change also corrects variance between operator practice and equipment documentation found during a recent internal audit.
- Rationale: Establishing a clear, documented system pressure limit will standardize commissioning checks, test procedures, and emergency response. It minimizes ambiguity for operations and maintenance personnel, ensures compatibility with hydraulic accessories, and supports compliance with machine safety reviews. The specified limit is applicable to all hydraulic circuits that are part of the press system and its ancillary equipment as defined in related documents.

Affected items
- Primary equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03 is subject to this change. All onboard hydraulic circuits, pressure sensors, relief valves, and pressure-limiting devices that govern system pressure are affected.
- Documentation: The following documents shall be updated to reflect the change and to provide consistent instructions across operations and maintenance: ECN-2026-049, MM-P2-L4-HP03, SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Procedures and training: Operator checklists, daily start procedures, and maintenance task plans that reference allowable pressure ranges must be revised. Training materials used for new and reassigned operators and maintenance personnel require update to include the new system pressure limit and associated verification steps.
- Spare parts and calibration: Any pressure transducers, gauges, or relief valves that are selected or staged for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 must be compatible with the established limit. Calibration records for pressure-sensing devices will reflect verification against the updated acceptance criteria.

Implementation
- New limit: The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar. This value is the maximum allowable system pressure for all applicable hydraulic circuits on the press.
- Engineering actions: Engineering will issue updated schematics and stamped notes that identify the locations where the system pressure limit applies. Relief valve setpoint documentation will be adjusted to ensure that settings and redundancy meet the new limit.
- Controls modification: PLC setpoints and alarm thresholds that reference system pressure shall be adjusted to trigger warnings below the limit and to initiate safe shutdown logic if pressure approaches the limit. All changes to control logic will be reviewed and tested in a controlled environment and recorded in the change log.
- Maintenance instructions: Maintenance work plans will include a mandatory verification step that confirms system pressure does not exceed the specified limit before any pressure-bearing fasteners are released or any hydraulic lines are opened. These verifications shall be recorded on maintenance service reports and stored with the asset history for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
- Commissioning and acceptance: After implementation, a controlled pressure test will be performed to demonstrate compliance. Test execution will be recorded, including the instrumentation used and calibration certificates for pressure measurement devices. The acceptance record will be retained with maintenance files and referenced in MM-P2-L4-HP03.
- Operator procedures: Operator tasks and start sequences will incorporate a pressure check to verify that system pressure remains below the specified limit prior to cyclic loading. Any excursion must be logged and escalated per SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Examples of application: When replacing a hydraulic hose assembly on EQ-P2-L4-HP03, maintenance personnel shall confirm system pressure is verified below the limit before depressurizing the line. When performing a pressure sensor replacement, technicians will validate the new sensor against calibrated equipment and document that readings correlate and remain below the limit during functional testing.

Records to keep
- Record types: Change implementation checklist, updated schematics, control logic revision log, pressure test reports, instrument calibration certificates, maintenance service reports, operator training acknowledgement records, and audit evidence of procedural updates.
- Storage location: Records will be filed in the document control system under the equipment folder for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and cross-referenced in the ECN record. Related document updates will reference ECN-2026-049, MM-P2-L4-HP03, and SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Retention note: All records associated with this change shall be retained as part of the asset history and made available for inspection during internal and external audits.

Approvals
- Approval requirements: The following approvals are required prior to implementation: engineering review and signoff, maintenance management approval, operations supervision acceptance, and document control closure. Each approver shall verify that procedures, control logic changes, and training materials have been updated and that records are in place.
- Post-implementation review: After initial implementation, a focused operational review will verify that the system pressure limit is being observed in day-to-day use and that alarms and interlocks function as intended. Findings will be documented and any corrective actions will follow the standard change management path referencing ECN-2026-049.
- Related documentation: Use this ECN in conjunction with ECN-2026-049, and ensure consistency with the maintenance manual MM-P2-L4-HP03 and the standard operating procedure SOP-P2-L4-03 for operational and maintenance guidance.

Prepared by: Engineering  
Distribution: Operations, Maintenance, Document Control, Safety

Attachments: Implementation checklist, updated schematic extract, sample pressure test report template, training slide excerpt.

# ECN-2026-043 - Change notice - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

## Reason for change
Background: During routine commissioning and subsequent process qualification of EQ-P1-L3-CN03 it was observed that the existing warm-up procedure did not reliably achieve stable spindle thermal conditions prior to production start. Process drift at the beginning of a run led to sporadic dimensional excursions on first-piece outputs traced to spindle thermal transient. The change clarifies and standardizes the spindle warm-up requirement to eliminate variability and to align operator practice with the capability observed during machine vendor validation and internal trial runs.

Rationale: Specifying a defined spindle warm-up time reduces operator ambiguity, prevents premature loading of parts, and provides a documented control to support first-article quality. The change is intended to reduce rework and inspection burden at the line level and to ensure consistent part geometry from start-of-run pieces. This ECN also aligns shop procedure with recorded best practice from the process trials summarized in SB-1014.

Related documents: implement this change consistent with SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-03.

## Affected items
Scope: This ECN applies specifically to Machining CNC turning center #3, equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03, located on line P1-L3 at plant P1. It affects operator start-of-shift activities, first-article production sequences, in-process inspection checkpoints tied to initial production pieces, and the machine log entry procedure.

Affected artifacts and records:
- Operator machine start checklist for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 referenced in SOP-P1-L3-02.
- First-article inspection records retained per SOP-P1-L3-03.
- Machine maintenance and event log entries referenced in SB-1014.

Examples of affected activities:
- Pre-production machine preparation steps that currently omit a standardized spindle run-in.
- First-piece verification where measurement is taken immediately after initial loading without consideration for spindle thermal stabilization.

## Implementation
Change description: Update the machine start procedure for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to require a spindle warm-up period of 27 minutes prior to loading production parts. This requirement is to be added to the operator checklist in SOP-P1-L3-02 and to be referenced in the first-article instruction in SOP-P1-L3-03. The warm-up is an active step: the spindle is run under the conditions specified in the machine control recipe for warm-up as documented in SB-1014, and operators shall not load production parts onto the chuck until the warm-up time is complete.

Step-by-step implementation tasks:
- Revise the operator checklist entry in SOP-P1-L3-02 to include: "Run spindle warm-up for 27 minutes; do not load production parts until complete."
- Update first-article instructions in SOP-P1-L3-03 to require that first-article sampling begins only after the warm-up procedure is completed and documented.
- Revise operator training materials and on-shop-floor quick reference for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to reflect the new requirement.
- Add a field to the machine log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to record start time and completion confirmation of the 27 minutes warm-up period in the machine event log governed by SB-1014.

Operator actions and examples:
- Example scenario: prior to a production shift, the operator performs machine safety checks and coolant verification per SOP-P1-L3-02, then initiates the spindle warm-up procedure and observes the spindle run indicators for the 27 minutes before proceeding to load the first raw blank.
- Example scenario: when a short trial run is required for program verification, the operator must still perform the 27 minutes warm-up and record the activity in the machine event log before producing verification pieces.

Records to keep:
- Machine event log entry for each warm-up showing equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and affirmation that the 27 minutes warm-up was completed; retain per SB-1014.
- First-article inspection record with timestamped note that inspection occurred after completion of the warm-up; file under the production batch per SOP-P1-L3-03.
- Training completion acknowledgment for operators assigned to EQ-P1-L3-CN03 indicating awareness and adherence to the warm-up requirement; file per existing training records practice.

Nonconforming condition handling:
- If an operator inadvertently loads parts before the 27 minutes warm-up is complete, immediate actions include halting production, segregating affected pieces, and initiating first-article inspection per SOP-P1-L3-03. All incidents must be recorded in the machine log and escalated to line supervision for disposition in accordance with SB-1014.

Timing and rollout:
- Owners: Machine steward for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 is responsible for updating SOP-P1-L3-02 and coordinating training. Quality owner to update SOP-P1-L3-03 references and inspection triggers. Documentation updates must reference SB-1014 for log retention practices.

Verification:
- After implementation, the first production shift will include confirmation that machine logs contain entries for the 27 minutes warm-up for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and that first-article inspections were performed post-warm-up. Deviations will be recorded in SB-1014.

## Approvals
Review and approval required from the following functions prior to release of revised SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 and shop-floor changes:
- Production lead for line P1-L3
- Quality assurance owner for P1 operations
- Maintenance steward for EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Document references for approval: SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-03

Approval signatures and dates will be recorded in the ECN control sheet and associated revision log maintained per SB-1014.

# ECN-2026-044 Change notice - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-RR02

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: During recent maintenance and inspection activities on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02), field maintenance personnel identified variability in mandrel seating and clamp stability that could contribute to off-axis runout and accelerated wear of the mandrel assembly. Investigation of assembly records, tool usage, and operator feedback indicated inconsistent clamp bolt preload as a likely contributor. The current documentation and work instructions referenced for clamp procedures did not specify a controlled target torque value for the mandrel clamp bolts for this specific machine, leading to inconsistent practice across shifts.

Purpose: This engineering change notice establishes a defined mandrel clamp bolt torque value for EQ-P3-L2-RR02 and documents the implementation and control measures required to standardize clamp preload during mandrel installation and maintenance. The change aims to reduce mandrel movement during rolling, improve dimensional stability of produced rings, and extend service life of mandrel-related components.

Supporting documents: Procedure and operational references to be used in conjunction with this change are SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-04. These procedures will be revised as noted in the implementation section to incorporate the new torque requirement and associated verification steps.

Affected items
--------------
- Equipment: Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02).  
- Assemblies: Mandrel clamp bolts and adjacent clamp hardware used to secure the mandrel to the headstock.  
- Procedures: Work instructions and standard operating procedures covering mandrel installation, clamp torqueing, and pre-roll checks associated with EQ-P3-L2-RR02 (see SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, SOP-P3-L2-04).  
- Records: Maintenance and inspection records, torque verification logs, and shift handover checklists where mandrel installation is recorded.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque specification
---------------------------------------
The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 475 N·m.

Implementation
--------------
Scope and applicability: This torque requirement applies whenever the mandrel is installed, reinstalled, removed and reinstalled after any mandrel service, or whenever clamp hardware is replaced or adjusted on EQ-P3-L2-RR02. The value is to be used as the target torque for final clamp bolt tightening when following the mandated tightening sequence and verification steps described below.

Procedure revisions: Update SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-04 to include:
- The specified mandrel clamp bolt torque value and the note that this value applies only to EQ-P3-L2-RR02.
- A prescribed tightening sequence for the clamp bolts to ensure even preload distribution (mechanics will follow the existing sequence patterns in the SOPs and annotate the change in the revision notes).
- A requirement that final torque be applied using a calibrated torque wrench or torque-control tool capable of delivering and documenting the specified value.
- Acceptance criteria for torque verification and instructions for corrective action if torque readings are out of tolerance, including re-torqueing and inspection of clamp threads and seating surfaces.

Tightening and verification steps (summary for incorporation into SOPs):
- Clean clamp bolt threads and seating surfaces, inspect for damage, and apply any specified assembly lubricant per the existing SOPs.
- Hand-start bolts and perform an initial snug sequence to seat the clamp.
- Apply the specified torque value to each clamp bolt following the prescribed sequence.
- Record the torque reading for each bolt in the torque verification log for the event.
- If any bolt cannot achieve the specified torque, stop installation, tag the clamp for inspection, and escalate to maintenance for thread or clamp surface evaluation before resuming.

Tools and calibration: Use calibrated torque wrenches or torque-controlled tools. Tool calibration records must be current and available for audit. Torque tool identification must be added to the torque verification log so that torque events can be traced to specific tools and calibration certificates.

Training and communication: Conduct targeted training for maintenance technicians and operators who perform mandrel changeover or clamp adjustments on EQ-P3-L2-RR02. Training will cover the revised SOP content, the rationale for the torque requirement, the tightening sequence, and required recordkeeping.

Examples and rationale: Examples of corrective actions include re-torqueing with a calibrated tool when a clamp shows evidence of movement during a trial roll or when torque logs indicate deviation from the specified value. Rationale: consistent clamp preload minimizes clamp loosening under operational loading, reduces eccentric loading on the mandrel, and lowers the risk of localized wear that could lead to mandrel failure or out-of-spec product.

Records to keep
---------------
- Torque verification log for each mandrel installation or reinstallation on EQ-P3-L2-RR02. The log must list the equipment id, the mandrel serial or identifier if applicable, the clamp bolt identification, the applied torque value, the torque tool id, operator or technician initials, and any corrective actions performed.
- Tool calibration certificate copies for torque tools used on EQ-P3-L2-RR02.
- Revised procedure records and training completion records referencing SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-04 updates.
- Maintenance work orders and inspection reports documenting any clamp or thread repairs that were required as a result of torque verification findings.

Approvals
---------
Implementation of this change requires approval from the equipment reliability engineer and the plant maintenance manager. Approval signatures will be appended to this ECN in the document control system and recorded with links to the revised SOP entries for SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-04. After approvals, the revised SOPs will be released and training scheduled to ensure compliance.

Notes
-----
This ECN is specific to EQ-P3-L2-RR02. Any changes for other ring rolling mills must be processed via separate engineering change notices and appropriate updates to their operating procedures. Refer to SOP-P3-L2-01, SOP-P3-L2-03, and SOP-P3-L2-04 for existing installation and safety requirements that remain in force unless explicitly superseded by this notice.

# ECN-2026-045 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HT02

Reason for change
- Background: Recent process audits and metallurgical review identified variability in carbon distribution and grain coarsening trends on parts processed in Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02). Root-cause analysis referenced ECN-2026-020 and furnace maintenance records in MM-P2-L4-HT02 and found the control profile used for austenitizing was not updated to match revised load scheduling and fixture changes implemented earlier in the year.
- Issue: As-built control setpoints and documented procedure in SOP-P2-L4-04 did not reflect the optimized austenitizing setpoint determined during the metallurgical validation trials. The difference contributed to a higher incidence of post-quench hardness scatter and secondary rework events.
- Objective: Update the furnace control setpoint to the validated austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 to ensure process stability, repeatable microstructure, and reduced rework. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C.

Affected items
- Equipment: Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) control configuration and HMI recipes. All operator screens and recipe storage for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 must be updated to reflect the new austenitizing setpoint.
- Procedures: SOP-P2-L4-04 must be revised to state the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 as 885 °C and include the validated acceptance criteria for metallurgical checks performed post-quench. Cross-reference ECN-2026-020 for justification and trial data.
- Maintenance documentation: MM-P2-L4-HT02 preventive maintenance and calibration records must include verification of control loop performance after setpoint change. Any adjustments or repairs discovered during implementation must be recorded against MM-P2-L4-HT02.
- Production batches: All production lots run in EQ-P2-L4-HT02 after implementation will be flagged for traceability and include a note in lot records indicating they were processed under the updated setpoint. Operators will follow the updated SOP-P2-L4-04 for lot control and sampling.
- Quality hold points: Parts processed under the new setpoint will be subject to the documented sampling procedure in SOP-P2-L4-04 (as revised) until statistical confirmation of process capability is documented. See ECN-2026-020 for the metallurgical trial plan and acceptance rationale.

Implementation
- Change control actions:
  - Update furnace recipe: Modify the stored austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 to read exactly 885 °C in the control system. Save the revised recipe with change note referencing ECN-2026-045.
  - Procedure revision: Revise SOP-P2-L4-04 to reflect the austenitizing setpoint 885 °C and include step-by-step instructions for loading, thermocouple placement, and post-quench sampling aligned with the validation in ECN-2026-020.
  - Maintenance verification: Execute checks per MM-P2-L4-HT02 to confirm control loop accuracy and thermocouple integrity after recipe change. Document results in the MM-P2-L4-HT02 record.
- Execution plan:
  - Pre-change activities: Notify affected shifts and quality engineering, and place EQ-P2-L4-HT02 under controlled change status. Archive the previous recipe per document retention rules.
  - Implementation window: Implement the setpoint update during a scheduled furnace outage or controlled changeover to avoid on-going loads in process. Operators will not process production loads in EQ-P2-L4-HT02 until post-change validation is complete.
  - Post-change validation: Run the validation load plan outlined in ECN-2026-020 using the updated recipe. Collect process logs and sampling results. Perform metallographic checks and hardness testing as specified in SOP-P2-L4-04 (revised).
- Records to keep:
  - Control system printout or screenshot showing the austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P2-L4-HT02 set to 885 °C, signed by the implementer and verifier.
  - MM-P2-L4-HT02 entries documenting post-change maintenance checks and any corrective actions.
  - Validation report summarizing trial loads, micrographs, hardness data, and disposition decisions; cross-reference ECN-2026-020.
  - Revised SOP-P2-L4-04 with version control reflecting incorporation of the austenitizing setpoint 885 °C.
  - Production lot records and quality hold tags for parts processed under the new setpoint until release criteria are met.
- Examples of acceptable documentation entries:
  - “Recipe EQ-P2-L4-HT02 austenitizing setpoint updated to 885 °C per ECN-2026-045. Implemented by [engineer], verified by [quality], see MM-P2-L4-HT02 for loop verification.”
  - “Validation run results: see attached report (ECN-2026-020 reference) and SOP-P2-L4-04 rev note. Lot numbers and sample IDs recorded in lot record.”

Approvals
- Engineering: Approval required from Heat Treat Engineering acknowledging that the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is set to 885 °C and that the change is consistent with metallurgical validation in ECN-2026-020.
- Maintenance: Approval required from Maintenance Supervisor per MM-P2-L4-HT02 confirming control system and sensor verification completed and documented.
- Quality: Approval required from Quality Engineering confirming SOP-P2-L4-04 revised language is acceptable and the validation sampling plan meets acceptance criteria prior to release of production lots processed under the new setpoint.
- Records of approval: Sign-off pages will be attached to ECN-2026-045, with links to MM-P2-L4-HT02 maintenance records, the validation data referenced in ECN-2026-020, and the updated SOP-P2-L4-04.

References
- ECN-2026-020
- MM-P2-L4-HT02
- SOP-P2-L4-04

End of notice.

# ECN-2026-046 - Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Reason for change
-----------------
Background: Operational trials and incoming quality trends identified variance in billet surface condition and machining tool wear correlated to billet soak level prior to machining. A review of in-process data and feedback from maintenance and production teams indicated that the control setpoint for Machining induction billet heater #1 did not align with metallurgical targets derived during process validation. The intent of this ECN is to align the heater control with the validated billet target to stabilize machining outcomes and reduce rework.

Rationale: Setpoint alignment is necessary to reduce variability in billet microstructure at the machining interface and to extend cutter life by producing a consistent billet temperature at machine transfer. The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Changing the heater control and associated operator steps to meet this target will reduce downstream variability and support consistent part quality.

Affected items
--------------
Scope: This change affects the following items in Plant P1, line P1-L3:
- Control logic and setpoint for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
- Associated operator procedures and checklists referenced in SOP-P1-L3-04 and SOP-P1-L3-05.
- Machine transfer and handoff criteria between heating and machining cells on line P1-L3.
- Shift log entries and batch records where billet temperature at handoff is recorded.

Components and roles impacted: Production operators working on line P1-L3, maintenance technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, quality engineers reviewing machining output, and process engineers overseeing thermal treatments.

Exclusions: Equipment and processes not explicitly listed for line P1-L3 are not altered by this ECN.

Implementation
--------------
Change description: Adjust the control system for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to hold billets at the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C at the machine transfer point. Update operator procedures in SOP-P1-L3-04 and SOP-P1-L3-05 to reflect revised acceptance criteria, measurement method, and required records.

Steps for implementation:
- Update control logic configuration for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to reference the target billet temperature of 1235 °C as the transfer setpoint. Confirm configuration change is logged in the control system change history.
- Revise SOP-P1-L3-04 and SOP-P1-L3-05 to:
  - Specify measurement method and instrument locations for verifying billet temperature prior to transfer.
  - Define acceptance wording that aligns with the new target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C.
  - Outline operator actions if the measured temperature deviates from the target.
- Conduct a controlled startup validation run where billets heated under the new setpoint are processed through machining and inspected. Document deviations and corrective actions in the validation record.
- Train affected personnel on revised procedures and make updated SOPs available in the document control system.

Examples of acceptable and unacceptable conditions:
- Example acceptable condition: Billet verification reading indicates alignment with the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C immediately prior to transfer; machining proceeds with standard feed and speed parameters described in SOPs.
- Example unacceptable condition: Measurement shows deviation from the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C; operator must hold the billet in heating station and notify maintenance and quality for disposition per SOP-P1-L3-04.

Verification and validation:
- Process engineer will review machining tool wear samples and first article parts produced under the new setpoint and record findings in the implementation report.
- Quality will perform dimensional and surface inspections per normal sampling criteria and log results. Any nonconforming trends will trigger a documented investigation.

Records to keep
---------------
Required records to be filed in the document control system and quality archive:
- Control system change record for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 capturing the configuration update and reason for change. Reference this ECN number when filing.
- Revised versions of SOP-P1-L3-04 and SOP-P1-L3-05 with change history and approval signatures.
- Training records for all operators and maintenance personnel who receive instruction on the revised procedures.
- Validation run report including batch identifiers, measurements, inspection results, and disposition of any out-of-spec billets.
- Shift logs and batch records indicating billet verification readings at transfer and any interventions.
- Corrective action documentation if unexpected deviations occur during rollout.

Approvals
---------
Approval by process engineering, maintenance management, and quality assurance is required prior to production use. The ECN references related documents for context and procedure control: ECN-2026-029, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P1-L3-05. Signatures below indicate acceptance of scope, implementation approach, and record requirements as described in this document.

Approver fields:
- Process engineering approval
- Maintenance approval
- Quality assurance approval
- Production management approval

Notes
-----
- This change is focused on aligning thermal control for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 to the validated target billet temperature stated above to improve machining stability and part quality.
- All implementation activities must be documented and retained in accordance with plant record retention rules.
title: Change notice - Machining induction billet heater #1

# ECN-2026-047 - Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and an independent review of bolted joint integrity on Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), discrepancies were identified between installed main ram bolt seating and expected preload behavior. Review of service records and physical inspection found evidence of bolt relaxation under cyclic loading for the main ram assembly. The potential for joint loosening presents an elevated risk to machine alignment, die seating, and operator safety. This ECN establishes a controlled update to the specified tightening requirement and associated verification practices to ensure consistent clamp load and reduce risk of unplanned downtime and safety incidents.
- Rationale: Engineering assessment determined that a single, clearly documented torque requirement and an updated verification process will reduce variability in assembly practice and improve long term joint reliability. The adopted torque value and verification actions reflect proven installation technique and are intended to align shop practice with inspection evidence and supplier guidance. This change improves traceability of maintenance actions and supports consistent workmanship across shifts.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) located on P1, line P1-L4.
- Functional impact: The change affects procedures and records for main ram bolt installation and verification. It applies to any maintenance, rebuild, or assembly activity affecting the main ram bolted joint.
- Documentation affected: Update required for Standard Work and procedure references that control bolting and torque verification on the press. Cite and reconcile with existing procedure documents: SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-05. Where those documents reference torque or installation acceptance criteria for the main ram bolt, the value and acceptance steps in this ECN shall take precedence until the referenced documents are formally revised.

Implementation
- New torque requirement: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m. This is the required applied torque for initial installation and for any work in the assembly where the bolt is removed and reinstalled.
- Installation method: Apply torque using a calibrated torque wrench or torque controlled device. Use a controlled, staged tightening pattern as defined in SB-1034 and SOP-P1-L4-02. Use lubrication practices that match those specified in the referenced procedures to ensure repeatable joint behavior. If additional tightening steps or torque-angle verification are described in SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-02, or SOP-P1-L4-05, those steps remain applicable and must be followed in combination with the specified torque value.
- Verification: After installation to the specified torque, perform a verification check using an independent torque instrument or calibrated witness device to confirm retention of applied torque. Record the measured value and the instrument identification in the equipment maintenance record. If measured retention differs from expected practice documented in SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-02, or SOP-P1-L4-05, perform corrective action per those documents and escalate per local maintenance governance.
- Examples and acceptable practice: Example scenario — a maintenance task that requires removal of the main ram bolt must include documented evidence of torque application to 970 N·m and a verification entry in the maintenance record. Example demonstration activities during training shall include hands-on torque application to the specified value and witness verification to reinforce technique and calibration awareness.
- Calibration and tools: Only use torque tools that are within their calibration cycle and traceable to the tool calibration program referenced in SB-1034. Calibration certificates shall be retained with the tool inventory record and referenced in maintenance entries when used for the main ram bolt.
- Records to keep: For every installation event involving the main ram bolt on EQ-P1-L4-HP02, retain the following in the equipment maintenance file: name of technician performing the work, tool identifier, calibration certificate reference, declared applied torque value, independent verification result, and a short note on bolt condition and lubricant used. These entries will be filed in the maintenance system and referenced during post-maintenance inspections and audits.
- Training: Update local maintenance training to include the new specified torque and verification workflow. Supervisors shall ensure technicians demonstrate competence in applying and verifying the specified torque value on representative assemblies prior to independent work.

Approvals
- Approval requirement: This ECN requires review and formal sign-off by the Plant Mechanical Lead, Maintenance Supervisor for P1-L4 line, and Quality Assurance representative responsible for heat treat line controls. The approval confirms alignment with SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-05 and that records and training updates are in place.
- Post-approval actions: Upon approval, revise or annotate SB-1034, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-05 to reflect the change or reference this ECN as the controlling document for the main ram bolt torque until a formal revision of those documents is issued. Communicate the change to shop floor maintenance staff and schedule verification audits to confirm implementation.
- Audit and monitoring: Maintenance supervision will perform follow-up inspections and audits of the retained records for a period following implementation to verify compliance with the specified torque requirement and recordkeeping practice. Any recurring anomalies or evidence of joint relaxation after implementation will trigger a review of installation method, lubrication, and joint condition as per SB-1034 and SOP-P1-L4-05.

Related documents
- SB-1034
- SOP-P1-L4-02
- SOP-P1-L4-05

Distribution
- Notify maintenance planning, operations supervision for P1-L4, quality, and tooling control groups. File this ECN in the document control system and reference in the equipment maintenance file for EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
title: Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

# ECN-2026-048 - Change notice - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a required safety and reliability correction to the cooling system of the Ring Rolling induction billet heater identified as EQ-P2-L2-IH01. Field inspection and operational trend review identified that coil cooling water flow had been marginal during several production shifts, creating risk of coil overheating and premature insulation degradation. The change clarifies the minimum allowable coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L2-IH01, updates machine-level controls and alarms, and amends maintenance and operator procedures to enforce the minimum flow requirement identified below.

The immediate goal is to eliminate ambiguity in operational limits, reduce forced outages attributable to coil damage, and ensure consistent implementation of protective interlocks and maintenance verification steps. This change is based on the technical assessment recorded in ECN-2026-012 and aligns required maintenance actions with documented procedures MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 and operational steps in SOP-P2-L2-04.

Affected items
- Induction heater EQ-P2-L2-IH01: coil cooling system operational parameters, PLC alarm settings, and HMI display labels.
- Operator procedure SOP-P2-L2-04: operator checks and start-up checklist entries that reference cooling system acceptance criteria.
- Maintenance instruction MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1: preventive checks and acceptance criteria for returned-to-service verification after any cooling system work.
- Machine documentation set and visible nameplate/labeling on EQ-P2-L2-IH01 where cooling flow minimum is displayed.

Mandatory requirement
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min.

Implementation
Scope
The implementation applies to EQ-P2-L2-IH01 and associated PLC/HMI, the operator start-up and monitoring workflow, and the preventive maintenance checklist for the heater coil cooling system. Implementation steps are staged to ensure safety interlocks remain active during work and to provide clear traceable records of modifications.

Control changes
- PLC configuration will be updated to enforce the coil cooling water flow minimum. The PLC logic will inhibit heater enable if measured flow is below the mandatory value and will log the inhibit condition to the historian and maintenance log.
- HMI screens and local nameplate labels at EQ-P2-L2-IH01 will be updated to display the mandatory coil cooling water flow minimum value and the failure action that will occur if the flow is not met.
- Alarm thresholds and alarm text will reference the mandatory value and direct operators to SOP-P2-L2-04 for corrective action.

Procedure updates
- SOP-P2-L2-04 will be revised to include the mandatory cooling water flow minimum in the pre-start checklist and in the corrective actions section when low flow is detected. The procedure will direct operators to note the flow reading and to notify maintenance per the existing escalation path documented in MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1.
- MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 will be revised to include acceptance verification steps after corrective work on the cooling circuit, requiring confirmation that flow meets the mandatory value prior to returning EQ-P2-L2-IH01 to service. Records of flow verification must be entered into the equipment maintenance record.

Physical modifications
- Where necessary, the existing flow transmitter and its calibration will be verified against one of the calibrated test units kept by maintenance. Any adjustments shall be performed according to calibration best practices and be recorded in the equipment calibration log referenced in MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1.
- A durable label stating the mandatory cooling flow value will be affixed adjacent to the local flow display on EQ-P2-L2-IH01.

Examples of operator actions
- During start-up, the operator verifies flow reading on the HMI. If the reading is at or above the mandatory value, proceed as per SOP-P2-L2-04.
- If the reading is below the mandatory value, the heater will remain inhibited. The operator follows the corrective action steps in SOP-P2-L2-04 and notifies maintenance. Maintenance will inspect cooling circuit, verify transmitter operation, and perform corrective repairs in accordance with MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 prior to re-enabling the heater.

Records to keep
- PLC change request and configuration export for the PLC update, archived in the control systems change folder and referenced to this ECN.
- HMI screen revision package and digital photo of updated local nameplate for EQ-P2-L2-IH01.
- SOP-P2-L2-04 revision with change log entry that references this ECN.
- MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 revision with change log entry that references this ECN.

# ECN-2026-049 - Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Reason for change
- Background: Recent maintenance reviews on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 identified variability in cylinder performance and increased incidence of seal replacement. Root cause analysis linked the variability to lubricant supply inconsistency and a history of mixed-use lubricants from multiple batches. To standardize reliability and simplify inventory traceability, the lubrication specification for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 is being formalized.
- Objective: Specify a single approved lubricant part number and update related procedural documents to ensure consistent application, storage, and recordkeeping for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
- Scope of change: This ECN applies only to the hydraulic forging press identified as EQ-P2-L4-HP03 on P2-L4. It does not change mechanical design, control logic, safety interlocks, or production parameters.

Affected items
- Equipment affected: EQ-P2-L4-HP03 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3).
- Consumable change: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450. CFW-LUB-450 is the only approved lubricant to be used on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 going forward.
- Documentation impacted: SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04, SOP-P2-L4-05 will be updated to reflect the approved lubricant, storage and handling requirements, and inspection checkpoints associated with this ECN.
- Inventory: Existing stock of other lubricants currently dedicated to EQ-P2-L4-HP03 must be dispositioned per existing inventory control procedures; inventory records must clearly mark CFW-LUB-450 as the approved item for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.

Implementation
- Implementation summary: Replace any ambiguous lubricant references in field procedures for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 with CFW-LUB-450. Update SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04, and SOP-P2-L4-05 to include specific handling, storage, labeling and inspection guidance tied to CFW-LUB-450.
- Step rationale and detailed actions:
  - Procurement and inventory: Purchasing will source CFW-LUB-450 and set the item as preferred stock for line P2-L4. Warehouse personnel will segregate CFW-LUB-450 stock and apply a unique shelf label indicating use for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 only.
  - Labeling and storage: All containers of CFW-LUB-450 shall be labeled with the part number exactly as CFW-LUB-450. Storage area signage will reference P2-L4 and EQ-P2-L4-HP03 to reduce cross-usage risk.
  - Procedural updates: Revision to SOP-P2-L4-02 will add a lubrication checklist item that requires visual verification of container labeling before dispensing. SOP-P2-L4-04 will be adjusted to record the part number CFW-LUB-450 in the maintenance log entry for lubrication events. SOP-P2-L4-05 will include a section on acceptance criteria for lubricant receipt, including container integrity and label verification.
  - Training: Operators and maintenance staff assigned to P2-L4 will receive briefing on the change and demonstration of the new labeling and documentation steps. Training records will be retained in the training file for line P2-L4.
  - Example scenarios:
    - Receipt inspection: Upon receipt, the warehouse inspector compares incoming label to CFW-LUB-450. If the label matches CFW-LUB-450, the item is accepted and entered into inventory for P2-L4. If the label does not match CFW-LUB-450, the item is segregated and escalated.
    - Lubricant dispense: Before dispensing to EQ-P2-L4-HP03, the technician confirms the container label CFW-LUB-450 and records the part number in the maintenance log entry required by SOP-P2-L4-04.
- Records to keep:
  - Purchase order references to CFW-LUB-450 and associated receiving records.
  - Receiving inspection records including container label verification and acceptance notes.
  - Maintenance log entries for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 that contain the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-450 as recorded per SOP-P2-L4-04.
  - Training attendance records demonstrating instruction on use of CFW-LUB-450 for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
  - Disposition records for any previously used lubricants removed from EQ-P2-L4-HP03 service.
  - Revised SOP documents: SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04, SOP-P2-L4-05 with revision notes referencing this ECN.
- Exceptions and controls: Any temporary deviation from use of CFW-LUB-450 requires documented approval from the maintenance manager and must reference this ECN in the deviation record. Deviation records become part of the equipment file.

Approvals
- Approval path: Maintenance Engineering, Quality Assurance, Production Lead for P2-L4, and Procurement must review and sign. Quality will confirm that SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04, and SOP-P2-L4-05 have been updated and stored in document control.
- Post-implementation verification: Quality Assurance will perform an audit of EQ-P2-L4-HP03 records to verify that CFW-LUB-450 is being used and recorded according to the updated SOPs. Audit findings will be attached to the ECN file.
- Related documents: See SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-04, SOP-P2-L4-05 for procedural detail and recordkeeping templates.

Revision note: This ECN Rev D formalizes CFW-LUB-450 as the approved lubricant for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and mandates coordinated updates to the listed SOPs and retention of associated records.

# ECN-2026-050 - Change notice - Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-RR03

Reason for change
- Background: Recent product audits and production feedback identified inconsistent documentation for maximum ring outer diameter capability associated with EQ-P2-L2-RR03. Existing material handling and process planning records referenced differing diameter limits across maintenance manuals and work instructions, which created uncertainty in ring sizing decisions and risk of tooling overload or inappropriate process selection.
- Purpose: This engineering change notice clarifies and records the maximum ring outer diameter capability for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P2-L2-RR03 to ensure process planners, operators, and maintenance personnel use a single authoritative value when evaluating work orders and setup requirements.
- Scope: This change updates the controlled data set used for quoting, job planning, setup checklists, and production verification for items routed to line P2-L2 that require processing on EQ-P2-L2-RR03. The update affects planning, maintenance scheduling, and operator setup procedures where diameter capability is a gating parameter.

Affected items
- Equipment records: The equipment specification sheet and capacity entry for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 maintained in the maintenance system referenced by MM-P2-L2-RR03 will be updated to reflect the clarified maximum ring outer diameter.
- Standard work: The ring rolling setup pages in SOP-P2-L2-05 that reference diameter capability or limits for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 will be revised to align with this notice.
- Safety bulletin linkage: Any interlock or guarding references and risk assessments tied to diameter handling will be cross-checked against SB-1017 to confirm compatibility with the recorded maximum.
- Planning documentation: Job routing templates and quoting checklists that include a field for maximum ring outer diameter when assigning EQ-P2-L2-RR03 will be updated to the value stated below.
- Training materials: Operator training materials that include machine capability summaries for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 will be annotated to reflect the new consolidated value.

Implementation
- Declarative change: The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill EQ-P2-L2-RR03 is 1525 mm. This value is the authoritative specification to be used in all planning, execution, and documentation related to rings processed on EQ-P2-L2-RR03.
- Document revisions: Initiate controlled revision of MM-P2-L2-RR03 to record the value above in the capacity table and equipment remarks. Update SOP-P2-L2-05 to include the value above in the setup acceptance criteria and the pre-run checklist. Include a reference to SB-1017 where guarding or handling limits are cited, ensuring no contradictions exist.
- Implementation steps:
  - Revision owner in Maintenance will update MM-P2-L2-RR03 and submit changes through document control for release.
  - Process owner will update SOP-P2-L2-05 and distribute the controlled revision to the operations group.
  - Safety officer will review SB-1017 cross-references and document any required mitigation or note that current safety controls are adequate for the stated maximum.
  - Production planners will update job templates and quoting checklists in the planning system to use the stated maximum as a gating parameter for assignment to EQ-P2-L2-RR03.
  - Training coordinator will schedule targeted briefings for operators and maintenance personnel to ensure the updated capability is understood and applied.
- Examples and application notes:
  - When evaluating a new job for EQ-P2-L2-RR03, confirm the ring outer diameter parameter on the customer drawing or job specification does not exceed the value stated above. If the required diameter exceeds the value, route to alternative equipment or initiate an engineering review for special handling.
  - For tooling selection, confirm tooling assemblies and backup rolls are suitable for rings with outer diameter up to the stated value and document the verification in the setup record.
  - During pre-run inspection, the setup checklist in SOP-P2-L2-05 shall include a signed acknowledgement that the ring outer diameter does not exceed the value stated above and that handling fixtures are rated accordingly.

Records to keep
- Revision history entries for MM-P2-L2-RR03 and SOP-P2-L2-05 documenting the change and approvals.
- Affected job records and route selection evidence where EQ-P2-L2-RR03 capability was evaluated using the stated maximum.
- Training attendance logs and signed operator acknowledgements that reference the updated capability.
- Safety review notes linking SB-1017 to the stated maximum and any action items closed or deferred with justification.
- Maintenance verification checklist entries confirming that tooling and handling fixtures were reviewed for compatibility with the stated maximum during the next scheduled verification activity.

Approvals
- Maintenance manager: signatory approval for update to MM-P2-L2-RR03 and equipment records.
- Process engineering: signatory approval for update to SOP-P2-L2-05 and process routing.
- Safety: signatory concurrence that SB-1017 controls are applicable or documentation of required mitigation.
- Operations management: signatory confirmation that training and planning changes will be executed and monitored.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L2-RR03
- SB-1017
- SOP-P2-L2-05

Notes
- This ECN is a controlled change. All updates to the cited documents shall be completed and record copies placed in the document control system prior to routing new jobs to EQ-P2-L2-RR03 that depend on diameter capability confirmation.

# FAQ-001 Engineering FAQ #1
Revision: Rev A

Q: What torque should be used on the main ram bolt for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)?
A: The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m. Background: This torque value is set to maintain clamping preload on the ram assembly without overstressing the bolt or mating threads. Rationale: Using the specified torque ensures the ram remains secure under operational loads and minimizes fretting and relative movement at the joint. Example procedure: clean threads, apply manufacturer‑approved lubricant to the bolt shank and threads as specified in EQ-P1-L3-HP02 maintenance references, and use a calibrated torque wrench to apply 1330 N·m. Records to keep: torque application log entry showing equipment id EQ-P1-L3-HP02, bolt identifier, technician name, tool calibration id, and confirmation that 1330 N·m was achieved. See ECN-2026-034 for the associated design change rationale and SB-1017 for special bolting precautions.

Q: What is the lubrication interval for the main roll bearing on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01)?
A: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 120 hours. Background: Regular lubrication maintains film strength in the bearing contact and removes heat and contaminants. Rationale: The 120 hours service interval balances lubricant life, bearing temperature rise, and production duty for the bearing application specified in EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Example application: top up or renew grease type approved for the bearing following locked‑out mill conditions; perform visual checks at lubricant points between scheduled lubrication events. Records to keep: lubrication log for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 listing date/time, operating hours counter reading at service (if available), lubricant batch/lot id, amount or cartridge id used, technician initials, and any anomalies observed. See SOP-P2-L2-04 for procedural steps and ECN-2026-034 for any post‑modification lubrication notes.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01)?
A: The system pressure limit for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 330 bar. Background: The pressure limit reflects component rating for the hydraulic circuit and the safety margin required by the press design. Rationale: Operating at or below 330 bar ensures seals, hoses, valves, and actuators remain within their rated capabilities and reduces risk of catastrophic failure. Example operational control: verify pressure gauge readings and relief valve settings against the 330 bar limit before press operation; do not permit operations that cause excursions above 330 bar. Records to keep: pressure verification record for EQ-P3-L1-HP01 capturing gauge calibration reference, pre‑operation pressure check, relief valve set confirmation, operator name, and any corrective actions taken if readings approach the 330 bar limit. Reference ECN-2026-034 for design acceptance and SB-1017 for any special hydraulic system instructions.

Q: What torque should be used on the mandrel clamp bolts for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03)?
A: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Background: Correct clamp bolt torque secures the mandrel to resist torsional and radial loads during ring forming. Rationale: Specifying 620 N·m provides sufficient clamp force to prevent slippage while avoiding overstress of the clamp hardware or mandrel assembly. Example procedure: degrease mating surfaces, finger‑start bolts, torque in a star or sequence recommended for the clamp geometry, and use a calibrated torque wrench to reach 620 N·m. Records to keep: clamping torque record for EQ-P2-L2-RR03 including bolt identifiers, torque tool calibration id, operator, and confirmation that 620 N·m was achieved. See SOP-P2-L2-04 for clamp sequencing and ECN-2026-034 for any design notes affecting clamp torque.

Q: What is the maximum allowable ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03)?
A: The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 1525 mm. Background: The outer diameter limit is driven by roll contact geometry, mandrel capacity, and guarding envelope for EQ-P2-L2-RR03. Rationale: Adhering to the 1525 mm limit prevents interference with roll frames, maintains safe clearances for guards, and ensures accurate rolling profiles. Example planning: for parts approaching the 1525 mm limit, confirm tooling setup, verify guard positions, and coordinate handling fixtures rated for that diameter. Records to keep: part setup record listing final ring outer diameter measurement, tooling identifiers, operator name, and any deviations or concessions approved per ECN-2026-034. See SB-1017 for special handling notes and SOP-P2-L2-04 for setup and measurement procedures.

# FAQ-002 Engineering FAQ #2
Revision: Rev A

Q1: What lubricant should be used for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01)?
A1: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-709 for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01). Background: This lubricant was selected for its compatibility with the cabinet materials, shot media, and seals. Rationale: Using the specified part eliminates variability that can cause premature wear of moving parts and reduces contamination of the blast media. Example: When replacing the supply on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, verify the container label matches CFW-LUB-709 before transfer. Records to keep: retain supply receipts and the equipment lubrication log entry that cites the container lot or batch linked to CFW-LUB-709. Refer to QS-PROC-10 for acceptance sampling and receiving checks.

Q2: What is the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01)?
A2: Tighten blast wheel liner bolts on Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) to 105 N·m. Background: Proper bolt torque secures the liner to prevent movement during operation and maintains wheel balance. Rationale: 105 N·m was determined to provide sufficient clamp force without overstressing the liner bolt threads or the liner material. Example: When replacing a worn liner, torque bolts to 105 N·m in a star pattern to distribute clamp load evenly. Records to keep: document the torque event in the maintenance work order including the equipment id EQ-P3-L3-SB01, date, technician initials, and the torque value 105 N·m. Consult SOP-P1-L3-04 for bolting procedures and torque verification steps.

Q3: What lubricant should be used for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03)?
A3: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-725 for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03). Background: CFW-LUB-725 is specified for high-temperature-bearing housings and feed mechanisms associated with induction heating lines. Rationale: Specifying CFW-LUB-725 ensures consistent lubrication film thickness and protects components exposed to thermal cycling. Example: During scheduled servicing of EQ-P2-L3-IH03, drain and apply CFW-LUB-725 to the designated lubrication points as listed in the machine lubrication chart. Records to keep: maintain the lubricant change record referencing CFW-LUB-725, equipment id EQ-P2-L3-IH03, and supplier batch details. See SOP-P2-L3-05 for lubrication point diagrams and service steps.

Q4: How long should the spindle warm-up for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) be?
A4: The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 27 minutes. Background: Controlled warm-up reduces thermal gradient across the spindle and bearings, improving geometric stability at the start of a production run. Rationale: A 27 minutes warm-up was derived from spindle thermal response tests and balances production throughput with dimensional control. Example: Before critical lots, follow the warm-up cycle on EQ-P1-L3-CN03 for 27 minutes at the machine default idle profile to stabilize spindle temperature. Records to keep: log warm-up start and completion times in the machine run log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and note any deviations from the 27 minutes duration. Reference QS-PROC-10 for production readiness checks.

Background: The setpoint defines the target temperature for the austenitizing stage to achieve the desired metallurgical condition prior to quench. Rationale: 845 °C was selected to match alloy process windows and to ensure consistent phase transformation for downstream hardness and microstructure requirements. Example: When running the austenitizing recipe for EQ-P2-L3-HT02, confirm the controller is set to 845 °C and that the profile holds at the setpoint for the prescribed soak time per the furnace procedure. Records to keep: maintain the furnace run sheet showing the setpoint 845 °C, actual recorded temperatures, lot numbers, and operator initials for traceability. See SOP-P2-L3-05 for furnace loading and monitoring instructions.

Related documents: QS-PROC-10, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P2-L3-05

Document control notes: update the equipment lubrication logs, torque verification records, machine run logs, and furnace run sheets as described above to support auditability and continual improvement.

# FAQ-003 Engineering FAQ #3

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the required thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and why is that interval specified?
A: The thermocouple calibration interval for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 55 days. Rationale: this interval balances traceability needs and operational risk for parts processed in that furnace, based on historical drift data and quality requirements documented in MM-P2-L4-HT02. Practical guidance: schedule calibrations in the maintenance planner to coincide with planned furnace shutdowns where possible to avoid production disruption. Records to keep: calibration certificate, serial number of the thermocouple, date of calibration, technician name, and any deviation noted during calibration. Retain records per MM-P2-L4-HT02.

Q: What is the documented coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) and what are the implications of low flow?
A: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. Rationale: maintaining the minimum prevents excessive coil temperature rise, preserves coil life, and avoids thermal damage to adjacent components. Operational checks: verify flow at start-up and monitor trend data where installed. Action on low flow: if flow cannot be restored to the minimum, shut down the heater per SOP-P2-L4-01 until the cooling system is repaired. Records to keep: start-up flow verification log, any corrective maintenance actions, and parts replaced. See SB-1048 for failure-mode examples related to inadequate cooling.

Q: Which lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and how should it be managed?
A: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is CFW-LUB-450. Rationale: the part number identifies the approved lubricant grade compatible with press seals and system materials, ensuring consistent wear protection and hydraulic cleanliness. Inventory management: ensure stock levels are adequate and that only CFW-LUB-450 is used on this press. Application guidance: follow the lubrication points and intervals in SOP-P2-L4-01 and note each lubricant top-up or change in the press maintenance record. Records to keep: batch/lot number of lubricant used, date applied, quantity, and technician initials. Reference SB-1048 for contamination control procedures.

Q: What is the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) and what checks should follow torque application?
A: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Rationale: the specified torque ensures clamp integrity during rolling loads without over-stressing bolt or clamp components. Procedure: use a calibrated torque wrench and apply the torque in the tightening pattern specified in SOP-P2-L4-01. Post-torque checks: inspect for proper seating of clamps, verify bolt threads and washers are free of debris, and log torque values in the equipment maintenance record. Records to keep: torque tool calibration certificate, date, applied torque value, and operator signature. See MM-P2-L4-HT02 for bolt replacement criteria if inspection indicates damage.

Q: What is the coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) and how should deviations be recorded and acted upon?
A: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min. Rationale: this minimum is set to maintain coil temperature within design limits for that specific heater geometry and process duty. Monitoring and action: verify flow at start-up and continuously where instrumentation exists; if flow drops below the minimum, follow the shutdown and lockout procedures in SOP-P2-L4-01 until the issue is resolved. Documentation: create an event log entry with time of deviation, measured flow value, corrective actions taken, and parts replaced or repaired. Retain these logs with the preventive maintenance record and reference SB-1048 if the deviation appears related to a systemic cooling issue.

text:
# FAQ-004 Engineering FAQ #4
Revision: Rev A

Question: What lubricant should be used on Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) and why?
Answer:
The lubricant part number for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is CFW-LUB-225. Use of CFW-LUB-225 is mandatory for the specified bearing housings and live tooling interfaces because its viscosity and additive package are matched to the mill's charge and contact conditions. Background: the mill OEM validation and earlier field trials used CFW-LUB-225 to control wear and particle generation without compromising ring surface quality. Rationale: consistent lubricant specification reduces variability in rolling forces and extends component life of rollers and housings. Example application: apply to bearing grease points and external gearing per the machine lubrication map. Records to keep: lubricator tag showing product batch, application date, and technician initials; maintenance log entry referencing CFW-LUB-225 and any observed anomalies. See related change notices: ECN-2026-010 and ECN-2026-046 for revisions to lubrication points and approved supplier changes.

Question: What is the correct target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) prior to machining?
Answer:
The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Background: final machining dimensional stability and metallurgical condition are sensitive to billet temperature; the target above balances thermal expansion for predictable machining allowances and material ductility for tooling life. Rationale: holding at 1235 °C ensures the billet reaches the intended microstructural state for the downstream machining process without promoting excessive grain growth. Examples: when the induction heater control reaches and holds 1235 °C, allow stabilization time per the control algorithm before start of machining cycle. Records to keep: billet temperature logs showing attainment of 1235 °C, heater run IDs, billet serial, and operator sign-off. Reference procedures and status in ECN-2026-046 for any recent setpoint validation updates.

Question: What austenitizing setpoint should be used in Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02)?
Answer:
The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is 885 °C. Background: the selected austenitizing setpoint is critical to achieving the required hardness profile and grain refinement for the parts processed in this furnace. Rationale: 885 °C is validated against part chemistry and quench response to produce the target microstructure while limiting retained austenite and excessive grain growth. Examples: follow the heat treat load schedule that ramps to 885 °C and holds as required by the process recipe. Records to keep: furnace cycle record with setpoint 885 °C, load identification, thermocouple calibration reference, and post-heat-treat hardness verification. See SOP-P2-L4-04 for furnace operation and monitoring requirements.

Question: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03)?
Answer:
The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Background: adequate cooling flow through the induction coil circuit prevents coil overtemperature, deformation, and insulation failure. Rationale: maintaining a minimum of 65 L/min ensures sufficient heat extraction under expected load profiles and prevents localized boiling or cavitation in the coil circuit. Examples: verify flow during startup and monitor for drops below 65 L/min; if flow falls below 65 L/min, de-energize the heater per interlock logic and follow troubleshooting steps. Records to keep: flow meter output logs indicating at-or-above 65 L/min, maintenance tickets for any pump or filter work, and operator incident reports. Refer to ECN-2026-010 for recent modifications to the cooling circuit.

Question: How long should the spindle warm-up procedure run on Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) before charged work is allowed?
Answer:
The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes. Background: spindle thermal stabilization reduces runout changes and maintains dimensional accuracy during the first operations after a cold start. Rationale: a fixed warm-up time of 21 minutes allows bearings, spindle housing, and thermal compensation systems to reach steady state so that compensation tables are valid. Examples: run the machine warm-up program and verify spindle temperature trend is stable before loading production work; if spindle shows abnormal thermal drift during or after the 21 minutes, escalate to maintenance. Records to keep: warm-up log documenting start time, completion time equal to 21 minutes later, operator initials, and any deviations. Consult SOP-P2-L4-04 for warm-up program checklist and verification steps.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01)?

Background: CFW-LUB-315 is the approved lubricant grade for bearings and sliding surfaces on the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Rationale: Using the specified part ensures compatibility with the metallurgy of the mill components and the environmental conditions in the Heat Treat area. Example application: When replenishing the reservoir or performing a lubrication point fill, confirm the tag on the lubricant container reads CFW-LUB-315 and match the container lot code to the material requisition. Records to keep: Log the container part number, container lot code, date of use, and the technician initials in the lubrication log tied to EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Question: What mandrel clamp bolt torque is specified for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01)?
Answer: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m. Background: The specified torque value applies to the clamping bolts that secure the mandrel assembly on the Heat Treat mill identified as EQ-P2-L4-RR01. Rationale: Applying the correct torque ensures clamping preload sufficient to maintain mandrel alignment without yielding the bolt or inducing bolt fatigue. Example procedure: During a mandrel change or after a mandrel maintenance event, apply torque to each clamping bolt using a calibrated torque wrench set to 525 N·m and follow the tightening pattern specified in the maintenance manual. Records to keep: Record the torque wrench serial number, calibration date, applied torque value (525 N·m), date, and the technician performing the operation in the bolting maintenance worksheet. Refer to MM-P1-L2-RR01 for the tightening sequence and SOP-P2-L4-03 for bolt handling and inspection steps.

Question: What is the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01)?
