Background: The clamping system on the Ring Rolling mill EQ-P1-L2-RR01 requires a different torque setting than other mills due to design and bolt grade differences. Rationale: A 395 N·m setting provides the intended clamp force without overstressing the bolt or the mandrel housing, preserving component life and maintaining process stability. Example procedure: Tighten bolts in the specified sequence from the maintenance manual using a calibrated torque tool and verify each bolt reaches 395 N·m. If any bolt does not hold the set torque, follow the inspection steps in SOP-P2-L4-03. Records to keep: Document the torque application event, noting the tool used and calibration traceability, the value applied (395 N·m), and corrective actions if any deviations occurred. Link the entry to MM-P1-L2-RR01 for torque sequence confirmation.

Question: Which lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02)?
Answer: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195. Background: CFW-LUB-195 is the approved hydraulic and lubrication fluid for the Heat Treat press EQ-P1-L4-HP02. Rationale: Using the approved part number avoids fluid incompatibility with seals, pumps, and valves and ensures the intended viscosity and additive package are present for safe operation. Example application: When topping up the hydraulic reservoir, verify the container label CFW-LUB-195 and document the lot number and quantity added. If changing fluid supplier or batch, follow the contamination control and flushing steps in SOP-P3-L4-05. Records to keep: Maintain a hydraulic fluid change log that includes the part number CFW-LUB-195, container lot, date, technician initials, and results of any fluid analysis. Reference SOP-P3-L4-05 for fluid handling and MM-P1-L2-RR01 for storage location and segregation.

Question: What is the dust collector alarm setpoint for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03)?

Background: The alarm setpoint of 1240 Pa corresponds to the differential pressure across the dust collector filter bank for the shot blast cabinet EQ-P2-L1-SB03. Rationale: The 1240 Pa threshold indicates a filter loading condition requiring filter inspection or change to maintain airflow and capture efficiency without risking damage to the collector or process downtime. Example response: When the instrument indicates the differential pressure has reached 1240 Pa, initiate the filter change and housekeeping procedure outlined in SOP-P2-L4-03. Verify the replacement filters are compatible with the collector and record the before and after differential readings. Records to keep: Log the alarm event with timestamp, measured differential pressure at 1240 Pa, actions taken, replacement filter part numbers, and the technician performing the work. Maintain these entries against the EQ-P2-L1-SB03 equipment record and coordinate with MM-P1-L2-RR01 to schedule follow-up inspections.

# FAQ-006 Engineering FAQ #6

Revision: Rev A

Related documents: MM-P2-L1-SB03, SB-1031, SB-1046

Q: What is the recommended way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01), and why is it set that way?
A: The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Background: the interval is set to maintain consistent film thickness on the guideways and ball screws under the machine's duty cycle and contamination risk in the heat treat cell. Rationale: frequent top-up prevents dry starts and reduces abrasive wear from furnace-borne particulates. Practical example: if the machine is run in a high-cycle production pattern that exposes it to frequent thermal cycling and dust, follow the stated interval exactly and avoid extending it. Records to keep: log each refill with date, time, technician initials, lube product batch, and pre- and post-refill way readings where applicable. Reference inspection notes to MM-P2-L1-SB03 for the lube material specification and acceptable contamination limits.

Q: How often should shot media be topped up for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), and what indicators should trigger an immediate top-up?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours. Background: media attrition and carryout in a hot forging environment reduces media size distribution and effective cleaning energy over time. Rationale: maintaining target media volume and size distribution preserves blast coverage and prevents accelerated wear of cabinet components. Indicators for immediate top-up: visible reduction in blast performance, increased cycle time to achieve specified cleanliness, or elevated media fines reported during sampling. Practical example: when a process audit shows escalating rework rates tied to surface cleanliness, perform a top-up and record pre- and post-top-up blast performance metrics. Records to keep: media top-up log entry with equipment id, media type, supplier lot number, operator initials, and inspection comments. See SB-1031 for media handling and disposal guidance.

Q: What is the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why must it be followed exactly?
A: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Background: proper liner bolt torque ensures even clamping of liners, preventing vibration, liner movement, and accelerated wear of wheel components. Rationale: under-torqued bolts allow relative motion that leads to fretting and fatigue; over-torqued bolts can distort liners and compromise bolt integrity. Practical example: during liner replacement, torque bolts to the specified value using a calibrated torque wrench; sequence the torque steps evenly across the liner circumference to achieve uniform seating. Records to keep: maintenance report listing equipment id, torque tool serial number, calibration date, technician initials, liner part id, and bolt torque confirmation for each bolt position. Cross-reference SB-1046 for wheel assembly replacement procedures.

Q: What torque should be applied to the blast wheel liner bolts for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and what special precautions apply?
A: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. Background: this cabinet uses a different liner material and bolt specification that requires a lower clamping torque to prevent thread stripping and to account for thermal expansion in the Hot Forge environment. Rationale: using the specified torque prevents both mechanical failure and distortion while maintaining acceptable sealing between liner sections. Practical example: before torquing, clean bolt threads and apply the manufacturer-specified anti-seize per MM-P2-L1-SB03; then torque each bolt to the specified value and record the result. Records to keep: bolt torque checklist including equipment id, bolt positions, torque achieved, tool calibration id, technician initials, and any deviations or corrective actions taken.

Q: What is the correct main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and what documentation should accompany the torque operation?
A: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Background: the main ram bolts are primary load carriers; correct torque is critical to maintain clamping preload and prevent joint loosening under forging loads. Rationale: insufficient preload can lead to fatigue failure of the bolts and loss of positional accuracy; correct torque ensures joint integrity while allowing for predictable tension under load. Practical example: perform torque application with a calibrated hydraulic torque wrench rated for the specified value; use the manufacturer-recommended tightening sequence and re-check after initial warm-up cycles as specified in the press maintenance schedule. Records to keep: torque application report containing equipment id, bolt identifiers, final torque readings, torque tool serial number and calibration certificate reference, technician initials, and any re-tightening actions. See SB-1046 for bolting safety procedures and MM-P2-L1-SB03 for approved lubricants and anti-seize compounds to use on threads prior to torqueing.

End of FAQ.

Background: The shot blast cabinet uses a specific lubricant for media reclamation bearings and seals that is compatible with abrasive media and dust-laden environments. Question: What lubricant should be used for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) and why?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-611 for EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Rationale: this formulation was selected during the last tooling qualification for turning operations because it balances film strength and washout resistance for our high-feed carbide inserts in this machine configuration. Background: the machine receives mixed ferrous and alloy workpieces and the lubricant must be compatible with downstream cleaning and heat treat processes. Example use case: when running continuous turning on long runs where surface finish retention is required, CFW-LUB-611 has shown improved tool life compared to general-purpose shop oils. Records to keep: log the part number used on the job traveler, note batch code of the lubricant dispenser, and attach a sampling result to the maintenance record for EQ-P3-L3-CN02. See ECN-2026-013 for the change notice that authorized the current lubricant selection and SOP-P1-L4-03 for the machine lubrication procedure.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) and what special handling is required?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-961 for EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Rationale: ring rolling requires a high-pressure boundary lubricant with anti-stick properties to prevent smearing on the mandrel and to maintain surface integrity of the thin wall sections produced. Background: radial ring rolling imposes sliding contact at high contact pressures and this lubricant reduces the risk of surface defects. Special handling: store CFW-LUB-961 in a dedicated, labeled dispenser to prevent cross-contamination and use dedicated filling tools for the ring rolling system. Records to keep: include the dispenser refill date and operator initials in the lubrication log, and retain a sample certificate of analysis with the RR01 maintenance file. Refer to SB-1043 for ring rolling surface defect guidance and to ECN-2026-013 for the approved material list.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) and are there downstream compatibility concerns?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 for EQ-P1-L4-CN01. Rationale: heat treat shop machining requires lubricants that are compatible with furnace loading and that do not introduce residues that affect austenitizing or quench behavior. Background: the heat treat area has classification and inspection constraints for residues; CFW-LUB-477 meets those constraints and has been validated for ease of removal during standard cleaning prior to furnace entry. Compatibility note: always confirm that the lubricant batch certificate is present and that no additives have been introduced that are outside the approved specification for the heat treat line. Records to keep: attach lubricant batch certificate and cleaning verification to the furnace load paperwork for parts processed from EQ-P1-L4-CN01. See SOP-P1-L4-03 for cleaning and furnace loading steps.

Question: What austenitizing setpoint should be used for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) and how should it be documented?
Answer: The austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 is 885 °C. Rationale: this setpoint was selected to achieve the required transformation for the specified alloy family while maintaining grain control per material specification. Background: setpoint adherence must be verified with calibrated thermocouple data and certified chart or digital record. Documentation: record the setpoint as part of the heat treat cycle sheet, capture temperature profile traces for each furnace load, and archive the profile with the job lot file. Records to keep: retain the furnace profile, operator start and stop signatures, and any deviation notes in the heat treat batch record. See ECN-2026-013 for the authorization of the setpoint and SOP-P1-L4-03 for the heat treat recording procedure.

Question: What is the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) and what monitoring is required?
Answer: The coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min. Rationale: induction coil cooling must maintain sufficient flow to prevent localized overheating and premature coil failure; the minimum was determined based on coil geometry and power loading. Monitoring: continuous flow indication is required at the operator station and interlock thresholds must be set to prevent operation below the minimum. Actions on low flow: operators must halt the heater feed and tag out the circuit until flow is restored to at least the specified minimum and the system is inspected for blockage or pump issues. Records to keep: log flow readings per shift, record any trips or interlock events, and file corrective action documentation with the equipment maintenance log for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Refer to SB-1043 for failure modes related to coil cooling and to SOP-P1-L4-03 for the procedure to verify cooling systems prior to production start.

Q: What is the recommended spindle warm-up procedure for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) and why is it required?

Background: A controlled warm-up minimizes thermal gradients in the spindle, reducing runout drift during the first pieces after machine start. Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach a stable thermal state reduces scrap risk and tool wear caused by changes in geometry during production start-up. Example procedure: Power the machine control, run the spindle at low to medium rpm per OEM guidance until the elapsed warm-up reaches the specified time, then proceed with normal cut verification. text:
# FAQ-010 Engineering FAQ #10

Revision: Rev A

Related documents: MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3, SOP-P1-L1-01, SOP-P2-L3-02

---

Question: What is the required spindle warm-up time before operating Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02), and why is it necessary?
Answer:
Background: Proper spindle thermal stabilization reduces axial and radial runout changes that cause dimensional drift during turning. The machine vendor and maintenance team validated a warm-up interval to reach thermal equilibrium of bearings, spindle housing, and drive components.
Requirement: The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes.
Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach thermal equilibrium minimizes part scrap and spindle bearing wear. The warm-up reduces the likelihood of mid-run compensations that introduce surface finish defects.
Example: For a production run that will run continuous turning cycles, start the warm-up immediately after initial power-up and before loading the first part. If the machine is already at operating environment equilibrium, perform the same warm-up prior to any precision job.
Records to keep: Log the operator start time and completion time in the machine start checklist and attach to the job traveler. Reference SOP-P1-L1-01 for start-up checklist format and retention requirements.

---

Question: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #3, and how was this value determined?
Answer:
Background: Induction coils require sufficient flow to remove resistive and proximity heating from coil conductors and maintain insulation life. Flow minima are set based on thermal modeling and manufacturer coil specifications.
Requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min.
Rationale: Maintaining at least this flow prevents localized overheating in coil turns and reduces the risk of dielectric breakdown in the coil insulation. This value aligns with the coil vendor test sheet and the facility hydraulic capability documented in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3.
Example: If measured flow approaches the minimum, reduce induction power and extend heating cycles until flow is restored. Do not increase power to compensate for low flow.
Records to keep: Record inlet and outlet temperatures, flow readout, and any flow adjustment actions in the induction heater log. Attach periodic verification against MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 during preventive maintenance.

---

Question: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2, and what actions should be taken if the flow is below minimum?
Answer:
Background: Ring rolling process coils operate under high duty cycles; inadequate cooling accelerates coil degradation and can lead to unscheduled downtime.
Requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min.
Rationale: The specified minimum prevents thermal runaway in the coil and ensures stable heating profiles for the billet. Operation below this flow increases risk of coil failure and variances in heating uniformity.
Example: When the flow indicator shows below the minimum, pause the heater operation and notify maintenance. Follow the isolation and lockout steps in SOP-P2-L3-02 before any intervention on the cooling circuit.
Records to keep: Document the flow measurement, time of detection, actions taken, and parts affected in the downtime log and the coil inspection record.

---

Question: What is the maximum allowed quench delay for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, and why is controlling delay important?
Answer:
Background: Quench delay is the time between removal from furnace soak and immersion in quench medium. Excessive delay can produce undesirable metallurgical transformations, reducing mechanical properties.
Requirement: The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.
Rationale: Limiting delay preserves the austenite-to-martensite transformation path required for specified hardness and toughness. The maximum reflects process trials and critical part acceptance criteria.
Example: For parts requiring tight hardness bands, synchronize furnace doors and quench station operation to maintain immersion within the maximum delay. If an operator error causes a delay beyond the maximum, segregate the affected lot and notify heat treat engineering for rework disposition.
Records to keep: Include time-out and time-in stamps for each loaded part in the heat treat log. Retain nondestructive test results and hardness readings for lots where delay approaches the maximum.

---

Question: What triggers the dust collector alarm on the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2, and what steps should be taken when it trips?
Answer:
Background: Pressure drop across filter media indicates loading or blockage; alarms prevent overpressuring the blast cabinet and maintain capture efficiency.
Requirement: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa.
Rationale: The alarm setpoint protects downstream filters and ensures blast cabinet airflow remains within capture design. Addressing alarms promptly prevents abrasive rebound issues and maintains workplace air quality.
Example: When the alarm reads at or above the setpoint, stop the shot blast operation, secure the cabinet per SOP-P2-L3-02, and inspect prefilters and baghouse elements. Replace or clean filter elements per MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 procedures if required.
Records to keep: Log alarm time, measured pressure reading, corrective actions taken, filter element identification, and replacement records in the dust collector maintenance log. Attach particulate intake and exhaust test results where applicable.

# FAQ-011 Engineering FAQ #11

Revision: Rev A

Question One — What is the correct lubricant part number to stock and use on Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is CFW-LUB-188.

Background and rationale:
- The induction coil support bearings and the drive coupling on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 were qualified with lubricant CFW-LUB-188 during commissioning. Using the specified part ensures compatibility with the bearing materials and the high frequency environment of the heater.
- Using the exact part CFW-LUB-188 avoids cross-contamination risks from general-purpose lubricants that are not rated for induction equipment.

Examples of correct usage:
- Replace grease during scheduled bearing maintenance with CFW-LUB-188 as described in the equipment lubrication checklist in SOP-P1-L1-01.
- Use OEM-approved dispensing fittings and avoid mixing partial containers from different lots.

Records to keep:
- Log of lubricant lot number, quantity used, and maintenance task in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P1-L1-IH03.
- Retain a copy of the purchase order referencing CFW-LUB-188 for traceability.

See also: SOP-P1-L1-01 for lubrication procedures and SB-1029 for material compatibility guidance.

Question Two — What lubricant part number must be used for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497.

Background and rationale:
- EQ-P1-L3-HP02 requires a hydraulic fluid and slideway compound that meet specific viscosity and anti-wear characteristics. CFW-LUB-497 was selected during equipment validation for those properties and for compatibility with seal materials.
- Use of CFW-LUB-497 supports consistent press performance and reduces the likelihood of seal degradation.

Examples of correct usage:
- Top up hydraulic reservoirs and apply slideway lubricant using CFW-LUB-497 per the press maintenance routine in SOP-P1-L3-04.
- When changing suppliers, verify that the replacement item references CFW-LUB-497 to maintain specification continuity.

Records to keep:
- Hydraulic fluid change or top-up entries in the press maintenance log specifying CFW-LUB-497.
- Batch numbers of CFW-LUB-497 used and the maintenance technician initials for audit.

See also: SOP-P1-L3-04 for press hydraulic procedures and SB-1029 for lubricant storage requirements.

Question Three — Which lubricant part number is specified for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02)?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is CFW-LUB-930.

Background and rationale:
- The high-load contact points and worm geartrain in EQ-P3-L2-RR02 require an extreme pressure lubricant with the additives found in CFW-LUB-930. This selection is required to maintain gear life under rolling loads.
- Using CFW-LUB-930 minimizes wear patterns known to cause dimensional drift in ring rolling applications.

Examples of correct usage:
- Apply CFW-LUB-930 to gearboxes and point lubrication locations during scheduled service intervals called out in the equipment maintenance plan.
- For spot adjustments during production, apply small measured amounts of CFW-LUB-930 to prevent over-application.

Records to keep:
- Gearbox oil change records that list CFW-LUB-930 and associated filtration steps.
- Infrared or vibration monitoring notes after lubricant changes to document return to baseline.

See also: SB-1029 for lubricant selection criteria and SOP-P1-L3-04 for gear maintenance steps.

Question Four — What is the thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02)?
Answer — The thermocouple calibration interval for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 50 days.

Background and rationale:
- The process control for EQ-P2-L3-HT02 depends on accurate thermocouple readings to meet part specification. A calibration interval of 50 days balances drift risk with calibration resource availability.
- Calibration frequency was set based on historical drift trends and criticality assessment in the process control plan.

Examples of correct usage:
- Schedule thermocouple calibration events in the calibration management system to recur every 50 days and notify responsible technicians in advance.
- When a furnace run shows temperature anomalies, perform an out-of-cycle verification even if the 50 days interval has not elapsed.

Records to keep:
- Calibration certificates for each thermocouple indicating date of calibration and acceptance criteria, filed under EQ-P2-L3-HT02.
- Calibration adjustment notes and any corrective actions taken as a result of calibration findings.

See also: SB-1029 for calibration traceability and SOP-P1-L3-04 for calibration procedure steps.

Question Five — What is the coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
Answer — The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours.

Background and rationale:
- Coil life and insulation integrity on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 are monitored by runtime. An inspection interval of 290 hours was established from life testing and risk assessment to detect early signs of wear before failure.
- Runtime-based inspection is preferred over calendar intervals for equipment with variable duty cycles.

Examples of correct usage:
- Track cumulative runtime on the heater control panel and schedule coil inspections when runtime reaches the 290 hours threshold.
- During inspection, look for coating damage, loose connections, and signs of thermal degradation; document findings and remediate per SOP-P1-L1-01.

Records to keep:
- Coil inspection checklist entries tied to EQ-P1-L1-IH03 runtime, including inspector name and disposition.
- Repair or replacement records referencing the 290 hours inspection trigger.

See also: SOP-P1-L1-01 for inspection checklists and SB-1029 for coil handling precautions.

# FAQ-012 Engineering FAQ #12
Revision: Rev A

Q: What should I do when the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) trips?
A: Background: The dust collector pressure differential is an indicator of media loading or airflow restriction. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Rationale: This alarm value is the confirmed threshold for initiating filter inspection and cleaning to prevent loss of blast quality and motor overload. Actions:
- Stop material flow to the cabinet and place the cell in a safe condition.
- Visually inspect the collector housing and filter access panels for signs of damage or bypass.
- Perform filter cleaning per the maintenance checklist in SB-1033.
- If cleaning restores acceptable airflow, document the event and restart operations.
Records to keep: filter inspection checklist, filter cleaning log, and the alarm event entry in the maintenance log. Reference: see SB-1033 and QS-PROC-08 for procedural and quality disposition requirements.

Q: What is the acceptable target for billet temperature before charging into Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
A: Background: Proper billet temperature is critical for forging grain structure and die life. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C. Rationale: Operators must confirm billets reach this target prior to transfer to the forge to ensure material plasticity and reduce risk of internal defects. Actions:
- Verify process temperature readouts against target prior to transfer.
- If readout is below target, hold the billet in the heater and follow heat-up practices in SOP-P3-L3-02 until target is achieved.
- If readout is above target, follow cooling and qualification steps in QS-PROC-08 before forging.
Records to keep: temperature logs, operator shift handover notes, and any nonconformance reports per QS-PROC-08. Reference: SOP-P3-L3-02 for heater operation and QS-PROC-08 for disposition.

Q: How frequently should way lube be refilled on Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02)?
A: Background: Way lubrication prevents wear and maintains machining accuracy and surface finish. The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. Rationale: This interval reflects combined factors of machine duty cycle and lubricant drain characteristics; adherence reduces risk of accelerated wear and guideway scoring. Actions:
- Schedule refills to align with routine machine checks and documented preventive maintenance.
- During refill, inspect reservoirs and feed lines for contamination and verify lubricant grade.
- Log refill actions including machine ID, lubricant lot, and operator initials.
Records to keep: way lube refill log entry and machine preventive maintenance record. Reference: SOP-P3-L3-02 for lubricant handling and QS-PROC-08 for quality records.

Q: What setpoint should be used for the austenitizing stage in Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02)?
A: Background: Austenitizing temperature determines phase transformation necessary for subsequent cooling and mechanical properties. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Rationale: Use of this setpoint ensures the material attains the required austenitic structure without excessive grain growth. Actions:
- Program the furnace control to the specified setpoint and verify with independent temperature monitoring prior to start.
- Hold time and cooling profiles remain per the applicable heat treat procedure; deviations require approval and record in QS-PROC-08.
Records to keep: heat treatment cycle log, controlled atmosphere records if applicable, and post-heat-treat hardness or metallurgical test results. Reference: QS-PROC-08 for approval and SB-1033 for furnace safety checks.

Q: What is the minimum acceptable coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03)?
A: Background: Cooling water flow is critical to protect induction coil integrity and prevent overheating failures. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Rationale: Maintaining at least this flow prevents thermal damage and supports expected heater lifetime. Actions:
- Verify flow rate with the in-line flow indicator prior to and during operation.
- If flow drops below the minimum, halt induction current immediately and follow troubleshooting steps in SB-1033.
- Inspect inlet strainers, valves, and pump performance; restore flow and perform system test before returning to production.
Records to keep: flow check log, pump maintenance records, and any incident reports filed under QS-PROC-08. Reference: SB-1033 for emergency stop criteria and QS-PROC-08 for recordkeeping.

Related documents: QS-PROC-08, SB-1033, SOP-P3-L3-02

# FAQ-013 Engineering FAQ #13

Revision: Rev A

Question — What lubricant is specified for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) and why is it required?
Answer — The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is CFW-LUB-497. Background: CFW-LUB-497 is the manufacturer-approved hydraulic fluid selected for compatibility with the press seals, valve materials, and expected thermal conditions in the machining area. Rationale: Using the exact part number avoids seal degradation, oxidation, and varnish buildup that cause control issues and increased wear. Example: When replacing fluid during component exchange, order and fit CFW-LUB-497 only; mixing with non‑specified fluids has caused degraded servo response in similar units and requires tank flushes. Records to keep: maintenance log entries must record changeover date, serial of replacement containers, filter element serials, and the document reference MM-P2-L3-HT02 for any flushing or heat‑related procedures.

Question — What is the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) and how is it used in process control?
Answer — The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C. Background: The austenitizing setpoint defines the target soak temperature prior to quench and is essential to achieve the required microstructure prior to ring rolling operations. Rationale: Holding to the specified setpoint ensures transformation behavior that supports subsequent forming without cracking. Example: For a typical batch, the controller program is set to reach 870 °C and hold per the applicable heat treat cycle; operators verify ramp profile and soak with thermocouple readings and the control chart. Records to keep: furnace load sheets must record actual peak temperature, soak duration, chart copies, and any deviation reports. Reference SOPs and procedural links: see MM-P2-L3-HT02 for heat treat recording practice and SB-1045 for alloy-specific handling cues.

Question — What is the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) and how does it affect machine setup?
Answer — The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm. Background: The maximum outer diameter is a physical limitation determined by roll spacing, mandrel capacity, and handling clearances. Rationale: Respecting the maximum outer diameter prevents collisions, overtravel of feeds, and handling jams that can damage tooling and workpieces. Example: When programming a job, verify CAD nesting and transferred dimensions do not exceed 1415 mm; if stock enters the mill larger than this, use alternate equipment or pre‑trim to compliant size. Records to keep: setup sheets must include measured incoming blank diameters, final part diameter, and any engineering dispositions when approaching the maximum. See SB-1045 for mill capacity notes and SOP-P3-L3-05 for handling and fixturing procedures.

Question — What is the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) and what steps are required when servicing that joint?
Answer — The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Background: The main ram fastening is a critical clamped joint that retains alignment and load path integrity under forging forces. Rationale: Applying the specified torque ensures consistent clamp load and prevents bolt fatigue or joint slip. Example: During a ram replacement, torque bolts in the specified pattern using a calibrated wrench and verify readings against the torque device certification. Records to keep: torque application records must include bolt identifiers, torque device serial, operator initials, and post‑torque verification notes. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-05 for lock‑tightening sequence and inspection requirements.

Question — What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) and when is this setpoint applied?
Answer — The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Background: Distinct furnaces and part families require different austenitizing temperatures to attain target microstructures prior to downstream machining. Rationale: Applying the correct setpoint prevents over‑hardening or under‑austenitizing that would compromise machinability and final mechanical properties. Example: For finishing lots routed through EQ-P2-L3-HT02, controllers must be programmed for 845 °C and operators must log thermocouple profiles for each cycle. Records to keep: heat treat logs, part lot numbers, thermocouple calibration certificates, and any hold/retention lot labels must be filed per MM-P2-L3-HT02 and retained per document retention rules. For alloy‑specific notes consult SB-1045 and follow load handling per SOP-P3-L3-05.

Related documents: MM-P2-L3-HT02, SB-1045, SOP-P3-L3-05.

# FAQ-014 Engineering FAQ #14

Revision: Rev A

Q1 — What lubricant should be used for the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and where is it stocked?
A1 — The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-426. Background: CFW-LUB-426 was selected for its high-temperature stability and low carbonization characteristics appropriate to furnace internal bearings and slideways. Rationale: Using the specified part number prevents chemical incompatibility with furnace insulation and avoids accelerated deposit formation. Example use: apply CFW-LUB-426 to furnace door guide rails after cleaning with approved solvent and prior to cyclic loading. Records to keep: log part number used, batch/lot code from the lubricant container, application location (furnace ID), and the operator initials in the maintenance record. See also ECN-2026-033 for the approval history and MM-P2-L3-HT02 for heat treat lubrication procedures.

Q2 — What torque value is required for the main ram bolt on Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01)?
A2 — The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Background: This is the assembly torque established during press rebuild and verified by engineering stress analysis. Rationale: Applying the specified 1425 N·m ensures pre-load consistent with the press design and prevents cyclic loosening or fatigue failure of the fastener. Example procedure: torque the main ram bolt using a calibrated torque tool capable of reading the specified value; confirm calibration traceability in tool records. Records to keep: record the applied torque value, torque tool ID and calibration certificate reference, operator initials, and the maintenance work order. Refer to SB-1016 for bolt inspection acceptance criteria and ECN-2026-033 for any historical changes to assembly requirements.

Q3 — Which lubricant is specified for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02)?
A3 — The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is CFW-LUB-611. Background: CFW-LUB-611 is specified for spindle and guideway systems where low-viscosity, anti-wear properties are required. Rationale: Specifying CFW-LUB-611 avoids cross-contamination with other lubricant families that may degrade seals or bearings. Example use: during scheduled bearing service, drain the existing lubricant following the machining center procedure, flush as required, and apply CFW-LUB-611 to the spindle and guide components. Q4 — What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02)?
A4 — The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Background: The 845 °C austenitizing setpoint matches the process requirements for the tool steels commonly processed in Machining heat treatment and was validated during process qualification. Rationale: Maintaining the specified 845 °C setpoint is required to achieve the metallurgical phase transformation targets and final mechanical properties. Example control: verify setpoint programming in the furnace controller prior to a run, execute the documented temperature ramp and hold profile, and confirm with calibrated thermocouple readings as part of the process control records. Records to keep: furnace controller program settings, thermocouple verification data, lot identifier of charges processed, and process operator sign-off. See MM-P2-L3-HT02 for heat treat procedure details and ECN-2026-033 for formal setpoint approval documentation.

Q5 — What is the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and how should top-up be performed?
A5 — The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Background: The 33 hours top-up interval reflects operational experience balancing media degradation, dust generation, and cabinet throughput. Rationale: Regular top-up at the interval prevents abrasive deficiency that can reduce cleaning effectiveness and increases media condition consistency across parts. Example procedure: at the end of the specified operating interval, inspect media cleanliness and size distribution, add approved shot media to restore working volume, and screen/remove fines as necessary. Records to keep: top-up event timestamp, media lot/grade, quantity added, pre- and post-top-up media inspection notes, cabinet ID, and operator initials. Consult SB-1016 for abrasive handling guidance and ECN-2026-033 for any changes to shot media specification.

# FAQ-015 Engineering FAQ #15

Revision: Rev A

Related documents: ECN-2026-038, MM-P1-L2-HT03, SOP-P1-L3-05

Question: What is the permitted quench delay for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03), and why is adherence important?
Answer: The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 13 seconds. Rationale: The quench delay directly affects phase transformation kinetics and final microstructure. Exceeding the quench delay maximum for this furnace can allow undesired pearlite or bainite formation, which reduces ductility and can increase residual stresses. Action: Monitor and log cycle timestamps from austenitizing end to immersion start for every charge processed on EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Examples of acceptable records: time-stamped heat cycle log exported from furnace control, operator sign-off showing immersion start, and a corresponding metallography batch identifier. Records to keep: heat cycle log, operator checklist, and any deviation report. See ECN-2026-038 for approved changes to furnace control logic and MM-P1-L2-HT03 for heat treat handling.

Question: What torque should be used on the mandrel clamp bolt for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01), and how to verify?
Answer: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 525 N·m. Rationale: Specified clamp bolt torque ensures consistent clamping force to prevent mandrel slippage during heat treat handling operations while avoiding bolt preload that could induce fatigue. Verification method: use a calibrated torque wrench capable of reading and recording applied torque, and capture the applied value on the maintenance work order. Examples of verification records: torque wrench printout or calibrated tool log, maintenance work order noting the applied torque, and follow-up inspection confirming no thread damage. Records to keep: torque application record, calibration certificate for the torque wrench, and the maintenance log entry. Refer to SOP-P1-L3-05 for the calibration and tool tracing procedure and to ECN-2026-038 for any related assembly changes.

Question: What is the minimum acceptable coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01)?
Answer: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Rationale: Minimum flow is specified to prevent coil overheating and insulation breakdown; insufficient flow shortens equipment life and can produce thermal runaways. Field practice: measure flow at the meter nearest to the coil supply line; if flow is below the coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P1-L3-IH01, execute the isolation and tagout procedure and notify maintenance. Examples of records: flow meter log for the heater, outage ticket showing the corrective action, and any temperature trend that led to the shutdown. Records to keep: flow meter trend export, maintenance corrective action report, and any vendor service report. See MM-P1-L2-HT03 for interfacing water systems and SOP-P1-L3-05 for meter calibration requirements.

Question: What austenitizing setpoint should be used for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03), and what controls ensure the setpoint is achieved?
Answer: The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. Rationale: The selected austenitizing setpoint produces the target solutionized microstructure for the alloy families processed in EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and provides the correct starting condition for quench response. Controls: verify setpoint entry in the furnace controller before charge start, confirm recorded thermocouple profile reaches and stabilizes at the austenitizing setpoint, and ensure thermocouple calibration certificates are current. Examples of records: furnace controller recipe printout showing 855 °C setpoint, thermocouple profile log for the charge, and calibration certificate for each thermocouple channel. Records to keep: recipe verification print, thermocouple profile archive, and calibration documentation. Refer to MM-P1-L2-HT03 for thermocouple placement guidance and ECN-2026-038 for any procedural revisions.

Question: What torque is required for the mandrel clamp bolt on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03), and what inspection/maintenance steps follow torque application?
Answer: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 620 N·m. Rationale: This torque ensures the mandrel is secured to handle radial rolling loads without slippage while avoiding overstressing the bolt assembly. Post-application steps: perform a visual inspection for thread engagement and correct washer seating, record the applied torque in the maintenance record, and schedule a follow-up inspection after the first production shift to confirm no loosening. Examples of records: maintenance work order with applied torque entry, visual inspection checklist, and production sign-off confirming mandrel integrity. Records to keep: torque application log, inspection checklist, and any nonconformance reports if issues are found. See SOP-P1-L3-05 for torque application procedure and tool calibration requirements and ECN-2026-038 for configuration changes affecting these assemblies.

Document control notes: retain all listed records in the document control system as referenced by MM-P1-L2-HT03 and SOP-P1-L3-05, and submit any proposed changes through ECN-2026-038.

text:
# FAQ-016 Engineering FAQ #16

Revision: Rev A

Question:
What does the alarm value mean for the dust collector on the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet and how should it be addressed?

Answer:
The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. This alarm indicates the differential across the collector media has reached the preset threshold and requires immediate evaluation of media condition, compressed air cleaning performance (if applicable), and hopper discharge. Background: excessive pressure drop increases motor load and reduces capture efficiency. Rationale: returning the differential below the threshold restores airflow balance and reduces risk to downstream equipment. Typical corrective steps: verify alarm is valid, confirm differential gauge reading, inspect inlet plenum for blockages, check bag/ cartridge integrity per SOP-P3-L2-02, and perform controlled cleaning or element replacement if cleaning does not restore acceptable differential. Records to keep: alarm event in the plant maintenance log, inspection checklist, media change order or cleaning record, and reference to ECN-2026-019 if the change involves a design or control update.

Question:
What is the austenitizing temperature setpoint for the Ring Rolling furnace and why is it critical?

Answer:
The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Background: achieving and holding the austenitizing temperature is essential to obtain the required microstructure prior to quench or subsequent thermal processing. Rationale: 855 °C is the controlled point established to meet hardness and grain size requirements for the specified material grades used in our ring products. Practical application: verify thermocouple calibration and furnace uniformity before a load, follow the soak schedule documented in the heat treat procedure, and confirm setpoint adherence on the furnace control historian. Records to keep: furnace run log, thermocouple calibration certificate, soak time confirmation, and any deviation reports filed against SOP-P3-L2-04 or change notices referenced in ECN-2026-019.

Question:
What is the minimum allowable coil cooling water flow for the Ring Rolling induction billet heater and how should flow issues be handled?

Answer:
The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. Background: adequate coil cooling prevents coil overheating and maintains inductive heating efficiency. Rationale: 46 L/min is the minimum flow required to keep coil temperatures and water exit temperature within allowable limits specified for reliable operation. Actions when flow is below minimum: stop induction heating per SOP-P3-L2-02, isolate and tag the heater, verify pump operation, check strainers and inlet screens for blockage, and confirm flow instrumentation calibration. Records to keep: flow log entries, pump and strainer inspection reports, lockout/tagout record, and any maintenance work orders tied to ECN-2026-019 if modifications or parts replacement are executed.

Question:
What is the specified bolt torque for blast wheel liner bolts in the Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet and why must it be adhered to?

Answer:
The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Background: correct bolt torque secures liners against centrifugal loads and minimizes liner movement, which can cause premature wear, imbalance, or fastener failure. Rationale: 100 N·m was selected to provide adequate clamp load without over-stressing the bolts or liner castings. Procedure: use a calibrated torque wrench, tighten fasteners in the pattern specified in the cabinet maintenance procedure in SOP-P3-L2-04, and mark torque-checked bolts with the approved marking method. Records to keep: torque verification sheet with bolt identifiers, torque wrench calibration certificate, liner installation report, and any deviation documentation referenced to ECN-2026-019.

Question:
What is the target billet temperature for the Hot Forge induction billet heater and what controls are used to confirm it?

Answer:
The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. Background: achieving the target temperature ensures material plasticity for forging and uniform deformation behavior. Rationale: 1180 °C is the process target validated for the billet chemistries used and matched to downstream die and cycle parameters. Controls and verification: use calibrated non-contact pyrometer(s) and thermocouple verification during setup, confirm temperature on process control displays before feeding billets to the die, and run periodic checks per SOP-P3-L2-04. Records to keep: billet heat records showing target attainment, pyrometer calibration and verification logs, any out-of-spec reports, and references to ECN-2026-019 when a change to target or monitoring method is proposed.

- SOP-P3-L2-04

# FAQ-017 Engineering FAQ #17
Revision: Rev A

Q1: What torque should be used when tightening the blast wheel liner bolts on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why?
A1: Use 100 N·m for the blast wheel liner bolt torque on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01). Rationale: liners must be retained firmly to prevent movement under centrifugal loads while avoiding bolt yield. Over‑tightening risks stud fatigue and liner distortion; under‑tightening permits loosening and wear pattern escalation. Procedure: clean bolt threads, apply appropriate thread lubricant as specified in SOP-P2-L2-01, and tighten in a star pattern to 100 N·m using a calibrated torque wrench. Verification: record bolt locations and final torque in the maintenance log and retain the torque wrench calibration certificate with the job record. Related procedure: SOP-P2-L2-01 describes fastener handling and torque tool calibration. See SB-1002 for blast wheel assembly drawings.

Q2: What is the recommended lubrication interval for the main roll bearing on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03), and what is the justification?
A2: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is 185 hours. Rationale: rolling contact demands consistent grease replenishment to maintain film thickness and to displace contaminants; the interval is set to balance bearing life and maintenance downtime. Implementation: log machine run hours and perform lubrication at the 185 hours threshold using the grease grade specified in the equipment lubrication sheet. If a scheduled maintenance event coincides with the 185 hours mark, perform lubrication at that event. Records to keep: add an entry to the bearing lubrication log indicating equipment id EQ-P2-L2-RR03, date, run hours at service, grease batch/lot, and technician initials. Reference: confirm grease type and handling in SOP-P2-L2-04 and cross‑check bearing assembly notes in SB-1002.

Q3: How often should shot media be topped up in Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and how should the operation be documented?
A3: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Rationale: media attrition and segregation reduce blasting effectiveness; topping up at 40 hours maintains consistent media mass and surface treatment results. Practice: monitor media level visually or by the cabinet level indicator and add fresh media to restore the recommended fill as specified in SB-1002, ensuring media type and size match the job specification. Documentation: record media top-up events on the shot media log with equipment id EQ-P3-L2-SB01, media type, quantity added (use units per material handling form), operator initials, and any abnormal observations (e.g., fines, broken media). Include the media top-up entry in the process quality record for the part batch to maintain traceability per SOP-P2-L2-01.

Q4: What alarm setpoint should be used for the dust collector pressure drop on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and what actions follow an alarm?
A4: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. Rationale: the setpoint reflects acceptable filter loading before performance degradation; an alarm at 1240 Pa indicates increased resistance and the need for inspection or service. Response steps: upon alarm, stop the blast cycle in a controlled manner, isolate the cabinet per SOP-P2-L2-04, and inspect filters and dust handling system for blockage, tears, or improper sealing. If filter change or cleaning is required, perform per SB-1002 filter replacement procedures and record the action. Records: log alarm time, equipment id EQ-P2-L1-SB03, observed pressure reading, corrective action taken, filter part identifiers (if changed), and technician name. Maintain the dust collector maintenance file and attach the alarm event log to the cabinet service record.

Q5: How long should spindle warm-up be allowed on Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) before precision work, and why is this necessary?
A5: The spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes. Rationale: thermal stabilization reduces spindle runout and thermal drift that would otherwise affect dimensional accuracy on precision parts. Procedure: run the spindle at low to moderate speed per the machine vendor recommendation during the 15 minutes warm-up period with no cutting load, then perform a test cut or calibration check before beginning production. Records: note warm-up time and confirmation of spindle checks in the machine log for EQ-P1-L4-CN01, including operator initials and any deviations observed. Reference SOP-P2-L2-04 for machine warm-up and verification steps and SB-1002 for machine capability notes.

Notes on records and traceability
- Always reference equipment id when entering logs (EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P2-L2-RR03, EQ-P2-L1-SB03, EQ-P1-L4-CN01).
- Maintain torque wrench calibration certificates and grease/ media lot information with each maintenance job record as specified in SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-04.
- Cross‑reference assembly and replacement details with SB-1002 where part interfaces or assemblies are involved.
- When any of the specified setpoints or intervals are exceeded or if abnormal conditions occur during service, attach a corrective action note to the equipment file and notify maintenance supervision per SOP-P2-L2-04.

# FAQ-018: Engineering FAQ #18
Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the required shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and why is it maintained at that interval?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Rationale: consistent media level maintains blast energy and part coverage to avoid under- or over-blasting of forgings processed for heat treat preparation. Example record entries should include equipment id (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), date/time, operator initials, and confirmation that the top-up interval requirement (48 hours) is met or the amount of media added. Q: Which lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), and what are the service expectations?

Records to keep: austenitizing setpoint confirmation should be logged with equipment id (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), setpoint value (845 °C), operator initials, and any deviations or corrective actions. Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), and what are the handling and record requirements?

Records to keep: maintenance log entries must record equipment id (EQ-P1-L1-IH03), lubricant part number applied (CFW-LUB-188), batch or lot number of the lubricant, quantity, date, and technician. # FAQ-019 Engineering FAQ #19

Revision: Rev A

Question: What lubricant should be used for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03), and why?

Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-159 for EQ-P3-L2-HT03. Background: The lubricant was selected based on compatibility with heat-treat furnace atmospheres and seal materials documented in ECN-2026-019. Rationale: CFW-LUB-159 provides the required film strength and oxidation resistance for bearings and lead screws exposed to elevated temperatures in the heat-treat enclosure. Example application: apply CFW-LUB-159 to furnace door hinges, rail bearings, and exposed guideways during scheduled lubrication activities per the maintenance checklist in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2. Records to keep: maintenance log entries must record the part number CFW-LUB-159, location serviced, technician initials, and a brief description of the quantity used and visual condition before and after application. Retain receipts or purchase orders referencing CFW-LUB-159 with the job file for traceability.

Question: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and how should it be managed?

Answer: The system pressure limit for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 is 295 bar. Background: The limit reflects the design and relief valve setting determined during commissioning and formalized in ECN-2026-019. Rationale: Maintaining system pressure at or below 295 bar prevents overpressurization of hydraulic lines and actuators, reducing the risk of seal failure and component rupture. Example procedures: verify pressure readings against the system gauge prior to initiating heavy forging cycles and after any hydraulic maintenance. If the gauge indicates pressure at or above 295 bar during a static condition, stop operations and follow the isolation and inspection procedure in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2. Records to keep: log pre- and post-operation pressure readings, corrective actions taken when readings approached or exceeded 295 bar, parts replaced, and any adjustments to relief valves. Include the gauge serial number and calibration record in the maintenance entry.

Question: What is the maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01), and what are the implications for material selection?

Answer: The maximum ring outer diameter for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 is 995 mm. Background: This maximum was established based on former trials and structural constraints captured in ECN-2026-019. Rationale: Staying within the 995 mm maximum ensures proper feed engagement, roll support, and acceptable roll gap geometry during radial rolling operations. Example: when planning a job, confirm part drawings and blank size such that finished outer diameter does not exceed 995 mm; if a design requires larger diameters, route the request using ECN-2026-019 for evaluation. Records to keep: production setup sheets must record the target outer diameter and a confirmation that it is less than or equal to 995 mm, including a signature from the setup engineer. Keep job traveler copies and any engineering change requests related to diameter limits alongside SB-1008 where applicable.

Question: What is the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01), and how should it be applied?

Answer: The chuck jaw bolt torque for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 is 90 N·m. Background: This torque value was validated during assembly and has been adopted in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 as the required tightening specification. Rationale: Applying 90 N·m ensures jaw retention without overstressing the bolt, preserving clamping accuracy and reducing the risk of bolt yielding. Example use: for jaw replacement or reindexing operations, clean threads and lightly lubricate per the vendor recommendation before applying 90 N·m to each jaw bolt in a star pattern to seat the jaw evenly. Records to keep: maintenance records should include the bolt identification, the applied torque value 90 N·m, the torque wrench calibration reference, technician initials, and any deviation with justification recorded in the job notes.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and what handling precautions are required?

Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-463 for EQ-P3-L2-SB01. Background: CFW-LUB-463 was chosen for components exposed to abrasive media in the shot blast cabinet, as detailed in ECN-2026-019. Rationale: CFW-LUB-463 provides abrasion resistance and adhesion suitable for exposed bearings and pivot points in a high-abrasion environment, extending component life and reducing downtime. Example handling: apply CFW-LUB-463 to pivot bearings and conveyor chain idlers during scheduled preventative maintenance; avoid over-application that could lead to accumulation in the blast area. Records to keep: lubrication log entries must specify CFW-LUB-463, equipment ID EQ-P3-L2-SB01, application locations, quantity dispensed, technician name, and date. Keep spare part tags and purchase documentation for CFW-LUB-463 with the equipment maintenance folder and reference MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 for storage and handling requirements.

# FAQ-020 Engineering FAQ #20

Question: What is the maximum allowed workpiece size for the Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2?
Answer:
- Background: Tooling and drive capacity dictate the maximum ring envelope that can be processed without risk to rollover, drive overload, or clamp interference.
- Direct specification: The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #2 (EQ-P3-L2-RR02) is 1415 mm.
- Rationale: This limit is set to ensure the ring remains within bearing and chucking envelope and to maintain required form control during rolling. Do not exceed the stated outer diameter without an engineering change.
- Example application: If a part print calls out an outer dimension near the stated value, plan blank sizing, clamp selection, and runout control to keep the formed outer diameter at or below the specified limit.
- Records to keep: For each run near the limit, retain the setup sheet, raw blank dimensions, run log, and final inspection report. Reference ECN-2026-044 for applicable change notices affecting envelope limits.

Question: What torque should be applied to the mandrel clamp bolts on Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1?
Answer:
- Background: Correct mandrel clamp bolt torque secures the mandrel to prevent slippage during rolling and ensures repeatable centering and concentricity.
- Direct specification: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 395 N·m.
- Rationale: The value represents the torque required to achieve the specified clamp preload for the mandrel interface. Under-torquing can cause mandrel movement; over-torquing risks stud or thread damage.
- Example application: During setup, torque each clamp bolt to the specified value using a calibrated torque wrench. If a bolt runs soft or you detect thread galling, stop the setup and consult maintenance before continuing.
- Records to keep: Log the operator, time, equipment id, individual bolt readings if available, and any deviations. Retain calibration certificate for the torque tool used.

Question: What is the target billet temperature for the Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 prior to charge?
Answer:
- Background: The correct billet temperature at charge is critical for material flow, forgeability, and final microstructure after forge and heat treat sequences.
- Direct specification: The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C.
- Rationale: This target balances furnace heating time, scale control, and metal plasticity for the alloy families processed on this line. Deviations impact die fill and may alter downstream cooling and heat treat outcomes.
- Example application: Verify thermocouple readout matches the target before feeding the billet to the press. Record actual measured billet temperature on the heat control log and reconcile any excursions with process engineering.
- Records to keep: Maintain a heater run log showing measured billet temperatures, cycle times, operator, and any alarms. Attach the log to the production batch record and reference ECN-2026-044 if the heater setpoints change.

Question: What is the way lubrication refill requirement for Machining CNC turning center #2?
Answer:
- Background: Proper way lubrication is essential for axis positioning accuracy, component life, and surface finish stability. Refill scheduling must align with production cadence.
- Direct specification: The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours.
- Rationale: The interval is established based on observed consumption and wear patterns on this machine model. Adhering to the interval reduces the probability of axis stick-slip and extends ways life.
- Example application: Track machine runtime against the refill interval and perform the lube refill at the interval indicated. If operating conditions produce heavy contamination or unusual wear signs, escalate to maintenance for immediate inspection.
- Records to keep: Record machine id, cumulative hours at refill, lubricant batch number, operator, and condition notes. See MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for lubrication procedure specifics.

Question: What is the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3?
Answer:
- Background: Main ram bolt preload maintains structural integrity and alignment under cyclic loads. Correct torque prevents loosening and fatigue failure.
- Direct specification: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m.
- Rationale: The torque value corresponds to the required clamp load for the main ram clamp studs. Applying the specified torque ensures even load distribution and reduces the chance of stud yield or joint separation.
- Example application: During scheduled maintenance or reassembly after ram work, torque the main ram bolts to the specified value using a calibrated hydraulic torque tool if required. If a bolt fails to reach torque at expected wrench turns, suspect damaged threads or washer seating issues and halt work until inspected.
- Records to keep: Keep a bolt torque log with equipment id, bolt identifier, measured torque, tool calibration reference, operator name, and date. Reference MM-P1-L2-RR01 for related press maintenance protocols.

Related documents:
- ECN-2026-044
- MM-P1-L2-RR01
- MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1

End of document.

# FAQ-021 Engineering FAQ #21
Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the recommended spindle warm-up time before cutting on Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03)?
A: Background: Proper spindle warm-up stabilizes bearing clearances and thermal gradients to ensure dimensional accuracy and tool life. For EQ-P1-L3-CN03, the specified spindle warm-up time is 27 minutes. Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach thermal equilibrium reduces runout drift and avoids premature reloads. Example: Start the spindle at idle RPM and monitor for consistent runout readings before initiating a finishing pass. Records to keep: Log the start and ready timestamps for each shift run in the machine's downtime log and note any deviations in the spindle warm-up period in the corrective action record. See SOP-P1-L3-04 for machine-specific pre-start checks.

Q: How often should the main roll bearings be lubricated on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01)?
A: Background: Proper lubrication of main roll bearings is critical to prevent metal-to-metal contact, overheating, and surface defects on rolled parts. Interval: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 is 120 hours. Rationale: A timed lubrication schedule ensures replenishment of lubricant film before degradation, based on operating duty and bearing design. Example: If the mill accumulates extended runtime during production runs, schedule lubrication actions according to the recorded run-hours clock and before any planned heavy roll changeover. Records to keep: Maintain the bearing lubrication log showing timestamped lubrication events, lubricant type used, and the technician initials. Reference SOP-P1-L1-02 for approved grease types and lubrication procedure steps.

Q: What warm-up procedure is used for the spindle on the Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02)?
A: Background: Each CNC turning center may have different spindle-bearing preheat characteristics depending on bearing preload and environmental conditions. The spindle warm-up time for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is 21 minutes. Rationale: Following the prescribed warm-up ensures concentricity and prevents thermal shocks when transitioning to cut speeds. Example: Apply the spindle warm-up cycle in the machine control panel, observe vibration meters, and confirm that tool offsets remain within established control limits before cutting. Records to keep: Document the warm-up run in the machine run log, including operator name, start and end times, and any anomalies found. SOP-P1-L3-04 contains control panel warm-up sequences and verification points.

Q: What alarm setpoint should maintenance verify on the dust collection system for the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03)?
A: Background: Dust collector differential pressure monitors protect process quality and equipment by indicating when filter media is loaded or when airflow is restricted. Alarm setpoint: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is 1510 Pa. Rationale: Setting and verifying the alarm at the specified differential pressure ensures filtration efficiency and prevents particulate bypass into the cabinet or downstream processes. Example: During filter replacement, reset the differential sensor after confirming the pressure drop falls below the alarm threshold and record the reset action. Records to keep: Keep a filter maintenance log with pressure readings before and after service, alarm event entries including trigger timestamp, and actions taken. See SOP-P3-L4-02 for filter change and sensor calibration procedures.

Q: What minimum coil cooling water flow is required to safely operate Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02)?
A: Background: Induction heaters rely on adequate water flow to cool coils and power electronics; insufficient flow risks coil damage and compromised heating profiles. Minimum flow: The coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min. Rationale: Maintaining flow at or above the stated minimum sustains heat removal capacity and avoids thermal runaway in coil windings. Example: Verify flow using the installed flowmeter prior to each production run; if flow readout is below the minimum, lock out the heater and follow the pump and piping troubleshooting checklist. Records to keep: Log flowmeter readings at startup and after any maintenance, record pump service events, and include any flow-related incidents in the equipment failure report. Consult SOP-P1-L1-02 for water quality and pump maintenance guidance.

Related documents: SOP-P1-L1-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P3-L4-02

Document control note: Retain warm-up, lubrication, alarm, and flow logs with the equipment history record for each listed asset (EQ-P1-L3-CN03, EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03, EQ-P2-L1-IH02) and reference this FAQ when performing audits or training.

text:
# FAQ-022 Engineering FAQ #22

Revision: Rev A

Q1: What is the correct main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and why is it critical?
A1: The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. This torque value clamps the ram assembly and maintains preload on the primary joint that transmits forging loads. Using the specified 1600 N·m prevents bolt fatigue from under-torque and joint slippage from over-torque that can introduce misalignment or accelerated wear. Rationale: hydraulic press rams operate under reversed loads; maintaining the specified preload ensures load distribution across the bolt shank and threads as designed. Example failure mode: loose ram fasteners manifest as axial play and extraneous vibration, often accompanied by uneven die contact. Records to keep: torque application record for each service action, including equipment id EQ-P3-L3-HP03, operator initials, and reference to SOP-P3-L3-04.

Q2: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02), and what are the consequences of inadequate flow?
A2: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. This minimum maintains coil temperature within design limits and prevents coil insulation breakdown and localized overheating. Rationale: induction coils require a consistent coolant flow to remove heat from densely wound conductors; falling below 46 L/min increases the risk of rapid insulation degradation and may reduce heater life. Examples: symptoms of low flow include elevated coil surface temperatures and tripping of thermal protection. Records to keep: flow verification logs for EQ-P1-L2-IH02, corrective actions taken when flow approaches the minimum, and cross-reference to SOP-P1-L4-05 for acceptable sensor and valve checks.

Q3: What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), and how should setpoint control be managed?
A3: The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. This setpoint ensures the part achieves the required microstructure prior to quench. Rationale: precise control of the 845 °C setpoint avoids under-austenitizing, which yields incomplete transformation, and avoids overexposure that can cause grain growth. Control approach: use calibrated thermocouple inputs and validated control loops to hold the setpoint within process tolerances defined in heat treat procedures. Examples: when parts display unexpected hardness or microstructure, verify that the furnace control reached and held 845 °C during the austenitizing soak. Records to keep: furnace run sheets that document setpoint, thermocouple readings for EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and references to SOP-P2-L1-01 for furnace calibration and procedure checks.

Q4: What is the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02), and how should operations respond to pressure excursions?
A4: The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar. This limit protects hydraulic components and seals from overpressure and ensures safe press operation within design safety margins. Rationale: exceeding 300 bar can lead to seal extrusion, component rupture, or uncontrolled movement. Operational response: on detection of a pressure reading above 300 bar, remove load from the press, secure the work area, and follow the shutdown and inspection sequence in SOP-P1-L4-05. Examples: repeated excursions to or above 300 bar indicate component wear or circuit restriction; investigate pump relief, accumulator condition, and return-line restrictions. Records to keep: incident log including recorded pressure peaks for EQ-P1-L4-HP02, maintenance actions taken, and any pressure transducer calibration records.

Q5: What is the minimum coil cooling water flow for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02), and what checks should be performed during commissioning or restart?
A5: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. During commissioning or restart, verify that the measured flow meets or exceeds 55 L/min before energizing the coil. Rationale: hot forge induction heaters typically operate at higher duty cycles; 55 L/min prevents rapid overheating under heavy load. Commissioning checks: inspect piping and fittings for leaks, verify pump operation and flow meter calibration, and confirm that cooling loop filtration is clear. Examples: if flow is below 55 L/min, do not energize the coil; instead, clear obstructions, service the pump circuit, and re-check. Records to keep: commissioning checklists and flow measurement records for EQ-P2-L1-IH02, including corrective actions and cross-reference to SOP-P2-L1-01 for startup procedures.

Related documents: SOP-P1-L4-05, SOP-P2-L1-01, SOP-P3-L3-04

Document control: retain this FAQ with the equipment history for each referenced asset and append torque and flow verification records to the preventive maintenance file for the corresponding equipment ids.
