# FAQ-023 Engineering FAQ #23

Revision: Rev A

Q1: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and why?

A1: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-426 for EQ-P2-L4-HT02. Rationale: this lubricant has been qualified for the metallurgical environment and temperature profile specific to the furnace cavity design used on this line. Background testing referenced in SB-1016 established compatibility with furnace internal seals and conveyor components, reducing deposit formation and maintaining thermal conductivity where required. Example application: apply the product at specified touch-up points during scheduled maintenance per SOP-P2-L4-03 to maintain sliding contact surfaces and prevent galling. Records to keep: log the part number, batch or lot identifier from the supplier, quantity issued to the asset, technician initials, and the maintenance checklist entry referencing SOP-P2-L4-03. Retain a copy of the supplier technical data sheet with the equipment file and attach a cross-reference to SB-1016 for qualification notes.

Q2: What blast wheel liner bolt torque is required for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and how should it be applied?

A2: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is 90 N·m. Rationale: liner retention hardware must be torqued to this value to ensure clamping without overstressing the liner or bolt threads, maintaining wheel balance and minimizing loosening under cyclic loading. Application procedure: use a calibrated torque tool set to the specified value and perform a star pattern progression to seat the liner uniformly. Background: torque value is derived from fastener grade and liner material properties as documented in SB-1016 and implemented in SOP-P3-L1-05. Examples of records: record the bolt torque check in the preventive maintenance record, note the torque tool serial or calibration identifier, and document any deviations with photographic evidence if liners show uneven wear or fastener damage. Maintain records in the equipment maintenance folder and reference SB-1016 for original design calculations.

Q3: What is the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and what are the implications for operation?

A3: The system pressure limit for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 is 320 bar. Rationale: this limit reflects the maximum safe working pressure of the hydraulic circuit components used on this press, including hoses, seals, and the main pressure relief valve. Operating within the limit prevents overstress, seal extrusion, and sudden component failure. Implementation guidance: ensure pressure readings are monitored using calibrated gauges and that relief circuitry is verified during start-up checks as directed in SOP-P2-L4-03. If pressure approaches the limit, stop operations and perform a leak and condition inspection per the SOP. Records to keep: log gauge readings at start-up and at completion of shift, record relief valve setpoint verification, and retain any fault reports generated when pressure excursions are detected. Cross-reference inspection findings with SB-1016 for component specification and maintenance history.

Q4: Which lubricant part number is specified for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), and what handling practices are required?

A4: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-278 for EQ-P3-L1-SB02. Rationale and background: CFW-LUB-278 has been selected for compatibility with the media and wheel materials used in the hot forge shot blast cabinet environment. It minimizes fling-off, resists breakdown under abrasive loading, and limits transfer to forged parts where possible. Handling practices: store the lubricant in the original container, protect it from contamination, and issue it to technicians in measured quantities. Apply in accordance with the dispensing steps in SOP-P3-L1-05 to avoid over-application that could affect blast effectiveness. Records to keep: retain issuance records including part number, container lot, issuing technician, and the maintenance task reference to SOP-P3-L1-05. Maintain a traceable link to SB-1016 for historical selection rationale.

Q5: What main ram bolt torque is required for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and what verification steps are recommended?

A5: The main ram bolt torque for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 is 1600 N·m. Rationale: the main ram retention hardware must be torqued to this value to assure axial clamping and alignment under machining forces and to prevent relative movement that could induce chatter or misalignment. Verification steps: use a calibrated torque wrench or hydraulic torque unit capable of the specified value, confirm calibration identifiers on the tool, and perform torque application in a controlled sequence to ensure uniform load distribution. If any fastener cannot be torqued to the specified value due to damaged threads or tool limitation, do not proceed with operation; escalate per SOP-P2-L4-03 for corrective action. Records to keep: document torque application in the machine maintenance log, include tool calibration reference, technician initials, and note any re-torquing intervals performed. Retain a copy of the verification report and link it to the equipment file and to SB-1016 for design support.

Related documents: SB-1016, SOP-P2-L4-03, SOP-P3-L1-05

End of document.

# FAQ-024 Engineering FAQ #24

Revision: Rev A

Question: What does the dust collector pressure drop alarm reading mean for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and what actions should be taken when it reaches the alarm value?
Answer: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 1240 Pa. This reading indicates a restriction in the filter/media or an evacuation obstruction that reduces flow through the dust collector. Background: The pressure drop across the collector is monitored to protect blast cabinet air flow and media life. Rationale: At the alarm value, differential indicates cleaning or maintenance is required to restore design flow and protect downstream processes. Actions: immediate visual inspection of intake and exhaust plenums; verify filter condition and sealing; check the pulse-clean or shaker mechanism for proper function; clear any visible blockages in ductwork and hoods. If filter replacement is required, use the parts and procedures referenced in SB-1021 and record the replacement in the equipment maintenance log. Example: If cleaning restores pressure drop below alarm, note cleaning method, personnel, and hours in the equipment record. Records to keep: pressure drop reading before and after corrective action, description of corrective action, references to SB-1021 for filter handling, and signature of the technician.

Question: How often must way lubricant be refilled for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01), and what documentation is required?
Answer: The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Background: The specified interval ensures consistent lubrication of sliding ways and carriage bearings to prevent accelerated wear. Rationale: Adhering to the interval prevents scoring and positional drift that could compromise machined surfaces. Procedure: At the end of each interval, perform a top-up using the approved lubricant specified in the machine lubrication drawer and cycle the axes to distribute lubricant. Example: Operator completes a refill event, cycles axes per SOP-P2-L1-05, and observes normal axis movement. Records to keep: machine hours counter snapshot at refill, lubricant lot number, technician initials, and any notes about abnormal consumption or leakage. If consumption deviates from historical norms, open a maintenance action referencing SOP-P2-L1-05 and MM-P2-L3-HT02 as applicable.

Question: What is the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01), and how should operators verify it?
Answer: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Background: This target is selected to achieve the metallurgical condition required for downstream machining operations, balancing hardness and ductility. Rationale: Precise temperature control reduces microstructural variability and ensures consistent machining performance and tool life. Verification: Use the calibrated thermocouple or pyrometer specified for the induction heater; verify instrument calibration status before critical heats per MM-P2-L3-HT02. Example: For a billet run, record the measured temperature at the end of the heating cycle and confirm it matches the target within the allowable tolerance defined by process control documents. Records to keep: instrument ID, measured temperature, operator initials, time stamp, and any corrective actions when target is not met. Cross-reference MM-P2-L3-HT02 for measurement device calibration requirements.

Question: What torque is required for the blast wheel liner bolts on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why is that torque important?
Answer: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Background: Correct bolt torque secures liners against centrifugal and impact forces from abrasive media. Rationale: Under-torqued bolts can loosen, causing liner movement and damage; over-torqued bolts can cause bolt failure or deformation of seating surfaces. Procedure: Use a calibrated torque wrench set to the specified torque and torque in a star pattern to achieve uniform clamping. Example: When replacing liners, apply the specified torque and run a short verification cycle to confirm no unusual vibration. Records to keep: bolt lot number if changed, torque wrench calibration tag, applied torque value, technician initials, and reference to SB-1021 for liner replacement instructions.

Question: Which lubricant part number is approved for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02), and how should it be managed?
Answer: The lubricant part number for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is CFW-LUB-373. Background: Using a single approved lubricant ensures compatibility with seals, bearings, and high-temperature application points specific to this furnace. Rationale: Mixing lubricants or using non-approved products can lead to seal degradation, increased wear, or contamination of heat treat atmospheres. Management: Store CFW-LUB-373 in designated controlled inventory per SOP-P2-L1-05, use first-in, first-out handling, and record lot numbers when installed. Example: During bearing service, note the lubricant part number, lot number, quantity used, and staff performing the work. Records to keep: purchase order reference, inventory issue log entries, installation records in the equipment maintenance file, and any deviation approvals. Refer to MM-P2-L3-HT02 for compatibility checks and SOP-P2-L1-05 for lubricant storage and control protocols.

Related documents: MM-P2-L3-HT02, SB-1021, SOP-P2-L1-05

Document control: retain equipment logs, calibration certificates, and maintenance records as part of the equipment file for the respective EQ identifiers noted above.

Q3: How long should I warm up the spindle on Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) before starting critical cuts?
A3: The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 27 minutes. Background: A controlled spindle warm-up stabilizes thermal growth and lubricant film development to achieve repeatable spindle geometry. Rationale: Following a prescribed warm-up time reduces part-to-part variation during the initial run-in period after machine start or after extended idle. Procedure example: With the machine in READY state, initiate the spindle warm-up program and allow the automated sequence to run for 27 minutes before loading the first critical production part. Background: Way lubrication interval is defined to maintain film thickness on slideways and prevent accelerated wear during normal machining cycles. Rationale: Adhering to the 70 hours interval prevents both under-lubrication and over-filling, the latter of which can attract contaminants. Procedure example: Track run time using the machine hour meter and schedule a refill at the next available planned maintenance window once the cumulative run time reaches the 70 hours threshold. Use approved filling tools and follow the machine's fill point sequence as documented in MM-P3-L3-CN02. Records to keep: way lube log with the cumulative hours reading at refill, lubricant used, operator initials, and any comments about leakage or abnormal wear observed. Reference: See MM-P3-L3-CN02 for the refill procedure and verification checklist.

Q5: What lubricant should be used for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01), and how do we ensure traceability?

# FAQ-027 Engineering FAQ #27

Revision: Rev A

Q1: What is the required coil cooling water flow for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and why is it critical?
A1: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min. Background: Adequate coil cooling flow prevents coil overheating, which can cause insulation breakdown, reduced induction efficiency, and accelerated component fatigue. Rationale: The specified minimum maintains heat transfer capacity under expected operating heat loads and provides a margin for transient conditions. Example: If records show the measured flow drops below the specified value during a run, stop heating and investigate pump supply, inlet strainers, and coil connections. Records to keep: log actual measured flow against the specification, note any corrective actions, and attach contemporaneous equipment readings to the job packet. See related procedures in SOP-P2-L1-03 for monitoring methods and ECN-2026-048 for design basis changes.

Q2: What torque is required for the mandrel clamp bolts on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01), and what is the tightening rationale?
A2: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. Background: Correct bolt torque ensures consistent clamp preload, minimizing slip and uneven loading during rolling. Rationale: Applying the specified torque achieves the designed clamping force without overstressing threads or bolts, preserving alignment and reducing wear on the mandrel assembly. Example: When replacing a mandrel clamp bolt, use a calibrated torque wrench to apply the stated torque in a controlled sequence, and verify torque on adjacent bolts to ensure uniformity. Records to keep: maintenance entry documenting bolt replacement, tool calibration certificate reference, torque values recorded, and any anomalies. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-02 for torque application procedure and ECN-2026-048 for any bolt material or size updates.

Q3: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02), and how should operators respond if it is approached?
A3: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Background: The system pressure limit protects hydraulic components and seals from overpressure failure and maintains predictable press behavior. Rationale: Operating within the limit reduces the risk of catastrophic seal failure, hose rupture, and uncontrolled movement. Example: If instrumented pressure approaches the limit during a cycle, suspend the loading activity, isolate the source, and follow lockout and troubleshooting steps. Records to keep: pressure traces for the event, operator notes, corrective action records, and inspection findings. See SOP-P1-L2-02 for hydraulic system isolation and ECN-2026-048 for any updated pressure component qualifications.

Q4: What minimum coil cooling water flow applies to Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02), and how is compliance verified?
A4: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. Background: Each induction heater coil has a specific cooling requirement determined by coil geometry and power duty; this minimum prevents localized overheating and maintains coil life. Rationale: Verifying and maintaining the minimum flow reduces thermal cycling stress and preserves electrical insulation. Example: Use the installed flow meter to confirm flow before initiating a heating cycle; if the meter reads below the specified value, do not energize the coil and perform the checklist for water system faults. Records to keep: pre-start checklists showing measured flow, any maintenance actions on the cooling loop, and follow-up verification after repairs. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-03 for flow verification procedure and ECN-2026-048 for history of cooling circuit modifications.

Q5: What is the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and why must it be controlled?
A5: The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Background: The target billet temperature is selected to obtain required material ductility and metallurgical state prior to ring rolling operations. Rationale: Controlling to the target avoids underheating that can cause cracking and overworking, and avoids overheating that can produce grain growth or undesirable phase changes. Example: Confirm the billet temperature using the calibrated temperature measurement method named in the process SOP before transfer to the rolling mill; if the measured temperature deviates from the target, follow the hold-and-adjust procedure. Records to keep: temperature logs tied to heat IDs, measurement device calibration records, and any corrective actions for temperature deviations. See SOP-P2-L1-03 for measurement technique and SOP-P1-L2-02 for related transfer and handling steps; consult ECN-2026-048 for any changes to target temperature rationale.

Q: What is the correct target billet temperature setting for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01), and why is this specific temperature used?
A: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Background: this target is the process setpoint used to achieve the metallurgical state required for downstream machining and forging. Rationale: setting the heater to 1235 °C ensures the billet reaches a uniform temperature profile that supports predictable material flow and surface condition during machining. Example application: verify that billets reach and hold 1235 °C prior to transfer to the machining station; if billets do not achieve the specified temperature, follow troubleshooting steps in SOP-P1-L3-03. Records to keep: log the heater setpoint, operator confirmation that billets reached 1235 °C, and any corrective actions taken. Reference procedures: consult SB-1037 for process validation data and SOP-P1-L3-03 for in-shift operator steps.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02), and what actions should be taken if the limit is approached?
A: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Background: this limit is the maximum allowable system pressure for safe operation and component life management. Rationale: operating at or below 295 bar reduces risk of hydraulic component overstress and maintains predictable press performance. Example scenario: if system pressure indications trend toward 295 bar during a production cycle, pause loading and follow the pressure-relief and inspection steps outlined in SOP-P1-L3-03. Records to keep: pressure readouts, time-stamped operator notes indicating when pressure reached a critical level, and any maintenance or adjustments performed. Reference procedures: see SB-1038 for hydraulic maintenance history and SOP-P1-L3-03 for operator response steps.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and what are the handling and documentation expectations?
A: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. Background: this lubricant was validated for compatibility with shot blast cabinet components and the heat-treat environment. Rationale: using CFW-LUB-526 avoids chemical incompatibilities and reduces wear on bearings and linkage. Example procedure: when replenishing or reapplying lubricant to EQ-P3-L4-SB03, use only CFW-LUB-526 and follow the application method in SB-1037. Records to keep: part number used, quantity applied, batch or lot identifier from the lubricant container, and the name of the person performing application. Reference procedures: SB-1037 contains approved lubricants list and handling notes; SOP-P1-L3-03 contains application checkpoint items.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03), and how should deviations be handled?
A: The lubricant part number for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is CFW-LUB-725. Background: CFW-LUB-725 was selected after compatibility testing with induction heater seals and conveyors. Rationale: using the specified lubricant maintains equipment reliability and prevents contamination of machining processes. Example of deviation management: if CFW-LUB-725 is not available, do not substitute without an approved deviation. Initiate the documented deviation request and reference SB-1038 for historical approvals. Records to keep: lubricant part number applied, justification for any deviation request, approval record, and post-deviation inspection notes. Reference procedures: consult SB-1038 for past deviation outcomes and SOP-P1-L3-03 for routine lubrication checkpoints.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and what inspection and recordkeeping practices are required?
A: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938. Background: CFW-LUB-938 is approved for ring rolling support equipment where specific high-temperature-compatible lubricants are required. Rationale: using CFW-LUB-938 minimizes bearing failures and preserves surface finish critical to ring rolling feed mechanisms. Example inspection practice: after lubricant application, inspect linkage points and record visual condition and any abnormalities in the equipment log. Records to keep: lubricant part number and batch identifier, date and time of application, inspector/operator initials, and any corrective actions taken. Reference procedures: SB-1037 lists approved lubricants and inspection checkpoints; SOP-P1-L3-03 details the log format and mandatory fields.

Related documents: SB-1037, SB-1038, SOP-P1-L3-03.

# FAQ-030 Engineering FAQ #30

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the required maintenance interval for shot media top-up on Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why is that interval used?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours. Background: consistent media size and quantity are required to maintain blast energy and part finish. Rationale: a fixed operating-hour interval prevents gradual depletion and segregation that lead to inconsistent surface condition. Example: if production runs are heavy, schedule a top-up at the next planned service opportunity that coincides with end of a shift to avoid mid-run interruptions. Records to keep: log the equipment id, date and time of top-up, operator name, batch of media used, and any observed contamination or abnormal media wear. Reference procedures: see SOP-P3-L2-04 for blast cabinet handling and media classification.

Q: What is the specified main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and how should it be applied?
A: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Background: correct bolt preload secures the ram assembly and maintains alignment under load. Rationale: using the specified torque prevents bolt yielding and ensures clamping force within design limits. Application steps: clean threads, apply the manufacturer-specified lubricant to threads if required by the applicable maintenance specification in SOP-P2-L4-02, and use a calibrated torque wrench rated for the required range. Perform torque in the pattern specified by the press assembly drawing to achieve uniform preload. Records to keep: maintenance record with equipment id, bolt identification if available, torque value applied, tool calibration id, technician initials, and any deviation or re-torque actions.

Q: Which lubricant part number is approved for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02), and what are the usage instructions?
A: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508. Background: using the correct lubricant ensures spindle and axis drive longevity and consistent thermal behavior during machining. Rationale: approved lubricants are qualified for viscosity, additive chemistry, and compatibility with seals and materials in the machine. Usage instructions: apply per the machine manufacturer recommendations and the lubrication schedule documented in SOP-P1-L1-05. Store lubricant in labeled containers, control stock rotation, and do not dilute or mix with other lubricants. Records to keep: batch or lot id from the lubricant container, date of application, quantity used, machine id, and responsible technician.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03), and what safeguards should be in place?
A: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar. Background: the hydraulic system components, hoses, valves, and actuators are rated to a maximum service pressure; exceeding that rating risks component failure and safety hazards. Rationale: setting relief valves and pressure monitoring alarms at or below the limit provides protection against transient overpressure events. Safeguards: verify relief valve settings and alarm thresholds during start-up checks, inspect pressure lines for wear, and ensure pressure gauges are calibrated and readable. Records to keep: calibration certificates for pressure gauges, relief valve set records, start-up check logs including instrument readings, and any incident reports related to overpressure. See SOP-P3-L2-04 for hydraulic system maintenance practices.

Q: What is the maximum quench delay allowed for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and how is compliance demonstrated?
A: The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Background: quench delay influences microstructure and mechanical properties; control of delay is critical to meet heat-treat specifications. Rationale: limiting delay prevents undesirable transformation and ensures repeatable part performance. Compliance demonstration: time each load transfer from furnace to quench and record the measured delay. If automated transfer is used, validate the automation cycle time and log the event timestamps. Records to keep: heat-treat job record with furnace id, lot id, operator, start and quench timestamps, measured delay, and any deviations or corrective actions. Reference procedures: follow SOP-P2-L4-02 for heat-treat cycle control and SOP-P3-L4-04 for furnace safety and verification where applicable.

Related documents: SOP-P1-L1-05, SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P3-L2-04

Document control note: maintain the records specified above in the document control system under the equipment file for each referenced asset.
